title: highlight: case-insensitive code block language matching
description:
Closes #1080.

A code block's language class now matches a grammar case-insensitively, as in Pandoc. ```` ```R ````, ```` {.R} ```` and ```` ```Dockerfile ```` (against a user grammar named `dockerfile`) now highlight. The author's class is left on the element unchanged (`<pre class="sourceCode R">`).

## What changed

- `crates/quarto-highlight/src/registry.rs` — `Registry::resolve` tries the class as written, then ASCII-lowercased. All built-in keys and aliases are lowercase. This also makes the public `highlight`, `highlight_captures` and `is_language_supported` case-insensitive, so the LSP / editor semantic tokens match the render.
- `crates/quarto-highlight/src/annotate.rs` — the walker asks the `UserGrammarProvider` for the class as written, then lowercased, and calls `highlight` with whichever key the provider recognized. Neither provider implementation needed changes (native wasmtime `UserGrammars` and the hub-client `JsUserGrammars`). A grammar registered under a mixed-case name still matches its exact class.

## Testing

- New tests, which failed before the fix and pass after:
  - `annotate::annotates_builtin_class_case_insensitively` (`R`, `Python`, `YAML`, `Js`; asserts the class is kept)
  - `annotate::builtin_lookup_api_is_case_insensitive`
  - `trait_provider::provider_matches_class_case_insensitively` (`dockerfile` grammar, `Dockerfile` class)
  - `trait_provider::provider_exact_case_match_wins_over_lowercase` (regression guard; passed before and after)
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-highlight -p quarto-lsp-core`: 101/101 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p quarto-highlight --all-targets -- -D warnings` (macOS host): clean.
- End-to-end: rendered the issue's repro with `q2 render`. All three blocks are now `<pre class="sourceCode R">`, `<pre class="sourceCode r">` and `<pre class="sourceCode R" data-filename="example.R">`.
- `q2 render --strict` on the plan note: no diagnostics for the note itself. The single-file project render reports one Q-12-13 error for an unrelated listing item (`plans/2026-11-05-navbar-responsive-text.html`), which comes from the partial render, not from this change.

**Not verified:**
- Windows cross-clippy (`--target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) can't build from macOS: the tree-sitter grammar crates' `cc` build scripts fail for that target. The change uses no platform-specific APIs.
- `wasm32-unknown-unknown` check: not run, because it needs the wasm clang/sysroot setup. The code is target-agnostic (`annotate.rs` already runs on both targets). CI covers it.
- Not checked in the hub-client browser preview.

description: The live preview now keeps its theme when a host frames it with `sandbox="allow-scripts"` and no `allow-same-origin`. Before, the document rendered unstyled. title: q2 preview: work behind a path-prefix proxy
description:
Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-05-q2-preview-proxy-base-path.md`

## Why

Posit Assistant's Canvas, Posit Workbench, JupyterHub (`/user/<name>/proxy/<port>/`) and code-server (`/proxy/<port>/`) serve a local port under a path prefix and strip it before forwarding. Quarto 1's preview works behind them. `q2 preview` didn't, in either mode, because both built URLs from the server root, so their requests landed on the proxy's own root:

- **Live viewer:** the WebSocket, `/health` and every `/api/preview/*` call missed, so the page never connected.
- **`--static`:** the first page loaded, but the reload stream (`/__q2-preview/events`) missed, and navigating to a root-absolute `reload` target left the prefix.

The prefix isn't known when `q2 preview` starts (Canvas creates it after the URL is printed), so this needs no flag.

## What

- **Live viewer:** a new `serverUrl` helper (`q2-preview-spa/src/serverUrl.ts`) resolves `/health`, `/ws` and `/api/preview/*` against `document.baseURI`, the way `hub-client/src/pandoc/nativeRender.ts` already does. Every call site in the SPA goes through it.
- **`--static` server:** every URL it emits is relative to the request: the `/` redirect, the directory slash redirect, the PDF-to-viewer redirect and its `?file=` (relative to the viewer page, which is what pdf.js resolves it against), listing links, and the viewer page's `<script src>`.
- **`--static` reload client:** the injected script carries `data-q2-root`, the relative way back to the site root (`./`, `../`, …). `client.js` resolves the event stream, `reload` targets and the viewer check against it. Unlike Quarto 1's regex over known proxy prefixes, this works under any stripping proxy.
- **`--static` URL encoding:** the printed launch URL and `reload` targets are now percent-encoded (the server's existing `encode_path`). Before, a page named `C#-notes.html` opened at, or reloaded to, `/C`. This bug predates the proxy work, but this PR rewrites the code that consumes those targets.

## Tests

- `quarto-preview` `static_mode.rs`: new tests resolve every redirect, listing link and injected root against a page under `https://host/p/abc123/` and check they stay under the prefix, at several depths and for a 404 page. Existing assertions that pinned absolute URLs (`location: /doc.html`, `EventSource("/__q2-preview/events")`) now pin the relative form.
- `q2-preview-spa/src/staticModeClient.test.ts`: runs `client.js` against a fake `window`/`EventSource` under `/p/abc123/`: stream URL, re-anchored navigation, reload-in-place, and the pdf.js viewer.
- `q2-preview-spa/src/serverUrl.test.ts`: the helper, plus a source scan that fails on any server URL built from the origin (`.host`, `.origin`) or passed to `fetch`/`WebSocket`/`EventSource` as a root-absolute literal or an ALL_CAPS route constant, including calls split across lines. Fixtures taken from `main`'s offending lines pin it; run against `main`'s sources it flags all seven sites this PR fixes.
- `q2` `preview_static.rs`: `output_urls_are_percent_encoded`.
- `preview_static_e2e.rs` and `StaleCaptureOverlay.integration.test.tsx`: updated for the relative URLs.

## Verification

- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-preview`, the `q2` static-preview tests, `cargo clippy -p quarto -p quarto-preview --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask lint`, and the q2-preview-spa unit and integration tests and `tsc` all pass locally (macOS).
- End to end, through a path-stripping proxy at `/p/abc123/` in headless Chromium, after rebuilding the WASM, the SPA and `q2`: in both modes the page renders, an edit re-renders it, and no request leaves the prefix. Under `--static`, editing another page navigates the browser to it, still under the prefix. The plan has the request logs.
- `q2 preview --static C#-notes.qmd` prints `http://127.0.0.1:4789/C%23-notes.html`, which serves the page (200).
- Not run: `cargo xtask verify`, the PDF viewer through the proxy in a browser (unit tests only), the encoded `reload` navigation in a browser, `--allow-edit` editing, and a Windows cross-check (no platform-specific code).

## Not covered

- `--ui editor` (hub-client) keeps its build-time `VITE_HUB_BASE_PATH`.
- `--join` and `--share` aren't covered either.
- The URL needs its trailing slash (`/p/abc123/`, not `/p/abc123`), as the SPA's own relative assets already do. Proxies redirect to add it.

title: diagnostics: warn on Quarto 1 {mermaid}/{dot} cells (Q-2-58)
description:
Closes #1067.

```{mermaid}` and ```{dot}` cells used to render silently as code blocks. They now draw a `Q-2-58` warning at the class: drop the braces for Mermaid, and Graphviz is not available yet for dot. One code covers both, so a project whose engine takes the brace form can set `diagnostics: {Q-2-58: off}`.

## What changed
- New read-only transform `brace-diagram-cell-diagnostics` (B1, after `reference-link-diagnostics`). It runs after engine execution, so cells an engine claimed are already replaced and never warn.
- Error catalog entry, `docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-58.qmd` (with its own example suppressed), docs nav, and a link from the Diagrams guide.
- Not changed: the `{mermaid}` class keeps its braces. Engine cell detection depends on it.

## Testing
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core -p quarto-error-catalog`: 6743 passed, 0 failed (incl. new unit tests and updated pipeline transform-list tests).
- `cargo clippy -p quarto-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Manual `q2 render` of the issue repro: warns for both `{mermaid}` and `{dot}` with correct lines; `Q-2-58: off` in front matter silences it.
- `q2 render --strict` on the plan and the new docs page: no warnings from these files. Partial renders in those projects print unrelated companion/listing errors for pages not rendered in the run.
- Not verified: Windows cross-clippy (`aws-lc-sys` cannot build for the msvc target on this machine; the change uses no platform APIs). No engine that claims the brace form was tested, only the pipeline ordering.

title: Execution records: one record per run, presented by Rust, with Jupyter-owned languages and inline expressions
description:
### Summary

An engine's output for one run of a document is now a single record, and one Rust presenter turns that record into markdown. The record is an nbformat 4.5 ipynb with `quarto_` metadata. Before this branch, q2 kept three separate caches of execution results (preview capture and splice, the stored-notebook replay engine, and the preview capture payload), and each engine formatted its own markdown.

Two user-visible features come with it:

- **Jupyter runs any language it owns.** The resolver assigns each language to an engine, and the Jupyter engine finds a kernel the way Quarto 1 does. A `{ggsql}`, `{julia}` or `{r}` cell now runs on an installed kernel. The `jupyter:` front-matter key selects the kernel.
- **Jupyter executes inline expressions.** A span such as `{python} 1+1` in prose is evaluated on the kernel and replaced by its value. This closes bd-u996g8g2.

Records also let `q2 preview` and hub show an up-to-date page after a prose-only edit, without re-running anything. Freeze is out of scope, and this branch lays only its groundwork.

### What changed

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| Presenter (EXR-1, 1b) | A format-agnostic Rust presenter, WASM-clean, with golden parity against the old output. The replay engine moved out of the native-only module. |
| Units (EXR-2) | One scanner finds code cells and inline spans in document order, shared by every engine. |
| Record (EXR-4) | A deterministic record format with an execution-input hash. Cell ids and hashes use Positron's format. |
| Jupyter (EXR-3, 5, 6) | Inline expressions, record emission in shadow mode, then the flip: Jupyter output is presented from the record. |
| Owned languages (JOL-1, 2a, 2b, 4, 5) | Resolver-assigned ownership replaces three hard-coded language lists. The `jupyter:` key is honored. The wire carries the owned-language set. |
| Julia, marimo (EXR-8, 9) | Julia is presented by core (`presentedBy: "core"`), and its records align to the owned units. marimo emits records but is never flipped, and its spans stay literal. |
| knitr (EXR-10 to 12) | Per-chunk options, one record unit per chunk holding knitr's rendered markdown, and inline expressions as recorded units. knitr's live path still returns markdown and is not flipped. |
| Preview and hub (EXR-13 to 15) | A new capture MIME, id-based splice, and per-unit staleness. Readers ship one release before writers. |
| Positron (EXR-16) | A display-only importer and conformance fixtures. Nothing is shared with Positron on disk. |
| Docs (EXR-18) | New pages on execution records and Jupyter kernels, plus three new error codes. The docs' inline-expression samples run as tests. |

### Where to look first

The branch is large: 21 commits (19 topical commits plus a julia-engine subtree pull), 748 files, +65,941 and −2,897 lines. About half of that is test fixtures (presenter goldens, Jupyter markdown goldens, the knitr corpus, Positron conformance vectors). The review-worthy code is concentrated in:

- `crates/quarto-core/src/presenter/` and `crates/quarto-core/src/record/` (the new core)
- `crates/quarto-core/src/engine/jupyter/text_execute.rs` and `kernel_select.rs`
- `crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/engine_execution.rs` and `record_splice.rs`
- `crates/quarto-preview/src/capture_driver.rs` and `cache.rs`

The design record is `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-28-execution-records-epic.md`. It lists 40-odd settled decisions and links one plan per phase. The Jupyter owned-languages epic is folded in and remains separately reviewable.

### Not in this PR

- **Freeze.** Only the groundwork exists: hashable inputs, self-contained records, deterministic bytes.
- **Legacy removal (EXR-17).** It is gated on a trigger and has no date. The old capture paths still exist.
- **Several kernels per document (JOL-3).** Deferred. A multiplexing kernel such as SoS covers mixed-language documents.
- **Widget outputs and HTML dependencies.** They move to a new widget epic (`claude-notes/plans/2026-11-02-widget-epic.md`). The Julia flip drops widget dependencies that the engine used to produce, and the new epic's first phase addresses that.
- **knitr structured records.** On this branch knitr still returns finished markdown. Its records hold one rendered-markdown unit per chunk, plus files, and they feed preview, hub and staleness only. Presenting knitr from structured outputs in the Rust presenter, the knitr flip, and making knitr a Positron engine are the follow-on knitr epic (`claude-notes/plans/2026-10-30-knitr-execution-records-epic.md`, branch `feature/knitr-execution-records-epic`).

### Things reviewers should know

- **Julia and marimo changes live on forks.** They are consumed by commit from `gordonwoodhull/quarto-julia-engine`, `gordonwoodhull/QuartoNotebookRunner.jl` and `gordonwoodhull/quarto-marimo`. The julia-engine subtree is pulled from `q2/node-port`. Upstreaming is a follow-up.
- **Snapshot and golden files.** The goldens under `tests/fixtures/` were added or updated in bulk and have not yet been summarized file by file.
- **Behavior change:** a prose-only edit no longer marks a record stale in preview.

title: knitr execution records: the shared presenter now renders knitr output
description:
### Summary

This PR moves knitr onto execution records. Until now, a knitr chunk reached the page as markdown that R had already written, and the record held only that finished text. Now R reports what each chunk produced, the record stores it in the same nbformat shape a Jupyter kernel would, and the shared Rust presenter renders it. To make that work, the presenter learned knitr's chunk features: echo, prompt, comment, collapse, results, error text, figures, and the cell options (`fig-cap`, `fig-subcap`, `layout-*`, `panel`, `code-overflow`, `class`). Jupyter reads the same options through the same code, so the two engines now behave identically on them.

One group of chunks stays outside the presenter: those with `child=`, an overridden knit hook, or `reticulate` Python keep knitr's finished markdown as a "fallback unit". Three new error pages tell the author when this happens.

The change shows up only when a record is wanted: `q2 preview`, hub, a trace, or `execute: {record: true}`. A plain `q2 render` still takes knitr's markdown. When a record is wanted, the presenter renders over a skeleton of marker comments that R leaves in place of each unit. A corpus of 292 knitr documents checks the result against Quarto 1: 280 match, 8 are allowlisted with a reason each, and 4 could not be compared.

This PR is based on `main`; the execution-records epic (#1007) and the Ark work (#1089) are already merged.

### How the pieces fit

| Step | What it does |
|---|---|
| Capture (KNR-1) | R reports the pieces `evaluate()` produced for each chunk; a mapper turns them into presenter inputs. |
| Presenter (KNR-2) | knitr's chunk features, plus a figure sink that honors `quarto_file_path`. |
| Records (KNR-3, 4, 5) | A structured hash profile; an adapter from chunks to record units; typed inline values that keep their mime type; Positron import accepts knitr `{r}` units. |
| Flip (KNR-6) | R emits one nonce-tagged marker per unit, and Rust presents the record into that skeleton. |
| Replay | `ReplayEngine` claims knitr languages, so a replay needs no R. |

Because records are now structured, a deleted `#|` option marks only its own chunk stale, and Positron can present knitr records.

### Review guide

**Behavior change to check:** Jupyter output for seven sweep rows (`fig-cap`, `fig-subcap`, forwarded cell options) now goes through the shared option layer and can differ from the epic's output.

The PR has 13 commits and 419 files (+30,517, −580). About 9,500 added lines are frozen corpus output and about 5,300 are plan notes, which leaves about 15,400 lines under `crates/`. Start in:

- `crates/quarto-core/src/presenter/` (the option layer shared with Jupyter)
- `crates/quarto-core/src/engine/skeleton.rs` and `engine/knitr/` (capture, `chunk_records.rs`, the marker skeleton)
- `crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/engine_execution.rs` and `record_splice.rs`

The design record is `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-30-knitr-execution-records-epic.md`.

**Also fixed here:** an `{sql}` chunk with `#|` options lost them in any recorded run, because the unit id used `--|` and knitr stops reading options at a different comment prefix. The id line now copies the prefix of the author's first option line. The bug predates this PR.

**Rebase note:** the Ark PR took the error code Q-18-11, so the knitr notes are Q-18-12 (cache off while recording), Q-18-13 (hook replaced) and Q-18-14 (child document kept as knitr wrote it). The knitr figure path now also reports unusable images (Q-18-11).

### Not in this PR

- Removing fallback units (KNR-8; gated on a trigger, not scheduled).
- Docs and end-to-end pass (KNR-7): only the figures page and the three error pages exist.
- Inline markers on knitr 1.44 and 1.52 are unchecked; the flip was verified on the installed knitr.
- The real-Ark half of the Positron check (K-S2) waits on RIU-3/4 and bd-wzz90981.
- Custom engines such as `listeng` run and match Quarto 1, but the corpus harness leaves them unowned, so `s5/01_odd_chunks` is allowlisted.

### Test plan

- [ ] End-to-end with the `q2` binary: render a document with `{r}`, `{sql}` and `{bash}` chunks, plain and with `execute: {record: true}`, and diff the output

title: Run `{r}` cells on Ark through the Jupyter engine
description:
## Summary

A `.qmd` with `{r}` cells now renders with Ark as the Jupyter kernel, plots included, using this front matter and no `engine:` key:

```yaml
jupyter:
  kernel: ark
  claims: {r: 1}
```

Three problems stood between Ark and a finished render, and one commit removes each:

- **Plots.** Ark sends `image/png` as base64 without padding, which the strict decoder rejected. The decoder now accepts missing padding and strips whitespace, so Ark's figures reach the page.
- **Failed images.** An image that cannot be decoded used to vanish, and its `[Image output]` placeholder raised a spurious `Q-2-49`. It now raises `Q-18-4` at the cell, and the placeholder is escaped.
- **Kernel choice.** The engine picked a kernel from a hard-coded language table, so `jupyter: nosuchkernel` ran `python3` without complaint. It now takes:
  1. a kernel named in the document;
  2. otherwise a registered kernelspec matching the first cell's language;
  3. otherwise the old table.

  An unknown name is an error that lists the available kernels.

A fourth commit documents the setup in `docs/guides/authoring/engines.qmd` ("Running R cells on a Jupyter kernel"). The first commit holds the Epic A and Epic B plans and a 49-case corpus that pins today's engine resolution.

## Why the `claims` line is there, and what comes next (Epic B)

`jupyter: ark` alone should be enough. Today it is not: knitr's claim on `r` ties with Jupyter's, so knitr wins, and the `claims` line is the interim way around that. That tie is the reason for Epic B. Making `jupyter: ark` work on its own means redefining the resolver tiers T1 and T2, and probably T3 and T4, together, not adding another tie-break.

This PR does not implement any of that. The Epic B plan (`claude-notes/plans/2026-11-04-engine-interface-review.md`) records the design review. Its provisional proposal, D2b, is a joint T1/T2 pass in which an explicitly listed engine wins its languages. It also holds seven questions (R1 to R7) for the owner. The 49-case corpus pins current behavior, and 14 of its cases are marked `pending-phase4`, meaning they are expected to fail until the resolver is redesigned. Please review the Epic B plan as a proposal, not as something this PR delivers.

## Verification

I ran the `q2` binary with only the `ark` kernelspec registered and inspected each output:

| Document | Result |
|---|---|
| `jupyter: {kernel: ark, claims: {r: 1}}` | Three outputs, including an 800×600 PNG at `example_files/figure-html/cell-3-output-1.png`. No warnings and no `.rmarkdown`. |
| `jupyter: nosuchkernel` | Exit 1: `kernelspec 'nosuchkernel' not found`, with the available kernels listed. |
| Corrupt image payload | `Warning [Q-18-4]` at the cell, and no `Q-2-49`. |
| `engine: jupyter` + `jupyter: ark` | Still runs knitr (documented). |

`cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build --skip-hub-tests` passes lints, clippy and the strict `claude-notes` render. Nextest runs 17897 tests with 200 skipped, all passing. No `.snap` files changed.

Two suites need a prepared environment on a developer machine:

- The Julia e2e tests need `JULIA_DEPOT_PATH`, `QUARTO_JULIA_PROJECT` and a real `julia` on `PATH`.
- The dashboard goldens need R's `bsicons` and `bslib` 0.12 or newer. Version 0.9.0 renders `card-header` without `bslib-gap-spacing`.

## Not verified

- The WASM leg (full `cargo xtask verify`) has not run locally; CI will cover it.
- Windows clippy could not run on the author's Mac, because `aws-lc-sys` won't cross-build. The change adds no platform-specific code. A native `cargo clippy -p quarto-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` on Windows would close this.

title: navbar: mark the item for the page's sidebar section active
description:
Closes #1064.

On a website, a navbar item is now also active on every page of the sidebar that links to it, as in Quarto 1, so readers can see which section they are in. Active navbar links also carry `aria-current="page"`.

## What changed

- `crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navigation_active.rs`: new `sidebar_hrefs` (every link and section-header href in a sidebar) and `mark_active_for_section` (marks the first top-level item, left then right, whose href is in that set).
- `crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navbar_generate.rs`: when `mark_active` finds no exact match on either side, falls back to `mark_active_for_section` using the page's resolved `navigation.sidebar`.
- `crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs`: `SidebarGenerateTransform` now runs before `NavbarGenerateTransform`, because the navbar reads the resolved sidebar. Neither reads the other's output otherwise. The doc list and the three exact transform-order test lists are updated.
- `crates/quarto-navigation/src/render_html.rs`: active `nav-link` anchors get `aria-current="page"`. Dropdown items are unchanged.

Two choices that differ slightly from Quarto 1:
- **Exact match wins.** Quarto 1 takes the first `a.nav-link` in document order that matches *either* way. Here the page's own link always wins over a section link that comes earlier in the navbar.
- **Duplicate exact links.** If the same page appears in the navbar more than once, q2 still marks every copy active, as it did before this change.

Dropdown children are not considered for the section fallback. This matches Quarto 1, which only checks `a.nav-link` elements.

## Testing

- New integration test `navbar_footer_pipeline::pipeline_navbar_active_for_pages_in_sidebar_section` uses the issue's repro project. Before the fix it failed (no active link on `guide/install.html`); now it passes. It also checks that each page has exactly one active link and that Home stays the active link on `index.html`.
- New unit tests in `navigation_active.rs` (href collection; first-match, left-before-right, dropdown and external links excluded); updated `render_html.rs` active/inactive tests for `aria-current`.
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core -p quarto-navigation -p quarto`: 7800 passed, 0 failed.

title: website: scroll the active sidebar item into view on page load
description:
Closes #1065.

On a long sidebar, q2 now scrolls `nav#quarto-sidebar` on page load so the active item is visible, as Quarto 1 does. Before this change the sidebar always started at the top.

## What changed

- `resources/js/quarto-nav/quarto-nav.js`: added Q1's "Scroll the active navigation item into view" block to `quartoNavMain`. A `ResizeObserver` on the sidebar waits until its height has resolved. Then, if `li.sidebar-item a.active` is below the visible area, it sets `scrollTop` to the item's `offsetTop`, once. The logic is the same as Q1's.
  - **Deliberate deviation:** Q1 skips this on `file://` pages, but only because the block sits inside its index.html link fixup. That fixup has nothing to do with the scroll, so q2 runs the scroll on every page.

title: Navbar: breakpoint-responsive item text
description:
## Summary

A navbar item's `text:` can now be a map keyed by Bootstrap breakpoint names. Wide screens can then show a full label, and narrower screens a short one that doesn't wrap.

```yaml
website:
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: docs/index.qmd
        text:
          xs: Documentation   # collapsed menu (< lg)
          lg: Docs            # expanded but cramped (992–1200px)
          xl: Documentation   # wide
    right:
      - icon: github
        href: https://github.com/…
        text: { xs: GitHub, lg: "", xxl: GitHub }   # icon-only while cramped
```

Semantics are mobile-first, like Bootstrap. Each variant applies from its breakpoint up to the next key. The lowest key also covers every narrower width, and `""` shows no text.

Design and decisions: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-05-navbar-responsive-text.md` (strand `bd-navbar-responsive-text-am98rw95`).

## Implementation

- **Model** (`quarto-navigation`): new `Breakpoint` enum plus `range_classes`. `NavigationItem` gains `text_variants`. `text` holds the canonical text (the widest non-blank variant), so existing consumers such as enrichment, search breadcrumbs, the sidebar and the footer are unchanged. The map round-trips through the generate→render handoff.
- **Render**: the navbar emits one `<span class="menu-text …">` per range, using Bootstrap `d-*` utilities (e.g. `d-none d-lg-inline d-xl-none`). Identical adjacent variants merge, and a single remaining range renders byte-identically to scalar text. Dropdown toggles and menu items are covered too. When some range shows no text and the author gave no `aria-label`, the link gets one with the canonical text.
- **Markdown and links**: variants are markdown. This uses a navbar-only path list in `config_markdown.rs`, because a `*` segment there matches only array elements. Link and Image targets inside variants are rewritten per page, and `text` is re-derived afterwards so each target is resolved and diagnosed once.
- **Diagnostics**: new `Q-13-18` warning for a non-breakpoint key or a map with no breakpoint keys. It is reported by `NavbarGenerateTransform` on the authored config, and coalesced across pages like other config-anchored warnings.
- **Scope**: this is a navbar-only experiment. Sidebar and footer items show only the canonical text.
- **Docs**: `docs/guides/projects/navbar-responsive-text.qmd` and `docs/errors/navigation/Q-13-18.qmd`.

Follow-up filed: `bd-navbar-menu-text-span-lil1bdes`, which would wrap plain navbar text in `<span class="menu-text">` for Q1 parity. Plain items are unchanged in this PR.

## Testing

- Unit tests: parsing, canonical-text derivation and round-tripping (`item.rs`); range classes (`breakpoint.rs`); span emission, run merging, the aria fallback, dropdowns and footer behaviour (`render_html.rs`); markdown parsing of variants (`config_markdown.rs`); variants surviving generate, and the `Q-13-18` warnings (`navbar_generate.rs`).
- Integration: `navbar_footer_pipeline::pipeline_navbar_responsive_text_renders_ranges_per_page`, which covers spans, markdown, per-page image rebasing, and footer canonical text.
- Manual: rendered a scratch site and checked in Chrome at 500, 800, 1000, 1250 and 1450px. Every item showed the intended variant, and the navbar stays on one line at lg. Not checked in `q2 preview`, which injects the same HTML string.
- Local `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 17852 passed, 2 failed. Both failures come from this machine's setup and are unrelated to this change:
  - `vendored_reveal_assets_match_npm_package`: the local `node_modules/reveal.js` has drifted from the vendored copy.
  - `smoke_all`: three typst docs fetch URL images, and the local pandoc is built without HTTP support.
  - The local `cargo xtask verify` stopped at those tests, so the steps after them (including the hub build) are left to CI.
- No platform-specific code was added.

title: Add hover anchor links on headings, figures and tables
description:
Fixes #1058 (bd-5kf2dnw4). Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-05-heading-anchor-links.md`.

## What
Ports Quarto 1's `anchor-sections`: hovering a heading shows a link icon that jumps to / copies that section's URL.

- `AnchorSectionsTransform` (Finalization, after `appendix-structure` and `crossref-render`) adds `anchored` to h2–h6, `.quarto-figure[id]` and `div[id^=tbl-]`, skipping `.no-anchor` and anything already `anchored` (the appendix headings, so no `anchored anchored`).
- Ships vendored AnchorJS 5.0.0 (byte-identical to Q1) as `js:anchor`, plus Q1's init snippet in `after-body`.
- Ports the `.anchorjs-link` rules from Q1's `_quarto-rules.scss` into `_bootstrap-rules.scss`.
- `anchor-sections: false` turns it all off. New docs page.

## Decisions (agreed on the issue)
Vendor AnchorJS; all Q1 selectors; render-only; Bootstrap path only.

## Things to know
- **String icon form.** I read Q1 closely: `anchor-sections: "<glyph>"` only takes effect on the unthemed/`minimal` path. title: Port the Quarto 1 dashboard format
description:
Ports Quarto 1's `format: dashboard` to Q2: render, live preview, and websites (braid strand `bd-dashboard-format-k21hd4vy`).

- **Assets:** bslib and Q1's dashboard Sass and JS are vendored (registered in `resources/vendored.toml`) and compiled into dashboard pages only.
- **Structure:** a `DashboardTransform` builds typed CustomNodes for pages, containers, cards and panels. `DashboardResolveTransform` lowers them to the bslib markup Q1's DOM postprocessor produces. Both run last in the pipeline.

title: Write search.json only when Algolia is configured (website.search.search-json)
description:
Braid: bd-cdehspam (child of the website search epic bd-eip0naf4; related to bd-w0xmxkhn).
Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-04-search-json-algolia-gate.md`

## Why

q2's search box reads the Pagefind bundle and never reads `search.json`. The only documented use for Quarto 1's record array is uploading it to Algolia. Even so, every website render extracted and wrote it. On this repo's claude-notes site (1598 pages) the file is 30.8 MB, larger than the whole 24 MB Pagefind bundle. With bd-w0xmxkhn's parallel indexing, extracting the records becomes the critical path of the search step.

## What changes

- **New key `website.search.search-json`** (books: `book.search.search-json`, which reaches `website.search` through the existing book-to-website key copy).
  - `true`: always write `search.json`.
  - `false`: never write it, even when Algolia is configured.
  - Absent: write it only when `website.search.algolia` is fully configured. An incomplete block (Q-5-40) counts as not configured.
  - A non-boolean value warns with Q-5-39 and falls back to the default.
  - The default is computed after all keys are read, so key order doesn't matter.
- **No work when the file isn't wanted.** `extract_records` is skipped entirely, including the scoped thread added in #1054.
- **Cleanup.** When the setting turns off, a `search.json` that a previous run wrote is removed, but only if it is unchanged. `.quarto/search/state.json` moves to v2 and stores the SHA-256 of the bytes written. A file that has been edited since, or that q2 never wrote, stays in place. A v1 state (boolean only, no hash) falls back to the old behavior once, so existing sites don't keep a stale file. The bundle and the per-page capture cache are untouched. This hash check is a courtesy for this one file, not a general promise about output-dir files; the docs word it that way.
- **Docs.** `website-search.qmd` gets the options table row, the output-files entry, the Algolia section, and a migration note in "Differences from Quarto 1": sites that read `search.json` without Algolia must set `search-json: true`. The Q-5-38 and Q-5-39 pages now list the key.

## Tests

- `config.rs` unit tests cover: default off, on with complete Algolia, off with incomplete Algolia, explicit override in both key orders, and a non-boolean value.
- New `website_search.rs` cases:
  - absent by default
  - `true` without Algolia
  - `false` with Algolia
  - flip off (file removed; bundle and cache kept), then back on
  - an edited file survives
  - a foreign file survives
  - v1 state
  - book default
- The existing record-shape tests now opt in through a `records_site` fixture. The Algolia test still asserts the file is written.
- `format_resolution_cli.rs` no longer needs to filter out `search.json`.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passes locally (macOS).
- `q2 render docs` renders the edited pages cleanly, and the docs site no longer writes `search.json`.
- Windows: `cargo clippy -p quarto-core --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` can't cross-build `aws-lc-sys` from macOS. The change adds no platform-specific code, but a native Windows check would need a Windows user.

title: perf: 8 small q2 render wins (website render −64% parallel / −43% serial)
description:
Eight small, independent performance fixes to `q2 render`. They came out of an unsupervised profile → change → measure loop that used a realistic website render as the benchmark: this repo's `claude-notes/` site, 1598 pages, 3508 output files.

## Result

Same-session [hyperfine](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine) A/B, `main` (`2ac954e74`) binary vs. this branch, cold project caches (`_site/` and `.quarto/` deleted before every run), Apple M4 Pro with 14 cores:

| mode | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| parallel wall (default jobs) | 24.53 s | **8.90 s** | **−63.7 %** |
| serial wall (`QUARTO_JOBS=1`) | 52.27 s | **29.66 s** | **−43.3 %** |
| parallel sys / user CPU | 102.0 s / 45.6 s | 8.0 s / 36.3 s | −92 % / −20 % |
| peak RSS | 2.73 GiB | 2.77 GiB | ~0 |

## Commits (one per change, each independently revertable)

Each Δ is relative to the previous commit, from the A/B the loop ran when it decided to keep the change.

| commit | change | serial | parallel |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | **link-resource discovery:** build the set of canonical project inputs once per document instead of once per link target. `is_document_or_render_output` canonicalized every project file for every candidate link: O(files × links) `realpath()` calls, and most of the parallel kernel-time contention | −24.5 % | −48.0 % |
| 2 | …and build that set lazily, consulting the project index first. Most links point at other documents, so most pages never need the O(files) canonicalize pass | −13.6 % | −11.3 % |
| 3 | compile the built-in full HTML template once per process (`OnceLock`), not per document (bd-wb9mp3lk) | −6.6 % | −1.2 % |
| 4 | search: run `search.json` record extraction on a scoped thread while pagefind builds the bundle. Pagefind is mostly single-threaded, so this takes ~1 s off the critical path. `QUARTO_JOBS=1` keeps the inline path | 0 | −10.0 % |
| 5 | `TemplateContext::child` is O(1): scopes are `Arc`-shared with copy-on-write `insert`. Before, every `$for$` iteration deep-cloned the parent scope; a big listing page was a 0.75 s single-threaded straggler (bd-x17470jx) | −4.6 % | −7.7 % |
| 6 | metadata merge: read each source file at most once per document. Extension manifests were read twice, once for each FileId they are registered under | −1.6 % | 0 |
| 7 | parser: `coalesce_abbreviations` returns its input untouched when no `Str` can start a coalesce, instead of rebuilding and deep-cloning every inline list. Also adds a cheap `'.'` precheck in `ends_with_abbreviation` | −2.8 % | 0 |
| 8 | parse the embedded `_language*.yml` files once per process instead of per document | −1.7 % | 0 |

Commits 1–2 account for most of the total. Commits 3–8 are the long tail.

## Verification

For every commit, before it was kept:
- the rendered `_site/` was **byte-identical** to `main`, checked with a SHA-256 manifest of all 3508 files;
- `cargo nextest run --workspace` passed;
- `cargo clippy -p <touched crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` was clean.

Local test caveat: `smoke_all` fails on that machine for three typst cases that fetch remote images, because Homebrew pandoc 3.12.1 is built without HTTP. This is unrelated to the PR and should pass in CI.

After rebasing onto the current `main`, clippy on `quarto-core`, `pampa` and `quarto-doctemplate` with `-D warnings` is clean.

**Not verified locally:** the hub-client WASM build (`cargo xtask verify` without `--skip-hub-build`). Commits 3, 5, 7 and 8 touch code that hub-client compiles (`quarto-core`, `quarto-doctemplate`, `pampa`). They use `std::sync::{OnceLock, Mutex, Arc}`, which should be fine on wasm32, but I'm relying on CI for that. Windows cross-clippy was not run either; nothing platform-specific changed.

## Not in this PR

These were quantified with throwaway prototypes and need a design decision first. The loop's plan doc (on branch `perf/overnight-render`, not in this PR) has the details:
- **Overlap pagefind indexing with pass 2.** Pagefind is now ~5.5 s of the 8.9 s parallel wall, nearly single-threaded. Estimated −35–40 % parallel.
- **Per-document extension discovery reusing `project.extensions`.** −4.2 % serial / −2.1 % parallel. It changes how manifest diagnostics are re-reported per document.
- **`BinaryDependencies` memoized per process** (bd-lu2w2fk6). −2.3 % serial; a long-lived `q2 preview` would go stale.
- **LRU index touch debounce** (bd-qff7qv13). ≤ −1.1 % serial; changes recency semantics that a test asserts.

title: Resolve citations in HTML when a bibliography is set, and link them (#1026)
description: Fixes #1026. An HTML document with `bibliography:` rendered `[@doe2020]` as the literal text `@doe2020`, with no reference list, no warning and exit code 0. An explicit `citeproc: true` did nothing on HTML either. Only `filters: [citeproc]` worked, and even then the output was plain `(Doe 2020)` with no citation span and no link. After this PR the issue's repro renders exactly what Quarto 1 does: ```html (Doe 2020) ``` Two commits, one per strand: ### 1. Run citeproc when a bibliography is set (bd-0hq9pwem) Q2 reached its citeproc filter only through the `filters` list. The one place that spelled out `citeproc: true` there was gated to Pandoc-hybrid formats, on the stale premise that "HTML has its own citation path". It doesn't for single documents. `apply_citeproc_shorthand` becomes `apply_citeproc_default`, driven by a per-render `CiteprocDefaults` that mirrors Q1's `citeMethod()`. Citeproc runs for `citeproc: true`, or for a non-empty `bibliography`/`references` with no LaTeX `cite-method`. `citeproc: false` and an explicit `filters` entry still win. The entry still goes after the `quarto` sentinel, because a pre-crossref citeproc fails on `@fig-x` (checked). | render | bibliography alone | `citeproc: true` | margin mode | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | HTML / revealjs | runs (**new**) | runs (**new**) | runs (**new**; nothing else resolves HTML margin citations) | | Pandoc-hybrid except Typst (docx, epub, gfm, …) | runs (**new**, Q1 parity) | runs | skipped, as before | | Typst | skipped (Q1's `citeproc: false` default) | runs | skipped, as before | | Book projects | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged | **Review point: books are excluded on purpose.** The default places citeproc in `.post`. A multi-file HTML book aggregates references only from a `.pre` citeproc and rejects `.post` with the Q-23-1 *error*. Applying the default there would turn every HTML book with a bibliography into a failing render, so books keep needing `filters: [citeproc]`, as `docs/guides/projects/book.qmd` already says. Making books follow the default is follow-up work. ### 2. Link HTML citations and keep the citation span (bd-390vcoox) pampa's citeproc filter replaced each `Cite` with one flat `Str`. It now: - renders through quarto-citeproc's Output AST (`to_inlines`), keeping CSL formatting and merging adjacent `Str`s as Pandoc's builder does. Split runs made Typst escape the `;` delimiter as `\;`. - applies `link-citations`, which was previously parsed and ignored. Each cited item links to `#ref-` with `role="doc-biblioref"`, for in-text styles only, as in Pandoc. - keeps the resolved `Cite` node for Q2's native HTML/revealjs writers, which gives the `` wrapper. **Review point: Pandoc-writer targets keep the old shape** (rendered text spliced in place of the `Cite`). Writers with the `citations` extension (markdown, org, typst) would re-emit `@key` for a surviving `Cite`, and an empty `Span` prints as `` in EPUB. The cost is that Q2's EPUB still lacks Q1's citation span. quarto-core defaults `link-citations: true` for non-minimal HTML and revealjs, as Q1's `format-html-bootstrap.ts` and `format-reveal.ts` do. Books keep `false`, since a chapter's `#ref-` link would point at another page. ### 3. Re-capture the citation pandoc recordings The `citations` recording fixture sets `bibliography:` without `citeproc`, so its docx/epub/pptx recordings had captured unresolved citations (empty spans, literal `@knuth1984`). They now resolve, and the hub-client `recordingParity.wasm.test.ts` failed until re-capture. I captured with pandoc 3.12.1, CI's version, and kept only `citations-{docx,epub,pptx}`. Every other recording changed only in capture noise and was left alone. That noise is the capturing machine's `q2` path leaking into `quarto-cli-path`, plus `date-modified`, which looks like a gap in the recording normalizer. ### 4. Preview parity for citations The hub preview renderer (`ts-packages/preview-renderer`) drew a `Cite` as bare inlines and dropped `role` from links. Now that resolved citations stay `Cite` nodes on HTML, the preview diverged from `q2 render`, and the first CI run's hub-client smoke-all E2E caught it. `Cite.tsx` now renders inside `span.citation[data-cites]`, and `Link.tsx` passes `role` through. Both have unit tests, and the fixture passes locally in E2E (chromium). ### Tests - Unit tests for the default's rules. Stage tests per format and project kind replace `citeproc_shorthand_leaves_html_untouched`, which pinned the bug. - New `tests/integration/html_citations.rs` covers: the issue repro with Q1's exact markup, `citeproc: true`/`false`, crossref plus citation, `link-citations: false`, and minimal HTML. - pampa unit tests cover node keeping, item links, the Pandoc-target shape and `Str` merging. Existing transform tests now feed rendered inlines instead of `(Citation, String)` pairs. - New smoke-all fixture `citations/bibliography-default.qmd`, which covers the hub-client WASM path. I confirmed it is exercised by making it fail on purpose. - One assertion changed: `book_multifile_bibliography` now expects the `citation` span around `[1]`/`[2]` in HTML book chapters. title: Fix #1050 regression: footnotes and code-block scaffold lost inside callouts
description:
Fixes a regression from #1050 (bd-akkproqy).

## Problem

#1050 moved `callout-resolve` from Normalization into the Crossref phase,
so a callout is still a `Callout` custom node while every Normalization
transform runs. Several of those transforms have their own recursion
that goes into `Div`s but not into custom-node slots, so they skipped
callout content. In HTML render:

- **Footnotes inside a callout were lost.** `[^b]` stayed an unresolved
  `quarto-note-reference` span, and `^[inline]` notes became a broken
  `[1]` link that collided with `#fn1`. Every later footnote was
  renumbered.
- **Code blocks inside a callout lost their `filename=` header and copy
  button**, because `code-block-generate` never visited them.
- **revealjs (from reading the code):** a callout's footnote wasn't
  renumbered per slide or moved into the slide's aside. A `.column` inside
  a callout lost its `flex-basis` width.

## How I found the extent

I rendered a document with a lot of content inside a callout, using the
pre-#1050 build (`28d1f5bff`) and `main` (`2ac954e74`), and diffed the
`<main>` output. Shortcodes, theorems, figures, equations,
cross-references, nested tabsets, proofs and sub-headings came out
identical; only footnotes and the code-block scaffold differed. I then
read the other walkers in that part of the pipeline. `example-embed` and
`image-alt-normalize` already go into custom nodes, `heading-id` uses a
generic traversal, and `reveal-slides` only works on top-level headings.
That left `reveal-footnotes` and `reveal-columns`.

With this PR, the same probe document differs from pre-#1050 only in the
intended change from #1050 (`Note 1: Callout title`).

## Fix

Each affected walker now goes into custom-node slots: block slots as
blocks, and inline slots as inlines where the walker handles inlines (a
callout title can carry a footnote, as it could before #1050). Slots are
stored in a `LinkedHashMap`, so they iterate in insertion order. A
callout's title comes before its content, which keeps footnote numbering
in document order.

- `footnotes.rs`: `collect_note_definitions`, `process_block`,
  `strip_ref_id_markers_in_block`
- `footnotes_resolve.rs`: `process_block`
- `code_block_generate.rs`: `walk_blocks_mut`, with a new single-block
  `walk_block_mut`. Its comment had listed `Custom` as a leaf container,
  which is the assumption #1050 broke.
- `revealjs/footnotes.rs`: `renumber_refs_block`
- `revealjs/columns.rs`: `walk_blocks`

## Tests

- Unit: footnotes in a custom node's title and content slots (reference,
  inline note, and a definition inside the body); a code block inside a
  custom-node slot; a `.column` inside a custom-node slot.
- Integration: a revealjs footnote inside a callout is collected into the
  slide's aside.
- smoke-all fixtures under `callouts/`. Each one shows the bug when
  rendered with `main`'s binary and is correct on this branch:
  - `callout-footnotes.qmd`: footnotes in a callout's title, body and
    inline form, plus one after the callout. It checks `#fn1`–`#fn4` in
    document order and that no `quarto-note-reference` survives. It
    passes in native render **and** in the hub-client q2-preview E2E, so
    preview's callout footnotes are covered now too.
  - `callout-tabset-footnote.qmd`: a footnote in a tabset inside a
    callout.
  - `callout-code-filename.qmd`: the filename header and copy scaffold
    inside a callout.

  The last two are on the preview parity list in
  `hub-client/e2e/helpers/smokeAllDiscovery.ts`, so their DOM checks run
  in native render only. Preview has no tabset component (existing
  bd-47afd5ro), and preview's `CodeBlock` doesn't render the filename or
  copy decorations for any code block (new bd-3zc4sye5). The first CI run
  failed on exactly this, because one combined fixture hit the tabset
  selector in preview. I ran the three fixtures through the browser E2E
  locally: 3 passed, with the two listed fixtures' DOM checks skipped.
- I confirmed each new test fails before its fix.

## Follow-up

Each transform here writes its own recursion and decides on its own
whether to go into custom nodes, which is how this slipped through.
bd-crqs956k tracks a shared block walker that goes into custom-node slots
by default, and a review of where the format-specific `*-resolve` steps
belong in the pipeline. This PR deliberately keeps to fixing the
regression.

title: Number crossref callout titles like their @refs (#1020)
description:
Fixes #1020 (bd-h14a4m83).

## Problem

A callout with a crossref id never showed its number in its title. The
`@ref` link said "Note 1" but the callout said "Note". Quarto 1 shows the
number in all three cases below:

| Callout | Quarto 1 | q2 before | q2 after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `#nte-x`, untitled | Note 1 | Note | Note 1 |
| `#nte-x`, `## My title` | Note 1: My title | My title | Note 1: My title |
| `#tip-z`, `appearance="simple"`, untitled | Tip 1 | *(no title)* | Tip 1 |

## Root cause

`CalloutResolveTransform` built the title in the Normalization phase,
before `CrossrefIndexTransform` numbered anything. The callout was then
numbered only by accident: `FloatRefTargetSugarTransform` wrapped the
already-resolved `Div#nte-x` as a float target. The triage doc
(`claude-notes/issue-reports/1020/triage.md`) has the full trace.

## Fix

- **Move `callout-resolve` to the Crossref phase**, right after
  `crossref-resolve`. Until then the callout stays a `Callout` custom
  node. Every transform in between already handles that shape, because
  the q2-preview pipeline never runs `callout-resolve`. Callouts also stop
  going through the float-target path.
- **Build the title Quarto 1's way** (`decorate_callout_title_with_crossref`):
  - untitled: `Kind N`
  - titled: `Kind N: title`
  - `simple` crossref callouts are titled too

  The number comes from `format_crossref_number`, so book chapters get
  `{chapter}.{n}`, matching the link. The kind comes from
  `crossref-<type>-title`, falling back to the registry `kind`.
- **Keep sectioning inside callout bodies.** This needed a change in
  pampa. A heading in a callout body used to be sectionized because the
  callout was already a Div. `sectionize_blocks` now treats a custom
  node's block slots like a Div's content. The absorb rule moved out into
  `absorb_section_wrapper`, and `callout-resolve` applies it to the body
  wrapper it builds afterwards. The DOM stays
  `<section id="body-heading" class="section level4 callout-body-container callout-body">`,
  the same as before and as Quarto 1. The `toc-containers` smoke test
  caught this.

**Behavior change to review:** in **q2-preview**, callouts stay custom
nodes for the whole pipeline. Headings in their bodies are now sectionized
there too (no absorb, since the custom node isn't a wrapper Div). This
brings preview closer to render, but it does change the preview AST.

## Tests

- `callout_resolve` unit tests cover untitled, titled, simple, the
  chapter seed, and the no-order fallback.
- `pipeline::tests::test_render_crossref_callout_titles_carry_number` is
  an end-to-end check. It fails if `callout-resolve` moves back before
  `crossref-index` (I checked that).
- pampa `sectionize` tests cover custom-slot recursion and
  `absorb_section_wrapper`.
- The pipeline name-order lists are updated.
- I rendered the triage fixtures and compared them against Quarto 1.
  Titles and the simple-callout DOM match.

Local `cargo xtask verify` passes, including the hub build and the hub-client
WASM tests. I couldn't run the Windows clippy cross-check (`--target
x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) for `pampa` or `quarto-core` from macOS, because the C
build scripts (`aws-lc-sys`, `tree-sitter`) fail for that target. The change
has no platform-specific code.

Scope: HTML render only. Callouts in pandoc-hybrid and Typst/LaTeX go
through other paths, which this PR doesn't touch.

title: theme: accept `default`; warn on and ignore `pandoc`
description:
Closes #1036.

`theme: default` now renders with plain Bootstrap, as in Quarto 1. `theme: pandoc` no longer fails: Quarto 2 doesn't implement Quarto 1's Bootstrap-free Pandoc-style page yet (that needs a deeper pipeline change), so the entry is ignored with a new **Q-14-12** warning and the page uses plain Bootstrap.

## What changed

- **`crates/quarto-system-runtime/src/sass_native.rs`**: before it reads any load path, grass tries the import relative to the importing file, which for the `stdin` bundle is a bare `mixins`. `RuntimeFs` asked the embedded provider first, and quarto-sass's provider also answers bare relative names like `_mixins.scss`. title: q2 render: support --no-execute (#1008)
description:
Fixes #1008.

## Problem

`q2 render --help` says "Execute code (--no-execute to skip execution)", but only `--execute` was declared, as a plain `bool`. As a result, `q2 render doc.qmd --no-execute` failed with `unexpected argument` (exit 2). `--execute` was also never read: the `Render` arm always passed `ExecutionPolicy::All`.

## Change

- `--execute` / `--no-execute` are now a negatable pair. They use clap's `overrides_with`, so the last one given wins.
- `--no-execute` selects `ExecutionPolicy::None`. This policy already exists (bd-sl79jjiq, used by `q2 preview --static` and `preview.engine: off`) and already reaches every render path, books included. No engine is started and no runtime is probed, so it works on a machine without R, Python or Julia. Cells render as code with no output. `.ipynb` files still show their stored outputs.
- No flag, or `--execute`, keeps the current behavior (`ExecutionPolicy::All`).

## ⚠️ Deliberate divergence from Quarto 1

In Quarto 1, `--execute` **forces** execution, overriding a document's `execute: enabled: false`. **In Quarto 2 it does not.** An explicit document setting wins, and `--execute` only cancels an earlier `--no-execute`. To force execution for one render, use `-M 'execute:{enabled: true}'`. I checked that this works for both `.qmd` and `.ipynb`.

Documented in:
- `docs/guides/authoring/computations.qmd`: a new "Rendering without running any code" section, with a "Migrating from Quarto 1" callout.
- `docs/guides/authoring/notebooks.qmd`: this page claimed that `quarto render x.ipynb --execute` re-runs a notebook. That was never true in q2 (the flag was a no-op), so the page now points to `-M 'execute:{enabled: true}'`.
- The `--execute` / `--no-execute` help text.

## Notes for review

- **Inert-cell appearance.** Skipped cells render as `<pre class="{r} code-with-copy">` without syntax highlighting. Quarto 1 would show highlighted R code. This is existing behavior of `ExecutionPolicy::None` (static preview shows the same thing), tracked in bd-4gzwls31, and out of scope here.
- **Edge case.** `--no-execute` on a notebook that demands execution (`execute.enabled: true`) shows the cells with no outputs at all, not the stored outputs. "`--no-execute` wins" seemed the right reading; say if you'd rather fall back to the stored outputs.
- **Out of scope.** Many other `q2 render` flags are still accepted and silently ignored (`-P`, `--execute-dir`, `--cache`, `--site-url`, …). They are tracked separately in bd-pyxh7mit.

## Tests

- `cli_parse_tests::render_execute_flags_choose_the_execution_policy` (unit): checks each flag combination against its `ExecutionPolicy`, including last-wins in both orders.
- `no_execute_cli` (integration, real binary): the fixture's R and Python cells fail if executed, so the tests don't depend on whether R or Python is installed in CI. `--no-execute` succeeds silently and shows the code with no `cell-output`. `--no-execute --execute` executes and therefore fails.
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passes locally (macOS).
- Windows cross-check: `cargo clippy -p quarto --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` can't run from macOS because `aws-lc-sys` compiles C for the target. The change adds no platform-specific APIs (std `Command`, `tempfile`, string checks only), but a native Windows `cargo clippy -p quarto --all-targets -- -D warnings` would confirm it.

The triage record is in `claude-notes/issue-reports/1008/triage.md`. Strand: bd-2luq2ath.

title: Honor execute options at top level and under format: <fmt>: (Q1 compat)
description:
Closes #1001.

`fig-width`, `fig-height`, `fig-format` and every other Quarto 1 execute option are now honored at the top level of the front matter (or `_quarto.yml` / `_metadata.yml`) and under `format: <fmt>:`, as in Quarto 1. Before this change, q2 read them only from `execute:` and cell options and ignored them anywhere else without a warning. `echo: false` at the top level was ignored too, so the gap covered the whole execute-options group, not only `fig-*`.

## What changed

- `crates/quarto-config/src/format.rs`: `resolve_format_config`, which `MetadataMergeStage` uses to flatten each metadata layer, now does what Q1's `metadataAsFormat` does:
  - **Fold:** at the top level and under `format.<fmt>`, each key in `EXECUTE_DEFAULTS_KEYS` is copied into `execute:`. The list is a verbatim copy of Q1's `kExecuteDefaultsKeys`. Keys are visited in YAML order and the later one wins, which matches Q1. A boolean `execute:` becomes `enabled:`.
  - **Deep merge:** `format.<fmt>.execute` now merges into the top-level `execute:` one level deep. Before, it replaced the whole map, so a `format: html: execute: echo: false` dropped every top-level `execute:` key. A `!prefer` tag still replaces.
- The fold runs on each layer *before* the layers merge, so precedence across layers is unchanged. For example, front-matter `execute: fig-format: pdf` still beats `_quarto.yml` `fig-format: svg`.
- The fix sits in metadata, not in an engine, so knitr and jupyter both pick it up through `ExecutionContext.execute_scope`.

**Judgment call to review:** the bare keys are *also kept* at the top level. Q1 removes them from the Pandoc metadata. Keeping them avoids changing behavior for any q2 code that reads a top-level key (e.g. `engine`, `freeze`). Removing them would match Q1 more strictly; that can be a follow-up if you prefer.

## Testing

- 9 new unit tests in `format.rs`: folding at both levels, the YAML-order tie-break, the deep merge, `!prefer`, boolean `execute:`, and a scalar `execute:` left untouched when there's nothing to fold. One cross-layer test in `metadata_merge.rs`.
- End to end with R 4.6 on macOS, using the issue's repro: top level, `format: html:` and `execute:` all now produce a 9×4 in SVG (`viewBox="0 0 648 288"`). Before, the first two produced a 672×480 PNG. Top-level and `format: html:` `echo: false` now hide the source.

title: Fix the WebKit pdf-viewer harness flake: wait on the shown PDF; cancel a superseded viewer load's watchdog
description:
Fixes the recurring WebKit failure of `pandoc-pdf-viewer.harness.spec.ts` ("the preview pane … keeps the reader where they were"), which accounted for 5 of the last 8 red Hub-Client E2E runs (latest: run 41437007253 on #1006), and a product bug the investigation exposed.

Strands: bd-pdf-pane-flash-flake-c76rrou5, bd-pdf-preview-status-transient-4cu7tgg2, bd-e09w5yhd (the flake, same root cause), bd-xmb7rdc7 (the viewer bug). Plan with the full diagnosis and local repro: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-02-pdf-viewer-harness-flake-root-cause.md`.

## Root cause

The test's readiness check returned as soon as pdf.js had `pagesCount` and `pdfDocument`, which is before any page is drawn and before the viewer promotes the frame (pdf.js 6.4 attaches a page's canvas only when its render finishes). On a loaded two-core Linux WebKit runner the poll regularly landed in that window, so:

- the rAF flash guard was armed against the unpainted first frame and counted frames until page 7 at 150 % finished drawing (`__empty` 2–6). Reproduced deterministically on macOS in WebKit and Chromium by arming at that instant: 2–3 empty samples, all within 31 ms, ~200 ms before the recompile's second iframe exists. A test-sequencing bug, not a viewer flash.
- the edit was issued while the pane still had no PDF, so its working phase rendered the spinner instead of the "Updating" status the test waited 60 s for.
- when the recompile's PDF arrived before the first frame had painted, the viewer discarded the pending first frame but left its 30 s watchdog armed; it later rejected the old `show()`, which the pane reported as "The PDF viewer drew nothing within 30 s" over a correctly displayed PDF (today's retry snapshot). That one is user-reachable.

## Changes

- **`@quarto/pdf-viewer`** (9e9f81418): `discard()` cancels a superseded load (watchdog cleared, listeners removed) and `show()` resolves a new `ShowResult` of `'superseded'` instead of rejecting later; `dispose()` goes through the same path. `PdfPreviewPane` ignores a superseded result. Unit tests drive the swap under jsdom with a stand-in `PDFViewerApplication`.
- **The spec** (200c6d148): every wait is on the state the next step needs. "A PDF is on screen" is the promoted frame (`iframe[title="PDF preview"]`), `viewState` reads only that frame and reports whether the current page is in pdf.js's FINISHED state, a replacement is told from its predecessor by tagging the live frame, the status is latched by a MutationObserver instead of polled for, and the guard records per-sample frame snapshots and a swap timeline attached to the test on failure. The harness Playwright config now keeps a trace of the retry and a failure screenshot (the job already uploads the report).
- Changelog entry and the plan note (11aa6db41).

## Verification

- `npm test -w ts-packages/pdf-viewer`: 6/6. hub-client `PdfPreviewPane.test.tsx`: 11/11. hub-client and q2-preview-spa typecheck, eslint on changed files, changelog render gate: clean.

title: quarto-core: stop leaking ~3.5 GB of embedded-resource temp dirs per test-suite run
description:
_We're all trying to find the guy who did this_ dept.

## Problem
`ResourceBundle` stored its extraction `TempDir` in a `static OnceLock`. Statics never run `Drop`, so every process that touched an embedded bundle (every `q2 render`, every test process that renders) left `quarto-builtin-extensions-*`, `quarto-orange-book-subtree-*` and `quarto-extension-subtree-julia-engine-*` (plus `quarto-knitr-*` and `quarto-fresh-*`/`quarto-test-*` from the bundle's own unit tests) in $TMPDIR, about 1.5 MB / 49 files per process. The "cleaned up on exit" doc comment was incorrect.

### Measured impact (one `cargo nextest run --workspace`, scratch TMPDIR)
| | entries | files | size |
|---|---|---|---|
| before (origin/main) | 7,379 | 122,801 | 3.97 GB |
| after | 549 | 11,789 | 413 MB |
| removed | 6,830 (93%) | 111,012 (90%) | ~3.56 GB (90%) |

Before: 2,259 each of the three extension prefixes, plus 50 knitr dirs. After: none of those prefixes remain. At ~4 GB per suite run, the ~400 GB observed on a dev machine is roughly 100 suite runs.

## Fix
Bundles extract once into `<os cache dir>/quarto/resources/<name>-<hash>/` (override: `QUARTO_RESOURCE_CACHE_DIR`), keyed by a SHA-256 of embedded paths + bytes. Extraction is atomic: stage in the cache root, rename into place; losing a race to an identical payload is fine. Adds a direct `dirs` dependency to quarto-core (already in the lockfile). Mirrors quarto-mcp-launcher's cache.

## Testing
- New regression test: two bundles over one payload, TMPDIR pointed at a fresh dir; asserts TMPDIR stays empty and the cache holds one entry. Failed before the fix.
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core --lib resources::` (56 pass); clippy `-D warnings` clean.
- E2E: two `q2 render` runs with scratch TMPDIR + cache: TMPDIR empty, 3 cache dirs reused.
- Full-workspace before/after run above. 20 tests (quarto-hub unix-socket, julia e2e, pdfjs/vendored-asset) fail in both runs; not caused by this change, not investigated. The script capped each run's failure list at 20 lines, so the two failure sets have not been diffed exactly.
- Not run: Windows cross-check.

## Not in this PR (remaining leak after the fix: 549 entries / 413 MB per suite run)
- 511 `.tmp*` dirs. 61 (~78 MB) come from seven integration tests that call `std::mem::forget(temp)`; the origin of the other ~450 is not yet identified. Follow-up.
- Smaller leakers: `quarto-trace-*`, `qts-test-*`, `q2-c7-driver-test-*`, `quarto-pandoc-failure-*.json`.
- Old hash dirs in the cache are not GC'd (~1.5 MB per payload change); a crash mid-extraction leaves a `.tmp-*` staging dir there.
- No snapshot files changed.

title: Make os.setlocale leave the process-global locale alone
description:
## Problem

The stock `os.setlocale` calls libc `setlocale`, which is process-global. With `os.setlocale("de_DE.UTF-8")` in one document, another document rendering at the same time got `1,5` from `string.format("%.1f", 1.5)` and `tostring(1.5)` in 2,497,076 of 2,497,076 samples, and the locale was never restored. A filter computing a number would silently write wrong content.

## Fix

Lua's number formatting reads the C library's locale, so a per-state locale isn't possible. The new `os.setlocale` never touches libc:

- A query, `"C"` and `"POSIX"` return `"C"`.
- Any other locale, including `""`, returns `nil`, which is how Lua reports a request it can't honour. Filters that try a locale and fall back keep working.
- An invalid category still raises.

This is a deliberate difference from Pandoc, recorded in `docs/guides/authoring/lua-filters.qmd`. WASM's synthetic `os` has no `setlocale` and stays without one.

## Testing

`cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passes locally, with new unit tests in `crates/pampa/src/lua/os_setlocale.rs`. Rerunning the cross-document test gives 0 of 2,407,133 samples affected.

- While one document was inside the callback, another document's working directory was wrong and its relative `io.open` failed in 146,249 of 146,249 samples.
- Overlapping calls saved and restored each other's directory, which left the process in the wrong directory after both had finished.

## Fix

The directory now lives on the Lua state, and no Lua API changes the process directory. `env_overlay` becomes `process_view`, one module for what a state sees of the process, ready for further per-state pieces.

- **Path APIs:** `pandoc.system.*`, `pandoc.path.exists` and `pandoc.mediabag` resolve relative paths against the state's directory.
- **Stock functions:** `io.open`, `io.lines`, `io.input`, `io.output`, `os.remove`, `os.rename`, `loadfile` and `dofile` are wrapped to do the same.
- **Child processes:** `pandoc.pipe` and `pandoc.system.command` start children there. `SystemRuntime::exec_command_with_options` and `CommandOptions` replace `exec_command_with_env`, which #1002 added.

## Behaviour changes

- `io.popen` and `os.execute` raise inside the callback, as they do inside `with_environment`. This is a deliberate limitation compared to Pandoc.
- A relative `package.path` entry still resolves against the process directory when stock `require` searches it. Modules beside the filter are not affected.
- A directory that doesn't exist, or a file, raises before the callback runs.

All three are documented in `docs/guides/authoring/lua-filters.qmd`.

## Testing

`cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` and the WASM tests pass locally, and host clippy passes for the touched crates. Rerunning the cross-document test gives 0 of 87,458 samples affected, and the overlap test ends in the original directory.

The new tests have not run natively on Windows. `cd` output and child start directory are the parts most worth checking there.

title: Resolve {{< meta date >}} and date keywords like Quarto 1
description:
## Problem

Reported while moving the Posit Connect docs from Quarto 1.11.7 to q2 0.39.0: with `date: today`, `{{< meta date >}}` prints `today`, while the title block prints the formatted date. Connect uses this shortcode for the build date in its release notes.

`shortcode-resolve` ran before `date-normalize`, so shortcodes read the date before it was resolved or formatted.

## Changes

- **Date normalization now runs inside shortcode resolution.** Shortcodes in `date`, `date-modified`, `date-format` and `title-block-style` resolve first, then dates normalize, then the normal metadata and body walk runs. A plain swap of the two transforms would have broken `date: "{{< meta base >}}"`, which works in q2 today.
- **`DateNormalizeTransform` is now the function `normalize_dates`**, so `date-normalize` is no longer a named pipeline transform.
- **`today`, `now` and `last-modified` use the machine's local timezone**, as Quarto 1 does, including book dates. This removes a documented deviation, and without it evening US builds would print tomorrow's date in the shortcode.
- **New `SystemRuntime::local_utc_offset_seconds`.** It uses `chrono` on native, which reads `TZ` through `std::env` rather than libc. WASM (hub-client and browser preview) stays on UTC. `chrono` adds no new crates to `Cargo.lock`.

## Behaviour changes

| Case | Before | After | Quarto 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `date: today` with `date-format: long`, in the body | `today` | formatted date | formatted date |
| `date: 2026-07-01`, no format, HTML | `2026-07-01` | `July 1, 2026` | `July 1, 2026` |
| `date-modified` with `date-format: long` | raw value | `March 7, 2026` | `March 7, 2026` |
| Map form `date: {value, format}` | `?invalid meta type` | formatted | formatted |
| `subtitle: "Built {{< meta date >}}"` | `Built today` | formatted date | formatted date |
| `today` near midnight UTC | UTC date | local date | local date |

Documents that relied on the shortcode printing the raw date will see a change in HTML. `date-meta` holds the ISO value and is now readable from `{{< meta date-meta >}}`; for keywords it is a full timestamp.

Remaining differences from Quarto 1, not changed here:

- Lua pre-filters still see the raw date.
- `date: "{{< meta base >}}"` works in q2, where Quarto 1 gives `Invalid Date`.
- An invalid `TZ` falls back to the system timezone, where Quarto 1 uses UTC.
- `dcterms.date` is a full timestamp for keywords, where Quarto 1 writes a date.

## Testing

- `cargo nextest run --workspace` on macOS: 17,585 passed, 200 skipped, including `smoke_all`.
- `cargo clippy -D warnings` on `quarto-core`, `quarto-system-runtime` and `quarto` on macOS: clean.
- New `crates/quarto/tests/integration/date_metadata_cli.rs`. It covers the cases above and checks local offsets by running `q2` under fixed `TZ` values; the `TZ` test only runs on Unix.

**Not verified locally:**

- `cargo xtask verify`, including hub-client and TypeScript tests.
- Linux runtime behaviour, which this PR's CI should cover.
- WASM: `quarto-system-runtime` passes `cargo check` for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, but `quarto-core` can't be checked from this machine because the `tree-sitter` build script fails.
- Windows: the cross-check can't run from macOS because the `aws-lc-sys`, `ring`, `tree-sitter` and `wasmtime` build scripts fail. Please run this on Windows, and check that `today` uses the system timezone there, since `TZ` isn't read:

  ```
  cargo clippy -p quarto-system-runtime -p quarto-core -p quarto --all-targets -- -D warnings
  ```

## Related

`bd-with-environment-process-env-5folaygy`, in progress separately, removes the process-environment changes in `pandoc.system.with_environment`. This PR doesn't depend on it.

title: CI: key test-suite's Rust cache on the pinned toolchain (bd-ejomahfu)
description:
The Rust cache in `test-suite.yml` misses when toolchains the build doesn't use change. `rust-cache` hashes every installed toolchain into its key, but the build uses only the one pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`.

## Evidence
From about 17 recent runs per OS:

| Cause | Evidence | Misses (Linux / macOS) |
|---|---|---|
| `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly` installs the latest nightly | A new nightly changed the Linux key from `a43a7415` to `0b0a91af` | 2 / 2 |
| macOS runner images carry stable 1.99.0 or 1.99.1 | `2a989ed5` and `3e8c82f7` differ only in this version | 0 / 3 |
| Main's cache disappeared or wasn't saved yet, possibly eviction under the 10 GB limit (unproven) | The key didn't change | 2 / 2 |

This PR addresses the first two. The third may improve, since there should be fewer stale keys.

## Changes
Only `test-suite.yml` changes, across the matrix, Windows clippy and `wasm-tests` jobs:
- Install the pinned toolchain with `rustup toolchain install --no-self-update`, replacing the floating nightly action.
- Uninstall every other toolchain before `rust-cache` runs, so its environment hash sees only the pin. A real toolchain bump still changes the key.
- Set `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` and `CARGO_TERM_COLOR` at workflow level, because the removed action set them.

The other workflows still use the floating nightly. They can follow if this holds up.

An earlier commit on this branch used `add-rust-environment-hash-key: false`. That also drops the lockfile hash, so the cache would never update, and the second commit replaces it.

## Risks
- The first run on each platform misses, because the key changes.
- Anything using an uninstalled toolchain would now fail. Nothing in `.github`, xtask or the build scripts I searched uses `+nightly` or overrides the toolchain, and CI on this PR covers `test-suite.yml`.

## Testing
This can only be tested on CI:
- Check that `rustc --version` reports the pinned nightly and the jobs pass.
- Check that a rerun restores the cache on Linux and macOS.
- The benefit across nightly updates will only show after a few days.

title: hub-mcp: upload local images without routing bytes through the conversation
description:
Closes #987.

Agents using `q2 mcp` could only add an image by sending it as base64 in a tool-call argument, which rules out full-size screenshots. This PR lets the server read the file itself.

## Changes

- **`edit` with `action: "upload"` (bd-llklgl70).** It takes `local_path` and a required destination `path`, and supports `expected_hash`, `create_only`, and `wait_for_sync`. It shares its write path with base64 writes. It is an arm rather than a new tool, per the consolidation plan.
- **Base64 validation fix (bd-jiwob9g7).** Writes above about 3 MB failed with `Maximum call stack size exceeded`. The new check accepted the same strings as the old regex on an exhaustive comparison of 2.4M short strings.
- **Docs.** Updated the tool description, server instructions, `docs/tools/q2-mcp.qmd`, and §8 of the HTTP design.

## Safety limits to review

Project text can carry prompt injection, for example asking an agent to upload `~/.ssh/id_rsa`. The arm therefore:

- accepts only PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP, verified by file content (a symlink is checked by its target's content);
- caps files at 10 MB, matching the hub-client limit;
- requires an absolute path and regular files, and never echoes file content in errors.

An image can still contain private content, and refusal messages reveal whether a path exists, so this reduces the exposure rather than removing it. The MIME type always comes from the content, so this arm has no `mime_type` parameter, unlike the bd-llklgl70 description.

**Not enforced yet:** the HTTP design now says this arm must not be offered over HTTP. There is no production HTTP transport today, so the HTTP work has to apply that exclusion.

## Testing

- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passes locally on macOS. The new tests are in `upload-local-file.test.ts`, plus a golden conformance case.
- Uploaded a real 4.4 MB screenshot through a spawned stdio server to the in-process test hub: 588 ms, a 571-character result, and matching SHA-256 from a second client.

**Not tested:**

- The real `q2 mcp` launcher and embedded bundle. `wasm-pack` isn't installed on this machine, so the check ran `node dist/index.js`, the server code the launcher starts.
- A real model host, so the claim that base64 fails before reaching the server remains inferred.

title: Keep a backslash hard break's newline on incremental write
description:
Fixes #965 (bd-o662eis5). Thanks to @davidrsch for the report and diagnosis.

## Problem

Editing any word in a paragraph with a backslash hard break dropped the newline after the backslash. `Last line\⏎next line.` became `LastZ line\next line.`. If emphasis followed the break, the leftover backslash also escaped its delimiter, so `Last\⏎*next*` lost the emphasis.

## Fix

The reader's cleanup step removes the `SoftBreak` after a `LineBreak` to match Pandoc, but it threw away that node's span, so no inline owned the newline. The incremental writer rebuilds a block from its kept inlines' spans and lost those bytes. The `SoftBreak`'s span now moves to the `LineBreak` through `combine`, the same way `merge_strs` handles merged `Str` nodes.

## Review notes

- **Fixture changes:** the `inline-types` and `zero-width` annotated-qmd fixtures changed. I compared the resolved ranges before and after: the only differences are three `LineBreak` ranges, each growing from `\` to `\⏎`.
- **`Concat` in body nodes:** hard-break `LineBreak`s now carry a `Concat` source info. `preview_untransformed_baseline_body_pool_is_all_original_own_file` stays green because its fixture has no hard break. Its message reads as a claim about every body node, but `a\_b` already produces `Concat` body entries before this change, so this isn't a new shape. I left the wording alone.
- **`annotated-qmd` suite:** `npm test` in that package is already red on `main` (83 of 161, `Unknown SourceInfo type 4`, filed as bd-einzpv4r), and neither `verify` nor CI runs it. So it gives no evidence about the regenerated fixtures. The fixture guard and the tiling corpus test do cover them.
- **Triage record:** the first commit adds `claude-notes/issue-reports/965/`, including a probe of related cases.

## Testing

- Added regression tests to `incremental_writer_tests.rs`: single break, CRLF, multiple breaks, break before emphasis, and unedited idempotence. The four edit cases failed before the fix.
- `cargo xtask verify` (full, including the hub build) passes locally on macOS.
- **Windows:** the `Clippy (Windows)` CI job passes, which covers compilation only. The change uses no platform-specific APIs.
