## What this does

Quarto 1's `quarto.js` keeps the "On this page" TOC in step with the reader: the current section's link is `.active`, nested lists collapse and expand around it (`toc-expand`), and `quarto-sectionChanged` fires on `window`. q2 rendered the same markup but shipped no script, so no entry was ever active and every level was always expanded.

### The default: a direct port

- `resources/js/quarto-toc/quarto-toc.js`: the TOC subset of Q1's quarto.js, quoted with line numbers in `claude-notes/plans/toc-scrollspy-investigation/q1-toc-reference.md`.
- `TocJsTransform` (`transforms/toc_js.rs`, Navigation phase after `toc-location`) ships it as the Project-scoped `js:quarto-toc` artifact on every page with a rendered TOC, the `quarto_nav_js.rs` pattern. The preview injects the same file from `entry.tsx`.
- `TocRenderTransform` now reads `toc-expand` (`true` → 99, `N` → N, `false` → -1, as Q1) into `data-toc-expanded` on the top-level `<ul>` (one producer for the three `nav#TOC` emitters), and marks the first link `active` so the no-script page shows a current entry.

**Behavior change to note:** nested TOC levels now collapse by default (depth 1 plus the active branch), as in Q1. `toc-expand: true` restores the always-open rendering.

Deviations from Q1, each documented in the script header:

- Not ported: the anchor reveal on click (q2 has no anchor-sections), the TOC overlap rollup and reader mode (separate features).
- One fix: above the first section, Q1 leaves whichever link was last active; the port makes the first entry active.
- Three extensions the preview needs: binding keyed off the TOC elements through a MutationObserver (React replaces the `<ul>` on every heading edit); sections looked up per pass; the scroll container resolved rather than assumed to be the window (the preview scrolls `#root` inside a viewport-sized iframe, where Q1's bottom-of-page test is always true).

### Customization: `toc-component: <src>`

Sugar for a `components:` declaration (bd-react-components-a8flgldm) named `quarto-toc` with the new, internal `Binding::Chrome`: the host is template chrome, so it is never matched in the AST and never Q-25-4; an author's `bind: chrome` is Q-25-6. `rendered.navigation.toc-component` makes the three emitters (`TOC_BLOCK_PARTIAL`, `toc_block_html`, the preview's `TocSlot`) put `data-quarto-component` on the nav, and `ComponentsResolveTransform` ships the module and the manifest unchanged. The component receives the structured TOC as `props` (`QuartoTocProps` in `@quarto/components`) and the static markup as `children`; the default script is not shipped. Inert without a rendered TOC, like `toc-location`. Mounting the component in the preview waits on bd-s73m7at2 (the preview shows the default markup until then; the docs say so).

Docs: `docs/guides/authoring/navigation.qmd` (two new sections), a cross-reference in the components guide, `Q-25-6`.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify` green locally.
- Unit tests (predicate, props, synthesized declaration, render attributes); `quarto-core/tests/integration/toc_js_pipeline.rs` through the real `ProjectPipeline`; `quarto/tests/integration/toc_component_render.rs` over the checked-in `components-toc` fixture; three smoke-all fixtures under `smoke-all/toc/` (Rust and WASM runners).
- Preview: new Playwright test in `q2-preview-spa/e2e/chrome.spec.ts` (active link follows scroll, nested lists collapse), chrome spec 11/11.
- Rendered output, by hand in Chromium over `q2 preview --static` on the fixture (no automated harness yet, bd-3swqhbsa): active link follows scroll, bottom-of-page rule, `toc-expand: 2` keeps two levels open, rebind after the list is replaced, the `.tsx` TOC component mounts over the nav and tracks the section, console clean. Both deviations above were found by these checks, not by the unit tests.
- Windows cross-check of `quarto-core` cannot run from macOS (tree-sitter's C build fails for the MSVC target); the change uses no platform-specific API.

title: pampa: editorial mark span includes its trailing attribute (#964)
description:
Fixes #964. Braid: bd-87t8pnx6.

## Problem

Editing a `Str` next to an untouched `[++ added]{author="Bob"}` made the incremental writer emit `[++ added]` with no attribute. `extract_delimiter_space_info` ended an editorial mark's source span at the closing delimiter token, so the attribute bytes belonged to no inline and the writer's verbatim copy of the "unchanged" mark dropped them. Affected all four marks (`[++ ]`, `[-- ]`, `[!! ]`, `[>> ]`) and kv, class and id attributes. Triage record: `claude-notes/issue-reports/964/triage.md`.

## Fix

The span's end is now the later of the delimiter-derived end and the grammar node's end (`text_helpers.rs`). Trailing-whitespace trimming still applies only inside the closing delimiter, which always precedes an attribute. Emphasis/strong/etc. share the function but cannot carry attributes, so their spans are unchanged.

## Tests

- Three regression tests in `incremental_writer_tests.rs`: nine sibling-edit cases (four marks, kv/class/id, two controls), a span-invariant test, and the real `editorial_marks_author_date.qmd` fixture.
- `roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd` added to the tiling corpus. The auditor had been reporting 14 containment violations on the editorial-marks fixture there; now zero. The 16 pre-existing `AttrAlignmentSkipped` census findings in that directory are pinned in `KNOWN` under bd-nq3ed2im (follow-up, not a range defect).

Follow-ups filed, not addressed here: bd-01hx04kh (tiling auditor ignores id/class ranges), bd-nq3ed2im (census findings above).

## Verification

`cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` green; `cargo clippy -p pampa --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. No platform-specific code.

Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-30-editorial-mark-span-attribute.md`

Package name: express
  • 5.3.0 - 2026-10-09

    Highlights

    🐞 Bug fixes

    • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @ YuryShkoda in #4893

      Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @ cuishuang in #7459

    • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @ davetashner in #7057 and #7478, and @ cyphercodes in #7305

    • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @ lazerg in #7474

    🚀 Improvements

    • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by @ Cherry in #7366

      // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
  res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
  res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
});

    • Improve HTML structure in res.redirect() responses when HTML format is accepted by adding <!DOCTYPE html>, <title>, and <body> tags for better browser compatibility - by @ Bernice55231 in #5167

    • When calling app.render with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by AkaHarshit in #6903

      app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected

    • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @ blakeembrey in #7234

      res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

    • The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as Error.cause and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's parent/original) are no longer swallowed - by @ Nitin-Mohapatra in #6464

    • Upgrade content-disposition to ^2.0.1, which changes the Content-Disposition header emitted by res.download(), res.attachment(), and res.sendFile(): file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by @ blakeembrey in #7233

      res.attachment('user.html');
// before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
// after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html

Invalid limit values now throw at parser initialization instead of being ignored - by @ Mayvis in #7390

title: Coalesce queued preview renders latest-wins (bd-r8iqmg2f)
description:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the [main-thread render-path plan](claude-notes/plans/2026-10-24-hub-client-main-thread-render-path.md) (finding 2, bd-r8iqmg2f).

Before, a burst of N keystrokes ran N full preview renders. Now the render queue keeps only the newest waiting render per entry point, so a burst runs at most 2 renders: the one in flight plus the latest. The ReactPreview render entry also goes through the queue now — before, it skipped the queue entirely and burst renders could overlap on non-reentrant VFS state.

Superseded renders settle with a `RenderSupersededError` rejection that both preview components swallow (name-matched, so partial `vi.mock('@quarto/preview-runtime')` doubles cannot break the check). The `lastContentRef` stale-result guards stay as the second line of defense and now fire only for the in-flight render.

## Measured

Node burst driver against the real WASM with a warm SASS cache; "before" is the same driver run at HEAD (reproduces the Phase 0 baseline):

| Scale | Burst | Renders before | Renders after | Wall before | Wall after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ~99 KB | 10 | 10 | 2 (8 superseded) | 3026 ms | 554 ms |
| ~800 KB | 5 | 5 | 2 (3 superseded) | 12 367 ms | 4476 ms |

Envelope `JSON.parse` bytes per burst fell 106.9 to 21.4 MB at 1x.

## Tests

- `renderQueue.test.ts`: 7 queue-level tests; the Phase 0 no-coalescing pin flips to the new contract.
- preview-runtime 88/88, hub-client `test:ci` 437 passed / 28 skipped, `npm run build:all` green, strict render of the plan file green. No snapshot changes.
- A full PR review (2026-10-30) was done; its follow-up commits are on the branch.
- Live-browser smoke done (2026-10-30): a Playwright drive of the dev server (vite dev + test hub + real WASM) typed a paced 10-keystroke burst on a ~300 KB document — ~5 renders ran, 6-7 superseded, preview converged to the last content, no `RenderSupersededError` leaked — and a print fired mid-burst serialized FIFO (popup contained the burst text). Two consecutive passes; recipe and observed output recorded in the plan.

title: Treat `'` directly after a word as an apostrophe (GH #943)
description:
Fixes #943. ## What changes A straight `'` directly after a word, outside an open single quote, is now an apostrophe instead of a quote mark. `Dogs' toys and cats' toys.` renders as `

Dogs’ toys and cats’ toys.

`, matching pandoc. Also fixed: `the cats'.`, `Cats'` at end of block, `It's the cats' toys.`, and `d'` before a code span (one half of #221). It works at paragraph start, in list items, headings, block quotes, the first cell of a pipe table, and inside double quotes. `'Dogs' toys'` still closes at the first `'`, and `'Hello world'` still pairs. ## How The external scanner applies pandoc's `notAfterString` rule for ASCII words. The tree-sitter lexer cannot look behind, so the decision is made at the start of each word: the scanner reads ahead, and if the word is followed by `'` plus a non-alphanumeric, it emits `word'` as one `_pandoc_literal_str`. Otherwise it returns false and the internal lexer proceeds as before. "Outside a single quote" is a serialized `single_quote_depth` counter maintained in the scan wrapper (+1 on open, -1 on close, reset at line endings and block closes). `valid_symbols[SINGLE_QUOTE_CLOSE]` cannot serve that purpose because a closer is not accepted right after whitespace inside a quote. One grammar change: a hidden zero-width `_paragraph_start` token, optional at the front of `pandoc_paragraph`. At a block start the scanner must also decide whether the line is a pipe-table header, and the two candidate tokens need different ends. When the first word ends in an apostrophe and the line is not a table header, the scanner emits the hint and the next call emits the word. No `conflicts:` were added; `tree-sitter generate` produced a deterministic table. ## Fallout - Regenerating the parser renumbers LR states, so `_autogen-table.json` and the Q-2-10 case files were rebuilt with `scripts/build_error_table.ts`. - Fixtures in pampa, quarto-core, quarto and qmd-syntax-helper that used `groups'`-style apostrophes as their parse-error trigger now use a `'` with whitespace around it, which still errors. Two LMD snapshots shifted by one column. - `docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-10.qmd`, `Q-2-7.qmd` and the markdown migration guide are updated. - Four `claude-notes/plans/*.md` files relied on an accidental pairing: a plural possessive such as `packages'` was read as an opening quote that a later `` `code`'s `` closed. With the possessive now an apostrophe, the `'` after the code span became an unclosed opener and the strict claude-notes render failed in CI. Those apostrophes are escaped as `` `code`\'s ``, per the migration guide. ## Known limits (pinned in tests) Words starting with a digit or a non-ASCII letter (`1990s'`, `Agnès'`), a `'` after a closing delimiter (`` `a.rs`'s ``, still Q-2-7), and a possessive inside an emphasis inside a quote. Each keeps its previous error. ## Verification - `tree-sitter test`: 840/840 (10 new corpus cases in `inline-quotes.txt`) - `cargo xtask test`: 17518 passed, 200 skipped - clippy (`-D warnings`) and `cargo xtask lint` clean - `tree-sitter parse --time` on a 300 KB document: unchanged within noise - Windows cross-check (`--target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) could not run: the tree-sitter C build needs Windows headers. The Rust changes are tests and fixtures only. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: hub-client: Phase 0 render-path measurement harness (bd-k8ptcrd9)
description:
Phase 0 of the [main-thread render-path plan](claude-notes/plans/2026-10-24-hub-client-main-thread-render-path.md): instrumentation and baselines only. No behavior changes.

## What changed

- Opt-in perf gauges on the render path (off by default; enable with `QUARTO_PERF_STATS=1`, `localStorage.quartoPerfStats = '1'`, or `?perf=1`): renders started/completed/discarded-stale, WASM envelope parse time and bytes, VFS write count and bytes, semantic-token requests, format-check timing.
- `perfCounters` now exists as two copies (hub-client and `@quarto/preview-runtime`) sharing one `globalThis` gauge table, with a drift-guard test. This makes the package's WASM-boundary code instrumentable without breaking the repo's partial `vi.mock('@quarto/preview-runtime')` mocks.
- Every `JSON.parse` on the WASM boundary in `wasmRenderer.ts` now goes through one `parseEnvelope` helper.
- New characterization tests: render-queue ordering and error propagation, format-classification edge cases, the exact UPDATE_AST payload key set.

## Baselines (per keystroke, ~99 KB document, release WASM)

- Full render: 302 ms. Discarded format-check parse: 79 ms (18%). Semantic tokens: 44 ms. Envelope JSON.parse: 14 ms across 16 MB.
- A 10-keystroke burst executes 10 renders: no coalescing today, so ~2.7 s of a 3.9 s burst is wasted work.

## Cost of the gauges when disabled

Effectively zero. Every instrumented wrapper has an early-return fast path: one property read, then the exact pre-instrumentation code shape (no try/finally, no gauge calls). Microbenchmark shows a flat ~5 ns residual per call with no payload scaling; an end-to-end A/B driver run against pre-change code is identical within noise. title: Copy local files that Markdown links point at into the output (bd-twfep08m)
description:
## Problem

A Markdown link to a local file that isn't a document, such as `[Data](data.csv)` or `[Dashboard](dashboard.json){download="my-dashboard.json"}`, rendered with its `href` unchanged, but q2 never copied the file into the output directory. The link was broken on the published site and the render printed nothing. Quarto 1 copies these files, so sites ported from it (for example the Posit Connect docs) silently lost their downloads.

## What changed

- **Discovery.** A new `LinkResourceDiscoveryTransform` runs in the Finalization phase, immediately before `link-rewrite`, so it sees links produced by shortcodes and pre filters while targets are still source-relative. For each `Link` target it drops any `?query`/`#fragment`, percent-decodes the path, and resolves it against the document's directory (a leading `/` resolves against the project root). It keeps the target if it is an existing file inside the project that is none of the following:
  - a `.qmd` file or any other project input;
  - a hidden path or a path under `_freeze/`;
  - a file under the output directory;
  - a likely render output of a project document, such as `report.pdf` next to `report.qmd`, which would otherwise overwrite the fresh output with a stale in-place copy.

  Each kept file is appended to `meta.resources`.
- **Attribution and Lua control.** `ResourceReportStage` publishes the discovered entries that are still in `meta.resources` after the post filters, under a new origin, `ResourceOrigin::AutoDiscovery { via: link }`. That origin is what appears in `.quarto/render-manifest.json`. A post filter can therefore remove discovered entries. Entries the author declared in YAML still can't be removed, as before.
- **Opt-out.** `resource-discovery: false` is ordinary merged metadata. It works in front matter, `_metadata.yml`, `_quarto.yml`, a `format:` block, `-M`, or from a pre filter.
- **New error `Q-5-52`.** Any value other than a boolean is an error that fails the document, so a typo like `flase` can't publish files the author meant to keep out. To make the error point at the right place, `AstTransformsStage` now passes a transform's `QuartoError::Parse` through as `PipelineError::Structured`. The span then resolves into `_quarto.yml` and `_metadata.yml` as well as front matter. No transform returned that variant before, so nothing else changes.
- **Images** still go through `ResourceCollectorTransform`, which Typst needs: images have to be in the output directory before `typst compile` runs.
- **Docs.**
  - `paths.qmd`: a new section, "Linked files are copied".
  - `lua-filters.qmd`: a new section on `meta.resources`, covering pruning from a post filter and the pre-filter alternative.
  - A new `Q-5-52` error page.

Plan, with the measured before/after repros and the design decisions: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-29-linked-resource-discovery.md`. Braid: `bd-twfep08m`.

## Things worth a look in review

- **Pruning in docx/pptx/typst.** For these formats, post filters run inside pandoc, after `ResourceReportStage`, so editing `meta.resources` there can't remove anything. The Lua docs tell those users to use `resource-discovery: false` instead.
- **Pipeline classification.** The new transform is classified B3 in `BUCKETS` (a shared post-core service) and runs for every format, because the resources channel itself is format-agnostic. It is also registered in the q2-preview profile, like `resource-collector`. In preview's VFS-root mode it does nothing.
- **Render-output check.** Deciding that a file is a render output of a project document is a static rule. A file is skipped when its extension is one of `html htm pdf docx pptx odt epub typ tex` and its path without the extension matches a project input.
- **Out of scope, with follow-ups:**
  - navbar, sidebar and footer `href:` values pointing at files are still not copied (Quarto 1 copies them);
  - an optional lint for local link targets that don't exist;
  - a separate bug, `bd-mejgdrlh`: a body link that climbs above the project root is silently retargeted inside the site.

## Testing

- **Integration tests.** `crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/linked_resources.rs` has 17 tests. They cover:
  - the issue's repro, plus query, fragment and `%20` targets;
  - root-relative links, and links in footnotes, tables and callouts;
  - links produced by a shortcode or a pre filter;
  - every case that must not be copied;
  - the stale-output check and an unrendered notebook;
  - the opt-out at each metadata layer (front matter, `_metadata.yml`, project level, format level), including a document overriding the project;
  - `Q-5-52`, post-filter pruning combined with the defense of author entries, the pre-filter opt-out, and the manifest origin;
  - a default project with a separate `output-dir`.
- **Unit tests** for link-target parsing, hidden-path detection, appending to `meta.resources`, and the report stage's classification.
- **CLI check by hand.** I checked the `Q-5-52` output for a typo in front matter, in `_quarto.yml` and via `-M` (correct spans, exit code 1). I also checked that `-M resource-discovery:false` disables discovery.
- **Verify.** `cargo xtask verify` passes, including the hub-client build and tests.
- **Windows.** `quarto-core` can't be type-checked for Windows from macOS, because the C build scripts of wasmtime and tree-sitter fail. The change adds no platform-specific APIs. Paths go through `Path::join`, `pathdiff` and `to_forward_slashes`.
- **No changelog entry.** The only changelog, `hub-client/changelog.md`, covers hub-client changes, and discovery does nothing in hub-client.

title: xtask lint config-path-base: no consumer-chosen base dir for a metadata path string (bd-40luf359)
description:
Stacked on #959 (base branch `feature/bd-0x1znhgb-config-paths-phase-3`); retarget after #959 merges. Phase 2 of the config-path late-binding plan: enforcement.

## The rule

In `quarto-core/src/{stage,transforms}/` a string that flows from a metadata read must not reach `.join(..)`, `Path::new`, `PathBuf::from` or a filesystem probe of the bare string (`is_file`, `path_exists`, `file_read_string`, `std::fs::*`, …). The resolver (`config_paths::resolve_config_path`) owns the base-directory decision.

Taint, per function body:
- a `let` from a metadata read (`<meta>.get(..)`, `as_plain_text()`, `as_str()`);
- a string-typed parameter of a function that also takes a `Path`/`PathBuf` — the ad-hoc helper shape `fn probe(raw: &str, doc_dir: &Path)` the consumer sweep kept finding;
- the parameters of a closure over a tainted receiver (`v.as_plain_text().map(|s| dir.join(s))`).

Closure-parameter taint is scoped to its closure, so a shared name like `|p|` elsewhere in the function is not contaminated (this was the one false positive on the tree, in `sidebar_auto.rs`). A `let` through a `resolve*` call or `pivot_form` / `declaring_dir` / `page_url_for` / `base_dir_for` / `file_base_dir` is clean. Test code and `metadata_merge.rs` are exempt. `// lint:allow(config-path-base)` + reason suppresses a site. The module doc lists the limits: intra-procedural, name-based, macro bodies opaque, `let` shadowing not modelled.

## What it found

- **Recall check**: the pre-Phase-0 versions of the eleven migrated consumers (main before #954), dropped into scope as probe files, flag `include_resolve`, `language_resolve`, `pandoc_write` (5 sites), `components_resolve`, `shortcode_resolve`, `title_banner`. Misses (`apply_template`, `typst_compile`, `listing_render`, `compile_theme_css`, `user_filters`) pass the string through a struct field or a directory-less helper — the intra-procedural limit.
- **Current tree**: one real violator the sweep missed, `transforms/book_cover_image.rs` (a hand-rolled `resolve_declared_path`), now routed through `resolve_config_path` with the project root kept as `book.cover-image`'s fallback. Four allows with reasons: `include_expansion::resolve_include_target` ×2 (markdown-space include targets are relative to the including file by the shortcode's contract, bd-udrn0q47), `prefetch_remote_images` (a file name generated from a URL), `components_resolve::resolve_relative_import` (an ES-module import specifier).

## Follow-ups (plan §Phase 2 handoff 2.4)

Widening the scope beyond `stage/` and `transforms/` and the stronger form (a distinctively named raw accessor on `Path`-kind values) wait on the mechanism-3 row review; the scope is one constant.

12 unit tests; `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` green locally (WASM rebuilt first).

title: Config paths Phase 3: extension project fragments as virtual files; site-rooted spelling for rebased website assets (bd-0x1znhgb)
description:
Stacked on #958 (base branch `feature/bd-7328beha-url-space-config-paths`); retarget to `main` after #958 merges.

## What was wrong

`resolve_metadata_path` re-derived a value's base directory from its source span. Two cases broke that: a value rebased by `rebase_fragment_paths` kept its `_extension.yml` span while its string was already project-root-relative, and an `href: index.qmd` in an extension's `contributes.project` fragment names a project page but was authored under `_extensions/<ext>/`. bd-74ktvzv7 patched both with a file-name check on `_extension.yml` — not shared by `config_paths::declaring_dir` or the glob provenance, and wrong for the manifest's `contributes.metadata` / `contributes.formats` values, which *do* name bundled files.

## What this does

- **Site-rooted spelling (plan §4.4 option a).** Rebased `FRAGMENT_SITE_PATH_PATTERNS` strings (`website.favicon`, `navbar.logo`, `navbar.logo-href`, `sidebar.logo`) are now `/_extensions/<ext>/…`: self-describing in URL space; every consumer already strips the `/`. Visible in `get-config` (documented in the extensions guide). A file outside the project keeps its OS-absolute form.
- **The project fragment is a virtual file.** At config time the fragment's spans are re-keyed to `config_paths::project_fragment_file_id` (`rekey_project_fragment`), and the merge stage plus every config-source binder (`config_sources::config_file_ids`, `register_config_source`, `bind_config_source`, `project_resources`, `compile_theme_css`) register that id with the manifest's path and bytes. One rule, `config_paths::file_base_dir(id, path, project_dir)`, gives the project root for a fragment id and the file's directory otherwise; `declaring_dir`, `resolve_metadata_path` and `glob::provenance::BaseDirContext::base_dir_for` all call it. Diagnostics still render into `_extension.yml`; the file-name check is gone; a fragment `listing.contents` / `resources:` glob now anchors at the project root too.

## Design note

A per-value provenance wrapper (`Generated { by: config-base, from: [invocation anchor] }`) was the first cut and is what the strand asked for. It was rejected: the published `quarto-error-reporting` renders a location from `start_offset()` / `length()`, which are `0` for `Generated`, so three CLI tests lost their `_extension.yml` snippet. `ConfigValue` has ~216 struct-literal sites, so a new field was out. The virtual-file id keeps every span `Original` and needs no plumbing. The plan's Phase 3 handoff records this; `file_base_dir` is the one place to switch if the source-map crate gains a first-class base.

## Tests

- `config_paths`: fragment id resolves against the root, the manifest's own id against the extension dir; re-keying reaches every span and leaves other files alone.
- `navigation_href`: fragment id → project-root-relative; a plain `_extension.yml` span → its own dir (the file-name rule is gone).
- `glob::provenance`, `custom_project_type` (new spelling), `metadata_path_resolution` (existing fragment logo/favicon/href tests unchanged; new fragment `resources:` glob test).
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` green locally (WASM rebuilt first).

title: Config paths Phase 1b: store marked paths in project-root pivot form (bd-okqrjh8v)
description:
Follows #955 (merged). Braid: bd-okqrjh8v. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-28-config-path-late-binding.md`, §4.6 and Phase 1b.

## What

Every marked config path (`ConfigValueKind::Path`) is now stored in **pivot form** (`config_paths::pivot_form`): the path relative to the project root with forward slashes, or absolute for a file outside the project. Before, the merge rebased each value to the consuming document's directory, so one declaration had a different spelling on every page: the SCSS cache-key misses of bd-79c4do6g, the `..` chains of bd-s0jupmmv, a different `q2 get-config` answer per document, and a Lua-visible value that varied by page.

- `mark_format_path_values` and `adjust_paths_to_project_root` (renamed from `adjust_paths_to_document_dir`) write the pivot, normalized lexically on every platform. The inherited platform fork ("keep `..` off Windows for symlinks, collapse on Windows for `MAX_PATH`") is gone: the resolver normalizes at use anyway, pivot form has no long chains, and the fork gave the pivot a per-OS spelling. The symlink caveat is one documented sentence on `pivot_form`.
- `!path /x` anchors at the project root, and `adjust_paths_recursive` classifies URLs with `is_external_url` instead of an `http`/`https` prefix list (two mechanism-2 defects from the sweep).
- A front-matter `!path` is rewritten at the merge like every other layer, so no marked value is document-relative any more; `resolve_config_path` joins a relative marked value onto the project root.
- The two consumers below quarto-core follow: `ThemeContext` is built on the project root (HTML and reveal), and pampa's citeproc base is the project root (the book single-file merge included).
- `FormatCssTransform`: when a render is served from the source tree (no resource resolver, or VFS-root mode in the browser preview) the template emits the `css` entry verbatim as `<link href>`, which only worked while the stored form was document-relative. It now relativizes each marked entry to the page (the WASM smoke-all run of `metadata/dir-metadata-paths` caught this).
- Docs: `docs/guides/authoring/lua-filters.qmd` notes that path-shaped keys reach filters project-root-relative, unlike Quarto 1's input-relative form, and points at `quarto.project.directory`.

## Spelling decision (differs from the plan text)

The plan's §4.6 described the pivot with a leading `/`. The stored form here has **no** leading slash: a marked `/x` would be ambiguous on Unix with the OS-absolute form used for files outside the project (a built-in extension extracted to a temp dir), and the resolver cannot tell those apart without probing the filesystem. The value's kind already says "resolved", so consumers gain nothing from the slash; for Lua the rule is documented instead. The leading-`/` spelling still applies to the unmarked, extension-rebased `website.*` strings (bd-0x1znhgb), where the string itself has to be self-describing.

## Behaviour changes

- **Lua filters** (accepted behaviour change, documented): a marked key such as `include-in-header`, `css`, `bibliography` or `theme` reads as `assets/hdr.html` on every page, not `../assets/hdr.html` on a subdirectory page. New test `lua_sees_marked_paths_in_project_root_form` pins this.
- An unmarked `bibliography`/`csl` (file missing at merge time) declared in a subdirectory document's front matter is now reported relative to the project root rather than the document; the file is missing either way.
- No change to rendered output: css hrefs, copies and includes are derived from the resolved file, which is the same file as before (the smoke-all `dir-metadata-paths` golden still asserts `../../shared/styles.css` in the page's link).

## Tests

- Unit expectations in `format_paths`, `project::tests` (adjust paths, directory metadata), `config_paths`, `filter_resolve` moved from document-relative to pivot strings; `pivot_form` unit test; `metadata_merge` test helper simplified.
- `tests/integration/config_path_consumers.rs::lua_sees_marked_paths_in_project_root_form`.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build`: green, with the WASM artifact rebuilt first so the hub-client WASM suite (462 tests, smoke-all and pandoc-request goldens included) ran against this change; 17,476 Rust tests; hub-client unit 1,741 and integration 229.
- `cargo clippy -p quarto-core -p quarto-sass -p pampa --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Windows cross-check of quarto-core is not possible from macOS (C build scripts). No platform-conditional code remains in the pivot path.

title: Resolve user filter paths against the file that declared them (#945)
description:
Fixes #945. Braid: bd-nqq41zgx.

## What

A relative path in a project-level `filters:` list (top-level or `format.html.filters` in `_quarto.yml`) was joined onto each consuming document's directory, so every page in a subdirectory failed with `Failed to read filter '<subdir>/<filter>.lua'`. The leading-`/` spelling the path-resolution contract guarantees as project-root-relative failed for every page (treated as OS-absolute).

This PR is Phase 0 of the plan in `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-28-config-path-late-binding.md`: it introduces the one resolver the contract's convergence target calls for and makes `filters` its first consumer.

- **`quarto_core::config_paths::resolve_config_path`** (new module): takes the `ConfigValue` (not the extracted string) and a `PathCtx { source_context, project_dir, document_dir }`, and binds the base directory late from the value's own `SourceInfo`: `_quarto.yml` → project root, `_metadata.yml` → its directory, front matter → the document's directory. A `Path`-kind value (explicit `!path`, `FORMAT_PATH_KEYS` marking, extension rebase) is already document-relative and is honoured as such. Leading `/` = project root; URLs classified by `is_external_url`; OS-absolute (Windows drive/UNC) used as written; no usable span (runtime `-M`, Lua, programmatic) → document dir, today's behaviour.
- **`filter_resolve::resolve_filters`** takes a `PathCtx` instead of a bare `document_dir`. The existence probe that decides "file or extension name?" and the final path now use the declaration-resolved candidate. Both call sites (`UserFiltersStage`, `PandocWriteStage`) pass `doc.source_context` and `ctx.project.dir`.
- Contract (`claude-notes/designs/path-resolution-model.md`): `filters` moves to Conforming; the stale "mechanism 1 degrades for `_quarto.yml`" caveat is corrected (the merge stage has registered every YAML layer file since bd-x113wg9v); the VIOLATIONS table is refreshed from a fresh consumer sweep (`claude-notes/issue-reports/945/consumer-sweep-2026-10-28.md`), which found twelve more sites of the same shape, now tracked under bd-lwvumpfk (Phase 1) and bd-okqrjh8v (Phase 1b).

## Behaviour changes

- Project-level and `_metadata.yml`-level `filters` entries now resolve against the file that declared them. Front-matter entries are unchanged.
- `filters: [/x.lua]` is project-root-relative (contract rule 2) when that file exists. An authored OS-absolute path to a filter outside the project keeps working through the existence fallback in `resolve_config_file` (Quarto 1's escape hatch; the same effective behaviour the css/theme marking already has). A leading-`/` entry that exists in neither place is reported at the project-root candidate. Extension-contributed filter paths are already absolute and bypass resolution.

description:
Closes #944. Braid: bd-ex8qvuwu. Triage record: `claude-notes/issue-reports/944/triage.md`.

## What

An alias whose redirect stub differs from a rendered page only by case (`r/index.qmd` declaring `aliases: [/R/]`) was a hard `Q-5-25` error with no escape hatch. That implemented decision 3 of the 2026-08-12 aliases plan, whose premise ("no realistic scenario wants a case-only pair") the Posit Connect docs port refuted: the site is served from S3, where `R/` and `r/` are distinct keys and the old URLs must keep redirecting.

This PR keeps the error as the **default** and adds an affirmative option:

```yaml
website:
  case-sensitive-paths: true
```

With it set:

- `plan_alias_stubs` compares paths exactly, so a case-only pair plans two stubs. Each stub that *would* have collided carries a `CaseFoldTwin` naming the page or earlier stub it folds onto.
- `write_alias_redirects` probes the **output directory** (probe file written lowercase, looked up uppercase; only when a twin exists) and, if the directory folds case, skips the twinned stub with the new warning **`Q-5-51`** instead of overwriting the page with a redirect. Pages always win; between two stubs the one that sorts first wins.
- Both `Q-5-25` diagnostics now end with a hint naming the option. A non-website project that sets it gets a "no effect" warning, like `website.llms-txt`.

Docs: `Q-5-25.qmd` and the aliases guide gain a "hosts that distinguish case" section and an expanded Quarto 1 comparison (Q1 compares exact strings, so it writes both files on Linux and silently replaces the page on macOS/Windows). New `Q-5-51.qmd`, catalog entry, sidebar entry. Decision 3 of the plan is amended with a pointer to the triage.

## Tests — please watch both filesystem kinds in CI

The new integration tests do **not** gate on `cfg!(target_os)`. Each probes the temp directory it rendered into and asserts the outcome that directory calls for:

- case-sensitive (Linux CI, or a case-sensitive macOS volume): both files written, no `Q-5-51`, stub redirects to its page;
- case-insensitive (default macOS, Windows): page intact, no stub, `Q-5-51` present, no probe file left in `_site`.

Locally both branches ran: default APFS, and a `Case-sensitive APFS` disk image mounted as `TMPDIR`. This is the first test in the repo whose assertions depend on the runner's filesystem, so the Linux and macOS/Windows jobs are exercising different branches of the same tests.

title: Lua API: quarto.project, quarto.doc paths, comparable quarto.version, os.exit fails the document (GH #939-#942)
description:
Closes #939, closes #940, closes #941, closes #942.

Four Lua API gaps reported by @atheriel while porting the Posit Connect docs from Quarto 1.9.32 to q2 0.36.0. All four are things a Quarto 1 filter does on its first few lines, and all four reproduced on `main` at 3f7d4b0e8. Plan with findings and design: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-27-lua-api-q1-parity-gh-939-942.md` (epic bd-pqj37chw; one `--no-ff` merge per sub-task).

## What changes

**#942 — `quarto.version` is a real `pandoc.types.Version`** (bd-5qepzwst)
`quarto.version` was the literal table `{0, 1, 0}`. It is now built from `quarto_util::cli_version()` (nightly override included, trimmed to the leading dotted-numeric part as Q1 does) as a new `LuaVersion` userdata behind `pandoc.types.Version`: comparable with strings on either side (`quarto.version >= "1.4"`), `tostring`, `must_be_at_least`, 1-based component indexing, and `table.concat(quarto.version, ".")` keeps working (Lua 5.4's `table.concat` accepts a userdata with `__index` + `__len`; pinned by test). `PANDOC_VERSION` / `PANDOC_API_VERSION` are Versions too; `pandoc.utils.type` reports `Version`.

**#939 — `quarto.project` and `QUARTO_PROFILE`** (bd-ip1lrgra)
New `HostContext` on pampa's `LuaOptions` (input/output file, project directory / output directory / offset, active profiles, environment snapshot), filled by quarto-core's new `lmd::lua_options_for_document` for both the user-filter stage and the shortcode transform. `quarto.project` has Q1's shape: `directory` / `offset` / `output_directory` nil outside a project, `profile` always a `pandoc.List`. `offset` is Q1's `projectOffset` (relative path back to the root, forward slashes, `"."` at the root).

`os.getenv` now reads from an **environment snapshot** the host takes once in `StageContext::new`, on the thread that builds the context, before any script runs: the runtime's environment, then `_environment` file values for keys the real environment lacks, then `QUARTO_PROFILE` forced to the active list. Rationale: filters run on tokio worker threads under `block_in_place`, and libc `getenv` there races any `setenv` in the process; a snapshot also gives every script in a render one consistent environment. Without a host (pampa tests, conformance suite) the stdlib `os.getenv` is left alone. `NativeRuntime::env_all` switched to `vars_os` so a non-UTF-8 entry no longer panics.

**#940 — `quarto.doc.input_file` / `quarto.doc.output_file` and a minimal `PANDOC_STATE`** (bd-diu7rtes)
Absolute paths, as in Q1, in both the filter and shortcode environments. `PANDOC_STATE = { input_files = pandoc.List{input}, output_file }`; the other pandoc fields stay nil on purpose so a filter that needs one fails at its own line rather than reading a plausible wrong default.

**#941 — `os.exit` fails the document, not the process** (bd-9u10sb4b)
`os.exit` on the `os` table (native stdlib or WASM synthetic) now raises an external `LuaExit { code }` error with Lua's code mapping; `apply_lua_filter` reports it as `LuaFilterError::Exit`: *Lua filter `<path>` called os.exit(`<code>`); the document was not rendered*. The rest of the project renders, later errors are still reported, the summary prints, and the run exits non-zero. `os.exit(0)` also fails the document (Q1 parity: pandoc exiting without output was a failed render). `pcall(os.exit, 1)` catches it, like any error. `error()` is unchanged.

**Docs**: three new sections in `docs/guides/authoring/lua-filters.qmd` (where the filter is running; checking versions; failing a render).

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify`: all steps green, including the hub-client tests against a WASM rebuilt from this branch (one smoke fixture, `extensions/builtin-version-shortcode`, hard-coded `0.1.0` and was updated to expect the real version; it is checked by both the native and the WASM smoke runs).
- WASM Lua tests (`cargo test -p pampa --test wasm_lua --target wasm32-unknown-unknown ...`): 10/10, including the extended synthetic-`os` test (`os.getenv`, `os.exit`).
- New tests: `pampa` unit tests (`version.rs`, `host_context.rs`, `os_exit.rs`), quarto-core tests for the snapshot layers and the offset, CLI e2e `lua_host_context_cli.rs` (two-page website under `--profile` with an `_environment` file; single-file render) and `lua_os_exit_cli.rs` (the issue's a/b/c project; `os.exit(0)`).
- The four issue repros re-run by hand against the built binary; each now prints what the issue's "Expected" section asks for.
- **Not verified: Windows.** `cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` cannot run from macOS for pampa, quarto-core or quarto (`aws-lc-sys`, `wasmtime`, `tree-sitter` compile C for the target). The new code uses no platform APIs; path assertions in the e2e tests are built with `Path::join`. A Windows run of `cargo clippy -p pampa -p quarto-core -p quarto --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the two new e2e tests would be welcome.

## Follow-ups (not filed)

- The rest of `PANDOC_STATE` (`resource_path`, `verbosity`, `log`, ...).
- `EnvShortcodeHandler` could read the same snapshot instead of its lookup-time merge.
- Siblings #943–#945 are separate issues with separate causes; note that #945 (filter path resolution) is why the new e2e fixture names its filter by absolute path.

title: Allow --trust with --dry-run in q2 add / q2 use brand (bd-cjqhcaz6)
description:
## Problem

Without a terminal (`--no-prompt`, `--json`, CI, an agent shell), you could not dry-run `q2 add` or `q2 use brand` against a remote source. Each error told you to do what the other forbade:

- without `--trust`: "Refusing to download … Re-run with --trust"
- with `--trust`: "--trust cannot be combined with --dry-run"

The guard's rationale ("--dry-run writes nothing, so there is nothing for --trust to authorize") is right for `--force` but wrong for `--trust`. A dry run of a remote source still **downloads** it to build the `[Install]/[Update]/[No Change]` table (add) or the file plan (use brand), and the trust gate governs that download.

Strand: bd-cjqhcaz6, discovered while installing `posit-dev/product-doc-theme` (bd-0i6fii0k).

## Changes

- **Guards** (`add/mod.rs`, `use_cmd/mod.rs`): only `--force` is rejected with `--dry-run`. The comments now say why `--trust` is different.
- **Mode-aware refusal hint** (both `confirm_trust` functions): a refused dry run is told to re-run with `--dry-run --trust`, a refused real run with `--trust`. Both functions already read `req.dry_run`, so no new parameter was needed.
- **Consent stays required in every mode.** A dry run without `--trust` and with no terminal is still refused before any request. An interactive dry run still asks the trust question before downloading.
- **Shared test fixture:** the localhost archive server and `tar_gz` moved from `add.rs` into `tests/integration/archive_server.rs` so `use_brand.rs` can use them too.
- **Docs:** `extensions.qmd` and `brand.qmd` explain that a dry run of a remote source needs trust, why a preview can prompt, and that `--trust` works with `--dry-run` while `--force` does not.
- **Plan:** `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-27-trust-with-dry-run.md` records the investigation and the design decisions.

## Tests

New or rewritten. All failed before the fix and pass after it:

- `add::a_trusted_remote_dry_run_shows_the_table_and_writes_nothing`: prints the `[Install]` table, leaves `_extensions/` absent, makes exactly one request.
- `add::a_remote_dry_run_without_trust_is_refused_before_any_request`: zero requests, and the hint names `--dry-run --trust`.
- `use_brand::trust_with_dry_run_previews_a_remote_source_and_writes_nothing`: replaces `trust_with_dry_run_is_rejected`.
- `use_brand::a_remote_dry_run_without_trust_is_refused_before_any_request`
- Unit tests `the_trust_refusal_hint_matches_the_mode` in `add/resolve.rs` and `use_cmd/brand.rs`.
- The existing `add` refusal test now also checks that the real-run hint does not mention `--dry-run`. `--force --dry-run` stays rejected in both commands (existing tests).

`cargo xtask verify` (full, including the hub build) passes locally on macOS.

**Windows:** `cargo clippy -p quarto --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` cannot cross-check from macOS: the `ring` and `aws-lc-sys` build scripts fail to compile C for MSVC. The change adds no platform-specific code. The moved test server uses `std::net::TcpListener` on loopback, unchanged from before.

title: Convert eligible ref-mirror effects to useEffectEvent (bd-t18384ia)
description:
Stacked on #936. Phase 5 (final) of `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-24-hub-client-useeffect-refactor.md` (bd-t18384ia).

## What changed

Converted the 3 ref-mirror effects whose call sites sit lexically inside an effect:

- `useAuthProbe`
- `useSessionKeepAlive` (both callbacks)
- `useWindowFileDrop`

## What didn't change, and why

The other 9 audited sites fail the `useEffectEvent` contract enforced by eslint-plugin-react-hooks v7 `rules-of-hooks`: an effect event may only be *referenced* from effect scope in the same component, and render-phase calls throw. They stay as ref-mirrors; per-site rationale is recorded in the plan.

- `useRouting` — read inside a `setState` updater (runs during render)
- `useDownloadAs` — read inside a click handler
- `Preview` / `ReactPreview` — read inside render-scope `useCallback`s
- `useSlideThumbnails` — recursive re-invocation from inside a `useCallback`
- `Editor.tsx` (3 refs) — cross hook / Monaco-callback boundaries

## Tests

- `useAuthProbe` / `useSessionKeepAlive` gained "latest callback without re-arming the interval" characterization tests, pinned green before converting; `useWindowFileDrop` already had one.
- Full `npm run test:ci` green (unit, integration, WASM); `npm run build:all` green; eslint clean on the five touched files.

## Browser smoke

- **File drop**: 13/13 `import-document.spec.ts` tests on chromium, including the four window-fallback drops (top bar, dialog backdrop, preview pane ×2).
- **Auth probe**: a throwaway Playwright spec on the auth-on e2e stack drove the probe live — disconnect armed it, two `/auth/me` probes fired through the converted effect event, no logout on network errors, reconnect restored the online pill.

title: Measure wide-dep useEffect cost; no fix warranted (bd-wfhd0dg5)
description:

title: xtask: run per-checkout commands against the invoking worktree; fix switch-task --from
description:
Fixes bd-cvk7jb11, which turned up during bd-73lilznv (#929).

## Commands that wrote to the main checkout from a worktree

`create_worktree::repo_root()` returns the **main** checkout, the parent of `--git-common-dir`. That is the right root for placing new worktrees, but four commands also used it to find the files they work on. Run from `.worktrees/<x>/`, each of them read or wrote the main checkout instead:

- `stage-doc-examples` rendered the main checkout's `examples/` and staged into its `docs/examples/`. The worktree's own `q2 render docs` then failed with "Declared resource …/docs/examples does not exist on disk".
- `check-noop-rebuild` built the main checkout's q2.
- `gen-math-spec` read and rewrote the main checkout's `commands.json`.
- `braid-snapshot` wrote the main checkout's `.braid/snapshot.jsonl`.

They now use `switch_task::current_worktree_root()` (`--show-toplevel`). The capture-\*, `pandoc-check`, `render-corpus-diff` and `pull-extension-subtree` commands already used it. `repo_root()` is renamed `main_checkout_root()` so the next caller can see what it returns. Its two remaining callers, `create-worktree` and `render-corpus-diff`'s reference copy, want the main checkout on purpose.

## `switch-task --from <branch>` branched off a stale tip

It fetched `origin/<branch>` but then branched off the **local** `<branch>`, while printing "after pull". The local branch is usually checked out, and stale, in another worktree; `main` in the main checkout is the common case. It now chooses the start point like this:

- It uses whichever of the local branch and `origin/<branch>` is newer.
- It stops if the two have diverged.
- It passes `--no-track`, so the topic branch never tracks the integration branch.

`.claude/rules/worktrees.md` is updated to match.

## Excluded crates walked up into the main checkout's workspace

cargo finds a crate's workspace by walking up parent directories. It skips, rather than stops at, a workspace that excludes the crate. In a worktree under `.worktrees/`, the walk therefore continues past the worktree's root `Cargo.toml` into the main checkout's, which doesn't list the crate. The three excluded crates without a `[workspace]` of their own were affected:

- `crates/wasm-qmd-parser` could not be built from a worktree at all.
- `crates/pampa/fuzz` and `crates/tree-sitter-language-wasm-shim` failed `cargo metadata`. This broke `check_feature_sets::discovers_the_wasm_consumers_in_this_repo` in every worktree.

Each now declares an empty `[workspace]`. That is what cargo's error message suggests and what `wasm-quarto-hub-client` already does for the same reason. A note at the root `exclude` list states the rule. Nothing changes in the main checkout or CI.

## Verification

- Run from a worktree, `cargo xtask stage-doc-examples` now stages into that worktree, and the main checkout stays untouched and clean.
- 6 new tests cover the start-point choice (behind, equal, ahead, diverged, local-only and remote-only) and check that the two root helpers differ in a linked worktree.
- `cargo nextest run -p xtask` passes 250/250 from a worktree; it was 249/250 before the `[workspace]` change.
- From the worktree, `cargo metadata` succeeds for all three excluded crates and `npm run build:wasm` passes; hub-client builds through the shim. `wasm-qmd-parser` now gets past workspace lookup. Its full `wasm-pack` build was not run locally; CI's WASM jobs cover it.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes on the host and with `--target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`.
- `q2 render --strict claude-notes` is clean.

title: Add autonomously-fix-small-issue skill
description:
Adds `/autonomously-fix-small-issue <N>`, which codifies the workflow from #930 → #934. It takes a small, unambiguous GitHub issue all the way to an open PR without asking the user anything along the way.

The name makes the risk obvious: once invoked, the run is unattended. The safeguards are built into the skill rather than relying on step-by-step confirmation:

- **User-invoked only.** `disable-model-invocation: true` means the agent never picks it on its own.
- **Scope gate first.** Before any strand or branch is created, the issue must be a single request, unambiguous, free of open product/UX/API decisions, small (about ≤3 production files and ≤100 lines, with no new dependencies or schema/API/CLI changes), testable, and the tree must be clean. If any check fails, the skill stops and suggests `/triage`.
- **Hard stop at the PR.** The skill never merges and never closes the issue or the strand.
- **Honest reporting.** The PR body lists every check that ran, separates pre-existing failures (re-checked on `main`) from new ones, and says what wasn't verified.
- **No touching in-flight work.** It branches in place only from a clean `main`. Otherwise it uses `cargo xtask create-worktree`. It never runs `switch-task` in the main checkout, because that rewrites `CLAUDE.local.md`.

Testing: this PR adds documentation only, with no code changes. I didn't run `cargo xtask verify`. The skill hasn't been exercised as a skill yet; the reference run (#934) was done by hand.

title: version history drawer: 'anonymous' / 'unknown' labels instead of a bare 0
description:
The version history drawer now shows **anonymous** for edits with no recorded author and **unknown** for edits with no recorded time, instead of a bare `0`.

### What was happening

Automerge decodes a change with no recorded time as `time: 0`, and that `0` flowed through to `{state.timestamp && …}` in the drawer header. React renders a falsy number inside `&&` as a literal text node, so the header showed a `0` where the timestamp and author chip belong. This is the common case on auth-less hubs (`--allow-insecure-auth` / local-prod) for authorless changes — imports, CLI/MCP edits, pre-author history.

### What changed

- `getMetadataAt` (sync-client) normalizes an unset change time (`0`) and empty attribution keys to `null`. This also fixes the scrubber hover tooltip showing a 1/1/1970 date for such changes.
- The drawer header now uses explicit ternaries: a missing timestamp gets an "unknown" label; a missing attribution key gets an "anonymous" chip — matching the app's existing anonymous-name vocabulary, and the honest word for a change stamped with no name.

### Testing

- New failing-first tests in `replay.test.ts` (0/empty → null normalization) and `ReplayDrawer.test.tsx` (label rendering + the timestamp-0 regression).
- Full hub-client unit suite (1688 tests), `npm run build`, `lint:css`, `test:wasm`, and sync-client `tsc` all green.
- Not verified in a live browser session; verified via jsdom tests and the production build.

title: website.announcement: announcement banner as a generate/render stage pair
description:
Implements Quarto 1's `website.announcement` banner for Quarto 2 (braid strand `bd-website-announcement-w1gtpzki`). It is built as a generate/render stage pair, like the navbar and footer. The motivating use is a "not yet reviewed by a human" banner on the preliminary docs site.

Plan and progress log: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-26-website-announcement.md`

## What it does

- **Generate** (`announcement-generate`, format-agnostic) reads `website.announcement` (or a top-level `announcement:`) from the page's merged metadata into `navigation.announcement`.
- **Render** (`announcement-render`, HTML only, not reveal) writes Quarto 1's banner markup into `rendered.navigation.announcement-{above,below}` inside `#quarto-header`. A banner on its own opens the header.
- **llms.txt:** the banner never appears in the `.md` companions, `llms.txt`, or `llms-full.txt`. It lives only in metadata, and the llms capture serializes the page body.
- **Per-page opt-out:** front matter or `_metadata.yml` can set `website: {announcement: false}`. A map such as `{type: danger}` merges field by field. Quarto 1 reads the banner from `_quarto.yml` only, so it can't do either.
- **Close control:** a labelled `<button>`, with a new localized `announcement-close` term. Quarto 1 uses a bare `<i>`.
- **`remember-dismissal`:** new q2 key, default `true` (Q1 behaviour). With `false`, closing hides the banner on the current page view only.
- **`quarto-nav.js`:** reveal/dismiss is keyed off the banner element in the script's existing MutationObserver, so the preview's remounts are handled.
- **Preview:** `AnnouncementSlot`.
- **Diagnostics:** Q-13-15 (link to a missing document), Q-13-16 (no content), Q-13-17 (invalid `type`/`position`), each with a docs page.
- **Docs:** new guide page `guides/projects/announcement.qmd`. The docs site turns the banner on site-wide (`type: warning`, `remember-dismissal: false`). No page opts out yet; which pages count as reviewed is for the docs owners to decide.

## Regenerated fixtures (review note)

The new language term is a q2-only addition to the vendored Quarto 1 language catalog. It is documented in `resources/language/README.md` and `vendored.toml`, and a catalog test fails if a future re-copy from Quarto 1 drops it. Because the term reaches every Pandoc request, these were regenerated:

- the pandoc recordings (`cargo xtask capture-pandoc-recordings`, pandoc 3.12.1). This also picked up the fig-alt docx filter backport (bd-ykjwiqcc), which `main` had not re-captured. The orphaned share tree was removed.
- the parity-book input golden and `schemas/pandoc-request.golden.json`.

Also updated: the single-doc `styles.css` baseline (re-captured with a note, for the banner SCSS) and the wasm crate lockfile (`sha2`). `@types/jsdom` is added to preview-renderer.

## Known gap (filed separately)

Links inside config *text* resolve from the project root everywhere, not from the file that declares them. That covers footer text, the navbar title, and now the announcement. The announcement follows the existing convention; the gap is filed as bd-3ys3nkw7.

## Testing

- `cargo xtask verify` passes locally.
- **Unit and integration tests:** the model and HTML renderer, both transforms, merge and opt-out, template placement and the header gate, and an end-to-end llms exclusion test with a real project render.
- **JS tests:** jsdom tests run the real `quarto-nav.js`; preview component tests cover the slot.
- **smoke-all fixtures** (`navigation/announcement-website`, `navigation/announcement-only-website`) pass in the native runner, the WASM runner, and Playwright, on Chromium and Firefox.
- **Windows:** clippy cross-check is clean for `quarto-navigation`. `quarto-core` can't be cross-checked from macOS (`aws-lc-sys`), so it relies on the CI Windows leg.
- **Manual:** checked in Chrome on the rendered docs site. The close button is focusable, closing re-pads the page, and the banner returns on reload.

title: q2 docs serve / open: browse the embedded docs site offline
description:
## Summary

Adds `q2 docs serve` (visible alias `q2 docs open`). It starts a local web server for the Quarto 2 documentation site embedded in the binary, which is the documentation for exactly the running version. It opens the site in the browser and serves it until Ctrl-C. Nothing is fetched from the network and nothing is written to disk.

```bash
q2 docs serve                            # home page
q2 docs open guides/projects/preview     # deep link, same spellings as `q2 docs llms <href>`
q2 docs serve --no-browser --port 4321
```

An unknown page fails before the server starts, with the same near-miss suggestions as `q2 docs llms`.

### One embed for both `docs serve` and `docs llms`

- **Staging** (`cargo xtask build-agents-docs`): clears and re-renders `docs/_site` (`q2 render` doesn't remove output for deleted pages), then stages the whole site under `agents-docs-dist/site/` plus the llms ledger. It now **fails if the site loads any remote subresource** (new `docs_offline_check`: HTML subresource tags, `<style>` blocks, CSS `@import`/`url()`). The only allowlisted remote resource is the theme's Google Fonts import; offline, text falls back to the system sans-serif.
- **Embedding** (`crates/quarto/build.rs`): a deterministic tar.zst ordered llms-first (metadata, ledger-listed files, then the rest). The 73 MB / 1454-file site compresses to 3.6 MB.
- **Runtime** (`commands/docs_embed.rs`): `docs llms` stream-decodes only the llms prefix; `docs serve` decodes everything once. `include_dir` is gone from the `quarto` crate.
- **Server** (`quarto_preview::static_mode::embedded_site`): a small read-only router over in-memory files. It reuses the static server's path-decoding, 404, and redirect helpers but has no reload client, SSE, or pdf.js.

### Measured (release build, M-series)
| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `q2 docs llms <page>` (hyperfine) | 3.7 ms | 4.8 ms |
| `q2 docs serve` launch → first 200 | — | ~19 ms |
| docs embed in binary | ~1.95 MB raw | 3.6 MB tar.zst (≈ +1.6 MB) |

### Also
- `docs/guides/embedded-docs.qmd`: new "Reading the docs in a browser" section (retitled "Embedded documentation"); AGENTS.md § embedded docs updated.
- Release workflow: a smoke check that the release binary's `docs serve` serves the home page (non-Windows legs, since backgrounding and killing a native process from Git Bash is unreliable; the existing `--embed-info` gate still covers Windows).
- Rename of `agents-docs-dist/` / `build-agents-docs` deferred to bd-7tkifpnh.

Plan with the design assessment and measurements: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-26-q2-docs-serve.md`. Braid: bd-x248xpyh.

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests: archive prefix and full decode, llms-first ordering invariant on the real embed, `DocsEmbed` ported to the decoded map (existing suite unchanged in behaviour; non-ledger site files invisible to `docs llms`), page → URL mapping, `serve`/`open` parse equivalence, router (index, dir redirect, MIME, percent-decoding, traversal 404, HEAD, 405), staging (whole site + ledger, dotfiles skipped, stale clearing), offline scanner fixtures

- [x] `cargo xtask check-noop-rebuild` green

title: Rewire hub from samod access-policy fork to upstream samod 0.16.0
description:
Switches the hub's sync engine from our patched samod fork to the official samod 0.16.0 release on crates.io.

* The `quarto-dev/samod` fork is retired. samod and samod-core now come from crates.io, and automerge stays at 0.12.0 with no new transitive dependencies.
* The fork's custom access-policy patch is replaced by samod's built-in `SharePolicy`. The hub keeps its current behaviour: it only serves documents a client asks for and never advertises document IDs.
* The per-document "Document accessed" audit lines are removed. samod 0.16 checks the share policy for every loaded document when a client connects, so those lines would name documents the user never opened. The audit log instead gains `ws_connect` and `ws_disconnect` events for each sync session.
* Includes samod 0.15's protocol hardening (stricter identity checks on direct messages) for free.

Verified end to end: all tests pass, existing data directories load unchanged, JS clients sync against the new hub, and presence works across two browser tabs.

title: Fix ts_engine race-test flake: answer mock requests by real id (bd-cig41dcs)
description:
Fixes the CI flake seen on #906: `test_race_free_instance_exclusive` hung until its 15 s watchdog fired (`DEADLOCK DETECTED`).

## Cause

The test's polling watcher thread could miss the `LaunchEngine` request in two ways:

- **Wrong id.** The watcher used a message's position in `sent_messages()` as its request id. When both threads send `LoadEngine` at once (an accepted double send in `ensure_loaded`), the order messages are recorded can differ from the order ids were allocated. The `Launched` reply then goes to an id that was already answered, the reader drops it, and the watcher stops anyway.
- **Early give-up.** The watcher stopped polling after about 3 s, so a slow runner could miss the request entirely.

In either case each `ensure_launched` waits out the 10 s `DISCOVERY_WINDOW`, which adds up to 20 s, past the 15 s watchdog.

## Change (test-only)

- `MockWriteHalf::auto_respond(pred, responses, delay)` answers matching messages inside `send()` under their real id. `sent_requests()` returns the sent log with ids; `sent_messages()` is unchanged.
- Four tests drop their polling threads in favour of `auto_respond`:
  - `test_race_free_instance_exclusive`: the reply is delayed 50 ms, so a naive get/launch/set `ensure_launched` still fails the test (20/20 runs, checked by hand). The test now requires both calls to succeed.
  - `test_race_free_discovery_convergence`: this test stopped polling after its first reply, so a second `LoadEngine` could go unanswered. That hazard is gone.
  - `test_poison_policy_{timeout,cancel}_poisons`: the relaunch `execute` used to time out silently after 5 s, because its reply was sent before the request existed and was dropped. It now gets its result and asserts `Ok("# done")`, which takes each test from about 5 s to about 0.5 s.
- New unit test for the `auto_respond` contract.

## Testing

- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passes (17227 Rust tests).
- **The CI flake did not reproduce locally,** even on the old code: under 36 CPU hogs on 18 cores, both old and new tests passed 40/40 runs. The case for the fix rests on the code analysis above.

Plan and investigation notes: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-22-ts-engine-race-test-flake.md`.

title: Implement link-external-icon/-newwindow/-filter for HTML output (bd-t3n1nghb)
description:
Implements `link-external-icon`, `link-external-newwindow` and `link-external-filter` for HTML output (braid strand bd-t3n1nghb). Before this change q2 accepted the three options but did nothing with them.

## What it does

- **`link-external-icon: true`**: adds the class `external` to each external link. CSS then draws a box-arrow icon in the link colour after it.
- **`link-external-icon: <bootstrap-icon-name>`**: puts `<span class="bi bi-NAME quarto-ext-icon" aria-hidden="true">` right after the link. Bootstrap Icons are now shipped for the page when the icon option is a string, and on websites as before.
- **`link-external-newwindow: true`**: adds `target="_blank"`, and `rel="noopener"` when the link has no `rel`. A `target` or `rel` the author wrote is kept.
- **Which links count as external:** absolute `http(s)` or `//host` URLs that aren't localhost and don't match `link-external-filter`. Relative links, `mailto:`, other schemes and `.no-external` links are never touched.
- **`link-external-filter`:** a Rust regex. It defaults to the escaped `website.site-url`, anchored with `^`.

## Design decisions (agreed during investigation)

- **When classification happens.** A Finalization-phase AST transform (`link-external`) classifies links at render time, not with browser JS as Quarto 1 did. This keeps it open to user filters later. It runs after `llms-capture`, so llms markdown keeps clean links.
- **Scope.** Only body-AST links are adorned. Raw HTML and navigation chrome are not.
- **Formats.** It runs for every HTML-family format, revealjs and the preview included.
- **Regex dialect.** The filter uses the Rust regex dialect. An invalid pattern raises the new warning **Q-13-14** and falls back to the default filter.
- **Styling.** The `.external` icon styles (`resources/scss/html/templates/link-external.scss`) are always bundled in HTML and revealjs CSS, so a hand-written `{.external}` link works too.

## Other changes

- `pampa` meta annotations now read `link-external-filter` as a plain string. Before this, front-matter markdown parsing ate the regex's backslashes.
- New error page `docs/errors/navigation/Q-13-14.qmd` and a new user guide `docs/guides/formats/html/external-links.qmd`. The guide covers the differences from Quarto 1.
- Updated the styles.css hash in the `phase5-single-doc-baseline` fixture. The only change is the four new rules: removing them gives back the old hash.

## Tests

- 18 unit tests in `link_external.rs`.
- SCSS compile tests for the default HTML theme and the revealjs theme.
- Smoke fixtures under `crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all/link-external{,-website}/`.
- Full `cargo xtask verify`, including the hub build, passes.

- **bd-na72nf6u:** a bug already on `main`: HTML CSS contains a literal `colorToRGB(#6c757d)` in the code-tools SVG fills.
- **bd-oq6tbfr3:** in the preview, the named-icon form probably shows an empty span, because the preview iframe loads only the theme CSS. Not checked in hub-client yet.

title: Fix Windows quarto-mcp-launcher failures: test compile error and cache GC rename-lock
description:
Two Windows-only failures in quarto-mcp-launcher, fixed together: the first masked the second.

The lib test target did not compile on Windows: q2_path_injection_skips_non_utf8_exe_paths built its non-UTF-8 OsString via the unix-only OsStringExt::from_vec, so clippy --all-targets failed with E0433/E0599 and the cache_tests integration tests never ran. The helper is now a cfg pair: unix keeps from_vec(0xff, 0xfe); Windows uses OsStringExt::from_wide(&[0xD800]) (a lone surrogate — ill-formed UTF-16, so to_str() returns None), exercising the same rejection path on all three platforms.

With the target compiling, 4 of 15 cache_tests failed on Windows: corrupt_cache_dir_self_heals, gc_removes_old_unlocked_bundles, crashed_instance_releases_lock_making_bundle_collectable, launch_after_gc_re_extracts.

## Root cause

remove_bundle_dir held its exclusive probe lock — an open handle to .lock inside the bundle dir — across the trash-rename. On Windows, renaming a directory while any handle is open inside it fails with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, so GC and the corrupt-dir self-heal could never remove a bundle dir and extract_and_lock bailed after 4 retries. Unix inode semantics allow the rename regardless, which is why this only failed on Windows (no CI leg runs Windows tests).

## Fix

On non-unix, drop the probe lock before the rename. The rename then doubles as the in-use check: it succeeds only when nothing in the dir is open, and every lock-holder opens .lock inside the dir. A failed rename skips the entry, same as a lost try-lock. The unix path keeps holding the lock through the rename, the tighter race guard there.

The underlying rule (never hold a handle into a directory across fs::rename of it) is now documented in .claude/rules/cross-platform.md.

## Verification

On Windows: cargo clippy -p quarto-mcp-launcher --all-targets -- -D warnings clean; cargo nextest run -p quarto-mcp-launcher 51/51 (was: target didn't compile, then 4 failures). cargo xtask verify not run; it is red on Windows for unrelated strands.

Supersedes the separate braid/bd-j0pgiips-windows-mcp-launcher-clippy branch.

Braid: bd-j0pgiips, bd-5tdzaf3t (follow-up audit of other fs::rename sites: bd-jdsx8lwu)

title: ci: add windows-latest clippy-only leg (no tests)
description:
Windows compile breakage keeps reaching main undetected: every CI leg runs on Linux/macOS, so Unix-only APIs (`std::os::unix`, `OsStringExt::from_vec`) and asymmetric `#[cfg]` gates pass clippy there and only fail on a Windows machine. The three recent instances — the quarto-mcp-launcher non-UTF-8 test (#913), the xtask capture-\* dead code (#834), and the cache-test coverage masked by an upstream compile failure (#914) — were all compile-level failures that `clippy --all-targets` on Windows catches without running a single test.

Stacked on #913: the leg is red without that fix, so this PR targets its branch and GitHub will auto-retarget to main when #913 merges. Only the last commit is new.

Add a `windows-clippy` job to test-suite.yml running the same gate as the existing "Clippy (deny warnings)" step:

```
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --profile ci -- -D warnings
```

Compile-only (`--all-targets` still compiles test and dev-tool code, which is where these failures live), so the job skips the matrix leg's pandoc/typst/tree-sitter/node setup. Verified on a fresh Windows checkout of #913 merged into main: green, ~8 min cold.

title: q2 add: install extensions from GitHub, archive URLs, or local paths
description:
Implements `q2 add` (braid bd-rfz4e3bw), replacing the "not yet implemented" stub. Plan and decisions: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-22-q2-add-extension.md`.

## What it does

- **Sources** (Quarto 1's grammar): GitHub `org/repo[/subdir][@ref]`, an archive URL (`.zip`/`.tar.gz`), or a local folder or archive.
- **Layout**: installs to `_extensions/[<owner>/]<name>/`. The owner is the GitHub org (from shorthand or a `github.com/.../archive/...` URL).
- **Table**: Quarto 1's `Install` / `Update a -> b` / `Revert` / `No Change`, using a new `semver` workspace dependency plus a helper that parses versions as leniently as npm's `semver.coerce`.
- **Flags**: `--no-prompt`, `--trust`, `--dir`, `--dry-run`, `--json`, `--force`.

## Deliberate deviations from Quarto 1

- **Trust fails closed**, like `q2 use brand`: the prompt defaults to *no*, and a remote source is refused before any request when the command can't prompt and `--trust` is absent.
- **Install root** is the project root (cwd outside a project). `--dir` overrides it, and there is no "install into project?" question.
- **Install record**: each extension gets a `.quarto-source.yml` (with a generated-file header) recording the source and a sha256 per file. Replacing an extension whose files changed since install needs `--force`. An install with no record (from Quarto 1, or copied by hand) updates with a note.
- **No Change writes nothing.** Quarto 1 re-copies the files anyway.
- No "open docs in browser" prompt; the learn-more URL is printed instead. `--embed` is out of scope.

Updates are staged inside `_extensions/` and renamed into place. The directory being replaced is checked to be inside `_extensions/` before it is removed.

## Fixes in `quarto-source-fetch` (also affect `q2 use brand`)

Found by running `q2 add posit-dev/product-doc-theme` against real GitHub:

1. **`pax_global_header` was refused.** Every `git archive` tarball starts with one, so *no* GitHub source could be fetched. It is now skipped and still counted against the extraction limits.
2. **Any symlink refused the whole archive.** Links are still **never created**, so a later entry written through one stays inside the destination. They are now skipped, name-checked and counted, and reported via `ExtractSummary::skipped_links` / `FetchedSource::skipped_links`. `q2 add` refuses when a skipped link is inside an extension it would install. `q2 use brand` warns when one is inside the brand folder.

Smaller changes: `RemoteTarget::owner`, a public `quarto_core::extension::read_extensions_dir`, and `fetch_into` now returns a `FetchedSource`.

## Testing

- 24 unit tests (`commands::add::*`) and 18 CLI tests (`tests/integration/add.rs`). They cover every source kind, install-root selection, each table action, mtime-checked No Change, edit detection with `--force`, untracked installs, `--dry-run`, `--json`, invalid and hostile sources, both symlink cases, a trust refusal with zero requests, a localhost URL install, and an installed custom project type that renders.
- Mutation checks: disabling the edit check, the trust gate, or the replace step each turns its test red.
- `quarto-source-fetch`: regression tests for the pax header, and link tests rewritten for skip-and-report (a hostile link name is still refused).
- Manual run against GitHub: `q2 add posit-dev/product-doc-theme --trust` installs `posit-dev/posit-docs` 8.1.4. The example site renders as `type: posit-docs`, and a second add reports No Change.
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build`: 17,244 Rust tests pass. Locally, `quarto-hub-mcp` vitest hits random 5 s timeouts; all 575 pass at 30 s, and that package's WASM bundle predates this branch. Filed as bd-myls3dvu.
