title: Map Bootstrap table shorthands in caption attributes to table-* classes (bd-hfghrqvh)
description:
## Summary

Quarto 1 lets you write Bootstrap table shorthands in a table caption's attribute block, and q2 now supports the same syntax:

```markdown
| a | b |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 |

: My caption {.striped .hover}
```

Output: `<table class="table-striped table-hover caption-top table">`.

Until now q2 emitted the classes unprefixed, which does nothing for Bootstrap. For `#tbl-` labelled tables and `::: {#tbl-}` floats it did not put the classes on the `<table>` at all. Needed for Posit's product docs (`posit-dev/product-doc-theme`).

This mirrors Q1's `quarto-pre/table-classes.lua` and `quarto-post/responsive.lua`:

- **Prefixing.** All Q1 shorthands are prefixed with `table-`: `primary secondary success danger warning info light dark striped hover active bordered borderless sm responsive responsive-{sm,md,lg,xl,xxl}`. Other classes pass through verbatim.
- **`sm` / `small`.** `table-sm` brings in `small`, and `small` brings in `table-sm`.
- **Responsive wrapper.** A `.responsive*` table is wrapped in `<div class="table-responsive*">`.
- **Float classes.** A `tbl` float's classes, including user classes, are copied onto every table inside it, skipping sub-floats. The float `<div>` keeps its own unprefixed copies, as in Q1, so existing Q1 CSS keeps working.

### Implementation

- **`table-bootstrap-class`** (existing, late Finalization) now does the prefixing, the `sm`/`small` pairing and the responsive wrapper. It walks the AST with `ast_walk`, so it also reaches tables inside custom-node slots.
  - This fixes an existing q2-preview gap. The preview skips `crossref-render`, so labelled tables stay inside `FloatRefTarget` nodes, and on `main` they got **no** classes in the preview, not even `table`.
- **`table-float-class-forward`** (new) runs just before `crossref-render`. That is the last point where a float's own classes are distinct from the `quarto-float …` classes Quarto adds.
  - It copies the classes unprefixed, and `table-bootstrap-class` prefixes them later.
  - It is registered like `table-bootstrap-class`: B4 bucket, in `PANDOC_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED`, and listed in the exact-order pipeline tests.
- **pampa parser fix.** product-doc-theme writes the caption on the line right under the table, with no space after the colon: `:Caption {.striped .hover}`. Pandoc accepts that.
  - In q2, that caption goes through the "caption parsed as last row" fixup, but `process_pipe_table_cell` had already thrown the attribute block away.
  - The attribute block is now kept only in a final single-cell row starting with `:`, and lifted onto the table by a `take_caption_attr` helper. The blank-line caption path now shares that helper.
  - Ordinary cells behave as before: the attribute is still dropped and the space before it trimmed.

### Reviewed divergence

The mapping is HTML-only. Q1 does it for every format in its pre stage. Follow-up: bd-7zw93czl.

## Test plan

- [x] Smoke-all fixture `crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all/markdown/table-caption-bootstrap-classes.qmd`. It covers:
  - an unlabelled caption, a `#tbl-` caption, and the `::: {#tbl-}` div form;
  - `.small`, `.responsive-md`, and the adjacent no-space caption;
  - a multi-table float with a sub-float.

  The expected class lists are Quarto 1's output for the same source. It fails on `main`.
- [x] Unit tests in `table_bootstrap_class.rs`:
  - every shorthand, `sm`/`small`, and the responsive wrapper;
  - idempotence for both steps;
  - custom-slot reach, multi-table and sub-float forwarding, and `fig` floats left untouched.
- [x] `crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/table_bootstrap_classes_preview.rs` pins the q2-preview AST. All three tests fail against the old transform code.
- [x] pampa tests: `test_adjacent_no_space_caption_attr_merges_into_table` and `test_attr_in_ordinary_table_cell_is_still_dropped`. The full pampa suite passes, including the refactored blank-line caption path.
- [x] The product-doc-theme example's `user.html` now renders `table-striped table-hover caption-top table`, matching Q1.
- [x] `cargo xtask verify` (full, including hub build) passes locally.

## Follow-ups filed

- bd-7zw93czl: do the class mapping for all formats, as Q1 does.
- bd-44t9rqtp: labelled table captions are placed at the bottom (`quarto-float-caption-bottom`); Q1 places them at the top (`-top`).
- bd-ymyeef2e: a multi-table float drops its inner tables' own captions. The bd-4m2n6qf1 caption removal is too broad.
- bd-0vje43lp: `:NoSpace` after a blank line is not parsed as a caption at all (grammar).

title: pandoc.read: source locations that resolve into the string, and a commonmark reader (#883, #884, #885)
description:
Fixes #883, #884, #885.

`pandoc.read` from Lua (filters, `{lmd}` cells, shortcodes) now produces nodes whose source locations point into the string that was read. Previously they resolved against the document. Warnings about those nodes show the text of the string, labelled with the call site, e.g. `doc.qmd[pandoc.read, line 14]`. `pandoc.read(text, "commonmark")` is new; use it for prose that was never written as Quarto Markdown.

Each sub-task is one `--no-ff` merge on this branch, so the first-parent history reads one entry per fix.

## What changed

**#883: the CommonMark reader registers its input once.** The reader used to register the input under two FileIds, and spans used the wrong one. It now uses the single id returned by `add_file`. There is also a new `commonmark::convert(input, file_id)` for callers that mint their own id.

**#884: `pandoc.read` locations resolve into the string.**
- Each call mints a hash-based FileId from the call site, the content and a per-runtime counter, masked to 53 bits so it survives Lua integers and JS numbers. It registers the string as a virtual file labelled `{chunk}[pandoc.read, line N]`.
- `qmd::read_as_file` parses as that file, using the new `ASTContext::file_id`.
- The host registers the minted files into both source contexts after user filters, `{lmd}` execution and shortcode resolution.

**qmd reader spans honor `parent_source_info`.** About 40 span constructions in the tree-sitter conversion (emphasis, attributes, quotes, editorial marks, the task marker and others) built `Original(current_file_id(), range)` and ignored the parent. They now go through `range_to_source_info_with_context`. This also fixes reparses of config and `!md` strings, beyond `pandoc.read`.

**bd-fwswbxnl: `pandoc.read` forwards the reader's diagnostics.** Warnings from the qmd reader, and from the JSON desugaring step, used to be dropped. They now reach the render's diagnostics. On a parse error, the diagnostics are reported before the Lua error is raised.

**#885: `pandoc.read(text, "commonmark")`.**

Each of these has its own strand:
- A structured `FileOrigin` for virtual files, in place of the label, which needs a quarto-source-map release. The plan appendix outlines it for a future design session.
- `pandoc.utils.stringify(doc)` returns `""` for a `Pandoc` value.

Format extensions such as `+smart` are still accepted and ignored, uniformly across formats.

title: Preview: render the skip-to-content link in hub-client preview (bd-21n09dwj)
description:
Follow-up to #889 (bd-rbd3jq4n), which added the "Skip to main content" link to rendered HTML only. Since #889 merged, the **Hub-Client E2E smoke-all** job has failed on `main` in chromium and firefox (e.g. scheduled run 39739998088). Four skip-link fixtures assert the link with `body > a#quarto-skip-link:first-child`, and the hub preview didn't render it.

## Changes

- **Preview renders the link.** `SkipLinkSlot` (`chromeSlots.tsx`) is the first element of `PreviewDocument`, ahead of the draft banner and site header. It is absent in minimal / `theme: none` mode, as render does.
- **Label.** It comes from the `skip-to-content` term the preview AST already carries at `meta.quarto.language`, so it follows the document language. React escapes it. A new Rust test (`preview_language_terms.rs`) checks that the term is in the preview AST, in English and with `lang: fr`.
- **Anchor jumps move focus.** The preview iframes intercept `#frag` clicks and only scrolled, so a skip link would have scrolled but left the next Tab in the navbar. A new shared `jumpToAnchor` helper scrolls, then calls `focus()` on the target. That moves focus only when the target can take it (`main[tabindex="-1"]`); for headings it does nothing, so TOC and cross-reference links behave as before. All three anchor-scroll sites use the helper:
  - the q2-preview entry;
  - `MorphIframe`, the q2-html-render iframe, which already showed render's link and had the same focus bug;
  - `DoubleBufferedIframe`.
- **Fixtures.** In the preview the link sits inside React's `#root`, not directly under `body`, so the four skip-link fixtures drop `body >` and `:first-child`. Render's "first element of the body" guarantee moves into an `ensureFileRegexMatches` regex in `skip-link.qmd`, which both runners evaluate against the full render. The website fixture keeps `a#quarto-skip-link ~ header#quarto-header`, which holds in both DOMs.

The design and its decisions are in `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-22-preview-skip-link.md`.

title: pampa: write DefinitionList as the .definition-list div the qmd reader parses
description:
**Stacked on #897** (base branch is #897's). Retarget to `main` once #897 merges.

## Problem

`write_definitionlist` emitted pandoc's `Term` / `:   Def.` syntax, which q2's qmd reader does not parse. As a result, no definition list survived a qmd write:

- a flat list re-read as `Para [Str "Term"], Para [Str ":   Def."]`;
- a multi-block definition re-read as an indented-code error.

There are two user-facing consequences:

- **hub-client / block editor.** The incremental writer always fully rewrites a `DefinitionList`, so **any edit inside a definition list turned it into paragraphs**. The existing `applyNodeEdit` test missed this because it only checked that the edited text was present.
- **docx import.** A docx using pandoc's "Definition" styles imported as qmd that does not re-read. The `writer-bugs-docx` recording carried an explicit `KNOWN_UNREREADABLE` exemption for exactly this case.

## Fix

Two commits:

1. **`ecae1e1c1`: blank lines inside list items are written empty.** `BulletListContext` / `OrderedListContext` used to indent blank lines too (`"  "`). The qmd reader takes an indentation-only line as making the list tight (bd-25ezfgs8), so `* Text.` followed by a blank line and an indented code block, list, quote or div read back as `Plain`. This also affects lists that are not definition lists. One snapshot (`editorial-divs`) changes: three whitespace-only lines become empty.
2. **`175af57b5`: `DefinitionList` is written as the sugar the reader desugars.** The writer now emits a `::: {.definition-list}` div with one `*` item per term and a `-` bullet list of its definitions. It goes through `write_bulletlist`, so nesting, tables and list-table cells come for free. Two edge shapes need special handling:
   - an empty term is written as `* []`, and `transform_definition_list_div` maps that back to an empty term;
   - a term with no definitions has no div spelling, so it falls back to a plain `.definition-list` div. Its content is kept, and pandoc's markdown cannot express this shape either.

### Tight / loose

Tight/loose is not always preserved. Single-paragraph definitions separated by blank lines read back tight. That matches pandoc's own definition-list reader. I compared pandoc's `: ` syntax with q2's div syntax and found that only `Plain`/`Para` differ (in both directions); the structure is the same in every case. Every case reaches a definition-list fixpoint after one cycle, and a test pins this behavior.

## Tests

- The two `#[ignore]`d definition-list sugar round-trip tests now run, plus a new nested one.
- Incremental edits inside a flat definition list and inside a nested one.
- `qmd_writer_pandoc_shapes.rs`: exact canonical output; an 11-shape round-trip table (nested lists, code, a list inside a definition, a definition list inside a blockquote or a bullet item, …); empty term; no definitions; the loose-to-tight fixpoint; and loose bullet/ordered items for commit 1.
- `qmd-json-qmd/definition_list_*.qmd`: 7 fixtures, including the three #895 nesting shapes.
- Snapshot `qmd/definition-list-nested`.
- hub-client `applyNodeEdit.wasm.test.ts`: the rewrite must still contain `::: {.definition-list}` and no `:   ` definition line.
- quarto-core import: the `writer-bugs-docx` exemption is removed and its `expected.qmd` regenerated. The diff is only the definition list.

`cargo xtask verify` is green. One run hit the known flake bd-7kp7kjdq (`head_peek_timeout_closes`, 4.998 s against a 5 s floor); it passed 3/3 when re-run on its own.

Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-22-qmd-writer-definition-list.md`. Fixes bd-byr1oonq.

title: Websites: draft-mode (gone by default) and website.drafts — Quarto 1 parity (bd-2hy80x1j)
description:
Ports Quarto 1's website `draft-mode` option to q2, with `gone` as the default. It also adds the `drafts` / `website.drafts` list.

| `draft-mode` | the draft page | links to it |
|---|---|---|
| `gone` (default) | blank `noindex` page | removed |
| `unlinked` | rendered, with the "Draft" banner | removed |
| `visible` | rendered, with the "Draft" banner | kept |

Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-21-draft-mode-gone.md`. User docs: `docs/guides/projects/drafts.qmd`.

## Behaviour change

Before this PR, q2 rendered every draft in full and left most links to it in place. Existing q2 sites with drafts will now publish them as blank pages, with no links to them. To get the old behaviour back, set `draft-mode: unlinked` or `draft-mode: visible`. The changelog calls this out.

## Design

- **One draft policy** (`project::drafts`). `DraftView` answers every draft question, and `ProjectIndex` exposes it as `is_linkable` / `linkable_profiles`. A guard test fails if non-test code reads a profile's `.draft` / `.draft_mode` directly. This absorbs bd-zeormbsa: before, the draft check was hand-written at 5 sites and missing at 19.
- **`draft-mode` is ordinary merged metadata.** It is read in either spelling (`resolve_website_value`) from each page's merged metadata, so `_quarto.yml`, `_metadata.yml`, front matter and `-M` all work and compose normally. The resolved value is stored on `DocumentProfile.draft_mode` (profile v16). A page's own mode governs both how it renders and whether other pages may link to it. This differs from Q1, which reads one site-wide value for links but lets document metadata change the body.
- **Reading vs authoring views.** `RenderAudience`:
  - `q2 render` and publish are **reading** views; `draft-mode` applies.
  - These are **authoring** views, where drafts are always `visible`: `q2 preview --static`, both hub-client pipelines, browser export, book downloads, and the preview server's PDF/download routes.
  - The audience never enters profiles, so cached profiles serve both.
- **`gone` pages.** The draft transform clears the blocks in Normalization (engine execution still runs, for its side effects). `ApplyTemplateStage` then writes a fixed shell: charset, robots `noindex`, `quarto:status=draft-remove`. Nothing else from the page or site leaks into it. HTML only, not slides, as in Q1.
- **Unlinking.**
  - Navbar, sidebar and footer entries are pruned in the Generate transforms, so active state, prev/next and breadcrumbs never see the draft.
  - Body links are replaced by their content (closes bd-p4sc).
  - Listings and feeds skip drafts. A glob that matched only drafts no longer warns Q-12-19.
  - The sitemap omits drafts (closes bd-4zdf).
  - Search and llms go through the same policy.
- **`drafts:` globs.** Patterns are resolved relative to their declaring YAML file through the shared glob API (new `GlobOptions::DRAFTS`). A match is folded into the profile and the merged metadata. Bad entries warn as Q-5-50.
- **Websites only (D5).** In other project types, `gone` is clamped to `unlinked`: drafts keep the banner and are never blanked. Follow-up: bd-4lhtudbo.

## Deviations from Q1 / known gaps

- **Sidebar sections.** A section whose header links to a draft keeps its children and only loses the link. Q1 drops the whole section, which would also hide published pages under it.
- **Config-text links.** Markdown links inside nav config *text* (e.g. a footer `text:` with a link) are not unwrapped.
- **`metadata-files`.** Q1's `metadata-files: [drafts.yml]` route awaits bd-spb7mobo.
- **Hub smoke runner.** The hub-client WASM smoke runner now skips `render-project: true` fixtures. Those fixtures assert on a native whole-project render, which is a reading view; the hub is an authoring view.

## Tests

- `crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/website_drafts.rs` (21 tests) covers:
  - every metadata placement and the precedence between them;
  - invalid values;
  - the authoring override;
  - the blank page;
  - unlinking across every surface in all three modes;
  - `drafts:` globs, directories, and `_metadata.yml` scoping.
- Unit tests in `drafts.rs`, `index.rs`, `sidebar_auto.rs`, `navigation_drafts.rs`, `link_rewrite.rs`, `llms.rs`, `document_profile.rs` and `preview_static.rs`.
- New smoke fixture: `smoke-all/drafts-website/`.
- Full `cargo xtask verify` passes.

Closes bd-zeormbsa, bd-p4sc, bd-4zdf and bd-98lngao9. Supersedes bd-w0o9.

title: pampa: process the content of rewritten definition-list / list-table divs (#895)
description:
Fixes #895.

## Problem

`desugar_div` rewrote a `.definition-list` / `.list-table` div with `FilterResult(_, false)`. The traversal is top-down, so nothing inside the new `DefinitionList` / `Table` was ever visited. This affected both the reader's postprocess pass and `desugar_blocks` (lmd cell results, `pandoc.read(…, "json")`, `--from json`, document import). The effects were wider than the issue lists:

- nested `.definition-list` / `.list-table` divs stayed divs;
- an image paragraph in a loose definition did not become a `Figure`;
- every reader lowering was skipped inside these blocks: note references (Q-3-31 error), math attributes, editorial marks, header auto-ids, and the Q-2-50 warning;
- `* - : b` in a list-table cell **panicked** ("CaptionBlock found in filter").

## Why not `FilterResult(_, true)`

The one-line fix suggested in the issue makes the traversal re-apply the filter to the new `Table` itself. The reader's `.with_table` pipe-table caption heuristic would then run on list-tables. A single-column list-table whose last cell starts with `:` (for example `\: b`) would lose that row and gain a caption. bd-9fy9p4zl had flagged this, and I confirmed it experimentally.

## Fix

- `desugar_div` now returns a `Block`.
- Both callers return that block as `Unchanged` from a new generic `Filter::with_block` handler. The traversal therefore descends into the new block's children without re-visiting the block itself. `with_cite` and `autoid.rs` already rely on this `Unchanged` idiom.
- The rewrite still happens top-down, before the content is visited, so the definition-list shape validation sees the same input as before.

The doc comments and `dev-docs/syntax-notes.md` § Structural desugaring contract now say that the set applies inside its own output.

Behavior changes, all toward pandoc: headers inside definitions and cells now get auto ids and take part in dedup, citations inside them now count toward `note_num` numbering, and reader warnings now fire inside these blocks.

## Tests

- `desugar.rs` unit tests: nested definition-list / list-table / figure in a definition, a definition-list in a list-table cell, an invalid nested list-table warns exactly once, and idempotency on nested output.
- `tests/integration/test_rewritten_div_content.rs` (reader): the issue's repros, Q-2-50, note refs / math attrs / editorial marks, header ids, the former panic, and a regression guard for the caption heuristic.

`cargo xtask verify` passes everywhere except 3 typst smoke-all docs that fetch remote images, which failed locally only because Homebrew's pandoc is built without `+http`.

## Not in this PR

The qmd writer emits `DefinitionList` in pandoc's `Term` / `:   Def.` syntax, which q2's reader does not parse, so even a flat list does not round-trip. That is tracked separately as bd-byr1oonq and comes next.

Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-22-definition-list-rewrite-content.md`. Also closes bd-9fy9p4zl.

title: Add duplicate-seq self-heal for file documents
description:
## Summary

* Fixes a permanent sync wedge: a duplicate-seq actor collision on a file document stuck that file for the receiving browser until a manual IndexedDB wipe.
* The sync client now discards the local copy and fetches a fresh one from the hub, as the index document already did (bd-6f21d4c6).

## Changes

* `recoverFileDocument` mirrors the index recovery, plus two additions: per-document backoff (3 attempts, 30 s cooldown, 300 s quiet window) and a circuit breaker that routes the file into the unavailable-files retry poll.
* Collision routing keys on the message's document id. File change handlers are tracked by document id, so recovery can detach the old subscription directly.
* Backoff values are injectable through `ConnectOptions.recoveryBackoff`, matching the `findDocRetry` pattern.

## Tests

* New full-stack test drives a real collision through an in-process hub, red-first. New unit tests cover backoff, the circuit breaker, and routing regressions.
* 191 sync-client and 462 hub-client tests pass. `npm run build:all`, `cargo xtask lint`, and `q2 render --strict claude-notes` are clean.
* Verification stopped at the in-process full-stack test. No browser session was run (a forced shared-actor collision is not expressible through the current `SyncClient` API).

Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-22-file-doc-duplicate-seq-recovery.md`. Closes bd-0h8crv6u.

title: placeholder shortcode: rasterize PNG locally with typst instead of svg2png.deno.dev (bd-gebcr1sa)
description:
## Summary

The `{{< placeholder >}}` shortcode fetched PNGs from `svg2png.deno.dev`, which is retired and answers 404, so every PNG placeholder crashed (q2's `mediabag.fetch` returned `nil` and the Lua died concatenating it). This ports quarto-cli bc2d42e00 (quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14724): the SVG is rasterized locally with `typst compile --format png`, and any failure is a loud `fatal()`.

Two q2-specific changes to upstream's Lua:

- **Default format:** PNG only where a raster image is needed, LaTeX (`latex`, `pdf`, `beamer`) and `docx`. HTML, Typst and everything else keep SVG. Upstream defaults to PNG for every non-Typst format.
- **No typst binary** (always the case in WASM/the hub): a PNG placeholder fails right away with a clear error instead of substituting other content.

## Lua API additions (pampa)

The port needed these. They're available to filters and lmd as well as shortcodes:

- `pandoc.pipe(cmd, args, input)`: returns stdout and raises on a non-zero exit (pandoc API).
- `pandoc.system.with_temporary_directory(template, fn)`: pandoc's two-argument form; q2 only accepted three.
- Global `fatal(msg)`: raises a Lua error at the caller's line. A script's own `fatal` replaces it.
- `quarto.paths.typst()`: returns the new `LuaOptions::typst`. quarto-core fills it with `render::find_typst`, the same lookup `BinaryDependencies::discover` now uses.

## Tests

- pampa unit tests for each API addition.
- `quarto-core/tests/integration/placeholder_shortcode.rs` runs the real `placeholder.lua`: the SVG/PNG defaults by format, the error without typst, the error with a broken typst, a real PNG data URI, and upstream's contract test that the dimension label renders with typst's embedded fonts. The two tests that run typst skip when it isn't installed; CI provisions it.
- No smoke-all fixture for `format=png`. The WASM smoke-all runner renders HTML without typst, so such a fixture would fail there by design, and native `tests.run.requires` only gates on engines.

## Verification

Locally, `cargo xtask verify` (with the hub build) passes every step except `smoke_all`. Its three typst fixtures that fetch remote images (`url-image-mediabag`, `online-logo`, `crossref-grand-finale`) fail because the local Homebrew pandoc is built without HTTP support. None of them uses the placeholder.

## Follow-up

bd-1hor86xh: PNG placeholders in the hub, possibly through the runtime's existing `<canvas>` SVG rasterizer.

title: HTML: skip-to-content link for Bootstrap-themed output (bd-rbd3jq4n)
description:
Ports Quarto 1's skip-to-content link (quarto-cli 7eebb00b9, #14685; WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks) to q2's full Bootstrap HTML template.

**Stacked on #882**, which brings in the `skip-to-content` language term. This PR targets that branch; retarget it to `main` once #882 merges.

## What changes

- **Markup** (`crates/quarto-core/src/template.rs`): a new built-in `skip-link` partial is the first element of `<body>`, linking to `#quarto-document-content`. `<main>` gets `tabindex="-1"` so the link moves keyboard focus. The text comes from the `skip-to-content` language term, is HTML-escaped, and can't be set from metadata.
- **Scope:** full Bootstrap template only. `theme: none`/`pandoc`, `minimal`, and revealjs output don't get the link. Custom templates opt in with `$skip-link()$`, documented in `docs/guides/authoring/templates.qmd`.
- **SCSS:** Quarto 1's focus rule, outline suppression on the content containers, and `$zindex-skip-link`, copied unchanged.
- **Preview:** render-only for now (follow-up bd-21n09dwj). The preview's `<main>` gets `tabIndex={-1}` so the preview/render DOM comparison still matches.
- **Order:** the link comes before the color-mode script, as in Quarto 1. It's hidden by CSS from `<head>`, so it can't cause a theme flash. The FOUC test now allows exactly this one element.
- `ts-packages/quarto-api` `kLanguageDefaultsKeys`: adds `skip-to-content` and the five `navigation-*-label` keys, fixing the existing Quarto 1 parity test.
- **Deliberate divergence:** under `page-layout: custom`, q2 keeps `<main>`, so the link targets `<main>`. Quarto 1 targets `div.page-layout-custom`.

title: Vendored dependencies: checked registry, upstream survey, and /upgrade-vendored-deps skill
description:
## What this adds

PR #876 vendored a Typst package to stop a CDN flake. It also showed that the repo had no reliable record of what it vendors, and no routine way to check those assets for updates. The prose inventory from May (bd-xm7l) had drifted: it was missing 18 assets and listed one that no longer existed. This PR replaces it with a registry that CI checks, and adds a survey workflow on top.

- **`resources/vendored.toml`** registers every vendored third-party asset (55 entries). Each entry records its paths, its version, the places in the tree that must agree with that version, and what decides the version. A `policy` field says whether the asset tracks its own upstream, follows another asset (Typst packages follow quarto-cli; orange-book follows its subtree), is frozen, or is repo-native. Entries also record the upstream, guard tests, the refresh procedure, and free-form `notes` for the agent doing an upgrade.
- **A new `vendored-registry` lint rule** (in `cargo xtask lint`) checks the registry against the tree. A recorded version that disagrees with its README, constant or manifest fails. So does any file under `resources/`, `hub-client/public/` or `crates/*/vendor/` that no entry claims, and so does a subtree whose registry entry doesn't match `pull-extension-subtree`'s table.
- **`cargo xtask vendored outdated [--json]`** queries npm, Typst Universe, crates.io and git. For assets copied from quarto-cli, it reports the upstream commits that touched the specific copied paths since the pinned ref, rather than just saying that a newer tag exists.
- **A broader hermeticity test.** `test_vendored_packages_cover_every_embedded_preview_import` extends #876's orange-book test to every `@preview` import that embedded sources can emit, including the Lua filters.
- **The `/upgrade-vendored-deps` skill** surveys and files strands. It is survey-only and sits alongside `upgrade-cargo-deps`.
- **Doc updates.** AGENTS.md's External Sources Policy now points to the registry. The May inventory is retired. New provenance READMEs cover `resources/formats/` and `resources/listing/` (List.js is Quarto 1's patched build, not the npm release).

## First survey

`claude-notes/plans/2026-10-21-vendored-survey.md` filed eight strands: quarto-cli copies, pandoc 3.12.1, reveal.js 6.0.2, CDN libraries, mermaid 12, pdf.js, React and the CSL style. Bootstrap was skipped on purpose, because Quarto 1 still ships 5.3.1.

Design and decisions are in `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-21-vendored-deps-registry-and-skill.md`.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passes.
- xtask tests pass (24 vendored-specific), and clippy is clean.
- Both lint checks fail as expected on a deliberately bad version and on an unregistered file. The hermeticity test fails as expected on a deliberately bumped `@preview/fontawesome:0.5.9` import.
- The `outdated` survey runs end to end against the live upstreams.

title: Stop build scripts from forcing a q2 rebuild on every cargo invocation
description:
Fixes #870.

## Problem

Cargo treats a `cargo:rerun-if-changed` path that **does not exist** as stale on every invocation. `crates/quarto-preview/build.rs` watched `hub-client/dist-preview-embed/`. Only `cargo xtask build-hub-client-embed` creates that directory, and neither `build-all` nor `verify` runs that step. As a result, every `cargo build`/`cargo run --bin q2` recompiled `quarto-preview` and `quarto` (~16s), and `build-agents-docs` paid that cost once per example project. Cargo's fingerprint log shows the cause directly:

```
dirty: FsStatusOutdated(StaleItem(MissingFile { path: ".../hub-client/dist-preview-embed" }))
```

Five other build scripts watched possibly-missing paths the same way. `quarto-trace` hard-coded `../../.git/HEAD`, which never exists in a linked worktree, where `.git` is a file. So in `.worktrees/*`, `quarto-trace` rebuilt on every build, and `quarto-core` and everything above it rebuilt with it. I reproduced this in a scratch worktree.

## Changes

- **New `quarto-build-support` build-dependency crate**
  - `watch_path` (recursive). For a missing path it watches the nearest existing ancestor directory instead, never the missing path.
  - `watch_entry`, the non-recursive form.
  - `write_if_changed`, so a rerun that produces identical archives keeps their mtime and doesn't recompile the crate.
  - All six embedding build scripts use it, and the four copies of `watch_recursive` are gone.
- **`quarto-trace`** resolves `HEAD`/`index` with `git rev-parse --git-path`, so the watch is correct in worktrees.
- **`cargo xtask check-noop-rebuild [--profile] [--rustflags]`** fails if a second `cargo build --bin q2` compiles anything. `verify` runs it after the Rust build, and CI runs it in `test-suite.yml` (Linux, after the claude-notes render, `--profile ci --rustflags "-D warnings"`; the flags are an argument rather than env so the xtask built by "Run custom lints" is reused).
- **`stage-doc-examples` / `build-agents-docs`** build `q2` once (`util::build_q2`, which reads the executable path from cargo's JSON) and run the binary directly, instead of one nested `cargo run` per render. Both take `--release`, and `build-all --release` passes it, so the release binary is reused instead of a separate dev `q2` being built.

## Verification (local, macOS)

```
$ time cargo run --bin q2 -- --help        # 1.07s (was ~16s)
$ cargo xtask check-noop-rebuild           # failed before the fix (quarto-preview, q2); passes after
$ cargo xtask build-agents-docs            # 43.7s wall, 0 q2 compiles (24 examples + 381-page docs)
$ cargo xtask build-agents-docs --release  # reuses the release q2
$ mkdir hub-client/dist-preview-embed && cargo build --bin q2   # exactly one rerun, then a no-op
$ rmdir hub-client/dist-preview-embed && cargo build --bin q2   # exactly one rerun, then a no-op
$ q2 docs llms --embed-info                # source: real, pages: 381
```

- In a scratch worktree, a second `cargo build -p quarto-trace` is now fresh (before the fix: `MissingFile …/.git/HEAD`).
- `hub-client` `npm run build:wasm` passes. The WASM crate's separate `Cargo.lock` is updated in the second commit.
- `cargo clippy -D warnings` is clean for the touched crates. The `xtask` and `quarto-build-support` tests pass.
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passed lint, fmt, build, and the new no-op step. Its Rust test step failed locally for environmental reasons only, and a `--no-fail-fast` workspace run shows 77 failures, all from the local toolchain: `typst` is not on PATH (Q-21-1), and pandoc is 3.12.1 where the oracle/recording tests pin 3.11, which also changes the docx-reader goldens and import fixtures. None are in crates whose code this PR changes, apart from build scripts. CI's pinned toolchain is the authoritative run.

## Follow-up

bd-0pwv0mhd: in the main checkout, every commit or `git add` still rewrites `.git/index` and so rebuilds `quarto-trace` → `quarto-core` → …. The fix is to move `QUARTO_GIT_HASH` into the leaf binaries.

title: Title only the live PDF viewer frame during a recompile swap (fixes typst PDF e2e flake)
description:
## Problem

`q2-preview-spa/e2e/typst-pdf-preview.spec.ts` › "an edit recompiles the PDF" flaked on #848 (all 3 attempts):

> strict mode violation: `locator('iframe[title="PDF preview"]')` resolved to 2 elements

The two iframes are intentional. On every recompile, `@quarto/pdf-viewer` loads the new PDF into a second iframe underneath the live one. It swaps the new frame in, in a single paint, only once it has drawn a page, so the reader never sees an empty viewer (bd-c72wsugj). Both frames carried `title="PDF preview"`, so the strict locator failed whenever a poll landed in that window. The window is longer on loaded CI runners. Assistive tech also saw two "PDF preview" frames, one hidden and still loading.

## Fix

- A new viewer frame starts with no title, `aria-hidden="true"` and `inert`. When it's swapped in, it gets `title="PDF preview"` and loses the other two. Painting is unchanged: the loading frame is still laid out and drawn underneath, which the swap's readiness check needs. The file header now records that the loading frame must never be hidden with CSS.
- `embed-typst-pdf.spec.ts` drops its `.first()` workaround, since the selector now matches a single frame.

## Tests

- **Unit** (`hub-client/src/pandoc/pdfViewer.test.ts`): only the live frame is titled. The loading frame is hidden from assistive tech but not with CSS.
- **E2E repro** (`typst-pdf-preview.spec.ts`): holds the second viewer's `viewer.mjs` with `page.route`, so the swap window stays open, then reads the text layer inside it. Against a build without the fix, both this test and the existing "an edit recompiles the PDF" fail locally with the CI error.
- **With the fix:** `typst-pdf-preview.spec.ts` (chromium + firefox) and `embed-typst-pdf.spec.ts` (embed) pass 20/20, and `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passes.

title: fix(hub-client): map cursor to reveal slide from the AST, not LSP symbols

## Summary

In revealjs split view the editor cursor drives which slide the preview shows. The mapping paired `parseSlides()` output with LSP header symbols by index; a heading with no text (`##`, `## ![alt](img)`, `## {background-image=...}`) produces no symbol, so every later slide inherited the next heading's line. The preview landed one slide early and the last slide was unreachable.

title: Stop CI from masking pampa feature-gating breaks (bd-yt3x1gwk)
description:
## Problem

The v0.34.0 release failed in `web-payloads`: pampa did not compile without `lua-filter` (fixed by #862). Per-PR CI had hit the same compile error and still reported green. Two gaps let it through:

- The quarto-hub-mcp parser-tier step builds `wasm-qmd-parser`, but its vitest global setup catches every build failure and skips the tier. PR #861's log shows `Compiling pampa … [qmd-parser] unavailable … 21 skipped` on a successful step.
- The workspace build never compiles the feature sets the out-of-workspace wasm crates use (`default-features = false`).

## Changes

- **`cargo xtask check-feature-sets`** (new). It finds every manifest under `crates/` that depends on pampa with `default-features = false`, using `cargo metadata --no-deps`. Cargo resolves workspace inheritance and renamed dependencies itself, and the excluded wasm crates are found too. It then runs `cargo check -p pampa --no-default-features [--features …]` natively for each distinct set: `{}`, `{lua-filter}` and `{json-filter, lua-filter}` today. A failure names the consumers that need that set.
  - Runs in `cargo xtask verify` as part of step 3, right after the Rust build. Skip it with `--skip-feature-sets`.
  - Runs in `test-suite.yml` as *Check pampa consumer feature sets* after Clippy, with `--profile ci` and `-D warnings`.
- **`QUARTO_QMD_PARSER_REQUIRED=1`** makes a failed parser build fatal in `vitest-global-setup.mjs`, and clears any stale skip marker. CI's parser-tier step sets it. Toolchain-free legs (`workspace-ts-suites`) and local runs keep the skip, and verify does not set the variable.
- Docs: `crates/wasm-qmd-parser/AGENTS.md`, a comment on pampa's `[features]`, and `.claude/rules/xtask.md`. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-17-parser-tier-ci-masking.md`.

The two guards cover different failures. The native check catches feature-gating mistakes in seconds, with no wasm toolchain. The required parser tier catches errors in `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]` code, which a native check cannot see.

Not addressed on purpose: `--no-default-features --features terminal-support` fails. No consumer uses that combination, so it is left until one does.

## Testing

- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passes.
- New tests:
  - xtask: discovery (no-default edges, renamed and dev dependencies, feature ordering, the real repo must yield the wasm consumers' sets), the verify gate, and checks that verify and CI both wire in the step;
  - vitest: `src/vitest-global-setup.test.ts`, which covers the required and best-effort paths.
- Negative tests (local, reverted):
  - An ungated `&mlua::Error` in pampa makes `check-feature-sets` fail on the `{}` set.
  - `QUARTO_QMD_PARSER_REQUIRED=1 npx vitest run src/qmd-ast.test.ts` on a machine without wasm-pack exits 1 with the build error and writes no marker.
- **For review on this PR's CI:** the parser-tier step on both ubuntu and macOS should *run* its tests, not report them skipped, and the new Rust step should appear after Clippy.

title: lmd: project-root and extension modules, lmd: modules: autoload, quarto.include (bd-76ogq4ew, phase 3)
description:
Braid strand: bd-76ogq4ew, Phase 3 (the last) of `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-15-lmd-modules-and-qol.md`. Follows #856 (Phase 1) and #858 (Phase 2), both merged; `origin/main` is merged in (2026-10-20).

## Modules across a project

- **Project root and extension roots for `require`.** `require("/components/cards")` resolves against the project root (the leading-`/` convention `components.src` uses; the document's directory for a single-file render). `require("badges/pill")` tries `_extensions/badges/pill` for a discovered extension named `badges`, after the document-relative directories so a local directory wins; a bare `require("badges")` is the extension's `init` module. Later extensions of the same name win, matching discovery's user-over-builtin order.
- **Autoload: `lmd: modules:`** in `_quarto.yml` or the front matter lists modules to `require` before a document's first cell, each bound to a global (a string entry binds its last path segment, a one-key map binds the key). A failing or malformed entry is `Q-26-9` at the entry; a failing one leaves every cell of the page as written, so a broken prelude fails the page once. Catalog entry and reference page added.
- **`quarto.include(file, params)`** evaluates a file every time and returns its blocks: an `.lmd` or `.lua` partial runs with `params` as its vararg (`local p = ...`), its return value read under the block-cell contract with the structural desugaring set applied (new row in `dev-docs/syntax-notes.md`); a `.qmd`/`.md` partial is read as a fragment and takes no params. The path is relative to the chunk that called `quarto.include`, read off the Lua stack from `@path` chunk names, so a module's function includes beside its module; a leading `/` is the project root (an existing absolute path is read as itself). Every read goes through the `SystemRuntime` (a WASM test over the VFS and a sandbox denial test pin it). Available to cells, filters and shortcode handlers.
- **`LuaOptions`.** The Phase 1 `_with` entry points take a `pampa::lua::LuaOptions` (dialects plus `ModuleRoots`) instead of a bare dialect slice; quarto-core builds it once from `ProjectContext`.

## Found on the way

- The leading-`/` rule collided with the GH #587 contract: Quarto 1 filters `require(quarto.utils.resolve_path("_modules/x"))`, an absolute path, and the `contract-filter-require` smoke test caught it (natively, then on the hub client's VFS where `Path::is_absolute` differs). A `/`-prefixed name is now tried as a path of its own first, then as project-rooted, for `require` and `quarto.include` alike.

- The `SandboxedRuntime` policy matched un-normalized paths, so `allowed/../vendor/x` passed an allow list for `allowed/`. `SecurityPolicy` now normalizes lexically before matching (symlinks still need the filesystem). Pinned by a policy test and the include denial test.
- An extension that ships only modules could not be declared: the manifest validator requires a contribution. `contributes: modules: true` (or a list of names) now counts. Every discovered extension is addressable by name regardless; the key only lets a module-only extension exist.

## Decisions taken without asking (please confirm or overturn)

The plan left two to decide with you: the extension-root spelling (chosen: the extension's name as the first path segment, no separate declaration beyond the validator-satisfying `contributes: modules`), and whether the include workaround stays documented as the prelude mechanism (the guide now documents `lmd: modules:` as the prelude and does not mention an include-based one). Both are recorded in the plan's Phase 3 section.

## Tests

Five loader tests for the roots; autoload tests in pampa and the execute stage; seven include tests plus the WASM one; a manifest test; a sandbox traversal test; and the new `lmd-project` fixture rendered through the binary (autoloaded root and extension modules, a rooted require whose module requires its neighbour, a parameterised include and a rooted markdown include). `cargo xtask verify` green.

## Docs

"Across a project" in the lmd guide, backed by `examples/lmd/10-project`; `Q-26-9` page; the "modules resolve next to the document" limitation leaves the list.

title: fix(jupyter): run {ggsql} cells; expand {resource_dir} in kernelspec argv
description:
## Summary

`{ggsql}` code blocks never ran under `q2 render`. The Jupyter engine passed them through as literal text, because it executes only the languages named in a hard-coded list. Once that list allows `ggsql`, a second defect appears: the kernel fails to start, because q2 never expands the `{resource_dir}` placeholder in the kernelspec's `argv`. This PR fixes both. It also adds an outline for removing the language list altogether.

## The two fixes

1. **Allowlist.** `is_executable_language` (`engine/jupyter/text_execute.rs`) now includes `ggsql`. The kernel name needs no mapping: `map_language_to_kernel` already passes unknown language names through, and the ggsql kernelspec is named `ggsql`.
2. **`{resource_dir}`.** `runtimelib` substitutes only `{connection_file}` in `argv`, but the Jupyter kernelspec contract also defines `{resource_dir}` (the kernelspec's own directory). The ggsql kernelspec launches `{resource_dir}/ggsql-jupyter`, so spawning failed with `No such file or directory`. `expand_resource_dir` (`engine/jupyter/daemon.rs`) now expands it, using an absolute path. This applies to any kernel that uses the placeholder, not only ggsql.

## Known limitation

A document gets one kernel, chosen from its first executable cell. A document that mixes `{python}` and `{ggsql}` therefore sends every cell to the first cell's kernel, and the other language's cells fail. Before this PR those ggsql cells were left unexecuted (or reported as unhandled in a multi-engine document), so this is a visible change in behavior for mixed documents.

## Longer-term fix (outline only)

The language allowlist is a stopgap. The resolver already assigns `ggsql` to the Jupyter engine, but the engine never receives that assignment. It receives only the set of languages to leave alone, so it cannot tell "mine" from "owned by nobody" and falls back on its own list.

`claude-notes/plans/2026-10-17-jupyter-owned-languages-epic.md` outlines an epic that would:

- pass each engine the languages it owns (absorbing Plan 4d's `owned_languages`);
- find kernels the way Quarto 1 does, by matching the kernelspec's `language` field;
- possibly support several kernels in one document.

**The multi-kernel part is a stretch goal.** It goes beyond Quarto 1, which runs one kernel per document, and it needs further design and discussion before anyone plans it in detail. The rest of the outline stands without it. The plan records what we verified, the decisions so far, and the open questions. It is an outline for review, not a commitment to this design.

## Testing

- Unit tests: `ggsql` in `test_is_executable_language`, plus two tests for `expand_resource_dir` (substitution; other args left alone).
- `cargo clippy -p quarto-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core` passed (6300 tests) before the final review fixes; after them I re-ran only the 109 jupyter tests.
- `q2 render --strict` passes on the plan file.
- By hand, with a locally built ggsql kernel (v0.5.2): a bar chart, a scatter plot with labels, and a three-block document (create a table, query it, plot it) all render, and the session carries across blocks. Before this PR the same documents rendered the blocks as literal text.
- Not tested: a mixed python and ggsql document with this fix, and the PyPI-installed kernel.

title: docs(release-runbook): change gears on a release-blocking defect
description:
Adds a triage step to §5 of the release runbook. The v0.34.0 release was the first to hit a substantive defect (bd-yt3x1gwk), so this writes down the process we used there:

- **Flake or infra:** file a strand, re-run the failed jobs, carry on.
- **Substantive defect:** stop the release, then:
  1. Diagnose, including *why per-PR CI missed it*.
  2. File a self-contained braid strand.
  3. Work it through `/investigate-beads` and a reviewed PR.
  4. Resume the release only after a non-publishing dry run shows the failed step passes.

title: fix(pampa): pandoc.utils.stringify handles pandoc.Nodes, Citation, meta proxies (bd-lt7rgi90)
description:
Strand bd-lt7rgi90, discovered while writing the D-numtext tests on #859. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-16-stringify-nodes.md`; repro with before/after output under `claude-notes/plans/stringify-nodes-investigation/`.

## Problem

`stringify_value` dispatched on `LuaInline` and `LuaBlock` and returned `""` for every other userdata, so `pandoc.utils.stringify(pandoc.Nodes(42))` was `""`. The #859 test worked around it by wrapping the Nodes in a `pandoc.Span`. Two sibling functions had the same gap: `blocks_to_inlines` silently dropped a `Nodes`, and `LuaNodes` had no `__eq`, so `pandoc.utils.equals` on two equal Nodes was false.

## Change

- **`pandoc.utils.stringify`** takes the Lua handle and has arms for a `Nodes` (by shape, delegating to the existing inline/block walks), a `Citation` (prefix + suffix, as pandoc), a `meta` map proxy (values concatenated in key order, pandoc's MetaMap rule), config specials (their text), and `Attr` / `ListAttributes` / `quarto.config.null()` (`""`). Any other userdata is a `Q-11-3: ... expected, got <type>` error, as in pandoc. `nil` stays `""` because a missing metadata key or shortcode kwarg reads as `nil` here; registered as **D-stringify-nil** in `divergences.md`.
- **`blocks_to_inlines`** accepts a `Nodes`, alone or spliced inside the list, resolved in block context.
- **`LuaNodes`** gets a structural `__eq`; two empty Nodes are equal whatever shape they were built with.
- The userdata-naming branch of `pandoc.utils.type` moved into `userdata_type_name` so the new error names types the same way.
- The D-numtext test drops its `pandoc.Span(...)` workaround.
- `pandoc.json.encode` of a Nodes is unchanged (still null); its guard was left as is on purpose.

## Verification

- `cargo nextest run -p pampa`: 5122 passed, conformance included; clippy `-D warnings` and fmt clean.
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build`: green except `editor_ui_serves_pdfjs_from_the_viewer_bundle`, which fails identically on `main` on this machine (stale `hub-client/dist-preview-embed/` from 2026-09-17 with no pdfjs tree). CI builds the hub, so it should not reproduce here.
- Eight new tests: stringify of Nodes / Citation / Attr-ListAttributes-null-specials / rejection, `blocks_to_inlines` with Nodes, Nodes equality, meta proxy stringify.

title: feat(pampa): numbers and booleans read as text in inline positions (D-numtext, bd-q4gnd5os)
description:
## Summary

Option (a) of bd-iqd6niat (#852). #852 made the lmd inline-cell boundary accept numbers and booleans, which left one seam the lmd authoring guide had to explain in three places: a `pandoc` constructor argument still rejected them, so `pandoc.Strong(meta.version)` failed, and so did an inline cell *inside a fragment*, because the fragment emitter splices it into the `pandoc.Para(...)` call the paragraph becomes.

Now the fuzzy inline peekers (`peek_inline_fuzzy`, `peek_inlines_fuzzy`) accept a Lua number or boolean and read it as the string `tostring` would give (`lua_tolstring`, so `tostring(x)` and bare `x` agree exactly), then apply the string rule. Every inline sink inherits it: constructor content arguments, `pandoc.Inlines`, `pandoc.Nodes`, filter return values, and the lmd cell boundary, which drops its private `scalar_text` and delegates.

**Block positions stay strict**, per the decision recorded on the strand: `peek_block_fuzzy` / `peek_blocks_fuzzy` refuse a bare number or boolean before their inline fallback, so `pandoc.Div(3)` and `pandoc.Blocks({3})` error as in pandoc. Error messages keep pandoc's wording.

Registered as divergence **D-numtext** in `crates/pampa/tests/lua-conformance/divergences.md`, next to D-num. No upstream conformance case asserts the old rejection, so `xfail.txt` is unchanged.

Docs: the lmd page, `Q-26-2`, `Q-26-6`, `lua-filters.qmd`, examples 03 and 06 and the patterns fixture drop `tostring()`.

Strand: `bd-q4gnd5os`. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-16-lmd-numtext-inline-coercion.md`.

## Tests

- Peekers: alone, as list elements, floats, `1e15`, both booleans, `3.0`; block strictness (bare and as element).
- Constructors: `Strong`, `Emph`, `Span`, `Para`, mixed `Inlines`, `Nodes`, `Str`, bare-vs-`tostring` agreement; `Div`, `Blocks`, `BulletList` rejections.
- Filter returns: `Str` handler returning `12.1` (unit and integration).
- Four tests that pinned the old rejection (`pandoc.Inlines(123)`, `pandoc.Nodes(42)`, two `handle_inline_return` cases, the Q-11-4 integration test) now use functions or assert the text.

title: lmd: footnotes in fragments, quarto.markdown, call-argument fragments, escapes and levels, highlighting (bd-76ogq4ew, phase 2)
description:
Braid strand: bd-76ogq4ew, Phase 2 of `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-15-lmd-modules-and-qol.md`. **Stacked on #856** (Phase 1, reusable modules); this PR's base is that branch and it should merge after it. Phase 3 (project-level module roots, autoload, `quarto.include`) follows.

## Fragment gaps

- **Footnotes inside a fragment work.** A note defined in a `{= … =}` fragment is paired with the fragment's references when the cell is desugared and printed as an inline `pandoc.Note`; the document's footnote transforms number it with the rest. A reference whose definition is in the document body stays the reader's reference span and resolves later (that already worked); an unreferenced definition is dropped, as pandoc drops one. The pairing lives in `pampa::transforms::fragment`, together with the derived-heading-id stripping that used to be quarto-core's own copy.
- **`quarto.markdown(str)`** reads a string as Quarto markdown at run time and returns a `pandoc.Nodes`, finished the same way as a fragment, for markdown that arrives as a string (metadata, data files, listing descriptions). Blocks where blocks go, inlines where a one-paragraph string lands inline.
- **bd-onsqz7sv fixed.** The reader built a shortcode's span (and its leading `Space`'s) against the file id instead of through the parse context, so the `Q-26-2` for a shortcode inside a fragment underlined the document's front matter. Both now reroot into the fragment. Shortcodes inside fragments stay unsupported (no Lua constructor for the `Shortcode` inline; `meta.key` says it directly) and the diagnostic gains a hint with that spelling. Decision recorded in the plan.

## Grammar (tree-sitter-lmd, parser regenerated)

- **`callout{=: … :=}`**: a fragment may be a call's whole argument list, as `f{…}` and `f"…"` are in Lua (Typst's trailing content block). The desugarer parenthesizes the expansion so the result is a Lua call; `f({= a =})` is unchanged.
- **Escapes**: a backslash makes the next character content to the scanner, so `\{=` does not open a nested fragment. Quarto markdown wants a lone brace escaped anyway, so the literal delimiters are `\{=` and `=\}`.
- **Levels**: `{==: … :==}`, `{==[ … ]==}`, `{== … ==}` (and more `=`) are raw up to the closer with exactly that many `=`, like a Lua long string, for a body that quotes fragment syntax. `{==}` stays the empty level-1 fragment.

## Highlighting

`quarto-highlight` registers `lmd` from the vendored grammar's `highlights.scm` (Lua's captures, plus the fragment delimiters as `punctuation.special` and the content as `string.special`, both styled by the highlight theme), so echoed and failed cells highlight. The hub-client editor opens `.lmd` files as Lua, the explicit fallback the plan called for.

## Tests

Fragment pairing unit tests in pampa; desugarer tests for footnotes, the call form (pretty and line-preserving), escapes and levels; desugar-stage and execute-stage tests for footnotes, `quarto.markdown` and the shortcode location; 7 new grammar corpus tests; a quarto-highlight capture test; lmd snapshot fixtures (`errors.qmd` swaps the footnote case for the shortcode, `fragments.qmd` gains footnotes, `quarto.markdown`, the call form, escapes and levels). `cargo xtask verify` green.

## Docs

Guide: "A fragment as the argument", "Quoting fragment syntax", `quarto.markdown` under metadata, a footnotes rule, a delimiters rule, the highlighting note; the footnotes line leaves "Current limitations". `Q-26-2` page and catalog message updated.

title: lmd: reusable modules via require("name") of .lmd files (bd-76ogq4ew, phase 1)
description:
Braid strand: bd-76ogq4ew. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-15-lmd-modules-and-qol.md` (Phase 1 of 3; Phases 2 and 3 follow in later PRs on the same strand).

## What this adds

`require("name")` from an lmd cell, a Lua filter or a Lua shortcode handler now loads `name.lmd`: a file of Lua with lmd fragments (`{=: … :=}`, `{=[ … ]=}`, `{= … =}`), compiled with the same desugarer the cells use. This is the "reusable component" piece of the lmd design: a card, a callout, a listing layout written once and required from many documents.

```lua
-- components/cards.lmd
local M = {}
function M.card(title, body)
  return {=: ::: card
### {= title =}
{= body =}
::: :=}
end
return M
```

```{lmd}
local cards = require("components/cards")
return cards.card("Hello", {=[ from a *module* ]=})
```

## How

- **Source dialects in pampa** (`pampa::dialect::SourceDialect`): a language that compiles to Lua, registered on a Lua state through mlua app data. The scoped `require` tries each dialect's extension before `.lua`, compiles on a hit, and loads the result with an `@path` chunk name so Lua reports the module's own file and line. pampa stays independent of quarto-core: quarto-core registers `LmdDialect` through new `_with` variants of the filter, shortcode and lmd entry points (the existing entry points wrap them with no dialects, so the ~150 existing call sites are untouched).
- **`.lmd` wins over `.lua`** of the same name, with a warning naming both files. The rationale (decision 3 in the plan): a stray `.lua` beside an `.lmd` is most likely a stale compiled copy.
- **`quarto.lmd.compile(source, name?)`** exposes the compiler to Lua.
- **`Q-26-8` "lmd module did not compile"**: a module whose fragment fails to parse is reported at the `require` line of the cell, with the module path and the parse error; the cell is left as written like other lmd failures. Catalog entry, reference page and sidebar entry included. A runtime error inside a module names the module file and line in the traceback.
- **File access goes through `SystemRuntime` only.** The loader never touches `std::fs`, so it works on the hub-client VFS, and `SandboxedRuntime` now actually enforces its `SecurityPolicy` read/write lists (it was a stub). A test pins that a denying policy makes `require` fail, which is the hook for Deno-style `--allow-read` limits later.

## Tests

- 9 loader tests in `quarto_api.rs` on a toy `Shout` dialect (resolution order, dotted names, `init` modules, shadow warning, compile error typing, runtime-only reads under a sandbox policy), plus 4 registration tests.
- 5 execute-stage tests (`lmd_execute.rs`) covering a module used from a cell, runtime error attribution, `Q-26-8`, sibling requires and the shadow warning; filter and shortcode-handler tests in `quarto-core/src/lmd/dialect.rs`.
- `modules.qmd` snapshot fixture (markdown output and diagnostics) and a wasm32 test over the VFS in `pampa/tests/wasm_lua.rs` (runs in Linux CI).
- `cargo xtask verify` green after merging `origin/main` (includes #855, #852, #849).

## Docs

- "Reusable modules" section in the lmd guide, backed by `examples/lmd/09-modules`.
- `docs/errors/lmd/Q-26-8.qmd`.

## Not in this PR

Deferred to later phases per the plan: project-root and extension module roots, autoload, `quarto.include(file, params)`, the trailing content-block call form (`callout{=: :=}`), `quarto.markdown(str)`, fragment footnotes, escaping. `q2 lmd compile` (stretch) is deferred; `quarto.lmd.compile` covers the in-document need.

title: fix(pampa): default list attributes serialize as DefaultStyle/DefaultDelim (bd-3h6iasmz)
description:
## Summary

`pandoc.OrderedList(items)` with no explicit attributes carries `ListAttributes (1, Default, Default)`. Both JSON writers tagged those `{"t": "Default"}`, which pandoc rejects, so every pandoc-leg format (`--to markdown`, `docx`, `pdf`, ...) failed with `Q-20-3` on such a list while the native HTML writer rendered it fine. The native writer printed `Decimal` / `Period` for the same values, with a comment asking whether that was right.

Seven sites spelled these names by hand. `ListNumberStyle` and `ListNumberDelim` (in `quarto-pandoc-types`) now carry `pandoc_name()` / `from_pandoc_name()`, with an `ALL` constant so the inverse is derived, and the JSON writers and reader, the native writer, the Lua constructors, `show` and the lmd emitter delegate to them. The native writer now prints `DefaultStyle` / `DefaultDelim`, which is what pandoc itself prints.

The lmd authoring guide, `examples/lmd/03-lists` and the patterns fixture drop the documented workaround (`pandoc.ListAttributes(1, "Decimal", "Period")`) and its limitation bullet.

Strand: `bd-3h6iasmz` (discovered from the lmd docs work, #855). Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-16-orderedlist-default-attributes.md`.

## Tests

- `quarto-pandoc-types`: round-trip unit test for the names; `Default` (the Rust variant name) is not accepted.
- `pampa::lua::readwrite`: a bare `OrderedList` written to JSON and native carries `DefaultStyle` / `DefaultDelim`, and the JSON reads back.
- `patterns.md.snap` (quarto lmd snapshots) now renders a bare `pandoc.OrderedList` through pandoc; output unchanged.

title: q2 preview: PDF preview, format downloads and import
description:
## Summary

Until now, only quarto-hub could preview PDF output, download a document or book in other formats, and import documents. This PR ports those features to `q2 preview`, where they run on native pandoc and typst instead of the browser's WASM builds. A second change comes with the port: one resolver now chooses a document's format, so `q2 render`, `q2 preview`, the WASM entries and hub-client agree on it.

## Hub features in `q2 preview`

- **PDF preview.** Typst output opens in a bundled pdf.js viewer, both in `--static` mode and in the SPA's `PdfPane`. The viewer reloads on re-render, and a toolbar Back button returns to the previous document. Escape sequences (ANSI, OSC 8) are stripped from the pane's diagnostics.
- **Downloads in other formats.** The preview server gains `/api/preview/pdf` and a general download route. Downloads carry scope, authorship, stats and the full format table, matching what hub-client offers.
- **Book downloads.** Books download whole or as a single chapter. The server reports book stats in `X-Q2-Stats`, and the embed offers "book" and "this chapter only" entries.
- **Document import.** `POST /api/preview/import` runs native pandoc on the server, and the embed calls it instead of the in-browser path.
- **Robustness.** `child_runner::run_child` runs typst and pandoc children under a deadline and a cancellation token, so a hung child no longer blocks the server. The pandoc version is gated before spawning. Preview writes into a managed output directory that is swept at start-up, with a watcher guard so those writes don't retrigger renders.
- **Images.** Formats written outside the source tree (docx, odt, epub, pptx, typst) now resolve images relative to the source document. This fixes native render as well as preview.
- **CI and docs.** Playwright coverage for the embed (book scope, chapter-only source, standalone pages, import), a CI leg with typst and pandoc installed, and user docs for `q2 preview`.

## Consistent format resolution (bd-7jjzqeys)

Before this PR, several call sites chose a format by different rules. `q2 render` picked one before the project was loaded, so project-level defaults such as `format: typst` in `_quarto.yml` were ignored.

- **One resolver.** A single resolver in quarto-core takes the requested format, the project and the document metadata. The book orchestrator decides a book's member format once, not per chapter.
- **After the project.** `q2 render` resolves the format after the project loads. Several named files each render on their own, with their own format.
- **One layer collector.** The metadata merge stage and the output-extension lookup share one layer collector, so they can no longer disagree about which layers apply.
- **Runtime metadata (`-M`).** A `RenderOverlay` carries `-M` values through every render entry. `pass1_key` hashes it, and `PROFILE_KEY_VERSION` is bumped to 4 so cached results aren't reused across different `-M` values.
- **Book scope as metadata.** Book scope is now an ordinary metadata request (`book-scope`) that the resolver reads. `--book-scope` is removed, and the boundaries between the preview, WASM and hub-client send a generic metadata object instead of a scope field. `ResolvedBookScope::Page` is renamed `NoBook`.
- **Every surface follows it.** `q2 preview --static` and the live viewer accept `--to`, `-M` and `--profile`. The WASM entries and hub-client's preview mode follow the Rust-resolved format.
- **Docs.** New render-options, preview-flag and profile-flag pages. The earlier preview-parity plans are marked superseded.

## New diagnostics

Q-5-41 through Q-5-48 cover book-scope situations (pages outside the book, invalid values, scope on a format with no whole-book output). They come with error pages and catalog entries. Main's `website.search` codes (Q-5-38 to Q-5-40) are untouched. This branch's codes were renumbered from 38–45 to 41–48 to make room, so a few commit messages still cite the old numbers.

## Testing

Rebased onto the latest main. Local clippy and nextest runs were still in progress at push time, so CI is the first full check.

title: feat(lmd): inline cells render numbers and booleans as tostring would (bd-iqd6niat)
description:
## Summary

q2 metadata hands lmd cells real Lua numbers and booleans (divergence D-num), so `` `{lmd} meta.version` `` with `version: 12.1` failed the inline-cell contract ("evaluated to a number") and forced authors to write `tostring(meta.version)`.

- The inline-cell boundary (`classify_inline_value` in `crates/pampa/src/lua/lmd.rs`) now accepts integers, floats and booleans, alone and inside a list. A new `scalar_text` helper formats them through `lua_tolstring`, so the bare form and a hand-written `tostring()` cannot drift (`3`, `12.1`, `1e+15`, `3.0`, `true`).
- Block cells still reject numbers. Constructors inside a cell keep pandoc's strictness: `pandoc.Strong(3)` is an error in pandoc 3.11 too. Widening pampa's fuzzy inline layer is filed separately as bd-q4gnd5os, since it would be a new divergence from pandoc.

title: fix(pampa): pandoc.read from Lua no longer leaks the reader's verbose trace to stderr (bd-okfxemnj)
description:
Fixes #847

## What

Calling `pandoc.read(text, "markdown")` from an `{lmd}` cell or a Lua filter on text containing a pipe table printed one unformatted `[TOP-LEVEL MISSING NODE] Warning: Unhandled node kind: -` line per delimiter-row dash to stderr. Two independent causes, both fixed:

1. **The Lua binding pointed the reader's verbose trace at stderr.** `readers::qmd::read` takes an output stream that is a `pampa -v` trace, not a diagnostic channel; every pipeline caller sinks it. `pandoc_read` in `lua/readwrite.rs` was the only production caller passing `std::io::stderr()`. It now passes `VerboseOutput::Sink`, like `lua/config_value.rs`. This alone closes the issue.
2. **Four marker tokens had no arm in the tree-sitter dispatch.** The `-`, `pipe_table_align_left` and `pipe_table_align_right` children of `pipe_table_delimiter_cell`, and the `![` opener of `pandoc_image`, are consumed by their parent processors by node name but fell through to the catch-all, which wrote the trace line. They now get explicit arms in the existing marker-token pattern (atx markers, task-list markers, math delimiters). Behavior-preserving: the catch-all already returned the same `IntermediateUnknown`. After this `pampa -v` is quiet on well-formed input, so the catch-all means what it says.

## Tests (written first, both red on the unfixed tree)

- `crates/pampa/tests/integration/test_trace_buffer_silence.rs`: the reader's trace buffer stays empty for a pipe table (all four alignments, alignments asserted) and an inline image.
- `crates/quarto/tests/integration/pandoc_read_stderr_e2e.rs`: `q2 render` of the issue's repro leaves stderr free of the trace lines and still emits both tables.

Also checked on the unfixed tree that hyphens in text, `a - b`, link destinations and titles, autolinks, code spans, math, list markers and thematic breaks never produce a bare `-` node, so the new `-` arm only ever sees delimiter-row dashes (probe and output under `claude-notes/plans/pandoc-read-delimiter-dash-noise-investigation/`).

## Out of scope, filed as follow-ups

- bd-fwswbxnl: `pandoc.read` still discards the reader's real diagnostics (the third tuple element).
- bd-yi613i1r: make the dispatch catch-all visible to tests instead of only to `pampa -v`.

Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-15-pandoc-read-delimiter-dash-noise.md`. `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` green on the branch.

title: lmd: structural desugaring contract for AST built outside the reader (bd-7gqr148v, #846)
description:
Fixes #846. Braid strand bd-7gqr148v. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-15-lmd-ast-desugar-contract.md`.

## The problem

A `.list-table` or `.definition-list` div that an `{lmd}` cell built from nodes reached the writer as a div of nested bullet lists, because the reader's div desugar only ever ran over blocks the qmd reader produced. The fragment workaround failed from the other side: `{=: ::: {.list-table} … :=}` parses to a `Table`, and the lmd emitter had no `Table` arm.

## The contract

The reader's postprocess mixes concrete-syntax clean-up with three *structural* rewrites that an author can also produce by constructing nodes: list-table div → `Table`, definition-list div → `DefinitionList`, single-image paragraph with alt text → `Figure` (pandoc's `implicit_figures`; applied at any depth, as pandoc 3.11 and the reader both do). This PR names that set as a contract: every block list that enters the pipeline other than through the reader is rewritten by it, exactly once. It is owed to lmd cell results, lmd fragments, `pandoc.read(…, "json")`, pampa's `--from json`, and document import. It is not owed to what user Lua filters return (pandoc and Quarto 1 parity). Written up in `dev-docs/syntax-notes.md` § Structural desugaring contract.

## Changes, one commit per phase

1. **Fixture** `desugar.qmd` pinning the gap, snapshotted through the native HTML pipeline (`--to markdown` runs Quarto 1's own list-table filter and hides the bug).
2. **pampa**: new `pandoc::desugar` module (`desugar_blocks` / `desugar_inlines` / `desugar_document`) replacing `transform_divs`; the reader shares the per-node helpers so the two cannot drift; the Lua `pandoc.read(…, "json")` arm applies the set like the CLI and import paths.
3. **lmd cells**: `execute_lmd_cells` runs the set per cell over what the cell returned (block and inline cells, so a `Note`'s blocks are covered). A `Q-2-35` from a malformed cell-built list-table is relocated onto the cell's code with an info line:

   ```
   Warning: [Q-2-35] Invalid List-Table Structure
       ╭─[ desugar.qmd:94:1 ]
       │
    94 │ return pandoc.Div({ pandoc.Para({ pandoc.Str("not a list") }) }, pandoc.Attr("", {"list-table"}))
       │ ────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────
       │                                                 ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────── list-table div's last block must be a bullet list (the rows)
   ────╯
   ℹ The node was built by this lmd cell.
   ℹ Check the list-table documentation for the correct structure?
   ```

4. **Emitter**: `Block::Table` is printed as `pandoc.Table(caption, colspecs, head, bodies, foot, attr)` in both modes, so pipe tables and list-tables work inside fragments. The tests and the `errors.qmd` fixture that used a pipe table as their *unsupported* example use a footnote definition instead.
5. **Docs**: the contract in `dev-docs/syntax-notes.md`; a section in the Lua filters guide; a note on the `Q-2-35` page.

## Tests

Eight unit tests for `pandoc::desugar`, six for the execute stage, three for the emitter, JSON and `pandoc.read` round-trips, and the `desugar` fixture (13 sections: literal controls, node-built shapes, fragment tables, invalid list-table, `pandoc.read` markdown and json, a list-table inside an inline cell's `Note`, a block cell nested in a fragment). Full `cargo xtask verify` green locally.

title: chore: bump zip to 9.0.4 and install wasm-pack from prebuilt binaries
description:
## Why

On 2026-10-16 the `zip` crate maintainers yanked every published version except 9.0.3 and 9.0.4 ahead of publishing security advisories ([zip-rs/zip2#1075](https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/issues/1075)). This broke the Hub-Client E2E job on #849 (and will break every job that runs `cargo install wasm-pack`), and it also means our own `zip 6.0.0` pin is a yanked version.

Tracking issue for the wasm-pack side: #853 (upstream: [wasm-bindgen/wasm-pack#1608](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-pack/issues/1608)).

## What

**Workflows.** `build-wasm.yml`, `hub-client-e2e.yml` and `q2-preview-spa-e2e.yml` switch from `cargo install wasm-pack` to `taiki-e/install-action@wasm-pack`, matching `publish-hub-mcp.yml`, `release-pipeline.yml` and `ts-test-suite.yml`, which already used it. The prebuilt binary carries the same wasm-pack 0.15.0 code, but our CI preinstalls `wasm-bindgen-cli` and `binaryen`, so wasm-pack never exercises its archive-download path here. Details in #853.

**zip 6 → 9.0.4.** Five `Cargo.toml` files plus the lockfile. zip 9 made entry-name decoding fallible, so:

- Production call sites in `quarto-output-extract`, `quarto-source-fetch` and `xtask` map a decode failure into the crate's existing error type.
- Nine integration-test files in `quarto-core` and `quarto` unwrap the new `Result` from `file_names()` / `name()`.
- zip 9 also enforces an entry's declared size inside the reader, so an entry that lies about its size is refused before `quarto-source-fetch`'s own streaming ceiling runs. The two tests that relied on reaching that ceiling through a zip now accept either refusal, and a new unit test (`archive::tests::streaming_ceiling_caps_a_reader_that_over_delivers`) drives the ceiling directly so it keeps mutation-catching coverage.

`zip` is not in any wasm32 dependency graph, so the WASM builds are unaffected. No snapshot changes.

## Verification

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- Tests pass for `quarto-source-fetch`, `quarto-output-extract`, `xtask`, and the zip-touching `quarto` e2e tests.
- Some `quarto-core` integration tests fail on my machine with pandoc reporting "Current working directory no longer exists". They fail identically on an untouched `main` with zip 6, so that is a local environment issue; CI is the real check for those.

title: Make workspace-wide test runs a recommendation, not a pre-push gate
description:
Since we were discussing this today, why not try making the slow nextest workspace runs a recommendation locally rather than required?

We'll see if it surprises us too much in CI. I expect that Claude will still catch most dependent tests, as recommended by this PR.

## Summary

`AGENTS.md` currently requires a full workspace build, a full workspace
`nextest` run, and `cargo xtask verify` before every push, and it ends every
bug fix with another workspace run. This PR requires only the tests that cover
the change, plus scoped clippy, and moves the workspace-wide steps to a
"Recommended before pushing" list.

## Why

CI already runs workspace-wide clippy with `-D warnings` and the full test
suite on every PR (`.github/workflows/test-suite.yml`). The mandatory local
workspace run repeats that check at a cost of several minutes per push, and it
slows iteration most on small, well-scoped changes.

The recommendation stays for changes that can break dependents. A scoped test
run cannot catch a break in a downstream crate, so the new text points to
`pampa`, `quarto-core`, and `quarto-pandoc-types` as the cases where a
workspace run is worth the time.

## What changed (`AGENTS.md` only)

- **Git push policy:** the checklist now requires scoped tests and scoped
  clippy. Workspace build, workspace nextest, and `cargo xtask verify` move to
  a recommended list, with CI named as the backstop.
- **Bug-fix workflow:** step 5 (workspace run) is now "recommended". The "NOT
  sufficient" warning becomes guidance to run dependents' tests when changing
  a widely used crate. Steps 1–4 (write the test, watch it fail, fix, watch it
  pass) stay mandatory.
- **Full Project Verification:** "IMPORTANT: Before committing" becomes
  "Recommended: Before pushing".

## Not changed

- The `hub-client` rule that `npm run build:all` must succeed (a stricter
  check than `tsc --noEmit` and `vitest`).
- The end-to-end verification requirement for user-visible features.
- `cargo xtask verify` itself, and the `CONTRIBUTING.md` description of
  `cargo xtask test`.

## Trade-off

Regressions in downstream crates move from "caught before push" to "caught in
CI" when the author skips the recommended workspace run. This PR accepts that
cost in exchange for faster local iteration.

## Testing

Docs-only change; no code or tests affected.

title: provide-hub: fail fast on a non-ws(s) --server URL (bd-q96fhj3q)
description:
## What this fixes

`q2 provide-hub --server https://…` used to retry for 30 seconds and then fail with "timed out connecting to hub" or "hub connection failed (auth rejected?)". Both messages named the wrong cause. The real problem: the scheme was `https`, and only `ws://` and `wss://` work. Retrying could never help, because the URL is fixed when the dialer starts.

## The change

- `build_auth_request` now checks the scheme up front and returns a new `ProviderError::InvalidUrl`.
- The dialer maps that error (and tungstenite's connect-time URL error) to `DialError::PermanentFailure`, so samod stops retrying at once. Token fetches and network errors stay transient: a fresh token is fetched per attempt, so an auth rejection can still clear on retry.
- `join` surfaces the real cause. The error now reads: `hub connection failed: invalid websocket url: unsupported scheme 'https' (the server URL must use ws:// or wss://)`.

## Verification

- Four new dialer tests and one join test, watched failing first. One surprise along the way: tungstenite 0.27 accepts `https://` when it builds the request and only rejects the scheme at connect, so the guard covers both layers.
- `quarto-hub-provider`: 45/45 pass.
- End to end: `q2 provide-hub someDocId --file index.qmd --server https://example.test/ws --token tok` now fails in about 2 seconds with the message above. Before, it took 30 seconds and blamed a timeout.
- Full workspace suite: the only failures were ten typst book tests. Their typst package download from packages.typst.org was throttled under full test parallelism; they pass on their own and at `-j 2`. This change does not touch typst.

Closes bd-q96fhj3q.

title: Fix hub-sliding-sessions-e2e login route (bd-gppva1ee)
description:
## What this fixes

The script `scripts/hub-sliding-sessions-e2e.mjs` failed at step 1. It logged in with `POST /auth/refresh`. That route was renamed to `/auth/session` in bd-s042qcxj (PR #417), so the hub returned 404 and the script crashed.

## The change

Renames the three mentions of `/auth/refresh` to `/auth/session`: one comment, one `fetch`, one check label. Nothing else changes. The request body (`{ credential }`) and the CSRF header already match what `/auth/session` expects. The script's mock IdP is a Generic OIDC provider, so `/auth/session` is the right login endpoint.

Ran the script against the real `hub` binary, before and after:
