title: Mint one author ID for both project ID spellings (bd-evxckg64)
description:
## Summary

The hub mints each project's author ID by hashing the project ID the client sends. The same document can arrive in two spellings — bare (`abc123`) or URL form (`automerge:abc123`) — and each spelling produced a different author ID. One person could therefore appear as two different authors in the same project.

This change makes the bare document ID the canonical input:

- The hub strips a leading `automerge:` before hashing, in the one function behind both `/auth/author` and `/auth/actor`.
- hub-mcp no longer adds the prefix before fetching its author ID.
- The SPA needs no changes.

## Why bare, not prefixed

- The SPA resolves and stores the bare ID for every project it creates. Only share-joined projects use the prefixed form.
- The author ID transition's end-to-end tests pinned the bare form byte-for-byte.
- Each project's creation history is already stamped with the bare-minted ID, so this choice keeps the most-used identity in each document continuous.

Supersedes bd-9t8zsh98; the reasons are recorded on that strand (comment `c-ien0j4vg`) and in `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-15-bare-canonical-author-id.md`.

## What changes for users

- Edits from hub-mcp now carry the same author as the same person's edits in the browser.
- One-time flip: people who joined a project through a share link, and hub-mcp users, get a new author key on their next edit. Their name and color follow automatically; their past edits keep the old key.

## Deploy order

Deploy the hub before releasing q2. The hub change accepts every spelling, so old and new clients keep working. The hub-mcp change only helps once the hub strips the prefix.

## Testing

- New unit test: both spellings mint the same ID. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- New HTTP-level test through the real routes, covering both endpoints. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build`: all 14 steps green.
- hub-mcp package suite: 621 tests passed.

title: release-pipeline: fixes found by dry-running the nightly (qmd-parser stamp, bundle smoke, aarch64-musl jemalloc)
description:
Three release-pipeline bugs, each found by dry-running the nightly (`force=true publish=false`). Together they block the v0.33.0 release (bd-8sicd4ji, #837).

## 1. qmd-parser `.build-stamp` never reached downstream jobs

Dry run [38625518489](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/38625518489) on main (after #835) failed all seven bundle-building jobs at `npm run bundle` with `rebuilding qmd-parser pkg (crate sources changed)... wasm-pack build failed`. `web-payloads` builds `crates/wasm-qmd-parser/pkg-nodejs` once (#797) and writes a freshness stamp to `pkg-nodejs/.build-stamp`, but `upload-artifact` drops hidden files by default. I confirmed this by downloading the artifact. **Fix:** `include-hidden-files: true`. None of the other staged dirs contain hidden files.

## 2. Bundle smoke test imported a bare specifier

With (1) fixed, dry run [38634938445](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/38634938445) built the standalone bundle, but its `Verify bundle` step failed: `import('ts-packages/…')` is a bare specifier, so node looked for a package named `ts-packages`. **Fix:** prefix `./`.

## 3. linux_arm64: jemalloc configure can't link atomics

The same run failed `linux_arm64` building `tikv-jemalloc-sys` (`Don't have atomics implemented on this platform`; configure reported C11, `__atomic`, and `__sync` atomics all unavailable). `pagefind` (#836) depends on `tikv-jemallocator` unconditionally on 64-bit musl targets. Only its own binary uses it, and no feature turns it off. Ubuntu's aarch64 gcc defaults to `-moutline-atomics`, whose `__aarch64_*` helpers `musl-gcc` doesn't link, so configure's C-only probes fail. `linux_amd64` is unaffected. **Fix:** `CFLAGS_aarch64_unknown_linux_musl=-mno-outline-atomics` on that leg only. I couldn't reproduce this locally (no container runtime), so the dry run below is the real test.

## Verification

Dry run with all three fixes: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/38642363021

title: hub-mcp conformance test: don't leak the loopback listener's rejection
description:
Fixes a timing flake that failed the macOS test suite on #837 ([log](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/38625984640/job/116065136187)): all 101 tests passed, but vitest reported `Unhandled Rejection: test: no callback coming` at `src/conformance.test.ts:817` and failed the run.

In the BP-18 authorization-URL tests, the fake loopback listener's `result` promise rejects 10 ms after creation. When the URL is refused, which is the case under test, the handler returns without ever awaiting `result`, so that rejection has no listener. On a fast machine the test file ends first; on a slow runner the timer fires and vitest reports it.

Fix: attach a no-op `.catch` to the promise. Anything that does await it still sees the rejection. Test-only change.

Local: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vitest run src/conformance.test.ts` 51/51.

title: release-pipeline: stage the wasm-pack pkg dir, not the hub-client symlink
description:
## Problem

The [2026-10-14 nightly](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/38534285349) failed on every downstream job (`hub-mcp-bundle` plus all six build legs) at `actions/download-artifact@v8` with:

```
Unable to download artifact(s): Unable to download and extract artifact: Artifact download failed after 5 retries.
```

The `web-payloads` artifact itself was fine (40.7 MB, digest matches, downloads cleanly with `gh run download`). What broke was **extraction**, and the action's retry loop swallows the real error, so it looked like flakiness.

8fd49ad36 added `hub-client/wasm-quarto-hub-client` to the `web-payloads` upload. That path is a **committed symlink** to `crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/pkg` (gitignored wasm-pack output). The upload job had built WASM, so the glob followed the symlink and uploaded the four pkg files under the symlink's path. Every downstream job does a fresh checkout and never builds WASM, so when `download-artifact` tries to `mkdir -p hub-client/wasm-quarto-hub-client` it hits:

- Linux/macOS: a dangling symlink → `ENOENT`
- Windows: a plain text file (checkout has no `core.symlinks`) → `EEXIST`

Both reproduce locally with a two-line Node script. Each attempt failed within a second; the five 5 s retry sleeps make up the 30 s step.

## Fix

- Upload the real directory `crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/pkg` instead of the symlink path (same pattern as `crates/wasm-qmd-parser/pkg-nodejs`). On Linux/macOS the committed symlink then resolves to the extracted files.
- `build-wasm-host.mjs`'s default pkg dir moves to the same real path, so the Windows legs (and Windows dev checkouts) find the artifacts without going through the symlink-as-file.

Verified locally: `build-wasm-host.mjs` with no `--pkg-dir` builds the real (non-stub) host from the new default; `build-wasm-host.test.ts` passes; `actionlint` is clean.

## Trying it on this branch

The nightly supports `workflow_dispatch` from a branch. A dry run exercises the whole pipeline without publishing:

```
gh workflow run nightly.yml --ref fix/release-pipeline-wasm-pkg-symlink -f force=true -f publish=false
```

Note the Windows legs' `npm run bundle` step has never actually run with the WASM host requirement (the nightly never got that far), so that is the step to watch.

title: Website search: Pagefind-backed port of website.search with federated search (bd-eip0naf4)
description:
Client-side full-text search for Quarto 2 websites and books: a port of Quarto 1's `website.search` surface on a new engine, plus federated search across sites. Epic bd-eip0naf4; design and living checklist in `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-14-website-search.md`.

## What this adds

- **Engine: Pagefind 1.5.2 as a native-only Rust library.** A `SearchCaptureStage` records each rendered page's body (section ids restored onto headings so Pagefind forms per-heading sub-results); `WebsiteProjectType::post_resources` builds the chunked bundle at `site_libs/quarto-search/pagefind/`, a `manifest.json`, and a Quarto 1-shaped `search.json`. Subset renders reuse a per-page cache under `.quarto/search/`, prune pages that left, and drop stale section anchors. The browser fetches only the index chunks a query needs; nothing loads until the reader focuses the box.
- **Configuration.** `website.search` with Quarto 1's keys and the defaults its code used (`limit` 50, `collapse-after` 3), the per-page `search: false` opt-out, a new `federate:` list, and `algolia:` (incomplete blocks warn and fall back). Misconfiguration warns with Q-5-38 / Q-5-39 / Q-5-40, each with a docs page.
- **UI.** Quarto 1's `quarto-search.js` ported from Fuse.js to Pagefind (grouping by document, `collapse-after`, crumbs, keyboard shortcut, copy button, `?q=` highlighting with tabset opening), Algolia Autocomplete 1.19.1 vendored as the widget, `quarto-search.scss` as a theme layer. Navbar/sidebar placement follows Quarto 1's rules and implements sidebar search (bd-6cme); the secondary nav gets the search button.
- **Federated search.** `website.search.federate` merges other sites' Pagefind indexes after a manifest version check; results carry the source site's title. `q2 preview --static` serves the bundle with an open CORS header for cross-origin development. Example: `examples/websites/09-federated-search/`.
- **Docs:** `docs/guides/projects/website-search.qmd`.

## Verification

- 48 unit tests and 16 integration tests for search; `cargo xtask verify` (Rust side) passes: lints, clippy, fmt, workspace build with `-D warnings`, grammar tests, all 16,402 Rust tests.
- `q2-preview-spa/e2e/website-search.spec.ts` drives `q2 preview --static` on Chromium and Firefox (overlay, grouped results with highlighted excerpts, `?q=` highlighting, shortcut, sidebar textbox mode).
- Federation and the example verified in a headless browser against three sites served under one origin.
- The hub-client WASM crate builds; the preview shows no search box by design (the capture/JS stages are cfg-gated out).

## Costs and trade-offs

- `q2` binary grows by about 13.8 MB in the dev profile: pagefind embeds 33 language search runtimes and stemmers. Noted in the plan as a candidate upstream feature (embed only selected languages).
- No typo tolerance (Pagefind has prefix matching and stemming, not fuzzy matching). Quarto 1's Fuse threshold was near-exact, so the practical regression is small, and it is documented.
- The single-doc CSS baseline hash was re-captured because `quarto-search.scss` joined the built-in theme layers.

title: xtask: fix Windows clippy failure in capture-*-recordings commands (bd-lhi82470)
description:
Closes bd-lhi82470.

## Problem

On Windows, the clippy step of `cargo xtask verify` fails with dead-code and unused-import errors in `crates/xtask/src/capture_pandoc_recordings.rs` and `crates/xtask/src/capture_import_recordings.rs`, both added in #796. CI runs only on Linux and macOS, so it stays green.

Each `run()` wrapped its body in `#[cfg(unix)]`, with a `#[cfg(not(unix))]` arm that bails. On Windows the body is compiled out, so the helpers, constants and imports it uses have no caller left, and `-D warnings` turns the resulting lints into errors.

## Fix

`run()` now starts with `if !cfg!(unix) { bail!(..) }` and keeps the body as is. The body uses no Unix-only API, so it compiles on every platform, the helpers keep a caller, and the portable unit tests in both modules (`relocate`, `pretty_sorted`, `import_argv`, fixture checks) now also run on Windows. Gating the helpers with `#[cfg(unix)]` was not retained, as it would have required gating those tests too.

Both commands stay Unix-only by design: they record native pandoc runs as fixtures, which every platform reads. The fixture READMEs now say so, and `.claude/rules/cross-platform.md` documents the runtime-guard pattern next to the existing cfg-gate rule.

## Test Plan

On Windows:

- [x] `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails before the fix and passes after
- [x] `cargo nextest run -p xtask`: all tests in both capture modules pass
- [x] `cargo xtask capture-pandoc-recordings` and `cargo xtask capture-import-recordings` exit with the Unix-only error

title: components: React components bound to document elements in format: html (bd-react-components-a8flgldm)
description:
Implements S1 to S5 of `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-13-react-components.md` (strand bd-react-components-a8flgldm).

A `.qmd` document can bind a React component to a Div or Span of its HTML output. The markdown rendering stays as written and is the no-script version; a small ES-module runtime mounts the component over it in the browser. A page with no `components:` key ships nothing new.

## What is in the PR

- **S1 — static binding.** `components:` metadata (`name`, `src`, `export`, `bind: "#id"`/`.class`, `content`, `props`); the `components-resolve` transform (Finalization, HTML render only, excluded from the preview and the Pandoc cut) marks bound elements with `data-quarto-component`, ships modules under `site_libs/quarto-components/`, registers vendored React ES modules (`resources/js/react/`, built by `cargo xtask vendor-react`) and the runtime (`resources/js/quarto-components/`), and injects an import map, a manifest and the runtime's module tag into the page head.
- **S2 — element route and props.** `component=<name>` and `component-props='{…}'` on elements, `props:` in declarations, `quarto.component(name, props, content)` in Lua, and `pandoc.json.encode` of AST values and `meta` proxies, so a `type: metadata` listing can be handed to a component by an lmd cell.
- **S3 — `content: ast`.** The bound node's source-free Pandoc JSON as a child script, read by the runtime as `node`; `ts-packages/components` (`@quarto/components`) is the type-only props contract.
- **S4 — TypeScript at render time.** New crate `quarto-transpile` (oxc 0.154, no source maps so it builds for wasm32): `.tsx`/`.ts`/`.jsx` sources are transpiled and their relative imports shipped transitively. Measured: ~18 s cold debug compile for the oxc set, +5.0 MB (2.7%) on the debug binary.
- **S5 — docs.** `docs/guides/authoring/components.qmd`, nine `Q-25-*` error pages (new `components` subsystem), listings guide cross-link.

## Verification

Each spike landed as one commit with full `cargo xtask verify` green (Rust tests, WASM leg, hub-client build) and clippy clean. 60 new Rust tests (unit, Lua, on-disk transform, 10 end-to-end pins over two website fixtures) plus the jsdom check for the vendored React. The three fixtures were verified by hand in Chromium over `q2 preview --static`; an automated browser harness for rendered output is filed as bd-3swqhbsa.

## Follow-ups filed

- bd-1qtykde1: `npm:` sources through the import map and a vendoring command.
- bd-s73m7at2: the preview half (mount the same components in the q2 preview renderer), sibling of bd-j3764r9a.
- bd-3swqhbsa: Playwright smoke harness for rendered output.

title: fix(quarto-system-runtime): deflake stalled-connection timeout test under load
description:
## Summary

Deflakes `quarto-system-runtime native::tests::fetch_blocking_gives_up_on_a_stalled_connection` (bd-u6pt7ubh), which flaked twice locally in full-workspace `cargo nextest run --workspace` runs (~8s wall-clock against a 1200ms bound).

- **Root cause, confirmed empirically:** the hard wall-clock bound can't survive process descheduling. Reproduced deterministically by freezing the test process (SIGSTOP for 2s) inside the measured fetch window: 4/4 failures with the exact flake signature, while the `Network` timeout error was still delivered every time. Plain CPU oversubscription (112 spinner processes × 30 stress runs) does *not* reproduce it — the measured window is dominated by the 200ms timer sleep, which needs no CPU; the real stalls require seconds-long descheduling late in the full suite.
- **Fix:** replace the wall-clock assertion with an error-identity assertion. `fetch_blocking` now names request timeouts in its error message (`timed out after {timeout:?}`, via reqwest's `is_timeout()` — reqwest's Display only says "error sending request"), and the test asserts the client's own 200ms timeout ended the request rather than the server dropping the stream after its 1500ms silence.
- **Discriminating power preserved** (the strand's design constraint): verified by regression injection — dropping the per-request `.timeout()` makes the client wait the whole silence, produces a connection-reset (non-timeout) error, and the test fails.
- **Bonus:** the user-facing error for timed-out fetches now says it timed out.

## Verification

- TDD: new assertion red before the production change, green after
- Freeze harness: 4/4 fail before fix → 4/4 pass after
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-system-runtime`: 136/136
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build`: all steps green (change is in `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))` code — the WASM leg can't be affected)

Closes bd-u6pt7ubh.

title: Fix dialog focus timers stealing focus back (flaky new-file-dialog harness)
description:
## Problem

`e2e/new-file-dialog.harness.spec.ts › Enter on the Cancel button cancels without creating a file` failed on Firefox on `main` ([run](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/38453591835/job/115490464918)). Pressing Enter on Cancel created a file.

`NewFileDialog` focused its filename input on a 100ms `setTimeout`. When focus moved before the timer fired, the timer pulled it back to the input, so Enter submitted the form instead of cancelling. This happened when the test focused Cancel quickly under CI load, and it can happen to a fast keyboard user too.

## Fix

`NewFileDialog`, `NewFolderDialog` (100ms timer) and `SearchFilesDialog` (50ms timer) all used this pattern. All three now use `autoFocus`. `ModalDialog` already supports that: it captures its restore target during render, before `autoFocus` runs. `ImportDialog` already relies on this.

Origins:
- The `NewFileDialog` timer dates from 50a6ef1cf. The harness spec that exposed it came from #636.
- The `NewFolderDialog` and `SearchFilesDialog` timers came from #744.

## Tests

I added five jsdom tests and checked that they fail before the fix. They check that the input is focused right after opening, and that focus moved to another element is not pulled back 500ms later.
- **New File dialog:** `NewFileDialog.integration.test.tsx`
- **New Folder dialog:** new `NewFolderDialog.test.tsx`
- **Search dialog:** `FileSidebar.search.test.tsx`

Results locally:
- `npm run test`: 1610 passed
- `npm run test:integration`: 218 passed
- `tsc`: clean
- `new-file-dialog.harness.spec.ts` with `--repeat-each=20` in Firefox and Chromium: 120/120 passed
- `reduced-motion`, `baseline-a11y` and `viewport-matrix` harness specs in Firefox and Chromium: 272 passed

title: wasm-quarto-hub-client: sync Cargo.lock with quarto-node-discovery dep (bd-o2pm4nzt)
description:
## Why

`quarto-core` has depended on `quarto-node-discovery` since b889c4662 (TS engine extensions run on Node), but the wasm crate's committed `Cargo.lock` predates that change. As a result, every local WASM build (`npm run build:all` / `build:wasm`) dirtied the working tree with the missing lockfile entry.

## What

Regenerated `crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/Cargo.lock` via:

```
cargo metadata --manifest-path crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/Cargo.toml
```

The diff is exactly the 9-line `quarto-node-discovery` sync (dependency entry + package stanza); a second resolution run is a no-op. No source changes.

Closes braid strand bd-o2pm4nzt.

title: hub-mcp Phase 7: tool-surface consolidation + default project set (bd-1ilystml)
description:
## What this PR does

Phase 7 of the [elevate-quarto-hub-mcp plan](claude-notes/plans/2026-10-05-elevate-quarto-hub-mcp.md) (bd-1ilystml), stacked on #799, plus four small changes on the same branch. The production tool list goes 25 → 8 (read-only: 6): first 25 → 23 by folding tools into each other, then 23 → 8 via multi-action tools (bd-lj6f7z9s).

## Consolidation 1: fewer tools (ERG-5)

- `create_file` → `write_file` with `create_only: true`
- `list_presence` → `get_project_info` with `include: ["presence"]`
- `authenticate_status` removed — `authenticate` already reports "Already authenticated as \<email\>"
- Shared `project` parameter description cut to one line (~6 KB off the tool-list payload)

## Consolidation 2: multi-action tools, 23 → 8 (bd-lj6f7z9s)

Four tools absorb the same-subject verbs, selected by an `action` argument; `wait_for_change`, `get_errors`, `docs`, and `create_project` stay standalone. Handlers are unchanged — this is a registration/dispatch refactor.

| New tool | Absorbs | Actions |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `auth` | `authenticate`, `authenticate_clear` | `sign_in`, `clear` |
| `project` | `connect_project`, `disconnect_project`, `get_project_info`, `list_projects`, `set_default_project_set` | `connect`, `disconnect`, `info`, `list_sets`, `set_default_set` |
| `read` | `list_files`, `read_file`, `get_outline`, `search_files`, `get_file_history` | `list`, `read`, `outline`, `search`, `history` |
| `edit` | `write_file`, `patch_file`, `delete_file`, `rename_file`, `restore_file_version`, `create_folder`, `delete_folder` | `write`, `patch`, `delete`, `rename`, `restore`, `create_folder`, `delete_folder` |

- Schemas are `z.discriminatedUnion` on `action`, so per-arm required fields survive into the advertised JSON Schema, and bad calls error naming the parameter
- The read/write split is preserved: read-only mode lists 6 (no `edit`, no `create_project`); `read` keeps `readOnlyHint`, `edit` is destructive + non-idempotent
- **Breaking rename, no aliases** — the 19 absorbed names are gone; errors, instructions, prompts, and `docs/tools/q2-mcp.qmd` name the new form (`` `read` with `action: "list"` ``)
- Plan + end-to-end transcript: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-13-mcp-tool-consolidation.md`

## Other changes

- **Default project set in the OS keyring** (bd-3h5hbfdv): the first explicit `list_projects` persists its argument; bare calls use the stored default; `set_default_project_set` overrides. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-13-list-projects-default-project-set.md`
- **Actionable no-default error** (bd-dadp0lqn): tells the agent to pass a `project_set` now and that the first success stores it
- **`parseProjectRef` URL forms** (bd-lirpxs1u): accepts `#/link-project-set/` and `#/join-collection/` alongside `#/share/`
- **Author-ID parity with the SPA** (bd-9t8zsh98): MCP edits mint the same author ID as SPA edits

## Tests

TDD throughout — the wire-level suites went red before each flip. title: hub-mcp Phase 6: distribution and remote access (bd-8iv9jty5)
description:
## What this PR does

Phase 6 of the `quarto-hub-mcp` plan: distribution and remote access. It stacks on the Phase 5 branch (`bd-rpra6kpq`).

**Packaging (CAP-15).** The server now packs as a real npm package. `scripts/pack-npm.mjs` builds the bundle from a clean tree and makes a tarball with one runtime dependency. A smoke test packs the tarball, installs it into an empty prefix, and runs the installed server against the test hub. The `.mcpb` one-click bundle for Claude Desktop works the same way, with the keyring addon for all eight platforms inside. Two public manifests ship: `server.json` for the MCP Registry and `mcpb/manifest.json` for the one-click install. The install dialog shows the exact command. Secrets come from prompted user config, never from baked defaults.

**Official conformance suite.** The MCP project's conformance suite now runs as a test against a test-only HTTP listener. All 37 required scenarios pass at the frozen 2026-07-28 requirement set. The list of allowed failures is empty. The suite drives a `test_*` fixture surface that never appears in the normal tool list.

**Design docs.** The CAP-16 design doc covers hub-served MCP over HTTP: tokens, consent, scopes, and the per-user connection pool. It answers open question Q-5. A one-page note covers MCP Apps: worth doing, not yet.

**Docs.** The `q2 mcp` docs page and the README now list the three channels: `q2 mcp`, npm, and `.mcpb`.

## What this PR does not do

It does not publish anything to npm. The workflow `.github/workflows/publish-hub-mcp.yml` packs and validates on every run, but publishes only on an explicit non-dry-run dispatch. That decision stays with bd-3tak0lyy.

## Test evidence

- `npm run test -w ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp`: 62 files, 545 passed.
- `cargo xtask verify`: green, all legs.
- Conformance suite: 37 of 37 required scenarios, 146 checks, exit 0.
- Agent-task eval suite: 15 of 15 PASS. Transcripts are in the commits.

## Notes for reviewers

Two bugs were found and fixed on the way. A listener leak in the resource bridge only appears under per-request HTTP serving. A race between the packaging tests and the bundle tests rebuilt a shared file while a test ran it. Both have regression tests.

title: hub-mcp Phase 5: MCP-native surfaces (bd-rpra6kpq)
description:
Phase 5 of the hub-mcp elevation plan (bd-rpra6kpq), stacked on #797. The MCP server now speaks two more parts of the MCP protocol: resources and prompts. Design and full record: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-05-elevate-quarto-hub-mcp.md`.

## Resources (BP-5)

* Every file in a connected project is an MCP resource. The URI contract is `hub://project/<indexDocId>/<path>`, with `?server=` when a share URL routed the project to a different hub (Q-2). The document id lives in the path, because URI normalizers lowercase the host and document ids are case-sensitive.
* `resources/list` paginates with `nextCursor` (100 entries per page) and lists the files of every connected project in a stable order. `resources/read` returns text contents, or base64 blob contents for binaries.
* A client can subscribe to a file's resource. On the 2026-07-28 protocol the client opens `subscriptions/listen`. On the 2025-11-25 protocol the client sends `resources/subscribe`. Both receive `notifications/resources/updated` when the file changes, and `notifications/resources/list_changed` when files are added or removed.
* Every write result carries a `resource_link` block to the file it touched. Hosts can use the link to attach or open the file.

## Prompts (BP-6)

* `review-draft` reads one file and walks the agent through a careful review. The draft is embedded under its `hub://` URI.
* `collaborate-with-human` teaches the etiquette for editing a project a human is working in.
* `safe-edit-workflow` teaches the read → patch → confirm loop, with `expected_hash` discipline.
* `fix-render-errors` teaches the render → diagnose → patch loop. It exists only with `--allow-render`, like the `render` tool itself. Read-only mode hides the two editing prompts.

## Other changes

* The server record, the prompts, and the resource template carry the Quarto icon (BP-9). Individual tools do not: an icon on each of 24 tools adds about 15 KB to every `tools/list`.
* `prompts/list` and `resources/templates/list` carry long cache hints, because both lists are fixed at startup (BP-17). The tools and prompts capabilities now declare `listChanged: false`, matching that fact.
* The server `instructions` describe the new surfaces, and the docs page gains a Resources and prompts section.

## Verification

* `cargo xtask verify`: all legs pass. The MCP suite: 527 passed, 3 skipped.
* New tests cover both protocol eras. Legacy tests run in process. Modern tests drive a 2026-07-28 client over a real stdio server.
* One verify run caught 82 unhandled rejections from a debounce race at shutdown. The fix is pinned by a regression test.
* Agent-task evals: 15 of 15 tasks pass, median 5 turns per task, no regression.
* Real-binary end-to-end recorded in the plan for both eras: list, read, subscribe, notified write, prompt render.

title: hub-mcp Phase 4: Quarto-specific intelligence (bd-738mbhpj)
description:
Phase 4 of the hub-mcp elevation plan (bd-738mbhpj), stacked on #794. The MCP server gains Quarto-specific tools: structural qmd editing, rendering, and the embedded documentation. Design and full record: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-05-elevate-quarto-hub-mcp.md`.

## New tools

* `get_outline` returns the heading tree of a `.qmd` file with 1-based line ranges (CAP-11).
* `read_file` and `patch_file` take a `section` selector that reads or replaces exactly one section (CAP-11). A section patch touches only the section's lines, so a collaborator's edits elsewhere survive. The replaced range is exactly the range `read_file` shows, heading included. An empty `new_string` deletes the section.
* `render` materializes the project to a temporary directory and runs `q2 render --json-errors` (CAP-12). It returns structured diagnostics with `Q-` codes and source locations. It removes the directory afterwards. The tool exists only with `--allow-render`, because rendering runs project code. It never appears with `--read-only`.
* `docs` answers Quarto usage questions from the documentation embedded in the `q2` binary (CAP-13). `query` searches titles and full text. `page` returns one page's markdown. No project connection or network is needed.

## CLI additions

* `q2 docs llms --list --json` prints the page list as a JSON array (bd-b6cocsxw).
* `q2 docs llms --embed-info --json` prints the embed provenance as JSON (bd-b6cocsxw).

## Build and CI

* `wasm-qmd-parser` was broken on main for every target. It builds again, and its local C shim is replaced by the shared `wasm-c-shim` crate.
* The crate gains a `nodejs` build, staged into the MCP bundle like the keyring addon. The server and the web preview now use the same parser.
* The `q2 mcp` launcher injects `QUARTO_Q2_PATH`, so the server can find the binary for renders and docs.
* Release pipelines build the parser once and stage it on every leg. CI runs the parser test tier on the toolchain-rich job and skips it where no toolchain exists.

## Decisions worth knowing

* `clear_capture` stays human-only (Q-4). It mutates shared state that drives other collaborators' preview engines.
* The tool surface is now at the 24-tool ceiling. Phase 5 additions must displace existing tools or move to resources and prompts.

## Verification

* `cargo xtask verify`: 14 of 14 legs pass. The MCP suite: 498 passed, 3 skipped.
* Agent-task evals: 15 of 15 tasks pass, median 5 turns per task, no unintended tool errors.
* Real-binary end-to-end recorded in the plan: outline, section read and replace, docs search, and a broken-include render that returned `Q-17-2` with file, line, and column.

title: hub-mcp Phase 3: collaboration awareness (bd-3qe7unp7)
description:
## What this PR does

This PR adds the collaboration-awareness surface to the `q2 mcp` server. It is Phase 3 of the [elevate-quarto-hub-mcp plan](claude-notes/plans/2026-10-05-elevate-quarto-hub-mcp.md) (strand bd-3qe7unp7). An agent can now see who is in a project and watch the whole project for changes. It can read the history of a file and undo its own edits.

This PR is stacked on #793 (Phase 2). The diff shows only the Phase 3 work.

## New tools (3)

| Tool | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `list_presence` | Shows who is in the project and which file they edit. The server only listens. It never announces itself. |
| `get_file_history` | Lists the changes of a text file with author and time. With `from_hash`/`to_hash` it returns a unified diff between two versions. |
| `restore_file_version` | Reverts a file to a prior version. The restore is a new change on top of history, so it syncs like any edit and can be undone itself. |

## Changed tools (1)

`wait_for_change` without a `path` now watches the whole project and returns every file that a collaborator added, edited, or removed. Pass your own post-write `hash` as `since_hash`, and the watch does not report your own write back to you.

A call that carries a `progressToken` now gets progress notifications while it waits (BP-4). A client cancel frees the waiter at once on both arms (BP-3 parity).

## Decisions recorded

- **Q-3 (agent presence):** the server never announces itself. It shares the author id of the human, so an announcement would rename the identity of the human. The honest fix is a hub-minted agent author id, filed as strand bd-b2wpeud0 for design with the author-id transition owner.
- **Q-6 (agent undo):** allowed. `restore_file_version` carries `destructiveHint` and a reversible result.

## Verification

- Package tests: 420 passed, 3 skipped.
- `cargo xtask verify`: 14/14 green, with the hub-client build.
- Agent-task evals: 12/12 pass, median 5 turns (no regression from Phase 2). Two new tasks drive the new tools without naming them.
- End to end: the real `q2 mcp` binary over stdio against an in-process hub. The plan file records every new tool call and its output.
- Tool budget: 19 of 24 data tools. This matches the tally in the plan.

title: hub-mcp Phase 2: complete the file and project surface (bd-oqp2kva8)
description:
## What this does

This PR gives the Quarto Hub MCP server the full file and project surface. It is Phase 2 of the [elevation plan](claude-notes/plans/2026-10-05-elevate-quarto-hub-mcp.md) and stacks on #791.

An agent can now work with files the way a human does in the web client: read images and other binaries, add images to a project, read big files in pages, search across the project, make and delete folders, ask what a project contains, list the projects in a collection, and hand back a share link.

## What changed

- `read_file` now reads binary files. Images come back as image blocks, other binaries as embedded blobs, with `mimeType`, `size`, and `hash`. `metadata_only: true` returns just the metadata. (CAP-4)
- `write_file` and `create_file` now write binary files with `encoding: "base64"`. `expected_hash` guards binary writes too. (CAP-5; the old "binary not supported" error is gone for good, HY-1)
- `read_file` now pages big files with `offset`, `limit`, and `max_bytes` (default 64 KB). Truncated results carry `next_offset` to continue from. `list_files` shows each file's size, MIME type, and line count. (ERG-3)
- New `search_files` finds text across the project (substring or regex) with snippets and a result cap. (CAP-7)
- New `create_folder` and `delete_folder` manage folders, and `list_files` shows them. (CAP-6)
- New `get_project_info` reports a project's shape and connection health in one call: counts, contributors, engine captures, auth mode, sync diagnostics, share URL. (CAP-2)
- New `list_projects` enumerates a project collection from its share URL. (CAP-3)
- `create_project` takes a `name`, and `create_project`, `connect_project`, and `get_project_info` results now carry a `shareUrl` the agent can hand a human. (CAP-1)
- New `disconnect_project` drops one project's connection. Pending watches settle with an honest error, and the next call reconnects. (HY-5)
- New docs page `docs/tools/q2-mcp.qmd` with a Tools sidebar: setup, sign-in, the collaboration model (hashes, `synced`), the tool reference, and the trust note. (CAP-17)
- The server instructions now describe the new tools.

Sync-client additions (additive only, no behavior change): `updateBinaryFileContent`, `readProjectSetDoc`, public `getIdentitiesFromIndex`/`getCapturesFromIndex`, project-set re-exports.

Tool count: 16 of the 24-tool budget (19 with auth) — exactly the plan's tally.

## Checks

- `cargo xtask verify` green (14/14).
- `quarto-hub-mcp` tests: 376 passed + 3 skipped. `quarto-sync-client`: 180/180.
- Every new tool declares an `outputSchema` and a golden case in the conformance harness.
- Drove the real `q2 mcp` binary end-to-end over stdio; output recorded in the plan file.
- Agent eval suite: 10/10 pass, median 5 turns (Phase 1: 5.5). Two new tasks cover binary image writes and search.

One note for Phase 5: binary blob results use a `hub://<project>/<path>` URI as an ephemeral reference; Q-2 will decide the public `hub://` contract.

title: hub-mcp Phase 1: correctness + protocol hygiene (bd-zv8u2sxi)
description:
## What this does

Phase 1 of the hub-mcp elevation plan: protocol correctness and agent ergonomics, in thirteen commits. Stacked on #790 (Phase 0) — this diff shows only Phase 1's work.

**The migration (checkpoint commit):** the server moves from MCP SDK 1.x to `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.3.1, and is now **dual-era**: one process answers both the 2025-11-25 `initialize` handshake and the 2026-07-28 `server/discover` probe (via `serveStdio`). Handlers are untouched — the migration is registration-only, so a revert would be cheap. Verified through the real `q2 mcp` binary on both eras.

**Fallout the migration buys for free:** wrong-typed arguments are tool errors naming the parameter (SEP-1303); unknown tools are JSON-RPC `-32602`; `tools/list` carries `ttlMs` on the modern era; input schemas declare JSON Schema 2020-12.

**The ergonomics batch:**

- `read_file`/`write_file`/`patch_file` return a content `hash`; writes accept `expected_hash` — a stale hash is refused with the current content + hash, so an agent can't silently revert a collaborator's edit.
- Every write waits ≤ 2 s for the hub's ack and reports `synced: true|false` (`wait_for_sync: false` to opt out). New additive sync-client export `awaitDelivery`.
- `outputSchema` + `structuredContent` on all ten data tools (JSON text fallbacks retained).
- Actionable errors: parameter, state, next tool, up to three near-match paths.
- `wait_for_change` is cancellable end-to-end (no waiter leaks).
- `instructions` rewritten as the operating guide (workflow, etiquette, auth, untrusted content).
- Auth URL validated before it reaches the browser (SSRF guard); `authenticate` serialized; new `authenticate_status` tool (budget 13/24).
- Real build identity on the `Implementation` record (`0.32.0+<commit>`) plus `description`/`websiteUrl`; human titles on every tool.
- Multi-server: a share URL's `server=` routes the call to that hub — authorless, since Bearer credentials never cross origins (closes bd-qt7h8h5g).
- Startup stderr is now zero bytes (closes bd-rgt8rglx, bd-2qnnrwbd).

## Tests

Both Phase 0 red-by-construction nets (`it.fails`) flipped to green — the suite has **zero expected-fails** now. New suites cover the dual-era handshake (via the production `serveStdio` path), compare-and-swap, stalled-hub delivery, error conventions, multi-server routing with a never-replay-Bearer regression, and a golden-case-per-`outputSchema` net.

## Checks

- `cargo xtask verify`: green (14/14; one pre-existing `doc-inventory` flake, bd-c72wsugj, rerun green)
- `npm run test -w ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp`: 328 passed + 3 skipped
- `quarto-sync-client`: 167/167 (one additive export)
- `quarto-mcp-launcher`: 50/50 (version injection)
- e2e-auth: 4/4 on the real `q2 mcp` launcher channel
- Eval suite: 8/8 PASS incl. the new `stale-write-recovery` task (agent hits the designed stale-hash refusal and merges around it). Transcripts committed.

Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-05-elevate-quarto-hub-mcp.md` (Phase 1 + completion record, bd-zv8u2sxi)

title: Run TS engine extensions on Node instead of Deno
description:
## Summary

TS engine extensions now run in a **Node 24+** subprocess instead of Deno, so q2 needs one JS runtime (`q2 mcp` already requires Node 24). The engine host, `@quarto/api` and the Rust wire protocol were already runtime-neutral; this replaces the spawn layer, the host adapter, the transport and the extension build.

- **Host:** `q2` spawns `node engine-host-node.mjs --control 127.0.0.1:<port>` with a one-time token on stdin and a loopback-TCP dial-back. The bundle is `.mjs` so a project-local `"type": "commonjs"` package.json cannot change how Node parses it.
- **Node discovery:** new `quarto-node-discovery` crate (`QUARTO_NODE`, then PATH, then well-known and version-manager locations; floor Node 24), lifted from the `q2 mcp` launcher. `QUARTO_NODE` now governs engines too.
- **Extension build:** `q2 call build-ts-extension` bundles with esbuild instead of `deno bundle`. The platform esbuild binary is staged by `cargo xtask fetch-esbuild`, embedded in `q2` by the new `quarto-esbuild-embed` crate, extracted to the cache dir on first use and spawned directly from Rust (`codesign -v` check and ad-hoc re-sign on macOS). A placeholder is embedded when staging is skipped.
- **Dual runtime:** extension bundles use `node:` built-ins, so the same bundle still runs under Quarto 1's Deno 2.x.
- **Bundled engines:** marimo (fixture re-synced to quarto-marimo 0.6.0) and julia-engine (subtree, 0.3.0) are vendored from the `q2/node-port` branches of the `gordonwoodhull` forks.
- **Deno is gone** from the host, CI workflows, tests and repo root. Third-party engines that call `Deno.*` get an actionable error naming the extension and the migration guide (`docs/guides/extensions/ts-engines-node.qmd`).

## Review guide

Five commits, in order: Node host core; embedded esbuild; fixture port to `node:`; marimo fixture re-sync plus the julia-engine subtree row change; the flip (rename to `@quarto/engine-host-node`, spawn swap, CI and Deno removal, docs). The branch ends with a real `git subtree pull` of julia-engine from the fork’s `q2/node-port` (one squash plus one merge commit, split `f6d75d172`, version 0.3.0), done with `cargo xtask pull-extension-subtree julia-engine`. The plan is `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-13-ts-engines-deno-to-node.md`.

## Testing

- CI on this branch: TS Test Suite, q2-preview-spa E2E, Hub-Client E2E and Test Suite (see checks below).
- Local (macOS, after rebasing on main): clippy clean; `cargo nextest` on `quarto-core`, `quarto-node-discovery`, `quarto-mcp-launcher` 6045/6045 pass, 32 skipped. A full workspace run before the rebase had one failure, `quarto-preview asset_manifest` (untracked `q2-preview-spa/public/`), identical to baseline.
- Hard-fail gate: with `QUARTO_CI=1` a missing Node fails the Node-gated tests instead of skipping them.
- **Windows (manual, no Windows CI):** `echo_engine_e2e` 13/13, `build_ts_extension_e2e` 5/5, behave/synth/fixture-build 14/14 after the esbuild alias fix below, marimo e2e 15 tests pass with `UV_PYTHON=3.13` (`sc10` flaked once). This covers spawn, the loopback dial-back, the `readSync(0)` token read and the embedded `esbuild.exe`.
- Windows bug found and fixed here: `Path::canonicalize` yields `\\?\C:\...` paths that esbuild cannot resolve as alias targets; `strip_verbatim_prefix` now cleans every alias target.

## Known gaps

- Not tested on Windows: `.cmd` shims for `QUARTO_NODE`/`QUARTO_JULIA`, and the julia PowerShell detached start.
- Not tested: Gatekeeper behaviour of a browser-downloaded `q2` and its extracted esbuild; the release pipeline's musl/Windows esbuild verify step has not run.
- `ts_process::tests::test_single_dial_invariant` times out at its 2 s watchdog on Windows. The test and its helpers are unchanged by this branch; probably the slow refused loopback connect on Windows.
- Marimo on Windows needs a Python with a `loro` wheel; with Python 3.15 `uv` builds from source and fails.
- The extracted esbuild cache (`<cache>/quarto/esbuild/<hash>/`) is never cleaned up.
- Until the ported marimo and julia code is released upstream, users installing from marimo-team get the Deno-only shim, which fails under q2.
- Follow-ups: publish `@quarto/api`/`@quarto/types` (bd-publish-quarto-api-types-bwygrciq); which bundler to use long term (bd-which-ts-bundler-l3iebero); Q1 `AGENTS.md` build docs for julia and marimo.

title: build-ts-extension: bundle with rollup under Node instead of an embedded esbuild
description:
Stacked on #829. Review only the single commit on top of it.

## What changes

`q2 call build-ts-extension` now bundles with rollup, run under the Node 24 that TS engine extensions already require. The embedded esbuild binary, its `quarto-esbuild-embed` crate, and the xtask code that fetched it are gone. quarto-core gains no Rust dependency.

## Why

The embedded esbuild added about 10 MB to every `q2` binary and a per-platform fetch to every release. The first alternative, linking rolldown into q2, failed: it turned on serde_json's `preserve_order` and `arbitrary_precision` across the workspace, which broke 18 quarto-core tests. Running a JS bundler under Node avoids both problems, because the process boundary keeps its dependencies out of the Rust build.

## How it works

- `ts-packages/quarto-ts-bundle` builds one self-contained ESM driver (`dist/ts-bundle.mjs`, 1.3 MB, committed). `quarto-core` embeds it with `include_str!`, pipes it to `node -`, and passes the job as JSON in `Q2_TS_BUNDLE_JOB`. Nothing is extracted to disk.
- The driver uses `@rollup/wasm-node` (pure JS plus one inlined wasm file, so Windows, musl and darwin-x64 behave identically), `plugin-node-resolve` and `plugin-commonjs`. TS types are stripped with Node's own `module.stripTypeScriptTypes`, falling back to transform mode for enums and namespaces.
- The existing contract holds: the `esbuild.json` alias tiers, the `source` and `import` export conditions, `node:*` left external, and byte-stable output from any directory. An unresolved import still fails and names its specifier, so the `node:` and `--workspace` hints still apply.
- `cargo xtask build-ts-bundle` rebuilds the driver; CI gains a freshness gate for it and runs its vitest suite (9 tests). `strip_verbatim_prefix` from #829 is now applied to the alias targets sent to the driver.

## Behaviour differences from esbuild

- Builds are slower: about 0.4 s for the host entry and 0.1 s for small ones, against about 0.1 s.
- A type imported without `import type` is now an error (with a hint). `.tsx`, tsconfig `paths`, `.js`-to-`.ts` specifier rewriting and JSON imports are unsupported; no extension in the repo uses them.
- Bundles are larger because stripped types leave whitespace: julia 28.9 to 42.1 KB, marimo 21.3 to 25.5 KB. The host bundle is unchanged and stays on esbuild.

## Verification

- `clippy -D warnings` is clean on quarto-core, quarto and xtask.
- `nextest -p quarto-core -p quarto -p xtask`: 6815 run, 6815 passed, 34 skipped. The e2e tests for CJS dependencies, enums, a missing Node, cross-directory byte stability and a failing `jsr:` import skip themselves without Node 24.
- Not verified: Windows and musl (only the release-pipeline verify step covers them), and the workspace-wide run.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Rename `esbuild.json`; the format is bundler-neutral.
- The julia and marimo freshness gates pin esbuild's bytes; they need to adopt this driver or re-pin.
- Node's TS stripper is experimental, so a Node bump could change bytes and trip the freshness gates.

title: listings: publish resolved items at meta.listings.<id>, resolve before lmd-execute, type: metadata (bd-2oqen84t)
description:
Infrastructure so a listing's items can be consumed by Lua code (a user filter, or an lmd cell from #823) instead of a doctemplate. Not a replacement for custom listings. Plan with the design, decisions and findings: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-13-lmd-listings.md` (braid strand bd-2oqen84t).

One commit per spike:

- **S1** Every resolved listing is published at `meta.listings.<id>` (`project/listing/metadata.rs`) in the template binding's vocabulary and native `ConfigValue` kinds: prose as inlines, paths and literals as strings, counts as numbers, dates pre-formatted with `date-iso` alongside, lists always present. A parity test pins the metadata item keys against the binding's keys with explicit omitted / renamed / added lists.
- **S2** A `listing-resolve` stage runs before `lmd-execute` and `user-filters-pre`, sharing `resolve_listings` with the generate transform; the result rides on `StageContext` into the AST transforms, and a `listings_resolved` flag keeps the transform from resolving (and diagnosing) a second time. End-to-end tests: a Lua filter and an lmd cell both read the items.
- **S3** `type: metadata`: resolves the items, renders nothing (no container, no "No matching items" div, no List.js). Categories sidebar, feed and dependency tracking keep working.
- **S4** `fixtures/lmd-blog`: the motivating example snapshotted through the real binary (cards, grouping by year, inline count).

title: Diagnose a language word followed by `{attrs}` on a code fence (Q-2-57)
description:
A fenced code block like

````
```python {.marimo}
code
```
````

used to fail with an uncoded "Parse error … unexpected character or token here" pointing at the space after `python`. The grammar accepts either a single language word or one braced attribute list on the opening line, not both, but nothing said so. Pandoc does accept the combined form, so people write it.

It now reports `Q-2-57` ("I didn't expect this after the code block's language.") with a hint built from the author's own attribute list, in the accepted order of identifier, then classes, then key-value pairs, with the language word folded in:

```
Error: [Q-2-57] Attribute List After Code Block Language
   ╭─[ t.qmd:6:11 ]
   │
 6 │ ```python {.marimo}
   │    ───┬── ────┬────
   │       ╰────────────── This is the code block's language. The opening line takes either one language word or one attribute list in braces, not both.
   │               │
   │               ╰────── I didn't expect this after the code block's language.
───╯
ℹ Put the language inside the braces: `{.python .marimo}` for a code block, or `{python .marimo}` for an executable cell.

1 error
```

The first form is a plain code block with the language as its first class. The second is an executable cell. Both `python {…}` and `python{…}` are covered.

The hint is only offered when a braced list follows the word. `python .marimo`, a list with two identifiers, and language names with punctuation (`c++`) keep the generic error.

The suggester reuses the attribute-order machinery from Q-2-55/56 (shared classification and ordering helpers, plus a new `language-with-attributes` suggester). The error is reported over the braced list, the text that wasn't expected, rather than the single character where the parser gave up; a suggester can now return a range along with its hint. The grammar is unchanged. Adds the `Q-2-57` docs page and catalog entry.

title: lmd: a Lua+Markdown mode for Quarto 2 (exploration, spikes 1-7)
description:
## Summary

An exploration of **lmd** ("lua+md"): a JSX-like mode for Quarto 2 where filter logic lives next to the markdown it acts on, as desugaring onto ordinary qmd plus Lua. Braid strand `bd-lmd-exploration-jqv2nbl4`; the full design record, decisions, samples and open questions are in `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-12-lmd-exploration.md`.

The example the work started from now renders as written:

````qmd
---
stuff: [a, b, c, d]
---

::: foo

```{lmd}
return meta.stuff:map(function(v) return {=: **`{lmd} v`** :=} end)
```

:::
````

## What is in the branch, one commit per spike

1. **`crates/tree-sitter-lmd`**: vendored fork of `tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-lua` v0.5.0, grammar renamed `lmd`, one new rule `markdown_fragment` on external-scanner tokens. `cargo xtask ts-test lmd`.
2. **Three fragment forms**: `{=: … :=}` → `pandoc.Blocks`, `{=[ … ]=}` → `pandoc.Inlines`, unmarked `{= … =}` → `pandoc.Nodes`. The plan's "Delimiter design notes" record why `{[ … ]}` cannot work (`{[k] = t[1]}` is valid Lua) and the corpus collision counts behind the choice.
3. **Execution**: `lmd-desugar` (pre-engine) rewrites `{lmd}` cells in place; `lmd-execute` (after the engine, before user pre-filters) runs them in one Lua state per document, in document order, block and inline cells alike. Return contracts are strict and explicit; failures are located diagnostics and the cell stays displayed. `--| echo: true` keeps the desugared Lua visible.
4. **Inline cells**: `` `{lmd} expr` `` anywhere inline. A bare `` `{lmd}` `` is a mention, not a cell.
5. **`pandoc.Nodes`**: a value whose shape (blocks or inlines) is fixed at construction and whose meaning is decided where it lands, resolved in pampa's fuzzy coercion layer so it works in every constructor and filter return. Every row of the resolution table is pinned. A reader-produced paragraph stays a `Para` in block context.
6. **`heading-id` transform** (also closes **bd-2wv8431v**): heading ids are re-derived after shortcode expansion and lmd execution for any heading whose reader-derived id went stale, unique document-wide; explicit ids and filter-built ids are never renamed.
7. **`quarto.metadata.get`** (Q1 parity, numeric path segments as an extension) and a **`meta`** proxy: maps are lazy read-only proxies, arrays are real `pandoc.List`s. Tagged `Inlines`/`Blocks` lists now splice as content-list elements.
8. **Source mapping**: fragment markdown errors are underlined at their byte inside the fragment (nested parses reroot through the parent span); Lua errors name document lines natively via `@path` chunk names and line padding over a line-preserving emitter, including under includes and the engine round trip.
9. **Snapshot suite** over the real binary: four fixtures, markdown output and normalized diagnostics pinned.

## Verification

- `cargo nextest run --workspace`: 16255 passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask lint`: clean.
- `cargo xtask ts-test lmd`: 53/53; the qmd grammar is untouched.
- `q2 render --strict claude-notes`: 1463/1463 (the new stages and transform now touch every document).
- hub-client WASM build (`npm run build:wasm`) passed at spike 1; later changes are Rust-only in crates that already build for wasm32.

## Follow-ups filed

- bd-f6tt2exg: `CodeBlock.text_source` for exact anchors under blockquote/list gutters.
- bd-o7ujtnk3: project-relative chunk names (Lua abbreviates names over 60 bytes).

title: hub-mcp: agents can see render errors — local WASM validation, render-checked writes, fix_errors prompt
description:
## What

Agents using the Quarto Hub MCP server can now **see render errors and verify their own edits**:

- **`get_errors` tool** (read-only, available in `--read-only` mode): renders project documents locally using the *same `wasm-quarto-hub-client` module the browser preview runs*, hosted in the MCP's Node process, and reports structured diagnostics (kind, title, `Q-*` code, line/column, hints) for exactly the content it read — `checkedContentSha256` names the bytes. Pass `path` for one document, omit it to check every `.qmd` (capped at 25). Engine execution errors are surfaced from the existing `captures` sidecar (they happen on executors elsewhere and can't be recomputed locally).
- **Writes render-check themselves**: `write_file` / `patch_file` / `create_file` on a `.qmd` stage the new text over the project file map, render it, and append the outcome to the tool response — `Render check: clean.` or the structured error list. Error visibility is part of completing an update, not a separate call the agent must remember. A check that cannot run degrades to a pointer at `get_errors` and never fails the write. Non-`.qmd` writes are unchanged.
- **`fix_errors` MCP prompt** (surfaced as a slash command, e.g. `/mcp__quarto-hub__fix_errors` in Claude Code): one-command entry into the loop — check, read, minimal patch, repeat until clean. The prompt only instructs; the LLM does the fixing with the existing tools.

## Why this architecture

v1 of this work had the browser preview publish diagnostics into an automerge index-doc sidecar. Review guidance from @cscheid killed that approach:

> Don't try to chase synchronization with the CRDT. Just grab the content of the file/project you care about and have an API entry point to check for the validity. You're never going to be able to know if the document you just changed ends up looking exactly how you expected it to, because it's a distributed system.

v2 (this PR) makes validity a function of content: render what you hold, report what you rendered. No schema change, no new API entry point, no cross-peer choreography, hub-client untouched. (v1 is preserved on `feature/hub-mcp-get-errors` if a human-facing "see collaborators' preview state" feature is ever wanted.)

## How

- `src/local-render.ts` — lazy-loaded WASM host (server startup stays instant; the ~38 MB init is paid on first use), VFS fill with the `/project/` prefix, renders serialized via a promise chain (the VFS is instance-global), diagnostics mapped and stripped of ANSI/`$schema` noise.
- `scripts/build-wasm-host.mjs` — esbuild-bundles the wasm-bindgen JS for plain Node: aliases the Vite-root bridge imports (`/src/wasm-js-bridge/*`) to `ts-packages/wasm-js-bridge` sources, bundles dart-sass in (the embedded bundle has no `node_modules`), inits from bytes. Consumed by both the tsc dev build (`dist/`) and the embedded bundle (`dist-bundle/`, via `cargo xtask build-hub-mcp-bundle`).
- `src/prompts.ts` — prompts capability + `fix_errors`.
- `src/tools.ts` — `get_errors` handler, `renderCheckSuffix` on the write tools.

Note: the q2 binary now embeds a second copy of `wasm_quarto_hub_client_bg.wasm` (~38 MB; the preview SPA already ships one). Deduping at the launcher level is a known follow-up, deliberately not in this PR.

## Testing

- `local-render.test.ts` — real WASM, no mocks: broken YAML/markdown → structured diagnostics with line/col; sibling pass-1 attribution; binary tolerance; render serialization.
- `get-errors-handler.test.ts`, `write-render-check.test.ts` — real `registerTools` dispatch against a fake connection manager, renderer mocked at the module seam; fail-first TDD.
- `get-errors-live.test.ts` — the real server binary + in-process test hub over stdio: create broken project → `get_errors` reports Q-2-13 at 5:24 → `patch_file` (response carries `Render check: clean`) → `get_errors` immediately clean.
- `bundle.test.ts` — pins that dist-bundle ships `wasm-host.mjs` + the `.wasm`.
- End-to-end beyond CI: exercised against production quarto-hub.com through the real `q2 mcp` binary — found and fixed a real unclosed-`**` error in a live deck, then authored a full revealjs deck through the MCP with every write returning its render check inline.

Plan doc with the full verification record: `claude-notes/plans/2026-07-28-hub-mcp-get-errors-v2.md`.

title: Retry Typst Google-font fetches, check HTTP status, keep diagnostic detail in smoke-all (bd-qvl8t3hy)
description:
Closes bd-qvl8t3hy. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-10-typst-google-font-flake.md`.

## Problem

`cargo xtask verify` runs smoke-all with network access, and the Typst Google-font fixtures occasionally failed with Q-21-4 ("Failed to download Google font") on a transient fetch error. Two things made this worse than a flake:

- The native `fetch_url` never checked the HTTP status, so a 503 from `fonts.googleapis.com` came back as a successful fetch of an HTML error page, and it had no request timeout at all.
- The test harness collapsed each `DiagnosticMessage` to its title, so the failure log never said which URL or which error was involved.

## Changes

**`quarto-core` / `typst_google_fonts.rs`** — the CSS request and each font-file download go through a three-attempt schedule (250 ms, then 1 s). The sleep is injected via `RetrySchedule`, so unit tests run without waiting and the wasm32 build never references a blocking sleep. Q-21-4 now reports the final error and the attempt count.

**`quarto-system-runtime` / `native.rs`** — one shared `reqwest::blocking::Client` with a 30 s request timeout. A non-2xx status is now `RuntimeError::Network("HTTP <status> for <url>")`; transport failures use the `Network` variant too. The native `fetch_url_hardened` override enforces its policy timeout, which the trait default never did. Loopback tests cover a 200, a 503, and a stalled connection.

**`quarto-test`** — render diagnostics become harness log messages carrying the full plain-text rendering (title, problem, hints) via one shared helper for both render paths. Multi-line messages are indented under their level prefix in assertion failures. `printsMessage` regexes are unanchored, so existing fixtures are unaffected.

**`quarto-error-catalog`** — the Q-21-4 entry describes the retry, timeout, and error-status cases.

## Behavior change for Lua filters

`pandoc.mediabag.fetch` (and anything else going through `fetch_url`) on a URL that answers 404 or 503 now returns `nil` with a stderr line, instead of handing the HTML error page back as content. This is intentional (design decision 2 in the plan).

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` green at 8f25d1331 (14 steps, 16102 tests, including smoke_all with network).
- WASM build via `npm run build:wasm` green, no new warnings.
- No fixture edits; the five Google-font fixtures stay under the default `noErrorsOrWarnings` assertion.

## Follow-up

bd-f48l642w tracks caching the Google Fonts CSS response so it is not refetched on every render.

title: Hub: unix domain socket transport for the trusted-proxy shape
description:
`q2 hub` can now listen on a unix domain socket instead of a TCP port, on Linux and macOS:

```bash
q2 hub --socket-path
```

A hub running this way binds no TCP port at all. Access is enforced by the kernel: the socket is `0600` in a `0700` directory, and the hub checks the connecting process's uid on every connection. The intended use is the classic app-server deployment — a same-host reverse proxy (e.g. nginx) terminates TLS and forwards to the socket. `--socket-group` and `--socket-allow-uid` let the proxy's user connect.

Other things worth knowing:

* The default TCP+WebSocket mode is unchanged; the socket mode is opt-in per invocation, never both at once.
* Browsers and `q2 mcp` cannot dial a unix socket, so they reach the hub through the proxy instead.
* Peering stays on TCP+WS: `--peer unix:///…` fails with a clear warning rather than retrying forever.
* A stale socket file from a crash is reclaimed on restart; a live hub on the same path fails loudly instead of being clobbered.
* Very long paths fall back to a short hashed path under `$TMPDIR`, recorded in a `hub.sock.path` pointer file.
* `--socket-path` cannot be combined with `--oidc-client-id`; a hub that needs OIDC stays on TCP behind its proxy.

Docs: `docs/guides/hub/unix-socket.qmd`. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-06-hub-unix-domain-socket-transport.md`.

Verification: full workspace test suite passes (the only 2 failures reproduce on pristine `main` and are tracked in bd-nn2fou8h); `cargo xtask verify` green; new CI leg runs the cross-uid accept test under sudo on ubuntu.

title: Fix the October flaky tests: sync delivery waits, PDF viewer swap invariant, typing hook, menu focus (bd-c72wsugj)
description:
Closes bd-c72wsugj (and its duplicates bd-fuw5gcni, bd-5sbguner, bd-tg3vnfxg, already closed in braid). Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-10-flaky-ci-tests-pass.md`.

## What was flaking

- **`doc-inventory.test.ts`** (local `cargo xtask verify`, filed four times): a flush race in the test helper. automerge-repo sends local changes through a 100 ms per-doc throttle; `createNewProject` awaits a SHA-256 between creating the text and the binary file, so under load the index doc's first flush carries only `main.qmd`. The helper's `hubHasDoc` presence check is satisfied by that partial index, and the creator then disconnects without draining. Reproduced 5 of 5 by delaying the digest.
- **`pandoc-pdf-viewer` "the preview pane"** (WebKit, the red check on #816 and two `main` runs): the swap gate accepted pdf.js's first draw at the default zoom, which happens before `setInitialView` applies the saved zoom and page and resets every page. Under load that draw finishes first, the new frame is promoted, and then empties itself. Both CI snapshots (page 7 selected at 150%, page 1 the only page with content; or all pages empty) are this.
- **`pandoc-warm` typing hook** (WebKit): the hook slept one debounce after the last edit and checked for runs; the viewer iframe booting pdf.js on the same thread delayed the debounce past it.
- **`projects-home-dialogs`** (Chromium): the New menu's placeholder item is replaced when the WASM registry answers; the focused placeholder unmounts, focus falls to `<body>`, and Enter goes nowhere. The spec had only ever exercised the placeholder.

## Changes

**quarto-sync-client.** `TestHub.hubHasHeads` / `hubHasHeadsOf` check that the hub holds every change up to the client's heads (by change hash). Every project-creating test helper waits on that before the creator disconnects. `project-creation-delivery.test.ts` forces the slow-digest schedule; reverting the helpers to `hubHasDoc` fails it deterministically. The hub-client E2E project factory drains its disconnect and its "flush synchronously" comment is corrected.

**PDF viewer.** The promotion gate is now: pages loaded, initial view set, current page's view FINISHED, re-checked on `documentinit` and every `pagerendered`. The 5 s promote-anyway timeout is gone (decided: the frame on top is never an empty viewer); pdf.js's `documenterror`, or 30 s without a paint, make the swap fail and keep the previous document. `PdfPreviewPane` shows a failed swap in the same banner a failed compile gets, and its "a PDF is on screen" flag flips when the viewer has drawn rather than at hand-off. Unit tests drive a fake `PDFViewerApplication` through both draw orders, a document error, and the watchdog.

**Typing hook.** `typing()` waits for a run start after the last edit and for every run to end, instead of sleeping.

**Menu.** `Menu` keeps keyboard focus when the focused item is replaced (tracked by the root's focus events, refocused in a layout effect). The dialogs spec waits for the real menu and drives Templates → Default. The five pre-existing `react-hooks/refs` lint errors in `Menu.tsx` are fixed.

**Docs.** `.claude/rules/hub-client-tests.md` gains a "presence is not delivery" section and two Playwright bullets, and now also covers the sync-client and hub-mcp tests. Audit findings for the rest of the October harness batch are filed on bd-ag1q1eho.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build`: all steps pass.
- quarto-sync-client: the touched suites plus `exit-drain` (26 tests) pass.
- hub-client unit: `pdfViewer` (6), `PdfPreviewPane` (9), `Menu.submenu` (8), `ProjectsHome.newMenu` (4) pass; ESLint clean on touched files.
- Harness, local, `--retries=0 --workers=1`: dialogs 8 of 8 under CPU load (a first version of the Menu fix failed 3 of 3 there, which is how the event-based version came about), typing hook 3 of 3 under load, viewer 6 of 6 at normal load and under load.
- Honest gap: the old viewer gate's failure did not reproduce locally under CPU load or Chromium CPU throttling; that fix rests on the pdf.js source, the CI snapshots, and the unit test. CI on this PR is the real check.

title: Listings: gate grid/default item templates on fields: (bd-p80b9jy9)
description:
Fixes bd-p80b9jy9.

## Problem

The built-in `item-grid` and `item-default` listing templates checked the effective field set only for categories. Image, title, subtitle, description, author, date and reading time rendered whenever the item had a value, whatever `fields:` said. A grid with `fields: [date, title, description]` still drew an image placeholder on every card. On the claude-notes plans page that meant 1053 empty grey bars.

## Change

- **Templates.** Every block in both item templates is wrapped in `$if(show.<field>)$`, as Quarto 1's `fields.includes(...)` / `showField(...)` checks do. The image block, including the placeholder branch, sits under `show.image`. The default field sets already contain `image`, so listings without `fields:` render as before.
- **`type: custom` without `fields:`** now gets every field at least one item carries (`binding.rs` `fields_items_carry`), matching Q1's `defaultFields(Custom, itemFields)`. Before, custom listings had an empty field set, so with gating a custom template wrapping `$items:item-default()$` would render empty cards.
- **Docs.** `docs/guides/projects/listings.qmd` gets a "Fields" section, and its `show.<field>` entry is updated.

## Tests

- `listing_render.rs`: `grid_and_default_render_only_explicit_fields` (red before the template change) and `grid_and_default_render_every_field_by_default`.
- `binding.rs`: `custom_listing_without_fields_uses_fields_items_carry`.
- `custom_template_sees_listing_fields_and_per_item_show` now sets `fields_explicit`, as config parsing does when `fields:` is written.
- Repro project and before/after/Q1 comparison: `claude-notes/plans/listing-fields-gating-investigation/`. The `fields:`-narrowed listings match Quarto 1 exactly.
- `cargo xtask verify` (including the hub build) passes locally.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- bd-n7g28c3o: q2's default field sets for grid/default differ from Q1's (subtitle, categories, reading-time, filename, file-modified). This now decides what default cards show.
- bd-x7c196m3: the rest of Q1's card structure (empty card-body omission, filename/file-modified footer, other-fields table, author/date justification).
- bd-9q7w7xhq: enforce `field-required:`.
- bd-f9unh898 (P4): warn when every card in a listing is an empty placeholder.

The description-precedence work (bd-listing-description-precedence-x4bh6w3m) edits the description and image blocks of the same two templates, so whichever lands second will hit a mechanical conflict.

Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-09-listing-fields-gating.md`

title: Listings: derive descriptions and images only when nothing is authored
description: Fixes two listing bugs that came from the same missing rule: derive a description or image only when the author didn't write one. - **bd-listing-description-precedence-x4bh6w3m**: default and grid listings replaced an explicit `description:` with the page's first paragraph. - **bd-listing-default-no-derived-desc-m0wrr8ty**: pages *without* a `description:` got no description at all. So q2 did the reverse of Quarto 1. It hit the claude-notes plans page: switched to `type: grid`, all ~1050 cards showed a body excerpt instead of the curated description. ## Behaviour For an item backed by a project document: ``` description: listing-item.description → description → abstract → first paragraph of the rendered page image: listing-item.image → image → the rendered page's preview image ``` Authored values are shown as written. This now holds in default, grid **and table** listings, and for records laid over a document. `listing-item:` (q2-only) still wins over the top-level keys. Against Quarto 1, the repro (`claude-notes/plans/listing-description-precedence-investigation/`) matches in all three layouts, apart from that intended `listing-item:` case. ## How - **Derived values travel separately.** `ListingItemInfoStage` writes the body-derived description and image to a typed side-channel (`DocumentAst::derived_listing` → `DocumentProfile::derived_listing`), always, instead of filling `meta.listing-item`. Authored and derived values can no longer be confused. The derived ones stay available for other consumers, such as a future search feature. `DocumentProfile` also gains `abstract`. Profile version 14 → 15. - **Items record where their values came from.** `ListingItem` gets `description_source` / `image_source` (`FieldSource`). The post-render (L7) placeholders are emitted only for derived or absent values. Templates show the description block when L7 may still derive one, and the table description cell gets the placeholder too. - **One shared head pipeline.** Pass‑1 used to hand-list its pre-checkpoint stages and had drifted: it lacked `LanguageResolveStage`, `IncludeResolveStage` and `ListingItemInfoStage`, so listing autofill never reached listings. Now `pipeline::build_head_stages()` is the only list; the full HTML pipeline extends it and Pass‑1 runs it. An integration test checks that Pass‑1 and full-pipeline profiles are equal. - **Pass‑1 cache key.** It now includes the source modification date the autofill records as `date-modified`. `PROFILE_KEY_VERSION` 2 → 3. ## Other visible changes - The grid keeps the description link when L7 substitutes a derived description. Before, substitution dropped the link. - L7 keeps a derived `` ahead of the listing's `image-placeholder` default. - Q‑12‑13 now fires only when there was a non-empty fallback; a page with no prose at all is silent, as in Quarto 1. - The llms.txt companion of a listing page shows derived descriptions, matching the HTML listing. - The derived description and image no longer leak into every document's pandoc metadata as `listing-item.description` / `image`. Two goldens were regenerated for this; the audited diff is only those keys. ## Tests - New: `tests/integration/listing_description_precedence.rs` (precedence in all three layouts, rendered-only derivation, image precedence, Pass‑1 == full profile), plus unit tests for hydration, binding gating, the table cell, L7 fallbacks and the cache key. - Rewritten because they asserted the old behaviour (an explicit `description:` being replaced): two tests in `website_post_render.rs`, two in `listing_pipeline.rs`, one in `listing_render.rs`. Two book tests in `pandoc_request_projects.rs` had passed only by finding "First chapter" in the leaked metadata string; they now use single-word markers. - Local: full `cargo xtask verify` (with hub build) is green. ## Docs Listings guide (new "Where descriptions and images come from"), listing-templates envelope section, Q‑12‑13 page and catalog message, `document-profile-contract.md`, `ejs-listing-port` skill. title: claude-notes: plans listing page, and title/date/description/status/braid front matter on every plan (bd-fvcip3t5)
description:
Adds a listing page for claude-notes plans and backfills the metadata it needs (braid: bd-fvcip3t5, child of epic bd-uk8zgkha). Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-09-plans-listing-page.md`.

## What changes

- **`claude-notes/plans/index.md`** is a table listing of every top-level plan (date, title, description, newest first), and the navbar gets a "Plans" link. It uses the table layout for now. Default and grid listings of this size depended on bd-mlmkev01 (#810), and titles with code spans depended on bd-8a9eum6p (#812). Both are merged.
- **Front matter on all ~1050 top-level plans:**
  - `title:` comes from the leading H1, which is removed so the title isn't shown twice. `date:` comes from the filename, or from git for undated files.
  - `description:` is one sentence written by Haiku.
  - `status:` is the plan's own claim, in a small vocabulary (`draft`, `approved`, `in-progress`, `blocked`, `done`, `superseded`, `abandoned`). The original Status text is kept as a YAML comment.
  - `braid:` holds `strand` (a bare id, for later lookup in the skein), plus `priority` and `labels` taken from the skein.
  - `date-modified:` comes from Updated lines.
- **`scripts/claude-notes-plan-frontmatter.py`** does all the file writing. Haiku only returned data (workflows ramped 10, 50, ~200, then the rest). The script checks the data before writing anything:
  - the status is in the vocabulary;
  - the strand id exists exactly in `braid list --all --json`;
  - dates are ISO;
  - the source lines appear verbatim;
  - no continuation line is left dangling.

  Moves are lossless. Multi-line entries stay in the body, and extra text goes into comments. Anything that fails a check stays in the body: for example `kyoto-*` ids that braid doesn't know, and `**Issue:**` lines that state a problem rather than an id.
- **Templates and docs:** the investigate-beads plan skeleton, the cargo-upgrade survey template and `claude-notes/instructions/writing-notes.md` now require this front matter.

Strands filed along the way: bd-mlmkev01 and bd-8a9eum6p (both fixed and merged), bd-pnajor0b (listing titles should fall back to the first H1, as in Quarto 1). I also added a comment on bd-2nb6i1qv about gaps in the listings guide.

## Testing

- `q2 render --strict claude-notes` with q2 built from `origin/main` @ `88549eed9`: 1457 / 1457 files, no diagnostics. The plans table has 1053 rows and no empty cells.
- I checked each stage mechanically: the diff contains only the intended front matter additions and header-line removals, plus a continuation audit. I also spot-checked descriptions and status mappings against the plans.
- The changes are in notes, scripts and skills only; `crates/` and `.github/` are identical to `origin/main`.

title: CI: run the claude-notes render step with the same RUSTFLAGS as nextest (bd-7v3trpxn)
description:
Follow-up to #809. Its first CI run showed the "Render claude-notes" step taking 12 minutes, not seconds: it recompiled all 836 crates before rendering, because the nextest step sets `RUSTFLAGS: "-D warnings"` and the render step did not, and RUSTFLAGS is part of cargo's fingerprint, so nothing in `target/ci` was reusable.

Reproduced from a clean `target/ci`: build with `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings"`, 826 crates; `cargo run` without it, 826 again; `cargo run` with it, 2. This PR sets the same env on the step, with a comment saying why, and records the episode in the epic plan.

The residual 2 are `quarto-preview` and the `quarto` bin: the `quarto-preview` build script names `hub-client/dist-preview-embed` in `rerun-if-changed`, and cargo treats a missing path as always changed, so those two rebuild on every cargo invocation without the embed (~19 s locally). Pre-existing and independent of the gate; filed as bd-9ccy9ktr. After this merges the step should read as that relink plus a two-second render.

`actionlint` shows only the pre-existing shellcheck infos; the plan renders clean under `--strict`.
