title: Listings: keep item title/subtitle/description markup through the re-parse (bd-8a9eum6p)
description:
Fixes bd-8a9eum6p. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-09-listing-title-reparse.md`

## Problem

A listing item's `title`, `subtitle` and `description` were flattened to plain text in the `DocumentProfile`. That text was then interpolated into the generated listing markdown, which is parsed again. This caused three failures:

- All formatting was lost: `` Plan for `q2 preview` and *emph* `` became plain text.
- Plain text with markdown meaning (`_scope`) broke the re-parse, and the **whole listing** was skipped with only a warning.
- Code-span text such as `<anonymous>` was re-read as a raw HTML element, so it disappeared in the browser.

## Fix

- **Profile v14.** Prose fields on `DocumentProfile` and `ListingItemInfo` become `Option<Inlines>`. Plain-text consumers (sort, filter, feed, sidebar, navigation, llms, book) use the same projection as before via `title_text()` and similar accessors, so their output is unchanged.
- **Binding writes markdown.** `ListingItem` prose is now `Inlines`, and the binding writes it with `write_inlines_fragment`. Before writing, links and notes are stripped (`strip_links_and_notes`, shared with the TOC) and line breaks become spaces, so ATX headings and table cells stay on one line. A `|` inside a code span stays inside its table cell.
- **`-html` twins.** New `title-html` / `subtitle-html` / `description-html` bindings serve custom templates that write prose inside raw HTML. They follow the existing `image-html` / `category-html` keys.
- **Multi-paragraph prose.** A description written as several blocks used to be dropped without a warning. It is now joined into one paragraph and warns with the new **Q-12-26**. The warning is reported at listing time, so it also appears when the profile is cached. Inline records get the same warning with a source location.
- **Truncation.** `max-description-length` now cuts the inline tree. On text without formatting the cut is identical to before.
- **Q-12-10 as an error.** A *failed* listing re-parse (listing skipped) is now an error. A re-parse that succeeds with diagnostics stays a warning.
- **Small shared moves.** `split_string_to_inlines` moves to `quarto-pandoc-types`, `inlines_to_plain_text` is now public, and `blocks_to_inlines_with_sep` is added.

## Testing

- New `tests/integration/listing_title_markup.rs` covers default, grid and table layouts, inline records, Q-12-26 (with and without a location) and Q-12-10 as an error. New unit tests cover round trips, truncation, flattening and warning precedence.
- `cargo xtask verify` passes locally.
- A simulation over all 1,044 real plan titles in one table listing passes `q2 render --strict` with no diagnostics.

## Merge ordering

**Land bd-mlmkev01 (the nesting-limit fix) first or alongside.** With Q-12-10 failures now errors, default and grid listings with 90 or more items would otherwise fail the render instead of silently disappearing.

Known, separate: bd-listing-description-precedence-x4bh6w3m (an explicit description is still replaced by the derived one in the default and grid layouts).

title: Listings: default/grid items render as siblings, not nested (bd-mlmkev01)
description:
Fixes bd-mlmkev01: `type: default` listings with ~90+ items (grid: ~89+) were dropped with a Q-12-10 warning ("too deeply nested (more than 99 levels)").

## Cause

`listing-default.template` and `listing-grid.template` applied their item partial with `$items:item-x()$`. doctemplate strips a partial's final newline (Pandoc semantics), so each item's closing `:::` was glued onto the next item's opening fence, forming `:::::: {.quarto-post …}`, a single opening fence. Every item nested one level deeper than the previous one. `listing-table.template` hit the same issue earlier and was fixed with `$for(items)$` in d31c4b62c.

## Changes

- Default and grid wrappers iterate with `$for(items)$ … $it:item-x()$ … $endfor$`.
- New integration tests in `listing_pipeline.rs`: item divs are siblings (3 items), and all 120 items render, for both default and grid. Both failed before the fix.
- Docs: a warning callout in `docs/guides/projects/listing-templates.qmd` against the `$items:partial()$` shorthand; the same fix in the `ejs-listing-port` skill's worked example.
- Investigation plan and repro: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-09-listing-nesting-limit.md`.

## Verification

- `cargo nextest run --workspace`: 16012 passed. No snapshot files changed.
- End to end with `q2 render` on the repro: item div depths are constant (`[3, 3, 3]`; at 120 items, all at depth 3, no Q-12-10). The current nightly gives `[3, 4, 5]`.
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build`: Rust steps green. Locally the ts-packages step failed because npm deps are missing from my `node_modules` (same on clean `main`), so CI is the check for the remaining legs.

Follow-ups: bd-p7eqsmmw (failed re-parse of a built-in template should be an error), bd-sgd9desh (detect glued fences in custom templates).

title: CI gate: q2 render --strict claude-notes in the test suite (bd-7v3trpxn)
description:
Follow-up to #807: keep `claude-notes/` rendering clean. Strand bd-7v3trpxn under epic bd-uk8zgkha; plan section "CI gate" in `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-25-claude-notes-q2-website.md`.

## What changed

One step at the end of the Linux `test-suite` leg:

```yaml
- name: Render claude-notes (warnings are errors)
  if: runner.os == 'Linux' && !cancelled()
  run: cargo run --profile ci --bin q2 -- render --strict claude-notes
```

`--strict` promotes warnings to errors and exits 1 on any diagnostic, so a note that fails to parse or warns fails the job with the same report `q2 render` prints locally. Per-document `diagnostics:` opt-outs in front matter are applied before the promotion and stay suppressed.

The binary is reused, not rebuilt: `crates/quarto`'s integration tests run q2 through `CARGO_BIN_EXE_q2`, so the preceding `cargo nextest run --tests --cargo-profile ci` has already built `target/ci/q2`; the step adds the render itself, about two seconds for 1452 files, nothing needed on `PATH`. (A first draft was a standalone workflow that built q2; dropped because `rust-cache` evicts workspace-crate artifacts, so it would have recompiled the workspace on every PR for a two-second render.)

Built from the branch and run on every PR, the step also fails when a parser change breaks the notes — ~1,450 documents of qmd corpus — and lets a q2 fix land together with the note changes it needs.

`AGENTS.md` and `claude-notes/instructions/writing-notes.md` now say to check a note with `q2 render --strict <file>` and name the gate.

## Verified locally

The exact command exits 0 with 1452 / 1452; a file with one Q-2-49 warning exits 1 under `--strict`. `actionlint` reports only the two pre-existing shellcheck infos in `test-suite.yml`; `cargo xtask lint` passes. This PR is the first run of the step in CI.

## Filed along the way (p3)

- bd-be8ve52f — `q2 render`'s per-diagnostic output keeps ANSI SGR and OSC 8 hyperlinks under `NO_COLOR` or redirected stderr; only the counts clause checks.
- bd-m7pqz8a5 — `cargo xtask switch-task --from main` fetches `origin/main` but branches off the stale local `main` while printing "after pull".

title: claude-notes as a Quarto 2 website (bd-uk8zgkha)
description:
Renders `claude-notes/` as a Quarto 2 website (`q2 render claude-notes`): 1451 / 1451 notes, no errors, no warnings. Epic bd-uk8zgkha; plan in `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-25-claude-notes-q2-website.md`.

## What changed

**`claude-notes/`** — a `_quarto.yml` (website; renders `**/*.md`, excludes the repro fixtures that exist to fail or warn and the nested repro projects), and syntax fixes across ~1,000 notes so they parse as qmd. Nothing was reworded: the edits are backslash escapes (`` `a.rs`\'s ``, `\_quarto.yml`, `\$5`, `\[label\]`, `\<placeholder>`), code spans around code expressions and generic types (`` `argv[1]` ``, `` `Vec<String>` ``), fenced blocks for indented code, four-backtick outer fences where a block holds another fence, `{=html}` raw inlines/blocks for real HTML, triple-braced `{{{< … >}}}` for quoted shortcodes (and `shortcodes="false"` on fences and on spans that show the escaped form), `::: ^1` block footnotes, and re-indented `- [x]` continuations. The star-emphasis cases were reviewed by hand.

**Guidance** — `docs/guides/authoring/migrating-markdown.qmd` (new; linked from the sidebar, the guides index and `markdown-basics.qmd`): what Pandoc/CommonMark habits q2 rejects, warns about, or reads differently, with the fix for each. `claude-notes/instructions/writing-notes.md` (new): the fifteen habits that break notes, in frequency order. `AGENTS.md` points at both.

**Scripts** — `scripts/q2-render-tally.py` (diagnostics by code, baselines), `q2-escape-openers.py` (escape exactly the delimiter a diagnostic points at, to a fixpoint), `q2-escape-literal.py`, `q2-dedent-task-items.py`, and `claude-notes-escape-fixpoint.sh` that runs the reviewed rules jointly. These are what a merge from `main` needs: new notes arrive unescaped.

## How it was done

Mechanical escaping to a fixpoint first (about 70% of the errors), then per-file Haiku agent batches through the Workflow tool — a fixer and an independent verifier per file, batches of 10 → 50 → full — with every batch reviewed by classifying each changed line (backslash / backticks / dedent / fence / …), rendering every changed file standalone, and reading every non-mechanical line; wrong edits reverted and a rule added. Thirteen such batches in all (errors, bracket warnings, shortcode warnings). The plan has the numbers per batch and the lessons.

## q2 findings along the way

Filed as strands, most already fixed on `main` (code-span backtick runs, nested-project boundary, whitespace-flanked delimiters, bare `@`, `⟨`): bd-ckbqmupi, bd-bare-at-literal-w3ytmu8e, bd-apostrophe-after-span-6l9c8c26, bd-code-span-longer-backtick-run-nycn85a8, bd-whitespace-flanked-delimiters-0ncy8bgq, bd-nested-projects-xyb28wnl, bd-angle-bracket-u27e8-parse-error-r6l55zmh, bd-dollar-math-flanking-wzjx4hn8, bd-unmatched-backtick-run-literal-tjfo21xq, bd-uncoded-braces-indent-9eq8004k, bd-jfjyds7r (setext headings silent), bd-fx3fr46j (Q-2-29 never emitted), bd-qcdweixf (no tilde fences), bd-e0e9kd4a (YAML provenance desync on folded scalars with non-ASCII; worked around here), bd-9vmlk2md (three warnings without a Q code). bd-v8t4l69h and bd-3djx9ris closed as by design and documented instead.

title: Regression test for non-ASCII block scalar YAML spans (bd-e0e9kd4a)
description: ## Summary This adds a q2 regression test for bd-e0e9kd4a. YAML front matter with a block scalar (`>` or `|`) containing non-ASCII text used to break source locations for everything after it. The fix is quarto-yaml 0.5.0 (posit-dev/quarto-yaml#22), which `main` already picked up in feca201b9; this PR only adds the test and the investigation notes. ### Example ```yaml status: > v2 — x beads: y ``` Rendering this produced "YAML string scalar has no content provenance" warnings. Every span after the scalar was also shifted, so any caret there pointed at the wrong bytes. ### Root cause Up to 0.4.0, quarto-yaml used yaml-rust2. In yaml-rust2, `scan_block_scalar_content_line` advances `Marker` index and col by `line_buffer.len()`, which counts bytes, not chars. quarto-yaml 0.5.0 switched to saphyr, whose scanner counts chars. ## Changes - **`crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs`**: new test `non_ascii_block_scalars_keep_later_spans_and_provenance`. - It parses real YAML with a `>` scalar and a `|` scalar holding non-ASCII text, followed by a key whose value contains raw HTML. - It asserts that no desync warning is emitted and that the two Q-2-9 carets underline exactly `` and ``. - Pinning quarto-yaml back to `=0.4.0` makes it fail: two desync warnings, and both carets collapse to end-of-input. - **`claude-notes/plans/2026-10-08-folded-scalar-provenance-desync.md`**: the investigation and the resolution, plus a small probe crate that prints the raw yaml-rust2 markers. ## Test plan - [x] `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passes (16010 tests). - [x] The new test fails against quarto-yaml 0.4.0 and passes against 0.5.0. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: verify: run hub-client lint:css with --prefix; lint against nested npm workspaces
description:
## Problem

`cargo xtask verify` has been failing at step 1 on `main` since 909eada30 ("Add vscode-sync-experiment"). npm resolves `-w hub-client` to **every** workspace at or under that path. `hub-client/vscode-sync-experiment` is now a root workspace inside `hub-client/`, so `npm run lint:css -w hub-client` also runs in `quarto-hub-vscode`, which has no `lint:css` script, and the step exits 1. Selecting by name doesn't help, because hub-client's package name equals its directory name: `npm pkg get name -w hub-client` returns both packages.

CI was already patched with `--if-present` in b8ce24b7c. `verify` was not, and nothing noticed, because `css_lint_command_matches_ci_workflow` only checked that the CI line *contains* the local command.

## Fix

- `CSS_LINT_ARGS` in `crates/xtask/src/verify.rs` and the `Lint hub-client CSS` step in `ts-test-suite.yml` now both use `npm run lint:css --prefix hub-client`. That runs exactly one package. Unlike `--if-present`, if the script is ever renamed the lint fails loudly instead of silently passing.
- `css_lint_command_matches_ci_workflow` now requires an exact line match.
- **New xtask lint `nested-npm-workspace`** (`crates/xtask/src/lint/nested_npm_workspaces.rs`) fails when any root workspace is nested inside another, which catches this class of bug at the source. It reuses `ci_test_wiring`'s workspace expansion.
- `AGENTS.md` now documents the `--prefix` form.

## Follow-up: please weigh in on moving `vscode-sync-experiment`

The new lint **allowlists `hub-client/vscode-sync-experiment`** for now, tracked by bd-prfbxrth. While the experiment stays nested, any `-w hub-client` still fans out to it. For example, `hub-client-e2e.yml:189` (`npm run build --workspace hub-client --if-present`) also esbuilds the extension. That's harmless today, and this PR leaves it alone.

The full fix is to move the experiment out from under `hub-client/` (e.g. into `ts-packages/` or a top-level `experiments/`), update the root `workspaces`, and drop the `ALLOWED` entry. Since it's your experiment, we'd like your take on where it should live before doing that.

## Testing

- `cargo nextest run -p xtask`: 200/200 pass. That includes 5 new unit tests for the lint, and the tightened sync test, which fails against the old `--if-present` CI line.
- With the allowlist entry removed, `cargo xtask lint` flags `package.json:8`.
- A seeded `margin-left: 0` in `hub-client/src/App.css` makes `npm run lint:css --prefix hub-client` exit 1, so the lint still bites.
- `cargo xtask verify` (without `--skip-css-lint`): all steps pass locally except `smoke_all`, which has 9 failures that are environment-only on my machine (R lacks `gt`/`flextable`, and Python lacks `pandas`/`polars`).

```
Error: [Q-1-1] YAML Syntax Error
   ╭─[ bad-frontmatter.qmd:4:7 ]
 4 │ format: html
   │       ┬
   │       ╰── illegal placement of ':' indicator
ℹ The YAML front matter at the top of this document could not be parsed
```

The precise position comes from **quarto-yaml 0.4.0** (posit-dev/quarto-yaml#21, upstream strand `qy-scan-error-location-f9r4yvxq`). Scan errors now carry `location`, and the message no longer embeds position text. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-08-frontmatter-yaml-error-code.md`.

## What changed

- **Dependency:** `quarto-yaml` 0.3.0 → 0.4.0.
- **New `pampa::utils::yaml_syntax_error`:** shared helpers that turn a `quarto_yaml::Error` into either a Q-1-1 diagnostic builder or prose ending in `(line L, column C)`. It also contains the end-of-input clamp described below.
- **Frontmatter** (`pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs`): emits a located Q-1-1 diagnostic with a hint naming the front matter.
- **The bump regressed every site that stringified the error, so this PR fixes them all.** Before 0.4.0, the message for `parse_file` callers ended in `… at byte N line L column C`, and that line number was file-relative and correct. After the bump, these sites would have printed no position at all:
  - **Located Q-1-1** via `QuartoError::Parse`, with the file content registered under quarto-yaml's FileId (`config_sources::yaml_parse_error`): `_quarto.yml`, profile overlays and `_quarto.yml.local`, `_metadata.yml`.
  - **Prose** via `describe_yaml_error`: extension manifests (shown inside a Q-16-1 warning), the `_variables.yml` warning, language term files (×2), and the `quarto use` config loader.
  - **No change needed:** the Jupyter cell-option paths already used `CellOptionsError::location()`. They gain precise spans automatically.
- **End-of-input clamp.** The scanner reports a missing closer (`[a, b` with no `]`) at end of input, which is past the trailing newline. That put the caret on the closing `---` of front matter, or on a code cell's first code line. Such locations are now pulled back to the end of the YAML's last content: `title: [unclosed` points at 2:17.

## Regression report: changed tests

Every existing test whose assertions changed:

| Test | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quarto::preview_static_e2e::a_failing_rerender_reports_diagnostics_and_does_not_reload` | asserted SSE text and stderr contain `Q-0-99` | asserts `Q-1-1` (2 asserts) | It pinned the bug: broken front matter was Q-0-99. |
| `quarto::preview_static_e2e::boot_with_a_failing_page_still_serves_the_rest` | stderr contains `Q-0-99` | stderr contains `Q-1-1` | Same fixture, same reason. |
| `quarto` `render_once_tests::page_error_is_reported_not_fatal` | diagnostics text contains `Q-0-99` | contains `Q-1-1` | Same. |
| `quarto-core::pandoc_request_books::a_chapter_with_broken_front_matter_fails_before_any_chapter_renders` | `out.error.to_lowercase().contains("front")` | `out.error == "YAML Syntax Error"`, **and** the chapter's Q-1-1 diagnostic has a hint containing "front matter" | **Worth a look.** `PandocRequestOutcome.error` is the *title* of the first error. The old title was "Failed to parse YAML frontmatter: …"; the new one is the catalog title, so the one-line summary no longer says "front matter". The context moved into the diagnostic's hint, which this test now asserts. This was a design decision (catalog title + hint); if hub-client surfaces only `error`, a custom title may be preferable. |
| `quarto-core` `project::…::test_directory_metadata_invalid_yaml_fails` | `to_string()` contains "metadata"/"parse"/"yaml" | is `QuartoError::Parse` with one Q-1-1 diagnostic, and the render contains `_metadata.yml:1:` | Tightened to the new structured shape. |
| `quarto-core::project_profile_overlays::overlay_yaml_parse_error_aborts_discovery` | `result.is_err()` | also asserts a Q-1-1 located in `_quarto-prod.yml` with that file's content registered | Strengthened; the input is unchanged. |

**Unchanged on purpose:** `ipynb_content_processor::cell_option_yaml_error_lands_in_owning_cell` failed after the bump alone. The caret had moved to row 1 (`print(1)`), off the `#| error: [unclosed` option line. The end-of-input clamp fixes this, and the test passes **unmodified**. `pampa::test_warnings` still pins Q-0-99 for the caption-without-table fallback, which is out of scope (see follow-ups).

### New tests

- `pampa::test_frontmatter_yaml_syntax_error`: Q-1-1 with no internal path, the exact offending byte, non-ASCII text before the error, and an end-of-input error staying in bounds.
- `pampa` `utils::yaml_syntax_error::tests`: location and fallback, `describe_yaml_error`, the end-of-input clamp, and `line_column` on char boundaries.
- `project_profile_overlays::base_config_yaml_syntax_error_is_located_q_1_1`: `_quarto.yml:3:6`.
- One position test per prose site: extension manifest, term file, `_variables.yml` warning, and `quarto use`.

### Not covered by a test

- The "before" strings for the config sites above come from reading quarto-yaml 0.3.0's `Display` (`Parse error: {ScanError}`, which ends in `at byte N line L column C`). They were not captured from a pre-change binary. The front-matter "before" was captured: `claude-notes/plans/frontmatter-yaml-error-code-investigation/`.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify --skip-css-lint`:
  - Rust tests: 16,007 / 16,008 pass. The one failure is `smoke_all`, whose failing cases all fail for local engine reasons: R/knitr "R process failed", and great_tables/pandas missing for Jupyter. The same documents fail on unmodified `main` in this environment.
  - Steps 6–14, including the hub-client WASM build and `test:wasm`: all pass.
- `--skip-css-lint` is needed because `main` is red on `lint:css`. `npm run lint:css -w hub-client` also selects the nested `hub-client/vscode-sync-experiment` workspace. This is unrelated to this PR and tracked in `bd-verify-css-lint-nested-ws-r0dd5vdk`.

## Follow-ups filed

- `bd-caption-warning-q099-5krqlz6w`: "Caption found without a preceding table" fallback is still Q-0-99 with a path in the title.
- `bd-depth-limit-q099-f1q9vqjw`: "too deeply nested" is Q-0-99 with no location.
- `bd-metadata-yml-error-swallowed-b8sjkxek`: a malformed `_metadata.yml` is **silently ignored** (`metadata_merge.rs` calls `.unwrap_or_default()`). This predates this PR. The error is now structured, but it still never reaches the user.

title: Ship native Windows ARM64 binaries (nightly + release)
description:
Braid: `bd-windows-arm64-nightly-xms5p652` · Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-08-windows-arm64-nightly.md`

Someone asked for Windows ARM binaries in the nightlies. Today ARM64 Windows gets `windows_amd64` and runs it under x64 emulation.

## Changes

- **`release-pipeline.yml`**: new `windows_arm64` build leg (`aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`), built **natively on `windows-11-arm`**. An x64 host can't execute an ARM64 binary, and the verify gates need to run it. This is the same reasoning as `linux_arm64` on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`.
  - Added to the asset-manifest parity list, the release completeness check and the notes table.
  - Ships on both channels (the pipeline is shared).
- **`install.ps1`**:
  - Detects the **OS** architecture from the registry, then `RuntimeInformation`, then env vars. This holds up when an x64 PowerShell runs under emulation.
  - On ARM64 it prefers `windows_arm64` and falls back to `windows_amd64` for releases that predate it.
  - New `-Platform` override.
  - x64 machines behave as before, with no extra API calls.
- **`nightly.yml` install-smoke**:
  - Adds `windows-11-arm`.
  - On Windows, runs the installer under both PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1.
  - Asserts the installed `q2.exe`'s PE machine type (`0x8664` / `0xAA64`) matches the runner, so the x64 fallback can't hide a missing ARM64 asset.
- Runbook and header comments updated.

## Testing

- `actionlint` passes on all three workflows.
- `install.ps1` was exercised offline with pwsh 7.6 and a mocked GitHub API, covering all selection and fallback paths (details in the plan).
- **Branch dry run** (Nightly, `force: true, publish: false`): https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/37824531935. This is the first build of the new leg. The PR isn't ready to merge until it's green.
- **After merge:** `install-smoke` only runs against a *published* nightly, so the first scheduled nightly after merge is the first end-to-end check of the installer changes on real ARM hardware.

title: Fix docx download naming comment authors by raw actor-id prefix
description:
## Problem
Downloading a document with editorial marks (e.g. span comments) as docx showed authors like `b25fbe97` in Word instead of the user's name.

## Causes
The identity table was empty, so `buildIdentityMap` fell back to `actor.slice(0, 8)`:

1. **Initial load raced the local identity.** App's one-shot initial URL load ran before `getUserIdentity()` resolved, so `screenName` and `localAuthorId` were `undefined`. With auth off, that connection stamped no author on edits and registered no identity. The load now waits for the identity. (With auth on, the author id comes from the server, but the screen name is still needed to register the identity, so a hard reload on a deep link could skip it.)
2. **Download-mode pane erased the table.** `useDownloadAs` wrote `{}` into the shared identity table when called without one (`DownloadModePane`). It now writes only when a table is passed.

## Notes
- Text already written without an author keeps its actor-id prefix; the history has nothing to resolve it to.
- Verified by hand on a dev server (auth off): hard reload, comment on new text, download docx shows the user's name.

## Testing
- `src/pandoc` unit tests (250) and integration tests (9) pass, including a new regression test for the table clobber; `tsc` clean for the changed files.
- Not run: workspace nextest, Playwright e2e. `App.tsx` change has no unit coverage.

title: q2 render --json-errors: plain rendered/error text (quarto-error-reporting 0.4.0)
description:
Tracks bd-ckbqmupi item 2 (and completes bd-6d9ew2up). Follows #795. Upstream: posit-dev/quarto-error-reporting qe-hal9cc7b, released as 0.4.0. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-07-json-errors-plain-rendered.md`.

## Problem

After #795, `--json-errors` stderr was pure NDJSON, but its human-readable strings were still full of terminal escapes:

- `rendered`: ariadne SGR color runs around single characters, plus OSC-8 hyperlinks;
- the pass-1 wrapper's `error`: `ParseError::render`, the same colored text.

Without an ANSI stripper, jq pipelines and agents can't read either one. On the claude-notes website, most of the 6.48 MB stream was escape sequences.

## Change

- **Bump `quarto-error-reporting` 0.3.2 → 0.4.0**, in the workspace and in the excluded `wasm-quarto-hub-client` (its own manifest and lockfile). The only breaking change is in `TextRenderOptions` struct literals: 15 sites move to `TextRenderOptions::default().hyperlinks(false)`.
- **`rendered` is plain under `--json-errors`.** `diagnostic_json` calls `diagnostic_to_json_with_options(.., &TextRenderOptions::plain())`. Link targets already travel structurally (`source_file`, `origin.notebook_path`). Other consumers (hub-client, preview) keep the default colored rendering.
- **New `failure_error_text`** re-renders a failure's message from its structured diagnostics, with the caller's options (same order and separator as `ParseError::render`). It feeds the pass-1 `error` and the legacy pass-2 "Render failed" `problem`. Opaque messages that have no diagnostics are sanitized when no color is requested.
- **bd-6d9ew2up:** text mode's no-color form (the `q2 preview --static` overlay) renders with real `color`/`hyperlinks` options instead of stripping escapes after the fact. Terminal output is unchanged.
- **Test change:** `ipynb_diagnostic_hyperlinks_real_notebook` now checks the notebook hyperlink in text mode, where hyperlinks remain the documented behavior. The JSON side asserts the plain label.

## Verification

- **Tests first:** the new `json_errors_strings_carry_no_terminal_escapes` walks every *decoded* string of every record; a raw-byte search of stderr can't see `\u001b` inside JSON strings. Before the fix, it failed on exactly the top-level `rendered`, the nested `diagnostics[].rendered`, and the pass-1 `error`.
- **Locally:**
  - `cargo nextest run --workspace` passes, except `smoke_all`, which fails only on machine-specific fixtures (R cairo, missing `great_tables`);
  - full `cargo xtask verify` (WASM build and hub-client tests included) is green, with the CSS lint skipped for bd-0jtxndiy.
- **End-to-end on `claude-notes/`:**
  - **0** decoded strings containing ESC;
  - stderr went from **6.48 MB to 1.45 MB**;
  - all 1,202 `rendered`/`error` texts equal the previous text with escapes stripped, so the change only removes escapes.

title: q2 render --json-errors: pure NDJSON on stderr, source_file on every located record
description:
Tracks bd-gnw9asuo (child: bd-ckbqmupi item 1). Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-06-json-errors-output-hygiene.md`.

## Problem

`--json-errors` exists so tools like `jq` can read and filter diagnostics, but rendering the claude-notes website with nightly `0.33.0-nightly.20261006` showed two gaps:

1. **stderr was not pure NDJSON.** The "Rendering project: …" and "Rendered N of M files …" status lines were mixed into the stream. The audit found more plain-text writers of the same kind:
   - render-script chatter;
   - CLI-raised warnings (Q-20-8 and Q-5-11 / project-config diagnostics), which were printed as ariadne text regardless of the flag.
2. **Located records had no file.** 422 of the 423 top-level `json-diagnostic` records had `start_line`/`start_column` but no `source_file`:
   - every per-page warning;
   - located project diagnostics;
   - discovery and render-script parse errors.

## Change

- **`RenderArgs::console_quiet()`:** `--json-errors` now implies `--quiet` for console output. That covers status lines, engine progress, and render-script output. The CLI help says so.
- **`emit_cli_diagnostic`:** diagnostics the CLI raises itself become JSON records under `--json-errors`. The text path is unchanged.
- **`diagnostic_json`:** every JSON conversion goes through this function. It sets `source_file` to **the file the record's coordinates refer to**, resolved from the diagnostic's own location through the same `SourceContext` (and the same `map_offset(0, ..)`) that `diagnostic_to_json` uses for the coordinates. This mirrors `quarto-error-reporting`'s `hyperlink_target`:
  - a notebook cell reports its notebook;
  - an on-disk file reports its own path;
  - the caller's file (page, config) is only a fallback, for records with no resolvable location.

  Paths are absolute (`std::path::absolute`, which keeps the plain form on Windows). One consequence: a page-render warning located in `_quarto.yml` (raw HTML in `page-footer`, Q-2-9) is attributed to `_quarto.yml`, not to the page.

## Verification

- 10 new e2e tests that run the real binary (`json_errors.rs`, `render_scripts_cli.rs`). A strict `parse_ndjson_strict` helper fails on any non-JSON line. 9 of the tests were confirmed to fail before the fix, for the expected reasons.
- Locally:
  - `cargo nextest run --workspace` passes, except `smoke_all`, which fails only on machine-specific typst fixtures (R cairo, missing `great_tables`).
  - `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build`: the Rust legs are green.
- End-to-end on `claude-notes/`:
  - non-JSON stderr lines went from 2 to **0**;
  - located records without `source_file` went from 422 to **0**;
  - with `source_file` stripped, the records are identical to the nightly's.

## Also in this PR: Q-13-x path quoting (bd-3801o1o0)

The missing-document diagnostics (Q-13-1/2/3/4/7) wrapped the path in `'…'`, so a path containing an apostrophe looked mangled. claude-notes links a placeholder `Q-X-Y'.qmd`, which rendered as `'plans/Q-X-Y'.qmd' is not in the project index.` The path is now quoted as a code span (house style): `` `plans/Q-X-Y'.qmd` is not in the project index. `` A unit test pins the wording.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- bd-ho1n0wui: non-JSON writers below the CLI layer (pampa `eprintln!`s, the replay of a failed script's stderr).
- bd-hgam88i2: `_quarto.yml` YAML syntax errors at discovery lose their location (span-less Q-7-8).
- Comment on bd-f5rpd: fixing the tracing filter would expose `quarto-core` warns as plain text in the stream.
- bd-ckbqmupi item 2: ANSI in `rendered` / the pass-1 `error` field. The `rendered` half is filed upstream as qe-hal9cc7b (posit-dev/quarto-error-reporting).

title: Run pandoc in the browser: Download as Word/PowerPoint/EPUB/ODT/Typst/PDF, Import from Word and friends, and margin comments
description:
## Summary

quarto-hub could render documents but could not convert them to or from other office formats. This PR adds pandoc.wasm to the hub client. With it, the hub can **export** the open document (or a whole book) to six formats and **import** five formats into a Quarto document. All of it runs in the browser, with no server-side conversion.

Comments get their own treatment. Word comments arrive on import as plain spans holding a comment, and they render as margin bubbles anchored to the commented text. That rendering is @vezwork's work on `feature/span-comments`. This PR carries his three commits with authorship intact (`91a2b2743`, `95c1364b5`, `b45470b17`), and the import work builds directly on them.

## What users get

**Comments in the margin** (@vezwork's `feature/span-comments`). A comment span renders as a bubble anchored to the text it covers. Adding and highlighting comments is reworked to match. Import and export below both rely on this.

**Download as.** The document top bar gains a "Download as" menu with progress, cancel and a warnings summary.
- **Formats:** Word, PowerPoint, EPUB, ODT, Typst source and PDF. PDF runs pandoc, then Typst, in the browser. The first PDF fetches about 33 MB of converter and fonts.
- **Books:** On a chapter of a book project, Typst, PDF and EPUB offer "Download book as" (all chapters in one file, with per-chapter progress) and "This chapter only".
- **Projects:** Documents inside a `_quarto.yml` project download too.
- **Editorial marks in Word:** `[++ ]` and `[-- ]` become real tracked changes, `[!! ]` becomes a highlight, and `[>> ]` becomes a Word comment, including replies. Each carries its author and date. PowerPoint shows each mark as formatted text.

**Typst PDF preview.** A document whose format is `typst` can show a PDF preview in the preview pane, in a built-in pdf.js viewer that keeps your page and zoom. It recompiles shortly after you stop typing and keeps the last good PDF on screen if a change breaks the build. Two warm pandoc workers bring the refresh to roughly 270 ms in Chromium and 320 ms in WebKit, down from 380 and 580 ms.

**Import.** An **Import** button sits next to "Add asset" in the Files sidebar. You can also drop a file anywhere in the hub window.
- **Formats:** docx, odt, rtf, epub and pptx. docx gets the most fidelity work.
- **Placement:** A dialog proposes a folder and name, and never overwrites. A taken name moves on to `name 2`.
- **Images:** Images go into `<name>_media/`, named by content hash. EMF/WMF images are converted to SVG in the browser.
- **Tracked changes and comments:** Word tracked changes, highlights and comments become editorial marks with author and date preserved. A comment on a range becomes a span followed by the comment and its replies, which render as margin bubbles.
- **Report:** An import report lists anything lost, converted, skipped or warned about.
- **Limits:** Files up to 25 MB are accepted. The first import fetches pandoc.wasm (about 16 MB) and caches it.

**Rich-text editor.** Highlight, delete and insert buttons mark the selected text, and those marks now edit in place with the brackets hidden. The buttons are disabled until text is selected.

**Fixes found along the way.**
- Preview images with a space or other percent-encoded character in their path (such as `name 2_media/`) no longer show as broken.
- The "Download as" status panel and the Render Error popup now have copy buttons.

## How it works

- **Ownership rule.** Rust builds the pandoc request and owns paths, format tables, AST transforms and every user-facing diagnostic. TypeScript mounts the files, runs pandoc in a worker, and stores the results. Image bytes never enter the main-thread Rust wasm, which grows about 4.5x the payload and never shrinks.
- **Host:** `@quarto/pandoc-host` provides the loader, the worker lifecycle and failure taxonomy, and a warm executor with poison and retire policy. The `PandocRequest` contract has a JSON schema.
- **Import:** The pipeline is `pandoc -f <fmt> -t json`, then pampa's lenient reader, AST transforms, and the qmd writer. It is a pure function of the source bytes. The qmd is committed as a single Automerge change, written after the images, so a failed import leaves no qmd with broken links.
- **qmd writer fixes** that import depends on:
  - Line-start markers (`1.`, `-`, `+`) are escaped.
  - Footnotes keep their multiple blocks and lists.
  - Adjacent lists stay separate.
  - Editorial-mark shorthand keeps its attributes.
- **Export transform:** A Rust transform in quarto-core's pipeline renders editorial marks to OOXML. It ports the `quarto-ooxml-editorial-marks` extension and adds commented ranges. Native renders and the hub share it.

## Not in this PR

- Re-importing an edited source over an existing qmd. The pipeline is built to allow it, but the merge itself is out of scope.
- Reconstructing Quarto's own docx output (layout tables back into figures, callouts and crossrefs).
- Splitting an EPUB into a book project.
- Import in `q2 preview`, which ships no pandoc.wasm.
- Fancy list markers (`a.`, `(i)`) and a multi-block definition-list writer bug. Both are reported rather than preserved.

## Testing

_To be filled in before marking ready: workspace nextest pass/skip counts and the hub-client vitest and Playwright results across the Chromium, WebKit and Firefox projects._

Much of the diff (1,293 files) is recordings, fixtures and goldens.

title: Let Rust own shortcode expansion: fix escaped shortcodes crashing pandoc, and expand them in footnote definitions
description:
## Summary

Escaped shortcodes such as `` `{{{< brand >}}}` `` crashed pandoc with exit 83 whenever the page was rendered through the pandoc path. Rust unescapes `{{{< x >}}}` once, and the vendored Lua shortcodes pass then expanded the result as a live shortcode. For handlers that Rust doesn't know (`brand`), the Lua side hit a nil `brandCommand` at `shortcodes-handlers.lua:111`.

The fix makes Rust the only place shortcodes are expanded. Two commits:

1. **Expand shortcodes in footnote definitions and `lst-cap` (bd-xjg7vl6c).** `shortcode_resolve` skipped `NoteDefinitionPara`, `NoteDefinitionFencedBlock` and the `lst-cap` attribute of listing code blocks, which the Lua pass had been covering. Quarto 1 expands all three, so Rust now does too. This has to land first. Without it, turning Lua off would leave `[^1]: Note {{< meta author >}}.` unexpanded.
2. **Disable the vendored Lua shortcodes pass (bd-2uva9urq).** The `pre-shortcodes-filter` entries in `main.lua` and `crossref/crossref.lua` now require `q2_lua_shortcodes_disabled`, a flag that is never set, so the runner skips them. This is a flag-gate rather than a removal. `shortcodes_filter()` must still be called because `foldcode.lua`'s `process_shortcodes` uses `_shortcodes_filter`. Both edits carry a `QUARTO2-PATCH` comment, and the README's "Ours vs. pinned" section documents them.

## Tests

- `shortcode_all_contexts`: a parameterized test over every context where a shortcode can appear. Contexts that Quarto 1 also leaves literal are pinned as literal.
- `shortcode_pandoc_escapes`: renders to `native` and checks that escaped brand shortcodes stay literal in a code span, a code span with arguments and a fenced block. A control confirms that a live `{{< brand >}}` still only warns. Three of the four cases failed with exit 83 before the flag-gate.
- `pandoc_filters::test_shim_group_shape_and_patch_markers` pinned exactly two `QUARTO2-PATCH` markers in `main.lua`. It now ignores the unrelated shortcodes marker.

## Not in this PR

- **Brand support.** A live `{{< brand >}}` still doesn't render. That stays with bd-qnylgu69.
- **pandoc-wasm.** `pandoc-request.golden.json` stores a hash of the embedded filter tree (`share_tree_version`), so editing the Lua changes it. That file only exists on `feature/pandoc-wasm`. Whichever branch lands second needs one `Q2_REGENERATE_GOLDEN=1` regeneration. The pandoc recordings are self-contained and don't need re-recording.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo nextest run --workspace` (running locally; result will be posted as a comment)
- [ ] CI green

title: Typst: resolve CSS generic font families to an installed font
description:
Typst has no generic font families, but we passed `serif`, `sans-serif`, `monospace` and friends straight through. Any brand or style that used one produced `unknown font family: sans-serif` warnings on every compile, and Typst then fell back to whatever it liked. `system-ui` and the `ui-*` keywords weren't recognized at all, so they were treated as font names.

Each generic keyword is now replaced, at its position in the font list, by the first installed font from an ordered candidate list. The lists are built from Chromium's per-OS defaults, fontconfig's `60-latin.conf`, Modern Font Stacks and Bootstrap's stacks, with Typst's bundled fonts last so `serif`, `monospace` and `math` always resolve. The keyword itself is never emitted, so `font-family: Roboto, sans-serif` becomes `Roboto` when it's installed and otherwise the first installed sans-serif candidate. The candidate lists are in `typst_css.lua` with their sources cited. No font is bundled.

When nothing in a generic's list is installed (realistically `sans-serif` on a bare Linux box), the keyword is dropped. If that leaves the list empty, we use Typst's default text font, because Typst rejects an empty `font: ()`. `generic(...)` is dropped, as it has no Typst equivalent.

Because the winning font differs per machine, the tests don't assert one. The resolver is a pure function, unit-tested against synthetic font sets. The smoke-all fixtures assert only that no keyword reaches the `.typ`. The ported `font-filtering-generics` fixture previously asserted the keyword was preserved, which is the behavior this changes.

This is also being backported to quarto-cli:

* quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14986

title: Port Q1's typst brand-yaml typography fixtures that pass today
description:
Ports the five Q1 `brand-yaml/typography` smoke-all fixtures that pass against Q2 today, and records what stops the rest of that directory from porting. No source changes: this is tests plus notes.

## What's covered

- `typography/font-list` and `title-inherit-base-family`, verbatim. They exercise comma-separated family lists, Google-sourced fonts and heading/base inheritance.
- `typography/kitchen-sink-1` and `kitchen-sink-2`, the most demanding per-element styling fixtures: font family, weight, style, size, colour, background, line-height and decoration across base, headings, inline/block code and links, checked both in the generated `.typ` and in the compiled PDF. Q1 relies on a sibling `_brand.yml` being found automatically; Q2 deliberately doesn't do that, so these add an explicit `brand: _brand.yml`.
- `typography/relative-path`, which loads a brand and its fonts from a subdirectory. Its fonts are variable TTFs, which Typst accepts but warns about, so it sets `noErrors: true` with a comment saying why. It keeps its own copy of the fonts because where they live is the point of the test.

Together these show that brand typography reaches Typst correctly once the brand resolves: the earlier suspicion that font filtering, fallback chains or per-element styling were broken didn't hold up.

`basefont-typst`, `dashed-font-weights`, `mainfont-typst` and `nobrand` are also in this Q1 directory but are already ported, with identical content, by #785, so they aren't repeated here.

## What's not covered, and why

The remaining fixtures fail for reasons unrelated to typography, so each is tracked with the bug that blocks it (the fixtures are noted on those strands and should land with the fixes):

- `typography/simple`, `complex`, `google` and the related header-using fixtures: `include-in-header` / `include-before-body` / `include-after-body` are silently dropped for every Pandoc-based format, not just Typst, so the `#set text(fallback: false, weight: 100)` these rely on never applies. Tracked in bd-7avt1ogu.
- `typography/brand-extension`: `project: brand:` is ignored, which is how a brand extension supplies its brand. Q1 reads `brand ?? project.brand`. Tracked in bd-fzxdas1i.
- `font-filtering-generics`: CSS generic families like `sans-serif` and `monospace` are passed through to Typst, which has no such families and warns. Tracked in bd-hkf3r8i1, which plans to resolve each generic to the first installed font from per-generic candidate lists rather than bundling one.

Minimal repros for the first two are committed under `claude-notes/plans/typst-brand-typography-fixtures-investigation/`.

## Testing

`cargo clippy -p quarto --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The `brand-yaml` smoke-all subset (17 fixtures) passes. The workspace `cargo nextest run` ran 15466 tests, all passing, with 202 skipped, which matches the count before this change, since fixtures are discovered inside the single `smoke_all` test.

`cargo xtask verify` currently fails at its `lint:css` step on `main` because of the new `hub-client/vscode-sync-experiment` workspace; that's unrelated and tracked separately (bd-0jtxndiy).

title: Port Q1's typst smoke-all fixtures and fix two bugs they exposed
description:
## Summary

Q1's typst smoke-all fixtures are the cheapest way to find where Q2's
typst output diverges from Q1. This branch ports 30 of them and fixes the
two real bugs the port exposed: an `authors.lua` crash on pandoc-hybrid
targets, and an empty TOC title when none is set. The other divergences
were fixed in separate PRs or filed as strands, all linked below.

Follows #745, which introduced the typst smoke-all suite.

## Changes

- **Fixtures (30 ported).** They live under
  `crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all/typst/`: basic-blocks (7), brand-yaml (10),
  citations (3), columns (4), theorem (4) and toc-tables (2). Rendered `.typ`
  outputs are gitignored. The triage plan in
  `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-29-typst-smoke-all-followup.md` records which
  fixtures were skipped and why.
- **TOC title.** The typst template fell back to the raw `toc_title` value
  instead of the computed default, so an unset title rendered empty. It now
  uses the computed default.
- **Author normalization.** For `typst`/`docx`/`pptx`/`odt`, the Rust
  `AuthorsNormalizeTransform` wrote normalized authors and affiliations, and
  the vendored `authors.lua` then normalized them again and crashed. Only
  those two keys shadow what `authors.lua` reads as raw input, so the
  transform now saves and restores just them around the normalization call.
  Skipping the transform wholesale would have removed the title block from
  `q2 preview`, whose native-HTML fallback never runs `authors.lua`. This
  unblocks the `two-column-landscape` and `two-column-title-block` fixtures.
- **Citations.** Q1's Cronbach example used `[@a, @b]`, which pandoc parses
  as a malformed nested cite. The ported fixtures use the correct `;`
  delimiter. Since #770, `citeproc: true` on typst resolves to the
  `typst-citations` writer target, so native `<ref-KEY>` labels appear and
  the duplicate `#bibliography()` call does not.
- **Research note.** `claude-notes/research/` gains a survey of the
  unclosed-delimiter autofix rules in qmd-syntax-helper. It is unrelated to
  the typst work and can be split out.

## Related work found during the port

Each finding below came out of rendering Q1's fixtures against Q2. Most were
fixed in follow-up PRs opened as the port went, linked here with their strands.

**Fixed in follow-up PRs**

| Finding | PR | Strand |
|---|---|---|

| #2 attribute-order diagnostics | #762 | `bd-6hf7nz7i` |

| #5 brand.yml logo generation | #751 | none |
| #7 definition-list content loss (the `Term\n: description` grammar is still unimplemented) | #753 | `bd-definition-lists-no-fallback-irykzp3g` |
| #8 extra `#block[` around knitr tables | #767 (draft, still open) | `bd-gb6u8qsz` |
| #10 Spanish `Figura` crossref crash | #757 | `bd-m2j4m3wg` |
| #11 `citeproc: true` on Pandoc-hybrid formats | #770 | `bd-ysqekrm2`, `bd-wjn7jdzw` |
| #12 Skylighting syntax highlighting for Typst | #772 | `bd-typst-skylighting-av61oid8` |
| #13 `css-property-processing: none` ignored | #764 | `bd-5adgk9hr` |
| #14 brand.yml color gaps (a fixture-authoring issue, not a capability gap) | #751 | `bd-x1iurczn` |
| #16 smart-quote `Bayes' Rule` hard error (diagnostic reworded; the heuristic is won't-fix by design) | #748 | `bd-7vz18qht` |
| #17 `source: google` fonts for Typst | #752 | `bd-mzrgikmu` |
| #18 `ensurePdfMetadata` harness assertion | #749 | `bd-0syqvgl2` |

All are merged except #767.

**Fixed in this PR**

|---|---|
| #6 `authors.lua` crash on bare-string affiliation | `bd-ymkkrn64` |
| #9 TOC title auto-fallback | none |

**Still open**

| #19 `q2 preview` drops TOC and crossrefs for explicit non-HTML formats | none |

## Known divergences from Q1/pandoc

The citation fixtures accept Q2's current output in these cases:

- Same-author clusters render `(Cronbach 1951a; Cronbach 1951b)`, where
  pandoc renders `(Cronbach 1951a, 1951b)`.
- `@key[pp. 100-115]` parses as a citation plus an empty span, so the
  locator loses its brackets. The bare-locator lines are left out of the
  fixtures until this is fixed.
- `bibliography: ./refs.bib` is normalized to `refs.bib`, and the
  leading-dot fixture accepts either form.
- The fixture asserts `p. 42` where Q1's assertion expects `42`. I did not
  check this against a real Q1 render.

## Testing

title: Emit book chapter titles as chapter headings in merged typst/EPUB output
description:
In a book rendered to one file (typst/PDF, EPUB), chapters lost their headings. A chapter with only `title: Preface` and some prose had no heading at all, and a chapter with a `title:` plus its own `# Heading` lost the title. The titles survived only in the table of contents.

Merged books now build each chapter's leading heading the way Quarto 1 does:

- With a `title:`, it becomes a level-1 heading ahead of the chapter body, and the body's own headings stay.
- Without one, the chapter's first heading of any level is promoted to level 1 and moved to the front, so text that preceded it follows it.
- With neither, the chapter gets an empty level-1 heading, as in Q1.

These headings are numbered like any other chapter heading, so a titled `index.qmd` is chapter 1. A part with `href:` prints its page title as `#part[…]`, matching Q1. Standalone documents and multi-file HTML are unchanged. The numbering fixtures that used `title: Home` for the index now use an unnumbered `# Home`, so their chapter-number assertions stay put.

title: Fix image paths for subdirectory chapters in single-file typst and epub books
description:
In a book rendered to typst, images in a chapter that lives in a subdirectory came out wrong. A chapter `sub/two.qmd` containing `![](local.png)`, `![](/img/a.png)` and `![](../top.png)` produced `image("sub/local.png")`, `image("sub/img/a.png")` and `image("sub/top.png")`. Only the first points at a real file, and it was never copied into `_book/` either, so typst failed with "file not found". Chapters at the project root were unaffected.

Two things were going wrong. Once the chapters are merged into one document, relative image paths were interpreted against the project root, so a chapter-local image was neither found nor copied. Then the vendored Lua `resourceRefs` filter prepended the chapter directory again to paths Rust had already made page-relative, which doubled the prefix for site-root images and left `../` images stuck under `sub/`.

Now a merge-time pass re-anchors each chapter-relative image at the project root, using the chapter markers the merge already emits. The existing link rewriting and resource copying take it from there. The same chapter now yields `image("sub/local.png")`, `image("img/a.png")` and `image("top.png")`, with all three files copied beside the `.typ`, and the book compiles. The Lua filter no longer touches images in single-file books, since the Rust pass owns them.

Tests render a book with a `sub/` chapter to typst and epub. The typst test checks the emitted paths, the copied files and that the PDF compiles. The epub test checks the images are packaged.

The wasm pandoc request's resource walk has the same chapter-blindness and isn't covered here.

title: refactor: move hidden inline-css under q2 call
description:
Moves the hidden `inline-css` command from the top level to `q2 call inline-css` (still hidden), following Q1's convention of keeping subsystem helpers under `quarto call` (cf. the hidden `call axe`).

- `CallCommands::InlineCss` replaces `Commands::InlineCss`
