title: Fix stale q2-preview-spa e2e specs; run the suite on Firefox too
description:
## Summary

Stacked on #776. Fixes three failing `q2-preview-spa` e2e specs, adds a Firefox project to that suite, and adds a non-gating CI workflow that runs it on both browsers.

Nothing in CI ran this suite before, so the three specs had gone stale unnoticed. They failed identically on Chromium and Firefox, so none is a Firefox bug.

## What changed

- `chrome.spec.ts` (TOC): website projects title the TOC "On this page" (Q1's `toc-title-website`, see `toc_title_term` in `toc_generate.rs`). The spec still expected "Table of Contents".
- `nesting-cursor.spec.ts` and `edit-chrome-placement.spec.ts`: both waited on `[data-testid="q2-breadcrumb-chip"]`, which commit 3fc6e6106 removed when it folded the chip into the pop-up edit toolbar. They now assert on `.q2-rt-toolbar` and its type/nesting indicator.
- The plain-block placement spec no longer asserts that the toolbar flips below. In that fixture the edit box starts about 34px down and the 25px toolbar fits above it, so it correctly stays above. The spec still asserts the toolbar is not clipped.
- `q2-preview-spa/playwright.config.ts`: new `firefox` project running the whole suite except `firefox-ws-queue.spec.ts`, which keeps its own project and open-timeout pref.
- `.github/workflows/q2-preview-spa-e2e.yml`: chromium/firefox matrix with `continue-on-error`. It runs on manual dispatch and on PRs that touch the workflow or the SPA Playwright config.

## Testing

Locally on Chromium, the three fixed specs pass and the suite is 47 passed, 6 skipped, 1 failed.

The one failure, `engine-capture-splice.spec.ts` (PC5), needs `deno`, which my machine has and CI does not (CI skips it). It fails 3 of 3 runs locally and I haven't investigated it. It is not caused by this PR.

The CI run on this PR is the first Firefox run of the corrected suite.

title: Run hub-client e2e on Firefox as well as Chromium
description:
## Summary

The hub-client Playwright suites now run on Firefox as well as Chromium, and everything passes on Firefox. In CI, the default e2e suite (77 passed, 1 skipped), the harness suite (180 passed) and smoke-all (157 passed, 1 skipped) all pass. The one skip in each of the default and smoke-all suites also appears on Chromium. No test needed a skip, a `fixme` or an edit, and no app code changed.

## What changed

- `playwright.config.ts` and `playwright.harness.config.ts` gain a `firefox` project that uses `devices['Desktop Firefox']`. The Chromium project is untouched. The smoke-all config inherits the new project from the base config.
- `hub-client-e2e.yml` runs the job as a `browser: [chromium, firefox]` matrix, so the two legs run in parallel and Firefox does not lengthen the Chromium leg. Each leg caches and installs only its own browser.
- The author-attribution and sync-test-harness steps run only in the Chromium leg. Smoke-all runs in both legs on the nightly schedule and on PRs that touch smoke-all fixtures. A new `smoke-all-browser` dispatch input (`both`, `chromium` or `firefox`) selects the browser for on-demand runs.
- Report artifacts are named `playwright-report-<browser>`, and Firefox reports are kept even when the run is green.

## Firefox is non-gating for now

The Firefox leg has job-level `continue-on-error`, so a Firefox failure shows up as a red leg without failing the workflow. To make it gating, remove that line and add `Hub-Client E2E Tests (firefox)` to the required checks. Check names change to `Hub-Client E2E Tests (chromium)` and `(firefox)`, so branch protection that requires the old name needs updating.

## CI time

The Chromium leg took about 22 minutes on this PR. Its test steps account for about 7 minutes of that: 3.8 for the default suite and 3.5 for the harness suite. Recent push runs on main took about 15–20 minutes, but they are two weeks old, and I haven't compared the same commit without these changes. The browser cache was cold on this run, so a later run should skip the download. The Firefox leg takes about 20 minutes on PRs, and about 20 on the nightly run once smoke-all is included.

## Not covered

- Firefox is not added to the author-attribution suite.
- `q2-preview-spa` is not touched. It already has its own `firefox-ws-queue` project.
- I couldn't test locally. Playwright's Firefox times out on launch on macOS 27.0, so all Firefox results come from CI.

## Testing

Run 37024091225 (PR trigger) and run 37024093547 (dispatch with `run-smoke-all=true`, `smoke-all-browser=firefox`) both finished green on every leg. Pass counts were read from the raw logs, because `continue-on-error` can hide failures.

title: Generate attribution data for Pandoc-hybrid formats, not just HTML
description:
`--attribution=git` only produced attribution data when rendering HTML. For docx, pptx, typst and the other Pandoc-hybrid formats, `quarto.attribution.lookup` returned nil for every node, even though the nodes had valid source info. A filter targeting those formats had no way to ask who wrote a given range.

Attribution data is now built for all Pandoc-hybrid formats when attribution is requested. Pampa-side Lua filters (pre-ast, post-ast, pre-quarto) can call `lookup`, `lookup_range` and `identities` as they do for HTML. For example, a docx render of an extension that stamps `author=`/`date=` onto editorial marks now gets the blamed author and date in `w:author`/`w:date` on `<w:ins>`, `<w:del>` and `<w:comment>`. Before, those fields were empty.

Filters at post-quarto and later run in a real pandoc subprocess, which has no `quarto.attribution`. They still can't read this data, and that is unchanged. PDF and revealjs are also unchanged. Nothing attribution-related is written into the non-HTML output itself.

Adds a stage test that docx, pptx and typst populate the attribution sidecar.

title: Canonicalize to plain paths on Windows
description:
On Windows, q2 hands verbatim `\\?\C:\…` paths to users. Run from a normal directory with a relative argument, `q2 render --json-errors` puts them in `notebook_path` and `source_file`, the status line reads `Rendering single file: \\?\C:\…`, and project scripts get the same form in `QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR`. The cause is `std::fs::canonicalize`, which always returns the verbatim form on Windows.

The shared `quarto_system_runtime::canonicalize` from the PR below now calls `dunce::canonicalize` on native targets. It returns the plain `C:\…` form when that names the same file, and keeps `\\?\` where it would not: paths longer than `MAX_PATH`, reserved names, network shares. Off Windows, `dunce::canonicalize` is `std::fs::canonicalize`, and the wasm32 body stays std. Since the PR below routed every site that emits or compares a canonical path through this function, they all change spelling together.

One limit remains. When a path past `MAX_PATH` is involved, two paths canonicalized separately can come back in different spellings (plain and `\\?\`), and a prefix comparison between them fails. A declared resource that deep under a short project is reported as outside the project. The reverse also happens: rendering a long input path keeps the discovered project root verbatim, so even a short resource like `data.txt` at that root is rejected. Before, both were verbatim. Fixing it touches about 40 comparison sites, so it is tracked as a follow-up.

Before, on Windows from a plain scratch directory:

```
{"notebook_path":"\\?\C:\…\probe\broken.ipynb"}
{"source_file":"\\?\C:\…\probe\broken.ipynb"}
Rendering single file: \\?\C:\…\probe\ok.qmd
```

After:

```
{"notebook_path":"C:\…\probe\broken.ipynb"}
{"source_file":"C:\…\probe\broken.ipynb"}
Rendering single file: C:\…\probe\ok.qmd
```

This also turns `json_errors::ipynb_parse_error_json_carries_cell_origin` from #743 green on Windows. CI has no Windows leg and the change is a no-op elsewhere, so Linux and macOS CI cannot catch a regression here; the Windows runs below are the check.

## Extension paths outside the project

The switch exposed an older defect: the `orange-book-margin` typst smoke test passes on main and failed on this branch. The built-in orange-book extension is extracted to a temp dir, and `adjust_paths_to_document_dir` rebased its `filters` entry onto the document dir with `pathdiff`, giving a `..` chain from the project up to the user dir and back down into temp. `resolve_filter_path` joins that onto the document dir without normalizing, and the 260-character result fails Lua `io.open`. On main the document dir is verbatim while the temp dir is plain, so `diff_paths` meets two different prefixes and returns the absolute path by accident. Linux and macOS build the same `..` chain and only get away with it because they have no `MAX_PATH`.

`adjust_paths_to_document_dir` now takes the project root and keeps the absolute path for every `Path` value that resolves outside the project, nested values included, as `rebase_candidate` already does for fragment paths. The joined path is normalized lexically before the boundary check, so a declaration that escapes the project with `..` counts as outside. Values inside the project stay document-relative.

`css` and `theme` get no exception. At this point both are filesystem paths: theme reads normalize the path, and the css href is derived later from the resolved source. `FormatCssTransform` emitted an outside-project css entry verbatim, so an in-tree extension declaring `css: ../../../shared.css` would have produced a `C:/…` href. That branch now links the source relative to the page. The file itself is still not copied into the output, the same as Quarto 1.

## Test Plan

- [x] New tests fail on Windows before the switch with a `\\?\` value and pass after: `json_errors::source_file_json_is_a_plain_path`, `render_cli_e2e::single_file_status_line_shows_a_plain_path`, `render_scripts_cli::project_dir_env_is_a_plain_path`. Their expected side comes from `dunce::simplified` on the temp path, not from the function under test.
- [x] `canonical.rs` contract tests: on Windows a short path comes back plain and a path over `MAX_PATH` stays verbatim; elsewhere the result matches `std::fs::canonicalize`
- [x] `json_errors::ipynb_parse_error_json_carries_cell_origin` passes on Windows
- [x] `adjust_paths_outside_document_tree_does_not_produce_dotdot`, `adjust_paths_outside_project_keeps_every_form_absolute` (theme as string, list and `{light, dark}`, css) and `adjust_paths_escaping_declaration_is_outside_project` fail before the rebase change and pass after; `adjust_paths_inside_document_tree_stays_relative` passes on both
- [x] `extension_css_outside_project_links_page_relative`; `theme_rebase_outside_project_loads_from_deep_document_dir` loads the theme from a deep document dir
- [x] Windows, the same six crate suites as the PR below: same results. `quarto-core` re-run after the extension change: only the existing Windows failures
- [x] `SMOKE_FILTER=orange-book-margin cargo nextest run -p quarto -E 'test(smoke_all)'` on Windows at the branch tip: passes (it failed before the rebase change)
- [x] `cargo build --workspace` on Windows at the branch tip; `cargo check -p quarto-system-runtime --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passes
- [ ] Linux and macOS CI

title: Route canonical paths through one shared function
description:
Prepares the switch to plain Windows paths in the PR stacked on top of this one. On Windows, `std::fs::canonicalize` returns the verbatim `\\?\C:\…` form, and q2 canonicalizes in about 60 production call sites, most of them directly rather than through `SystemRuntime::canonicalize`. Changing the spelling in the runtime alone leaves plain and verbatim paths meeting in comparisons, prefix strips and map keys. A prototype of that switch failed about 130 tests on Windows and hid a product bug: `resources:` declared for a single-file preview dropped out of its dependency set.

The shared function added here still calls `std::fs::canonicalize`, so no path spelling changes in this PR. The one behavior change is the overwrite guard below.

## Shared canonicalize

`quarto_system_runtime::canonicalize` and `canonicalize_deepest_existing` (moved from `output_sink.rs`, for planned outputs that do not exist yet) are now the one place q2 canonicalizes, and `NativeRuntime::canonicalize` delegates to the former. Both are exported on every target. On wasm32 the body is `std::fs::canonicalize`, which is what the routed sites called before, so the WASM build does not change. `quarto-hub` gains the `quarto-system-runtime` dependency to reach it. The name and location are a small API decision in a foundation crate, open to review.

## Audited call sites

Each production `canonicalize` call in the crates linked into `q2` was classified by following its result to its consumers. A site is routed when the result is emitted, or compared, joined, prefix-stripped or used as a map key against a path from another source. A site whose comparisons only involve its own output is left as it is. The table, with the reason per site, is in `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-29-windows-plain-canonical-paths.md`. Two real splits it found: book chapter seed keys built with std while `DocumentInfo.input` comes from the runtime, and include cycle detection seeded from the runtime but probing std paths. The project-render cache in the `quarto-test` runner is routed too: its map keys are canonicalized render inputs and its lookups use the routed path of the test file, so std keys would stop matching once the spelling changes.

Tests that check which file a path names now canonicalize both sides through the shared function, so they hold under either spelling. Tests that pin what q2 emits (`QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR`) still compare the exact string.

## Overwrite guard

The guard in `render_to_file.rs` refused an `--output` equal to the input only lexically. `q2 render doc.qmd --output sub/../doc.qmd` passed it on every OS and replaced `doc.qmd` with the rendered HTML. On Windows, the plain spelling of the (verbatim) canonicalized input did the same. The guard now also compares the canonical forms of both paths through the runtime, and keeps the lexical check for runtimes that cannot canonicalize.

## Test Plan

- [x] `render_cli_e2e::output_via_dotdot_spelling_of_input_refuses_and_preserves_source` (every OS) and `output_via_plain_spelling_of_input_refuses_and_preserves_source` (Windows) fail before the guard fix and pass after
- [x] Windows, `quarto`, `quarto-system-runtime`, `quarto-core`, `quarto-hub`, `quarto-preview` and `quarto-test` suites: same results as on the unchanged branch
- [x] Same six crates with the shared function temporarily switched to plain paths: same results, `single_file_deps_resources_glob` fixed
- [x] `cargo check -p quarto-system-runtime --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
- [ ] Linux and macOS CI, including the hub-client WASM build that compiles the routed `quarto-core` modules

title: Rework json_errors ipynb tests around Windows verbatim paths
description:
On Windows, `json_errors::ipynb_diagnostic_hyperlinks_real_notebook` fails. The product emits a correct `file:///C:/.../broken.ipynb` link, but the test builds its expected URL as `file://` plus the display of a `std::fs::canonicalize`d path, which on Windows is the verbatim `\\?\C:\...` form. On Linux and macOS the two strings happen to agree.

The same investigation found that the verbatim form does reach wire output: run from a plain cwd, `q2 render --json-errors` emits `\\?\C:\...` in `notebook_path` and `source_file`. The existing `notebook_path` check, `ends_with("broken.ipynb")`, accepts that.

## Tests

The hyperlink test now parses the OSC 8 target as a URL, requires a `file:` URL with no fragment, and resolves it back to the notebook with `Url::to_file_path`. The comparison is path to path, so it no longer depends on how each platform displays a canonical path.

`ipynb_parse_error_json_carries_cell_origin` now requires `notebook_path` to be absolute, free of the `\\?\` prefix, and to name the real notebook. `dunce` is added as a dev-dependency to check that the fixture path has a plain form at all, so the assertion cannot fail because of the machine's TEMP location.

> [!NOTE]
> On Windows, `ipynb_parse_error_json_carries_cell_origin` fails by design until the wire-path fix lands (`notebook_path must be a plain path, got: \\?\C:\...`). That fix is #760 (canonicalize to plain paths), stacked on #759 (route canonical paths through one shared function), which sits on top of this one. CI has no Windows leg, so CI is unaffected. This PR stays a draft so the three merge together.

## Test Plan

- [x] `cargo nextest run -p quarto -E 'test(json_errors::)'` on Windows: 14 pass, 1 intended failure (above)
- [x] Hyperlink assertion fed a verbatim-path URL, a URL with a fragment, the wrong file, and the pseudo-path fails on each; the correct target passes
- [x] `cargo build --workspace` on Windows
- [ ] Linux and macOS CI green

title: Keep the `.cell` wrapper around knitr floats so Typst doesn't double-wrap tables
description:
A captioned table produced by a knitr chunk (for example `knitr::kable()` with `#| label: tbl-…` and `#| tbl-cap:`) rendered to Typst as

```
#figure([
#block[
#table(
```

The extra `#block[` between `#figure([` and `#table(` is the shape Quarto's issue 10086 fix removes.

The cause was in q2's float desugaring. A `.cell #tbl-…` div was turned into a `FloatRefTarget` with the `.cell` div discarded. Quarto's Typst post filter only marks `cell-output-display` as scaffolding, so it disappears from the output, when it sits under a `.cell` parent. Without that parent, the div reached Pandoc's Typst writer and came out as a block.

q2 now keeps the `.cell` div around the float and leaves only the `cell-output-display` divs inside it, as Quarto's `parsefiguredivs.lua` does for non-layout cells. Layout cells and cells with no output div are unchanged.

The same knitr table now produces `#figure([` followed directly by `#table(`, matching Quarto. `typst/tbl-align-issue10086.qmd` is ported from Quarto's smoke-all corpus with its two assertions. The first requires that shape, and the second rejects a block wrapped around the whole figure.

q2's output for this fixture was centered before and after, so the rendered PDF is unchanged. The fix guards against the double-wrapped `#block[ #figure([ #block[` shape, which left-aligns the figure in Quarto when the scaffold rule fails to match. Because the `.cell` div is back, that shape would now reappear if the scaffold rule stopped matching. The second assertion covers that case.

Not addressed: for `echo: true` chunks using the `#| label:` shorthand, the code listing is still placed inside the figure, where Quarto puts it above.

title: Keep the local-prod proxy alive when a proxied connection is reset
description:
`scripts/local-prod-server.mjs` bridged upgraded WebSocket connections between the browser and the hub with a bare `pipe` in each direction and no error handling on either socket. If one side was reset (a tab closing abruptly is enough), Node threw the resulting `ECONNRESET` as an unhandled `'error'` event and the entire proxy process exited. Every other connection through it then failed with `ECONNREFUSED`.

That is what took down the Hub-Client E2E run on #770. After the two-tab scenario in `author-attribution.spec.ts` the proxy on `:3999` died, and the next test, the auth-on legacy doc, couldn't connect at all.

A reset now tears down only the connection pair it happened on. Closing either socket closes the other, and an error on either is swallowed rather than thrown. A client that disconnects before the hub answers the upgrade also cancels the upstream request. The plain HTTP path gets the same treatment. If the hub fails after headers are sent, the proxy destroys the response instead of throwing from a second `writeHead`. A client that goes away mid-request cancels the upstream request.

`scripts/local-prod-server.test.mjs` starts the real server in front of a fake hub, upgrades a WebSocket, resets it from the client side and from the hub side, and checks that the proxy process is still alive and still serving requests. Both cases fail without the change. Note that `scripts/*.test.mjs` isn't run by any CI job; run it with `npx vitest run scripts/`.

title: Make `citeproc: true` and post-position `citeproc` work on Pandoc-hybrid formats
description:
`citeproc: true` did nothing for Typst. Q2's citeproc filter only ran when `"citeproc"` appeared in `filters`, and nothing translated the boolean into that list. Citations passed through as `Cite` nodes to pandoc's native Typst writer, which printed `@key` plus a `#bibliography()` call, exactly as if citeproc were off.

Separately, `filters: [quarto, citeproc]` was silently ignored on Pandoc-hybrid formats. Citeproc lands in the post group there, and the hybrid leg drops post-position filters because it forwards them to `main.lua`'s entry points. Citeproc is Q2's own filter and has no such entry point, so it was discarded. That affects docx and the other hybrid formats too, not just Typst.

Now:

- `citeproc: true` on a Pandoc-hybrid format adds citeproc after the `quarto` sentinel, so it runs after crossrefs resolve. An explicit `citeproc` in `filters` takes precedence.
- Post-position `citeproc` runs on hybrid targets.
- When citeproc resolved the citations, Typst is written as `typst-citations` (as Q1 does). The writer then prints the resolved text, and no native `#bibliography()` is emitted alongside citeproc's own `<refs>` div.

Unchanged: `citation-location: margin` documents (the Lua margin handler owns citation rendering), book chapters (citeproc stays deferred to the merged document), and HTML.

Known gap: citeproc doesn't add year suffixes (`1951a`/`1951b`) or render multi-citation groups correctly. That is in `quarto-citeproc`, reproduces on HTML, and is separate from this change.

title: Typst: syntax highlighting via Skylighting
description:
Typst output has been using pandoc's `idiomatic` mode: code blocks are emitted as plain fenced blocks and highlighted by Typst's own `raw` highlighter at compile time. Quarto's Skylighting mode, which is Quarto 1's default, was only reachable by passing `highlight-style` through pandoc's deprecated flag. `syntax-highlighting:` was ignored, there was no default style, `.theme` files didn't work, and brand `monospace-block` backgrounds had nothing to apply to.

Now:

- Typst renders with Skylighting by default, using the `arrow` palette like Quarto 1.
- `syntax-highlighting:` (and `highlight-style:` as its alias) accept any bundled palette, a `.theme` file path relative to the document, `none`, or `idiomatic`. Bare adaptive names such as `arrow` or `github` follow the document's `brand-mode`, since Typst has no dark mode of its own.
- Code blocks come out full-width with padding and rounded corners. Pandoc's own definitions draw a bare `block(fill: …)`, and Quarto 1 patches that afterwards with a regex. Here the `highlighting-definitions` block is generated from the vendored `.theme` palettes and handed to pandoc, so nothing patches the output.
- A brand's `monospace-block` background replaces the palette background. Without one, the palette's own background is used.
- `code-line-numbers: true` now produces numbered Skylighting blocks.

The generated token functions match pandoc's output for every bundled palette. The one difference: palettes that give their canvas colour in `editor-colors` now get a background, where pandoc drops it.

The thirteen `syntax-highlighting` smoke-all fixtures from Quarto 1 are added and pass. I added `brand: _brand.yml` to the six `brand-monospace-*` ones, because Quarto 2 doesn't auto-discover a `_brand.yml` and warns if it isn't referenced.

title: Include in-text citations in same-author/year disambiguation
description:
When two different references share an author and year, citeproc is supposed to tell them apart with year suffixes ("1951a", "1951b"). That didn't happen if one of them was cited in text:

```
As shown [@first], and @second also says so.
```

rendered `(Cronbach 1951)` and `Cronbach (1951)`, and both bibliography entries showed a bare "1951".

Disambiguation renders every cite, groups them by their text, and suffixes any group that spans more than one reference. It only considers "normal" cites, so cites tagged author-only are left out; that's right for a real author-only fragment, which renders just the name. But a lone in-text `@id` is also tagged author-only, even though the engine renders it as the full "Name (year)". It was dropped from the comparison, the other cite looked unique, and nothing was flagged.

A lone in-text cite whose style has a separable names element, and which therefore renders the full "Name (year)", is now tagged as a normal cite and takes part in disambiguation. The example above now renders `(Cronbach 1951a)` and `Cronbach (1951b)`, with matching bibliography entries. Genuine author-only items keep their tag.

Tests: an engine-level test for the in-text case plus a two-item-cluster regression test, and a pampa end-to-end render of the example above, which fails without the engine change.

title: Replace the missing juice.ts with an in-process CSS inliner for raw HTML tables
description:
gt and pandas tables arrive as raw HTML with their styling in a `<style>` block. Q1 ran them through `juice` before converting them for Typst, so the rules landed on the cells. In q2 that step pointed at a `juice.ts` that doesn't exist, so it always failed quietly and the table went through unstyled. Alignment, borders, header size and weight, and the stub column styling were all dropped. Only styles already inline on the element survived, such as `data_color` fills.

This keeps the same step but runs it differently: a hidden `q2 inline-css` subcommand built on the `css-inline` crate, which `normalize/astpipeline.lua` now pipes raw tables through for Typst. Remote stylesheets are never fetched. For an R gt table the Typst output is now byte-identical to Q1's.

The filters run in the real `pandoc` process, so they reach the CLI through the `quarto-cli-path` param that `init.lua` already reads. `q2` registers its own path at startup. In-process callers such as the smoke-all harness leave it unset, and the filter then skips inlining instead of piping to an executable that isn't `q2`.

Long data URIs are no longer swapped for placeholders, because nothing size-limited sits in the path anymore. The regression test from #763 still covers that.

Tests: unit tests for the inliner, CLI tests checking that class rules from a `<style>` block reach a Typst cell and that the subcommand filters stdin to stdout, and a params test for when `quarto-cli-path` is emitted.

title: Disambiguate same-author, same-year citations when one is in-text or nested
description:
When two different references share an author and year, citeproc is supposed to tell them apart with year suffixes ("1951a", "1951b"). That didn't happen if one of them was cited in text:

```
As shown [@first], and @second also says so.
```

rendered `(Cronbach 1951)` and `Cronbach (1951)`, and both bibliography entries showed a bare "1951".

Disambiguation renders every cite, groups them by their text, and suffixes any group that spans more than one reference. It only considers "normal" cites, so cites tagged author-only are left out; that's right for a real author-only fragment, which renders just the name. But a lone in-text `@id` is also tagged author-only, even though the engine renders it as the full "Name (year)". It was dropped from the comparison, the other cite looked unique, and nothing was flagged.

A lone in-text cite whose style has a separable names element, and which therefore renders the full "Name (year)", is now tagged as a normal cite and takes part in disambiguation. The example above now renders `(Cronbach 1951a)` and `Cronbach (1951b)`, with matching bibliography entries. Genuine author-only items keep their tag.

Tests: an engine-level test for the in-text case plus a two-item-cluster regression test, and a pampa end-to-end render of the example above, which fails without the engine change.

title: Transition quarto-hub from stable actor IDs to automerge author IDs
description:
## Why

Two browser tabs of one user shared one stable actor ID. Concurrent edits from that actor wedge the document with a `duplicate seq` error (bd-6f21d4c6). Automerge 3.5.0 gives attribution its own field, so the actor ID can be random per document session.

## What changes

- The hub mints per-project author IDs at `GET /auth/author`. The mint uses the same HMAC as before, so each user's attribution key does not change.
- The sync client stops choosing actor IDs. It stamps the author ID on each document, and automerge picks a random actor per session.
- Attribution readers resolve `change.author ?? getAuthorForActor(...) ?? change.actor`. Documents written before this change keep their credit through the actor fallback.
- Hub-server writes stay authorless on purpose, and new tests pin that.
- `quarto-hub-mcp` fetches the author ID over the Bearer path, so bot edits carry the signed-in user's credit.
- A new end-to-end suite proves the behavior against a real authenticated hub.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify`: all 14 steps green (15332 Rust tests, plus 1264 unit, 143 integration, and 153 wasm hub-client tests).
- New Playwright suite, 4/4 pass on repeat runs: two-user attribution and "me" highlight, the two-tab collision as a negative test, auth-disabled parity, and legacy-document continuity.

## Not in this change

- bd-6f21d4c6 stays open until the capture plan completes or Gordon waives the specimen.
- Removal of the old `/auth/actor` endpoint and the duplicate-seq self-heal: bd-8oyidg7h, bd-lh7e13o5.
- H1 and H2 defect dispositions: bd-bks7az35, bd-w7x5ajsv.

Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-30-automerge-author-id-transition.md` (epic bd-o1yn1fqy).

title: Fix `{{< placeholder >}}` (and other Lua shortcodes) producing an empty image src
description: \`![alt]({{< placeholder 200 >}})\` rendered with \`src=""\` in every format. In Typst that became \`image("")\`, which fails the compile with \`failed to load file (is a directory)\`. It showed up as a hard failure with seven placeholders in a \`layout=\` panel, but a single placeholder was already broken, and in HTML it silently gave an \`\`. Shortcodes inside plain-text fields (link and image targets, attribute values, code text) were called with the \`"inline"\` context. The \`placeholder\` shortcode returns a \`pandoc.Image\` in that context and a data-URI string only in \`"text"\` context, so flattening its result to text produced the image's empty alt text. Text-field expansion now passes the \`"text"\` context, as Q1 does. Built-in shortcode handlers treat it the same as inline, so their output is unchanged. With this, each placeholder expands to a data URI. The existing mediabag handling then writes it once and all seven references in the \`.typ\` point at the same file. Adds an integration test for a Lua shortcode in an image src, and ports Q1's \`fraction-layout\` fixture into smoke-all. Q1's own output for that fixture is \`columns: (1fr, 2fr, 2fr, 1fr, 3fr, 1fr, 1fr)\`, so the fixture's regex now matches that instead of the stale \`9.1fr, 18.2fr, …\`. Not covered: nested shortcode arguments in a text field still resolve with the inline context, and the include-slot metadata expansion now also uses the text context without a Q1 comparison.

title: Forward `css-property-processing` to the Typst filter params
description:
Setting `css-property-processing: none` for Typst output had no effect. Borders, colours and vertical-align on raw HTML tables were still translated to Typst, exactly as with the default `translate`.

The translation is done by Quarto 1's `typst-css-property-processing.lua`, which skips itself unless `param('css-property-processing', 'translate')` is `translate`. We never put that key into the filter-params blob, so the filter always saw its own default and the option could never be turned off.

`TypstFilterParamsContributor` now carries the document's `css-property-processing` value and forwards it alongside `brand-mode` and the other Typst params. With `none`, raw HTML table cells are left untranslated (`[B]` rather than `#set text(fill: rgb(255, 0, 255)); B`). `translate` and the unset default behave as before.

I added Quarto 1's three `css-property-processing` smoke-all fixtures (`none`, `default`, `translate`) to the `quarto` smoke-all suite.

title: Fix leaked placeholder UUID in raw HTML tables with data-URI images
description: Raw HTML tables containing base64 `` tags longer than 2000 characters failed to compile to Typst with `file not found (searched at …/273dae7e-3633-4385-9b0c-203d2d7a2d37)`. Before handing table HTML to `juice.ts` for CSS inlining, `juice()` replaces long data-URIs with a placeholder UUID so the script doesn't truncate them, then swaps the real URIs back afterwards. q2 doesn't ship `juice.ts`, so that call always fails, and the fallback returned the placeholder-substituted HTML, leaving the UUID as the image `src`. Shorter images were never substituted, so a table with one short and one long image came out half-working. `juice()` now restores the data-URIs whether or not the script ran. Both images are extracted to the mediabag and referenced by their content-hash paths, matching what Q1 produces for its `juice/test.qmd` smoke fixture. A regression test renders a table with one short and one long data-URI image to Typst and checks that both land in the mediabag and no placeholder appears. CSS inlining for raw HTML tables is still skipped in q2; this only stops the fallback from corrupting the output. Porting it is tracked separately.

title: Diagnose every misordered attribute list, with the fix written out from your own text
description:
Pandoc and Quarto 1 accept the parts of an attribute list in any order: `{k=v .c #i}` is fine. Quarto 2 requires one order: identifier, then classes, then key-value pairs. The strictness is deliberate and the grammar stays as it is, but the strictness breaks documents that Quarto 1 renders without complaint. A deliberate break like this should tell authors exactly what to change.

Until now only one of the three possible inversions did. `{k=v .c}` reported Q-2-3, while `{.c #i}` and `{k=v #i}` failed with the generic "Parse error / unexpected character or token here", in every construct that takes an attribute list.

Two new diagnostics close the gap:

- `Q-2-55`: identifier after a class (`{.c #i}`)
- `Q-2-56`: identifier after a key-value pair (`{k=v #i}`)

Two entries are enough for every construct (spans, images, inline code, the four editorial spans, headings, fenced divs, editorial divs, fenced code blocks, table cells). They all go through the same grammar productions and reach the same two parser states.

Each ordering diagnostic (Q-2-3, Q-2-55, Q-2-56) also carries a hint that rewrites the author's own list in the accepted order. `::: {.callout-tip #tip-alignment}` gets "Reorder the attributes as `{#tip-alignment .callout-tip}`". Quoted values pass through intact, and the whole list is reordered at once. A list with two identifiers (`{#a #b}`) fails in the same parser state as `{k=v #i}`, but reordering cannot fix it, so it keeps the generic error rather than a wrong suggestion. Hints come from a new `suggestion` field on corpus entries, which other diagnostics can use.

`qmd-syntax-helper`'s `attribute-ordering` rule recognises all three codes (by code, not title) and fixes a list that draws several diagnostics once rather than once per diagnostic.

A table-driven test runs each inversion through every construct, so a grammar change that splits one of these parser states fails there instead of shipping an uncoded error.

title: Use canonical float types for Q1 category lookup
description:
Q1 uses `FloatRefTarget.type` as a key to look up a canonical cross-reference category. The Pandoc shim was passing the localized display label instead, so a Spanish figure’s `Figura` label caused an `unknown float type 'Figura'` error.

The shim now maps the stable wire `ref_type` to Q1’s category and passes its canonical name as `float.type`. Localized title parameters still control the caption text, keeping category lookup separate from display localization.

Add a Spanish DOCX regression test that exercises the localized wire value and checks the rendered caption.

Focused verification: `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core --test integration test_localized_float_kind_is_accepted_by_q1_renderer` (1 passed). Broader coverage is delegated to PR CI.

title: Make brand.yml `source: file` fonts available to Typst
description:
A brand declaring `source: file` fonts had no effect on Typst output. Typst was never told where the font files live, so any reference to the family printed `unknown font family` and fell back to a default face.

Each `source: file` font's containing directory is now passed to Typst as a `--font-path`. Paths resolve against the brand's own directory (the project root for an inline `brand:` block) and come after the document's `font-paths:` entries. Like Quarto 1, this reads the resolved brand's typography only, and doesn't vary with `brand-mode`.

The same path set goes to both `typst compile` and the `typst fonts` discovery run that feeds the CSS font-fallback filter, so the two can't disagree about which fonts exist. It's a sibling of `with_google_font_cache`, and the two compose over the same base `resolve_font_paths` result.

Adds the `typst/font-paths/brand-font-paths` smoke-all fixture (brand with a bundled `Amaranth-Regular.ttf`, asserting no `unknown font family` warning); it fails without this change.

This stacks on #752 and should be retargeted to `main` once that merges.

title: Download `source: google` brand fonts for Typst output
description:
Brand fonts declared with `source: google` were never available to Typst. Typst only uses fonts that exist as files on its `--font-path`, so a brand like `typography.fonts: [{family: Fira Code, source: google}]` rendered with a fallback font. Typst printed `warning: unknown font family: fira code` and nothing else. HTML output wasn't affected, because the browser follows the `@import`.

When rendering to Typst, Quarto now requests the same Google Fonts CSS that the HTML path uses. It reads the font file URLs from the `@font-face` rules and downloads the TrueType/OpenType files into `<project>/.quarto/typst/fonts`, the same cache location Q1 uses. That directory is passed to both `typst fonts` and `typst compile`. Files already in the cache aren't downloaded again; only the small CSS request repeats on each render.

Q1 finds the URLs by scanning the CSS line by line with a regex. This version parses the CSS with `cssparser`, which was already in the lockfile through `scraper` and `selectors`. It also handles minified CSS, comments, quoted URLs, and `local()` entries whose names contain commas.

Nothing here fails the render. If the machine is offline, the family is misspelled, Google only offers woff2 (which Typst can't load), or the font is `source: bunny`, the render continues with a fallback font and a `Q-21-4` warning. The warning explains the cause and suggests `source: file`. `Q-21-4` has a docs page and a sidebar entry.

Google serves TTF to requests without a browser User-Agent, and the runtime's `fetch_url` sends none. The code doc comment records that dependency, and a woff2-only response produces the warning above.

Known limit: Google font files are downloaded at render time. There's no vendored fallback.

Closes bd-mzrgikmu.

title: Warn when a Q1-style brand file exists but no brand: key references it (bd-yl1bpj82)
description:
## Summary
- Quarto 1 auto-discovers `_brand.yml`, `_brand.yaml`, `_brand/_brand.yml`, `_brand/_brand.yaml` when no `brand:` is set. Q2 deliberately does not (settled 2026-07-27), so Q1 projects silently lost their brand. This adds warning **Q-5-37** instead of implicit discovery.
- Checked per document in `MetadataMergeStage` on merged metadata, so `brand:` from `_quarto.yml`, a profile, `_metadata.yml` or front matter all count. Suppressible with `diagnostics: { Q-5-37: off }`; native-only. `q2 render` collapses the per-page warnings into one group listing affected documents.
- `q2 use brand` now refuses an existing `_brand/` candidate.
- qmd-syntax-helper: opt-in `q-5-37` autofix appends `brand: <file>` to the enclosing `_quarto.yml` (Q1's last-existing-wins order).
- Docs page `docs/errors/project/Q-5-37.qmd`; plan in `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-30-warn-unreferenced-brand.md`.

## Test plan
- [x] Per-crate nextest: quarto-core, quarto, qmd-syntax-helper, quarto-error-catalog — 6170 passed, 38 skipped
- [x] `cargo clippy -D warnings` on quarto-core, quarto, qmd-syntax-helper
- [ ] Workspace-wide nextest not run before push; left to CI
- [ ] `q2 preview` not manually checked (shares the per-document pipeline)

Closes bd-yl1bpj82.

title: Keep unsupported definition-list text visible
description:
## What was broken

Pandoc definition-list syntax (`Term` followed by `: definition`) was parsed as table captions and discarded when no table preceded it. This silently removed definitions; nested-list bodies could also leave their remaining items orphaned from the definition.

## What changes

No-table caption lines now remain as literal text. Likely definition-list syntax following a paragraph or plain block receives Q-2-54 with guidance for the supported `::: {.definition-list}` form and the existing `qmd-syntax-helper convert -r definition-lists` migration. Nested-list definition bodies are kept literal rather than emitted as a detached structured list. Ordinary standalone captions retain the generic warning, and valid table captions are unchanged.

Adds a Q-2-54 reference page documenting the unsupported syntax and migration paths.

## Verification

- Pampa nextest: 4,877 passed, 2 skipped.
- Focused caption and definition-list regressions: 27 passed.
- `cargo check -p pampa` and `cargo clippy -p pampa --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-error-catalog`: 18 passed.
- `cargo xtask lint` passed.
- Rendered the supplied two-page repro: both pages rendered; definition lines remained visible with Q-2-54, and the link-reference control retained its Q-2-46 behavior.

title: Fix Typst brand.yml dark-mode and logo layout support
description:
Typst's `brand.yml` support had two independent gaps: the `logo` block was never wired into the filter pipeline, and dark-mode brands were never resolved at all. This PR fixes both, along with the follow-on issues each fix exposed, and ports the fixtures that pass once the fixes land.

## Logo layout

The vendored `typst-brand-yaml.lua` filter reads its logo configuration through `param('logo')`, but Q2 never populated that param — it was always nil, so the filter's entire logo translation (unit conversion, location-to-alignment mapping, padding shorthand, brand-image path resolution) was dead code. Raw metadata leaked through Pandoc's own template substitution instead, which crashed `typst compile` on unconverted units and otherwise left the logo box empty.

`build_logo_param` (`crates/quarto-core/src/pandoc_filters/typst_brand.rs`) builds that param now, mirroring Q1's `fillLogoPaths`/`resolveLogo` narrowed to what the Lua filter actually needs. Five reproductions are ported as regression tests under `crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all/typst/brand-yaml/logo/`.

## Dark mode

Two bugs compounded to make dark mode a no-op: `quarto_sass::resolve_brand` only ever resolved the light half of a split brand, and Q2 never set a `brand-mode` filter param at all, so the Lua filter's `param('brand-mode') or 'light'` always fell through to `'light'`. Fixing either one alone would have regressed documents that pass today only by accident — they happen to render acceptably on the light-content fallback.

`resolve_brand_variants` (`crates/quarto-sass/src/config.rs`) resolves both halves of a split brand, wired alongside a `brand-mode` param read straight off already-merged metadata. This also surfaced a latent bug in `build_logo_param`: its default brand-path lookup was hardcoded to `"light"` for both sides of a document's own `{light:, dark:}` logo spec, so the dark side would have silently defaulted to light brand data. It's mode-aware now. Two dark-mode logo fixtures land alongside this fix.

## Explicit-brand fixtures

Q2 doesn't auto-discover `_brand.yml` the way Q1 does — that's a deliberate design difference, not a bug — so several color and font-filtering fixtures that assumed implicit discovery were failing for a reason unrelated to the above. Given an explicit `brand: _brand.yml` key, they pass: `color/{exper,homedepot,posit}/brand-color.qmd`, `font-filtering/typst-font-filtering.qmd`, and `font-filtering-fallback/font-filtering-fallback.qmd` (the last needed `noErrors: true`, since it deliberately references nonexistent font names to exercise the all-unavailable fallback path, and typst legitimately warns about each one).

## Not included

`typography/kitchen-sink-1` and `font-filtering-generics` still fail even with an explicit brand key: both need a real Google-sourced font file actually available to typst at compile time, which requires font-fetching support that doesn't exist yet (bd-mzrgikmu). Also out of scope here: the implicit-brand-discovery diagnostic (bd-yl1bpj82, in progress elsewhere) and a stderr-classification gap that swallows some `quarto.log.warning` output in Pandoc-hybrid formats (bd-r6tcmzlz, filed separately).

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo clippy -p quarto-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` / `cargo clippy -p quarto-sass --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core` / `cargo nextest run -p quarto-sass`
- [x] `cargo nextest run --workspace`
- [x] `crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all/typst/brand-yaml/**` fixtures pass

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Wire font-paths metadata into Typst's --font-path resolution
description:
## Summary

Typst renders declare a `font-paths` metadata key for pointing at custom font files, but it was never actually read — `font_path_args()` only ever staged the vendored package-cache fonts directory. Any document, book, or project setting `font-paths:` for a locally-shipped font got a silent "unknown font family" warning from Typst and fell back to a substitute font instead.

`font-paths` now resolves the same way Quarto 1 did: a leading `/` is project-root-relative, everything else resolves against the document's own directory. Both the real `typst compile` invocation and the CSS font-fallback-filter discovery step (`typst fonts`) pick up the same resolved paths, so they can't drift out of sync with each other.

Two smoke-all fixtures are added covering the project-relative and document-relative cases.

Not covered by this change (confirmed still broken, tracked separately): brand.yml-declared local font files (`source: file`), extension-contributed `font-paths` (needs extension-relative resolution instead of document-relative), and brand.yml Google-sourced fonts (no fetch path exists yet).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy -p quarto-core -p quarto --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core` — 5316 passed
- [x] `cargo nextest run -p quarto` — 602 passed (includes `smoke_all`, covering the two new fixtures)
- [x] Reproduced the original warning against unpatched code, confirmed it clears with the fix, against Q1's own fixtures (`custom-fonts.qmd`, `font-paths/subdir-font-paths`, `relative-font-path/report1`)

title: Add ensurePdfMetadata test assertion for checking PDF document metadata
description:
Quarto's test harness could check a rendered PDF's *text content* (`ensurePdfRegexMatches`, `ensurePdfTextPositions`) but had no way to check its *document metadata* — Title, Author, Keywords, Creator, the fields PDF viewers and accessibility tools read from the Info dictionary. Any fixture that tried to assert on them failed immediately at spec-parse time with "Unknown assertion type," before rendering even started, because `parse_format_spec` only recognized a fixed allowlist of keys.

This mattered concretely: Typst sets these fields from a document's `title`/`author`/`keywords` metadata via `set document(...)` in the shared template, so a rendered PDF's metadata is observable, meaningful output — not an implementation detail. Q1 had a dedicated `ensurePdfMetadata` assertion for exactly this; Q2 had nothing, so fixtures ported from Q1 that checked it had to drop the check entirely or approximate it by grepping the generated Typst source instead of the compiled PDF.

`ensurePdfMetadata` now exists in Q2:

```yaml
_quarto:
  tests:
    typst:
      ensurePdfMetadata:
        title: "Test Document"
        author: "Alice Smith"
        keywords: [quarto, typst, testing]
        creator: "Typst"
```

Each field is a case-insensitive substring match against the PDF's actual Info dictionary value (matching Q1's semantics); `keywords` accepts a single string or an array, and every entry must be present. It reads the Info dictionary straight off the `lopdf`/`pdf-extract` `Document` the project already links for the other PDF assertions — no new dependency.

Closes bd-0syqvgl2.

title: Q-2-10: reword possessive-apostrophe note to neutral phrasing
description:
\`Q-2-10\` fires when a stray \`'\` gets read as a closing quote mark instead of a possessive apostrophe — most commonly something like \`users'\` in a heading or inline code title. The diagnostic's secondary note pointed at the mark and said "This is the opening quote," which is backwards for exactly the case that trips this code: there's no opening quote anywhere, that's the whole problem. Anyone hitting this on a plain possessive would read a note confidently misdescribing their own text.

The note now says "No opening quote was found before this mark. If you meant an apostrophe, escape it with a backslash." — accurate for the possessive case and still correct for the general "stray closing quote" case the code covers.

\`Q-2-7\` (unclosed quote at end of block) keeps its old "this is the opening quote" wording; that one really is describing an opening quote with no closer, so the phrase fits.

This doesn't change how the parser distinguishes an attached possessive from a detached stray quote — that question was already closed as Won't Fix, since both shapes hit the same parser state on the same token and there's no structural signal to tell them apart. This only fixes what the diagnostic says once it fires.

bd-hsb5fext

title: Bundle the Julia engine as a vendored extension subtree
description:
## Summary

q2 vendors `gordonwoodhull/quarto-julia-engine` as a `git subtree` and registers its `_extensions/` payload directly in the binary, so a `{julia}` cell resolves with zero `_extensions/` install — the same static, pass-1 resolution every other built-in engine gets. Three problems surfaced while wiring that payload in, and this PR fixes all three:

- **WASM's subtree loader had the wrong shape (F1).** It embedded the whole `extension-subtrees/` tree and pointed extension discovery at that directory itself; discovery expects a root whose *children* are extensions, so the first real payload would have silently found nothing. Fixed to embed and expose one `_extensions/` root per subtree, matching native. (This also fixes the same latent bug for `orange-book`, vendored on `main` after this branch diverged — it never got the WASM fix either.)
- **No diagnostic when Julia isn't installed (Q9).** A `{julia}` cell on a machine without Julia now fails with a dedicated Q-18-3 error and docs page, not a raw subprocess/engine-host error.
- **A hand-maintained julia fixture had drifted from upstream.** With the bundled copy now the source of truth for every test that touches the engine, the fixture is unreferenced and removed.

## Changes by phase

1. **Vendor** — `cargo xtask pull-extension-subtree julia-engine` pulls `gordonwoodhull/quarto-julia-engine@q2-static-declarations` (q2's upstream of record pending PumasAI#15 / quarto-cli#14936) into `resources/extension-subtrees/julia-engine/`.
2. **Register the payload, native + WASM** — `JULIA_ENGINE_SUBTREE` joins `EXTENSION_SUBTREE_PAYLOADS`; the WASM loader's per-subtree fix (F1, above) lands here too, verified against a real `wasm32-unknown-unknown` build via `cargo xtask verify`'s hub-client leg.
3. **Q9 diagnostic** — `Q-18-3` ("Engine Runtime Not Found"), its `docs/errors/` page, and its sidebar listing, fired from `TsEngine::ensure_loaded` (the earliest point that knows it's about to launch the julia engine and can fail before any subprocess spawns). The mapping is generic on `ExecutionError::RuntimeNotFound`, so knitr's and jupyter's own runtime-not-found errors also become coded diagnostics as a side effect.
4. **Wrap-up** — the hand-maintained fixture is deleted; `julia_engine_e2e.rs` already validates purely against the bundled copy (all seven J1–J7 rows pass live against real deno + julia).

## Explicitly out of scope

- The fork's `worker-busy-recovery` hardening (busy-worker forceclose recovery, PC4a) is **not** merged into `q2-static-declarations` and the bundled copy does not carry it. `PC4a` stays `#[ignore]`d/env-gated; revisit only if that scenario needs exercising against the bundled engine. J7 (failed-run leak check) passes live without this hardening, confirming plain upstream v0.2.2's close-on-failure fix is sufficient.
- Re-filing the static-declarations PR upstream to PumasAI — blocked on `quarto-cli#14936` reaching a stable release.
- `claims-files` `processor:` support beyond what Plan 7b already shipped.

## Test plan

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo nextest run --workspace` — 15317/15317 passed, 201 skipped, 0 failed
- `cargo xtask lint` — clean
- `cargo xtask verify` (ts-packages build, hub-client build including the WASM leg, hub-client tests) — all green

title: Add format: typst smoke-all testing (orange-book port) and fix 22 rendering bugs it found
description:
## Summary

`format: typst` had no smoke-all fixture coverage at all — Q2's Typst output was tested only by six hand-written Rust integration tests, a reduction of the real thing, not a verbatim exercise of it. This PR closes that gap by porting Quarto 1's richest numbering-correctness corpus into Q2's smoke-all suite: `orange-book`, `orange-book-lang`, `orange-book-margin`, `override-orange-book`, the 86-file `margin-layout` family, `marginalia-only-project`, and `pdf-text-position-test`. 

Two pieces of infrastructure make that port possible: a Typst/PDF assertion vocabulary (`ensureTypstFileRegexMatches`, `ensurePdfRegexMatches`) that reuses the existing two-array match/no-match shape, and `ensurePdfTextPositions` — a from-scratch walk of a tagged PDF's `/StructTreeRoot` that resolves marked-content ids to semantic roles and evaluates all eight of Q1's positional relations (`leftAligned`, `rightAligned`, `topAligned`, `bottomAligned`, `rightOf`, `leftOf`, `above`, `below`). 

The smoke-all harness itself also gained project-aware book rendering, since these fixtures are the first in the suite to need `render-project: true` semantics rather than independent per-file rendering.

The position predicate depends on a personal fork of `pdf-extract` (`gordonwoodhull/pdf-extract`, pinned by commit), because upstream doesn't expose what the predicate needs. Two changes live only in the fork so far:

- **Marked-content (MCID) surfacing** — upstream discards the marked-content ids a tagged PDF's content stream carries; the fork exposes them so they can be resolved against `/StructTreeRoot`.
- **A `/W`-array glyph-width fix** — Typst emits every glyph's width as a singleton range (`c_first == c_last`), which upstream's exclusive-range parsing silently drops to `/DW 0`, zeroing every glyph advance. The fork parses the singleton case correctly.

Both are narrow, self-contained fixes we'd like to contribute upstream; until that lands, the pin keeps them available to this repo.

Running Q1's real fixtures against Q2 surfaced 22 genuine bugs in production rendering code — gaps no synthetic test had exercised. Each is its own commit, preserved separately from the porting work above so it stands on its own record:

**Citeproc & bibliography**
- Book-merge resolved every citation before Typst's margin-citation filter ran, so `citation-location: margin` silently did nothing in books; skip the Rust-side resolution there and let the existing Lua handler do it on the merged document.
- Bare `@id` citations rendered fully parenthetical instead of Pandoc's author-in-text form — `evaluate_citation_to_output_impl` had no handling for `author_only` citations at all.
- A `@cite` nested inside a callout, custom crossref float, or theorem was invisible to citeproc, since citation collection never walked `Block::Custom`/`Inline::Custom` node slots.
- `typst.lua` discarded a citation's per-instance locator/prefix/suffix/author-suppression, since it only ever read citeproc's per-key bibliography entries, not its per-occurrence rendering.
- `quarto.doc.cite_method()` always saw `nil`, because Rust never emitted a `cite-method` filter param — so margin citations never took the citeproc branch even when `citeproc: true` was set.

**Crossref & numbering**
- A chapter-level `@sec-*` reference resolved only for HTML, because sec-target registration was wrongly bundled with an HTML-only gate meant for a different piece of state.
- Chapter-level `@sec-*` references rendered with the generic "Section" supplement instead of "Chapter"/"Appendix" — Q1's chapter/appendix prefix-swap logic had never been ported into the Typst shim.
- Knitr's own label echo, left over from re-injecting a label so knitr could see it, got promoted to a duplicate `FloatRefTarget` and collided with the real one under the same crossref id.
- The same echoed label, nested inside a table chunk's output, was miscounted as a subfloat, routing five margin-table fixtures through the wrong Typst rendering path.
- Nothing created `.quarto/` before a book chapter tried to write its crossref index there, so every chapter's write silently failed unless a stale directory happened to exist from a prior render.

**R/knitr engine**
- `PreEngineSugaringStage` lifted a code cell's crossref label onto the wrapping div for Q2's own numbering, but knitr never saw that label again, so it fell back to positional `unnamed-chunk-N` filenames instead of the label-derived ones authors expect.
- `column`/`cap-location` cell options landed only on a knitr chunk's inner `.cell` div, never reaching the ancestor float those classes need to be on.
- Stripping `label`/`fig-cap` before knitr ran also stripped the info knitr's own multi-panel (`fig-subcap`) numbering depends on, so every panel image came back unlabelled.

**Typst margin layout**
- `citation-location`/`reference-location` metadata never reached Typst's filter params at all, so margin citations and margin references silently did nothing.
- A margin figure or caption authored as a plain markdown image never registered as a margin float, because its `.column-margin`/`cap-location` classes live on the inner `Image`, not the auto-promoted `Figure`, and nothing merged them.
- An absolute `mediabag-dir` path, required because Pandoc's working directory isn't controlled, got double-rooted once handed to Typst's `image()`, which treats a leading `/` as already relative to `--root`.
- `<reftype>-cap-location`/`cap-location` cell options were silently dropped instead of being forwarded to the wrapping div, so non-default caption placement (e.g. "bottom") was ignored.
- Margin citations rendered correctly for a single document but not inside a merged book, for the same book-merge-ordering reason fixed above.

**Typst CLI, brand, and book output**
- A bare `--toc-depth` CLI flag isn't valid for Typst's writer (Pandoc caps it 1-6; Typst's outline has no such cap), and simply skipping the flag silently reset `toc-depth` to Pandoc's built-in default of 3 — because the vendored `typst.lua` reads it from `PANDOC_WRITER_OPTIONS`, which only reflects a real CLI flag or defaults file, never a bare `--metadata` value. Fixed by routing `toc-depth` through a Pandoc defaults file instead.
- Fixing that CLI-arg handling surfaced a brand `MetaString` type mismatch; guarding it also fixed named-logo image resolution and the book output-directory path base.

**Test harness & fixtures**
- `DocumentMetadata`'s default markdown parsing misread the smoke-test harness's own machine-facing assertion strings under `_quarto.tests.*` (e.g. bracket-label regexes read as HTML tags), producing about 110 false-positive warnings on the `orange-book` fixture; added a `_quarto.tests.**` entry to the metadata annotations table, the same mechanism `brand.**` already uses, to keep that subtree a plain string.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` at branch HEAD (pre-rebase): 15295 run, 15294 passed, 1 failed, 201 skipped (718.9s). The one failure is the pre-existing, separately-filed `bd-gak8uiza` gap (`{{< embed >}}` unimplemented, drops a figure in `orange-book-margin`) — not a regression.
- [x] Delta against `main` baseline (15188 run, 15188 passed, 201 skipped): +107 tests, 0->1 failed (the accepted gap above), skip count unchanged.
- [x] The six pre-existing Rust book-numbering integration tests still pass unmodified, confirmed individually via `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core`, coexisting with the new smoke-all fixtures as intended.
- [ ] Re-run `cargo nextest run --workspace` after the rebase onto current `main` (36 new upstream commits landed, none touching this epic's files) to reconfirm before merge.

title: Feature/files improvements
Force-reconnect the sync WebSocket on wake and network change
description:
## Problem

The sync WebSocket can die silently when the computer sleeps or the network changes. A half-open connection sends no close event, so neither side learns of the drop. The sync protocol sends no data while nothing changes, so no traffic shows the fault. The app stops receiving live updates until the user refreshes the page. The status badge also still shows "Online" over the dead connection, because the badge only changes on a close event.

## Fix

The WebSocket adapter now watches the two events that the browser can see:

- Wake from sleep: a 10 s timer compares the wall clock between ticks. A gap of more than 90 s means that the machine was suspended.
- Network changes: the window `online` event, and the `navigator.connection` `change` event (Chromium only).

When one of these events fires, the adapter closes the suspect socket and starts the usual reconnect path at once. Before this change, the adapter waited for the browser to close the dead connection, which can take up to a minute. The badge now goes Offline and back to Online, so it tells the truth.

There is no heartbeat, and no hub or protocol change. The reconnect uses the same code path as a hub restart. Known gap: a silent drop on an awake machine (for example a VPN idle timeout) still needs a refresh. The plan file lists the trade-offs: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-28-ws-wake-reconnect.md`.

## Tests

- 13 new tests: the adapter triggers, plus the full Offline → Online chain against a real in-process hub.
- `cargo xtask verify` (full) is green.
- Real-browser check: the badge went Offline then Online after a network event, with no page refresh.
- Remaining manual check: physical sleep and Wi-Fi toggle on a real machine (bd-sob0j19j).

title: hub-client: reset browser tab title when leaving a project
description:
## Summary

Closes #721.

The Editor set `document.title` to `file — project — Quarto Hub` while a project was open, but nothing restored the default when it unmounted, so the stale title persisted on the project selector (Safari, Chrome).

## Fix

New `useDocumentTitle` hook ([src/hooks/useDocumentTitle.ts](hub-client/src/hooks/useDocumentTitle.ts)): sets `document.title` while mounted and restores the default `Quarto Hub` (matching `index.html`) in its effect cleanup. Editor now computes the title string and delegates to the hook; in-project behavior is unchanged. Because the reset rides on Editor's unmount, it covers both UI variants (classic selector and collections home) and any future non-project view.

## Testing

- TDD: [useDocumentTitle.test.ts](hub-client/src/hooks/useDocumentTitle.test.ts) failed before the hook existed; now passes (set / update / reset-on-unmount).
- Full hub-client unit suite: 1246 tests green.
- `npm run build:all` succeeds; `npm run test:wasm` green (changelog render gate).
- Not verified in a live browser session; the reset is pinned by the unmount-cleanup unit test.

title: Bound html_element lexing: tag must start with a letter and cannot cross a blank line
description: Tracking: bd-html-element-runaway-k1eo50h8. Plan and measurements: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-28-html-element-runaway.md`. ## Problem A paragraph with `typescript-eslint (supports <6.1)`, a blank line, then a pipe table whose cell contains `` `--packagePath ` `` fails with Q-2-2 and a bare "Parse error", both located in the table row, hundreds of columns from the trigger. `parse_open_angle_brace` in the external scanner accepted any non-whitespace character after `<` and walked to the next `>` in the file, across newlines and blank lines, so `<6.1)` … `` lexed as one five-line `html_element` that ate the table header. ## Change (scanner only, no grammar regeneration) - **(A) Tag-start gate.** `html_element` only starts when the character after `<` is an ASCII letter, `/`, `?` or `#` (the `<#id>` anchor shorthand). `<6.1`, `<-`, `<=b`, `<5>` become literal text, matching pandoc and CommonMark. Autolinks keep their own predicate since a CommonMark email autolink may start with a digit. - **(B) Paragraph-bounded scan.** A candidate tag may span a newline (``, per bd-ly83qewg) but not a blank line; the scan stops there and `<` falls back to the bd-j9cf literal. This follows CommonMark rather than pandoc's markdown reader, which lets an inline tag cross a blank line. Naked HTML already warns (Q-2-9), so nothing supported is lost, and any residual mis-lex now stays inside the paragraph that caused it. - Once a `>` closes nothing, or the autolink reading dies with no tag possible, the scan stops instead of walking to EOF. ## Tests - `test/corpus/html-element-bounds.txt`: 7 behaviour cases (all failed on main) + 4 regression pins (``, ``, `<#sec-intro>`, `<1user@example.com>`). - `test_bare_lt_str.rs`: 11 pampa integration tests, including the reported document verbatim (OrderedList + Table, zero diagnostics). - `tree-sitter test` 830/830; full `cargo xtask verify` green; no `.snap` changed. ## Measurement `pampa --json-errors --no-prune-errors` over the 1459 `.md` files in `claude-notes/`: files parsing clean 730 → 741, zero regressions. The moved files contained `<100ms`, `<2GB`, Rust lifetimes `<'proj>` and similar. ## Docs One paragraph under "No naked HTML support" in `dev-docs/syntax-notes.md` stating both rules and the CommonMark-vs-pandoc divergence. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Isolate tree-sitter's compiled-grammar cache per checkout (bd-agsgrbfn)
description:
## Problem

The tree-sitter CLI caches compiled grammars at `$TREE_SITTER_LIBDIR/<grammar-name>.dylib`. When the variable is unset, it uses `~/.cache/tree-sitter/lib`. The cache key is only the grammar name (`markdown`), and a cached library counts as fresh when it is newer than `src/parser.c`. As a result, every q2 checkout on a machine shares one compiled grammar, and whichever checkout compiled most recently wins. When two rooms regenerate the parser close together, `cargo xtask verify` step 4 runs one checkout's grammar against the other checkout's corpus. We saw this happen: 9 false corpus failures in room-5, caused by room-2's grammar.

## Fix

- New xtask module `tree_sitter`. Every tree-sitter CLI run goes through `tree_sitter::command`, which sets `TREE_SITTER_LIBDIR` to `<root>/target/tree-sitter-lib`. It uses the literal `target/`, not `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, which can be shared across worktrees. It also overrides any value the caller has exported.
- `verify` step 4 uses it. The CRLF parity run gets a private cache directory inside its tempdir, so it always compiles fresh.
- New `cargo xtask ts-test [--grammar qmd|doctemplate] [--rebuild] [-- <tree-sitter test args>]` for hand runs. It runs `generate`, `build`, and `test`. AGENTS.md now points agents at it instead of bare `tree-sitter test`, and gives an `export` line for other hand runs.
- Adding the doctemplate corpus to `verify` is split out as bd-0njf3lab.

Plan and investigation: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-25-tree-sitter-libdir-isolation.md`

## Verification

- Unit tests for the helpers (`tree_sitter::tests`), written first.
- End-to-end, run with a scratch `HOME` so the shared `~/.cache` was never touched. I planted a grammar built from `206826fd6^` in the default cache:
  - a bare `tree-sitter test` failed 43 of 721 cases (the bug);
  - `cargo xtask ts-test` passed 721/721, even with `TREE_SITTER_LIBDIR` exported to the poisoned directory;
  - `verify` step 4 and the CRLF run each passed 721/721;
  - the planted library was left untouched.
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build --skip-hub-tests` on the rebased branch: all steps passed. Grammar tests passed 819/819 (LF and CRLF) and all 15,227 Rust tests passed. Hub-client WASM tests were skipped because the local WASM build is stale. This change is xtask-only.

title: Add book projects to Quarto 2 (ProjectKind::Book)
description:
## Summary

`ProjectKind::Book` previously dispatched to the `DefaultProjectType` stub and rendered
nothing book-specific. This PR gives it a real implementation across nine phases (P0-P8):
chapter-aware numbering, single-file merging for Typst/EPUB, project-wide cross-chapter
crossref and bibliography resolution for multi-file HTML, `q2 create`/hub scaffolding, a
usage guide, and book-aware preview.

It reuses two prior epics as much as possible - the website-projects epic's
sidebar/`ProjectType` machinery, and pandoc-writer-hybrid's single-document Typst/EPUB
renderer - and builds only the genuinely new pieces: chapter-local numbering, the
single-file chapter merge, and the multi-file cross-chapter registries.

The real, unpatched Q1 `orange-book` Typst extension is vendored as a git subtree
(`resources/extension-subtrees/orange-book/`, via `cargo xtask pull-extension-subtree
orange-book`) and used unmodified throughout.

## What's included, phase by phase

- **P0** - `@sec-` crossref targets and chapter-local numbering seed for headers.
- **P1** - foundations: `BookRenderItem`, sidebar translation from book config, `BookProjectType`.
- **P2/P2b/P2c** - single-file chapter merge for Typst/EPUB: each chapter runs the pipeline
  individually, then merges at the Pandoc level into one document before the shared
  single-document renderer takes over; cross-chapter links and deferred citeproc are
  handled post-merge.
- **P3** - wires the merge through to a real Typst/EPUB compile; proves part/chapter/appendix
  numbering and figure numbering survive it.
- **P4** - multi-file HTML books: each chapter renders as its own page, numbered from P0's
  seed, with book chrome (sidebar nav, cover image).
- **P5** - a project-wide crossref registry so a reference from one chapter to another
  resolves even though each chapter renders independently.
- **P6** - extends that aggregation to citations: one shared numbering and one merged
  bibliography across chapters.
- **P7** - the book usage guide, the `q2 create project book`/hub template, and removal of
  the "not yet supported" diagnostics.
- **P8** - book-aware `q2 preview`: chapter-scoped numbering and cross-chapter link
  resolution in preview, via a new pre-engine sweep.

## Known v1 limitations

- DOCX/PPTX/LaTeX book output: not implemented (LaTeX/PDF has no Pandoc-hybrid output in Q2
  at all yet, for any project type; DOCX/PPTX book output isn't a real feature upstream in
  Q1 either).
- Numeric citation styles renumber per chapter in multi-file HTML books - an inherited Q1
  bug, confirmed present in Q1's own code, not introduced here. Author-date styles are
  unaffected; single-file merge is unaffected.
- No incremental rebuilds for books; no cross-chapter bibliography preview or
  single-file-merge preview in P8.
- Per-chapter title-block metadata (subtitle, author affiliation, date, abstract) isn't
  ported; tracked separately as `bd-ock6cyiy`.
- Manuscript (`ProjectKind::Manuscript`) is untouched by this epic.

## Test coverage gap: orange-book is not yet ported to Q2's `smoke-all` harness

Q1's own test suite has a fixture family that is the deepest numbering-correctness corpus
it has - `tests/docs/smoke-all/typst/{orange-book,orange-book-lang,orange-book-margin,
override-orange-book}` - using Typst/PDF-specific assertion predicates
(`ensureTypstFileRegexMatches`, `ensurePdfRegexMatches`, and `ensurePdfTextPositions`, the
last of which reads the compiled PDF's tagged structure tree for layout assertions like
margin-note placement).

This PR does **not** port those fixtures verbatim into Q2's `crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all/`
harness. Instead, it used Q1's real compiled-PDF output as ground truth to write new,
reduced Rust integration tests (`book_numbering_torture.rs`, `book_appendix_letter_parity.rs`,
`book_part_appendix.rs`, `orange_book_lua.rs`) against the same real, unpatched extension.
The reduction is deliberate and documented in each test's own doc comment (e.g. image-based
figures instead of knitr cells, since Q2 can't execute those; bibliography/citations tested
separately), but it means:
- Q2's `smoke-all` harness has no `format: typst` fixtures at all yet, and no PDF-text or
  PDF-layout assertion predicates in its schema (`crates/quarto-test/src/spec.rs`).
- The `orange-book-margin` and `override-orange-book` variants aren't covered by Q2's tests
  at all.

A follow-on epic is being scoped to close this gap (extend the smoke-all harness with
PDF-text/PDF-structure assertions, add multi-file project-fixture support, and port the
four Q1 fixtures). Flagging here so this is a known, tracked gap rather than a silent one.

## Testing

`cargo check --workspace --all-targets` is clean. The full `cargo nextest run --workspace`
was kicked off before filing this PR and is still running locally as of this writing (this
branch also just absorbed 57 unrelated commits from a `main` rebase, so the pass/skip count
needs a fresh measurement rather than reusing an earlier phase's figure) - CI will confirm
the authoritative result; will report the local number here once it finishes.

## Closes

`bd-m1fzvpov`. Manuscript's still-unimplemented half is split out to `bd-q0wjtmbu`.

title: fix(jupyter): probe that jupyter runs in is_available, not just PATH presence
description:
When a machine has a `jupyter` executable that resolves on PATH but doesn't actually run — e.g. a stale tool-manager shim trampoline pointing at a deleted environment — `JupyterEngine::is_available()` reports available and jupyter-gated tests hard-fail instead of skipping. Surfaced on Windows by `jupyter_kernel_cleanup_e2e::render_leaves_no_kernel_behind`.

## Root Cause

`is_available()` was `self.jupyter_path.is_some()` — binary *presence* only, so a broken shim looked identical to a working install. Separately, the jupyter-gated test guards checked engine availability but not whether the specific kernelspec the fixtures need (`python3`) is registered, so a legitimate R/Julia-only jupyter install also failed instead of skipping.

## Fix

- `is_available()` now spawns `jupyter --version` and requires exit status 0. The contract is exit status only: stdout is not parsed because the output format differs across jupyter_core versions (a bare version string on older releases, a package table on newer), and the observed stale-shim failure already exits non-zero.
- The probe result is cached per resolved path (`JUPYTER_PROBE_CACHE`), so the per-render engine-registry rebuild doesn't re-spawn jupyter per document — same rationale as the existing `JUPYTER_PATH_CACHE` (bd-c5u2g).
- Test guards in `capture_splice_engines.rs` and `jupyter_kernel_cleanup_e2e.rs` additionally probe `find_kernelspec("python3")` and skip with a note on `KernelspecNotFound`; any other discovery error still fails the test.

Stub-binary tests pin the contract: a jupyter stub exiting non-zero reports unavailable, a working stub reports available, and two engines sharing a path spawn the binary exactly once.

## Scope

Phase 1 of bd-t0wpbq59 (jupyter detection and test environment): honest detection only. The `q2 check jupyter` health check (bd-elhgm6ff) and CI Python provisioning (bd-ek7njozm, bd-z09fx92g) are follow-ups tracked separately. The same PATH-presence defect exists in `KnitrEngine::is_available` and is deliberately not fixed here — tracked as bd-s8xe0lac.
