title: hub-client: fix ProjectsHome teardown flake and first-run E2E race; guard against recurrences
description:
## Summary

Fixes two intermittent CI failures in hub-client, both caused by a test not waiting for async app state. It also adds guards and agent guidance for both.

### 1. Vitest teardown flake (`TS Test Suite`, on `main`)

For example [run 36206474802](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/36206474802/job/108303984822). Every test passed, but the job failed with:

```
EnvironmentTeardownError: [vitest-worker]: Closing rpc while "onUserConsoleLog" was pending
```

Five of the last 40 failed runs were this error, from the two `ProjectsHome` integration test files. `ProjectsHome` calls `getUserIdentity()` on mount, which opens fake-indexeddb and runs migrations in the background. The migrations' `console.log` calls outlived the test file.

- Mock `projectStorage` and `userSettings` in both `ProjectsHome` integration tests.
- New `settleDb()` in `storage/db.ts`. The integration setup awaits it after every test, so DB work a component starts on mount can't outlive its test.
- Migration progress logs go through `logMigration()`, which is silent when `MODE === 'test'`. Warnings and errors are unchanged.

### 2. `first-run.spec.ts` E2E race (`E2E — interactive`, on this PR)

[Run 36255258279](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/36255258279/job/108440808711): `getProjectSetDocId()` returned `null` (1 failed, 1 flaky). This existed before the PR and is unrelated to its changes. Since 440098e41 the projects home renders while the project set is still `connecting`. The bootstrap helper waited only for the home UI, and its comment still claimed the status gated the render. A non-null doc id isn't enough either: the root connection exists before its pointers are saved and the status reaches `connected`.

- `App.tsx` publishes the project-set status as `data-project-set-status` on `<html>`.
- New `waitForProjectSetDocId()` in `e2e/helpers/projectFactory.ts` waits for `connected`, then reads the id. The bootstrap helpers call it, so every spec starts with a connected root. The stale comment is corrected.
- `first-run.spec.ts` reads the root id through the helper.

### Agent guidance

`.claude/rules/hub-client-tests.md` is new and path-scoped to hub-client unit, integration and E2E tests. It says to:
- mock storage when rendering top-level components;
- treat `EnvironmentTeardownError` as a real leak, not a flake to re-run, and how to find the leak;
- in Playwright, wait on the state being asserted rather than on a visible proxy, use retrying assertions, make waits discriminate, and not use sleeps as synchronization.

## Test plan

- [x] hub-client unit suite: 106 files, 1243 tests pass
- [x] hub-client integration suite: 20 files, 147 tests pass, and no test file writes console output
- [x] `npm run typecheck` is clean. ESLint shows no new problems (`App.tsx` has the same 12 existing ones as `main`).
- [x] Full E2E suite, rebuilt bundle, `--retries=0`: 78/78
- [x] `first-run.spec.ts --repeat-each=5 --retries=0`: 15/15
- [x] Drain check: the unmocked `main` version of the New-menu test now keeps every migration log inside the first test (previously they spilled into tests 3 and 4)
- [ ] Both failures were intermittent in CI, so I couldn't reproduce them locally.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

An audit of the test suites found about 30 more instances of these two patterns: async work that outlives a test in Vitest, and one-shot reads of settling state in Playwright. They are left for follow-up work.

title: Bare @ that cannot be a citation typo is literal text (a @ b, main @ sha, user@example.com)
description:
Fixes braid strand `bd-bare-at-literal-w3ytmu8e` (child of the claude-notes-as-a-website epic, bd-uk8zgkha).

## Problem

Any `@` without a citation key after it failed the whole document with an **uncoded** `Parse error`. The most common source in claude-notes was the plan-header line ``**Branch:** `main` @ `6bee9ebe` ``; 141 files there had their first error on an `@`. Separately, `user@example.com` parsed silently as `Str "user"` plus a citation of `example.com`, which renders as an unresolved `???`.

## Policy

Pandoc treats every non-citation `@` as text. q2 deliberately does **not** go that far. An `@` next to citation-like punctuation is more likely a mistyped citation than prose, and guessing would let the typo reach the output. So an `@` is literal only where it can't be read as a citation attempt:

| literal now (matches pandoc) | still an error (likely a citation typo) |
|---|---|
| `a @ b`, `a @` (EOL/EOF), `@` alone, `text\n@ more` | `@-foo` (meant `-@foo`?), `@:foo`, `@~`, `@<` |
| `a @"x" b`, `a @'x' b`, `a @“x” b`, `a @‘x’ b` | `a @, b`, `(see @)`, `[see @]` (missing key) |
| `> @ b`, `- @ b`, `1. @ b`, `# @ b`, indented continuation lines | `-@`, `a -@ b`, `@@`, `@@foo`, `a (@) b` |
| `user@example.com`, `mermaid@11`, `a@ b`, `a@.` (one Str) | `@}`, `@{foo`, `@{weird key}`, `(@ b`, `x ~@ y` |

Citations are unchanged: `@ref`, `-@ref`, `[@a; @b]`, `(@foo)`, `"@foo"`, `@{https://…}`. The kept errors are still uncoded; bd-2o8rq2xj gives them a Q-code and a `\@` hint.

## Changes

- **scanner.c, standalone `@`:** `parse_cite_author_in_text` emits the existing literal-Str token (bd-j9cf) when the `@` is preceded by whitespace or line start and followed by whitespace, EOL, EOF, or a straight or curly quote.
- **scanner.c, line-content anchor:** a block-quote marker, list marker, soft line ending, or block continuation token swallows the line prefix *and the whitespace in it*. Without the anchor, `> @ b` or `text\n  @ more` would not count as "preceded by whitespace". The new `Scanner.line_content_column` (serialized) records where line content starts. It's set only at emit sites where the token end is provably the lexer position. My first attempt was a plain flag, which is unsound: tree-sitter restores the last external token's state before every `scan()`, so the flag leaked past `(` in `> (@ b`. Corpus probes pin that.
- **grammar.js:** `wordAtRegex` (`[alnum]@`) lets an `@` continue a `pandoc_str` word. That gives `word@`, `word@word`, and emails as one Str. This is pandoc's "a textual citation cannot follow a Str" rule.
- **atx_heading.rs, fixed in passing:** a heading that starts with a literal-Str token got a leading `Space` (`# @ b`, and already `# < b` and `# * b` on main). Leading Spaces are now stripped like trailing ones, which matches pandoc.

## Behaviour changes to note

- **One success → error:** `word@{key}` was `Str "word"` plus a braced Cite glued to a word. It now reports the existing coded **Q-2-41** at the brace.
- **Updated tests:** two pampa tests (`test_citation_without_leading_space`, `test_citation_multiple_spacing_patterns`) used `Hi@cite` as their example of a citation with no leading space. That input is now one Str, as in pandoc, so they use `Hi(@cite)`, which keeps what they test.
- **Writer:** `[Str "foo", Cite bar]` with no space in between (only reachable from JSON or a filter) writes `foo@bar` and reads back as one Str. Pandoc's markdown writer behaves the same.

## Tests

- `test/corpus/at-as-str.txt`: 87 cases. Expected trees are derived rather than hand-written: tier-1 targets come from the same input with `@`→`<` (same literal token path), and guards come from the unchanged parser. It includes kept-error `:error` cases and anchor leak probes.
- `crates/pampa/tests/integration/test_bare_at_str.rs`: native output against pandoc for each shape, source ranges (the `@` Str covers only the `@`), and qmd writer round trips. Four `qmd-json-qmd` round-trip fixtures.
- claude-notes scan: **718 → 770** clean files, 0 newly failing, and no first error on an `@`.

## Overlap with #732

Both PRs edit `PANDOC_REGEX_STR`. A trial merge conflicts **only in the generated `parser.c` / `grammar.json`**; `grammar.js` auto-merges into a regex carrying both changes. After `tree-sitter generate`, the merge passed 816/816 corpus tests and 5127 pampa/syntax-helper/lsp tests. To resolve whichever lands second: keep the merged `grammar.js`, run `tree-sitter generate`, then `tree-sitter test` with an isolated `TREE_SITTER_LIBDIR` (bd-agsgrbfn).

## Local verification

- Full `cargo xtask verify` passed all 14 steps before the last commit. That run covered the tree-sitter corpus plus the CRLF parity rerun, 15010 Rust tests, and hub-client incl. WASM.
- The last commit is the curly-quote rule (scanner plus tests). After it, I re-ran the corpus (808/808, isolated lib dir) and the pampa, qmd-syntax-helper, and quarto-lsp-core suites (5122 passed).

Follow-ups filed: bd-2o8rq2xj (Q-code for kept `@` errors), bd-0idqzj33 (other uncoded parse errors), bd-5qmh5acq (Unicode citation keys), bd-yl0a8kdi (`a - @key` silently parsed as suppress-author). Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-25-bare-at-as-str.md`.

title: Accept every non-ASCII punctuation/symbol code point as Str (⟨ ⌈ 「 （ …)
description:
Fixes braid strand `bd-angle-bracket-u27e8-parse-error-r6l55zmh` (child of the claude-notes-as-a-website epic, bd-uk8zgkha).

## Problem

`a ⟨b` and `Revert ⟨hunk⟩ then RED` were uncoded `Parse error`s. Pandoc 3.11 renders both as plain text. The `pandoc_str` token enumerated the Po/Pc/Sm/Sk/Sc ranges by hand and never covered **Ps/Pe** (opening/closing punctuation). As a result, every non-ASCII bracket was rejected. That includes math brackets (⟨⟩ ⌈⌉ ⌊⌋ ⟦⟧) and all CJK brackets (「」『』【】《》（）［］). The hand-typed tables had also drifted: Unicode 14+ Po characters and U+20B0 ₰ were missing.

A sweep of every assigned non-ASCII code point (149,718) found **196 failures**.

## Fix

- The enumerated tables are replaced by one class intersection, `[[\p{P}\p{S}]&&[^\x00-\x7F]]`. Every non-ASCII punctuation or symbol character is now Str, which matches Pandoc. The policy is that q2 reserves no non-ASCII punctuation as syntax.
- ASCII punctuation stays explicit (`#%&()/:+=-`).
- `pandoc_str` now uses `RustRegex` instead of `new RegExp(…, 'u')`, because JS's `u` flag rejects `&&`. `RustRegex` passes the pattern to tree-sitter's regex-syntax without JS validation. The grammar already uses it for `shortcode_name`.

- `crates/pampa/tests/integration/test_unicode_punctuation.rs`: a curated per-family list parsed at token start, mid-word, and word end, plus an AST-stable qmd round trip.
- The sweep scripts live in `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-25-unicode-punctuation-coverage-investigation/` as a manual tool. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-25-unicode-punctuation-coverage.md`.

title: Flanking rules for * _ ~ ^: whitespace-adjacent delimiters are literal text
description: ## Summary A `*` / `_` run followed by whitespace cannot open emphasis and one preceded by whitespace (or at line start) cannot close it (CommonMark §6.2). A `~` / `^` only opens a sub/superscript when its closer appears before the next unescaped whitespace (Pandoc's markdown rule, what Quarto 1 does). A delimiter that can do neither is emitted as the literal-Str token that bd-j9cf introduced for bare `<`, renamed `_pandoc_literal_str` / `LITERAL_STR`. Before, `O(N * D)`, `foo *`, `a ** b` were Q-2-12/Q-2-13 errors, and an even number of stray delimiters paired up silently: `a * b * c` → `a b c`, `~5 and ~10` → subscript, `_quarto.yml and _metadata.yml` → emphasis. After, all of these are literal text, as in pandoc (`markdown` and `commonmark` readers agree on every case in the plan except the closer quirk noted there). Over the 1441 `.md` files in `claude-notes/`, files that parse clean go from 491 to 718; files whose first error is Q-2-17 (`~`) go from 348 to 0. Plan with probe tables, measurement, and design: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-25-star-as-str.md`. Closes bd-star-as-str-qigl02pz and bd-whitespace-flanked-delimiters-0ncy8bgq. Tier 3 (unmatched left-flanking opener → literal: `*.md`, `*args`, `a *b c`, `_quarto.yml`) is bd-unmatched-opener-literal-dni5aiwd. ## How it works - `scan()` records the whitespace it consumed on the current call in a per-call (non-serialized) field; the delimiter handlers read that plus `get_column() == 0` for "preceded by whitespace / line start". "Followed by whitespace" is a one-character lookahead after the contiguous run. - `~` / `^` use a bounded forward peek (no `mark_end`) for the closer before the next whitespace, skipping backslash escapes. - Each handler now `mark_end`s after every character of the contiguous run, so the token can end there even though the loop goes on to consume inter-run spaces (`* * *`). The old "ugly hack" that emitted a star closer before looking at anything is gone. - Thematic break, list marker and `TRIPLE_STAR` (Q-2-32) precedence is unchanged. One peek adjustment: a `*` alone on a line is an empty list item, which cannot interrupt a top-level paragraph (`para\n*` is now one paragraph, as pandoc) but still starts an empty sibling item inside an open list. - The qmd writer now escapes `Space` / `SoftBreak` as `\ ` inside sub/superscripts (pandoc's writer does the same), otherwise a Subscript holding a real Space (JSON, filters, commonmark_x) would round-trip to literal text. ## Behaviour changes to track tree-sitter corpus tests removed: none (721/721). One expectation updated: `_hello __strong__ world_` parses the same, but the space after the `__` closer is its own `pandoc_space` node instead of being inside the closer token. Parses that were successes and are now errors (none had tests; pinned as tier-3 boundary cases): - `**bold **` → Q-2-13 (pandoc-markdown said Strong, CommonMark literal) - `*a and then *b` → Q-2-12 (was `a and thenb`) - `_quarto.yml and _metadata.yml`, `a_ and _b` → Q-2-5 (were silent ``) - `(* comment *)` → Q-2-12 (was `(` Emph `)`; pandoc: literal) - `~a and b~`, `^a and b^` → literal (were sub/superscript; Pandoc-markdown/Quarto 1 rule) Fixtures: `smoke/001.qmd` now parses; error-corpus cases that became valid (`a *`, `foo* a `, `**`, `__`, `_`, `~`, `^`) replaced by word-followed openers (Q-2-16/17 use a closer swallowed by a code span, the remaining way to leave a sub/sup unclosed), one `'a'` tiling dropped from four codes, `case-files/` and `_autogen-table.json` regenerated; syntax-helper Q-2-16/17 tests updated. ## Verification - `tree-sitter test`: 721/721 - `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` and `cargo xtask verify --skip-rust-build --skip-rust-tests`: all steps passed (14866 Rust tests, 1174 hub-client tests) - claude-notes scan before/after in the plan 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: engines: render percent, spin, and .ipynb with native content processors
description:
q2's Rust engines could render none of the three input formats this branch adds: percent scripts, knitr spin scripts, and Jupyter notebooks. It renders all three natively now — `# %%` percent scripts (Python, Julia, R, …), `#' ` spin scripts, and `.ipynb` notebooks replayed from their stored outputs — through a new content-processor registry that converts each in-process to qmd. A notebook needs no jupyter installation at all.

```qmd
# %% [markdown]
# Percent cells become qmd

# %%
print("hello")
```

TS engines are where the old conversion path hurt: an engine claim used to imply engine launches, and Pass-1 converts every claimed non-qmd file to markdown just to index it — so a project of N julia percent scripts launched Deno N times before any render, exactly what the rule "claims must not load expensive engines merely to index a document" forbids. Engines now name a native processor on their `claims-files` entry (`processor:`), the built-in engines route their conversion through the registry, and julia's `.jl` claim flips from a dynamic TS-engine claim to `percent`. A claim-time coherence check and a spawn-count tripwire enforce that indexing stays launch-free.

## percent and spin (plan 7b)

- **percent** is a faithful port of `percentScriptToMarkdown`, parameterized by `(comment_open, fence_language)`.
- **spin** is a native reimplementation of `knitr::spin`'s grammar; `tree-sitter-r` (already in both builds) decides whether a `#'` marker is real or inside a string, and a knitr-generated golden corpus pins the behavior.
- `SourceInfo` gains `Concat`/`Original` parents through the render pipeline, so a diagnostic in converted text points at the original script's file/line/column.

## pampa: front-matter diagnostics under converted sources

Every node kind rerooted its source info through `parent_source_info` except the three YAML front-matter sites (one hardcoded `FileId(0)`). `Concat` parents — which percent/spin produce — exposed the gap: error snippets labeled the synthetic converted buffer (`broken.R (converted by knitr)`) instead of the real file. All three sites now use the shared helper, so a forced error in a spin `.R` labels `broken.R:2:4` with the real `#'` lines (regression test red→green).

## .ipynb (plan 7c)

- `.ipynb` is the registry's third entry: jupyter claims it and names the processor, so admission and conversion launch nothing.
- Each cell becomes its own ephemeral source file, so every diagnostic — including a `#|` YAML option error — names the cell that caused it.
- **Stored-output replay**: when the input is `.ipynb` and `execute.enabled` is not `true`, the execution stage replays each cell's stored outputs through the same mime-bundle machinery used for live kernel results. No jupyter needed; metadata that demands execution still routes to live execution unchanged.
- Registered cells carry structured **FileOrigin** provenance; two e2e tests pin the `--json-errors` wire (notebook-cell origin, hyperlink back to the real `.ipynb`).
- Picks up upstream **quarto-error-reporting 0.3.1** (PR #7 there): a diagnostic rooted in a later cell labels that cell with an in-cell snippet instead of clamping into cell 1, and spans crossing cells read "cell N through cell M".

## Docs

- Project guide: "Listed scripts with a declared processor" in the render-list page.
- Authoring guide: new `notebooks.qmd` for rendering `.ipynb` inputs.

## Filed, not fixed here

- bd-5t6wvu7m: image outputs render as placeholders — to be fixed for the replay and live paths at once.
- A `--execute` CLI flag does not exist yet; notebook metadata is the only way to demand live execution.
- Stored-output replay is compiled out of wasm builds.

## Testing

- Workspace nextest at this HEAD: 14861 passed / 201 skipped, 0 failed (live run).
- New: spin golden corpus, ipynb converter + replay integration suites, two `--json-errors` e2e pins, pampa reroot regression.
- `cargo xtask verify` green at branch close (7c plan record).

Plans: `claude-notes/plans/2026-07-08-plan7b-native-content-processors.md`, `claude-notes/plans/2026-07-08-plan7c-ipynb-content-processor.md` (braid bd-19nc56ao).

title: Code spans: emit in-span backtick runs whole so the CommonMark exact-length rule holds
description:
Closes bd-code-span-longer-backtick-run-nycn85a8.

## Problem

An inline code span whose content contains a backtick run *longer* than its delimiter was an uncoded parse error:

```
a `x``y` b             -> Parse error
a ` ```mermaid ` b     -> Parse error
a `` ```{r} `` b       -> Parse error
```

CommonMark's rule is that the closer is a backtick run of *exactly* the opener's length; any other run is content. The external scanner already implemented that rule and already tracked (and serialized) the opener length. What defeated it was the grammar: the `pandoc_code_span` content rule matched single backticks one at a time, which split any inner run. The scanner then saw a leftover fragment equal to the delimiter and closed the span early; the real closer became an unmatched backtick and errored. About 127 of the uncoded parse errors in the claude-notes render (bd-uk8zgkha) were this class.

## Fix

- **Scanner:** a new hidden external token, `_code_span_backtick_run`, emitted by `parse_code_span` for any run inside an open span whose length differs from the opener. Gated on both the token and `CODE_SPAN_CLOSE` being valid, so error recovery cannot emit it with a stale delimiter length. No new scanner state.
- **Grammar:** the `/[`]/` content alternative is removed in favour of the new token.
- **Paragraph start:** a run of three or more backticks whose would-be info string contains a backtick is not a fence in CommonMark, so `parse_fenced_code_block` now lets it open a code span (`` ``` x ``` b `` at paragraph start).
- **Error table:** regenerated with `build_error_table.ts`; byte-identical, since one anonymous token out and one external in left `SYMBOL_COUNT` and `STATE_COUNT` unchanged.

## Tests

- 15 new corpus cases in `test/corpus/code_span.txt` and one pipe-table cell case: every (delimiter, inner-run) class found by scanning claude-notes, the in-scope CommonMark spec examples, multi-line spans, no leaking into following text, paragraph-start triple/quadruple runs, a real-fence guard, and a case documenting that a fence-looking line inside an open span stays span content (bd-ilv8p behaviour, kept on purpose).
- 3 pampa integration tests asserting the extracted `Code` text.
- `tree-sitter test` 641/641; `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` green.

## Acceptance on claude-notes

`claude-notes/plans/code-span-backtick-run-investigation/compare-corpus-lines.py` parses every prose line holding an affected span under the old and new grammar:

| | lines |
| --- | ---: |
| affected | 158 |
| erroring before | 154 |
| erroring after | 15 |
| fixed | 143 |
| newly erroring | 4 |

The 4 newly erroring lines are malformed under the CommonMark rule itself (the spec-correct parse leaves a trailing unmatched backtick), so pandoc reads them the same way. Unmatched backtick runs stay a strict parse error by design; a diagnostic for them is filed as bd-038l5b3k (Q-2-24 exists but has been dormant since bd-ilv8p).

Plan and investigation record: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-25-code-span-backtick-run.md`.

title: Add Pandoc's long-tail output formats to the hybrid path
description:
q2 can now render 48 more output formats. `quarto render doc.qmd --to rst` —
and odt, org, djot, docbook5, s5, mediawiki, all six bbcode flavors, forty-odd
more — goes through the same pandoc-hybrid path docx/pptx/epub/typst already
use: serialize the AST, shell out to a real pandoc with the vendored Quarto
Lua filters, let pandoc write the file.

**Why this is smaller than it sounds.** The tail has no custom code in Quarto
1 — we checked the source. `defaultWriterFormat()` enumerates everything, but
the tail branches are one-liners over three generic helpers
(`plaintextFormat`, `createWordprocessorFormat`, `createEbookFormat`), and the
vendored Lua core is format-agnostic (`crossrefFilterActive` gates on
metadata, not format). Most of this change is therefore tables: one
`FormatIdentifier` variant + writer name + extension + defaults row per
format, organized into four tiers by verification story.

**The plumbing wasn't free.** Three latent problems had to be fixed before
the first new variant could land safely:

- The defaults tables were keyed by *output extension*. Fine for
  docx/pptx/epub/typst, where extensions are unique; wrong for a tail where
  opendocument and docbook both write `.xml` and nine markdown flavors share
  `.md`. Re-keyed on `FormatIdentifier`, which also unified two call sites
  that were silently passing different keys (extension vs. writer name).
- `format-identifier.base-format` was sending the extension. Coincidentally
  right for the shipped four, actively wrong for typst — it reported `"pdf"`.
  Now sends `canonical_name()`.
- The CLI gate was a hardcoded `matches!(Docx|Pptx|Epub|Typst)` allow-list.
  Now `FormatIdentifier::is_pandoc_hybrid()`, so the gate widens itself as
  variants land — with gfm/commonmark getting explicit writer arms *first*,
  because the gate change would otherwise have admitted two enum variants
  that existed but fell through to `-t md` (pandoc: "Unknown output format
  'md'").

**Decisions a reviewer might want to argue with:**

- *Bare invocation for the 12 stretch formats* (djot, ansi, the bbcodes,
  chunkedhtml, …). Q1 gives these no format object at all —
  `unknownFormat("txt")` — and pandoc 3.11 ships default *templates* for
  several of them, so `--standalone` is not a no-op: it would prepend title
  chrome Q1 never produced. Bare is parity. Extensions, though, follow
  pandoc's own conventions where they exist (`.dj`, `.zip` for chunkedhtml) —
  a deliberate improvement over Q1's blanket `.txt`, flagged in the docs for
  migrants.
- *Bare `-t gfm`*, not Q1's `commonmark+footnotes+tex_math_dollars+…`.
  Archaeology in the plan: those extensions were workarounds for bundled
  pandocs predating 2.15/2.19, which put them in gfm's defaults. Pandoc
  3.11's gfm is a strict superset of Q1's frozen 2022 string. Tradeoff
  accepted: output tracks pandoc's evolving defaults instead of freezing
  2022 GitHub.
- *First output postprocessor on the hybrid path.* Pandoc's markdown writers
  emit escaped shortcodes (`{{\< meta title \>}}`) and nothing un-escaped
  them, because the hybrid path had zero output postprocessing. We added the
  narrowest thing that works: a shortcode-unescape pass over the written
  file for markdown-family formats, gated on the file actually containing
  `{{\<`/`\>}}`. It is not a general postprocessor hook; when one is needed,
  design it then.
- *`crossref-numbering: external`* wherever a real FloatRefTarget renderer
  exists (odt, gfm, the four slide formats) — without it, pandoc's
  auto-indexer renumbers floats q2 already numbered. Placeholder-renderer
  formats leave it unset, where the indexer runs harmlessly.

**Deliberately not here:** bibtex/biblatex/csljson and opml (pandoc discards
the document body — they're bibliography/outline exporters, not document
writers), latex/beamer/context (latex epic), jats/ipynb/asciidoc/dashboard/
email (each has real Q1-side logic; per-format follow-on plans).

**Known degradations, same as Q1** (documented, not fixed): crossref floats
scaffold with a warning outside the renderer formats; callout/theorem chrome
drops except on slides; no mermaid/OJS fallback (inherited unchanged from
the shipped four).

**Docs:** a user-facing "Other output formats" reference
(`docs/guides/formats/pandoc/`), verified by rendering it — including the
discovery that pandoc's bare `docbook` is an alias of `docbook5`.

**Testing:** red-first throughout — each phase's tests failed with
`Unknown format: X` before the variants landed. e2e through the real `q2`
binary for at least one variant per family (odt/fb2/plain, all nine markdown
flavors, djot/chunkedhtml, slidy/s5 with a knitr cell proving `echo: false`
reaches the engine); output inspected by hand, not inferred from exit codes.
Textile gets a fresh-baseline snapshot — Q1's textile branch is dead via a
`"texttile"` typo in `formats.ts`, so there is no upstream baseline. Workspace
nextest at every phase boundary; `cargo xtask verify` green at the tip
including the WASM leg (14,798 passed / 200 skipped).

Upstream follow-up worth filing: Q1's `"texttile"` typo (needs approval to
open on quarto-cli).

title: q2 preview --static: seed the content tracker before the port opens (fixes preview_static_e2e flake)
description:
## Summary

Fixes the recurring `preview_static_e2e` flake on the ubuntu leg of CI (`no \`reload\` event within 30s` / `no \`render-start\` event within 30s`). Braid: bd-tp0yym04. Plan and full assessment: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-25-preview-static-tracker-seed-race.md`.

Observed on main runs 35910422721, 35995038328, 36056788947 and on PR #726 (run 36095220439). A different test failed each time, and none of those PRs touched the preview code.

## Root cause

PR #712's `ContentTracker` ignores watcher events whose file hash hasn't changed. Its baseline was taken **after** the listener was bound and the server spawned. A client could connect and edit a file in that gap, and its edit then became the baseline. The edit's watcher event compared equal and was dropped (`event without a content change; ignored`), so no render and no reload happened. On a busy runner, the driver's main thread can be preempted at the boot-line write or at `tokio::spawn(serve)`, long enough for the test to subscribe and edit first.

## Changes

- `preview_static.rs`: seed the tracker in the before-anyone-can-connect block, right after `start_watcher`. The baseline is the same (the boot render has finished), but it is now recorded before the port exists.
- `preview_static_e2e.rs`: `SseReader::wait_for` panics now include the server's stderr. The harness also sets `RUST_LOG=…,q2::commands::preview_static=debug` so a dropped event is named in the failure output. Before this, the CI logs gave no clue.

## Verification

- **Mechanism confirmed** by widening the window with an injected 300 ms sleep after `spawn(serve)` (not committed). The old order fails exactly like PR #726, and the stderr dump shows the dropped event. The new order passes all five edit-driven e2e tests with the same sleep.
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build`: all 14767 Rust tests pass. The hub-client WASM tests failed locally only because this checkout's prebuilt WASM predates #670 (`Unknown format: q2-html-render`). This PR does not touch any code compiled to WASM.
- There is no deterministic regression test; that would need a test-only delay hook in the driver. See the plan's follow-ups.

title: Fix hub preview failure on listing pages with item images (bd-yqlbfrln)
description: ## Problem Creating a project from the **Blog** template and opening `index.qmd` in the hub preview fails: ``` Pass 2 failed for /project/index.qmd: output destination /project/_site/posts/post-with-code/image.jpg is not under any allowed root (/.quarto/project-artifacts) ``` `ListingGenerateTransform` registers a `ResourceCopyIntent` for each listing item's front-matter `image:` (bd-qv2lsab0) so the thumbnail lands in the output tree even though no page body references it. The destination is `output_dir.join(img)`, which is right for native renders but in the hub-client's VFS-root resolver mode points at `/project/_site/...`. The only allowed write root there is `/.quarto/project-artifacts`, so `OutputSink` refuses the copy and the whole Pass-2 render of the host page fails. ## Fix Mirror `ResourceCollectorTransform`: in VFS-root mode the hub's asset walker serves `` straight from the VFS, so the transform skips copy intents there. Native output is unchanged (copies still land under `_site`). ## Tests - `listing_generate.rs`: `item_image_copy_intent_targets_output_dir_natively` (website resolver, exact `_site` destination) and `item_image_copy_intent_skipped_in_vfs_root_mode` (red before the fix). - `hub-client/src/services/listingItemImage.wasm.test.ts`: renders a Blog-shaped project (website, listing over `posts/`, `feed: true`, `categories: true`, one post with `image:` and real bytes) through `render_page_in_project_with_attribution` in both q2-preview and HTML modes; the thumbnail `src` survives. - Verified in a local-prod build: New → Blog → `index.qmd` renders the listing with no error. ## Found on the way (not in this PR) - bd-960vrfbm: the listing thumbnail bytes do not load in q2-preview. The listing is a `RawBlock html`; `assetWalker.ts` only manifests structured `Image` nodes, so the raw `` 404s against the web origin and the thumbnail column renders blank. title: Replace CLAUDE.md with AGENTS.md
description:
## Summary

- Move the project instructions from `CLAUDE.md` to `AGENTS.md`. Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md`, the same as other agents.
- Rename the per-crate instruction files (`pampa`, `wasm-qmd-parser`, `wasm-quarto-hub-client`) to `AGENTS.md`.
- Update all references in comments, skills, and notes.

No code changes. Comment and documentation text only.

## Test plan

- `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo xtask lint` pass.
- A repo-wide search confirms that no stale `CLAUDE.md` references remain. Two groups of references stay on purpose: the filename detection in `project/discovery.rs` (user projects can still use `CLAUDE.md`), and historical notes in `claude-notes/`.

title: qmd: block-level editorial marks (::: ++ / ::: -- / ::: >> / ::: !!)
description:
Adds block-level counterparts to the inline editorial marks `[++ …]`, `[-- …]`, `[>> …]` and `[!! …]`:

```qmd
::: >> {author="cs"}

A comment that runs over several paragraphs.

:::
```

Plan and design discussion: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-24-block-editorial-marks.md` (braid bd-an9gkxnp).

## Parsing and AST
- **Grammar:** anything that follows `::: ` now goes through one "fenced-div sigil" dispatch in the scanner: `^id` note definitions plus the four new markers. The shared body/closer part of the grammar is a JS helper, so refactoring it left `parser.c` byte-identical. A marker must be followed by whitespace, the end of the line, or `{`.
- **AST:** there is no new node type. A block mark becomes a `Div` whose first class is `quarto-insert`, `quarto-delete`, `quarto-edit-comment` or `quarto-highlight`. These are the classes the inline marks already turn into, so the existing CSS and consumers apply. The qmd writer writes the marker form back out; a hand-written `::: {.quarto-delete}` comes back as `::: --`.
- **Breaking change:** a div info string can no longer start with `-`. `::: --foo`, `::: ---` and `::: -x` now fail with the new error **Q-2-53**, which has hints and a docs page. Neither 5.6k local div openers nor a GitHub code search turned up a div class starting with dashes.

## Consumers
- **Document profile:** a `::: >>` block is extracted as a single comment, with author and date from its attributes.
- **CSS:** block framing (padding, last-child margin reset) and a left border on block comments. The phase-5 `styles.css` byte-identity hash is re-recorded; the only difference is these three rules (verified).
- **Docs:** new "Editorial marks" section in the authoring guide. The docs had no coverage of the inline marks either.

## Existing bugs fixed on the way
Each has a regression test that failed before its fix:
- `::: ^id` as the last bytes of a file made the scanner loop forever.
- With CRLF line endings, note ids kept the `\r`.
- Inline marks dropped their attribute source info when turned into Spans, so the attribute's source positions no longer lined up with its classes.
- bd-2281lkrx: an inline editorial mark inside a `list-table` panicked pampa.

## Filed, not fixed here
- bd-9fy9p4zl (P1): the contents of `list-table` and `definition-list` blocks are never postprocessed. As a result, footnote references, standalone attributes and editorial marks in cells fail (Q-3-31/32/33).
- bd-i4xrcdqx: a blank line containing only spaces before `:::` in a list item makes the list tight. The qmd writer emits exactly that shape.
- Follow-up bd-t1avfz0n: comment chrome in q2-preview for block comments.

## Testing
- `cargo xtask verify` passes locally, including the tree-sitter corpus in both LF and CRLF modes (647/647).
- Error table regenerated; every error code keeps the same number of mappings.
- New tree-sitter corpus file, pampa integration tests, native/qmd snapshots, and round-trip and smoke fixtures.

title: Nested projects: a nested _quarto.yml bounds the implicit render list
description:
Braid: bd-nested-projects-xyb28wnl (epic bd-uk8zgkha)
Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-23-nested-project-boundaries.md`

## What changes

A subdirectory with its own `_quarto.yml` or `_quarto.yaml` is now a **nested project** that owns its subtree, even when the file has no `project:` key. This is option C from the strand.

- **Implicit patterns skip it.** These are the default `**/*.qmd` and any glob that doesn't name the nested directory (`**/*.md`, `*/page.qmd`). **Q-5-31** warns once per render and lists every nested directory that would otherwise have contributed files. A `!` pattern over the directory (`"!sub/**"`) silences it.
- **Explicit patterns still render.** A pattern is explicit when the part before its first wildcard reaches the nested directory or goes below it: `sub/page.qmd`, `sub/*.qmd`, `sub/**/*.qmd`, bare `sub`. The matched files render with the **outer** config, and **Q-5-32** points at the pattern that reached in.
- **`q2 render sub` is unchanged.** The nearest project still wins.

This is a deliberate divergence from Quarto 1, which ignores a nested `_quarto.yml` when rendering the outer project, without any warning. The render-list guide has a new "Nested projects" section with a Quarto 1 callout for migrating users.

## Implementation

- `project/discovery.rs`:
  - The walk tags each candidate with its innermost nested root, and `select_from_walk` decides per pattern.
  - `discover_project_files` now returns `DiscoveredFiles { files, nested }`.
  - The new `nested_project_diagnostics` is pure, like `render_pattern_diagnostics`.
- The report is stored on `ProjectConfig::nested_projects`, and the orchestrator emits it next to the Q-5-13 family.
- A separate commit fixes `q2 preview`'s `find_project_root_above`, which ignored `_quarto.yaml` (closes bd-nqj8gmrb). The shared marker list is `PROJECT_CONFIG_FILENAMES`.

## Known limits / follow-ups

- `diagnostics: {Q-5-31: off}` does not suppress these warnings yet, because project-scoped diagnostics bypass the policy. That gap is bd-aow4qio3, and the docs say so.
- Preview/hub parity at page-selection points (`pickInitialPage`, `is_config_like`, `is_preview_relevant`) is split out to bd-smerrfma.

## Testing

- 13 new unit tests in `discovery.rs`.
- CLI end-to-end tests in `crates/quarto/tests/integration/nested_projects_cli.rs`.
- Acceptance run on a copy of `claude-notes/` with `render: ["**/*.md"]`:
  - none of the 53 nested repro projects produced output;
  - Q-5-31 lists the 7 that contain renderable `.md`.
- Local `cargo xtask verify` (full, with WASM rebuild) passes.

title: Installers: authenticated, retried nightly release lookup (fixes flaky install-smoke)
description:
## Why

The Nightly workflow's builds, release gates and publish have been green, but its **install smoke** job keeps failing. That job runs the README install one-liners on Linux, macOS and Windows against the nightly it just published, and it is the only CI coverage `install.sh` / `install.ps1` get. Each failure came from the same step: the installers' **single, anonymous, unretried** call to `api.github.com/.../releases/tags/nightly`, which resolves the nightly. There were three distinct triggers:

| Run | What failed | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-22 scheduled | Windows | GitHub API returned a 5xx ("Server Error · GitHub") |
| [2026-09-23 scheduled](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/35836439914) | all three OSes | Lookup ran 6–15s after the pipeline **deleted and re-created** the `nightly` release; the API briefly 404'd (macOS) or served the release without its assets yet (Linux/Windows) |
| [2026-09-23 manual](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/35911553029) | macOS, twice (re-run ~90s later too) | Not the race; the same install works locally. Consistent with the **60 requests/hour per-IP anonymous rate limit**, which GitHub's shared macOS runners exhaust. (Unconfirmed: the old `curl -f … 2>/dev/null` discarded the HTTP status, which this PR also fixes.) |

Real users hit the same issues: anyone behind a shared NAT or corporate egress, or who runs the one-liner right after a nightly is published.

## What

**`install.sh` and `install.ps1`**
- **Token when available.** Send `GH_TOKEN` (or `GITHUB_TOKEN`) as a bearer token on the release lookup. That moves the request off the anonymous per-IP budget. The token is optional, and without one the behavior is unchanged.
  - `install.sh` sends it **only to `https://api.github.com/`**, never to a `Q2_RELEASES_API_BASE` override, and passes it to curl via `-K -` on stdin so it doesn't show up in `ps`.
  - **A stale token never breaks an install:** on a 401, the installer warns and retries anonymously.
- **Retries** with a 2/4/8/16s backoff (5 attempts, 30s worst case) on 5xx, 404, network errors, and on a release that doesn't list this platform's archive yet (the replace race). A 403/429 is **not** retried, because a rate limit lasts up to an hour.
- **Errors name the HTTP status.** For example: `HTTP 403: GitHub API rate limit, most likely; set GH_TOKEN …`. The next failure will diagnose itself.
- `install.ps1`'s stable `releases/latest` lookup now goes through the same helper. `install.sh`'s stable path is unchanged: it already falls back to the non-API `releases/latest` redirect.

**`nightly.yml`**: the smoke steps get `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`. This is the automatic per-job token; no new secret is needed. The workflow already grants `contents: write`, and reading a release needs only read.

**Docs**: README (nightly section), `install.sh --help`, `install.ps1` header, release runbook.

## Testing

- `bootstrap_sh` suite: 41/41 pass. New `nightly_retries_while_the_release_is_being_replaced` serves an asset-less release on the first read and the full one after the (shimmed) backoff. The no-release test now also asserts that the retries are bounded. The nightly tests shim `sleep` so the backoff costs no wall time.
- `shellcheck install.sh` and `actionlint nightly.yml` are clean.
- **`install.sh`, by hand against real GitHub:** a bogus token gives the 401 warning, then an anonymous install succeeds. A real token installs directly. The piped `curl | bash` form still works.
- **`install.sh` against a local stub server:**
  - 403 fails immediately with the rate-limit message.
  - 404 and 500 retry 4 times, then fail with the status.
  - A `GH_TOKEN` set while `Q2_RELEASES_API_BASE` points at the stub sends **no** `Authorization` header.
- **`install.ps1` under PowerShell 7.6 (portable, on macOS):**
  - Against real GitHub, with {bogus, real, no} token × {`-Nightly`, stable}, run through the README scriptblock one-liner: all six cases pass.
  - This caught and fixed a bug: `$script:` scope is wrong under the one-liner, so the token now lives in a hashtable.
  - Its API helper against the stub: 403, 404, 500 and the race case all behave as above.
- **Not tested:** Windows PowerShell 5.1. `Get-HttpStatus` is written to handle 5.1's `WebException` shape, but only PS7 was exercised.

## Before merge

The smoke job only runs when a nightly is published, so CI on this PR doesn't exercise the installers end to end. After merge, the next nightly's install smoke is the real check. To verify sooner, run `gh workflow run nightly.yml --ref bugfix/bd-n9yh30c8-installer-token-retry -f force=true -f publish=true`, which republishes the `nightly` release from this branch. Otherwise, merge and watch tonight's run.

title: Fix q2 preview --static shutdown on Windows Ctrl-Break
description:
Since #712, `cargo xtask verify` fails on Windows: clippy reports `Server.stdout` in `preview_static_e2e.rs` as never read, because its only reader, the SIGINT shutdown test, is `#[cfg(unix)]`.

That gate also hid a behaviour gap. On Windows, `ShutdownSignal` only listened for Ctrl-C, so a Ctrl-Break killed the preview with the default handler (exit `0xC000013A`) instead of the graceful shutdown SIGTERM gets on unix. No test exercised the Windows shutdown path.

## Fix

`ShutdownSignal` now also listens for Ctrl-Break on Windows, and the shutdown test runs on every platform. Windows cannot send Ctrl-C to a single process group, only to the whole console (which includes the test runner), so on Windows the test spawns the preview in its own process group and sends `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT`. On unix it still sends SIGINT. `GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent` only reaches processes sharing a console, so the test allocates one first when the runner has none, as on a headless CI runner.

Closing the console window (`CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT`) is left unhandled, as Windows terminates the process a few seconds after that event anyway.

## Test Plan

- [x] `cargo clippy -p quarto --tests -- -D warnings` clean on Windows
- [x] `interrupt_exits_cleanly` fails on Windows before the `ShutdownSignal` change (exit `0xC000013A`) and passes after
- [x] Same test passes when the test binary runs with no console attached
- [x] Manual check on Windows: Ctrl-C in Windows Terminal and a scripted Ctrl-Break both print the shutdown line and exit 0
- [x] Linux and macOS CI (unix side not built locally)

Related to #712

title: chore: update iroh to 1.2.0 and blake3 to 1.8.7
description:
## Summary

- Update `iroh` 1.0.3 → 1.2.0 and `blake3` 1.8.5 → 1.8.7. Lockfile-only change; the caret constraints in `quarto-p2p` already permitted both.
- iroh 1.1.0/1.2.0 bring relay-reconnect fixes (priority messages kept answered during reconnect backoff, relay task draining) and relay rate-limit signaling — directly relevant to the preview tunnel's relay-fallback path.
- blake3 1.8.7 drops the mandatory `arrayref` dependency, so `arrayref` is no longer reachable from the iroh subtree (it remains in the lockfile only via `usvg`/`tiny-skia-path` in the typst chain).

## Compatibility

- The only upstream `[breaking]` flag in 1.0.3 → 1.2.0 is the `CustomAddr` postcard serialization fix (1.1.0). It does not affect our tickets: `PreviewShareTicket` only ever carries `Ip` and `Relay` transport addrs (custom transports are not enabled), so ticket wire interop across versions is preserved.
- All iroh/blake3 usage is confined to the native `quarto-p2p` closure: no satellite lockfile (`wasm-*`, `tree-sitter`, `test-unwind`, `experiments`) references either crate, so the root `Cargo.lock` is the only one touched. The WASM leg is unaffected (Gate 0 intact).

## Lockfile churn

All 38 changed package lines are the transitive closure of the two bumps: the iroh family in lockstep, the noq 1.3 QUIC stack, and the DNS resolver swap (hickory stack out, `n0-dns-resolver` + friends in). `cargo update -p` is conservative; nothing unrelated was updated.

## Verification

- `cargo build -p quarto-p2p`; `cargo nextest run -p quarto-p2p` (15/15, including hermetic loopback QUIC tunnel integration tests)
- `cargo check -p quarto-preview -p quarto`
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` — lints, clippy, build green (hub build skipped: neither crate is in the WASM closure)
- `cargo nextest run --workspace` — 14,711/14,711 pass. Six pandoc-typst L-tier tests were excluded locally: they require a `typst` binary on PATH, which this machine lacks; CI installs typst 0.15.1 and runs them there.

title: fix(xtask): switch-task no longer claims a worktree in the main checkout
description:
When `cargo xtask switch-task` runs in the main checkout, it prepends a context block to `CLAUDE.local.md` that says "This is a **worktree** of the q2 repository. Main repo: `../..`". That is false in the main checkout, and `CLAUDE.local.md` loads into every Claude Code session started there.

`switch-task` is documented to work in the main checkout as well as in `.worktrees/*`, but it reused the `create-worktree` section template, which assumes the file always sits two levels below the main repo.

`switch-task` now compares `git rev-parse --git-dir` with `--git-common-dir` to tell the main checkout from a linked worktree. `build_section` takes the checkout kind, and the main-checkout variant keeps the strand context under a `# Task Context` heading without the worktree declaration. Skipping the block entirely in the main checkout was considered, but it would drop the documented "rewrite the context block" behavior for anyone who runs `switch-task` there. `create-worktree` output is unchanged.

## Test Plan

- [x] New unit test: main-checkout sections for all three section kinds carry no worktree claim or `../..` path
- [x] New test using a real git repo plus linked worktree: `detect_checkout` returns the right kind, including from subdirectories
- [x] End to end in a scratch repo: `switch-task --no-claim` in the main checkout writes `# Task Context` and keeps existing notes below it; re-running replaces the block; in a linked worktree the output is identical to before
- [x] `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean

title: quarto-core + xtask: extension-subtree infrastructure (julia epic Steps 3 + 4-infra)
description:
### What this is

This PR ports Quarto 1's extension-subtree machinery to q2 and proves it end-to-end — **without vendoring any real engine**. It is the infrastructure half of Step 4 of the [julia-engine epic](claude-notes/plans/2026-09-03-julia-engine-static-declarations-epic.md), deliberately split out so it never waited on external PRs. The original gate on the julia-specific remainder (a PumasAI-hosted branch, PumasAI/quarto-julia-engine#15) is gone as of 2026-09-24: the epic's Step 2c pivoted to using the `gordonwoodhull/quarto-julia-engine` fork as q2's upstream of record until the Q1 schema change ([quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14936](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/pull/14936)) ships in a stable release. What still gates vendoring julia is only q2-internal sign-off (epic Q8/Q9). Once cleared, bundling the Julia engine is one row in a table and one `include_dir!` registration — the runbook is included here (`claude-notes/instructions/extension-subtrees.md`).

It also carries an independent q2 bug fix (epic Step 3 / finding F5): static engine-claim lookup was case-sensitive while dynamic claiming was not, so a ` ```{Julia} ` cell claimed dynamically but missed its own static declaration.

### The three pieces

**1. `cargo xtask pull-extension-subtree`** — a port of Q1's hidden `pull-git-subtree` dev command (`src/command/dev-call/pull-git-subtree/cmd.ts`). Maintains vendored extension repos as git subtrees under `resources/extension-subtrees/`: finds the last split via the `git-subtree-dir:` trailer, `subtree add --squash` on first run, no-op when there's nothing new, `subtree pull --squash` otherwise. The `SUBTREES` table ships **empty** — adding the julia row is the gated Step 4 remainder. Test-only seams (`QUARTO_SUBTREE_ROOT`, `--table <json>`) let the tests run real `git` against fixture remotes in tempdirs; this is xtask's first test module that shells out, and it's hermetic.

**2. Multi-root builtin discovery.** `discover_extensions` / `discover_project_extensions` now take `&[&Path]` builtin roots instead of `Option<&Path>`; subtree payloads are scanned after the regular builtin dir and before user extensions, so last-match-wins still lets a user install override a bundled extension. `builtin_extension_subtree_roots()` resolves roots from (a) the `QUARTO_EXTENSION_SUBTREES_DIR` dev/test override, (b) per-subtree embedded `ResourceBundle` payloads, (c) the WASM VFS. Along the way this fixes a real inconsistency: `discover_extensions_only` hardcoded `None` for builtins on WASM — WASM builds got **no** builtin extensions at all. That split is gone; native and WASM share one path.

**3. End-to-end proof with a fake extension.** `synth-echo` (a fixture shaped like a vendored repo, claiming a `synthsub` language) is discovered via the subtree-root mechanism with **zero `_extensions/` install** and executed by the real Deno engine host through `render_to_file` — the same entry `quarto render` uses. The fake lives under `tests/fixtures/` and never ships: release binaries embed a placeholder README, and nothing is registered in `EXTENSION_SUBTREE_PAYLOADS` yet.

### Design decisions reviewers should know about

- **List of builtin roots, not one merged bundle** (mirrors Q1's separate `extension-subtrees` root). Each future subtree gets its own `include_dir!` static so we embed only its `_extensions/` payload (~68K for julia), never the whole vendored repo (~14M of tests and CI config).
- **No `filterBundledSubtreeEngines` analogue needed.** Q1 strips bundled engines from pandoc metadata because it resolves engine objects into it; q2's extension-contributed engines are registry-only and never enter writer metadata. This is asserted by test (the engine's own name must not appear in rendered HTML), not merely surveyed.
- The one deliberate deviation from Q1's script: after `subtree add`, the port returns instead of falling through to a same-invocation `pull` check — an apparent quirk in the JS, not reproduced.

### Test story

TDD throughout; every phase gated on clippy `-D warnings` + per-crate nextest, with full `cargo xtask verify` (including hub-client build/tests) green at each boundary. Workspace totals at the final gate: **14485 passed, 0 failed, 200 skipped** — +9 tests over the branch point, exactly the ones this PR adds:

- 4 xtask tests driving real `git subtree` against fixture remotes (add, no-op, pull, unknown-name, all-rows)
- 3 discovery/roots unit tests (multi-root ordering, user-overrides-subtree, env-override honored)
- 2 e2e tests (zero-install discovery; real Deno execution + the registry-only assertion)
- 3 case-sensitivity tests (RED before the F5 fix, GREEN after)

Full details, including the empirical `git subtree` behaviors the tests encode, are in the [plan](claude-notes/plans/2026-09-23-extension-subtree-infrastructure.md).

### Explicitly out of scope

- Vendoring the actual julia engine — will subtree from the `q2-static-declarations` branch of `gordonwoodhull/quarto-julia-engine` (epic Step 2c pivoted to the fork on 2026-09-24); gated only on the 14M git-history sign-off (epic Q8) and the no-Julia UX decision (Q9). Planned as a stacked PR on this one.
- Fixture convergence (hand-maintained julia fixture vs. bundled copy) — epic Step 5.
- UX on a machine without Julia installed (epic Q9).

title: chore: update samod to 0.14, automerge to 0.12 (JS 3.5.0)
description:
## What this PR does

This PR updates the two sync dependencies:

- `samod` 0.13.0 to 0.14.0, from the `access-policy` branch of `quarto-dev/samod` (commit `20d306f`).
- `automerge` 0.11.0 to 0.12.0. This is the Rust crate that pairs with `@automerge/automerge` 3.5.0, which the JS workspaces already use.

## Code changes for the new APIs

1. `automerge` 0.12 renamed the `Value` methods `to_str` and `to_bool` to `as_str` and `as_bool`. The rename is a naming cleanup only. The behavior is identical. The workspace denies deprecation warnings, so the old names are hard errors. This PR updates the 10 call sites.
2. `samod` 0.14 added the associated type `Error` to the `Dialer` trait. The new `DialError` type splits errors into `TransientFailure` (samod retries) and `PermanentFailure` (samod stops and reports the error). `BearerDialer` maps all errors to transient. This keeps the samod 0.13 behavior, which retried every error.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passed: lints, clippy with `-D warnings`, build, and the TypeScript legs. The WASM leg is not affected, because no WASM crate depends on `automerge` or `samod`.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace` passed 14,711 tests. The 6 failures are typst tests that also fail on `main`, because the typst binary is not on PATH on this machine.
- The `quarto-sync-client` vitest suite dials the real hub binary and passed. This shows that Rust automerge 0.12 syncs correctly with JS automerge 3.5.0.

## Notes

- This PR first pulled samod from the `shikokuchuo/samod` fork to run CI. Commit `d3f3b456f` moved the source to `quarto-dev/samod`. Both forks carry the identical commit `20d306f`, so the compiled code does not change.
- One vitest run showed a flaky failure in `doc-inventory.test.ts` under load. The test passed on all 4 reruns. The strand bd-tg3vnfxg tracks this flake.

- No snapshot changes.

title: hub-client: q2-preview is the default renderer; format: q2-html-render opts into the full-DOM iframe (bd-kltzdhle)
description:
## Summary

Brings `q2 preview`'s renderer choice to hub-client. A document with no `format:` key, `format: html`, or a `format: html: {…}` map now previews through the q2-preview React renderer (Q2PreviewIframe), so comments, the Edit pill, Authors, and the printable version are available on every plain document. The old full-DOM MorphIframe renderer stays reachable with the new `format: q2-html-render` (a builtin pseudo-format that `q2 render` treats exactly like `q2-debug`: plain HTML output).

Plan and decision record: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-09-hub-client-default-q2-preview.md` (strand bd-kltzdhle).

## What changed

- **Rust** (`quarto-core`, `wasm-quarto-hub-client`): register `q2-html-render`; `render_page_in_project_with_attribution` gains an optional `prefer_preview_format` argument that applies the `q2 preview` substitution (`html → q2-preview`, `revealjs → q2-slides`) while keeping `RenderHost::HubClient` (so Q-5-12 still fires — the reason the SPA's `render_page_for_preview` could not be reused). The response now reports the resolved `format`.
- **hub-client**: `getQ2Format` maps `html → q2-preview` and `q2-html-render → full-DOM`; `ReactPreview` renders every preview-pipeline format through the one entry point with the knob, which also moves reveal decks off the SPA-only entry point (attribution now reaches decks; the Authors pill gate is a follow-up, bd-jx8b0ax9). Editor chrome gates key on the router-reported format and need no change.
- **q2 preview SPA**: a successful render that came back as `html` (`q2-html-render`, `pdf`, …) shows a "no live preview in q2 preview … run `q2 render`" message naming the format instead of `console.error` + the boot screen.
- **e2e**: the iframe kind names the renderer (`q2-html-render | q2-debug | q2-preview`, no default); smoke-all picks the kind from the fixture's own front matter; the CSS assertion helper reads the render string instead of the old iframe's DOM.
- **Phase 4b (partial)**: the draft-alert banner now renders in q2-preview (bd-3cpv7dah); the three title-banner fixtures pin placement on the render output instead of a `body >` selector the React root can never satisfy (bd-xiz1a2go). Each is its own commit.

## Known: 6 fixtures keep their e2e DOM assertions skipped

`DOM_ASSERTIONS_PENDING_PARITY` (`hub-client/e2e/helpers/smokeAllDiscovery.ts`) lists fixtures whose `ensureHtmlElements` selectors do not yet hold in the q2-preview iframe. Only that assertion type is skipped — the fixtures still render in the default iframe with their regex / CSS / diagnostics assertions live — and each skip logs a `[smoke-diag] dom-assertions-skipped strand=…` line. title: quarto-math: MathML Core writer (bd-9z83tcv0)
description:
Phase 2 of `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-21-equation-numbering-and-mathml.md` (strand bd-9z83tcv0). **Stacked on #706** (quarto-math); quarto-math only.

## What this adds

`Target::MathMl` and `crates/quarto-math/src/mathml.rs`: `MathAst` → one complete `<math>` element, written against MathML Core only (the subset every current browser renders natively):

- coarse runs split into `mi`/`mn`/`mo` via `split::split_run`, one letter per `mi`; `-` becomes U+2212, `'` a prime;
- symbols classify by alphabet (Greek → `mi`, uppercase Greek upright, relations/arrows → `mo`); bare delimiters get `stretchy="false"`, `\left…\right` fences stretch;
- big operators place limits by mode, the integral family keeps side limits, `\limits` pins `movablelimits="false"`; functions get U+2061 function application;
- `\mathbf`/`\mathbb`/`\mathcal`/… map characters into the Mathematical Alphanumeric Symbols block (holes included), since Core keeps only `mathvariant="normal"`; `\text` keeps edge spaces as NBSP;
- environments become `mtable` (fenced matrices, `{` for cases, right/left `columnalign` for aligned); a top-level `\\` becomes a table of lines; `\cancel` emits `menclose` (plan decision 3).

The source TeX rides in `<semantics>` as an `application/x-tex` annotation, so `Normalized` gains a `text` field.

## Tests

A corpus-wide validity check (quick-xml walk: Core element allowlist, fixed child counts for `mfrac`/`msub`/…/`munderover`, `mathvariant` only `normal`), 263 per-fixture snapshots, 13 structural tests, unit tests for the variant table and accents.

## Normalizer fix found by the snapshots

Primes were dropped (`f'` → `f`; the committed Typst snapshot for `basic/prime` read `f ( x ) = f ( x )`). mitex parses `f'` as an attachment without a `^`/`_` operator and `attach` returned only the base. Now a prime is a superscript `Sym`, repeated primes merge into `″`/`‴`/`⁗`, and `x'^2` shares the superscript slot (5 tests in `normalize.rs`). Six snapshots changed (`basic/prime`, `scripts/prime-with-sup` × normalize/OMML/Typst). The same fixture shows mitex taking `= f` as the base of `f''` after a relation — filed as bd-0mzhnxft.

## Verification

`cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` green; the crate checks for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

title: Equation numbering as a format-specific post-filter stage (bd-vlhi2zkj)
description: Phase 1 of `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-21-equation-numbering-and-mathml.md` (strand bd-vlhi2zkj). Independent of quarto-math; lands on `main` first so the stacked MathML PRs on #706 can build on it. ## Why `CrossrefRenderTransform` appended `\tag{N}` to every numbered equation's TeX. `\tag` is an amsmath command only MathJax and KaTeX read: Quarto 1 emits it solely for those two engines and writes `\qquad(N)` otherwise, and any converter that reads math alone (Pandoc's, quarto-math's for the coming `html-math-method: mathml`) rejects the whole expression. The encoding of the number is a presentation decision, so it leaves the format-agnostic transform. ## What changes - **Crossref-render** leaves the `Math` text byte-identical and records the number on the reserved span attribute **`quarto-eq-number`** (`EQ_NUMBER_ATTR` in `crossref/mod.rs`). - **New `EquationNumberStage`**, placed after `UserFiltersStage::post` and before `CodeHighlightStage`, encodes the number from the format and `html-math-method`: `\tag{N}` for MathJax/KaTeX, ` \qquad(N)` for `plain`/unknown, a sibling `span.quarto-eq-number` outside the math (plus a `quarto-eq-sibling-number` modifier class) for `mathml`, nothing for non-HTML formats. It removes the attribute in every case. Running after the post filters is the point: a Lua filter can read, rewrite or delete `el.attributes["quarto-eq-number"]` — documented in the Lua filters guide as the supported way to customize equation numbers. - **`math_method.rs`** parses `html-math-method` once (string and object forms); `MathEngine::from_meta` in math-js maps over it so the two stages cannot drift. - **`equation-number.scss`**, a shared SCSS layer loaded at every HTML compile site and in `assemble_reveal_scss` (like `copy-code.scss`), lays the sibling label out at the right edge of the equation row. - The pipeline design doc gains a "post-filter presentation slot" section; `Equation.tsx`'s comment points at the stage (the preview keeps its own KaTeX `\tag` append). ## Tests Written first. Crossref-render unit tests assert the attribute instead of the tag; 13 stage unit tests (encodings, selection, walker); 13 end-to-end tests in `equation_numbering_pipeline.rs` covering every encoding, revealjs, KaTeX, the object form, unlabelled math, sequential numbering, and Lua post filters rewriting/deleting the number plus a pin that pre filters never see it; quarto-sass asserts the layer in the HTML and revealjs CSS. Collateral: the HTML stage-list assertions (25 → 26 stages) and the `styles.css` byte-identity baseline (`tests/fixtures/phase5-single-doc-baseline/expected_hashes.txt`, re-captured with a dated note; the layer is additive, `doc.html` unchanged). ## Verification Full `cargo xtask verify` green. End-to-end through `cargo run --bin q2 -- render` (recorded in the plan): default → `\tag{1}` inside the math with MathJax loaded; `plain` → ` \qquad(1)`; `mathml` → `(1)` after the math and no engine loaded. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: quarto-math: TeX math front end with OMML and Typst writers (Phase 1)
description:
Phase 1 of `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-21-quarto-math-and-native-docx.md` (strand bd-entbg6x3, epic bd-pq9k90z2: native docx writer). **Stacked on #705** (pampa `Math.text_source`), which it builds on; **draft** while both are held.

## What this adds

A new crate `quarto-math`, a micro-pandoc for math expressions: one reader, a spec we own, one writer per target.

- **Reader** (`reader.rs`): the mitex LaTeX parser, vendored under `crates/quarto-math/vendor/` (4 crates, Apache-2.0, 7 documented local patches in `VENDORED.md`), plus a leaf → original-span side table. Macro bodies map to their definition, macro arguments to the use site.
- **Spec** (`spec/commands.json`, 1013 rows): generated by `cargo xtask gen-math-spec` from mitex's spec dump plus `spec/overrides.json`, with `codex` resolving Typst symbol names to Unicode. Each row is `{parse: mitex item, sem: writer semantics, typst: alias}`. Drift, coverage and corpus-acceptance tests.
- **`MathAst` + normalization** (`ast.rs`, `normalize.rs`): folded scripts, bound `\limits`, resolved `\left…\right`, environments split into rows/cells, symbols resolved, exact nested spans, errors as nodes plus problems; never panics.
- **Diagnostics** (`diagnostics.rs`): `Q-22-1`…`Q-22-13` under a new `math` subsystem (catalog, `docs/errors/math/` pages, sidebar). Locations are substrings of the math text's `SourceInfo` (pampa's `Math.text_source` from #705).
- **OMML writer** (`omml.rs`): every fixture validates against the vendored ECMA-376 `shared-math.xsd` (12-file transitional closure under `tests/schemas/ooxml/`, from python-docx's `ref/`).
- **Typst writer** (`typst.rs`): plain Typst math, no mitex prelude; every syntax choice probed against Typst 0.15; the whole corpus compiles in one `typst compile` (skipped without the binary).
- **`convert()` seam** (`convert.rs`): the entry point the docx/Typst writers will call. Output is withheld when the tree has an error so writers fall back to verbatim TeX. End-to-end test through pampa: a block-quoted multi-line equation with an unknown command yields a diagnostic that resolves to exactly the `.qmd` bytes.

Fixture corpus: 263 TeX snippets in 14 groups (`tests/fixtures/`), including 26 copied verbatim from `docs/`, the Q1 test corpus and quarto-web; each is snapshotted for the AST, OMML and Typst.

## Not in this PR

Phase 2 (OPC package layer, validation harness), Phase 3 (docx writer, `--to docx` wiring), Phase 4 (sidecars, comment round trip). MathML is bd-9z83tcv0. Two mitex macro-engine gaps (`\def` with parameters, optional macro arguments) are filed as bd-f047ynng and allowlisted.

`cargo xtask verify` (full: lint, clippy, workspace tests, ts-packages, hub-client build and tests) passed at the tip. 138 tests in quarto-math and the vendored crates plus the pampa seam tests.

title: pampa: record byte-for-byte provenance of Math.text (Math.text_source)
description:
Prerequisite for the `quarto-math` crate (bd-entbg6x3, plan `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-21-quarto-math-and-native-docx.md`, Phase 0). Strand: bd-ieldbghj.

**Opened as a draft on purpose:** the branch is complete and verified, but we are holding the merge for a while (it will follow #704). Expected rebase conflicts against `main` once #704 lands are three regenerable artifacts only: `Cargo.lock`, `crates/pampa/snapshots/json/math-with-attr.snap`, `ts-packages/annotated-qmd/examples/academic-paper.json`.

## Why

`Math.source_info` spans the whole `$…$` / `$$…$$` node, but `Math.text` is not a plain substring of it once a math node spans lines: the reader folds each soft break of inline math to a literal `\n` and strips the block-continuation gutter (`> `, list indentation) from the interior lines of display math. A consumer that parses `text` further (the coming `quarto-math` crate) needs to map any byte of it back to the `.qmd`.

## What

- **quarto-pandoc-types:** `Math.text_source: Option<SourceInfo>`, length equal to `text.len()`, `map_offset(i)` lands on the byte `text[i]` came from. `None` means no mapping finer than `source_info` is known.
- **pampa reader:** `location::provenance_builder_with_context` (a `ProvenanceBuilder` rooted the way `node_source_info_with_context` roots node spans). Inline math: text segments verbatim, a bare `\n` soft break verbatim, any other soft break (gutter, CRLF) a replacement so the folded newline maps to the source line ending. Display math: first line and every `\n` verbatim, each stripped gutter a zero-length replacement. The strip behavior itself is unchanged (bd-q6ed / bd-qpa2 still own it).
- **JSON wire:** new `textS` sidecar (bare pool ref) after `t`, emitted by both the `Value` and the streaming writer, read back by the reader; absent/null reads as `None`. Documented next to `a`/`targetS` in `claude-notes/designs/raw-json-format.md`.
- **Filters and transforms:** Lua assignment to `.text` clears the mapping; `pandoc.Math()` builds with `None`; `crossref_render` keeps the mapping when appending `\tag{N}` by concatenating a zero-width synthesized piece; every other constructor passes `None`.
- **Strip lists:** `textS` added to Rust `remove_location_fields` and the TS `stripSourceInfoFields` (+ unit test), `pampaOracle`, tiptap spike `canonical`/`pampa`; `textS?: number` on the TS `Annotated_Inline_Math` type.

## Tests

- `crates/pampa/tests/integration/math_text_source.rs` (15): single- and multi-line inline math, blockquote and list gutters, display math plain / quoted / nested-quoted / listed / labeled / inside strong, several nodes per paragraph, JSON round trip of `textS`, JSON without the sidecar reads as `None`, and a sweep over every in-tree `.qmd` with math (21 files, 36 nodes) asserting each text byte maps inside the node span to the identical source byte unless it is a folded newline.
- quarto-core `crossref_render`: `equation_tag_extends_text_source_instead_of_dropping_it`.
- `test_location_health` validates `text_source` alongside `source_info`.

## Snapshot changes (reviewed)

- `crates/pampa/snapshots/json/math-with-attr.snap` (1 file): each of the three `Math` nodes gains a `textS` ref and the pool gains the matching body ranges (e.g. `29..37` for `E = mc^2` inside `$E = mc^2$` at `28..38`). Nothing else changed.
- `ts-packages/annotated-qmd/examples/academic-paper.json` regenerated with the live `pampa -t json` binary (guard test); only `textS` refs and pool rows added.

## Verification

`cargo nextest run --workspace` (14,032 passed) and full `cargo xtask verify` (all steps passed) on this branch.

title: q2 preview --static: Quarto-1-style preview (render, serve, watch, lazy execution)
description:
## Summary

Adds `--static` to `q2 preview` (bd-sl79jjiq): the Quarto-1-style preview early testers asked for. It renders the document or project to disk through the same path `q2 render` uses, serves the output directory over a static HTTP server, watches the sources, re-renders what changed, and reloads the browser over a server-sent-events channel injected into every served page. None of the hub / SPA / WASM machinery behind the default `q2 preview` is involved, so it also works in a checkout that has never built the SPA.

Plan and design: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-22-q2-preview-static.md`.

- **CLI**: `q2 preview --static [PATH] [--no-watch] [--no-navigate] [--to FORMAT]` plus the existing `--port/--host/--no-browser/--browser`. Hub-mode flags are rejected alongside it. Only `html` and `revealjs` are served.
- **`render_once`** extracted from the render command so one process can render repeatedly; `q2 render` stderr is byte-identical on clean / warning / error fixtures.
- **`quarto_preview::static_mode`**: the router (index/default-file/listing for `/`, directory redirects, the site's `404.html`, `no-store`, traversal refusal, mime_guess types, client injected before `</body>`), the SSE reload channel, the inline client (badge, diagnostics panel, navigate-or-reload, reload-on-reconnect), and a pure change classifier (ignore / subset / full).
- **Driver**: input edits are `RenderMode::Subset` renders (dependency-graph augmented); config, extension, and resource edits are full renders (0.7 s for the 295-page docs site). A failed re-render keeps the old output and shows the diagnostics in the browser. Startup order is watcher → signal handlers → bind → print URL, so nothing can connect before edits are observable.
- **Lazy code execution**: a new `ExecutionPolicy {All, None, Only(set)}` in `quarto-core`, plumbed like the engine registry override and consulted by the engine stage right after the pure resolver. `--static` renders `Only(viewed pages)`; the first view of a page with code executes it and reloads. `preview.engine: off` disables execution. `q2 render` is unchanged (`All`).
- **Config**: Quarto 1's `project: preview: {port, host, browser, watch-inputs, navigate}` are the defaults; CLI flags win; `timeout` / `serve` warn as unsupported.
- **Docs**: a new *Previewing* guide page; `scripts.qmd` notes that `--static` runs render scripts on every re-render.

Deferred follow-ups are filed as seven strands linked to bd-sl79jjiq (stale-only startup, resource→page invalidation, deleted-output cleanup, `--timeout`/IDE channel, PDF viewer, site-path 404 rewriting, open-page-first full renders). Also filed: bd-6d9ew2up (upstream color switch for `TextRenderOptions`; the browser text strips ANSI until then) and bd-b53re0r9 (`wasm-quarto-hub-client/Cargo.lock` is stale on `main`; every full verify rewrites it).

## Test plan
