title: Support docx, pptx, epub, and typst output via Pandoc writers
description:
## Summary

Quarto can now render `docx`, `pptx`, `epub`, and `typst` documents by handing its own document representation to Pandoc's native writers, rather than routing them through Quarto's own HTML-only rendering path. To do this, Quarto feeds its custom AST nodes — crossrefs, callouts, theorems, tabsets, floats — over a documented wire format to a vendored copy of Quarto 1's Lua filter pipeline, which turns them into the constructs each Pandoc writer understands.

Trigger a format the same way as any other: `format: docx`, `format: pptx`, `format: epub`, or `format: typst` in front matter or `_quarto.yml`, or `--to <format>` on the command line. `docx`, `pptx`, and `epub` shell out to a `pandoc` binary on `PATH` (or one pointed to by `QUARTO_PANDOC`); `typst` shells out the same way to a `typst` binary (or `QUARTO_TYPST`) and compiles the intermediate `.typ` source to a PDF.

## What carries over from Quarto 1

- **Cross-references and numbering** — `@fig-`, `@tbl-`, `@eq-`, and theorem-family refs resolve and number correctly in every new format. Typst numbers natively through its own compiler rather than through Quarto's numbering pass, so the two always agree.
- **Callouts and theorems** (`callout-note`, `.theorem`, proofs, etc.) render with their format-appropriate styling.
- **Tabsets** render their content in every format; EPUB and (where applicable) other non-interactive readers show all panels expanded rather than collapsing to one active tab, since there's no JavaScript to hide the rest.
- **Captions, figures, and images** — including image resource staging into the output container (e.g. `word/media/` in docx).
- **`reference-doc` / `template`** for docx/pptx, and custom `.typ` templates for typst, resolve the same way other Quarto paths do and fail with a clear diagnostic if the file is missing.
- **`brand.yml`** colors and typography apply to typst output the same way they apply to other formats.
- **Typst margin notes** via the vendored `marginalia` package, and automatic fetching of any additional Typst Universe package a document's raw Typst content references.
- **EPUB-specific options**: `epub-chapter-level`, `epub-cover-image`, `epub-metadata`, `epub-embed-font`, and an additional `css` stylesheet merged with Quarto's own callout/layout styles.
- **`content-hidden` / `when-format` conditional content** is honored for all of these formats, including content nested inside custom nodes.

## Rendering more than one format

If a document's front matter declares more than one `format:`, Quarto still renders only one target per invocation — but it now warns, naming which format it used and which it skipped, instead of silently dropping the others.

## Known gaps

- **`latex`/`pdf` is not yet supported** — `--to pdf` and `--to latex` still refuse to render.
- **Mermaid diagrams don't rasterize** in docx/pptx/epub: no image is embedded, though the code cell's source text is preserved in the output. (Quarto 1 renders these through a headless browser; the new pipeline doesn't yet invoke one.)
- **Pandoc-specific failures get their own diagnostics instead of a generic error.** New `Q-20-*` codes cover a missing `pandoc` binary, a version too old, a nonzero pandoc exit (with its stderr/filter traceback attached), and a couple of internal wire-format consistency checks.

title: Fix Windows dead-code build failure in dial-back test helpers
description:
On Windows, `cargo xtask verify`'s clippy pass (`-D warnings`) fails with `constant DIALBACK_PREAMBLE is never used` and two similar errors for `DIALBACK_READ_UNTIL_EOF` and `deno_dialback_child` in `crates/quarto-core/src/engine/ts_process.rs`. Linux CI and Mac contributors never see this.

## Root Cause

Those three items are gated `#[cfg(test)]` only. Their only callers are `proc_tests` (this file) and `registry.rs`'s `test_shutdown_all_kills_ts_engine`, both gated `unix`-only. On Windows `unix` is false, so both callers compile out entirely, leaving the three items with zero callers in the Windows test build — hence dead code. On Linux and Mac `unix` is true, so the callers compile in and the items are used, and the warning never fires there.

The loopback-TCP dial-back mechanism itself is not unix-specific — `ensure_started`/`start_with_command` use it unconditionally in production, and `accept_and_handshake` even has an explicit Windows accommodation for blocking-mode sockets. `proc_tests` is unix-gated because two of its seven tests use genuinely unix-only checks (a `kill -0` PID-liveness probe, and a self-SIGKILL exit-code assertion); `registry.rs`'s test has no unix-specific check of its own and is only conservatively gated to match.

## Fix

Tighten the three items' gate to `#[cfg(all(test, unix))]`, matching their callers exactly. This changes zero test execution on any platform — `proc_tests` already never ran on Windows before this fix, and still doesn't after it; the change only stops the Windows build from failing on a dead-code false positive.

Also corrected a stale header comment on `proc_tests` (it claimed `/bin/sleep`/`sh -c` dependencies that had already moved to portable `#[cfg(unix)]`/`#[cfg(not(unix))]` helper pairs elsewhere in the file), and added a `cross-platform.md` rule: a test helper's cfg gate must match its only caller's gate exactly, since Windows isn't in CI and this class of mismatch is otherwise invisible until someone builds on Windows.

A separate follow-up (not in this PR) would make `proc_tests`'s five portable tests actually run on Windows by per-test-gating the two genuinely unix-only ones instead of gating the whole mod — that's real new coverage, this PR is just the minimal unblock.

## Test Plan

- [x] `cargo clippy -p quarto-core --tests -- -D warnings` on Windows — confirms the three dead-code errors are gone
- [ ] Existing Linux CI gate (`cargo xtask verify`) — unaffected by this change, passes as before

title: Fix lint:css exception matching on Windows
description:
On Windows, cargo xtask verify fails at the hub-client lint:css step even though no CSS was touched. Every grandfathered violation in lint-css-exceptions.json reports twice: once as a fresh violation and once as a stale-exception.

The lint script keys violations and exceptions by the file path relative to src/, computed with node:path's relative(). On Windows that returns backslash separators (components\Editor.css), while lint-css-exceptions.json was generated on macOS/Linux and uses forward slashes (components/Editor.css). The lookup in scripts/lint-css.mjs:239 never matches, so every exception both fails to suppress its violation and gets reported as stale.

Normalize the relative path to forward slashes before using it as a lookup key.

Verified with `npm run lint:css` in hub-client on Windows: previously exited 1 with ~140 spurious errors, now reports clean.

title: Hephaestus plot documents (.hep): render to SVG with brand colors, and live preview in q2 preview / hub-client (bd-3qych45b)
description: ## Summary Phases 1 and 2 of [hephaestus](https://github.com/posit-dev/hephaestus) support (bd-3qych45b, plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-17-hephaestus-hep-integration.md`). ### Phase 1 — `q2 render` (native) - `![](plot.hep)` in `html` / `revealjs` output is rendered at render time with hephaestus's **renderer-free SVG backend** (no wgpu, no GPU), stored as a page-scoped artifact under `_files/figure-html/`, and the image is pointed at it. Size comes from `width`/`height` attrs, else the document's own hint, else 7in × 5in at 96 dpi; the plot re-flows at that size rather than being scaled. - **Brand colors**: with `brand:` declared, the light brand's `background` / `foreground` / `primary` become the plot's `paper` / `ink` / `accent`. Only hex values cross; anything else warns (`Q-19-4`). - **Bundled Roboto faces** (`resources/hephaestus/fonts/`, OFL) are registered once per process and mapped onto `sans-serif`, so the same `.hep` renders byte-identically on every machine and matches what hephaestus's browser client draws. - New `image` diagnostics subsystem, `Q-19-1`..`Q-19-4`, each with a docs page and sidebar entry. Failures are warnings and leave the image as written. (Numbered 18 until the merge of main, where the new `engine` subsystem had taken 18.) - `transforms/image_walk.rs`: the mutable body-image walker extracted from `responsive_image` so both transforms share one container set. - Runnable example: `examples/plots/01-hephaestus-basic` (captioned figure, explicit size, missing-file case, dark brand). ### Phase 2 — `q2 preview` and hub-client (bd-sxiv2tio) - `HepImage` in `@quarto/preview-renderer` is the registry's `Image` entry: for a local `.hep` target it fetches the asset-walker bytes and mounts a live `PlotView` from the npm `hephaestus-svg-wasm` client (0.4.1, exact-pinned to the crate version; parity tests on both sides); anything else delegates to the plain ``. Covers q2-preview documents and `format: revealjs` decks in both `q2 preview` and hub-client, since `RevealDeck` renders slide content through the same registry. - The client loads on demand (cached dynamic import); plot-free documents never fetch the 2.4 MB wasm. Its Roboto faces ship as hashed assets in every bundle (SPA, hub-client, sandboxed frame). - Sizing: `width` attr → document hint → 672 px, capped at the column, height via CSS `aspect-ratio`, so narrow columns and slides get a re-solved layout while wide columns match `q2 render`. - `.hep` added to the binary-extension allowlists (`quarto-hub::resource` and its `quarto-automerge-schema` mirror) — without it the bytes never reached the preview VFS. - Manifest miss → "file not found in the project" error box; load failures → error box with the message. - Not in this PR: the separate-origin sandboxed frame (bd-9t5nmq81) and brand colors in the browser, which need an upstream palette API on the wasm client (bd-qcltc0ll). ### Why SVG and not PNG hephaestus rasterizes through wgpu, which needs a GPU adapter a headless render machine may not have, and GPU output is not byte-stable across machines. The SVG backend needs no GPU, keeps text as real ``, and is deterministic. PDF/Typst outputs plug into the same transform later (`latex` → the `pdf` backend, `typst` → SVG) — bd-br9bmysi. ### Dependency notes - quarto-core gains `hephaestus = 0.4.1` (`document-read`, `svg`, `png`) in the native-only table; both `Cargo.lock`s pick up parley / fontique / skrifa / kurbo / peniko / clipper2-rust / png. All pure Rust. The main WASM bundle does not compile hephaestus. - On Linux, parley → fontique would link `libfontconfig` at build time by default. fontique's `fontconfig-dlopen` feature is enabled for Linux so building q2 does **not** require `libfontconfig1-dev`; a missing library at run time just yields an empty system font collection (fine — plot text uses the bundled faces). - preview-renderer gains `hephaestus-svg-wasm = 0.4.1` (npm, MIT); `optimizeDeps.exclude` in hub-client and the SPA keeps dev pre-bundling from breaking its `import.meta.url` asset lookups. ## Test plan - [x] `crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/hephaestus_render.rs`: end-to-end tests through `render_to_file` (artifact path, determinism, bundled font, sizing, id prefixes, revealjs, untouched non-hep images, missing / invalid file, brand applied / non-hex slot / no brand) + unit tests, incl. the npm-version parity test. - [x] `HepImage.test.tsx` (20 cases: mount, delegation, external/data targets, load-once, errors, `free()` on unmount, remount on new bytes, sizing rules, a11y attrs, registry layering, version pin vs `package.json` and `Cargo.lock`); `resource.rs` + `fileType.test.ts` for the `.hep` extension. - [x] Full `cargo xtask verify` green (Rust + WASM + hub-client build/tests + SPA), before and after merging main. - [x] `cargo run --bin q2 -- render examples/plots/01-hephaestus-basic`, output inspected. - [x] Browser checks (recorded in the plan): `q2 preview` html document + revealjs deck; hub-client (`q2 preview --ui editor`) `format: q2-preview` document + revealjs deck. Plots mount as reflowed SVG; missing file shows the error box; `.png` stays an ``. - [x] CI green on Linux, macOS and Windows on the phase-1 and phase-2 pushes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: perf: push-into AST traversal, no postprocess deep clones, mimalloc, and a 32-byte SourceInfo (bd-w0x91nmh, bd-1c085k3a)
description:
## Summary

Two rounds of allocation-side work from the fact-finding note `claude-notes/research/2026-09-19-topdown-traverse-alloc-perf.md`, measured on the Connect docs (`docs-quarto-2`) with a `release-perf` build on an M-series Mac.

**Round 1 (bd-w0x91nmh):**
- **`pampa::filters` push-into traversal.** `topdown_traverse_{inline,block}_into` append to the caller's `Vec` instead of returning `vec![node]` for every visited node, and `walk_vec` reserves the input length. A no-op pass over a 200k-inline document goes from 268k to 43k allocations and 29 ms to 15 ms. Public signatures unchanged.
- **`postprocess`: no deep clones.** The combined `with_inlines` closure moves inlines through instead of cloning every element twice; `merge_strs` moves `Str` text instead of cloning it.
- **mimalloc as the `q2` binary's `#[global_allocator]`.** Native only. Decision D4 in `claude-notes/plans/2026-07-28-linux-release-static-musl.md` deferred this until a real repro existed — this is it.

**Round 2 (bd-1c085k3a, plan `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-19-source-info-generated-box.md`):**
- **`SourceInfo` shrinks from 136 to 32 bytes** via `quarto-source-map` 0.2.0 (posit-dev/quarto-source-map#7), which boxes the `Generated` payload. Every AST node carries at least one `SourceInfo`, so with no change to `quarto-pandoc-types`, `Inline` goes from 776 to 360 bytes and `Block` from 1552 to 824. This PR migrates q2's 114 `Generated { .. }` sites (constructions → `SourceInfo::generated` / `generated_with`, patterns → `Generated(g)`) and bumps `quarto-source-map` 0.2.0, `quarto-yaml` 0.2.0 and `quarto-error-reporting` 0.3.0 in both cargo workspaces (root and `crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client`); `cargo tree -d` shows a single copy of each. The serialized JSON shape is unchanged (newtype variant of a struct) — **no `.snap` file changed**.

## Timings (hyperfine, warm, back to back)

| | `main` | round 1 | round 1 + 2 (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size_of` `SourceInfo` / `Inline` / `Block` | 136 / 776 / 1552 | same | **32 / 360 / 824** |
| `api/index.qmd` alone (10 runs) | 1.049 s | 0.875 s | **0.680 s** (−35%) |
| full site, `QUARTO_JOBS=1`, 352 files (3 runs) | 5.657 s | 4.758 s | **4.025 s** (−29%) |

Root cause, for the record: memmove was 27.5% of the render profile because every by-value move in any walker copies a whole `Inline`/`Block`. Remaining levers (boxing `Link`/`Image` source infos and `Table` in `quarto-pandoc-types`; an in-place `&mut` visitor for the read-mostly passes) are described in the research note and not part of this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `crates/pampa/tests/integration/topdown_traverse_alloc_budget.rs`: a counting global allocator in the pampa integration binary asserts a no-op traversal makes ≤ ~2 allocations per container (fails on the old traversal: 10,708 vs budget 264), and `ast_node_size_ceilings` pins `SourceInfo` ≤ 32, `Inline` ≤ 400, `Block` ≤ 900.
- [x] `cargo xtask verify` (full, including hub-client WASM build and tests) green against the released crates: 13,997 Rust tests, all TS suites.
- [x] No snapshot files changed.
- [ ] **Open:** whether `libmimalloc-sys` builds on the static musl release legs. Its `build.rs` has no libc-specific branches and upstream supports musl, but nothing here has exercised it — the nightly will tell.

title: Nightly release workflow: build main as a rolling 'nightly' prerelease whenever it has unreleased changes (bd-p4ljdp2e)
description:
## What

A scheduled `Nightly` workflow that, every night `main` has changes no release has shipped, builds it through the **same** pipeline releases use and publishes the result as a rolling **prerelease** on the `nightly` tag. Stable releases stay human-cut via the runbook; `releases/latest` never returns a prerelease, so the stable install one-liners are unaffected.

Plan with decisions, evidence and run records: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-19-nightly-release-workflow.md`. Strand: bd-p4ljdp2e.

## How

- **`release-pipeline.yml`** (new, `on: workflow_call`): the build / verify / sign / publish jobs moved out of `release.yml` verbatim (comment blocks kept), keyed on inputs `ref`, `version`, `tag`, `channel` (`release` | `nightly`), `publish`, `notes_range`. A `check-inputs` job rejects channel/tag/version mismatches before any runner is spent. `publish: false` builds, verifies and signs, then uploads the would-be release as a `release-set` artifact (dry run).
- **`release.yml`**: now trigger + preflight + `uses:` the pipeline; gains a `publish` dispatch checkbox for dry runs.
- **`nightly.yml`** (new): cron `0 8 * * *` → `scripts/nightly-gate.sh` (skip iff HEAD is exactly the newest `v*` tag or the current `nightly` tag) → pipeline with `channel: nightly` → `install-smoke` on ubuntu / macOS / Windows running the README one-liners against the fresh nightly and asserting `q2 --version`. That smoke job is the first CI that exercises either installer against a real release.
- **Version**: `<next minor>-nightly.<YYYYMMDD>` (e.g. `0.33.0-nightly.20260919`, sorts above the release it contains), injected at build time via a new `QUARTO_VERSION_OVERRIDE` (`option_env!` in `quarto-util`) so `Cargo.toml` and both lockfiles stay untouched and `--locked` holds. A malformed override fails at compile time. Every consumer of "the Quarto version" now reads one function, so `q2 --version`, the HTML `generator` tag, the cache key, the `version` template variable, the LSP server info, the asset filenames and the release title all carry the same string; the pipeline's verify gate enforces it.
- **Installers**: `install.sh --nightly` / `install.ps1 -Nightly` resolve the `nightly` release by tag and pick the platform asset by name. Checksum and signature checks are unchanged. `Q2_RELEASES_API_BASE` is an offline-test seam for the tags lookup only (threat model documented above the variable and in the plan: it exposes strictly less than the existing `--artifact-url` flag, and the pinned-key signature check remains the trust boundary — one test redirects the seam and proves the install is refused).
- **Docs**: README nightly one-liners; runbook § Nightlies + dry-run recipe; two stale claims fixed (CLAUDE.md's "one approving review", the installer test header's "smoke-tested by the release workflow").

## Tests

Written first, per CLAUDE.md: `quarto-util` version helper unit tests; 8 offline `bootstrap_sh.rs` cases for `--nightly`; 15 `nightly_gate.rs` cases driving the script against throwaway repos; cache-key build-id wiring. `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` green. actionlint + YAML parse clean on all three workflows.

## Verification

- **Local**: an override build prints `q2 (quarto 2) 0.33.0-nightly.20260919` and renders `<meta name="generator" content="quarto-rust-0.33.0-nightly.20260919">`; a plain build prints `0.32.0`.
- **CI dry run of the refactored pipeline**: run [35456861792](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/35456861792) — `release.yml` from this branch against `v0.32.0` with `publish=false`. Every job green. The `release-set` artifact has the same 18-asset file set as the published v0.32.0, checksums verify, every `.minisig` verifies against the pinned key, the darwin binary runs natively with bundled hub defaults and a real docs embed; no release or tag touched.
- **Not yet possible from a branch**: GitHub only registers a `workflow_dispatch` workflow once it exists on the default branch, so `nightly.yml` has had no run. After merge: `gh workflow run nightly.yml -f force=true -f publish=false` (dry run of the nightly channel), then `-f force=true -f publish=true` for the first real nightly, which also fires `install-smoke` (the first execution of `install.ps1 -Nightly` — no pwsh here to parse it). The following scheduled run should skip.

## Follow-ups (filed / listed in the plan)

- bd-5qepzwst: Lua `quarto.version` is hardcoded to `{0,1,0}` (found while inventorying version consumers).
- bd-9nf0ucdf (docs embed recompiles q2 per example, 31 of the 40 web-payloads minutes) is now paid nightly.
- Auto-cutting stable releases would be one more caller of `release-pipeline.yml`, if ever wanted.

title: pampa: drop two redundant tree walks from the qmd reader (~6% of read)
description:
Removes two full tree-sitter walks that `readers::qmd::read` did on every parse, besides the one that builds the AST. Profiled with samply on the 1.1 MB `q2-connect-docs` `api/index.qmd` (`release-perf` build):

| callee of `read` (share of all samples) | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `print_whole_tree` into `io::sink()` | 2.44% | — |
| `concrete_tree_depth` | 1.63% | — |
| `treesitter_to_pandoc` (now also does the depth check) | 23.61% | 22.70% |
| **`read` total** | **45.01%** | **38.95%** |

Two commits, one per change, for easier review.

### 1. Fold the depth check into the conversion walk (bd-t7i6oanu)

The "too deeply nested" check, which stops fuzzer-style inputs from overflowing the stack later on, used to be its own pass over the tree. ~90% of its cost was tree-sitter's cursor code, so a tighter loop wouldn't have helped much; the saving comes from dropping the walk.

- `quarto-treesitter-ast` gains `bottomup_traverse_concrete_tree_with_depth_limit`, which stops with `DepthLimitExceeded` as soon as it *enters* a node past the limit, before the visitor has run on anything that deep. The existing unlimited traversal now calls it with `usize::MAX`, so there is still one implementation.
- `treesitter_to_pandoc` uses it with `MAX_CONCRETE_TREE_DEPTH`. `utils/concrete_tree_depth.rs` is deleted.
- **The same documents are accepted as before.** The old count started at 1 and also counted the root, so `> 100` really meant "deepest node at depth ≥ 100". The new limit is 99, with a comment explaining why.
- **User-visible:** the message is now `too deeply nested (more than 99 levels)`. It used to report the true maximum depth, which a walk that stops early doesn't know.

### 2. Stop dumping the tree on every read (bd-khect2gq)

`read` wrote a line for every node into the caller's verbose stream. Only `pampa -v` reads that stream. quarto-core passes `io::sink()`, which still paid for the walk and the formatting, and include expansion passes a `Vec` it never reads. - **User-visible:** `pampa -v` now also prints the tree for documents that fail to parse.

- A 5,000-deep nested-span document read on a 2 MiB thread. With the check switched off, this overflows the stack.
- Unit tests for the depth-limited traversal: exact boundary, the visitor never runs past the limit, and the result is identical to the unlimited walk.

title: knitr: render HTML dependencies; Q-18 engine diagnostics for unreadable results and includes
description:
Closes #683.

Any knitr document whose R output attached an HTML dependency (`reactable`, `DT`, every htmlwidget, or a plain `htmltools::htmlDependency`) failed with

```
Failed to parse R results: invalid type: sequence, expected path string
```

Root cause: `execute.R`'s `create_pandoc_includes` wraps each include path in `I()`, so jsonlite emits a one-element array per slot (Quarto 1's declared type is `string[]`), while `KnitrIncludes` typed each slot as a single `Option<PathBuf>`. `gt` "worked" only because it inlines its CSS and attaches no dependency.

## Commit 1 — the fix (`7b456302`)

- `KnitrIncludes` slots are `Vec<PathBuf>`, accepting a bare string, a list, or `null`, via serde visitors (no intermediate `Value`, so field errors keep their path).
- `convert_includes` reads every file in each slot, in order.
- Unit tests include the verbatim results JSON captured from the failing render. New R-gated e2e test `knitr_html_dependency.rs` uses only `htmltools`, so it needs no widget package.
- Verified: `q2 render` of the issue's repro succeeds and the reactable table hydrates in Chrome.

## Commit 2 — engine diagnostics (`50a61b71`)

The parse failure was reported as an uncoded error carrying 500 bytes of the `markdown` field, and the results file was deleted before anyone could look at it. This opens the `engine` (`Q-18`) error subsystem:

- **`Q-18-1` Engine Returned an Unreadable Result.** `ExecutionError::MalformedResult`; `parse_results` deserializes through `serde_path_to_error` (field path down to the element index), keeps the results file on disk via `NamedTempFile::keep()`, and drops the JSON dump (and its byte-slicing panic on a multi-byte boundary).
- **`Q-18-2` Engine Include File Could Not Be Read** (warning, `--strict` promotes). `convert_includes` no longer silently drops an include file it cannot read. `ExecuteResult` gains `warnings`, drained into the stage diagnostics after the capture emit.
- New `engine/diagnostics.rs` is the single seam from `ExecutionError` to `DiagnosticMessage`; the stage's `map_err` goes through it instead of `e.to_string()`. Only `MalformedResult` is coded here; the rest of the variants are bd-yd94iyq9.
- Catalog entries, `docs/errors/engine/Q-18-{1,2}.qmd`, and an `engine` errors-sidebar section.

Both codes were exercised through the real binary with throwaway patches (reverted); the exact output is in the plan. Full `cargo xtask verify` green.

Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-18-knitr-includes-and-engine-result-diagnostics.md` (strand bd-gy2ozix3). Follow-ups: bd-yd94iyq9 (remaining `ExecutionError` variants), bd-rfug8fxo (`quarto-json`).

title: quarto-hub-mcp: size the exit-drain test's budgets to automerge-repo 2.6 (bd-ppu6xmvv)
description:
## Summary

TS Test Suite has been red on every push to `main` since #685 (automerge-repo 2.6.0-alpha.5, bd-d08gpqvu): `exit-drain.test.ts > create_project then immediate stdin EOF must not lose the created docs` trips its 30 s vitest timeout on one platform per push (runs 35245424175 macOS, 35249754405 ubuntu).

**Cause.** Sync between two automerge-repo *JS* peers (the MCP server and the in-process `startTestHub()`) got several times slower with 2.6. Same machine, same probe, dependency trees swapped — drain-to-exit per round, 64 × 64 KB files:

| hub / MCP client | drain to exit |
|---|---|
| 2.5.6 / 2.5.6 | 1.7 / 2.0 / 4.6 s |
| 2.6 / 2.5.6 | 9.8 / 8.0 / 9.5 s |
| 2.5.6 / 2.6 | 7.4 / 22.8 / 26.2 s |
| 2.6 / 2.6 | 10.3 / 20.9 / 33.1 s |

Checking the hub's repo directly shows the 64 docs only finish arriving ~13 s after `create_project` returns; once they've landed the drain exits in <1 s. So it is raw throughput, not a drain-signal bug (zeroing `saveDebounceRate` on the test hub changes nothing). Whole-test time on CI went from 10-13 s to 36-39 s. Against the real Rust hub the drain takes ~5 s with both client versions, so production is not affected; the slow path needs a JS automerge-repo peer as the server, which only the test rig is.

**Change.** Raise the test's drain budget to 60 s and derive the two bounds that must contain it: the exit hang-detector (budget + 5 s) and the vitest timeout (exit bound + 30 s for `create_project` and the hub checks). This also fixes a pre-existing inconsistency: the exit wait was 35 s inside a 30 s vitest timeout, so the exit assertion could never fire and a hung server always surfaced as an opaque "Test timed out". The payload is deliberately unchanged (see the measured floor in the test's header comment).

Chasing the throughput drop upstream in automerge-repo 2.6 is left as follow-up on bd-ppu6xmvv.

title: Self-heal a permanently-stuck index document after an actor-id collision (bd-6f21d4c6)
description:
## What's actually wrong

`actorIdFromUserId` (`hub-client/src/services/userSettings.ts`) deliberately derives a *stable* Automerge actor id from the local `userId`, reused across every session/tab for that user — "instead of a fresh random actor each session," per its own doc comment. That's fine in isolation, but it means two live sessions for the same person (two tabs, a stale tab plus a fresh reconnect) share one actor id. If both commit a local edit to the same document before either has synced the other's change, both edits can end up claiming the same `(actor, seq)` pair — a genuine identity violation, not a CRDT merge conflict.

When that happens, `automerge` correctly throws `RangeError: duplicate seq N found for actor <id>` out of `receiveSyncMessage`. `automerge-repo`'s own `Repo#receiveMessage`, however, catches it with:

```ts
this.synchronizer.receiveMessage(message).catch(err => {
  console.log("error receiving message", { err, message })
})
```

— a bare `console.log`, no retry, no escalation. Because the throw happens before either side's sync state advances, the hub keeps resending the identical colliding change on every subsequent attempt, and the affected client keeps rejecting it, identically, forever. This is not "a client that's a bit behind" — it's a permanent wedge, and the only known workaround was manually clearing the browser's `automerge` IndexedDB database, which nobody would think to automate without knowing the mechanism.

Confirmed directly against the vendored `automerge`/`automerge-repo` v2.5.6 source and reproduced end-to-end: two real `SyncClient`s sharing one actor id, racing a local edit each against a real in-process hub, hit this exact swallowed catch and go permanently stuck.

## What this PR does — and doesn't do

It gets an already-stuck client **unstuck**. It does not stop the collision from happening in the first place — that's a separate, not-yet-attempted fix (either give `actorIdFromUserId` a per-session-unique component, or contribute upstream, where the right primitive — `RepoConfig.actorIdPrefix` — was prototyped in 2024 and never shipped). Scope is deliberately narrow: **index documents only**, not file documents, since the reported symptom is specifically an `IndexDocument` going stale (Q-13-4 squiggles on links to files that genuinely exist).

`installDuplicateSeqRecovery` wraps `repo.synchronizer.receiveMessage` — a public method on `Repo`'s own public `synchronizer` field — at the *instance* level for the connection's own `Repo`. It calls through to the original method and taps its rejection with an additional `.catch()`, so the existing swallow still fires unchanged; nothing in `automerge-repo` is edited, and no other `Repo` instance is affected. On a match (`message.documentId` is this connection's index doc, error is a `RangeError` matching `/duplicate seq \d+ found for actor/`), `recoverIndexDocument` runs the automated, scoped equivalent of the manual IndexedDB wipe, entirely through public API:

- `repo.delete(indexDocId)` — confirmed against source to drop the `DocSynchronizer`'s wedged per-peer `SyncState` for that one document *and* purge its persisted storage entry, leaving every other document untouched.
- `findDoc<IndexDocument>(indexDocId)` (the same retry-aware helper `connect()` already uses) forces a clean full resync from the hub instead of replaying the poisoned local history.
- Swaps in the fresh handle, re-subscribes, and reconciles file/identity/capture state against whatever changed while the client was stuck.

A guard mirrors an existing race-defense already in `findDoc`'s retry loop: if the connection was torn down or replaced while the re-fetch was in flight, the stale result is discarded rather than applied to unrelated new state.

## Why this is safe to ship without touching `automerge-repo`

The monkey-patch is an own-property override on one `Repo` instance (`synchronizer.receiveMessage = wrapped`), not a class/prototype edit — `CollectionSynchronizer.prototype.receiveMessage` in `node_modules` is untouched. If `repo.synchronizer` isn't the expected shape (a few existing tests mock `Repo` without one), installation is a silent no-op rather than a crash — this is a best-effort enhancement, not a required invariant for `connect()` to work.

## Test plan

- `full-stack-actor-collision.test.ts`: two real `SyncClient`s share one actor id against a real `startTestHub()`. Each commits its own `createFile()` synchronously (no `await` between the two calls, so neither can process the other's message first — plain JS run-to-completion semantics, no fake-timer trickery needed). Asserts, in order: the collision + swallowed catch really happen; the fix's recovery log fires; a subsequent edit from an uninvolved third client (different actor id) reaches **both** previously-colliding clients within a bounded window; a second later edit also reaches both, ruling out "one lucky retry."
- Verified **red before green**, per this repo's TDD rule: temporarily commented out both `installDuplicateSeqRecovery` call sites, confirmed the test failed exactly as expected (collision still fires, no recovery log, full poll timeouts consumed), then restored and confirmed green. Stable across repeated runs (~0.4–0.6s each).
- `actor-id-collision.test.ts` independently confirms the underlying collision at the bare-automerge level (no `automerge-repo`, no network, no hub) — the fact the fix's detection regex depends on.
- Full package suite: 140/140. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean in both `quarto-sync-client` and `hub-client` (which bundles this package from source).

Design writeup with both decision points (detection mechanism: wrapping `receiveMessage` vs. sniffing `console.log`; recovery scope: index-doc-only vs. generalized) and the alternatives considered: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-17-index-doc-duplicate-seq-self-heal.md`.

title: chore(npm): @automerge/automerge 3.5.0 + automerge-repo 2.6.0-alpha.5 (bd-d08gpqvu)
description:
Tracks **bd-d08gpqvu**. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-17-automerge-npm-upgrade.md`.

## What

Two commits on the automerge npm stack, across every consumer in the workspace (`hub-client`, `quarto-sync-client`, `quarto-hub-mcp`, `preview-runtime`, plus the `deno.lock` spec mirror):

1. **`@automerge/automerge` 3.4.1 → 3.5.0** (stable minor, released 2026-09-16) and alignment of the drifted `automerge-repo` ranges (`^2.5.1` / `^2.5.4` → `^2.5.6`; the lockfile already resolved 2.5.6 everywhere).
2. **`@automerge/automerge-repo` family 2.5.6 → 2.6.0-alpha.5** (`-network-websocket`, `-react-hooks`, `-storage-indexeddb`, `-storage-nodefs`), with the code port that requires.

## Why the alpha

Upstream has shipped no stable automerge-repo since 2.5.6 (2026-05-18). Everything since May is `2.6.0-alpha.*`, and npm's `latest` dist-tag now points at 2.6.0-alpha.3 (`next` at alpha.5, published 2026-09-16). The alpha line also carries the `uuid` 9 → 14 bump that clears the moderate `uuid` advisory (GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq) `npm audit` reports against the whole 2.5.6 family, plus a long list of robustness fixes (throttle, storage teardown, websocket timers, react-hooks stale results, ephemeral delivery). The decision to take the alpha now rather than wait was made in the session (see the plan).

## What changed upstream, as it hits us

- **Availability moved off the `DocHandle`.** The xstate machine is gone; `DocHandle.state` is only ever `ready`/`deleted`. Availability lives on the new `DocumentQuery` (`repo.findWithProgress(id).peek().state`: `loading` / `ready` / `unavailable` / `failed`).
- **`repo.find()` never hands out an unavailable handle** — it rejects with `Document <id> is unavailable` once every peer answered `doc-unavailable`. `allowableStates` is ignored; `whenReady()` on a handed-out handle resolves at once.
- **`repo.handles` lists a handle for every query, including unavailable ones — and they report `state === 'ready'`.** Anything that read `handles[id].state` as an availability signal silently reads `ready` for a missing doc.
- `DocHandle.doc()` / change payload `doc` are typed `Doc<T> | undefined`.
- `WebSocketClientAdapter.onError` is `() => void` and only logs; `disconnect()` now cancels the queued reconnect (the timer half of the bd-jit6pdwq zombie bug is fixed upstream).

## The port

Three existing tests went red on the bare bump and are the regression tests for this port (they failed before any code change):

- `quarto-sync-client` `doc-inventory.test.ts` / `sync-diagnostics.test.ts` — a dangling index entry reported `handleState: 'ready'` instead of `'unavailable'`.
- `hub-client` `projectSetService.connect.test.ts` — a live peer lacking the collection doc classified as `sync-unreachable` instead of `not-found`.

Changes:

- `quarto-sync-client/src/client.ts`: `getSyncDiagnostics` / `getDocInventory` read the verdict from the *existing* DocumentQuery (`cachedDocState`; never creates a query), guard the now-optional change-payload `doc`.
- `quarto-sync-client/src/StoppableWebSocketClientAdapter.ts`: `onError` takes an optional event to match upstream's `() => void`; subclass/control-test comments updated (upstream fixed the timer path; a direct `connect()` after `disconnect()` still resurrects, which the subclass keeps closed).
- `hub-client/src/services/projectSetService.ts`: `findCollectionDoc`'s second attempt classifies from `find()`'s rejection (unavailable → `not-found`, abort/timeout → `sync-unreachable`) instead of `allowableStates` + `handle.state`; dead `raceHandleReady` removed.
- `hub-client/src/services/presenceService.ts`: guard `doc()` returning undefined.
- `hub-client/src/debug/components/DocumentViewer.tsx`: state badge from a `findWithProgress` subscription (`useDocHandle` can no longer surface `unavailable`).

## Verification

- Fast gate on the alpha: ts-packages builds; vitest — `quarto-automerge-schema` 78, `quarto-sync-client` 137, `preview-runtime` 78, `quarto-hub-mcp` 251, `sync-test-harness` 8 (its **hub tier runs the real Rust hub**, samod 0.13 / automerge 0.11, and passed with the alpha client: create project + reconnect at 0 s / 1 s / 5 s), `hub-client` 1217. `hub-client` typecheck clean; eslint on touched files clean (the repo-wide eslint baseline of ~215 pre-existing problems on `main` is unchanged).
- Full gate: `cargo xtask verify` passed all 14 steps on the final tree (Rust 13,924 tests / 199 skipped; ts-packages builds; hub-client `build:all` incl. WASM; `test:ci`; trace-viewer; preview-*; hub MCP; q2-preview-spa build).
- Not exercised locally: `hub-client` e2e (Playwright) — relying on the `hub-client-e2e` workflow here.

Third commit is the `hub-client/changelog.md` entry (two-commit workflow). Opened for CI; please review before merging.

title: Validate @import'ed partials in the sass cache so edited partials recompile (bd-m3hga05o)
description:
## Summary

Fixes bd-m3hga05o: the compiled-SCSS cache keyed only on the top-level theme file, so editing a partial the theme `@import`s (posit-docs' `_posit-colors.scss`, or any split custom theme) served the previous compile until the user deleted `.quarto/cache/sass` by hand.

The import closure is only known *after* a compile, so it cannot be in the key. Instead the compilers report it and the cache validates it on the next lookup (the make/ninja depfile pattern):

- `SystemRuntime::compile_sass` now returns `SassOutput { css, loaded_files }`. Native: the grass `Fs` adapter records every read that reaches the runtime (embedded Bootstrap excluded). WASM: `jsCompileSass` returns `{ css, loadedUrls }` from dart-sass's `loadedUrls`, mapped to VFS paths.
- Every value in the `sass` namespace is an envelope: a header line, a JSON manifest of `(path, sha256)` for the closure, then the CSS. A lookup re-hashes the listed files; a mismatch is a miss (new `stale` counter in the `perf.sass` gauge) and the recompile overwrites the entry under the same key. The namespace version stamp gains a format tag so pre-envelope entries purge in one go.
- The normalized path from #679 stays in the key; no longer load-bearing, but it keeps same-text themes in different directories apart without a manifest read.

Design and repro: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-14-scss-cache-import-closure.md` (option R, agreed with @cscheid).

## Tests

Written first and seen failing at HEAD: the `ProjectPipeline` end-to-end (stale CSS), the JS bridge test (result was a string), the new-API unit tests (compile errors).

- Stage unit: edit / remove the imported partial between runs.
- `tests/integration/sass_cache_key.rs`: three-depth site, edit the partial, assert the linked CSS carries the new colour, one cache entry, `stale=1`, warm render compiles nothing.
- `sass_native.rs` + `sass.test.ts`: the compile reports exactly the runtime-loaded files, transitively, once each, embedded resources excluded.
- Envelope round-trip and legacy/malformed rejection; manifest validation against real files.
- `hub-client/src/services/sassCachePartials.wasm.test.ts`: real WASM module + dart-sass bridge + in-memory cache, spying on `jsCompileSass` — unchanged inputs hit, edited partial recompiles exactly once. Fails at that step with `loadedUrls` blanked.

title: hub-client: create the project set silently on first run; drop the setup screen
description:
## Summary

A brand-new user (no collection pointer, no legacy projects) used to land on the `ProjectSetSetup` screen after sign-in and had to click **Create New Project Set** before seeing the app. This PR establishes the personal root collection silently against `DEFAULT_SYNC_SERVER` and goes straight to the collections home's "No projects yet" empty state. Which sync server a deployment uses is fixed at build time (`VITE_DEFAULT_SYNC_SERVER`); users never choose one.

Strand: bd-4h1hv60p. Plan with resolved design questions and the end-to-end verification record: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-15-auto-create-project-set-on-first-run.md`.

## Changes

- **`useAutoEstablishRoot`** (new hook): fires `createProjectSet` on `needs-setup` and `migrateProjects` on `needs-migration` (legacy IDB projects migrate silently; the legacy store is retained), at most once per initialization cycle, re-armed when status passes through `loading`. Replaces the two gated copies of this effect that `App.tsx` carried for collection invites (bd-fxdcxbpq) and ephemeral previews (bd-zf4ryvuq).
- **Link boot URLs keep their meaning.** The hook is suppressed for a `#/link-project-set/…` boot URL, whose handler links the other browser's set *as the root*; an auto-created empty root would have demoted it to a secondary collection.
- **`useCollectionSets.retry()`**: re-reads the pointers and re-enters the state machine after an `error`.
- **`ProjectSetError`** replaces the setup form on the error path: a minimal "Couldn't connect to the sync server" card with **Try again**. Previously a failed root *reconnect* showed the fresh setup form, whose Create button could stack a second pointer.
- **`ProjectSetSetup.tsx` / `.css` deleted** (all four modes). Dev-harness `setup-*` pages replaced by `project-set-error`, scanned by the a11y baseline in both themes.
- **E2E:** the e2e build now sets `VITE_DEFAULT_SYNC_SERVER=/ws` (npm scripts + `hub-client-e2e.yml`), which `vite preview` proxies to the e2e hub, so the auto-created root reaches the local hub. Bootstrap helpers wait for the home instead of driving the form (31 specs go through the shared helper; the two private copies now ride it too). New `first-run.spec.ts` covers the collections home, the classic selector, and the link-project-set boot URL.
- Live guidance (`playwright.config.ts` header, `claude-notes/instructions/testing.md`, spec header comments) now gives the full e2e build command.

## Summary

quarto-hub.com is a live demo. Every card a visitor can reach without a session now carries a disclaimer above its sign-in button: **use test data, not real data**, and **anything you enter is not protected, and we won't return it** (Posit and third-party services may retain it; no confidentiality, security, or deletion guarantee).

## Summary

Two related sass-cache bugs found by the Connect-docs render profile (bd-fq44dlnm), fixed in individually reviewable commits:

1. **bd-79c4do6g (P1)** — `compile_theme_css::cache_key` hashed the *document-relative* spelling of a custom theme path (`../theme.scss`, `../../theme.scss`, …), so every document directory got its own cache entry for byte-identical CSS. On the Connect docs (352 docs / 349 dirs) that was 682 grass compiles for 2 distinct outputs — 78 % of the serial render. Fix: `ThemeContext::resolve_path` now lexically normalizes (new `quarto_util::normalize_lexically`); the path stays in the key because it is the proxy for the file's `@import` context.
2. **bd-ddahjqr1 (P2)** — the LRU index's unlocked read-modify-write lost updates under parallel Pass 2, leaving cache entries on disk untracked and never evicted (one project: 315 files / 101 MB against a 10 MB budget). Fix: a process-wide async mutex around the index RMW (new dep `async-lock`, wasm-safe), plus `SystemRuntime::cache_list` + reconcile-on-write so other-process races and pre-fix cache dirs self-heal on the next compile.

Also brings over the `perf.sass hits/compiles/uncached` gauge (`QUARTO_PERF_STATS=1`) from the profiling session, which the fix is verified with.

| serial `perf.sass` | hits=22 compiles=682 | hits=702 compiles=2 |

title: Re-encode zero-width/format characters as entities in the qmd writer; accept them raw in prose
description:
Fixes #672. Since the named-entity decode (#488) the reader folds `​` into a `Str` holding the literal U+200B, but the qmd writer emitted that codepoint verbatim and the grammar's prose regexes accepted no `Cf` character except ZWNJ/ZWJ, so pampa's own output failed to re-parse. Inside a heading superscript (quarto-web's `# Welcome to Quarto^​[®]{.trademark}^`) the failure cascaded into Q-2-16 Unclosed Superscript. ## What changes **Writer** (`caa29d6c`): `escape_markdown` spells every Unicode format character (general category `Cf`) as a character reference — the preferred WHATWG name where one exists (`​`, `­`, `‎`, `‏`, `⁠`, `⁡`, `⁢`, `⁣`), else `&#xXXXX;`. ZWNJ/ZWJ stay raw: they already parse, they are ordinary content in Persian/Indic text, and ZWJ is structural inside emoji sequences. The `Cf` range table and the preferred names live in the new `writers::format_chars`, with a comment linking the WHATWG table and the alias rule, pinned by tests against the `regex` crate's `\p{Cf}` and against the shared entity table. **Grammar** (`caa29d6c`): `PANDOC_COMBINING_MARKS` widens from `\p{M}\u{200C}\u{200D}` to `\p{M}\p{Cf}` (a strict superset), so raw zero-width characters — pasted from the web, or written by older pampa builds — parse as verbatim `Str`, matching Pandoc. Raw format characters are therefore accepted but not canonical at the text level: they re-emit as references. (Pandoc's readers behave the same way: `⁡`, `⁡` and a raw U+2061 all become one `Str`, so the source spelling is not recoverable and the writer emits the preferred name for all three.) **`&` escaping** (`b15868ed`, bd-i18zoy4n, folded in): the writer never escaped `&`, so a literal `Str "©"` (from `\©`) re-read as `©`. With the writer now emitting references itself this became load-bearing. `starts_character_reference` mirrors the grammar's two tokens (numeric refs by regex shape; named refs via the reader's own `entity_table()`) and emits `\&` only for those — `AT&T`, `a & b`, `&`, `&AM;` are untouched. Pandoc's markdown writer escapes the same way. ## Tests All written and verified failing first: 7 corpus cases (`test/corpus/format_characters.txt`), 8 parser coverage tests, 9 writer unit tests, 4 pin tests, and four round-trip fixtures (`named_entities.qmd` extended; `format_characters_raw.qmd`, `zero_width_in_heading_superscript.qmd`, `ampersand_escaped_entities.qmd` new). No existing test or snapshot changed. `parser.c` regenerated (+496/−489 lines, character-class rows only; generate took 0.26 s). Full `cargo xtask verify` (including the hub-client/WASM legs) green for both code commits. ## End-to-end ``` $ printf 'a​b\n' | pampa -t qmd | pampa [ Para [Str "a​b"] ] # was: Parse error $ cargo run --bin q2 -- render gh672.qmd # quarto-web heading + raw U+200B + \©

Welcome to Quarto​®

Raw zero-width: a​b and soft hy­phen.

Literal reference kept as text: © and ​.

``` ## Follow-up - bd-5rr4lgj1: a leading UTF-8 BOM (U+FEFF) is not stripped by the reader. After this PR a BOM-prefixed file parses (BOM inside the first `Str`) instead of erroring; Pandoc strips it, and so should we. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-11-zero-width-chars-writer-parser-gh672.md`. title: Expose the YAML frontmatter body in the grammar so a `---` inside a value cannot truncate the metadata
description:
Closes #671.

## Problem

The reader located the frontmatter body by `split("---")`-ing the opaque `metadata` token's text and keeping the second piece, so the first `---` inside a value ended the YAML there: a plain scalar silently dropped every later key, a quoted scalar failed with Q-0-99. Since #290 the qmd writer canonicalizes every em dash to `---`, which made both shapes reachable from any document with an em dash in a frontmatter string (in the wild: quarto-web's `2026-04-14-chrome-headless-shell/index.qmd`).

The tree-sitter scanner was never at fault — it closes the block only on a column-0 `---` line — but it emitted the whole block as one external leaf token, which is why the Rust side had to rediscover the body by hand.

## Fix

The grammar now parses the block as four external tokens and exposes the body as a `yaml` child under the `body` field:

```
(metadata body: (yaml))
```

pampa takes the YAML text and range straight from that node. `extract_between_delimiters` and the `block.text.find(content)` offset hazard are deleted; nothing in Rust knows about `---` any more. The `yaml` node is also what a YAML injection query would target in external tooling.

Scanner details: `_minus_metadata_start` is the opening `---` (it shares the thematic break's `mark_end` position so the confirming look-ahead can run speculatively), then `_minus_metadata_open_newline`, `_minus_metadata_body`, `_minus_metadata_end`, then the ordinary `choice(_newline, _eof)` tail — so a closing `---` at EOF without a newline now also closes the block. A new `STATE_IN_MINUS_METADATA` bit gates the interior tokens against tree-sitter's mark-everything-valid error recovery.

## Consequences worth reviewing

- **Fixtures/snapshots (please eyeball):** the `RawBlock quarto_minus_metadata` carrier now holds the body text and the body range, so the body is no longer trimmed, the metadata span ends after the final line break (`4..30` instead of `4..29`), and the source-info chain is one layer shorter. Resolved key/value offsets are unchanged. That renumbers every `s` index in the 20 `ts-packages/annotated-qmd/examples/*.json` fixtures (regenerated with the documented loop; I verified every non-`astContext` difference is an `s` renumbering) and 4 insta snapshots under `crates/pampa/snapshots/json/`.
- `Block::BlockMetadata` for a lexical block now spans the YAML body rather than the delimited block. Carrying both ranges would mean building `BlockMetadata` at tree-conversion time instead of via the RawBlock carrier — flagged as a follow-up in the plan, not done here.
- `parser.c` regeneration renumbers LR states, so the state-keyed `resources/error-corpus/_autogen-table.json` was rebuilt (`crates/pampa/scripts/build_error_table.ts`); only the table changed.
- One corpus expectation (`div.txt: 2`) gains the `block_continuation` child every block in a div already carries.

## Tests

- `crates/pampa/tests/integration/test_frontmatter_delimiters.rs`: the three shapes from the issue, an indented `---` inside a block scalar, trailing whitespace on the closing line, CRLF, metadata nested in a div, exact key offsets after a `---`-containing value, qmd-writer round trips for single- and multi-line em-dash values, and the tree shape/range of the `yaml` node (including closing `---` at EOF).
- 5 new GH #671 cases in `test/corpus/metadata.txt`; 9 existing `(metadata)` expectations gained the child.
- The three file-based tests in `test_meta.rs` now go through the real reader instead of handing whole documents to `rawblock_to_config_value`.
- Full `cargo xtask verify` green locally.

End-to-end (output inspected):

```
$ printf -- '---\ndescription: "Hello — world"\nauthor: Z\n---\n\nx\n' | pampa -t qmd | pampa -t json | jq -c .meta
{"author": Z, "description": Hello — world}          # both keys, em dash restored
$ printf -- '---\ndescription: "a --- b"\nauthor: Z\n---\n\nx\n' | pampa -t json | jq -c .meta
{"author": Z, "description": a — b}                  # no Q-0-99
$ q2 render dash.qmd    # title/description with em dashes + author
<title>Dashes — everywhere</title> … <meta name="description" content="Hello — world"> … <meta name="author" content="Z">
```

Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-10-frontmatter-delimiter-split-gh671.md` (bd-mjo6ao32). Found along the way and filed separately: bd-wl58atds (pre-existing provenance warning on block scalars with multi-byte characters).

This should be effective sandboxing to prevent user code from accessing quarto-hub.com via http request or websocket. the q2-sandboxed-preview application sends specific data back and forth from/to a quarto-hub tab over `postMessage`. ## VFS URL proxying The q2-sandboxed-preview preview app runs a service worker that intercepts HTTP requests to relative URLs and retrieves (over postMessage) the data for that file url from the VFS (Virtual File System) of the quarto-hub app. In other words: In the sandboxed preview, any relative url will get requested from the quarto-hub project's VFS rather than via an http request to a server. Note that this poses security challenges that we have not yet grappled with. It means that any user-defined JS running in the preview could load any files it wants from the VFS, as long as it has their name (which it could fuzz). We should probably design a mitigation to this risk. Some ideas off-the-top: keep track of urls we expect to be requested based on the .qmd contents and only give access to those; detect and disable rapid requests. Note that there is only risk that untrusted JS in the preview could access files in the VFS of the project, not of other projects you have on quarto-hub. title: Publish source: file brand fonts beside the theme CSS (bd-ve916wr8)
description:
Fixes bd-ve916wr8.

## Problem

Local fonts declared in `_brand.yml` (`source: file`) were never copied into the output, and the `@font-face` URL was document-relative while the compiled theme CSS lives in `site_libs/quarto/` (website) or `{stem}_files/` (single doc). Every local brand font 404'd. The per-document prefix also split a site into one theme bundle per page depth on a cold SASS cache, and aliased pages onto whichever compiled first on a warm one, because the cache key never included it. Evidence and repro fixtures: `claude-notes/plans/brand-file-fonts-website-investigation/NOTES.md`.

## Fix

Fonts are published as project-scope artifacts in a `fonts/` directory beside whichever theme CSS references them (`site_libs/quarto/fonts/`, `{stem}_files/fonts/`, `…/revealjs/fonts/`), and the SCSS layer emits the constant `url('fonts/<basename>') format('woff2')`. The URL no longer depends on the document, so one compiled theme serves every page and the cache key is complete by construction. Artifacts flush through both the native sink and the preview VFS, so the same mechanism covers `q2 preview`.

- **quarto-brand**: `published_font_name`; `BrandFontFileEntry::Explicit` becomes a struct that tolerates unsettled per-file keys (`format:`, `display:`) and exposes them; `ResolvedBrand` remembers its file.
- **quarto-sass**: `brand_to_layers(&Brand)` drops the font-path prefix; `ThemeContext::with_brand` drops `brand_dir`; `resolve_brand_layers` is gone (reveal resolves the brand and publishes fonts itself).
- **quarto-core**: new `brand_fonts` module (publish, leading `/` = project root per the path contract, dedupe identical bytes). `ArtifactMergeConflict` carries the producers' `source` metadata, and font clashes map to `Q-14-10` from both the serial tail and the parallel Pass-2 reducer.
- **Diagnostics**: `Q-14-9` font file missing (warn, continue), `Q-14-10` same name / different bytes (hard error naming both sources), `Q-14-11` unsupported key on a file entry (warn, ignore). Numbered past `Q-14-6/7` (#661) and `Q-14-8` (#663).
- **Docs**: "Local font files" section in the brand guide; three error pages + sidebar; inventory row in `path-resolution-model.md`.

Design decisions (fonts as artifacts, collision is an error, `/` = project root, warn on unknown keys) are recorded in `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-08-brand-file-fonts-website.md`.

## Tests

- 12 end-to-end cases in `crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/brand_fonts.rs` through `render_to_file` / `ProjectPipeline`: website at two depths (one bundle), nested-only page, rooted path, brand in a subdirectory, light/dark distinct fonts, identical-bytes dedupe, both collision shapes, missing file, unknown key, single doc, reveal. All confirmed failing at HEAD first.
- Unit coverage in quarto-brand (`font_files_test.rs`), quarto-sass (`brand_layer_test.rs`), quarto-core (`brand_fonts` module).
- `cargo nextest run --workspace` 13,763 passed; clippy `-D warnings` clean on the touched crates; `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-tests` green including the WASM leg (hub-client vitest is red on `main` from the Node 26 `localStorage` issue, bd-lh30hlvd).

## End-to-end

```
cargo run --bin q2 -- render claude-notes/plans/brand-file-fonts-website-investigation/repro
```

One bundle `site_libs/quarto/quarto-theme-<fp>.css` linked by `index.html` and `posts/one.html`, containing

```
@font-face{font-family:"EB Garamond";src:url("fonts/EBGaramond-VariableFont_wght.woff2") format("woff2");font-weight:400;font-style:normal}
```

and `site_libs/quarto/fonts/EBGaramond-VariableFont_wght.woff2` byte-identical to the source. The single-doc fixture publishes `doc_files/fonts/…` next to `doc_files/styles.css`.

## Coordination

Expected textual conflict with #663 (bd-5fseopxy) in `file_font_face_block`, `types.rs`, and the theme stage; whichever lands second rebases. On merge: comment on bd-r1y48cx0 (`css:` files never copied) pointing at this mechanism.

title: hub-client: Edit pill in the bottom bar toggles q2-preview block editing (bd-ew0vak6b)
description:
## Summary

`format: q2-preview` in hub-client was always editable, which made links hard to follow: a mouse click on any editable paragraph opens that paragraph's editor, so a click on a link inside a paragraph also opened an editor. `q2 preview` already has this distinction via `--allow-edit`, and the renderer already implements read-only mode behind `editingDisabled` (bd-ov4gqk3m); hub-client never set it.

This adds an **Edit** pill to the document bottom bar (before **Authors**) that turns block editing on and off. Off makes the preview behave like a read-only `q2 preview`: no edit affordances, no hover outline, links are plain links. The choice persists as the `previewEditing` preference (default on).

- `previewEditing` preference (`.default(true)`, migration-safe like `richText`), read by `ReactPreview` and forwarded through `ReactRenderer` to the iframe as `editingDisabled`; `handleSetAst` also drops edit payloads while off (defense in depth, as in the q2-preview SPA).
- `ReplayDrawer`: `EditToggle` pill, disabled for formats other than q2-preview. Authors and Edit share a `.replay-drawer__pill*` CSS base; the rainbow ring stays attribution-only.
- preview-renderer: when `editingDisabled` turns on while an edit session is open, both editor surfaces (textarea, rich text) close through their own commit path — commit if dirty, else cancel.

Design and decisions: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-09-q2-preview-edit-toggle.md`.

## Tests

- Unit/integration (written red first): schema defaults + migration; ReplayDrawer pill (states, disabled, ordering); ReactRenderer forwarding; ReactPreview forwarding + drop guard; preview-renderer close-on-disable (dirty textarea commits once; unchanged textarea/rich close without commit; re-enable restores the affordance).
- Playwright `hub-client/e2e/q2-preview-edit-toggle.spec.ts`: off removes affordances and hover outline, a link navigates to the other document without opening an editor, the choice survives a reload, on restores. Passed in Chromium against a real hub.
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-rust-tests` and `cargo xtask lint` green (no Rust changes).

Not covered: a *dirty* rich-text session closed by the toggle (nothing makes the tiptap editor dirty in jsdom today; it uses the same `commit` the blur path does).

title: bd-bpt089zw: resolving the last comment no longer leaves an empty pill or a stuck glow (q2-preview)
description:
## Summary

In hub-client's q2-preview, resolving the **last** comment on a block (the `✓` in the comment bubble) left two artifacts behind: a small empty pill where the bubble was, and a block "glow" that never cleared — not after moving the mouse away, not after clicking elsewhere.

Both are state-lifecycle bugs in `CommentWrapper` (`ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/custom/CommentBlock.tsx`). Blocks are keyed by index, so the bubble component instance and its state survive the commit round-trip, and nothing reset it:

1. **Empty pill.** `selfExpanded` outlived the last comment, so the bubble rendered its expanded branch with zero rows. Fix: a layout effect collapses the self-expanded state when the comment count reaches zero with no inline input open (the one legitimate empty-and-expanded state: `+` just clicked). Layout, so the pill is never painted.
2. **Stuck glow.** The block-wrapper glow was set from the bubble's own `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave`. The resolve re-render unmounts the button under the pointer; Chrome re-evaluates `:hover` after layout without boundary events, and the next `mouseout` comes from the *new* hovered node, which the bubble is not an ancestor of — so the bubble's leave never fired. Fix: derive the glow on the wrapper's `mousemove` (containment of `e.target`) and clear it on the wrapper's `mouseleave`; a layout effect re-derives it from geometry (last pointer position vs the re-measured bubble rect) whenever the bubble changes shape, so a stationary pointer gets the right answer in both directions.

Both fields date from Comments v1 (#441); not a regression from the rich-bubble work.

## Tests

`CommentBlock.resolveLast.integration.test.tsx` — 8 jsdom tests (T1–T7 + T6b), each verified failing before the fix (T7 against the clear-only variant of the geometric re-check). Full preview-renderer integration (56 files) and unit (43 files) suites green; `cargo xtask verify` green.

## End-to-end

Verified in Chrome against a local vite dev server: after `✓` with the pointer stationary, the chrome collapses to the hover-only `+` and the glow is on only because the pointer actually rests inside that `+`; after a real move away, wrapper box-shadow is `none` and no chrome remains. DOM probe output is recorded in the plan.

title: Enforce the Node pin: xtask preflight, engine-strict, docs (bd-lh30hlvd)
description:
## Summary

The repo has pinned Node 24 since `ca6d47c8` (`.nvmrc` + `engines.node`), but the pin was advisory: `.nvmrc` needs a version manager, `engines` only warns at `npm install`, and xtask never looked. A `brew upgrade` on 2026-09-04 relinked `node` to 26.8.1 on a dev machine and the hub-client vitest suite went red four days later with 23 unrelated-looking `localStorage` failures (Node ≥ 25 defines a `localStorage` accessor that vitest 4.x's jsdom environment refuses to overwrite; fixed upstream only in vitest 5).

Decision: keep `engines.node` at `^24.0.0` for now and make the pin **enforced**.

- **`crates/xtask/src/node_version.rs`** (new): reads `engines.node` from the root `package.json`, probes `node --version`, classifies the result. Ranges use npm's own grammar (`nodejs-semver`) — Cargo's `semver` crate rejects the space-separated `>=24 <25` form. An unparsable range is an error, never a silent pass. 17 unit tests, written first.
- **`cargo xtask verify`**: "Preflight: Node toolchain" before Step 1 — fails in seconds on a mismatch or missing `node` with an actionable message; prints the version found on success; skips itself when every npm-driven step is disabled. `Q2_ALLOW_NODE_MISMATCH=1` warns and continues (deliberate experiments only).
- **`cargo xtask dev-setup`**: warn-only check with per-platform fnm install hints.
- **`.npmrc`**: `engine-strict=true` — `npm install`/`npm ci` fail with `EBADENGINE` under a Node outside the range (verified under 26.8.1) and succeed under 24 (fresh `npm ci`).
- **Docs**: `claude-notes/instructions/node-version.md` (the pin, what enforces it, fnm setup incl. why `~/.zprofile` not `~/.zshenv` on macOS, the Homebrew relink trap, bump procedure); pointers from `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/worktrees.md`.

Investigation record, timeline and fix-candidate table: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-08-node26-vitest-localstorage.md`. Deferred vitest 5 / shim work for the eventual Node 26 bump: bd-s84z961e.

## Verification

- Full `cargo xtask verify` under Node 24.20.0: all 14 steps green (13,757 Rust tests; hub-client 1084/119/133; trace-viewer, shared preview-*, hub MCP suites).
- Under Node 26.8.1, `cargo xtask verify` stops at the preflight with exit 1 before any Rust build.
- Clippy (`-D warnings`), `cargo fmt`, `cargo xtask lint` clean.

CI runs `actions/setup-node` with `node-version: '24'` in every workflow, so `engine-strict` and the preflight are no-ops there — this PR is mainly to confirm that.

title: Support brand.yml font weight ranges; make invalid weights a Q-14-8 error (bd-5fseopxy)
description:
Fixes bd-5fseopxy.

## Problem

brand.yml allows a variable-font weight range written as a string (`weight: 400..700`). Quarto 2 parsed it as an unknown keyword and then:

- **google**: `enumerate_weights` did `weight_name_to_number(s).unwrap_or(400)` — the `@import` requested only weight 400, bold fell back to synthetic bold, no diagnostic.
- **file** (`files[].weight: 300..800`): the string was written verbatim into `@font-face` as `font-weight: 300..800;`, which grass rejects — the whole theme silently fell back to the 7 KB `DEFAULT_CSS`.
- **slot** (`headings: {weight: 500..700}`): same verbatim passthrough into `$headings-font-weight: 500..700 !default;`, same silent fallback.

Any other unrecognised weight string (`Bold`, `semibold`, `bolder`) also became a silent 400. Quarto 1 fails hard here (`Unknown font weight`).

## Change

- **`quarto-brand`**: `BrandFontWeight::Range(BrandFontWeightRange { min, max })`, deserialised from exactly `<digits>..<digits>` (anything else stays `Name` so it can be reported verbatim). New `Brand::validate()` (`validate.rs`) checks every `weight:` under `typography` and returns `BrandError::InvalidFontWeight { path, value, reason }` with a `BrandPath` such as `typography.fonts[0].files[1].weight`. Rules: numbers in `100..=900`; keywords from the closed Q1 table (`weight_name_to_number` now lives here); ranges numeric only, `min <= max`, allowed on `fonts[]` entries but not on slots.
- **`quarto-sass`** emission: google emits the `wght@400..700` axis (with italics: `ital,wght@0,400..700;1,400..700`); bunny expands a range to discrete weights (`400,500,600,700` — Bunny has no range syntax and silently serves 400 for `400..700`, checked against fonts.bunny.net); `@font-face` emits `font-weight: 300 800`. Unknown keywords and slot ranges are `Err`, never a fallback.
- **`quarto-sass`** location: `load_split_brand` validates after parsing and, on failure, re-parses the brand text with `quarto_yaml::parse_file` and walks the path to the offending scalar. Inline `brand:` blocks are validated at extraction time while the `ConfigValue` tree (with per-node spans) is in scope. New `SassError::InvalidBrandFontWeight { path, value, reason, location, brand_file }`.
- **`quarto-core`**: new **`Q-14-8` "Invalid brand font weight"** in `theme_diagnostic`; the error's `brand_file` is added as a bind candidate so the snippet renders from `_brand.yml`. The two `stage_error("brand resolution: …")` sites now route through `theme_diagnostic`, so brand-shape errors render with `Q-14-1` too.
- Catalog entry, `docs/errors/theme/Q-14-8.qmd`, sidebar entry, and the `weight` section of `docs/guides/authoring/brand.qmd`.

## What the user sees now

```
$ q2 render repro-slot-only
Error: [Q-14-8] Invalid brand font weight
   ╭─[ …/_brand.yml:9:13 ]
 9 │     weight: 500..700
   │             ────┬───
   │                 ╰───── `500..700` at `typography.headings.weight` is not a font weight Quarto
                            understands: a typography slot takes a single weight, not a range; …
ℹ Use a number from 100 to 900, a keyword such as `bold` or `semi-bold`, a list of those, or —
  on `typography.fonts` entries — a numeric range such as `400..700`?
```

and for the valid forms the compiled CSS contains

```
@import url("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=EB+Garamond:ital,wght@0,400..700;1,400..700&display=swap")
@font-face{font-family:"Local Var";src:url("LocalVar-VariableFont_wght.woff2");font-weight:300 800;font-style:normal}
```

## Tests (written first, observed failing)

- `quarto-brand/tests/integration/font_weight_test.rs` — 24 tests: parsing of the range variant, the keyword table, every accepted shape, and each rejection (reversed, out of range, keyword ends, half-open, unknown keyword, list index, file-entry path, slot range, every slot name).
- `quarto-sass` — emission (google axis, italics, bunny expansion incl. non-round ends, file pair, keyword list regression guard, defensive `Err`s), grass compile of the range brand, and the location tests (path form: span keyed by `file_id_for_filename`, covering exactly the scalar; inline form: the `ConfigValue` node's span).
- `quarto-core` `theme_diagnostic` — `Q-14-8` renders with code/path/value/reason and a snippet from `_brand.yml` with no caller-supplied candidates; span-less form; catalog registration.
- `quarto/tests/integration/brand_font_weight.rs` — five CLI end-to-end tests through the `q2` binary.

## Notes for review

- Design decisions and the investigation record: `claude-notes/plans/2026-09-08-brand-font-weight-ranges.md`; repro fixtures under `claude-notes/plans/brand-font-weight-ranges-investigation/`.
- Coordination with bd-jsvetdea (theme compile errors, in flight): that work claims `Q-14-6`/`Q-14-7` and edits `theme_diagnostic.rs` and `quarto-sass/src/error.rs`; this PR adds one arm and one variant to each. Small, but expect a trivial merge in whichever lands second.
- `source: file` is touched only on the `font-weight` line of the `@font-face` block, deliberately; the suspected deeper file-handling bugs are being planned separately.
- Default weights when `weight:` is absent stay at `400;700` (Q1 parity); the brand.yml reference requests all nine — split off as bd-b1rrnzp1.
- Verification: `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-tests` green through Rust build, clippy, workspace tests, ts-packages, and the hub-client WASM build. The hub-client vitest leg is skipped for the known Node 26 `localStorage` environment failure (bd-lh30hlvd). The preview-renderer integration suite failed once on a stale local `node_modules` (KaTeX 0.17 installed vs 0.18.4 pinned) and passes after `npm install`.

title: Theme compile failures are structured hard errors, not silent DEFAULT_CSS (bd-jsvetdea)
description:
## Summary

A grass failure while compiling the theme bundle used to be caught in `variant_css`, logged as a `Warn` trace event (which no CLI observer receives), and replaced by the static 7 KB `DEFAULT_CSS`. The render reported success. A one-line unit mistake in a user theme (`$grid-body-width: 52rem`) silently shipped an unstyled page.

Every theme compile failure is now a `PipelineError::Structured` through `theme_diagnostic`:
