title: Fix smart-punctuation ellipsis at every position (bd-ellipsis-not-smart-48bv2pe6)
description:
Pandoc's `smart` extension rewrites every run of three dots to `…` (U+2026). q2 did it only when the run followed a word character: | input | before | after | |---|---|---| | `the ... menu` | `the ... menu` | `the … menu` | | `**...**` | `...` | `…` | | `... and then` | `... and then` | `… and then` | | `see (...) here` | `see (...) here` | `see (…) here` | | `a...b` | `a…b` | `a…b` (unchanged) | ## Root cause The conversion function was never at fault. `apply_smart_typography` runs **per prose-str node** — deliberately, because that is what keeps `a\.\.\.b` literal (each escaped dot arrives from tree-sitter as its own backslash-plus-dot node). tree-sitter was emitting a dot run at *token start* as one single-character `pandoc_str` node per dot, so each node held a run of one, which correctly stayed literal, and `merge_strs` concatenated them only afterwards. The asymmetry is in `startStrRegex`, which admits `-` but not `.` as a token-start character. That is why the dash path was already position-independent (`--` lexes as one node) while the dot path was not. The decisive probe: **`x -... y` renders `-…`** — prefixing a hyphen *repaired* the ellipsis. That rules out the originally-hypothesized cause (a dot-leading token being routed down an attribute-class path that never reaches the conversion); the function is reached in every case, it just never saw more than one dot. ## The fix One alternative added to `PANDOC_REGEX_STR`: ```js "[.]+", "[>.,;!?]", ``` Chosen over adding `.` to `startStrRegex`, which would make `.class` a single token next door to the `{.class}` / `[x]{.class}` attribute grammar. Longest-match in the lexer keeps a lone `.` at one character, and `..` stays a literal two-dot run. Also in scope (deliberate, agreed): four dots now give `….` — an ellipsis plus a literal remainder, per Pandoc's three-at-a-time rule. Confirmed against `pandoc -f markdown -t native`, which emits `Str "\8230."`. ## Verification - `tree-sitter generate`: **no conflicts**, so the deterministic-LR design invariant at `grammar.js:136` holds. `tree-sitter test`: 590/590. - `resources/error-corpus/_autogen-table.json` regenerated with a **zero diff** — no LR state the error catalog maps to has moved. This was the main risk going in; it did not materialize. - `cargo nextest run --workspace`: 11,736 passed. - `cargo xtask verify` (all 14 steps, WASM leg + hub-client build): passed. - `cargo xtask lint`: 958 files, all passed. - **End-to-end through `q2 render`**, output inspected in the generated HTML: ```html

Click the … menu to open it.

Wait for it… then see (…) here.

Four dots …. and two .. dots.

Escaped a...b stays literal, code ... untouched.

``` The first line is the exact construct from the Connect docs that motivated the report. ## Tests Added 8 Rust integration tests (`test_smart_typography_positions.rs`), 8 tree-sitter corpus cases (`dot-runs.txt`), and one native snapshot fixture (`smart-typography-positions.qmd`). TDD confirmed: 4 of the 8 Rust tests failed before the fix, while the 4 controls (short runs, escaped runs, code spans, dashes) passed throughout. The pre-existing coverage only ever exercised word-adjacent dot runs — `smart-typography.qmd` has `ellipsis...`, and `dashes_spaced.qmd` starts from an already-converted `…`, so it tested round-tripping rather than conversion. That is why this shipped. ## Reviewer notes **Snapshots: 1 added, 0 modified, 0 removed.** No pre-existing snapshot changed — notably `smart-typography.snap` is byte-identical, confirming word-adjacent behavior is untouched. **One pre-existing grammar test changed.** `test/corpus/punctuation-vs-image.txt` case 5 feeds the literal input `...` and asserted **three** `pandoc_str` nodes — its expectation encoded the buggy tokenization directly. It now asserts one node. This is the only pre-existing test touched, and the change is forced by the fix rather than incidental. **Incidental finding, not addressed here.** `## Heading with ... dots` produces the id `heading-with-...-dots` in q2, where Pandoc gives `heading-with-dots` — q2's heading-id algorithm does not strip punctuation. Pre-existing and independent, though this fix does make such a heading's *text* use U+2026 while its id keeps ASCII dots. Probably deserves its own strand. Strand: `bd-ellipsis-not-smart-48bv2pe6`. Plan and investigation record: `claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-ellipsis-not-smart.md`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Warning suppression (`diagnostics:`) + Q-2-49 lone-bracket diagnostic
description: Implements **bd-lone-bracket-diagnostic-mxu41qbt**. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-warning-suppression-and-lone-bracket-diagnostic.md` ## The question, and why it needed two changes The strand asked whether q2 should decline to warn about a construct merely because someone might use it intentionally. `reference_link_diagnostics.rs` had documented exactly that reasoning for a lone `[text]`: > There is no way to tell it apart from a deliberate `[text]` span, so warning on it would fire on legitimate documents. The reasoning was sound; one premise was not. A project that *did* use bare spans deliberately had no way to say so — which made "someone might mean it" unanswerable, paid for by every reader of every other project getting silently wrong output. Two Posit Connect pages documented the wrong default mail subject prefix (`[Posit Connect]` → `Posit Connect`) for the whole duration of the port. So this adds the missing mechanism first, then the diagnostic it was blocking. ## Warning suppression ```yaml # _quarto.yml, a directory's _metadata.yml, or a document's front matter diagnostics: Q-2-49: level: off reason: "bare spans are markers for our annotate.lua filter" ``` `off` is the only level. The shape is a **per-code map** rather than a flat `suppress:` list so `warning` / `error` levels are reachable later without a competing config key. **Where it applies.** `--strict` (bd-yjs54ptg) had already built a severity-policy seam, but at the `ProjectRenderSummary` boundary — which is CLI-only and would have excluded `q2 preview` and hub-client. The seam used here is instead **`run_pipeline`'s tail** (`pipeline.rs:811`), the one expression every per-document diagnostic passes through for *every* frontend. One edit covers render, preview, and hub-client. Because it runs inside the render it also lands strictly before `--strict` promotes warnings to errors, so suppress-then-promote falls out of the placement rather than needing enforcement. Resolution is split out into `MetadataMergeStage`, where merged metadata exists — so project → directory → document precedence comes from the existing merge, not a second set of rules. **Deliberate limits**, all documented in the module and user docs: - Errors are never suppressed. - Diagnostics with no code cannot be suppressed (bd-m2w7a is the backfill). - Project-*scoped* diagnostics are out of reach in v1. This is **not** the same as "`_quarto.yml` doesn't work" — that works, because project config is merge layer 1. Malformed entries report **Q-5-23** rather than being ignored: q2 has no config schema layer, so a silently-dropped entry is indistinguishable from a suppression that failed. ## Q-2-49 A lone `[text]` renders as `text` — brackets discarded, sentence changed. Worth noting for reviewers: a bare span carries no class, no id, no attributes, so a deliberately-authored lone `[text]` accomplishes nothing in the output. The one substantive legitimate use is a Lua filter hooking bare spans, which is exactly what suppression serves. `scan_inlines` now tracks a `claimed` bitmap so a span consumed by Q-2-45/Q-2-46 is **not** also reported as Q-2-49 — one mistake, one diagnostic. ## Review notes - **One pre-existing test changed.** `does_not_treat_a_mid_line_colon_span_as_a_definition` asserted *no* diagnostic; its actual claim is "not a definition", and the silence it relied on is the gap Q-2-49 closes. Now asserts Q-2-49. No other existing test changed. - **No snapshot (`.snap`) files** added, modified, or removed. - New catalog codes ship with their docs pages in the same commit (`error-docs-page-missing` lint). - `DiagnosticPolicy` uses `LinkedHashMap`: lookup-only today, but the deferred unused-suppression report will iterate it for user-visible output. ## Verification `cargo xtask verify` (full, 14/14 including the WASM leg and hub-client tests) green; 11700 workspace tests pass; `cargo xtask lint` clean. **End-to-end on the strand's repro with the real binary**, output inspected: ``` $ q2 render Warning: [Q-2-45] `[the RedHat documentation][gcc-toolset]` … Warning: [Q-2-45] `[noexec][noexec]` … Warning: [Q-2-49] `[Version TBD]` has no attribute block, so it renders as an empty span and the brackets are discarded — the reader sees `Version TBD`. … Warning: [Q-2-49] `[1]` … Warning: [Q-2-49] `[2]` … Warning: [Q-2-49] `[Posit Connect]` … Warning: [Q-2-46] `[gcc-toolset]:` … Warning: [Q-2-46] `[noexec]:` … ``` All four previously-silent cases now warn with precise spans; the reference-link shapes are unchanged (no double-reporting). With `diagnostics: {Q-2-49: {level: off, reason: …}}` in `_quarto.yml`, only `2 [Q-2-45]` / `2 [Q-2-46]` remain. With all three suppressed, `q2 render --strict` prints nothing and exits 0. Corrupting an entry to `Q-2-45: shout` yields `2 [Q-2-45]` + `1 [Q-5-23]` — reported, and suppressing nothing. **Not verified:** a live `q2 preview` browser session. The preview pipeline is covered by a unit test driving `render_qmd_to_preview_ast`, and it shares the seam with the CLI, but no browser was opened. ## Follow-ups filed - **bd-91rgxmav** — unknown-code validation, unused-suppression reporting, `--show-suppressed`, path globs, per-line suppression, project-scoped coverage, a lint requiring codes on new warnings, additional levels. - **bd-cljk1g5p** — re-key `qmd-syntax-helper`'s `literal-brackets` rule to the `q_2_49.rs` convention (deliberately not done here: it touches a documented CLI surface and is a real refactor, not a rename). ## Open question for the reviewer Is *"q2 may warn on an ambiguous-but-usually-wrong construct, because suppression exists"* now standing policy? If so it belongs in `CLAUDE.md`, and it is worth auditing which other diagnostics were scoped down for the same reason. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix: allow empty project-set creation while sync is offline
description:
Fresh Quarto Hub users currently cannot finish setup when the configured sync server is unavailable. The active `useCollectionSets` flow calls `createCollection`, which waits up to ten seconds for a peer and throws before importing the empty root document, so the hook enters `error` and the setup screen returns. Because the document is empty and the Repo already has IndexedDB storage plus a reconnecting WebSocket adapter, the personal root can be created and used locally before a peer is available. Existing-set linking must still require either a cached document or a reachable server.

## Summary

Add an explicit creation policy in `projectSetService.ts`: ordinary shared collections remain server-gated, while the fresh personal-root wrapper imports the empty document immediately, flushes it to IndexedDB, and observes server readiness in the background so a later reconnect can sync it. Update `useCollectionSets.ts` to use that offline-capable wrapper only for `createProjectSet`; migration and user-created shared collections continue through the server-gated path to avoid changing their durability guarantees. Preserve the configured sync-server URL in both stored pointers so reloads reopen the cached root and resume background synchronization against the intended server.

## Verification

- Happy path: with a reachable server, creating a fresh personal root immediately persists both pointers, reaches the projects home, and the background peer connection synchronizes the empty document.
- Edge cases: with no peer, creation still reaches `connected`; after a reload the cached empty root opens from IndexedDB and retains its configured server; migrations and ordinary shared-collection creation remain server-gated.
- Error paths: IndexedDB import or flush failures still surface setup error state, and linking an uncached existing project set while offline still reports that the collection must first be synced online.

Closes #405

title: Fix adjacent footnote definitions merging into one note
description:
Fixes **bd-adjacent-footnote-definitions-miif1k1z**. Two footnote definitions on consecutive lines parsed as one: the second was absorbed as lazy paragraph continuation into the first note's body, and its reference rendered as an **empty span** — no marker, no diagnostic. The reader saw no footnote at all, and note 1 had a foreign sentence glued onto it. Real-world hit in the Posit Connect docs: `user/manifest/index.qmd` (the `[^wsgi]`/`[^asgi]` pair, committed here as the repro fixture) and `admin/integrations/tableau`. ## Root cause Neither `SOFT_LINE_ENDING` gate in `scanner.c` treated `[` as a possible block opener, so a `[^id]:` line was lazy paragraph text. Same class as bd-digit-line-splits-paragraph-w6tod0gh (92737cdd), and the inverse symptom: there a line that was *not* a block opener ended the paragraph; here a line that *is* one failed to. ## What landed `scanner.c` only. No grammar change, so `parser.c` is untouched and there are no generated diffs — same shape as 92737cdd. One peek helper, `peek_ref_id_specifier`, wired into both gates on a `[` lookahead under 92737cdd's indentation rule. ### The subtle part: the peek must never be looser than the parser `inline_ref_def` is `seq(ref_id_specifier, _whitespace, pandoc_paragraph)`, so the whitespace **and** a non-empty body are both mandatory: | Input | Parses to | | --- | --- | | `[^x]: two.` | `inline_ref_def` | | `[^]: two.` | `inline_ref_def` (empty id is legal) | | `[^x]:two.` | **ERROR node** | | `[^x]:` | **ERROR node** | | `[^x]: ` (empty body) | **ERROR node** | Had the peek merely mirrored `parse_ref_id_specifier`, those ERROR-node lines would have had their soft break suppressed and then failed to form any block — a **hard parse error, which drops the whole file from the render**. That is the bd-j7be7kuc failure mode. The helper is deliberately stricter, and the invariant is written into its comment: stricter is always safe (the line stays paragraph continuation), looser turns benign prose into an unrenderable file. ### One deliberate departure from 92737cdd's shape The dash/plus branch sets `first_peeked` *outside* its indentation guard. Copying that verbatim was wrong, and the over-indented-list-item corpus case caught it — it regressed from passing to failing, gaining a `(block_continuation)` child inside its `pandoc_soft_break`. The `[` branch never advances the lexer on the over-indent path, so leaving `first_peeked` false reproduces byte for byte what the line did before `[` had a branch at all. Both `first_peeked` and `second_peeked` are set **inside** the guard, noted in the code so nobody "restores symmetry" later. ## Behavior change beyond the reported symptom Batched deliberately. `[^id]:` now interrupts an **ordinary** paragraph too: ```markdown hello there. [^b]: two. ``` is a paragraph **plus a definition**. Pandoc keeps one paragraph — its note body is a raw-line collector that stops at the next definition, so a definition never interrupts ordinary prose there. This divergence is deliberate and documented in the gate comment: q2's note body is an ordinary paragraph, so `#` and `-` **already** interrupt it where Pandoc absorbs them as literal text. Scoping this to definition bodies only would require the scanner to know it is inside an `inline_ref_def` — a grammar rule, not an open block, so not state the scanner has. The full sweep after the fix matches the Pandoc column on every cell except that one (and its in-a-list twin). Both sweeps are committed under `claude-notes/plans/adjacent-footnote-definitions-investigation/`. ## Not in scope The strand suggested designing the peek to serve link reference definitions too. **That premise is false**: qmd has no such construct — `CLAUDE.md` says so, `grammar.js` has no rule for it, and `[ref]: url` parses as a bracket span plus literal text. The peek is scoped to the `[^id]:` footnote form. ## Tests 11 corpus cases covering the indent × context sweep required by `claude-notes/instructions/scanner-indentation-contexts.md` (indent 0/1/3/4+ × top level / list item at and past the content column / block quote, plus three negatives). Confirmed failing **first**, and failing in exactly the right places: **6 failed / 5 passed**, the 5 passers being cells that must *not* change. After the fix: 11/11. - `tree-sitter test`: **593/593**, zero regressions. - Full `cargo xtask verify` (**not** `--skip-hub-build` — the grammar feeds the WASM parser): all 14 steps passed, Rust tests **11728 passed** / 197 skipped. - **Zero snapshot files changed.** ## End-to-end `cargo run --bin q2 -- render repro.qmd --to html`, output inspected. Both references now resolve to real superscript links, four correctly-numbered notes, and no `quarto-note-reference` span survives anywhere in the output: ```html

App modes: python-api (flask1) and python-fastapi2.

``` Before the fix the same file emitted `` — an invisible empty span — with the second definition's text pasted into note 1. ## Still open, unchanged by this fix - **bd-jttkymsw** — an unresolved reference still renders as an invisible empty span with no diagnostic. This PR removes one *cause* of unresolved references; it does not touch the resolution path, so a typo'd note id still vanishes. - **bd-v9zs83zj** — the `Footnotes` appendix heading is still missing. - **bd-mt1ksg9b** — the `*` gate peeks still lack their indentation guard; kept separate on purpose, since `*` has emphasis wrinkles that need their own sweep. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Implement `aliases:` redirect stubs for website projects
description:
Closes the largest structural gap between the Q1 and q2 renders of the Posit Connect
docs: q2 silently dropped the `aliases:` front-matter key — no redirect stubs, and no
diagnostic. The silence was the expensive part; a porting project got no signal that its
redirects had disappeared.

Strand: `bd-aliases-redirects-missing-sch7cd1g` (duplicate `bd-hzwecpyk` closed).
Plan, with the full design record: `claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-aliases-redirect-stubs.md`.

## Result

**The Connect-docs gap is closed exactly: 451 HTML files against Quarto 1's 451**, with
all 99 redirect stub paths identical in location to Q1's.

## This found a live bug in Quarto 1

The first render of the *unmodified* Connect docs **failed**, with two `Q-5-25`
case-only-collision errors. Both are real author errors, and both are actively
destroying pages in the published Q1 site.

`cookbook/content/integrations/msgraph/viewer/r/index.qmd` renders to
`…/viewer/r/index.html` and declares the alias `…/viewer/R/` — capital `R`. On macOS
those are one file. Q1's collision guard is an exact string compare, so it does not
notice, writes the stub, and the stub lands on top of the rendered page:

```
$ head docs-quarto-1/_site/cookbook/content/integrations/msgraph/viewer/r/index.html
<html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">
<head>
  <title>Redirect</title>
    var redirects = {"":"../r/index.html"};
```

That file is not the documentation page. It is a redirect **pointing at itself**. The
same happened to `…/integrations/sharepoint/viewer/r/index.qmd`.

The counts reconcile as Q1 = 350 real pages + 101 stubs; q2 = **352** real pages + 99
stubs. Same total, two more actual pages. The 451-vs-451 measurement was taken on a
scratch copy with those two aliases removed, so the port repo was never modified — but
they do need removing there before it renders under q2.

## How it works

- `DocumentProfile` gains `aliases` + index-aligned `alias_sources` (v9 → v10). Kept
  **raw**: resolving an alias needs only the page's own `output_href`, while *validating*
  one needs every other page in the project. Both therefore move to post-render — which
  is also the only place a diagnostic survives profile caching (the lesson
  `rejected_resources` already records).
- New pure module `project::aliases` — resolves aliases to stub paths (Q1's `fixupHref`
  rules), folds every page's claims into a stub map, detects conflicts, renders the stub.
- `write_alias_redirects` in `website_post_render.rs` does the writing, alongside the
  existing favicon/sitemap/robots hooks.

q2 needs none of Q1's ~60-line incremental-render workaround: Pass 1 profiles every file
regardless of `RenderMode`, so `index.profiles()` always carries the full alias set.

## Deliberate divergences from Quarto 1

| | Quarto 1 | Here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stub over a real page | warns, skips | error `Q-5-23` |
| Two pages, same alias | silent, last writer wins | error `Q-5-24` |
| Paths differing only by case | undetected | error `Q-5-25`, on **every** platform |
| Alias escaping the output dir | no guard | error `Q-5-26` |
| Redirect without JavaScript | blank page | `<noscript>` meta-refresh + `rel=canonical` + visible link |
| `draft: true` page | emits stubs | emits none |
| Non-website project | silent | warns the key is inert |

Conflicts are collected and reported **together** — a site with 69 aliasing files should
not learn about its mistakes one render at a time.

Case-folding is ASCII-only and runs on case-sensitive platforms too, so a Linux CI build
cannot ship a site that breaks the moment it is served from macOS or Windows. The stub
changes mean generated files differ from Q1's byte for byte; that is intended and
documented for porters.

## Two supporting fixes found on the way

- **`config_sources::rebase_source_candidates`.** A collision diagnostic names two
  documents, and both root their front matter at the dense `FileId(0)`. The existing
  binder registers the first file to claim an id and skips the rest, so the second
  document's byte offsets would have rendered against the *first* document's text — the
  exact mis-pairing `bd-m6wmztln` and the `add-file-with-id` lint exist to prevent,
  reached from the other direction. Spans are now re-keyed onto each file's own
  path-derived id, using only blessed APIs.
- **`orchestrator`** no longer stringifies a `post_render` error that already carries
  structured diagnostics. That flattened Ariadne spans into an opaque message the caller
  could not inspect, re-render, or serialize.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` green; 11793 workspace tests pass; `cargo xtask lint` clean.
- 50 unit tests in `project::aliases`, 16 integration tests in `website_aliases.rs`, 4 profile-extraction tests.
- End-to-end through the binary on the in-tree repro fixture, output inspected directly.
- New codes `Q-5-23`–`Q-5-26` ship with their `docs/errors/` pages in the same commit,
  plus a user guide at `docs/guides/projects/aliases.qmd`. Docs site renders 236/236 and
  the cross-links resolve.
- No snapshot (`.snap`) files added, modified, or removed.

Follow-up `bd-wdhhl0t9` tracks stale-stub cleanup (a removed alias leaves its stub
behind across renders — Q1 does the same), deliberately out of scope here.

title: Fix indented continuation lines parsing as hard errors (bd-j7be7kuc)
description:
## Summary Fixes the P0 v0.18.0 regression tracked by `bd-indented-continuation-parse-error-j7be7kuc`: a soft-wrapped continuation line starting with `-`, `+`, or a digit became a **hard parse error when indented**, dropping the entire file from the render. Introduced by 92737cdd (the bd-w6tod0gh fix), whose new gate peeks were only exercised at indent 0. Real-world impact: the Posit Connect docs port lost its entire 53k-line API reference page. A 280-cell characterization sweep (leader × indent 0–10 × context top/bullet/ordered/quote, pandoc 3.9 as reference) showed 118 regressed cells. All are fixed; the only remaining sweep errors are the 28 deliberate `*5 stars` unclosed-emphasis cells. ## Mechanism When a SOFT_LINE_ENDING gate peek judged an indented line "prose", the peeked path skips `mark_end` (the lexer cannot rewind to post-indent/pre-delimiter), stranding the line's leading indentation. If the continuation resumed as plain text, the internal lexer produced `_whitespace` — which the grammar state after `_soft_line_ending` could not shift. Backtick/star peeks survived by accident (their continuations start with external-scanner tokens that absorb the whitespace); in-list cases survived only when the indent equaled the content column exactly. ## Fix (two parts) - **Grammar**: `_soft_line_break` absorbs an optional trailing `_whitespace` under `prec.right`. Continuation-line leading whitespace contributes nothing to the inline stream, matching pandoc. Parser regenerated; error-message table regenerated (state renumbering). - **Scanner**: the marker peeks are now shape-only; indentation judgment moved to the call sites where the reference column is knowable. Gate 1 (pre-`match_line`, raw columns) compares against a new `claimable_list_indentation()` (the leading LIST_ITEM* run of the block stack) + 3, skipping the peek on over-indent so the non-peeked `mark_end` absorbs the indentation; gate 2 (post-`match_line`) compares the residual indentation against 3 on both paths. This fixes three defects: the raw-vs-relative misread of `peek_ordered_marker`'s old internal guard (a nested `1.` at indent 4 now nests — the Connect-docs case), the missing guard on `peek_dash_plus_opens_block` (over-indented bullets are now lazy prose per CommonMark, not phantom block openers), and `first_peeked` being set by peeks that never advanced. ## Testing - New 138-cell table-driven integration test (`crates/pampa/tests/integration/test_indented_continuation.rs`), fail-first verified: the 72+27+3 pre-fix failures matched the sweep prediction cell-for-cell. Expectations follow CommonMark; pandoc agrees on every regressed cell; deliberate qmd deviations are pinned as controls. - New tree-sitter corpus file `test/corpus/indented-continuation.txt` (10 cases) adds the previously-missing indent dimension. - `tree-sitter test` 582/582; `cargo nextest run --workspace` 11727/11727 with **zero snapshot changes**; full `cargo xtask verify` (including the WASM leg) green. - E2E: the Connect-docs repro project renders **3/3 files (was 0/3)**; inspected HTML shows the digit-leading wrap joined into a single `

` and the nested `

    ` markup present. ## Discovered work (filed, not fixed here) - `bd-mt1ksg9b` — the `*` peeks share the same over-indent defect (pre-existing: `hello\n * item` still hard-errors). - `bd-z69hr4o0` — spurious `Space` after `SoftBreak` on indented backtick/star continuations (pre-existing). Also adds `claude-notes/instructions/scanner-indentation-contexts.md`: scanner line-start changes must sweep indent × context, with the raw-vs-residual `s->indentation` trap and the `mark_end`/residual-whitespace mechanics documented. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Lua filters: support the returned-table and filter-list forms (bd-lua-filter-table-form-ignored-ph23becz)
description:
Fixes `bd-lua-filter-table-form-ignored-ph23becz`. Also fixes `bd-18a2r2lp`,
which was discovered while scoping this.

## The bug

A Lua filter written in Pandoc's standard returned-table form ran none of its
handlers and emitted **no error, warning, or diagnostic of any kind**:

```lua
return { Str = function(el) … end }   -- silently did nothing
function Str(el) … end                -- worked
```

`apply_lua_filter` loaded the chunk with `exec_async()`, discarding its return
value, and rebuilt a handler table from globals only. `get_filter_table`'s own
doc comment described supporting both forms; only the globals half was ever
implemented. This is not a regression — the function arrived globals-only with
the original Lua landing (`0f9fc8da`, 2025-12-02).

Real-world hit: the `posit-dev/mermaid-zoom` extension used by the Posit
Connect docs port is written in this form, so its pan/zoom overlay was silently
absent from all 14 diagram pages. Diagnosing that took a bisect against a
hand-written control filter, because nothing in the render output said a
declared filter had done nothing.

## What changed

Filter scripts now follow pandoc's rule, **pinned by probe against pandoc
3.9.0.2** — the version `differential/ORACLE_VERSION` pins, so the probes
became oracle-backed test cases:

| The script… | q2 uses… |
| --- | --- |
| returns nothing | the script's **global** functions |
| returns a table, `rawlen == 0` | that **table**; globals ignored |
| returns a table, `rawlen > 0` | each entry as a **successive pass**, in order |
| returns anything else | **`Q-11-6` error** |

Two implementation choices where the obvious reading is wrong, both commented
at the call site:

- **`call_async`, not `eval_async`.** mlua's `eval` first tries to compile the
  source as an *expression*, which would make q2 accept a filter file holding a
  bare `{ Str = f }` that pandoc rejects as a syntax error. `call_async`
  compiles strictly as a block, like pandoc's `dofile`.
- **`MultiValue`, not `Value`.** `Value` collapses "returned nothing" and
  "returned nil" into the same `Value::Nil`, but those must diverge (globals vs.
  error). The classifier switches on a **count** of returned values.

### Strict pandoc parity is a deliberate behavior change

Five filter shapes that "worked" before now behave differently. This was
discussed and decided rather than stumbled into: each is a filter doing two
conflicting things at once (returning a value *and* defining globals), so there
is no defensible way to pick between them, and matching pandoc is the least
harm.

| filter shape | pandoc | q2 before | q2 now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| global `Str` + `return {Str=g}` | `TABLE-RAN` | `GLOBAL-RAN` | `TABLE-RAN` |
| global `Str` + `return {}` | nothing runs | `GLOBAL-RAN` | nothing runs |
| global `Str` + `return { {} }` | nothing runs | `GLOBAL-RAN` | nothing runs |
| global `Str` + `return nil` | error | `GLOBAL-RAN` | `Q-11-6` |
| global `Str` + `return 5` | error | `GLOBAL-RAN` | `Q-11-6` |

### Diagnostics

`Q-11-6` (invalid filter-script return) and `Q-11-7` (unrecognized handler
name), each with its catalog entry **and** `docs/errors/lua/<code>.qmd` in the
same commit, as the `error-docs-page-missing` lint requires.

```
$ pampa input.md -F typo.lua -t plain
Warning [Q-11-7]: Lua filter 'typo.lua' defines a handler 'Strs', which is not
an element type Quarto knows about, so it will never run. Did you mean 'Str'?
```

**Known limitation:** `Q-11-7` covers the returned-table form only. A typo in a
*global* handler name is indistinguishable from an ordinary helper function, so
that case stays silent. The docs steer authors toward `local` helpers.

### bd-18a2r2lp, and why `types.rs` changed more than you might expect

The walker dispatches on `tag_name`, but the globals scan had its own
hand-written ~50-name list, and the two had drifted: `Attr`, `BlockMetadata`,
`CaptionBlock`, `NoteDefinitionFencedBlock` and `NoteDefinitionPara` were
dispatchable but never copied from globals, so filters defining them were
silently dropped. Proven with `doc:walk`, which hands the walker a table
directly and bypasses the scan — the same handler name fired as a table entry
and not as a global.

Writing the list a second time with a test to keep the two in step would have
rebuilt exactly the arrangement that caused the bug, just with an alarm on it.
Instead an `element_tag_names!` macro generates **both** the `tag_name` match
arms and the list of names it can return. The match stays exhaustive, so a new
AST variant fails to compile until it is listed, and the constant cannot
disagree with the dispatch. **This is the most reviewable-worthy part of the
diff** — if you would rather keep `tag_name` as plain match arms and accept a
test-guarded duplicate list, that is a clean revert of one hunk.

## Tests

TDD throughout: every test was **observed failing first**, with the failure
messages recorded in the plan's phase log.

- **22 unit tests** in `filter_tests.rs` — the return-value forms, the five
  parity flips, the `return nil` vs fall-off-the-end distinction, the
  bd-18a2r2lp regression, and the warning + edit-distance helpers.
- **8 differential cases** with committed oracles generated by real pandoc
  3.9.0.2. Snapshot-style artifacts, so explicitly: **8 oracles added, 0
  existing oracles changed** (checked with `git status` after
  `regen-oracles.sh`, which rewrites every case). The three error-shaped probes
  cannot be oracle cases — the harness compares JSON ASTs and pandoc produces
  none — so they are unit tests.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify` — **all 14 steps pass** (Rust 11708/11708 with
  `-D warnings`, hub-client 861 + 109, WASM 131/131 against a freshly built
  artifact).
- End-to-end through the real binary: the four-document repro now renders
  `TABLE-FORM-RAN` and `LIST-FORM-RAN` where it rendered an untouched `MARKER`;
  output inspected, not inferred from the exit code.
- `run-parity-matrix.sh` matches pandoc on every AST-shaped row.

## Docs

`docs/guides/authoring/lua-filters.qmd` gains sections on both filter forms,
ordered passes, and when a handler never runs. Rendered with `q2` (never Q1)
and inspected. The errors sidebar listed only `Q-11-1` of the six existing lua
pages; all seven are now listed.

Plan, phase log, repro and probe scripts:
`claude-notes/plans/2026-08-11-lua-filter-returned-table-form.md`.

Downstream verification tracked in the connect-docs skein as `br-vuf8asgk`.

title: Give navigation item text: markdown semantics; fix page-footer item model
description:
Fixes bd-page-footer-items-f4th80mj (P1, `parity`/`websites`). Real-world hit: the Posit Connect docs port, all 352 pages, on the most-seen chrome of the site. ## What was broken Navigation item `text:` written in `_quarto.yml` was HTML-escaped instead of rendered, and a bare-string page-footer item became an unusable empty link. Five defects, none of which emitted a warning: 1. `text:` escaped, so markup showed as literal text. 2. A bare-string footer item landed in `href=` with an **empty** link body. 3. Shortcodes stayed literal in item strings. 4. Named entities stayed literal there. 5. An item with `text:` but no `href:` was still wrapped in ``. Not page-footer-specific — navbar and sidebar item `text:` were escaped identically. Meanwhile `page-footer.center` already worked, so two regions of one feature disagreed. **(5) had to land with (1).** The common cookie-preferences pattern carries its own `` inside `text:`. Fixing the escaping alone would have put that anchor *inside* q2's unconditional wrapping anchor — nested anchors, invalid HTML, on every page. ## Approach **Defects 1/3/4 were interpretation, not rendering.** `render_text` already walked `PandocInlines` correctly; item `text:` simply arrived as a literal scalar, because untagged strings stay literal in `ProjectConfig` context. Confirmed by control: `!md`-tagging the identical string rendered it perfectly, with no renderer change. Fixed by extending **`MARKDOWN_CONFIG_PATHS`** in `quarto-core/src/transforms/config_markdown.rs` — the registry bd-shortcodes-in-metadata-bp06aub8 built for exactly this class, whose plan explicitly rejected load-time parsing and named item `text:` fields as the growth path. pampa's `ANNOTATIONS` table is untouched. (The original bug report proposed extending `ANNOTATIONS`; that would have been the wrong mechanism.) New in the pattern language: a **`**` segment** matching zero or more levels of nesting through arrays *and* maps, so one entry covers the sidebar's recursive `contents:` and the navbar's nested `menu:`. Descent is bounded at `MAX_CONFIG_DEPTH = 32` and reports **`Q-1-27`** past it — a code that already existed in the catalog, with a docs page, but had never been emitted by anything. That page has been rewritten to describe what actually emits it. **Defect 2 follows Q1's real rule, which measurement showed is _not_ "bare scalar is text".** Given a project containing `about.qmd`: | footer item | Q1 | | --- | --- | | `- about.qmd` | link titled "About Us" | | `- https://example.com` | plain `
  • ` text | | `- nonexistent.qmd` | plain `
  • ` text | | `- Copyright 2026 Example, Inc.` | plain `
  • ` text | So it is **resolution-dependent**: a link iff it names a project document, display text otherwise — bare external URLs included. A blanket "bare scalar is text" rule broke four existing tests that encode the resolving case (`enrich_navigation_items` exists precisely to give `- about.qmd` its title). Since that decision needs the project index, the parser records the scalar in `NavigationItem::bare_text` as a fallback and keeps a provisional href so enrichment runs normally; `FooterGenerateTransform` then demotes whatever enrichment could not resolve. **Demotion runs only when an index was actually consulted** — with no index attached (single-file renders) nothing resolves, so demoting there would convert every bare footer item to text on no evidence. That corner keeps today's behavior and does not claim Q1 parity. **Defect 5:** `render_footer_item` emits the label directly in the `
  • ` when there is no href, mirroring Q1 and the sidebar's existing `SidebarEntry::Heading`. ## Deliberate divergences from Q1 - **Sidebar item text is markdown here.** Q1 resolves entities but does *not* parse markdown in sidebar item text (measured), while it does in the navbar. That inconsistency looks like a Q1 bug; matching it would mean building an entities-only interpretation q2 does not have. - **Item text parses as inline, not blocks.** Q1 emits `

    ` inside footer item anchors. q2's existing blessed `center:` region already omits it, so inline is the internally-consistent choice and avoids `

    ` inside ``. ## Verification - `cargo xtask verify` — all 14 steps passed. - Full workspace suite green (11659). **No snapshot files changed.** `cargo xtask lint` clean. - **End-to-end through the real binary** (`REPRO_YEAR=2026 q2 render` on the committed repro), output inspected: ```html

  • Copyright © 2015-2026 Example, Inc. All Rights Reserved.
  • Cookie Preferences
    • ``` plus navbar `Navbar © bold emph 2026` and sidebar `Sidebar © emph`. The cookie-preferences item emits exactly one anchor. - Docs site (`q2 render docs/`): 229 files, 25 warnings — all pre-existing `Q-13-4`/`Q-5-6`, no `Q-1-27`, nested sidebar intact. Repro configs and the recorded q2/Q1 markup are committed under `claude-notes/plans/2026-08-11-navigation-item-text-markdown-investigation/`. ## Reviewer notes - **Silent behavior change.** Any existing site whose item `text:` contains `*`, `_`, `<`, or `&…;` now renders differently, with no warning. Same tradeoff already accepted for `website.title`; `!str` cannot opt a blessed key out (pre-existing documented limitation of the mechanism). Probably worth a release note. - **`Q-2-9` noise.** Item `text:` carrying raw HTML now raises the informational "HTML element converted to raw HTML" — the repro went 4 → 7. Same diagnostic `center:` and `website.title` already raise, but sites with `` in footer items will see it every render. Happy to file a suppression for blessed config keys if reviewers want one. - **One unrelated commit** rides along: `6516a330` syncs `crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/Cargo.lock` to 0.17.0 (regenerated by `npm run build:wasm`; the lockfile still carried 0.16.0 for in-workspace crates). No dependency changes. Easy to drop. Follow-ups filed: **bd-qzn1azon** (sidebar `section:`, the display-text sibling deliberately left out of scope) and **bd-xygsu15r** (cross-reference the two config-interpretation tables, since the wrong one was proposed once already). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Fix digit/dash/plus-leading continuation line terminating the paragraph
description:
Fixes the P1 parity bug in `bd-digit-line-splits-paragraph-w6tod0gh`. ## The bug A soft-wrapped paragraph line whose first character was a digit, `-` or `+` terminated the paragraph, producing two paragraphs where the author wrote one and splitting a sentence mid-clause: ```markdown To make license leases last 30 minutes you would use the following syntax. ``` Worse, when the wrap fell inside link text the block ended before the closing `]` and the render failed outright: ``` Error: [Q-2-1] Unclosed Span I reached the end of the block before finding a closing ']' for the span or link. ``` This hit 8+ pages of the Posit Connect docs port, wherever a version number, port, timeout or RFC number happened to land at the start of a wrapped line. Authors can't reasonably be expected to avoid wrapping before a number. ## Root cause Both `SOFT_LINE_ENDING` gates in `scanner.c` excluded those characters as a blanket character class, with no peek — unlike the adjacent `` ` `` and `*` branches, which peek and block the soft break only when a fence, list marker or thematic break really forms. `parse_ordered_list_marker` already implements the CommonMark interruption rule correctly, but was unreachable from the gates: the paragraph had already been closed by the time it would run. ## The fix Two peek helpers mirroring the existing `*` peek. No grammar change — `parser.c` is untouched, so there are no generated diffs. - `peek_dash_plus_opens_block` — a single `-`/`+` plus whitespace/EOL (list marker), or 3+ `-` plus whitespace/EOL (thematic break). - `peek_ordered_marker` — returns `{well_formed, may_interrupt}`, bailing past 9 digits (the longest marker `parse_ordered_list_marker` accepts). ### The subtle part The two gates need **different answers from the same peek**. Gate 1 runs before `match_line`, so it cannot distinguish a sibling list item from a paragraph continuation and has no `all_will_be_matched` guard — it may only ask `well_formed`. Gate 2 runs after `match_line`, where `all_will_be_matched` proves the line belongs to the open blocks, and is the only place the CommonMark interruption rule applies. That split is what separates two cases identical at the character level: ```markdown The number of windows in my house is 14. cannot interrupt -> soft-break (CM 284) 14. The number of doors is 6. 1. a 2. is a sibling item; match_line fails to 2. b match item 1's indent -> new item ``` Two approaches were tried and rejected; both are recorded in code comments so nobody retries them: 1. Applying the "only a bare `1` interrupts" rule in **both** gates broke six existing tests (`issues.txt` #72, `list.txt` 4/15/16, CommonMark Examples 261/282) — all sibling list items, where gate 1 swallowed `2.` into item 1's paragraph. 2. Consulting `valid_symbols[LIST_MARKER_*]` the way `parse_ordered_list_marker` does fails, because at line-ending scan time the parser is asking for `LINE_ENDING`/`SOFT_LINE_ENDING`, so the marker symbols are not in the valid set and read false for every marker. Separately, the `mark_end` guard after gate 2 was keyed on the character (`!= '`' && != '*'`). With three more peeking branches that proxy no longer holds, so it is now an explicit `second_peeked` boolean — otherwise a peeked run gets swallowed into the `SOFT_LINE_ENDING` token's range. ## Behavior changes beyond the reported symptom Batched deliberately, so habits only need relearning once: - `2.` / `14.` after a paragraph no longer open a spurious `
    `. That was wrong under **both** CommonMark and pandoc-markdown, and was a direct consequence of the paragraph closing before the marker parser ran. - `-5 degrees`, `+5 percent` and `-- em dash` stay in the paragraph. `pampa -t native` now matches `pandoc -f commonmark -t native` **exactly** on the committed `interrupt.qmd` and `dashplus.qmd` fixtures. ## Three hand-escaped workarounds removed The repo already carried workarounds for this bug in the conformance suite. All three failed before this change and pass after: - `new-spec.txt` Example 284: input restored from `\14.` to `14.`, dropping the title *"qmd: start your soft breaks with \1, i'm sorry."* Its expected tree also loses the extra `pandoc_str` the backslash produced. - `block_quote.txt` test 4: input restored from `\1` to `1`, dropping *"but don't start continuation line with 1"* — a lazy-continuation case found during implementation. A fourth instance existed outside this repo: the connect-docs porting session independently hand-escaped an RFC number as `\3986`. ## Tests 15 new `paragraph.txt` cases (15–29) covering digit prose, digit + punctuation, a run longer than any legal marker, `14.`/`2.` not interrupting, `1.`/`1)` still interrupting, the fatal link-text variant, both second-gate paths (list-item and block-quote continuation), `-5`/`+5`, and guards for `- item` / `+ item` / `---`. TDD sequence: 12 tests confirmed failing before any scanner edit. **No `.snap` files added, modified or removed.** Snapshot churn was the main predicted risk and it did not materialize — the AST only changes for inputs that were previously mis-blocked, and no existing snapshot covered one. | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | `tree-sitter test` | 572/572 | | `cargo nextest run --workspace` | 11626 passed, 197 skipped | | `cargo xtask verify` (full, incl. WASM leg) | green | ## End-to-end verification `cargo run --bin q2 -- render doc.qmd`, output inspected in `doc.html`: ```html

    To make license leases last 30 minutes you would use the following syntax.

    The set of characters that must be encoded can be found in Section 3.2.1 of RFC 3986.

    Buy these:

    1. apples
    2. oranges
    ``` The first paragraph is no longer split; the link that previously failed with `Q-2-1` renders intact; a real ordered list still works. ## Out of scope `bd-cxiopjw7` — a `:`-leading continuation line *silently deletes the colon* (`Defined at` / `:host scope.` parses to `Str "at", SoftBreak, Str "host"`). Found while checking the sibling blanket exclusions. Because a single paragraph survives, the colon is consumed somewhere beyond the gate, so this fix does not cover it; filed separately. ## Note for the reviewer Running the WASM build refreshes `crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/Cargo.lock` from `0.16.0` to `0.17.0` version strings — pre-existing staleness after the release bump, unrelated to this change. It is deliberately **not** in this PR to keep the diff focused, but it will show up dirty for anyone running full verify and is worth a separate cleanup. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Bundle the mermaid runtime into rendered sites instead of loading it from a CDN
description:
Closes the CDN dependency in rendered output for `bd-mermaid-runtime-not-bundled-vxejw159`.

## Problem

Every HTML page containing a diagram emitted a module script importing the mermaid runtime from jsDelivr, and nothing was written into the rendered site:

```html
<script type="module">
  import mermaid from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11.12.0/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs';
```

```
$ find _site -iname '*mermaid*'
(nothing)
```

Three separable consequences: air-gapped/closed-network hosting was impossible; published documentation executed third-party code at load time and leaked reader IPs to a CDN; a CDN outage silently degraded every diagram page. The sharpest real-world case is the Posit Connect docs' *"running Connect without internet access"* guide, which itself needed internet access to draw its diagrams.

## Change

The runtime is vendored at `resources/mermaid/mermaid.min.js`, embedded via `include_str!`, registered as an `ArtifactScope::Project` artifact, and referenced with a resolver-computed relative URL. Mechanically this mirrors `resources/revealjs/`.

```
$ ls _site/site_libs
bootstrap  mermaid  quarto

# root page
<script src="site_libs/mermaid/mermaid.min.js"></script>
# nested page
<script src="../site_libs/mermaid/mermaid.min.js"></script>
```

## Two design points reviewers should know

**1. Vendoring `dist/mermaid.min.js` is load-bearing — not `dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs`.** The file we previously imported is a **26 KB stub** that statically imports 10 chunks and *dynamically* imports ~25 more — **one per diagram type** — from a 146-file / 13 MB tree. Vendoring it would leave offline rendering broken *per diagram type*: a flowchart page would work while a gantt page silently failed. The UMD build is self-contained (2.62 MiB, zero dynamic imports) and is byte-identical (SHA-256 `07e37dfa…`) to the copy Quarto 1 ships. Two always-on unit tests guard this.

**2. The artifact is keyed `mermaid:runtime`, deliberately not `js:`.** `ApplyTemplateStage` emits a head `<script>` for every `js:` artifact, which double-loaded the 2.6 MiB bundle. But simply deferring to the template is also wrong: the reveal scaffold collects only `js:revealjs:*`, so a `js:`-keyed runtime would emit **no** tag at all in a deck, silently breaking every diagram in a presentation. The transform therefore owns its own emission into the after-body slot, which both the Bootstrap template and the reveal scaffold wire up. Both halves are pinned by tests (`runtime_is_not_keyed_as_a_template_script`, `revealjs_deck_bundles_the_runtime`).

## Staleness guarding — one deliberate deviation from the reveal.js precedent

Reveal compares embedded bytes against `node_modules` because it has two live sources that must agree. Mermaid has one, and replicating that form would mean adding a devDependency of **66 MB / 793 files** purely to anchor a comparison with nothing to disagree with. Instead:

- **always-on:** the bundle's own embedded `version:"…"` must equal `MERMAID_VERSION` (the string occurs exactly once);
- **always-on:** the bundle must contain no `import(` and no `chunks/`;
- **conditional:** the reveal-style npm byte-compare, skipped while mermaid is absent from `node_modules`, so it starts working automatically if #bd-1vwtdwtq adds it.

Mechanisms 1–4 of the precedent (vendored dir, README, `include_str!`, Project-scoped registration) are followed exactly.

## Verification

- 16 new tests: 7 integration (website sharing, nested-page depth, diagram-free pages, single-doc, **revealjs deck**) and 9 unit.
- Two smoke-all fixtures that asserted the CDN URL now assert a relative `<script src>` and **forbid** `cdn.jsdelivr.net`.
- Full `cargo xtask verify` including the WASM/hub leg: green.
- **End-to-end:** a 3-page website rendered with the real binary, served locally, loaded in Chrome. Flowchart, gantt, and class diagrams all drew as real SVG — three distinct chunks under the ESM build, which is the direct check that the chunk trap is gone — with **zero external network requests**. The nested page resolved `../site_libs/` and got a `304` on the shared copy.

No snapshot files affected.

## Cost

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Vendored file | 2,748,992 B (2.62 MiB) |
| `wasm_quarto_hub_client_bg.wasm` | 38.9 MB → 41.8 MB (**+7.3 %**) |

The WASM growth was not anticipated in design: `quarto-core` is linked into `wasm-quarto-hub-client`, so the bundle is embedded there too (confirmed by probing the `.wasm` for mermaid strings, not inferred from the delta). Accepted by the author. Those bytes are currently unused by the preview path but make #bd-1vwtdwtq's chosen design cheaper, so they are deliberately **not** `cfg`-gated out — gating would also make WASM-side HTML export silently CDN-dependent.

## Follow-ups filed

- `bd-1vwtdwtq` — `q2 preview` / hub-client still load mermaid from jsDelivr
- `bd-93ensbpn` — mermaid CSS/theming parity with Quarto 1
- `bd-43gpsd7c` — investigate compressed compile-time embedding (`include_compressed_str!`)

title: smoke-all: hold fixture patterns under source-location, gate on fixture PRs
description: Fixes the three smoke-all fixtures that have been red in the nightly E2E, and closes the loop that let them land red in the first place. Braid: bd-nhn7snpg ## What was wrong Three fixtures assert markup adjacency — `strong>_bringit_`, `renv`, `Note…`. That holds under `q2 render`, but the hub preview renders with `format.html.source-location: full`, which puts `data-sid`/`data-loc` on the opening tag, so the text no longer sits flush against `>`. Nothing regressed. The fixtures never passed the preview harness: | Fixture | Added by | First nightly red | |---|---|---| | `extensions/contract-doc-shortcodes` | #450 (2026-07-31) | 2026-08-01 | | `extensions/contract-return-coercions` | #450 (2026-07-31) | 2026-08-01 | | `quarto-test/callout-title-attribute` | #496 (2026-08-10) | 2026-08-11 | The nightly's last green was 2026-07-31 — the night before #450 landed. ## Why nobody saw it These fixtures have three consumers, and only one renders the way preview does: | Consumer | Renders with | Catches this | |---|---|---| | `smoke_all.rs` (native, every PR) | no source-location | no | | `smokeAll.wasm.test.ts` (vitest, every PR) | no source-location | no | | `smoke-all.spec.ts` (Playwright) | `source-location: full` | **yes** | The Playwright leg was nightly/dispatch-only, so an author validated against `q2 render`, saw two green gates, landed, and the failure surfaced next morning in a run nobody watches. ## Changes **Patterns** get `[^>]*` slots so they hold under both renderers, plus `!str` so the `[...]`/`<...>` aren't parsed as markdown reference-link syntax or raw HTML — warnings that fail the fixtures' `noErrorsOrWarnings` assertions. `!str` is q2's documented opt-out, the `yaml` package the E2E discovery uses resolves it to the plain scalar, and other fixtures in the tree already use it. **The negative guard** in `callout-title-attribute` got the same treatment for a sharper reason: without it that guard is *vacuous* under source-location. title: Recover doc ids from case-folded splay dirs (bd-eb2wnxkp Part A + collect guard)
description:
## Summary

Fixes the macOS/Windows doc-id mis-identification in the `hub admin` scan/collect tooling (bd-eb2wnxkp) and, with it, the ~2%-per-run macOS CI flake in the `admin_collect_lifecycle` / `admin_scan_real_store` test families (bd-u0tldu4z).

samod splays a doc id across `<2-char-prefix>/<rest>/` directories. Base58 is case-sensitive; APFS/NTFS are not: when two ids' prefixes differ only by case, both docs share one level-1 directory and every id read back through it inherits the first-creator's casing. A mis-cased **live** doc then fails the string-compared live-set check, classifies as orphaned, and becomes eligible for quarantine — the data-loss path. Stress evidence: 3 failures in 142 isolated iterations pre-fix, all the case-flip signature; captured logs in `claude-notes/plans/flaky-admin-collect-lifecycle-investigation/`.

### Part A — checksum-validated case-variant recovery (`fb1e2818`/rebased)

- `recover_doc_id(prefix, rest)` tests the ≤4 case variants of the splay prefix against `DocumentId`'s bs58check checksum: exactly one parses (~2⁻³² false accept); zero or multiple distinct matches hard-fail (`Unidentifiable`/`Ambiguous`) so the collector never acts on a guessed id.
- `list_doc_ids_filesystem` is now fallible; `hub admin scan` and `collect()` abort on error; recovery that changes casing emits a warning.
- Recovery returns the recovered id *string*, deduped by parsed id preferring the as-read casing — legacy-UUID hex parses case-insensitively (several casings, one id) and must neither read as ambiguous nor be re-encoded.
- **On-disk layout unchanged — no store migration.**

### Defense in depth — collect round-trip guard (`7657c71d`/rebased)

`collect()` maps every recoverable id to the on-disk director(ies) whose *actual names* round-trip to it; a candidate that doesn't round-trip to exactly one real directory is skipped regardless of liveness, and the quarantine rename source comes from that map — never from path construction + filesystem case-folding.

## Test plan

- [x] TDD red confirmed pre-fix (deterministic hand-built-splay tests; no random id draw)
- [x] 8 unit tests on checksum-verified fixtures, incl. the always-present `st/` adapter-dir collision and duplicate-dir ambiguity
- [x] 4 integration tests, incl. end-to-end: folded live doc survives `collect --execute`; folded orphan still quarantined under its true id (runtime case-insensitivity probe; skip honestly on case-sensitive filesystems)
- [x] E2E through the real binary: `hub admin scan` on a hand-built folded store emits the recovery warning and the true id in the manifest; refusal exits 1
- [x] Full workspace: 11483/11483; `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` green
- [x] Post-fix stress: **150/150 clean iterations** (pre-fix baseline 3/142)
- [ ] CI on macOS runners — the point of this PR; the flake fired there most recently (PR #479)

Braid: bd-eb2wnxkp (in_progress; Parts B/C still open), bd-u0tldu4z (stays open for a dedicated post-merge stress verification), bd-3uw7uufa (upstream samod follow-up).

title: Lint: require a docs page for every error code (bd-u2qj4y29)
description:
Closes the loop bd-u2qj4y29 was filed about: an error code could reach `main` with no documentation page, so the `docs_url` every diagnostic prints would 404.

## The rule

`crates/xtask/src/lint/error_docs.rs`, called from `lint::run_check`, so it fires in `cargo xtask lint`, in step 1 of `cargo xtask verify`, and in CI — before a PR opens, which was the stated requirement. It checks exactly two things:

- **missing page** — the catalog declares `Q-X-Y`, no `docs/errors/<subsystem>/Q-X-Y.qmd` exists.
- **`docs_url` drift** — the entry's `docs_url` is not the canonical `https://quarto.org/docs/errors/<subsystem>/<code>`.

The second one earns its place: `Q-3-42` and `Q-3-43` had shipped with the `<subsystem>` segment missing entirely (`.../docs/errors/Q-3-42`), which a file-existence check alone would have passed while the link the user clicks stayed broken.

This is the first **repo-level** rule in that module — the other three grep a single Rust file each — so `run_check` grows a seam for whole-tree checks. Violations anchor at the offending entry's line in `error_catalog.json`, where the declaration promising the page lives.

## It immediately caught a live one

Rebasing this branch onto `origin/main` (v0.17.0) brought in PR #499's diagram cell-option diagnostics, renumbered to `Q-2-47`/`Q-2-48` by `91342cf8`. **Both had shipped with no pages**, and the lint failed on them within seconds of the rebase:

```
crates/quarto-error-catalog/error_catalog.json:1367:3: [error-docs-page-missing]
  Q-2-47 has no documentation page; diagnostics carrying this code link to
  https://quarto.org/docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-47, which 404s until
  docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-47.qmd exists
```

bd-u2qj4y29's description records those two as "shipped page-less in PR #499, fixed in a follow-up" — but the follow-up only renumbered them. The pages were never written, and v0.17.0 released with the 404. Both are written here.

## The backfill

30 pages total. 28 had accumulated before this branch, each added by a feature PR that stopped at the catalog:

| Subsystem | Count | Codes |
| --------- | ----: | ----- |
| `project` | 11 | Q-5-8…Q-5-12, Q-5-17…Q-5-22 |
| `extension` | 9 | Q-16-1…Q-16-9 |
| `lua` | 4 | Q-11-2…Q-11-5 |
| `writer` | 2 | Q-3-42, Q-3-43 |
| `theme` | 1 | Q-14-3 |
| `markdown` | 1 | Q-2-42 |

`docs/errors/extension/` did not exist at all — the whole subsystem was undocumented. Plus `Q-2-47`/`Q-2-48` from the rebase.

title: Process mermaid %%| cell options: captions, cross-references, alt text (bd-mermaid-cell-options-9wo3crl0)
description:
Processes mermaid `%%|` cell options, so `fig-cap` / `fig-alt` on a ```` ```mermaid ```` fence reach the output instead of sitting verbatim in the diagram source (bd-mermaid-cell-options-9wo3crl0). Plan, design rationale and full verification record: `claude-notes/plans/2026-08-10-mermaid-cell-options.md`. ## The finding that shaped this The caption / figure / crossref machinery **already worked** for a mermaid fence — it just keyed off the `#|` marker. At the previous HEAD, a ```` ```mermaid ```` block with `#| label:` + `#| fig-cap:` rendered a full `quarto-float` figure with numbering and `aria-describedby`; only the `%%|` spelling was unrecognized. `cell_options::comment_syntax_for` had no mermaid entry, because Q1 keeps mermaid's `%%` on the language handler and in `constants.lua` rather than in `kLangCommentChars`, which is what that table was ported from. The architectural constraint: this has to happen in `PreEngineSugaringStage`, not in `transforms/mermaid.rs`. That transform is on `Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED` (so preview would diverge) *and* runs after `crossref-render` (so a `label:` could never be numbered). Doing it pre-engine gives preview/render parity for free. ## What changed, commit by commit | | | |---|---| | `cell_options` learns mermaid's `%%` | with a cross-talk test against matlab/tikz's single `%` | | shorthand migrated onto `cell_options` | language-aware marker + real YAML parsing, replacing a private `#|`-only `split_once(':')` matcher | | `fig-cap` parsed as markdown inlines | via the same entry point document metadata uses | | unlabelled `fig-cap` → `Block::Figure` | `fig-scap` → `Caption::short` | | `fig-alt` → mermaid's `accDescr:` | and stop consuming options we cannot route | | Q-2-47 / Q-2-48 diagnostics | source-mapped to the offending key | | preview-parity test, docs, worked example | | Three pre-existing defects in the shared `#|` shorthand are fixed along the way — all reproduced on a plain ```` ```python ```` cell first, so they were never mermaid-specific: - **bd-5jcmmj1f** — `fig-cap: "A caption."` rendered as `Figure 1: "A caption."` with literal quote characters. - **bd-sdpp9rw4** — `fig-cap: A *strong* claim` rendered the asterisks literally. - **bd-il6pxq4f** — `fig-alt` and `fig-scap` were consumed (stripped from the body) but never read back out; the text vanished with no warning. Authors who wrote `fig-alt` believed they had an accessible description and did not. ## Behavior changes worth reviewing **`#|` in a mermaid fence is no longer a cell-option marker.** Deliberate (Q1 parity; q2 is in `0.*` and accepting both would teach that `#|` is universal), but it is a *visible* break: `#` is not a mermaid comment, so leftover lines become diagram source and mermaid fails on them. Q-2-48 reports this at the exact source line rather than leaving a silently broken diagram. **A diagram cell warns about options it cannot act on** (Q-2-47), scoped to diagram cells only. On an executable cell an unrecognized key is normally an engine option (`echo`, `eval`, …), so warning there would fire on essentially every real document. Q1 accepts `theme` and `mermaid-format` on mermaid cells and q2 does not yet, so those warn today — `DIAGRAM_OPTION_KEYS` carries a note to add `theme` when the mermaid theming strands land. **`fig-alt` on a non-diagram cell is now left in the body** for the engine instead of being consumed. Strictly better than the previous silent drop, and for jupyter/knitr `fig-alt` is a real engine option. ## Verification `cargo xtask verify` (full, including the hub/WASM leg) passes on the rebased base. **No snapshot files changed** anywhere in the workspace. End-to-end through the binary, output inspected — e.g. a `%%| fig-cap` + `%%| fig-alt` diagram with no label now emits: ```html
``` **The accessibility claim was verified against real mermaid 11.12.0** (the pinned version) under jsdom, because both browser routes were unavailable in the session: the injected line becomes `` inside the SVG with the SVG's `aria-describedby` pointing at it, and a negative control confirms mermaid *rejects* `accDescr:` placed before the diagram-type line — which is why the directive is inserted after the first declaration line rather than at the top. Not verified: presentation in an actual screen reader, and the `q2 preview` UI in a live browser session. ## Note for reviewers `main` claimed Q-2-42 … Q-2-46 while this branch was in flight (#497), so the two codes here were renumbered to **Q-2-47 / Q-2-48** during the rebase. The Phase 6 commit *message* still names the pre-rebase numbers; code, catalog, tests and plan all use the final ones. ## Follow-ups filed - **bd-vg8p5yoj** — `qmd-syntax-helper` rule rewriting ```` ```{mermaid} ```` → ```` ```mermaid ````. This is the other half of the Connect-docs story: all 33 diagrams there are brace-form and still render as source text until it lands. Cell options need no rewrite — Q1 documents already write `%%|`. - **bd-e3m3rkik** — pre-existing, surfaced while reading the preview AST: because `mermaid-render` is excluded from preview, `CodeBlockRenderTransform` wraps mermaid blocks in copy-button chrome there that `q2 render` suppresses by transform ordering. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Expand {{< include >}} inside fenced code blocks (bd-include-in-code-block-f8mvtczn)
description:
## The bug

An `include` standing alone inside a fenced code block — the Quarto 1 idiom for embedding a source file as a listing —

````markdown
```{.python filename="app.py"}
{{< include app.py >}}
```
````

rendered with the entire fence body replaced by the token `?include`. A `Q-17-4` warning fired, but its hint ("put the include shortcode in its own paragraph, surrounded by blank lines") was actively wrong here — following it would change what the page means.

Motivating corpus: the Posit Connect docs port, where this is the single largest content loss — **44 listings across 20 files**, ~1300 lines of embedded source. Every cookbook integration recipe embeds its `requirements.txt` / `app.py` / `app.R` this way.

## Why the fix is in `IncludeExpansionStage`, not the transform

The strand originally proposed handling this in `ShortcodeResolveTransform`'s text-expansion path — which is where `?include` is written. That site cannot work: the transform runs in `AstTransformsStage` (pipeline stage 13), *after* `DocumentProfileStage` (stage 6) drains the include side-channel into `DocumentProfile.includes`. Profiles are read-only, so an include registered there could never become a dependency — editing `app.py` would not rebuild the page embedding it.

`IncludeExpansionStage` (stage 3) already holds `ctx.runtime`, `base_dir`, `project_dir`, `recorded_includes` and the cycle stack, and expanding there means the shortcode is gone before stage 13 — so `Q-17-4` stops firing for this shape with no change to the diagnostic, preserving the invariant documented at `shortcode_resolve.rs`.

## Behavior

Verified against `quarto-cli` @ `abc6a78ed` (source read) and a real `quarto render` of the repro.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Recognition** | Line-strict — the shortcode must be the sole content of its line. This matches Q1's `isBlockShortcode` (`/^\s*{{< … >}}\s*$/`) exactly; the strand's "Q1 substitutes anywhere in code text" framing was wrong. Indented include lines splice without re-indentation, as Q1 does. |
| **Recursion** | On, matching Q1's `standaloneInclude`. Cycles caught via the existing canonicalized `include_stack` (`Q-17-1`). |
| **Trailing newline** | Exactly one trimmed. Q1 *appends* newlines but Pandoc's markdown re-read absorbs them; q2 emits HTML straight from the AST, so without the trim every listing gains a blank final line. |
| **Opt-out** | `shortcodes="false"` still wins. The predicate is now shared with `ShortcodeResolveTransform` instead of duplicated. |
| **Leftovers** | An unhandled include in *code* text is preserved verbatim rather than becoming `?include`. Mid-line includes are deliberately unrecognized, and Q1 leaves them untouched and silent. |
| **Dependencies** | Fence targets flow through the shared `collect_include_paths` walker, so the preview dep-graph rebuilds a page when its embedded file changes. |

### Deliberate divergences from Q1

- **Consecutive includes in one fence** — Q1 renders `AAA\n\nBBB`, we render `AAA\nBBB`. Q1's blank line is the same `standaloneInclude` artifact as the trailing-newline case: a markdown block separator that is noise inside a fence.
- **Nested-path anchor** — we resolve nested includes against the *including file's* directory (matching block-position includes, bd-1fz3vh99); Q1 resolves against the document. Confirmed empirically: Q1 fatally aborts the render on `sub/outer.qmd` including a sibling.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify` — all 14 steps green, WASM/hub-client leg included
- 19 unit tests + 8 full-pipeline integration tests (`include_code_fence.rs`) + 1 smoke-all fixture (`includes/in-code-fence/`)
- Full workspace: 11,376 tests passing; clippy and `cargo fmt` clean
- **No snapshot files added, modified, or removed**
- Three `quarto-preview` dep tests updated — they pinned the old "a fence include is not a dependency" contract

### End-to-end on the real corpus

`352 of 352` files rendered. Corpus-wide `?include` count dropped to **1**, and that one is not a fence — it is the raw-HTML shape the strand itself calls docs-fixable (`licenses/index.md`: an include directly under an HTML comment, swallowed into a `RawBlock`), where `Q-17-4`'s existing hint is exactly right. The worst-case page (`databricks/viewer/python/index.qmd`, ten listings across five framework tabs) renders all of them, including a 92-line `app.py`.

## Follow-up

**bd-cq0xhxg5** (docs, P2) — `include` is absent from the built-ins table in `docs/guides/authoring/shortcodes.qmd`, absent from its "Where shortcodes are evaluated" section, and there is no includes guide page at all. Filed to document the two expansion mechanisms once this lands.

Plan with full decision record: `claude-notes/plans/2026-08-10-include-in-code-block.md`
