title: Add lua infra and built-in extensions
description:
## Summary

This PR ports five built-in extensions from TS Quarto — **lipsum**, **version**, **kbd**, **placeholder**, and **video** — and builds the general infrastructure needed to run them unchanged in both the native CLI and the hub-client WASM environment.

The extensions themselves are relatively thin. The real substance of this PR is the infrastructure: a Lua API layer, a dependency pipeline, WASM file I/O overrides, and hub-client post-processing that together allow TS Quarto extensions to run as-is on our Rust engine.

## Infrastructure

### 1. Lua constructor type coercion

`pandoc.Para("text")` now auto-coerces strings to Inlines via `peek_inlines_fuzzy`, matching Pandoc's Lua marshal behavior. TS Quarto extensions routinely pass bare strings to constructors that expect Inline lists, so this is a prerequisite for running them without modification.

### 2. Built-in extension discovery and embedding

Extensions in `resources/extensions/quarto/` are embedded in the binary at compile time via `include_dir!`. At runtime they're extracted to a temp directory (native) or loaded into VFS (WASM). The discovery system merges built-in extensions with user-installed extensions, with user extensions winning on name collision — the same semantics as TS Quarto.

### 3. quarto.doc Lua API and dofile/loadfile for WASM

The `quarto.doc` namespace provides the APIs that extensions use to interact with the rendering pipeline: `is_format()`, `add_html_dependency()`, `include_text()`, and `has_bootstrap()`. A script-directory stack ensures `quarto.utils.resolve_path()` resolves relative to the calling script rather than the document, which matters when extensions load sibling files.

`dofile()` and `loadfile()` are overridden in the WASM and test environments to route through `SystemRuntime`, since the native C `fopen` doesn't work in WASM. The `dofile` override pushes and pops the script-directory stack, so nested `resolve_path` calls work correctly (this is the pattern `video-filter.lua` uses to load shared code from `video.lua`).

### 4. Pipeline wiring for HTML dependencies and text includes

A new `dependency.rs` module provides `store_html_dependencies()`, which reads CSS/JS files via the runtime and stores them as artifacts at `libs/{name}/{filename}`, and `push_text_includes()`, which routes `include_text("in-header"|"before-body"|"after-body")` calls into `PandocIncludes`. The template integration adds `$for(scripts)$` and `$for(include-after)$` loops, and `render_to_file` writes dependency artifacts to `{stem}_files/libs/` on disk.

### 5. Resource prefix for native file rendering

Extension artifact paths like `libs/kbd/kbd.css` need a `{stem}_files/` prefix in the HTML `<link>` and `<script>` tags to match where the files are actually written on disk. A `resource_prefix` field threads from `render_to_file` through to the template stage.

### 6. Hub-client post-processor for VFS resources

The preview iframe can't fetch `libs/` URLs — those files only exist in VFS. The post-processor now reads extension CSS and JS from VFS and inlines them: CSS is converted to data URIs on `<link>` tags, and JS is inserted as inline `<script>` elements. A synthetic `DOMContentLoaded` event is dispatched after inlining so that extension scripts which register listeners (like kbd.js) get their initialization callback.

### 7. quarto.utils.as_inlines and as_blocks

Type coercion functions matching TS Quarto's `_utils.lua`. These convert between Pandoc AST types (Inlines, Blocks, single elements, tables, strings) without parsing markdown. Our implementation uses lookup tables for block/inline type classification because our `pandoc.utils.type()` returns specific element names (`"Para"`, `"Str"`) rather than generic categories (`"Block"`, `"Inline"`).

### 8. Testing infrastructure

A `SMOKE_FILTER` environment variable allows running individual smoke-all fixtures across all three test runners (native Rust, WASM Vitest, and Playwright E2E), which made iterating on extension bugs much faster.

### 9. Preview iframe sandbox (for discussion)

The preview iframe's sandbox attribute currently blocks all script execution (`allow-same-origin allow-popups` without `allow-scripts`). This restriction was added recently in d6eb0604 without specific rationale — before that commit, the iframes had no sandbox at all. The final commit in this PR adds `allow-scripts` to re-enable extension JS execution. This needs team discussion before merging: do we want to allow scripts in the preview, or should extensions degrade gracefully when JS can't run?

## Extensions

All five extensions are byte-identical copies from TS Quarto, with one exception: `placeholder.lua` has a small simplification where TS Quarto checks `quarto.format.is_typst_output()` to choose between SVG and PNG output formats. Since we don't have that API yet, we default to SVG, which works for HTML output.

title: fix(hub-client): add onKeyDown guard for async Automerge change events
description:
Fixes #35. Follow-up to #100.

## Bug

Automerge-repo's message pipeline has `await` boundaries between the WebSocket message and the DocHandle `change` event. The immediate callback from #102 fires in a later microtask, which usually drains before the next keystroke — but not always. In the rare case where a keystroke macrotask fires first, Monaco is still stale and characters land at wrong positions.

## Fix

Add an `editor.onKeyDown` guard that syncs Monaco with Automerge before the keystroke is processed. A `pendingRemoteSync` dirty flag (set only for remote changes via an `isApplyingLocal` guard) ensures the expensive `getValue()` + diff only runs when a remote change is actually pending. Solo typing costs one boolean check per keystroke.

title: Fix first keystroke lost after selection in Monaco editor
description:
Fixes https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/35. Follow-up to https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/pull/100.

Two independent bugs caused the first keystroke after a selection to be lost in the Monaco editor.

**Bug 1 — intermittent, any selection direction:** `handleEditorChange` was recreated every render, so `@monaco-editor/react` disposed and re-subscribed its `onDidChangeModelContent` listener on every render via `useEffect`. Keystrokes landing between paint and effect execution were silently dropped.

**Fix:** Wrap `handleEditorChange` in `useCallback` (using a `currentFileRef` to avoid stale closures). Also promote the inline `options` object to a module-level constant — it was a new reference every render, triggering a second unnecessary effect. Two regression tests verify the callback stays stable across re-renders and still picks up file switches via the ref.

**Bug 2 — deterministic, backward selections only:** On macOS, typing the first character into a backward (RTL) selection is silently dropped by the browser. Monaco receives the `keyDown` event but the hidden textarea never fires an `input` event, so the model never changes. Confirmed by instrumentation: `editor.onKeyDown` fires, `model.onDidChangeContent` does not. The selection sync, presence hook, and reconciliation effect were all ruled out by targeted disabling.

**Fix:** An `onKeyDown` handler detects RTL selections on printable keystrokes and flips them to LTR (same highlighted range, cursor moves to end). The browser's input pipeline then processes the character normally. The hot path (no selection or already LTR) is two cheap checks before returning.

title: Extension shortcode support (Phase 3)
description:
## Summary

Implements Lua-based shortcode support for Quarto extensions, allowing extensions to define custom shortcodes via Lua scripts (e.g., `{{< hello >}}`). This is Phase 3 of the extensions roadmap, building on the extension discovery/metadata (Phase 1) and filter resolution (Phase 2) work already merged to main.

### What's new

- **Lua shortcode engine** (`pampa/src/lua/shortcode.rs`): Loads and dispatches Lua shortcode handlers. Supports both `return-table` and `env-function` Lua conventions, matches TS Quarto's calling convention (`args`, `kwargs`, `meta`, `raw_args`, `context`), and handles inline and block-level return values.

- **Block-level shortcode results**: Added `ShortcodeResult::Blocks` variant with two-pass resolution logic — a `Para`/`Plain` containing a single shortcode gets block context; otherwise falls back to inline with graceful flattening.

- **Pipeline wiring**: `AstTransformsStage` now builds the transform pipeline JIT in `run()` (moved from `new()`) so it has access to `StageContext` — extensions, runtime, and format — for the shortcode transform. Unknown shortcode names trigger on-demand loading of matching extension Lua scripts.

- **`quarto.*` Lua API** (`pampa/src/lua/quarto_api.rs`): Adds `quarto.json`, `quarto.log`, and `quarto.utils` namespaces expected by real-world extensions (e.g., lipsum). Includes `quarto.utils.resolve_path` with per-handler script directory tracking.

- **Per-format shortcode paths**: Extension metadata `shortcodes` keys under format-specific sections are now marked as `ConfigValueKind::Path` so they resolve correctly relative to the extension directory.

- **Smoke tests**: Three new smoke-all fixtures covering inline shortcodes, block shortcodes, and per-format shortcode dispatch.

### CI fix

- Re-enable `MetadataMergeStage` in `parse_qmd_to_ast` (was inadvertently commented out alongside `AstTransformsStage`). This restores format injection into merged metadata, fixing 4 `formatDetection.wasm.test.ts` failures.
- Remove `AstTransformsStage` from `parse_qmd_to_ast` entirely — the function intentionally returns a pre-transform AST for the React debug renderer.
- Uncomment `test:ci` in `ts-test-suite.yml` so hub-client tests actually run in CI.
- Delete stale `PreviewRouter.test.ts` (component moved to `render/` subdirectory; test was never visible in CI).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes (`test-suite.yml` — Rust nextest including smoke-all)
- [ ] CI passes (`ts-test-suite.yml` — hub-client test:ci, now enabled for the first time)
- [ ] CI passes (`hub-client-e2e.yml` — Playwright smoke-all)
- [ ] Two Playwright E2E failures for extension tests (`shortcode-extension`, `filter-extension`) returning 401 — under investigation

title: refactor(hub-client): extract useAutomergeSync hook from Editor.tsx
description:
- Extract ~120 lines of bidirectional Automerge↔Monaco sync logic from `Editor.tsx` into a dedicated `useAutomergeSync` hook
- Add comprehensive test suite covering real-time remote edits, reconciliation, echo prevention, replay gating, and edge cases
- Follow existing `usePresence`/`useReplayMode` pattern for hook structure and editor mount wiring

title: fix(hub-client): prevent characters landing at wrong positions during concurrent editing
description:
Fixes #99.

This is a different bug from the one fixed in #87. That fix stopped the sync effect from reverting edits due to stale closure data. This fix closes the async gap between Automerge receiving a remote change and Monaco being updated — during that gap, keystrokes used stale positions, causing characters to appear in the wrong order.

## Bug

When two users type concurrently, remote Automerge changes update the CRDT text immediately, but Monaco stays stale until a passive `useEffect` fires after paint. During this gap, local keystrokes generate positions relative to Monaco's stale text but `splice()` applies them to Automerge's already-updated text — characters land at wrong offsets, reversing letter order.

This happens even when users edit completely different paragraphs: any remote insertion at offset R shifts all higher offsets by the inserted length.

## Fix

Add a synchronous callback slot in `automergeSync.ts` that fires from within `onFileChanged`, before the React state update. Editor.tsx registers a callback that applies remote diffs to Monaco via `executeEdits` within the same macrotask as the WebSocket handler, so no keystroke can interleave.

Local changes hit a fast path (`model.getValue() === content` → no-op). The existing `useEffect` is kept as a fallback for initial file load and file switching.

title: fix(pampa): make is_absolute/is_relative tests cross-platform
description:
On Windows, Unix-style paths like `/home/user` are drive-relative, not absolute — `std::path::Path::is_absolute()` correctly returns `false`. The `test_is_absolute` and `test_is_relative` tests hardcoded Unix paths with Unix-only expectations, causing failures on Windows.

## Fix

Use `#[cfg]` attributes for platform-specific assertions and add Windows-style path tests (`C:\Users\user`) gated behind `#[cfg(windows)]`.

title: fix(hub-client): read live Automerge content in sync effect to prevent selection-replace race
description:
Fixes #35. Race condition where typing to replace a selection loses the first character                                                                 
                                                                            
###  Details                                                                   
                                                                            
The `useEffect` that syncs Automerge → Monaco reads `fileContents` from its closure (render-time) but `model.getValue()` from the DOM (effect-time).

Since React passive effects run asynchronously after paint, a user keystroke can update Monaco before the stale effect executes — causing it to see a mismatch and revert the editor content.

This is most visible when replacing a selection because the gap between the previous edit's effect and the next keystroke is longer (the user pauses to select), leaving the pending effect still unexecuted when the replacement keystroke fires.

### Fix

Read content live from the Automerge handle via `getFileContent()` so both sides of the comparison reflect the same point in time. `fileContents` remains in the dependency array as the trigger.

title: Cancel in-progress CI runs on new PR pushes
description:
When multiple commits are pushed to a PR in quick succession, all triggered CI runs
complete independently, wasting runner minutes on outdated commits.

Adds `concurrency` groups to `test-suite` and `ts-test-suite` workflows using the
same pattern as quarto-dev/quarto-cli. Pushes to the same PR cancel previous runs,
while pushes to `main` each run to completion (group key uses unique `run_id`).

title: fix(pampa): fix Windows path escaping in Lua test strings
description:
When running pampa Lua filter tests on Windows, backslash paths interpolated into Lua string literals cause syntax errors:

```
invalid escape sequence near '"C:\U'
```

Lua interprets `\U`, `\t`, etc. as escape sequences inside quoted strings. Eight tests in `filter_tests.rs` had no escaping at all and were failing on Windows.

## Why this is a test-only fix

Production Lua code in `filter.rs` passes all file paths through the Lua C API (`lua.globals().set()`, `lua.load().set_name()`), which pushes string values directly — backslashes are just characters, not escape sequences. This matches how pandoc handles it.

The problem only exists in test code, where `lua.load(format!(...))` constructs Lua source strings with interpolated paths. Every `lua.load(format!(...))` call in the codebase lives inside a `#[cfg(test)]` module.

## Fix

Add `quarto_util::to_forward_slashes(&Path) -> String`, matching quarto-cli's `pathWithForwardSlashes()` convention. Forward slashes are accepted by Windows APIs, making this safe for both file operations and Lua string embedding.

Replace all 27 ad-hoc path escaping instances across three test files:
- `filter_tests.rs`: 8 unescaped `order_file.display()` calls (the bug)
- `mediabag.rs`: 6 `.replace('\', "/")` chains
- `system.rs`: 13 `.replace('\', "\\\\")` chains

title: Implement cursor screen name indicators
description:
Closes #96. As we now have per-project identity -> screen name / colour mapping.

Adds name labels next to remote cursors so you can see who's editing where. Labels stay visible as long as the cursor is present.              
                                                                            
Key changes:                                                            

- Name labels rendered via CSS `::before` pseudo-elements on the existing cursor decoration                                                         
- Style management switched from per-color to per-peer, so users with the same color get independent styles and name labels update correctly    
- Injected `<style>` elements are cleaned up when peers leave or the component unmounts                                                        
- Selection highlight opacity reduced (33 → 22) for less visual noise
- Decoration rendering moved to `useLayoutEffect` to prevent flicker from stale cursor positions being painted before repositioning

title: Cleanup PR caches on close
description:
## Summary

- Add workflow to automatically delete GitHub Actions caches when a PR is closed or merged
- Rust build caches are ~700 MB each and accumulate per PR branch, with the repo currently at ~10 GB (the GitHub limit)
- Uses `gh cache list --ref refs/pull/<N>/merge` to scope deletions to only the closed PR's caches — main branch and other PR caches are never touched

## How it works

Caches created by `Swatinem/rust-cache` and `actions/cache` are scoped to the git ref that triggered the workflow. For PRs, that ref is `refs/pull/<N>/merge`. The cleanup workflow lists caches under that ref and deletes them by ID, logging sizes and results.

Adapted from quarto-dev/quarto-cli's equivalent workflow.

title: Drop .sh filter dispatch on Windows
description:
Follow-up to #89. The bash dispatch for `.sh` filters doesn't work on Windows because
path translation varies across bash variants — WSL uses `/mnt/c/`, Git Bash uses `/c/`,
Cygwin uses `/cygdrive/c/`. Rather than detecting and handling each variant, drop `.sh`
dispatch on Windows entirely since it's not a realistic user scenario.

- Remove `find_bash()` and the `.sh`/`.bash` match arm from `build_filter_command`
- Convert `test_invalid_utf8_filter` to use a Python script (cross-platform)
- Add `test_invalid_utf8_filter_sh` with `#[cfg(unix)]` for Unix coverage

title: fix(hub-client): replace `updateText` with positional splice for CRDT sync
description:
Fixes #74 - a race condition where edits from other users could be silently deleted during collaborative editing.

### Problem

When you type in the editor, the app sends your full document text to the sync engine, which diffs it against its own copy to figure out what changed. But if a collaborator's edit arrives between reading the editor and running that diff, the diff sees their new text as "not in the editor" and deletes it.

### Fix

Instead of sending the full document and diffing, we now send the exact edit operations — "insert 'x' at position 5" or "delete 3 characters at position 10". The sync engine applies these directly as positional splices. Since it never diffs against the full document, there's no window where a collaborator's edit can be misinterpreted as something to delete. Automerge's CRDT is designed to merge concurrent positional edits correctly.

This also improves how the preview panel writes content back to the editor (e.g., when you reorder slides by dragging). Previously this used the same racy full-document path. Now it routes through the editor as a normal edit, which also means `Ctrl+Z` undoes it.


| | **Before (`updateText`)** | **After (`splice`)** |
|---|---|---|
| **What's sent** | The entire file content | Only the characters that changed |
| **What Automerge does** | Diffs old vs new full text to find changes | Applies the insert/delete directly at the given position |
| **Concurrent edit scenario** | User B sends their full text, which doesn't contain A's edit → Automerge interprets the missing edit as a deletion → A's work is removed | User B sends "insert at offset 500" → says nothing about A's edit at offset 5 → both edits merge cleanly |
| **Root cause** | "I don't have your change" is indistinguishable from "I deleted your change" | Each edit is scoped to exactly what it touched |

### Unchanged

Replay mode still uses the old full-document path, which is fine — it doesn't involve concurrent editing.

### Tests

1. applyEditorOperations.test.ts (unit tests, mocked Automerge)

2. concurrent-editing.test.ts (e2e, real hub server):
- stale content destroys remote edit — demonstrates the bug: `updateFileContent` with stale text causes Automerge's diff to delete the remote peer's edit
- propagates to a second client — verifies a splice edit from client A arrives at client B with correct content                                                                       
- concurrent edits preserve all text — both clients splice simultaneously at different offsets; verifies both edits survive and documents converge                                
- stale offset preserves remote edit — client B splices using a pre-remote-edit offset; the character lands in the wrong spot, but crucially no text is destroyed (unlike `updateFileContent`)       
- batch splice propagates — a 3-change find-replace batch from client A arrives correctly at client B

title: Improve wasm-bindgen-cli setup: version pinning and clear error messages
description:
## Summary

- `build-wasm.js` now checks the installed `wasm-bindgen-cli` version against the version locked in `Cargo.lock` **before** the build starts, and exits with a clear, actionable error if they don't match — no more cryptic mid-build "schema version must exactly match" failures
- `cargo dev-setup` now installs `wasm-bindgen-cli@0.2.108` (pinned) instead of `wasm-pack`, and version-checks any existing installation, reinstalling if the version is wrong
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` updated: documents `wasm-bindgen-cli` requirement, explains version pinning, and adds the macOS Homebrew LLVM prerequisite that was missing entirely

## Background

The Lua WASM work (527169ed) replaced `wasm-pack` with `cargo build + wasm-bindgen CLI` because `wasm-pack` doesn't support `-Zbuild-std`, which is required for Lua's `panic=unwind` error handling. The developer tooling (docs, `cargo dev-setup`) wasn't updated at the same time.

The result: contributors with a previously-installed `wasm-bindgen-cli` at a different version (e.g. from another project) hit a confusing error mid-build. CI is unaffected — it always installs the pinned version fresh.

## Error message (before vs after)

**Before** — failure deep in the build with no guidance:
```
error: it looks like the Rust project used to create this Wasm file was linked against
version of wasm-bindgen that uses a different bindgen format than this binary:
  rust Wasm file schema version: 0.2.108
     this binary schema version: 0.2.115
```

**After** — caught before the build starts:
```
Error: wasm-bindgen version mismatch.
  installed: wasm-bindgen 0.2.115
  required:  wasm-bindgen 0.2.108  (from Cargo.lock)

The CLI version must exactly match the wasm-bindgen crate version.
Fix with:
  cargo install -f wasm-bindgen-cli --version 0.2.108
Or run: cargo dev-setup
```

## Notes

The pinned version (`0.2.108`) now appears in two places: `dev_setup.rs` and `ts-test-suite.yml`. When bumping the version, both need updating.

title: Fix json_filter script invocation on Windows
description:
`Command::new("filter.py")` fails on Windows with OS error 193 (not a valid Win32 application) because Windows has no shebang support for script files.

## Fix

Add `build_filter_command()` using a Pandoc-style exists-then-dispatch pattern:

- If the filter file exists on disk and we're on Windows, dispatch by file extension: `.py` files go through the discovered Python interpreter, `.sh`/`.bash` files go through `bash` (if available)
- If the file doesn't exist on disk, treat it as a bare command name for PATH resolution (e.g., `pandoc-crossref`)
- On Unix, pass through to `Command::new` — shebangs handle everything

`find_python()` probes interpreter candidates with `OnceLock` caching, checking `.bat`/`.cmd` variants for pyenv-win compatibility. Python 3 variants are probed before Python 2 to avoid selecting a legacy interpreter. The Microsoft Store `python3` stub (exit code 9009) is correctly rejected via `status.success()`.

`find_bash()` similarly caches bash availability, so `.sh` dispatch degrades gracefully on Windows machines without Git Bash.

title: Remove v8 Windows test exclusions and fix workspace build
description:
The v8 crate now produces rlib on Windows, so all 12 previously-excluded
crates compile tests successfully.

## Changes

- Remove `WINDOWS_EXCLUDED_CRATES` list and platform-conditional logic from `cargo xtask test`
- Move `pampa-fuzz` from workspace `members` to `exclude` — `libfuzzer-sys` requires nightly Rust and only supports Linux/macOS, so it cannot compile as part of `cargo build --workspace` on Windows. The fuzz target remains usable via `cargo fuzz run` from the pampa crate directory.
- Update `windows-dev.md` to reflect that v8 exclusions are no longer needed

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --workspace` succeeds on Windows (previously failed on `pampa-fuzz`)
- [x] `cargo xtask test` runs all workspace crates without manual exclusions
- [ ] CI passes on Linux/macOS (no regression from `pampa-fuzz` exclusion)

title: Fix: initialize IndexedDB with upgrade callback regardless of call order
description:
Fixes #82.

`userSettings.ts` opened the database without the upgrade callback that creates the stores. If it ran before projectStorage.ts (which it does on page load), the database was created empty and the stores were never created.                                                                  
                                                                            
This PR creates a single shared `getDb()` in the storage module, used by both services.

title: Fix: prevent remote edits from being silently deleted on concurrent updates
description:
Fixes #74.

When two people edit the same file at the same time, the second person's changes could get silently thrown away.                   

What was happening: When you type in the editor, two things happen: (1) your edit gets merged into the shared document via Automerge, and (2) the app updates its local copy of the file content. The problem was that step 2 was overwriting the local copy with just your text — ignoring any changes the other person made in the meantime. The next time you typed, the app would compare against that stale copy and effectively erase the other person's work.

We removed the redundant local state update in App.tsx and the redundant callback in the sync client. Both were unnecessary because the Automerge change handler already pushes the correctly-merged document state back to the app. Now there's only one source of truth for file content — the merged Automerge document — so remote edits can't get lost.

title: Fix Windows compilation: cfg-gate unix permissions in json_filter tests
description:
`pampa/src/json_filter.rs` uses `std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt` and `set_mode()` unconditionally, preventing test compilation on Windows.

## Fix

Extract a `make_executable()` helper with `#[cfg(unix)]` and `#[cfg(not(unix))]` variants. On Windows, Python scripts don't need execute permission — they're invoked via the interpreter.

Also adds `.claude/rules/cross-platform.md` to catch this pattern going forward.

title: Fix: use HMAC actor ID from first change in project creation
description:
This addresses issue 2 in #65. We will still want to upstream the simple solution, but we're able to work around in the meantime.

## Issue

Project creator's session used random Automerge actor IDs because our HMAC actor ID (derived from the `indexDocId`) was only available after document creation — a chicken-and-egg problem.

## Fix

Fix by pre-generating the documentId, resolving the HMAC actor, then creating documents via `Automerge.from()` + `repo.import()` so every change uses the correct actor from the start.

Also removes the `actorId` React state from App — `ReplayDrawer` now reads it directly from the sync client via `getActorId()`, avoiding unnecessary re-renders.

title: Per-project actor IDs via HMAC-SHA256
description:
Closes #75.

fyi @cscheid this is the follow up to #71 as we discussed on Friday.

Previously, every user had a single actor ID across all projects (SHA-256 of their OIDC `sub` claim). This meant anyone who could observe Automerge sync traffic across several projects could trivially correlate activity to the same user.

This PR makes actor IDs project-scoped.

### How it works

Actor IDs are derived by signing the combination of the user's identity and the project ID with a server-held secret. This means the same user gets a different actor ID in each project, so activity cannot be correlated across projects. Within a single project, the ID is stable across sessions and devices.

### Server changes

A new `/auth/actor?project=<id>` endpoint returns the actor ID for the authenticated user scoped to a specific project. The HMAC key is a 32-byte secret stored in `hub.json`, auto-generated on first startup. It can be overridden via the `QUARTO_HUB_SERVER_SECRET` environment variable for container deployments. The `hub.json` file is written with restricted permissions (`0o600`) so other system users cannot read it.

`/auth/me` no longer returns an actor ID, since the ID depends on which project is being accessed.

### Client changes

The actor ID is no longer fetched at login. Instead, it is fetched from the server just before connecting to a project, since the ID depends on which project is being opened. If the session has expired at that point, the user is sent to the login screen immediately.

title: Fix beads git tracking after bd to br migration
description:
This repo was originally set up with steveyegge/beads (`bd`), which auto-manages `.beads/.gitignore` at runtime — `bd init` creates it, `bd doctor --fix` regenerates it, and since `bd` rewrites it on the fly, the root `.gitignore` excludes it from tracking (line 17: `.beads/.gitignore`).

After switching to Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust (`br`), this breaks: `br` writes `.beads/.gitignore` once during `br init` and never touches it again. There is no `br doctor` that auto-repairs it. With the root `.gitignore` still blocking it, the file is invisible to git and the patterns inside (like `.br_history/`) have no effect.

The result is that local-only artifacts get committed on every `git add .beads/`: `.br_history/` snapshots (~545KB full copies of `issues.jsonl` after every mutation), the SQLite database, temp files, and migration artifacts.

## Changes

1. Add `.beads/.gitignore` matching `br init` defaults. Ignores `*.db`, `.br_history/`, lock files, merge artifacts, and other local-only files.

2. Replace `bd`-era beads rules in root `.gitignore` with a one-line comment pointing to `.beads/.gitignore`.

3. Untrack files that should be local-only: `.br_history/`, `last-touched`, `.local_version`, `deletions.jsonl.migrated`.

4. Comment out `sync-branch: "beads-sync"` in `config.yaml` — a `bd` feature not used by `br`.

5. Add 5 beads issues for known Windows test failures discovered during #72 (CRLF in quarto-doctemplate, file-locking in quarto-hub, CSL manifest, pampa test skips, pampa Windows ports).

After this change, only portable files remain tracked: `issues.jsonl`, `config.yaml`, `metadata.json`, `README.md`, `.gitignore`.

title: Actor identity mapping: resolve screen names in replay
description:
Closes #64.

Store `actorId` → `screenName` and `color` in the `IndexDocument` so replay shows human-readable names with colored badges instead of truncated hex hashes.

- Add an identities map and schemaVersion field to IndexDocument in `quarto-automerge-schema`, with V0 → V1 migration
- Write each user's identity (screen name + color) on connect via `quarto-sync-client`; use `auth.name` as the default screen name
- Resolve actor IDs to screen names in `ReplayDrawer` with colored badges (blue for current user, grey for others); falls back to truncated hex when no identity is available
- Set color along with screen name so identity changes propagate consistently                                                              
- Add Reset and Randomize buttons in the screen name UI, with live sync to the replay view                                                          
- Backwards compatible: older clients ignore the new fields; newer clients transparently migrate V0 documents

title: Add Windows development support and contributor onboarding
description:
Windows builds and tests require specific tooling and workarounds that were undocumented. New contributors had no setup path, and the 12 crates depending on v8 (which lacks rlib on Windows) caused test compilation failures with no clear workaround.

## Changes

1. Add `CONTRIBUTING.md` with setup instructions covering Rust toolchain, Pandoc 3.6+ requirement, and editor configuration.

2. Add `cargo xtask dev-setup` to install nextest and wasm-pack, with binstall detection and cargo-install fallback. Checks Pandoc version and warns (does not fail) if absent.

3. Add `cargo xtask test` for platform-aware test execution. On Windows, automatically excludes the 12 crates affected by v8 rlib unavailability. On other platforms, runs the full workspace.

4. Add `rust-toolchain.toml`, `.vscode/extensions.json`, and `.config/nextest.toml` for consistent contributor environments.

5. Add `default-members` to root `Cargo.toml` to exclude `pampa-fuzz` (libfuzzer-sys is Linux/macOS only).

6. Document known Windows test failures in `claude-notes/instructions/windows-dev.md`: 8 CRLF failures in `quarto-doctemplate`, 2 file-locking failures in `quarto-hub`, and the v8 exclusion list.

## Known Windows test failures (not addressed)

All pre-existing, documented for follow-up:

- 8 CRLF in `quarto-doctemplate` — template files checked out as CRLF, tests compare against LF
- 2 file-locking in `quarto-hub` — Windows mandatory locking vs Unix advisory
- 12 crates excluded from compilation due to v8 rlib unavailability

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo xtask dev-setup` installs tools on Windows
- [x] `cargo xtask test` runs 2093 tests, skipping v8-dependent crates (2082 pass, 11 known failures)
- [x] `cargo build --workspace` succeeds with pampa-fuzz excluded via default-members
- [x] Full suite passes on WSL (6665/6665)

title: Replay performance: incremental editor updates during playback
description:
Every replay frame was calling `model.setValue()`, which re-tokenizes and re-layouts the entire document even for single-line changes.

Now we use `applyEdits` with a minimal diff for single-step changes (playback ticks, manual stepping), and only fall back to `setValue` for large jumps like slider scrubs or initial entry (as this can be more efficient for large changes).

Also skips all work entirely when content hasn't changed between frames.

title: Fix crash when slide index exceeds available slides after deletion
description:
Fixes #58. Clamps the slide index to the valid range before rendering.

When a large deletion shrinks the document, the AST may produce fewer slides than before, but `currentSlide` still holds the old index. Accessing `slides[currentSlide]` out of bounds returns `undefined` and crashes the page.

The fix uses `Math.min(currentSlide, slides.length - 1)` to fall back to the last available slide.

I came across this while developing another feature I'm working on. This should fix at least one cause of #58, there could always be others. fyi @vezwork

title: Fix: `format: html` documents incorrectly showing slides view
description:
`getQ2Format()` in `PreviewRouter.tsx` was extracting the raw format string from AST metadata and returning it for any format, including "html". Since "html" is truthy, it routed HTML documents to `ReactPreview` → `ReactRenderer`, which treats any non-q2-debug format as slides.

Fixed by filtering `getQ2Format()` to only return formats starting with "q2-". All other formats (including html) now correctly fall through to the normal Preview component.

title: Replay: UI improvements
description:
Improve replay drawer UI:

Replay mode banner:

title: Implement persistent identity
description:
Closes #47.

When authentication is enabled, document changes are now attributed to the user who made them. Previously, every browser session generated a random anonymous identity, making it impossible to tell who edited what in the document history.

This means:

- Consistent attribution: The same person always shows up as the same author, regardless of which device or browser they use
- Replay recognition: In replay mode, your own changes are labeled "Me" instead of an opaque identifier, making it immediately clear which edits are yours vs. others
- Privacy by design: The identity stored in document history is a one-way hash - it can't be reversed to reveal email addresses or other personal information
- No-auth fallback: When authentication is disabled, everything works exactly as before with anonymous random identities

Deferred

- Display names in replay: A future addition will map identities back to human-readable names and emails, so other collaborators show as "Alice" rather than a short hex code. The design for where to store this mapping (client-side, server-side, or hybrid) is still open.

title: Scroll sync editor and preview in replay mode
description:
Closes #54. During preview, playback or scrubbing to a point in history now scrolls both editor and preview panes to the point where changes are being made.

This works reasonably well now. Especially after #61, there is no longer any flickering to the loading page during fast playback. Notably ratio-based sync provides more robust behaviour for replay versus the normal `scrollToLine` approach.

title: Fix preview unmount/remount cycle on every keystroke
description:
Fixes #57. (I _think_ I was also encountering this when working on #54).

PreviewRouter was setting `isChecking=true` on every content change, which unmounted the Preview component while `parseQmdToAst` ran, then remounted it from scratch.

On not-small documents this created a feedback loop where fast typing kept destroying and recreating the preview faster than it could render. 

Now only the initial format check (and file switches) show the loading state. Subsequent re-checks run in the background while Preview stays mounted.

--

Note: there's probably more that can be done for performance, but this is likely the main culprit.

`ts-test-suite.yml` runs on the same triggers and actively builds the WASM module, so no coverage is lost.

title: Extract replay logic into `quarto-sync-client`
description:
Closes #48.

Moves the non-React replay plumbing (Automerge history walking, doc cloning, text caching, WASM lifecycle) out of the `useReplayMode` hook into a new framework-agnostic `ReplaySession` API in `@quarto/quarto-sync-client`. The hook becomes a thin React wrapper. This lets other consumers (MCP server etc.) use replay without pulling in React.

Also defers the waveform actor-color computation to a `requestAnimationFrame` callback so the replay UI appears instantly instead of blocking on the metadata calls.

title: Replay for Quarto Hub
description:
This PR adds **replay** to Quarto Hub collaborative editor.

This allows you to explore and step through the full document history, and provides an interface to automerge-native versioning / undo.

Adds a Replay button along the bottom edge of the editor. Clicking it opens a drawer and enters Replay mode. Replay mode is a personal exploration space - it doesn't affect other collaborators. Syncs continue in the background, and exiting replay returns you to the live collaborative document.

The drawer contains playback controls to play through the document's history like a video, or scrub back and forth along the timeline. The timeline scrubber shows a visual "waveform" - coloured bars representing different authors, so you can see at a glance when different collaborators contributed.

At any point during replay, hit the Restore button to revert the document to that moment in time - this adds a new change to the document. To undo this, simply go back into replay mode, step back one frame, and click Restore again.

There are keyboard shortcuts (spacebar, arrow keys, Home/End, Escape) to navigate without clicking.

[video.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f853cf46-6d60-420d-be78-943952b8c3c8)

title: Update quarto-hub to samod 0.8+ and re-implement document access audit logging
description:
This currently depends on our [fork](https://github.com/shikokuchuo/samod/tree/q2) of samod, which implements `AccessPolicy` in line with the js reference, with the expectation that this will be upstreamed.

We always allow access, only log — `AuditAccessPolicy::should_allow()` always returns true. It's used for audit logging, not authorization. Authorization can be layered on later by returning false for denied peers.

## Summary
                                                                            
- Upgrade samod dependency to 0.8+ (3af4595), adopting the new `AcceptorHandle`, `dial_websocket`, and `AccessPolicy` APIs
- Replace the custom peer connection loop with samod's built-in `dial_websocket` dialer (automatic reconnection with exponential backoff)
- Switch inbound WebSocket handling from the old `accept_axum` → handshake_complete → finished pattern to the new event-stream pattern (`AcceptorEvent::ClientConnected` / `ClientDisconnected`)
- Implement document access audit logging via samod's upstream `AccessPolicy` trait, replacing the previous `ConnectionId`-based approach with a `PeerId`-based one

title: Fix: preserve share link hash across auth redirect
description:
Fixes #31.

Share link hash is lost during Google OAuth redirect because the server redirects back to `/` after auth, and hash fragments are never sent to the server.

## Approach

Before React mounts, `main.tsx` runs `restorePreAuthHash() || savePreAuthHash()`:

- **First visit** (share link, not authed): restore finds nothing, save captures hash to `sessionStorage`
- **Return from auth** (hash is empty): restore finds saved hash, sets it back, skips save

## Security

The `indexDocId` acts like a bearer token. Storing it in `sessionStorage` does not widen the attack surface: any XSS that can read `sessionStorage` can already read `window.location.hash` on the initial page load when the token is in the address bar. During the Google auth roundtrip, the token sits in `sessionStorage` but no JS is running on the origin (the browser has navigated away). On return, `restorePreAuthHash()` removes it from `sessionStorage` before React mounts.

title: Generic OIDC authentication for quarto-hub server
description:
Replace Google-hardcoded auth with provider-agnostic OIDC so any compliant identity provider (Auth0, Azure AD, Okta, Keycloak, etc.) can be used via CLI flags.

This means that switching to another auth provider would be a drop-in replacement for the server, and we'd only need to wire this into the front end.

## CLI changes 

```                                                                       
# Before
hub --google-client-id <ID>

# After (Google — defaults make this a drop-in rename)
hub --oidc-client-id <ID>

# After (custom provider)
hub --oidc-client-id <ID> \
  --oidc-issuer https://your-provider.com \
  --oidc-image-domains avatars.your-provider.com
```

  - `--google-client-id` / `QUARTO_HUB_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` → `--oidc-client-id` / `OIDC_CLIENT_ID`
  - New: `--oidc-issuer `/ `OIDC_ISSUER` (default: `https://accounts.google.com`)
  - New: -`-oidc-image-domains` / `OIDC_IMAGE_DOMAINS` (default: `lh3.googleusercontent.com`)

  The JWKS URL is always discovered automatically from `{issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration` — no flag needed.

## Scope

- Backend only. Frontend remains Google-specific (`@react-oauth/google`) and will be updated separately when a new provider is needed.
- Single provider. Multi-provider support is a non-goal.

title: update runtimelib and jupyter-protocol
description:
This upgrades `runtimelib` from 1.0 to 1.4 and upgrades `jupyter-protocol` from 1.0 to 1.4.

You can view the [full `jupyter-protocol` crate CHANGELOG on GitHub](https://github.com/runtimed/runtimed/blob/main/crates/jupyter-protocol/CHANGELOG.md). The main changes are improved compatibility with kernels that omit or deivate from spec required fields. There's more defensive deserialization for those cases.

On the runtimelib side, `.split()` is now supported on the Jupyter shell channel to make it so reader and writer can be owned separately. I haven't looked at your code deeply enough to see if you can make use of it. Within Zed and Deno it made the code cleaner and allowed us to drop extra tasks and channels.

On the nbformat side, it now supports v3 notebook parsing and upconversion to v4. There are also some fixes to handle both string and array for cell source (noticed with how JetBrains writes out notebooks, still valid nbformat).

title: Fix uploaded text files showing empty editor
description:
Fixes #27.

When uploading a file via "+New" > "Upload File", all files were routed through `createBinaryFile`. Text files (.qmd, .md, etc.) uploaded this way had no text content in the Automerge document, so the editor appeared empty when opening them.                                                               

We now detect text files by extension and delegate to `handleCreateTextFile`, which creates a proper text document and navigates to it.

title: (quarto-hub) implement document access logging
description: When authentication is enabled, there is currently no audit trail of which user accessed which document. The server authenticates at WebSocket upgrade time but doesn't log per-document access. This PR implements server-side logging of all documents accessed. ### samod changes - Adds a `document_served` effect to samod that fires once per (connection, document) pair — the first time sync data for a document is transmitted to a remote peer. - The detection piggybacks on existing state that already tracks whether a connection has been served, so there's zero overhead on subsequent sync round-trips and no additional bookkeeping. - Implemented at `shikokuchuo/samod@quarto`. ### quarto-hub changes - The authenticated email is captured at WebSocket connect time. - When the callback fires, it resolves the connection to an email and logs via `tracing::info!`. - Fully backwards-compatible — the callback is optional and defaults to off. - Client-side changes: none required. ### Screenshot ### To do - [x] samod fork to be moved to `quarto-dev` org.

title: Google OAuth2 authentication for Quarto Hub
description:
### Summary                                                                   
                                                                            
Adds optional Google Sign-In across the Hub server and and web client.
Auth is off by default and enabled by passing `--google-client-id <ID>` to  the hub server.

### Architecture

```
   Browser (Google Sign-In)                                                  
            │                                                            
       ID token (JWT)                                         
            │
            ▼                                                               
    ┌───────────────────────────────┐
    │       Hub Server (Axum)       │                                       
    │                               │                       
    │  ── auth boundary ──────────  │
    │                               │
    │  REST API    Automerge sync   │
    └───────────────────────────────┘
```

Auth is enforced at the transport layer (HTTP/WebSocket upgrade) before any request processing begins.
The sync protocol (samod/Automerge) is completely unaware of authentication — unauthenticated connections are rejected before they reach it. This keeps auth concerns out of the collaboration engine entirely.

#### Server (quarto-hub)

- New auth module that validates Google ID tokens locally using cached public keys (no per-request call to Google).
- All endpoints (`/health`, `/api/*`, and WebSocket sync) require a valid token when auth is enabled.
- Operators can restrict access to specific email addresses or domains via `--allowed-emails` and `--allowed-domains`.
- Env vars `QUARTO_HUB_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `QUARTO_HUB_ALLOWED_EMAILS` and `QUARTO_HUB_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` allowed in place of arguments.
- Startup check ensures TLS is accounted for before accepting tokens.

#### Web client (hub-client)

- When a Google client ID is configured, unauthenticated users see a login screen with Google's standard Sign-In
  button.
- After sign-in, the ID token is stored as an `HttpOnly` cookie, which is included by the browser as a header for all sync and API connections.
- Token expiry is monitored automatically; silent refresh renews the session without interrupting the user when possible.
- Sign-out button with Google avatar shown in the ProjectSelector header.

title: metadata: apply _metadata.yml in the project root
description:
A `_metadata.yml` next to `_quarto.yml` now applies, and so does one beside a document rendered outside any project:

- The project root's `_metadata.yml` applies to every document in the project, between `_quarto.yml` and any deeper `_metadata.yml`. Quarto 1 applies it only to documents directly in the root; that looks accidental, so q2 treats the root like any other directory, and the new directory-metadata docs page lists the difference.
- A lone document gets the `_metadata.yml` in its own directory and none above it, as in Quarto 1.

## Validation

1. In an empty directory, create `_quarto.yml` with `project: {type: default}`, `_metadata.yml` with `toc: true`, and `doc.qmd` containing a `## Section` heading and some text. Copy `doc.qmd` to `sub/doc.qmd`.
2. Run `q2 render`. Both `doc.html` and `sub/doc.html` have a `<nav id="TOC">`.
3. Add `format: {html: {theme: [t.scss]}}` to `_metadata.yml` and create `t.scss` with `/*-- scss:defaults --*/` and `$body-bg: #abcdef;`. Re-render: both pages have the `#abcdef` background, so `sub/doc.qmd` resolves `t.scss` against the root.
4. Delete `_quarto.yml` and run `q2 render doc.qmd`: `doc.html` still has a TOC. Run `q2 render sub/doc.qmd`: `sub/doc.html` has no TOC, because the parent's `_metadata.yml` doesn't apply outside a project.

title: Port lightbox (GLightbox image galleries) from Quarto 1
description:
Ports Quarto 1's built-in **lightbox** (GLightbox image overlays and galleries) to Quarto 2 HTML output. Braid: bd-kcpkgftw. Plan, decisions, and verification log: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-06-lightbox-port.md`.

## What users get

- `lightbox: true` / `auto` / `{match: auto}` lightboxes every figure and every image alone in its paragraph. `.nolightbox` opts an image out. Images already inside a link are never wrapped.
- With no option set, only images with the `.lightbox` class are lightboxed. `lightbox: false` turns everything off.
- Options: `effect`, `desc-position`, `loop`, `css-class`.
- Per-image attributes: `group` (galleries), `description` (markdown), `desc-position`, `title`.
- The `#| lightbox:` cell option works with knitr, including per-plot lists.
- The lightbox title is the caption. Cross-referenced figures get "Figure 1: …".
- GLightbox and its init script ship only on pages where an image was actually wrapped.

## How it is built

- **`LightboxTransform`** (`crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/lightbox.rs`), a Rust port of Q1's `filters/layout/lightbox.lua`.
  - Runs right before `crossref-render`, so floats are still `FloatRefTarget` nodes, which is the shape q2-preview sees too.
  - Ships `js:glightbox`/`css:glightbox` as Project-scoped artifacts and Q1's init script verbatim, keeping the onload chaining (#9727) and Q1's stable option order (#11124).
- **Assets.** GLightbox 3.1.0 is vendored byte-identical to Q1's copy (`resources/js/glightbox/`, registered in `vendored.toml`).
  - Q1's `lightbox.css` relies on `--quarto-body-*` variables, which Q2 doesn't define.
  - Its five rules are ported into `_bootstrap-rules.scss` using `--bs-body-*` instead.
- **Retired extension.** A `filters: [lightbox]` entry that resolves to the retired `quarto-ext/lightbox` extension is dropped with warning **Q-16-13** (Q1 `kBuiltInExtNames`). Other `lightbox` extensions still run.
- **Preview.** The links are added in q2-preview too, for DOM parity. The preview `Link` ignores clicks on `a.lightbox`, because the preview has no GLightbox and the raw image href would navigate the iframe away.
- **hephaestus.** `hephaestus-render` re-points a lightbox link at the SVG it renders for a `.hep` image.

## Deliberate differences from Q1

All are recorded in the plan.

- An invalid option value now warns **Q-19-5** at its source location and falls back to the default. Q1 aborts the render.
- `loop` defaults to `false`, which is Q1's actual behaviour; Q1's docs say `true`.
- Per-image `desc-position` (and the other forwarded attributes) are applied. Q1 docs promise this, but its filter appears to read the image *field* rather than the attribute.
- Link attributes go into the AST already `data-`-prefixed. The rendered HTML is the same, and the preview `Link` also renders them.

## Out of scope (follow-up strands)

- revealjs: bd-nmlowtlh
- dashboards: bd-uv0biqlj
- a clickable lightbox in q2 preview: bd-3qzcdxow
- Jupyter forwarding of unknown cell options to the cell div, which `#| lightbox:` needs under Jupyter: bd-cm1mwyuq
- subfigure galleries once subfloats land (blocked on bd-plcqhfcn): bd-lnb5x22l

## Testing

- `cargo xtask verify` passes locally.
  - One earlier run hit the known flaky `join_frontend::head_peek_timeout_closes` (bd-7kp7kjdq). It passed 3/3 in isolation and on the re-run.
- New tests:
  - unit tests in `transforms/lightbox.rs` and `filter_resolve.rs`;
  - `tests/integration/lightbox_pipeline.rs`: byte-identical `site_libs` assets, a single init script, nothing shipped when unused, and the book cover staying unwrapped (Q1 #11520);
  - 15 `smoke-all/lightbox/` fixtures. Their DOM selectors key on link `href`s, so they also pass in the hub-client preview E2E; render-only structure is checked with regexes. They are ported from Q1's corpus (#8697, #7516, #7619, descriptions, cell options, legacy extension, …);
  - a `dom-parity: true` fixture (preview ↔ render DOM match);
  - preview `Link` tests.
- The phase-5 `styles.css` baseline hash was re-captured. I checked that the only delta is the five GLightbox rules.
- Browser click-through of a rendered page: the overlay opens, galleries page through, the markdown description shows on the left, and theme colours apply.
- **Windows:** I couldn't cross-check `quarto-core` from macOS, because the C build scripts fail for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`. CI's **Clippy (Windows)** job passes on this PR.

title: test: fix j7 flake from shared julia_transport.txt sentinel
description:
## Problem
`julia_engine_e2e::j7_failed_run_does_not_leak_worker` (and the ignored `pc4a_*` row) ended with a `SharedTransportSentinel` that asserted the real `~/Library/Caches/quarto/julia/julia_transport.txt` kept the same existence and mtime for the whole run (4-6 minutes under load). Other Julia processes (another session's tests, a real preview, a server idle timeout) legitimately create, rewrite, and remove that file, so j7 failed even though its own worker-leak assertion passed.

## Evidence
- Measured: j7 plus `j1_minimal_julia_render` in a separate nextest process failed with "shared transport file ... existence changed during the run (before: false, after: true)", panicking at the sentinel, after the worker-leak assertion passed. One run, one failure.
- Measured: j7 alone passed 4 of 5 runs (221-262 s each); the one failure was not captured.
- On this branch's base (main `b3a25f6b8`) the baseline j7 passed. My j1 run reused the live server and left the file untouched, so there was no disturbance. I did not synthetically touch the shared file, because other sessions use it. The failing repro above ran on an earlier integration commit whose sentinel code is identical to main's.

## Fix
- The sentinel now asserts the stable property: the shared file never names the isolated run's server pid. A missing or unparsable shared file passes.
- Three fast tests (`sentinel_tests::*`) cover absent, rewritten-by-others, and leaked.
- `engine_output_parity::parity_julia_cell_and_inline_span` also runs the Julia engine on the real HOME but was outside the `julia-shared-transport` nextest group; it is now in it.

## Not covered
- The nextest group only serializes within one invocation. Concurrent invocations still share the real server; making every j-test hermetic (own temp HOME) would be slower and is out of scope here.
- A separate report of `j1` failing with `Execution failed in julia: undefined` is not addressed and not reproduced here.

## Testing
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core --test integration -E 'test(j7_failed_run) | test(sentinel_) | test(parity_julia)'`: 5 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p quarto-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Windows cross-clippy could not run locally (wasmtime's C build script fails for the msvc target); the changed code uses no platform-specific APIs.
- Not run: workspace nextest. Test-only change.

title: Run `{r}` cells on Ark: plots render, and failed images get a located warning
description: ## Summary A `.qmd` with `{r}` cells now renders on Ark, plots included, with this front matter and no `engine:` key: ```yaml jupyter: kernel: ark claims: {r: 1} ``` The execution-records epic (#1007) already selects a Jupyter kernel by name and by language, Ark included. Two things still stood between Ark and a finished render, and one commit removes each: - **Plots.** Ark sends `image/png` as base64 without `=` padding, and kernels differ in line wrapping. The decoder rejected both, so every Ark plot was silently dropped. It now strips all ASCII whitespace and makes padding optional. One decoder (`decode_image` in `presenter/figures.rs`) serves the filesystem sink, the WASM sink and `ipynb_replay`. - **Failed images.** An image that cannot be used used to vanish, and its `[Image output]` placeholder parsed as a span and raised a location-less `Q-2-49`. The placeholder is now the literal `\[Image output\]`, and a new `Q-18-11` warning points at the cell. (The epic took `Q-18-4`, hence the new code.) The catalog entry, docs page and sidebar entry are included. A third commit documents the setup in `jupyter-kernels.qmd` ("Running R cells on Ark"), and a fourth reconciles the plan with the end-to-end record. This PR replaces #1076, which was built on `main` before the epic rewrote the Jupyter engine. title: pampa: CommonMark loose/tight lists, decided on source rows (bd-az53ojvo)
description:
Strand: bd-az53ojvo. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-06-commonmark-loose-tight-lists.md` (Results section has the numbers and the rule).

## What changed

The tree-sitter grammar does not distinguish loose from tight lists; the decision is made in `process_list` while the concrete tree becomes the AST. The old code used four signals and each was wrong somewhere: a blank line after an item ending in a sublist, code block or block quote was invisible; nothing inside a block quote or div container was ever loose; whitespace-only separator lines were missed (bd-25ezfgs8, bd-i4xrcdqx); `- a\n  # h\n  b` came out loose; only the first paragraph of a tight item became `Plain`.

**Reader.** The two clauses of the spec (Lists, spec.txt 5262-5267) are computed directly on source rows: a list is loose iff the row above some item after the first, or above some direct block child after the first within an item, is blank once the enclosing block quotes' `>` prefixes are stripped. The row above a block's first row is always the previous block's last content row, the marker row, or a blank line, so blank lines inside fenced code, block quotes and sublists never count (spec examples 320-323). In a tight list every direct `Paragraph` of every item becomes `Plain`, as pandoc's commonmark reader and comrak do.

**Writer.** A list is spelled tight unless some item directly contains a `Paragraph` (the old "every item starts with Plain" rule lost `[[BulletList ..], [Plain]]`), and a block pair the reader would merge (quote then quote; quote or sublist then paragraph) gets a blank line even in a tight item.

## Tests

`crates/pampa/tests/integration/list_looseness.rs` compares the list shape (block kinds, `Plain` vs `Para`, recursively) against comrak on:

- every CommonMark spec example whose reference AST has a list;
- an exhaustive enumeration of 18,446 list documents (markers, spacing, blank / whitespace-only / tab / indented separators between blocks and items, empty items, fenced code with inner blanks, quotes with `>` lines, headings, divs, display math, sublists, containers, tails);
- proptest samples over a larger grammar (`PROPTEST_CASES` sizes it; 5,000-case runs are clean);
- a qmd-writer round trip over the same generator.

Documents with fenced divs are checked metamorphically against a block-quote substitute. `scripts/commonmark-list-survey.py` cross-checks against pandoc 3.12: comrak and pandoc agree on all 18,446 documents.

| Class (enumerated corpus) | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| agree | 12,244 | 14,705 |
| looseness (Plain vs Para only) | 2,461 | 0 |
| other shape (block quotes merging, bd-se0yhp3o) | 3,345 | 3,345, known |
| parse error (items starting with a blank line, bd-qgswtht1) | 396 | 396, known |

Spec examples 317 and 328 now pass. Non-looseness disagreements the corpus found are filed with repros (bd-se0yhp3o, bd-9xnwn3z7, bd-qgswtht1, bd-6522kqyw) and recorded as known families; the harness fails when a family stops failing, so the entries cannot go stale.

Two pinned tests change: the bd-25ezfgs8 cells in `test_indented_continuation` now expect loose (as pandoc says) for both the whitespace-only and the blank-line variant, and the definition-list "settles into tight" test becomes a lossless round trip for both spellings.

## Rendering change

Lists in these shapes rendered tight before and render loose now, matching CommonMark, pandoc and Quarto 1: items separated by a blank line inside a block quote or fenced div; a blank line after an item whose last block is a sublist, code block or block quote; an empty item followed by a blank line; a whitespace-only separator line. One shape goes the other way: two paragraphs in one item separated by a heading, fence or quote with no blank lines is tight now.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify`: all 14 steps green.
- `cargo clippy -p pampa --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Windows cross-check (`--target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) is blocked by `aws-lc-sys` compiling C for the target from macOS. The change is byte scanning of the input with no platform-specific code; `\r` is treated as whitespace.

title: pampa: strip fence indentation and keep blank lines in fenced code bodies
description:
Fixes two reader bugs in fenced code bodies, reported from the Connect docs migration. Strand: `bd-fenced-code-list-indent-wsirymk4`. Plan and assessment: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-06-fenced-code-container-indent-blank-lines.md`.

## Bugs

1. **Fence indentation not stripped.** CommonMark and pandoc remove up to N spaces from each body line when the opening fence is indented N past its container's content column. This applies inside a list item, and at top level for 1–3 spaces. pampa removed nothing, so `1. Run:` followed by a 4-space-indented fence produced `" chmod 750 x.sh"` (50 blocks on 22 Connect pages).
2. **Blank lines dropped in fenced code inside list items.** The scanner's `LIST_ITEM` continuation token runs over blank lines. `code_fence_content.rs` discarded the whole token, including its line endings, so `"a\n\nb"` became `"a\nb"`. This also hit **executable cells** inside list items, which changed their code (5 blocks on 5 pages).

## Fix

The fix is entirely in `process_code_fence_content` (`crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/code_fence_content.rs`). The scanner is unchanged; it only gets a comment.

- Keep the line endings (`\n` or `\r\n`, as written) found inside each `block_continuation` that the function skips.
- Strip up to N columns of leading whitespace from each body line. N is the leading whitespace of the opening `fenced_code_block_delimiter` token, which is where the extra indentation lives. A tab that straddles the limit is split.
- A whitespace-only line that is indented deeper than the fence keeps its excess spaces. This follows strict CommonMark rather than pandoc, which blanks the line. We agreed on this during plan review, because those lines can be executable code.

## Tests

- 7 new `pandoc-match-corpus/markdown/fenced-code-*.qmd` cases: over-indented, top-level indented, one and two blank lines, a bullet item, a list inside a blockquote, and over-indentation combined with a blank line. With the fix reverted, the corpus test fails on them.
- Unit tests for line stripping, including CRLF and tabs, and for line-ending extraction.
- A qmd → JSON → qmd round-trip fixture.
- `quarto-core` `body_source_for`: a one-line body under an indented fence is still located exactly. A multi-line body falls back to the whole block's span; it is no longer a contiguous substring of the source. The real fix for that is `bd-lm75ion7`.
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passes locally, after rebuilding the hub-client WASM.

title: Support CommonMark angle-bracket link destinations: [x](<a b.png>)
description:
## Summary

CommonMark (and Pandoc) let a link or image target be wrapped in angle brackets so it can contain spaces:

```markdown
![](<a path with spaces.png>)
[link](<foo bar.html> "title")
```

Before this change, q2 got both forms wrong:

| Input | `main` | this PR (= pandoc 3.12.1) |
|---|---|---|
| `![](<a path with spaces.png>)` | Q-2-33 error | `"a%20path%20with%20spaces.png"` |
| `![](<nospace.png>)` | URL `"<nospace.png>"` (brackets kept) | `"nospace.png"` |
| `[x](<a\>b.html>)` | `"<a\\>b.html>"` | `"a%3Eb.html"` |

**Grammar** (`tree-sitter-qmd`). The angle form is a single token, `_angle_bracket_url`, aliased to `url`. This keeps highlight queries and other `(target (url))` consumers working. The token is tagged with the `angle_bracket_url` field, because tree-sitter renames an always-aliased token, so `grammar_name()` can't tell the two forms apart. It follows CommonMark's rules: no line ending, no unescaped `<` or `>`, and backslash escapes allowed. Because it is one token, an unclosed `[x](<foo)` still falls back to today's bare-URL parse.

**pampa.** pampa strips the brackets, resolves backslash escapes, and applies Pandoc's `escapeURI`, so the AST matches Pandoc. The URL source span covers the bracket contents.

**Diagnostics.**
- Q-2-33's message now suggests the angle form.
- New **Q-2-60** "Text after angle-bracket link destination" covers `![](<my file>.png)` and `[x](<a b> unquoted title)`. On `main` these silently produced wrong links; CommonMark and Pandoc don't treat them as links. Following `crates/pampa/AGENTS.md` ("one LR state per inline container"), there are corpus cases for every inline container, plus a reconciliation test.
- A newline inside `<…>` reports the existing Q-2-37.

**quarto-core: resource collector fix (bug that already existed on `main`).** The end-to-end check found that `ResourceCollectorTransform` did not percent-decode image URLs. A `%20` image, whether hand-written or produced by `<…>`, got a false Q-5-6 "file does not exist" warning, and in a website render it was **not copied to `_site`**. It now decodes the URL the same way `link_resource_discovery` already does. This also fixes the `q2 preview` single-file asset sync, which uses the same collector.

**Out of scope, filed separately.** bd-z4lqspcd: Q-2-33 has the same inline-container coverage gap. Other divergences in bare (non-angle) URLs are left for a separate session; see the plan.

Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-06-angle-bracket-link-destinations.md` · Strand: `bd-angle-link-dest-qkqkegqo`

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo xtask verify` passes locally (lint, clippy, fmt, build, tree-sitter corpus, nextest, hub-client WASM build + tests, claude-notes render)
- [x] New tree-sitter corpus cases in `test/corpus/link.txt`
- [x] Unit tests for `decode_angle_bracket_destination` / `escape_uri`; expected values were checked against pandoc 3.12.1
- [x] `tests/integration/test_angle_bracket_link_destination.rs`: Pandoc parity, source span, qmd round trip, Q-2-33/Q-2-37 unchanged, Q-2-60 in all 21 contexts
- [x] `resource_collector` unit test for percent-encoded image paths
- [x] Manual: `q2 render` of a website using `![](<figs/sales chart.png>)` copies the image to `_site/figs/sales chart.png` with no warnings; Typst output embeds the image
- [x] Windows: CI's `Clippy (Windows)` job passes (couldn't cross-check locally from macOS); no platform-specific code was added.

title: html: wrap code blocks in div.sourceCode for every language Quarto 1 recognizes
description:
Closes #1079.

Code blocks in a language that Pandoc's highlighter knows now get the `div.sourceCode > pre.sourceCode > code.sourceCode` nesting, and with it the theme's code-block box, even when q2 has no grammar for the language. This covers `ini`, `default`, `toml`, `conf`, `markdown` and others. The rule matches Quarto 1 exactly. Blocks in other languages (`text`, `nginx`), output blocks (`cell-output*`) and blocks with no language stay a bare `<pre>`, as in Quarto 1.

## What changed

- **`crates/quarto-highlight/src/pandoc_languages.rs`** (new): `is_pandoc_known_language`, a port of skylighting's `lookupSyntax`. It checks the full name, then the short name (both case-insensitive), then the class as a file extension against each syntax's globs (case-sensitive), and handles the `csharp`/`fortran` special cases.
- **`pandoc_languages_table.rs`** (generated) and **`scripts/gen_pandoc_languages.py`**: the syntax table from skylighting-core 0.14.7, the version Pandoc 3.10 requires (Quarto 1 pins 3.10), plus Quarto 1's own syntax definitions (`k`, `q`, and replacements for `r`, `markdown`, `scss`). The script reproduces the committed file byte for byte.
- **`annotate.rs`**: a code block that has no spans but a class Pandoc knows gets an empty `data-hl-spans` list (`[]`), so no new attribute is needed. Inline code is unchanged.
- **`crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs`**: wrap a code block whenever `data-hl-spans` is present, even if empty. This also fixes grammar-language blocks that produce no captures.
- **`ts-packages/preview-renderer/.../CodeBlock.tsx`**: the same rule, for preview/render parity. This makes four production files, one more than the small-fix budget, but the change is two lines.
- Triage record: `claude-notes/issue-reports/1079/` (repro project, findings, and excerpts of the Quarto 1 and q2 output inline; the rendered pages are not committed, per `cargo xtask lint`).

Out of scope, filed as bd-hodntkwd: both writers take the *first* class as the language. So `{.cell-code .toml}` now gets the wrapper, but q2 puts `cell-code` on the `pre`/`code` where Quarto 1 puts `toml`.

title: Highlight qmd / markdown / md code blocks with q2's qmd grammar
description:
Closes #1081.

Code blocks with class `qmd`, `markdown` or `md` used to render as a plain `<pre>`. They are now highlighted with q2's own qmd grammar:

- **Markdown structure:** headings, emphasis, links, attribute specifiers, shortcodes and fences.
- **Front matter:** highlighted as YAML.
- **Code cells:** highlighted in their own language, with the `#|` options as YAML.

## How

- **The editor already did this.** `quarto-lsp-core/src/tokens.rs` had a composer that builds the highlighting in three layers: qmd structure, front matter, and code cells. That code moves into `quarto-highlight` as `qmd::qmd_spans`. The editor now consumes it, so the editor and rendered HTML share one implementation. The editor's structural corpus snapshot is unchanged.
- **No injection queries.** The composer embeds YAML and cell languages in code, so every built-in grammar query stays injection-free. `builtin_configs_have_no_injection_or_locals` still holds, with an updated comment. This covers markdown's part of bd-v9pi6ty9; a general injection engine is still needed for other host grammars, such as HTML's `<script>`.
- **Registry.** It gets a composite entry kind. `qmd` is registered with `markdown` and `md` as aliases.
- **Render class names.** The theme CSS matches exact class names, and the qmd query's names (`markup.heading.2`, `markup.strong`, and so on) have no rules. Structural captures are now mapped onto `hl-*` classes the theme already styles, such as `markup.strong` → `markup.bold` and shortcodes → `function.macro`. Two tests pin the contract: every query capture has a mapping, and every mapping has a rule in `highlight-default.scss`.

## Tests

- New unit tests for the composer and the aliases.
- Golden snapshots for `qmd` and the `markdown` alias. The shared fixture also feeds hub-client's WASM highlight test.
- A new smoke-all fixture, `highlighting/11-builtin-qmd.qmd`. I confirmed it fails when an expectation is broken.
- Existing render tests that checked text inside `markdown` display blocks against raw HTML now check the tag-stripped text, via a shared `html_text::display_text` helper: `nested_cell_mask_render` (self-documenting cells) and the shortcode opt-out tests. That text is now split across highlight spans. Checks for markup, such as the masking marker and `cell-output`, still use the raw HTML.

Local: `cargo xtask verify` passes, including the hub WASM build and hub-client tests. I did not run the Windows clippy cross-check. The change has no platform-specific code, and `tree-sitter-qmd` compiles C, which may not cross-check from macOS.

Triage record: `claude-notes/issue-reports/1081/triage.md`. Braid: bd-wf4swupu (and the markdown part of bd-v9pi6ty9).

Overview

Overview

title: citeproc: list unsorted-style bibliographies by citation number (bd-mumobar8)
description:
Follow-up to #1116 (issue #1109).

## Problem

For a CSL style with no bibliography `<sort>` (IEEE, for example), q2 listed bibliography entries in the order the references were loaded, which is bibliography-file order. A document citing `[@second]` and then `[@cited]` rendered `[2] Smith` before `[1] Adams`. Pandoc, and so Quarto 1, lists them by citation number.

## Change

`crates/quarto-citeproc/src/types.rs`:

- **No-sort order:** the no-sort branch of `generate_bibliography_to_outputs` orders entries by initial citation number, which is first-cited order. References that never got a number come after the numbered ones, in insertion order (a stable sort). pampa numbers uncited `nocite` references in load order (#1116), so they come after the cited entries in load order. That matches what Pandoc 3.12.1 does, regardless of the order `nocite` names them in.
- **Merged generators:** `generate_bibliography` (string output) now renders the entries from `generate_bibliography_to_outputs` instead of repeating the sort and renumber logic. Side effect: the string API now applies `subsequent-author-substitute`, which only the Output API applied before. Only tests call the string API.

**CSL conformance:** the harness cites every input item in input order unless a test supplies its own citations. I checked the 15 bibliography-mode tests that supply citations and whose style has no `<sort>`; all of them cite in input order. So no conformance test can tell the old order from the new one, and the enabled set still passes, including the 7 tests #1118 enabled.

## Testing

- New tests that failed before the fix:
  - `quarto-citeproc` (`tests/integration/bibliography_order.rs`): citation order; the unnumbered-reference fallback; the string API matches the Output API; the string API applies `subsequent-author-substitute`.
  - pampa `citeproc_filter`: cited entries in citation order; `nocite` entries in load order.
- After merging current `main`: `quarto-citeproc` and `pampa` pass 6,293/6,293; `quarto-core` and `quarto` pass 8,693/8,693. That excludes `capture_classifies_pieces`, which fails locally with R 4.6 (unrelated; filed as bd-54odm3rz; CI skips it because CI has no R). Clippy is clean for both crates. No snapshot files changed.
- End to end: I ran `q2 render` on the four fixtures in `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-07-citeproc-unsorted-bibliography-order-investigation/` and inspected the output. Entries, numbers, and order match `pandoc --citeproc` (saved as `pandoc-3.12.1-expected.txt` next to `q2-after-fix.txt`), apart from punctuation inside quotes (`work”,` against Pandoc's `work,”`). That difference is tracked as bd-citeproc-cluster-collapse-kns8uggw.

Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-07-citeproc-unsorted-bibliography-order.md`.
