title: Make sidebar section toggles keyboard-operable buttons (Q1 #14826 parity)
description:
Strand: bd-3bg8h1rx · Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-07-sidebar-section-toggle-buttons.md`

## Problem

q2 renders sidebar section toggles as `<a>` elements with no `href` and with `role="navigation"`:

```html
<a aria-expanded="true" aria-label="Toggle section" class="sidebar-item-toggle text-start"
   data-bs-target="#quarto-sidebar-section-0-2" data-bs-toggle="collapse" role="navigation">
```

- An `<a>` without `href` is not focusable, so keyboard users cannot expand or collapse sections.
- `role="navigation"` is a landmark role, so screen readers announce every toggle as a navigation region.
- The label doesn't name the section and isn't localized, and `aria-controls` is missing.
- The theme's button-reset rules don't exist in q2.

q2's sidebar markup was ported before Quarto 1 fixed this in quarto-cli#14826 (released in 1.11).

## Change (ports quarto-cli `a8b5b2ba6`)

- **Section with `href`**: the header stays an `<a>`, and its label becomes `<span class="menu-text" id="{id}-label">`. A separate `<button type="button" class="sidebar-item-toggle text-start">` sits beside it, with `aria-controls` and `aria-label="{toggle-section}: {plain-text title}"`. The chevron has `aria-hidden`.
- **Section without `href`**: a single `<button class="sidebar-item-text sidebar-item-toggle sidebar-link text-start">` holds both the label and the chevron, so the section is one tab stop.
- Each `<ul>` gets `aria-labelledby="{id}-label"`.
- The `toggle-section` language term is threaded through a new `SidebarRenderOptions::toggle_section_label`, the same way `search-label` already is.
- SCSS: the button reset, the flex layout for `button.sidebar-item-text`, and the chevron's `margin-left: auto`, ported from Q1's `quarto-nav.scss` into `_bootstrap-rules.scss`.
- The secondary nav's click-anywhere `a.flex-grow-1` loses `role="navigation"` and its duplicated `aria-*`. The `<button>` beside it remains the accessible control. This was part of the same Q1 commit.

q2's path-based section ids (`quarto-sidebar-section-0-2`) are kept. Q1 uses a running counter instead.

## Tests

- `quarto-navigation` unit tests cover both button forms, `aria-labelledby`, the absence of `role="navigation"` and href-less anchors, a plain-text label for a formatted title, a localized and escaped label, and the secondary-nav flex link.
- `quarto-sass`: a compiled-CSS test for the reset and layout rules.
- `quarto-core` pipeline test: a website with `lang: pt` renders `aria-label="Alternar seção: Grupos"` through the real language path.
- A smoke-all fixture `navigation/sidebar-disclosure/`, ported from Q1's fixture of the same name. It uses `render-project: true`, because a per-file render marks no page active.
- The Phase 5 `styles.css` baseline hash was re-captured. I checked that the SCSS hunk is the only delta: removing it reproduces the old hash.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build`: all Rust tests pass except two:
  - `knitr::capture_tests::capture_classifies_pieces`, caused by the local R install (`rlang_error` vs `simpleError`).
  - `quarto-preview` `head_peek_timeout_closes`, a timing test that passes on rerun.

  Hub-client suites pass after a WASM rebuild.
- Browser check on the rendered fixture:
  - Appearance is unchanged; the chevrons stay at the right edge.
  - Tab reaches the "Group" button, and Enter toggles it (`aria-expanded` flips, the list shows).
  - The accessibility tree shows `button "Toggle section: Linked" expandable expanded`, with no per-toggle landmarks.
- **Windows:** the `--target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` clippy cross-check can't run from macOS because `aws-lc-sys` compiles C for the target. The change adds no platform-specific code.

## Follow-ups (filed)

Other Quarto 1.11 accessibility changes that q2 lacks: bd-erecx4j8 (nav landmark labels, #14813), bd-kwgtllvn (navbar dark toggle as `role="switch"`, #14739), bd-59go2q2g (navbar search tab order, #14754), and bd-4iuoquu8 (unified focus ring, #15163).

title: Sidebar: rotate the chevron of expanded sections (bd-rl7r38pw)
description:
Fixes the sidebar disclosure chevron: expanded sections (`aria-expanded="true"`) showed the same right-pointing chevron as collapsed ones, so readers couldn't tell open sections from closed ones. Strand: bd-rl7r38pw. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-07-sidebar-chevron-rotation.md`.

## Cause

The markup was already correct. `render_html.rs` emits `a.sidebar-item-toggle[aria-expanded] > i.bi-chevron-right`, and Bootstrap's collapse plugin updates `aria-expanded` when a section is toggled. The fault was in the CSS port: the sidebar block of `_bootstrap-rules.scss` was ported from Q1's `quarto-nav.scss` but left out its chevron rules.

## Change

- `resources/scss/bootstrap/_bootstrap-rules.scss`: ports Q1 `quarto-nav.scss:412-432` (toggle icon size, a 200ms `transform` transition, `[aria-expanded=false]` → `none`, `[aria-expanded=true]` → `rotate(90deg)`) and `756-762` (chevron sizing inside `.sidebar-section`).
- Out of scope: Q1's `<button>` reset rules, because q2 still emits `<a>` toggles, and Q1's secondary-nav chevron rotation, because q2's secondary-nav toggle icon isn't a chevron.

## Tests

- New `quarto-sass` test `test_sidebar_toggle_chevron_rotates_when_expanded` checks the compiled default CSS. It failed before the fix and passes after.

I checked that the six new rules are the only change: stripping them from the new CSS reproduces the base hash exactly (`187803ae…`, after merging main, which had re-captured it for the GLightbox port). The `doc.html` hash is unchanged.
- Local `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` / workspace nextest: the only other failures come from this machine. Local pandoc is 3.13, outside the oracle range of 3.6–3.12 and not the pinned 3.12.1 that the recordings and docx-import fixtures need. Local R/cairo is also broken (dashboard goldens, smoke-all typst margin tests). CI pins those tools.

## End-to-end check

I rendered a 3-page website (`collapse-level: 1`, two sections) with `cargo run --bin q2 -- render` and inspected the output:

- `a.html`: the open section's toggle has `aria-expanded="true"`; the other has `"false"` plus `collapsed`.
- The compiled theme CSS contains `.sidebar-item .sidebar-item-toggle[aria-expanded=true] .bi-chevron-right::before{transform:rotate(90deg)}`.

title: citeproc: use the document lang for the citation locale (#1110)
description:
Fixes #1110.

## Problem

The document `lang` was read into the citeproc config but never passed to `quarto-citeproc`. Citations always used the CSL `default-locale`, or en-US. With `lang: nl`, q2 rendered `Smith, Jane. 2020. “A Page”. July 12.`

## Target behavior

Quarto 1 hands citations to Pandoc, so Pandoc's citeproc is the reference. I probed Pandoc 3.12.1 directly; the script and its output are in `claude-notes/issue-reports/1110/`. Pandoc's rules:

- `lang` > CSL `default-locale` > en-US. `lang` overrides the style's locale.
- A bare code uses its CSL primary dialect (`nl` → `nl-NL`, `pt` → `pt-PT`). An unknown language falls back to en-US.
- The locale also sets the **quote marks** (`‘A page’` in Dutch, `„A page“` in German), written as text, not as a `Quoted` node.
- Title case applies only to English. A reference with no `language` field takes the document's language.

| `lang` | Pandoc / Quarto 1 | q2 before | q2 after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nl` | `Smith, Jane. 2020. ‘A page’. juli 12.` | `… “A Page”. July 12.` | `… ‘A page’. juli 12.` |
| `de` | `Smith, Jane. 2020. „A page“. Juli 12.` | `… “A Page”. July 12.` | `… „A page“. Juli 12.` |
| `nl` + `default-locale="de-DE"` style | `A page en 12 juli 2020` | `A page und 12th Juli 2020` | `A page en 12 juli 2020` |

## Changes

- **quarto-citeproc**
  - `Processor::with_lang(style, lang)` computes the effective locale. `Processor::new` is unchanged and still uses the style's locale.
  - `normalize_lang` accepts `nl`, `NL`, `nl_NL` and `nl-nl`.
  - A CSL primary-dialect table replaces "first file whose name starts with the code", which had sent `pt` to `pt-BR` and `en` to `en-GB`.
  - A locale with no bundled file loads en-US instead of returning no terms at all.
  - The style's own `<locale>` blocks now apply only when their `xml:lang` matches the effective locale (exact, then base language, then unscoped), for terms, date formats, quote terms and locale options. Before, every block applied: a style's `<locale xml:lang="en">` terms would have leaked into a Dutch document.
  - The title-case check falls back to the loaded locale when a reference has no `language`.
  - `get_quote_config` now honors quote terms the style overrides.
- **pampa**
  - The citeproc filter passes `lang`.
  - Citeproc `Quoted` nodes become `Span [Str open, …, Str close]` with the locale's marks, matching Pandoc's AST.
  - Bibliography entries keep their existing unmerged `Str` chunks.
- **quarto-core**: the book-wide bibliography merge passes the references chapter's `lang`.
- **docs**: a "Citations and Bibliographies" subsection in the Document Language guide.

## Visible changes outside non-English documents

- Typst bibliography titles now use literal curly quotes (`“…”`) where the writer used to print straight `"…"`. Pandoc's Typst output does the same. `book_refactor_guard/typst-smoke-orange-book.txt` was re-recorded; its diff is quote characters only.
- HTML wraps quoted titles in a bare `<span>`, as Pandoc does.

## Tests

- **quarto-citeproc**
  - Unit tests for precedence, spellings, primary dialects, the unknown-language fallback, `xml:lang` scoping of style locales, and reference-language title case. Expected strings come from Pandoc.
  - Three CSL conformance tests now pass and are enabled (`locale_NonExistentLocaleDef`, `locale_OverloadWithEmptyString`, `locale_TitleCaseEmptyLangNonEnglishLocale`). All 759 enabled tests pass.
- **pampa**: a nested-quote localization test.
- **quarto-core**: a book-merge `lang` test, which fails without the fix.
- **smoke-all**: `citations/lang-nl-citation-locale.qmd` (the issue's repro) and `citations/lang-overrides-csl-default-locale.qmd`. Both fail with the fix reverted.

## Local verification

- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build`: all 18,761 Rust tests pass, plus clippy and fmt.
- Verify then stopped at the ts-packages build, because this worktree has no `node_modules`. No TypeScript changed. CI's hub-client WASM smoke tests will be the first run of the new fixtures under WASM.
- Full `q2 render docs` succeeds (416 of 416 pages), with no warnings from the edited page.
- Windows: `cargo clippy -p quarto-citeproc --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -- -D warnings` passes. pampa and quarto-core can't be cross-checked from macOS, because `wasmtime`'s build script compiles C. Their changes use no platform-specific APIs.

## Not in this PR (filed separately)

- en-US punctuation-in-quote (`“A Page”.` vs Pandoc's `“A Page.”`): `bd-citeproc-cluster-collapse-kns8uggw` (existing).
- English ordinal day suffix under non-English locales (`12th Juli`): `bd-mn9jphx3`.
- Typst can't compile citations to front-matter `references:` (also broken on main): `bd-yjf99rzx`.

title: Render editorial marks as Typst annotations (#1102)
description:
Fixes #1102.

## Problem

In `format: typst` output, editorial marks (`[++ ]`, `[-- ]`, `[!! ]`, `[>> ]` and their `:::` block forms) were printed as plain body text. A PDF showed deleted text and reviewer comments as if they were content, with no warning. Word and PowerPoint already had `EditorialMarksOoxmlTransform`; Typst had nothing.

## Change

- **`EditorialMarksTypstTransform`** (`crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/editorial_marks_typst.rs`). A Finalization transform in bucket B3 that only acts on `typst`, registered right after its OOXML sibling. It rewrites each mark into a raw Typst call:
  - inline: `#quarto-insert(author: "…", date: "…")[…];`
  - block: `#quarto-insert-block(…)[` … `]`

  The trailing `;` ends the embedded expression. Without it, text that begins with `(` or `[` right after a mark is parsed as more call arguments, and Pandoc can't escape it after a raw `]`. Marks nest naturally. `author` and `date` come from the mark's attributes, or from `--attribution` blame data through the shared `stamp_attribution` helper (moved out of the OOXML transform in the first commit).
- **Typst functions in one place.** A new q2-only partial, `resources/pandoc-filters/typst-template/editorial-marks.typ`, defines `quarto-insert`, `quarto-delete`, `quarto-highlight` and `quarto-edit-comment`, plus `-block` variants. Changing how marks look means editing only these functions. The template is vendored unmodified from quarto-cli, so the partial is pulled in by one `QUARTO2-PATCH` line at the end of `definitions.typ`. I put the include there rather than in `template.typ` so a user's custom `template:` (which replaces only `template.typ`) still gets the functions. Both are recorded in the pandoc-filters README under "Ours vs. pinned".
- **User overrides without Lua.** Redefine a function in `header-includes`, which the template splices in after the definitions:
  ````yaml
  header-includes: |
    ```{=typst}
    #let quarto-delete(author: none, date: none, body) = text(fill: gray)[(removed)]
    ```
  ````
  `include-in-header` would be the natural place, but it doesn't reach Pandoc formats yet (bd-7avt1ogu, linked as related).
- **Docs.** A "Typst and PDF output" section in `docs/guides/authoring/markdown-basics.qmd`.

Default look: insertions are underlined in green, deletions struck through in red, highlights get a solid yellow background, and comments sit in a small blue box prefixed with the author. Block forms add a colored rule down the left side.

## Tests

- 15 unit tests: every kind, inline and block, nesting, attribute passing and Typst string escaping, title metadata and custom-node slots, attribution stamping (highlights not stamped), and format gating.
- New smoke-all fixture `crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all/typst/editorial-marks.qmd` checks the emitted calls and the `(` edge case, and that the unfixed plain text is gone. It also compiles the PDF, so the functions must be defined. I broke one regex on purpose to confirm the fixture fails.
- The last commit regenerates Typst goldens. Every `.typ` now includes the new definitions, so `book_refactor_guard` was re-recorded and the six `*-typst` pandoc recordings re-captured. The docx/epub/pptx re-captures differed only by machine-specific noise (the capturing `q2` path and a file date), so they stay as they were.
- Triage record and visual fixtures: `claude-notes/issue-reports/1102/`.

## Local verification

`cargo xtask verify` passed, with these exceptions:
- `engine::knitr::capture_tests::capture_classifies_pieces` fails locally (`rlang_error` vs `simpleError`). It's an R-environment difference and also fails on `main`.
- One `quarto-hub-mcp` conformance test hit vitest's 5 s timeout during the run and passed on re-run (51/51).
- **Windows cross-check not run.** `cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` can't build `quarto-core` from macOS (`aws-lc-sys` compiles C for the target). The change uses no platform-specific APIs.

## Out of scope

- An accept/reject mode that applies or drops marks instead of showing them; that's a separate design question.
- LaTeX/`format: pdf` output.
- Blamed authors in the hub's Typst download: the hub sends attribution data only for docx. Explicit `author=` attributes still show.

title: citeproc: list only cited + nocite references in the bibliography (#1109)
description:
Fixes #1109.

## Problem

With `bibliography:` (or inline `references:`), the citeproc bibliography listed every loaded reference. Pandoc and Quarto 1 list only the references a document cites, plus those named in `nocite`; `nocite: "@*"` lists every reference. `nocite` was parsed into `CiteprocConfig` but never read.

## Change

`crates/pampa/src/citeproc_filter.rs` now filters references before they reach the `Processor`, following Pandoc's `getReferences` (`Text/Pandoc/Citeproc.hs`). A reference is kept if:

- the document cites it, in the body or anywhere in the metadata (this covers `nocite: "@a, @b"`, which parses as citations), or
- a plain-string `nocite` names it (`nocite: !str "@a, @b"`).

A `*` id in `nocite` keeps every reference. Uncited `nocite` entries are numbered after the cited ones, in load order, so numeric styles don't print them without a number.

The filter lives in pampa rather than `quarto-citeproc`: the CSL conformance suite calls `generate_bibliography_to_outputs` and expects every input item in the output.

Also in this PR:
- `test_bibliography_delimiters` asserted on an entry the document never cited. It now cites both references.
- `docs/guides/authoring/migrating-markdown.qmd` documents `nocite: !str "@*"`, because `@*` doesn't parse as a citation yet (Q-1-20; tracked as bd-ae2i9ei1). The untagged form still lists every entry, but it prints the warning.

Triage record: `claude-notes/issue-reports/1109/triage.md`. Related follow-ups, not in this PR: bd-mumobar8 (styles with no bibliography sort follow file order instead of citation order), bd-69rqex6n (Typst-native bibliography ignores `nocite`).

## Testing

- 8 new unit tests in `citeproc_filter::tests`: cited only; `nocite` citation; `nocite` `*` citation; plain-string ids; plain-string `@*`; a citation in other metadata; inline `references:` filtered the same way; numbering of `nocite` entries. Five failed before the fix. The two wildcard tests passed already, since everything was listed.

title: Fix install.ps1 under `irm | iex` (drop [ValidateSet] on -Platform)
description:
The documented Windows one-liner fails before installing anything:

```
PS> irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/quarto-dev/q2/main/install.ps1 | iex
iex : The attribute cannot be added because variable Platform with value  would no longer be valid.
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : ValidateSetFailure,Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.InvokeExpressionCommand
```

### Cause

`Invoke-Expression` doesn't run the text as a script with parameters; the `param(...)` block executes as ordinary variable declarations. The `[ValidateSet('windows_amd64', 'windows_arm64')]` on `-Platform` (added in v0.38.0) is then attached to a variable whose value is empty, which the set rejects. Minimal repro:

```powershell
$s = "param([ValidateSet('a','b')][string]`$Platform)`n'ok'"
Invoke-Expression $s                 # ValidateSetFailure
& ([scriptblock]::Create($s))        # ok
```

CI didn't catch it because the nightly install smoke uses the scriptblock form (`& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm …))) -Nightly`), which binds parameters normally.

### Changes

- `install.ps1`: drop the `[ValidateSet]` and validate `-Platform` by hand after `Die` is defined, with the same accepted values and a clear error.
- `nightly.yml`: add an install-smoke step (Windows PowerShell 5.1) that runs the literal `irm … | iex` one-liner. It installs the latest stable release to the default `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin` and checks that `q2.exe --version` runs.

### Verification (Windows 11, Windows PowerShell 5.1)

- `Get-Content -Raw install.ps1 | Invoke-Expression` (with `USERPROFILE` pointed at a scratch dir): installs v0.42.0, checksum verified, `q2 (quarto 2) 0.42.0`.
- `-Platform bogus` via the scriptblock form: `q2 install: unknown -Platform 'bogus' (expected windows_amd64 or windows_arm64)`.
- `-Platform windows_amd64 -Dest <dir>` via the scriptblock form: installs normally.

Until this lands, the workaround is `& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/quarto-dev/q2/main/install.ps1)))`.

title: Publish stable releases to a Homebrew tap
description:
Lets macOS and Linux users install and upgrade q2 with Homebrew:

```sh
brew install quarto-dev/tap/q2
brew upgrade q2
```

Today the only way to upgrade is re-running `install.sh`, since `q2 update` isn't implemented.

## What this adds

- `scripts/homebrew-formula.sh` renders `Formula/q2.rb` from a release's `checksums.sha256`. It uses the prebuilt darwin/linux arm64 and amd64 archives the pipeline already publishes. If an archive is missing or the version isn't a bare `X.Y.Z`, it fails without printing a formula.
- Three `homebrew-*` jobs at the end of `release-pipeline.yml`, for stable releases only (nightlies, prereleases and dry runs skip them):
  - `homebrew-formula` renders the formula from the release job's verified checksums (a new `release-checksums` artifact), not from the published release.
  - `homebrew-test` runs `brew style`, `brew audit --strict --online`, `brew install` and `brew test` on `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest`. The install downloads the published archives, so it also checks that they match what the run built.
  - `homebrew-tap` pushes the formula to `quarto-dev/homebrew-tap`.
- Four tests in `crates/quarto/tests/integration/homebrew_formula.rs`. They are unix-only, like `nightly_gate.rs`.
- One runbook row for the new secret.

## Setup needed before it does anything

1. Create a public, empty `quarto-dev/homebrew-tap` repo.
2. Add a `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` secret to this repo: a fine-grained token with Contents read/write on the tap only.

Until the secret is set, the push job logs a notice and exits (the render and test jobs still run). It runs after the release job, so a tap failure can't block or undo a release.

## Design choices

- **A formula in our own tap, not homebrew-core or a cask.** homebrew-core builds from source and has notability rules. Casks get quarantined by Gatekeeper, and q2 isn't notarized. A formula that installs the prebuilt binary avoids both and covers Linux too.
- **WinGet and Scoop are left out.** Each WinGet version is a reviewed PR to `microsoft/winget-pkgs`, which is a lot of churn at the current release rate. Also, WinGet IDs are hard to change if q2 ships under another name.

## Testing

- The 4 tests fail without the script and pass with it, run under Linux (WSL). Clippy passes with `-D warnings`.
- Against the real v0.42.0 `checksums.sha256`, the script renders a formula with the right URLs and checksums, and `ruby -c` reports `Syntax OK`.
- Not tested: the job itself (it needs the tap repo and secret) and an actual `brew install`. Both should be checked after the first release once the setup is done.



## Follow-up (review by cbrnr)

All six review points are addressed in 1c440fe8c: no `version` stanza, so `brew audit --strict` passes; a caveat about Node.js 24+ for `q2 mcp`; a test block that renders a `.qmd`; brew audit/install/test in CI; checksums taken from the release job's own verified set; and the tap renamed to `quarto-dev/homebrew-tap`. Against v0.42.0 on macOS arm64, `brew style`, `brew audit --strict --online`, `brew install` and `brew test` all pass.

title: quarto-core: skip discarded preview AST capture
description:
Strand: bd-wpmqf039 (Phase 3A only; Phase 3B1 follows separately) · Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-24-hub-client-main-thread-render-path.md`

## Problem

Multi-file project previews parsed the QMD three times. Project pass 2 captured an untransformed AST with a fresh parent-less parse and JSON serialization, then immediately discarded it when constructing `WasmPassTwoOutput`. The response builder independently recaptured the payload with the original `active_path`.

## Change

- Add an internal capture-aware `render_qmd_to_preview_ast_with_capture` while preserving the existing public function as a capture-on wrapper.
- Disable capture only in project pass 2. Response construction still captures with the original `active_path`, preserving source-name provenance and response bytes.
- Add raw-WASM characterization coverage that pins both AST payload hashes and the relative source name. Existing `applyNodeEdit` round trips remain unchanged.
- Record the optimization in the hub-client changelog and consolidate the Phase 3 plan.

There are no response-shape, TypeScript-call-site, editing, or comment behavior changes. No snapshot files changed. Phase 3B1 capture gating is not included in this PR.

## Performance

Same driver, release WASM, 10 warm-cache project renders per scale:

| Fixture | Before | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1x, 99 KB | 356.940 ms/render | 284.122 ms/render | **−20.4%** |
| 8x, 792 KB | 2811.396 ms/render | 2211.554 ms/render | **−21.3%** |

Envelope bytes were exactly unchanged at both scales; the improvement comes from removing the discarded parse and serialization inside the WASM call.

## Verification

- Seven focused `quarto-core` tests and strict clippy passed.
- Rebuilt raw-WASM characterization and unchanged `applyNodeEdit` round trips: **27/27 passed**.
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-rust-tests`: all 14 legs passed.
- Selected workspace suite: **19,193/19,193 passed**. This excludes the two known R-package-version cases in bd-qwscag8b and the load-sensitive `socket_group_relaxes_permissions`, which passed in isolation. `head_peek_timeout_closes` failed once by 136 microseconds under load, then passed in isolation and in the following full run. The unfiltered local verify remains blocked by the documented R-version skew; CI's pinned R environment is the backstop.
- Real Chromium smoke: a multi-file paragraph edit reached Automerge, and a comment added and resolved with editing off appeared in and disappeared from `main.qmd`. The real-ProseMirror bold control also passed and produced `**Hello world paragraph.**` in Automerge. Output was inspected through test hooks.
- The consolidated plan passes `cargo run --bin q2 -- render --strict claude-notes/plans/2026-10-24-hub-client-main-thread-render-path.md`.

title: Make the color-scheme toggle an accessible switch (Q1 #14739 parity)
description:
Strand: bd-kwgtllvn (absorbs duplicate bd-ix7psky0) · Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-08-navbar-dark-toggle-switch.md`

## Problem

The dark/light toggle was an `<a href="">` with a hard-coded English `title`:

- It had a link role, so Space did nothing.
- Its state was conveyed only by an icon swap, and never reached assistive tech.
- The floating fallback on pages without a navbar was appended to `<body>` outside any landmark.

Quarto 1 fixed all of this in quarto-cli#14739 (released in 1.11). q2 already had the dashboard toggle's markup, but its `aria-checked` was stuck at `"false"`.

## Change (ports quarto-cli `fa48b15ea`)

- **Navbar toggle** (`quarto-navigation`): now `<button type="button" role="switch" aria-checked="false">`. Both `title` and `aria-label` carry the localized `toggle-dark-mode` term, as in Quarto 1. The term is resolved in `NavbarGenerateTransform` and threaded through `Navbar::dark_toggle_label`, the same way `search_label` is. The shared helper is `crate::language::toggle_dark_mode_label`.
- **Runtime** (`crates/quarto-core/resources/js/quarto-color-mode.js`):
  - `setColorSchemeToggle()` now sets `aria-checked` on every toggle, on load and on each switch. This covers the navbar, the dashboard, and the fallback.
  - The floating fallback is a localized `<button role="switch">` inside a landmark of its own, ported with Quarto 1's banner detection: a `<header>` when the page has no banner yet, otherwise a `<div role="region" aria-label=…>`. The label arrives through a new `data-toggle-label` attribute on the inline script tag.
- **`.top-right` utility** (`_bootstrap-rules.scss`): ported from Quarto 1's `_quarto-rules.scss:3-7`. The fallback has carried this class since the light/dark runtime landed, but q2 held the rule back in bd-q36vnfdp because it seemed unused. As a result, the toggle has been rendering at the **end of the page** instead of the top-right corner. I found this during the browser check.
- The stale SCSS comment that said site navbars use an `<a>` is updated.

> Custom CSS targeting `a.quarto-color-scheme-toggle` needs to target the button instead (Quarto 1 made the same change). Nothing in q2 used that selector.

## Tests

- `quarto-navigation`: unit tests for the switch markup (localized, escaped, with an English fallback) and a round-trip test for `dark-toggle-label`.
- `quarto-core` `theme_light_dark`: a website with `lang: fr` renders the French label on the navbar switch and in `data-toggle-label`. The existing assertions are updated for the button and the new script attribute.
- `quarto-sass`: a compiled-CSS test for `.top-right`.
- **JSDOM behavior tests** in `ts-packages/preview-renderer` (`quarto-color-mode.integration.test.ts`, 13 cases) run the real runtime as an inline script. They cover:
  - `aria-checked` on load (light default, dark default, stored preference) and after toggling, across several toggles.
  - The fallback's role, type, and label, including the English fallback, and that no fallback is added when a toggle already exists.
  - The landmark choice: no banner; a body-level header; a header nested in a plain wrapper; an explicit `role="banner"`; a header only inside sectioning content.
- A smoke-all fixture `navigation/dark-toggle-switch` (`lang: de`).
- The Phase 5 `styles.css` baseline was re-captured. The only CSS delta is `.top-right`; the branch's other SCSS edits are comments.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build --skip-rust-tests` passes, including the hub-client WASM suite on a rebuilt bundle.
- Rust `--no-fail-fast` fails only on local-environment issues: the R install (`knitr::capture_classifies_pieces`), and the local pandoc. 3.13 is outside the oracle range; Homebrew's 3.12.1 lacks HTTP support for three remote-image smoke fixtures.
- Browser check on rendered repros:
  - Navbar: Space toggles the mode, and the accessibility tree shows `switch "Toggle dark mode" checked`.
  - Plain document: the fallback sits top-right in the page's only `banner`, and Enter toggles it.

title: annotated-qmd: support SourceInfo kinds 3/4 and synthesized attrs; gate its tests in CI
description:
## Summary

`@quarto/annotated-qmd` was broken against current pampa output: **83 of 161 tests failed on `main`**, unnoticed because the suite was excused from CI. This fixes it, gates the suite in CI, and gets the package ready to publish 0.2.0 through `publish-npm.yml` (as the second end-to-end test of trusted publishing, after `@quarto/pandoc-types`).

Strand: bd-htza1cii (epic bd-kf7za8ey).

### Fixes

- **SourceInfo kinds 3 and 4** (`src/source-map.ts`). The reader injects `quarto_pandoc_reader_opts` with a code-4 `Generated { by: config-default }` source, so every document hit "Unknown SourceInfo type 4", followed by "No top-level MappedString for file -1". The new behavior mirrors `quarto-source-map` (`resolve_byte_range`, `invocation_anchor`):
  - code 4 resolves through its `invocation` anchor; without one it has **no source location**;
  - code 3 with a numeric head is a Substring of its parent; with a string head (filter provenance) it has no location.

  "No location" is now a distinct, non-error result. `getSourceLocation` returns `fileId -1` at `[0,0]`, `getAnnotatedParseSourceFields` returns an empty source, and Concat pieces without a location contribute nothing. There is a new `hasSourceLocation(id)`.
- **Metadata** (`src/meta-converter.ts`): location-less top-level entries no longer stretch the mapping's range to offset 0. They stay in `result` but are left out of `components`, since the tree describes source text and such a key would otherwise claim offset 0 of the user's file.
- **Synthesized attributes** (`convertAttr`, inline and block): the `quarto-shortcode__` Span the writer creates has no `a` field. It used to crash (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'classes')`); it now gets no attribute components. Found by running the packed tarball on real pampa output for a document with a shortcode.
- **Publish tooling** (`scripts/npm-publish/pack.mjs`): a workspace dependency left out of the run (here `@quarto/pandoc-types`) is now checked against the registry, instead of needing a flag the workflow can't pass.

### CI

`ts-test-suite.yml` now runs `npm test -w ts-packages/annotated-qmd`, and the `EXCUSED` list in `ci_test_wiring.rs` is now empty.

### Fixture changes

The 20 existing `examples/*.json` are **unchanged from `main`**. A first push regenerated them from the examples directory, as `examples/README.md` said, which renamed `astContext.files[].name`. That failed `annotated_qmd_fixture_guard`, which regenerates from the repo root and compares bytes. They're regenerated from the repo root again, and the README now documents the guard's convention. The only fixture change is the new `examples/shortcode.{qmd,json}`, which the guard and `tiling_corpus_tests` (the source-range auditor) also cover and pass.

### Filed, not fixed here

bd-1f3cfv2k: pampa gives shortcode argument Spans a made-up `file 0, [0,0]` location (`empty_source_info()` in `crates/pampa/src/pandoc/shortcode.rs`), and writes the shortcode Span without the `a` that `@quarto/pandoc-types` declares as required. Until that's fixed, `shortcode` is kept out of the strict tree-validation list (with a comment).

### Testing

- `npm test -w ts-packages/annotated-qmd`: **174/174** (161 existing + 13 new). On `main` it was 78/161.
- `node --test scripts/npm-publish/*.test.mjs`: 14/14.
- `node scripts/npm-publish/pack.mjs --check-unpublished ts-packages/annotated-qmd`: tests pass; `@quarto/pandoc-types@0.1.0` is found on the registry; the clean-project install pulls it from npm, type-checks with `skipLibCheck: false`, and imports.
- **End to end:** I installed the packed tarball in an empty project and converted fresh `pampa -t json` output of a document with `{{< meta title >}}`. Inspected output:
  - the mapping spans `[4,16] "title: Hello"`;
  - the shortcode Span is `[35,53] "{{< meta title >}}"`;
  - `result` keys are `title` and `quarto_pandoc_reader_opts`, and only `title` is in `components`.
- `cargo nextest run -p pampa annotated_qmd_fixture_guard tiling_corpus`: pass.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -D warnings`, the `ci_test_wiring` tests and `cargo xtask lint`: pass. actionlint on `ts-test-suite.yml` reports only a pre-existing SC2162 note at line 41.

### After merge

Dispatch `publish-npm.yml` with `packages: ts-packages/annotated-qmd`. The name already exists on npm, so it needs `npm trust` but no placeholder.

title: Upgrade pinned pandoc 3.12.1 → 3.13 (native, CI, pandoc.wasm)
description:
Upgrades q2's pinned pandoc from 3.12.1 to 3.13 everywhere: native pandoc, CI, and the pandoc.wasm that hub-client uses for "Download as" and document import. Quarto 1's 1.12 prereleases are moving to 3.13 as well (quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15320). Braid: bd-dti84hkx.

## Changes

**Pins (all moved together; `cargo xtask lint` checks that they agree).** `PANDOC_PIN`, `PANDOC_VERSION` in `test-suite.yml`, `ts-test-suite.yml` and `q2-preview-spa-e2e.yml`, dev-setup's `PANDOC_HYBRID_MIN_VERSION`, the filters README, the `vendored.toml` entries, and pampa's `PANDOC_ORACLE_MAX_VERSION` (`cargo xtask pandoc-check`: all 4 oracle tests pass on 3.13).

**pandoc.wasm asset name.** Upstream renamed the release asset from `pandoc-3.12.1.wasm.zip` to `pandoc-3.13-wasm.zip` (the folder inside the zip changed too). Five places got the version by stripping a `.wasm.zip` suffix. `resources/pandoc-wasm.json` now has an explicit `version` field, and every consumer reads it: `fetch-pandoc-wasm.mjs`, `capture_pandoc_recordings`, the recording replay check, and `vendored.toml`. New zip and wasm SHA-256s; the two request goldens' hash and `job_id` change to match.

**Minimum version.** The version floor follows the pin's major.minor, so q2 now rejects pandoc < 3.13 with Q-20-2 (as the 3.12 bump did for 3.11). The docs still said "3.11 or newer" and now say 3.13.

**Workflow comment.** Replaced "pinned to match Quarto 1.9". It dates from the 3.8.3 pin in February and has been wrong since the 3.10 bump. The new comment says what actually governs the pin. The bump runbook (`dev-docs/pandoc-wasm-bump.md`) is updated, including a warning that upstream's asset names change.

**Fixtures.** Only the `basic-docx` import recording changes: 3.13's docx reader fixes a regression introduced in 3.11 (jgm/pandoc#11969), so a right-aligned table column now imports as right-aligned (`| ----: |`). The native pandoc-recordings were re-captured too, but **that re-capture is not committed**: all ~85 changed files were capture noise (machine paths, the capture date, random EPUB uuids, temp-dir names), none caused by pandoc, and the existing recordings replay unchanged under 3.13. Cleaning up that non-determinism and the machine-path leaks is filed as bd-b8jy5t5p.

**Also checked.** Pandoc's `default.csl` is byte-identical in 3.13 (re-recorded). The 3.13 switch to YAML 1.2 parsing (`yes`/`no` are strings; duplicate keys are errors) doesn't reach our pandoc inputs: metadata goes to pandoc as JSON, and our one defaults file only emits `true`/`false` and an integer.

## User-facing changes (hub-client changelog entry included)
- Imported Word tables keep each column's alignment again.
- Imported RTF no longer drops the letter after a non-ASCII character.
- In Word output, a list item with several paragraphs stays a single list (jgm/pandoc#9197).

- pandoc browser harness: Chromium 348 passed, WebKit (macOS) 79 passed.
- Windows: not cross-checked. The Rust changes are JSON field reads and constants, with no platform-specific code.

title: npm publishing via trusted publishing (publish-npm.yml) + reusability plan
description:
## Summary

Sets up publishing q2's `@quarto/*` npm packages from GitHub Actions with npm **trusted publishing** (OIDC, no npm token stored anywhere) and **staged publishing**: CI stages a version privately, and it goes public only after a maintainer approves it with 2FA. It also adds the assessment plan for making hub-client / q2-preview reusable by Connect and Canvas (bd-kf7za8ey).

Strand: bd-korgbhew (child of epic bd-kf7za8ey). Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-09-reusable-hub-client-infrastructure.md`, section N1.

### What's added

- **`.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml`**, dispatch-only, with inputs `packages` (workspace dirs) and `dry-run` (default **true**).
  - `pack` job: unit-tests the tooling, then runs `pack.mjs --check-unpublished`.
  - `stage` job (non-dry-run only): runs in the `npm-publish` environment, with `id-token: write` and npm 11.15 or later, and runs `npm stage publish` for each tarball in dependency order.
  - It must stay top-level under this file name, because npm validates the *calling* workflow's file name.
- **`scripts/npm-publish/manifest.mjs`** derives the registry manifest from the workspace `package.json`:
  - `types`/`exports` point at `dist/*.d.ts`, and the `source` condition is dropped;
  - workspace dependencies become `^<sibling version>`;
  - `repository` is `quarto-dev/q2` plus `directory`, which provenance requires.

  Workspace files are untouched, so in-repo dev still consumes source. 12 `node:test` unit tests.
- **`scripts/npm-publish/pack.mjs`** builds, runs the package's own tests, stages and packs each package, then smoke-tests the tarballs. The smoke test installs them into an empty project **outside the repo** (so the repo's `node_modules` can't mask a missing dependency), runs `tsc` with `skipLibCheck: false`, and `import()`s each package in Node.
- **`scripts/npm-publish/bootstrap-placeholder.mjs`** reserves a new name with a README-only `0.0.0`, since trusted publishing can only be configured on an existing package.
- The `repository` URLs of `pandoc-types` and `annotated-qmd` now point at `quarto-dev/q2`. The `annotated-qmd` exemption reason in `ci_test_wiring.rs` is refreshed.

### Pilot: `@quarto/pandoc-types`

`@quarto/annotated-qmd` (published at 0.1.1 in Oct 2025 from q2's early code) can't go first, for two reasons:

- It depends on the unpublished `@quarto/pandoc-types`.
- Its test suite fails on `main` (83/161): pampa's JSON now emits SourceInfo kinds 3/4 that its reconstructor doesn't handle. The suite is excused from CI, so the drift went unnoticed. Filed as bd-htza1cii. `pack.mjs` correctly refuses to pack it.

### Already done outside this diff

Created the `npm-publish` GitHub environment, with a required reviewer (`cscheid`) and deployments limited to `main`.

### Testing

- `node --test scripts/npm-publish/*.test.mjs`: 12/12 pass.
- `pack.mjs ts-packages/pandoc-types` locally: builds, packs (10 files), the smoke project type-checks and imports.
- `pack.mjs ts-packages/annotated-qmd ts-packages/pandoc-types`: builds in dependency order, then stops at the failing suite, as intended.
- `bootstrap-placeholder.mjs --dry-run`: works for `pandoc-types` and refuses `annotated-qmd` (already exists).
- actionlint 1.7.12 (with shellcheck): clean.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -D warnings`, the `ci_test_wiring` tests and `cargo xtask lint`: pass.
- `q2 render --strict` on the plan: no warnings from the new note.
- **Not yet exercised:** the workflow on GitHub (it can only be dispatched once on `main`) and the `stage` job against npm (needs the trusted-publisher setup after merge).

### After merge

1. Dispatch a dry-run from `main` with `packages: ts-packages/pandoc-types`.
2. Placeholder publish of `@quarto/pandoc-types@0.0.0`, then `npm trust github …`.
3. Dispatch for real within 2 days, then `npm stage approve`, deprecate `0.0.0`, and disallow tokens on the package.

description:
## Summary

UI polish for the edit context toolbar (the pop-up over a block being edited in the preview):

- **SVG icons** replace the emoji/text glyphs for the markdown mode toggle, bold, italic, strikethrough, link (🔗), comment (💬), highlight (`!!`), mark deleted (`--`), mark inserted (`++`), and the paragraph (`¶`) type crumb. They live in a new `richtext/ToolbarIcons.tsx`, share a 16×16 viewBox, and fill with `currentColor`. Sub/superscript stay text.
- **One glyph color** for everything in the toolbar, set by `--q2-edit-toolbar-color` (default `#334155`, the existing button color; see *Theming* below). The editorial buttons lose their yellow/red/green, the type crumbs lose their per-category colors, and the ◀ ▶ nesting arrows lose their grey. The active/pressed state now shows only as the background tint; the glyph no longer turns blue.
- **Markdown icon at 2× scale.** Its art only fills y≈5–12 of the 16×16 box, so the viewBox is cropped to that band and drawn at 2× without making the toolbar taller.
- **Left alignment.** The rich-surface toolbar moves from `left: -2px` to `left: -7px`, so its outer edge lines up with the edit box's visible ring (5px tint bleed + 2px box-shadow). Before, it sat 5px to the right of the ring. The plain-text surface draws no ring and is unchanged.

## Theming

Every edit-chrome color is a CSS custom property, read with the current value as its fallback, so nothing changes visually at the defaults:

| Variable | Controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--q2-edit-toolbar-color` | glyph color for every toolbar button, crumb, and arrow | `#334155` |
| `--q2-edit-toolbar-bg` | toolbar background | `#fff` |
| `--q2-edit-toolbar-border` | toolbar border | `rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.35)` |
| `--q2-edit-toolbar-shadow` | toolbar drop shadow | `0 2px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12)` |
| `--q2-edit-toolbar-hover-bg` | button hover background | `rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.12)` |
| `--q2-edit-toolbar-active-bg` | pressed/active button background | `rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.18)` |
| `--q2-edit-toolbar-separator` | dividers between button groups | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12)` |
| `--q2-edit-toolbar-notice-color` | transient refusal notice text | `#b91c1c` |
| `--q2-edit-toolbar-input-border` | link URL input border | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2)` |
| `--q2-edit-ring` | ring around the rich edit box | `rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.35)` |
| `--q2-edit-tint` | background tint of the rich edit box | `rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.08)` |

The stylesheet only **reads** these variables and never sets them, so a theme or user stylesheet can override any of them from anywhere without specificity fights:

```css
:root {
  --q2-edit-toolbar-color: #1f2937;
  --q2-edit-ring: rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.4);
}
```

Buttons, crumbs, and nesting arrows inherit their color from the toolbar, so `--q2-edit-toolbar-color` is the single source for glyph color. A new `richtext/styles.test.ts` pins this: each variable is read with a fallback, none is set, and no toolbar or edit-box rule has a color outside a `var()` fallback.

Possible follow-up (not in this PR): chain the fallbacks to Bootstrap variables, e.g. `var(--q2-edit-toolbar-color, var(--bs-secondary-color, #334155))`, so the toolbar follows dark themes automatically.

## Notes for review

- The `¶` crumb is now an icon with no text content, so crumbs carry a `data-abbrev` attribute, and the existing crumb assertions read it instead of `textContent`. `abbrevForSourceNode` is unchanged.
- An SVG can't be underlined, so the "current crumb" underline is drawn as a 1px bottom border on icon crumbs.

## Testing

- `preview-renderer`: `tsc --noEmit` clean; unit suite (656 passed, including the new `styles.test.ts`) and integration suite (720 passed) green.
- `edit-toolbar.integration.test.tsx` now asserts that each icon button renders an SVG and no text glyph.
- `hub-client`: `npm run build` (production `tsc -b && vite build`) succeeds.
- Checked visually in the hub-client dev server for the icons, color, and sizing.

title: Resolver-only format classification (bd-luoo7qgu)
description:
Phase 2 of the [hub-client main-thread render-path plan](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/main/claude-notes/plans/2026-10-24-hub-client-main-thread-render-path.md) (finding 1).

Previously, every keystroke paid a full `parse_qmd_to_ast` in `PreviewRouter` just to read `success` — 18% of per-keystroke cost at 1x in the Phase 0 baseline, scaling linearly with document size.

## What changed

- `preview_pseudo_format`'s `q2-*` arm now gates on `Format::from_format_string` (the same gate `format_class` already used), so a partial or misspelt `q2-*` key classifies `neither` like any unknown key. With `pseudoFormat` and `class` consistent, the router's parse guard was provably vacuous.
- `PreviewRouter` drops the per-keystroke parse and the `result.success || …` guard; the mode is now the resolver's answer, re-read synchronously on every content change. This also fixes a latent bug: the guard held the previous mode when a runtime `format` (`q2 preview --to`) should have reclassified a document whose own key is unknown.
- `preview-runtime`'s now caller-less `parseQmdToAst` wrapper is deleted (`ReactPreview` uses `parseQmdToAstWithAttribution`).

## Behaviour change (accepted in the plan)

While a `q2-*` format name is being typed, the pane shows the `neither` view for the partial key (e.g. `q2-s`) instead of holding the previous preview, then mounts at the completed key — exactly what typing `docx` or `revealjs` already does.

## Performance

Measured with the Node driver on a Phase-0-style fixture (quiet machine, A/B on the same build):

| Scale | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1x (99 KB) | 526.9 ms | 423.7 ms | −19.6% |
| 8x (792 KB) | 3987.3 ms | 3299.6 ms | −17.2% |

The format check itself is ~1 ms in the browser (was 80–700+ ms); `parse.qmd-to-ast` no longer fires from the router; envelope `JSON.parse` bytes per keystroke −31%.

## Verification

- Pins written red-first on both sides (Rust `formats.rs`, wasm classification suite); wasm suite 445 passed / 28 skipped.
- Workspace `cargo nextest` 19194/19194 and full `cargo xtask verify` green; zero snapshot changes. (Two R-package version-skew failures on the dev machine were excluded after reproducing them with this diff reverted — filed bd-qwscag8b, unrelated.)

Full measurement tables and the verification record are in the plan file's Phase 2 result section.

title: fix(hub-client): support long collaborator display names
description:
Fixes #1053.

This PR increases the display-name limit to 513 Unicode code points and makes long collaborator labels usable across presence, version history, tooltips, and attribution.

The limit accommodates first and last names of up to 256 code points each, joined by one space: `256 + 1 + 256 = 513`. `isValidUserName()` now counts Unicode code points rather than JavaScript UTF-16 code units, so multibyte characters follow the same boundary. Names at 514 code points or longer are rejected.

The UI changes keep long names readable without overflowing compact layouts:

* Presence cursors, collaborator lists, and version-history labels truncate with ellipses and expose the full name in tooltips.
* Attribution badges wrap long names, remain adjacent to the attributed text, and stay within narrow viewports.
* Cursor styles are reused until a peer name or color changes, rather than being rebuilt on every presence update.

Regression coverage includes the 513/514 boundary, Unicode names, UI overflow, and attribution placement. The hub-client unit, integration, and WASM suites pass, along with the production build and a two-browser end-to-end scenario using maximum-length names.

title: Listing: sort date fields by the parsed date, not the raw text
description:
Closes #1154.

A listing with `sort: date` (or `date-modified`) now orders items by the parsed date, as Quarto 1 does. Before, it compared the author's date text, so `01/5/2024`, `5/5/2023`, `6/1/2023` sorted in string order. The order for zero-padded ISO dates is unchanged.

## What changed

`crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/sort.rs`, `compare_items`: for `date` and `date-modified`, both values go through `crate::dates::parse_date` (the parser that display and `data-listing-date-sort` already use) and are compared by `unix_millis()`.

- A value that doesn't parse sorts after every parsed date, in both directions, the same rule as missing values. Two unparseable values keep the old text comparison.
- Missing values still sort last.
- Other fields are unaffected.

## Testing

- New unit tests in `sort.rs`: M/D/YYYY dates ascending and descending (the issue's data), the list form `["date", "title desc"]` with same-day ties, mixed ISO/US/timestamp forms on `date-modified`, and unparseable values sorting after parsed ones. Three of the four failed before the fix. The fourth (mixed forms) passed by coincidence, so I changed its data so the text order and the date order differ.
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core`: 7921 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `engine::knitr::capture_tests::capture_classifies_pieces`, which also fails locally on `main` (it depends on the local R environment). It is not related to this change.
- `cargo clippy -p quarto-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- **Not verified:** the Windows cross-clippy (`--target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) can't build `aws-lc-sys`'s C code from macOS. The change uses no platform-specific APIs.
- `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo xtask lint`: passed.
- End to end: I rendered the issue's repro project with the built `q2`. Order is Bravo, Charlie, Alpha for both `sort: "date"` and `sort: ["date", "title desc"]`, matching Quarto 1.
- `q2 render --strict` on all of `claude-notes`: 1709/1709, no warnings.

Note: the `data-listing-date-sort` values still differ from Quarto 1's by the local-timezone offset, because q2 assumes UTC. That was already the case and doesn't affect the order; it is out of scope here.

title: typst: report citations to inline-only references before Typst runs (bd-yjf99rzx)
description:
## Problem

Typst output keeps Quarto 1's default of formatting citations with Typst's own bibliography, which reads only the files listed in `bibliography:`. A citation whose key exists only in front-matter `references:` reached Typst as `@key` and failed `typst compile` with a bare `label <key> does not exist in the document` (Q-21-3). Quarto 1 fails the same way.

## Decision

We keep Quarto 1's behavior, so no automatic citeproc and no conversion of `references:` for Typst. But when q2 knows Typst will fail, it stops first with a clear error. Documents that Quarto 1 renders still render.

| Typst, `citeproc` unset | Quarto 1 | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| cites a key defined only in `references:` | fails | fails (raw Typst error) | **Q-21-5 error** at the citation |
| key in `references:` and a `bibliography:` file (Typst uses the file's entry) | renders | renders | renders, **Q-21-6 warning** |
| `references:` present but not cited; or cited keys all in `.bib` | renders | renders | renders |
| `citation-location: margin` (single document or book) with an inline-only key | fails | fails | **Q-21-5 error** |
| book, default citation mode | fails | renders (book merge runs citeproc) | renders |
| `citeproc: true` | renders | renders | renders, no check |

Full investigation, including the q2 vs Quarto 1 probes: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-07-typst-inline-references.md`.

## Changes

- `crates/quarto-core/src/typst_citations.rs` (new) is the check.
  - It looks only at `Cite` nodes still in the final AST, i.e. the ones Typst will see as `@key`, and only at keys defined in `references:`.
  - It reads keys from BibLaTeX `.bib` files (via the `biblatex` crate pampa already uses) and Hayagriva `.yml` files.
  - If any `bibliography:` file can't be read or parsed, Q-21-5 is suppressed, so q2 never refuses a file Typst might read.
- `PandocWriteStage::prepare()` runs the check for Typst. That one call covers native renders and browser (`PandocPrepareStage`) renders. Bibliography paths resolve with the same helper the PDF request uses.
- New catalog entries Q-21-5 and Q-21-6, error pages under `docs/errors/typst/`, sidebar entries, and a "Citations" section in the Typst guide.
- Both `Cargo.lock` files gain one line: `quarto-core` now depends on `biblatex 0.12.0`, which was already in both lockfiles.

## For review

- **Typst source only.** With an `output-ext` other than `pdf`, Typst never runs, so Q-21-5 is a **warning** there and the `.typ` is still written. This wasn't in the plan; I decided it during implementation.
- **`citeproc: true` turns the check off entirely.** In margin mode the vendored Lua margin handler then formats citations inside Pandoc, after `prepare()`. I verified with a `keep-typ` render that no `@key` remains.
- **Possible false positive:** a document where `@key` matches a Typst label, e.g. a heading with that id, and the same key is defined only in `references:`. Typst would resolve that as a cross-reference. I judged it too unlikely to special-case.

## Tests

- 12 unit tests in `typst_citations.rs`: each rule, `citeproc: true`, an unreadable file, source-only output, `.bib` and Hayagriva key reading.
- 7 smoke-all fixtures:
  - single-document Typst fixtures: inline-only, margin, shadowed by `.bib`, shadowed by Hayagriva `.yml`, `citeproc: true`, source-only;
  - a margin-mode Typst book (`typst/inline-references-book-margin/`).
- With the check disabled, all 5 fixtures that expect a Q-21-5/Q-21-6 diagnostic fail, and the `citeproc: true` fixture still passes.

## Local verification

- Rust: 19,207 of 19,208 tests pass before the merge from `main`, and 8,715 of 8,716 quarto-core and smoke-all tests after it, with pandoc 3.13 (CI's new pin).
  - The single failure in both runs is `knitr::capture_tests::capture_classifies_pieces`: this machine's R reports `rlang_error` where the test expects `simpleError`. It passes in CI and on `main`.
- `cargo xtask verify` steps 1–4 and 6–14 pass, including the WASM hub-client build and tests. Lints, fmt and clippy are clean.
- A full `q2 render docs` succeeds: 421 of 421 pages, with no warnings from the new or edited pages.
- Windows: quarto-core can't be cross-checked from macOS (`wasmtime` compiles C). The new code uses no platform-specific APIs; CI's Clippy (Windows) job covers it.

## Follow-up

- `bd-74zz2qko`: report a cited key that is defined nowhere (a typo), which still fails with Typst's raw label error. It can reuse this key reading.

title: citeproc: warn with Q-23-2 at an unknown citation key instead of failing (#1111)
description:
Fixes #1111. Braid: bd-s1kn2w1r.

## Problem

Citing a key that isn't in the bibliography failed the render:

- **HTML:** `Error: Citation processing error: Reference 'missing2020' not found`, with no Q-code and no location. Only the first missing key was reported.
- **Typst:** Typst's own bibliography failed the compile with a generic `Q-21-3`, pointing at a line in the generated `.typ` file.

Pandoc (and Quarto 1) don't fail here. They warn `citation X not found` and render the citation as bold **X?**. This PR matches that for both formats and gives the warning a code and the key's location in the `.qmd`.

## What changes

**Output.** A missing key renders as bold `key?` inside the citation's normal parentheses and delimiters, as Pandoc does: `(Doe 2020; **missing2020?**)`, `(see **missing2020?**)`. The item keeps its prefix and drops its suffix and locator. It takes no citation number in numeric styles, so the numbers of later references don't shift, and it sorts last within its citation. I checked each of these against Pandoc 3.12.1; the fixtures and observed output are in `claude-notes/issue-reports/1111/` from the triage commit.

**Warning.** One `Q-23-2` warning per missing key, at the key's span (just after the `@`) in its first citation:

```
Warning [Q-23-2]: Citation Key Not Found
No reference has the citation key `missing2020`, so the citation renders as `missing2020?`.
```

**Code.** `Q-23-2` is new, in the existing `citeproc` subsystem (Q-23), with a catalog entry, a docs page, and a sidebar entry. The issue noted that citeproc's `Q-10-2` collides with the template subsystem (bd-be2f7); this PR doesn't use the Q-10 codes, so the collision isn't made worse. bd-be2f7 still tracks fixing the remaining Q-10 codes in `quarto-citeproc/src/error.rs`.

## Where

- `quarto-citeproc/src/eval.rs`: an unknown item goes through `unknown_item_output` instead of returning `ReferenceNotFound`. Unknown ids are skipped when assigning citation numbers and sort last.
- `pampa/src/citeproc_filter.rs`:
  - `apply_citeproc_filter` collects unknown ids. Only when there are some does it walk the document again for the key spans (`Citation.id_source`), so renders without missing keys pay nothing extra.
  - New `check_citation_keys` for the Typst path: it loads the bibliographies, warns, and replaces only the unknown items with `**key?**`. Known items stay a `Cite`, so Typst still resolves them (`@doe2020 #strong[missing2020?]`).
  - If any bibliography can't be read (e.g. Hayagriva `.yml`, which Typst reads but Q2 doesn't), it leaves the document alone and Typst reports as before.
- `quarto-core/src/stage/stages/user_filters.rs`: runs `check_citation_keys` in the post pass for Typst when Q2's citeproc isn't in the filter list and margin citations aren't in use (the Lua margin handler needs the original `Cite` nodes). This runs after `AstTransformsStage`, so cross-reference `@fig-x` cites are already resolved and can't be mistaken for missing keys. The HTML citeproc filter already relies on the same ordering.

## Not changed

- `CiteprocFilterError::ProcessingError` still turns any remaining citeproc error into a string (the `e.to_string()` the issue pointed at). A missing key no longer reaches it. Carrying structured diagnostics through `FilterError` → `PipelineError::stage_error` is wider plumbing than this fix needs.
- The `ReferenceNotFound` sites in `types.rs` (`format_bibliography_entry*`) still use `location: None`. They take a bare id from callers that have no source span, and the render path no longer hits them for a missing key.

## Tests

- 8 new unit tests in `pampa` (`citeproc_filter::tests`, `unknown_key_*` / `key_check_*`). They cover the bold marker and warning location, prefix kept and suffix dropped, one warning per key at its first citation, no citation number in a numeric style, and for the Typst check: partial replacement, a cite where every key is missing, separators between markers, and an unreadable bibliography. Written first; the citeproc ones failed with the old "must not fail the render" error.
- 2 new end-to-end tests in `quarto-core` (`unknown_citation_keys.rs`) that render a `.qmd` to HTML and to Typst. They assert the `Q-23-2` warnings, their `index.qmd` row and column, and the output markers.

Local run: `cargo nextest run --workspace` passed 19,220 of 19,221 tests. The one failure is `engine::knitr::capture_tests::capture_classifies_pieces`: the local R install reports the error class as `rlang_error` instead of `simpleError`. It's unrelated to this change, and `main` at the merge base is green in CI. Lint, fmt, the warnings-denied build, tree-sitter, and ts-packages steps of `cargo xtask verify` pass. The hub-client tests weren't run locally because the WASM package isn't built in this fresh worktree (`--skip-hub-build`); CI covers them.

Cross-platform: `quarto-citeproc` passes `clippy --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -D warnings`. `pampa` and `quarto-core` can't be cross-checked from macOS because their C build scripts (tree-sitter, aws-lc-sys, wasmtime) need Windows headers. The change adds no platform-specific code; the tests compare paths by file name and use the same `/mem` runtime pattern as the existing tests.

title: Give code cells the Quarto 1 execute environment (QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO and friends)
description:
Closes #1131.

Code cells now see the environment Quarto 1 gives them:

- `QUARTO_PROJECT_ROOT`, `QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH`, `QUARTO_DOCUMENT_FILE`
- `QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO`: path to a JSON file with `document-path` and the resolved six-bin `format` (`identifier`, `execute`, `render`, `pandoc`, `language`, `metadata`), including `format.render.brand.{light,dark}`
- `QUARTO_FIG_WIDTH`, `QUARTO_FIG_HEIGHT`, `QUARTO_FIG_DPI`, `QUARTO_FIG_FORMAT`

## Design

q2 never mutates its own process environment. The values are computed once per document in `EngineExecutionStage` (`ExecutionContext.execute_env`) and each engine delivers them:

- **knitr**: `Command::envs` on the per-document R process.
- **Jupyter**: kernels are shared by every document of a project (sessions keyed by kernel and directory), so spawn-time env cannot carry per-document values. A silent `execute_request` (`store_history: false`, `silent: true`) sets them inside the kernel before the document's first cell, for Python, R and Julia kernels. This is how Quarto 1 already sets `QUARTO_FIG_*`.
- The execute-info file is written into the document's temp dir, only when code runs.

`engine/execute_info.rs` ports Q1's `metadataAsFormat`. Its key lists are tested against `ts-packages/quarto-api/src/config/index.ts`, so the file and the Node engine host can't drift apart. `quarto-sass` gains `resolve_brand_modes`, which returns the dark half only when the brand defines dark values.

## Cost

Measured with the new `QUARTO_PERF_STATS=1` gauge (`perf.execute-info`), debug build:

| Project | Bytes | Build + write |
|---|--:|--:|
| `claude-notes` website | 6,359 | 0.24 ms |
| `docs` website | 19,406 | 0.35 ms |
| Quarto 1, lone document | 6,513 | |

The cost is per document that executes code, small next to starting an engine. Most of the `docs` size is the website sidebar config, which Quarto 1 includes too.

## Differences from Quarto 1

These are listed in the new docs page `docs/guides/authoring/execution-context.qmd`:

- `brand.dark` is present whenever the brand defines dark values.
- Each brand mode has `data` and `brandDir`, not Q1's whole internal `Brand` object.
- `QUARTO_FIG_*` report q2's figure defaults (`png`, 96 dpi), not Q1's HTML `retina`.
- The `julia` and `marimo` engines don't receive the variables yet (bd-x3h4zjhl).

## Tests

- Unit tests in `engine/execute_info.rs`: partition, key-list parity, fig env, paths, brand, per-language setup code with escaping.
- `quarto-sass` brand-mode tests.
- `execute_env_cli_e2e`: drives `q2 render` with a knitr document in a subdirectory with a light/dark brand, and two Jupyter documents on one shared kernel, each seeing its own document. Skips without R+knitr or a `python3` kernel.
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core -p quarto-sass -p quarto-brand -p quarto`: 9,152 of 9,153 pass. The one failure is `capture_classifies_pieces`, which also fails on `main` with newer rlang (bd-54odm3rz).
- Clippy with `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask lint`, and `npm run build:wasm` pass.
- The Windows cross-check is not possible for these crates (C build scripts). The new code uses no platform-specific APIs.

No snapshot files changed.

## Found along the way (separate strands, not fixed here)

- bd-i7yz08uh (P1): parallel project renders interleave cells of different documents on one shared Jupyter kernel. Reproduced with `QUARTO_JOBS=2`. The new Jupyter test runs with `QUARTO_JOBS=1` until it is fixed.
- bd-08hfh3ut (P1): a project-level `brand:` resolves against the document directory once code runs, for a document in a subdirectory. This is pre-existing on `main`.

Triage record: `claude-notes/issue-reports/1131/triage.md`. Plan and measurements: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-10-execute-environment.md`.

title: listing: grid thumbnails honor image-height like Quarto 1
description: Closes #1155. Grid listings now size thumbnails the way Quarto 1 does: every grid thumbnail gets an inline `style="height: …;"` (default **150px**, or the listing's `image-height`) and the `card-img` class, so large images no longer render at full size. For the issue's repro, q2 now emits: ```html ``` ## What changed (`crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/`) Mirrors Q1's `utilities.img` / `imagePlaceholder` / `imageSrc` / `emptyDiv` and its per-type defaults in `website-listing-read.ts`: - `config.rs` `apply_type_defaults`: `image-height` defaults to grid `150px` and table `40px`, with none for the default type. Q1 sets none there, and q2's old `120px` was never emitted. title: theme: read engine-reparsed theme paths as written (Q-14-4 on underscored extension themes)
description:
Closes #1152.

On pages that run code, an extension's `theme:` entry such as `_extensions/acme/demo/_colors.scss` lost both underscores and failed with Q-14-4. These pages now render with the same theme as pages without code.

**Cause.** `EngineExecutionStage` serializes the merged metadata to qmd for the engine and re-reads the result. The qmd writer emits a `Path`-kind value as a plain YAML string, so the re-read parses it as markdown. The text between the two underscores becomes `Emph`, and `ConfigValue::as_plain_text` flattens the inlines without the delimiters.

**Fix.** A markdown-parsed config string is now read back from the text its span covers, decoded as a YAML scalar so quotes and escapes come out right. The flattened inlines are used only when the span isn't a single range in a file whose content is available.

- `crates/quarto-core/src/config_paths.rs`: new `config_value_text` and `literal_config_strings`. `resolve_config_path` and `resolve_config_file_with` (via `ConfigPath::from_value_in`) now use `config_value_text`.
- `crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/engine_execution.rs`: the engine intermediate's source slot now stores its markdown. Before, it stored only the line index, so the re-parsed spans had no text to read. Cost: one extra copy of the engine output per document. A side effect is that diagnostics pointing into an intermediate can now render snippets.
- `crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/compile_theme_css.rs`: `ThemeConfig::from_config_value` gets a metadata copy whose `theme:` strings are literal, read through `doc.ast_context.source_context`, the context that holds the intermediates.

**Known gap (follow-up `bd-8svy3p89`).** Stages build `PathCtx` from `doc.source_context`, which never registers engine intermediates. On engine pages, other path keys (e.g. `template: _partials/_page.html`) still fall back to the flattened inlines. The theme path, which this issue reports, is fixed.

## Testing

- New tests, each confirmed failing before the fix:
  - `config_paths::tests::markdown_strings_are_read_from_their_source_text`: plain, double-quoted, and single-quoted (`''` escape) scalars.
  - `config_paths::tests::markdown_path_values_resolve_by_their_source_text`
  - `config_paths::tests::literal_config_strings_rewrites_markdown_leaves_only`
  - `engine_execution::tests::reparsed_metadata_strings_read_back_as_written`: a `Path` theme value through the real engine stage with an echo engine. Fails when the slot is registered without content.
- The issue's repro (website + extension with `theme: [main.scss, _colors.scss]`, pages `plain.qmd`, `code.qmd` (jupyter), `rcode.qmd` (knitr)). Before: 1 of 3 rendered, Q-14-4. After: 3 of 3 rendered, and the compiled CSS contains `$accent` from `_colors.scss`.
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core -p quarto --no-fail-fast`: 8707 passed, 1 failed. The failure, `engine::knitr::capture_tests::capture_classifies_pieces` (`rlang_error` vs `simpleError`), also fails on `main` locally because it depends on the local R environment.
- `cargo clippy -p quarto-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo xtask lint`: passes.
- `q2 render --strict` on the plan note: clean.
- The Windows cross clippy (`--target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) could not compile tree-sitter's C from macOS locally. CI's **Clippy (Windows)** check passed.
- **CI:** all 13 checks green on `92adcec`.

title: Speed up attribution history replay
description:
## Summary

Loading authorship for the Authors overlay and Word/PowerPoint downloads replays the document's Automerge history on the main thread. This PR makes that replay several times faster for typed histories and stops it freezing the editor. Attribution output is unchanged.

- **Batches changes.** One `applyChanges` call costs time proportional to the text length, however many changes it carries. Consecutive changes with the same author and second now go in one call.
- **Yields on a time budget.** The initial build hands control back to the browser after 8 ms of work, instead of after every 500 changes.
- **Uses one replay loop** for the initial build, its catch-up, and incremental updates, and drops the history traversal and unused bookkeeping.

Tracking: bd-kckdpt8j.

## Performance

Typing fixtures are 2,000 single-character changes at six per second. "Longest slice" is the longest stretch the main thread is held without a break.

| Fixture | Initial build | Longest slice |
|---|---:|---:|
| Typing, 20k characters | 9,370 → 1,641 ms (5.7×) | 2,415 → 52 ms |
| Typing, 100k characters | 44,945 → 7,633 ms (5.9×) | 11,257 → 241 ms |
| Every change in its own second, 400k characters | 9,835 → 9,848 ms | 9,764 → 950 ms |

An eight-edit incremental update within one second drops from 706 to 90 ms at 400k characters.

Histories where every change has its own second do not batch: their total time is unchanged and only the longest slice improves.

## Tests and verification

New tests pin the batching and yielding behaviour and check that runs equal a change-by-change replay over random concurrent histories. Hub-client tests, the production build, type checking, and a Chromium run of the overlay with an edit burst and toggle cycle all pass. The Rust workspace suite was not rerun; no Rust source changed.

title: qmd writer: keep adjacent lists apart inside list items
description:
Strand: bd-2bcre8cr · Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-10-qmd-writer-list-separator.md` (investigation and probe in `claude-notes/plans/qmd-writer-ordered-list-separator-investigation/`)

## Problem

The randomized test `pampa::list_looseness::sampled_list_documents_round_trip_through_the_qmd_writer` failed on one CI run of PR #1137, with input `- 1.\n  1)\n`. Investigation showed a wider **writer** bug.

The qmd writer put a bare `<!-- -->` between every two adjacent ordered lists, and inside list items it wrote that line tight, with no blank lines. The reader's HTML-block extent is the paragraph. That's deliberate, and it matches pandoc `markdown`, so Quarto 1 does the same. So the separator line came back as a lazy continuation of the list's last line:

| Input | Written | Re-read |
|---|---|---|
| `- 1.\n  1)` | `* 1.\n  <!-- -->\n  1)` | the empty `1)` becomes `Plain [Str "1)"]` |
| `- 1. a\n  1) b` | `* 1.  a\n  <!-- -->\n  1)  b` | `a` silently gains a `RawInline` |
| `- x\n  1. a\n  1)` | blank lines around the separator | the item turns loose (`Plain x` becomes `Para x`) |
| `- 1. a\n\n  <!-- -->\n\n  1.` (author-written separator) | `* 1.  a\n  <!-- -->\n  1.` | **the two lists merge into one** |

Blank lines around a bare separator, as pandoc's own writer uses, don't help in q2. q2 follows CommonMark looseness (bd-az53ojvo), so the blank lines make the item loose.

## Change

- **Separate only when needed** (`qmd_prepass.rs`). A separator is inserted only when the two lists' *written* markers collide: `Default` and `Period` both write `.`, and `OneParen` and `TwoParens` both write `)`. A delimiter change already starts a new list when read, so documents read from qmd, whose adjacent lists always differ in delimiter, no longer need a separator or trigger the pre-pass copy. Example (`(@)`) lists are always separated, because of a separate reader issue (bd-bumesax9).
- **Fence inside tight items** (`qmd.rs`). In a tight list item, a bare-written HTML `RawBlock` directly after a list is written as a ```` ```{=html} ```` fence. That covers inserted and author-written separators alike. The fence closes explicitly and keeps the item tight; pampa and `pandoc -f markdown` both read it back as `[OL, RawBlock, OL]`. Top level and loose items keep the bare form, so this is a narrow, list-item-only exception to the 2026-09-04 bare-HTML rule.
- **Remove `loosen_items_with_separators`.** This earlier workaround turned the item's first `Plain` into a `Para`, and it missed items that start with a list.

## Tests

- `list_looseness`:
  - a deterministic `ADJACENT_LIST_CASES` table, one case per failure class;
  - `imported_same_delimiter_lists_stay_apart`, for the pandoc-shaped ASTs that qmd can't express;
  - adjacent sublists in the **enumerated** corpus, so the class fails deterministically instead of as a proptest flake. The comrak oracle tests still pass on it.
- The round-trip check now also fails when a raw node appears that the first read didn't have. The block shape alone hid the `RawInline` case.
- The proptest seed is committed in `crates/pampa/tests/proptest-regressions/list_looseness.txt`.
- Prepass unit tests cover differing delimiters (no copy) and colliding written markers (separator).
- `qmd_writer_pandoc_shapes::adjacent_ordered_lists_in_a_tight_item_are_not_swallowed` now requires an exact round trip plus the fence, instead of ignoring the Plain/Para difference.

## Verification

- Locally, `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passes every non-Rust step. The Rust suite runs 19,209 tests; the only failure is `knitr::capture_classifies_pieces`, which depends on the local R install.
- `PROPTEST_CASES=200000` runs of the sampled oracle and round-trip tests pass.
- The investigation probe (`roundtrip.sh`) shows all eight cases round-tripping unchanged after the fix (`roundtrip-output-after-fix.txt`).

## Follow-ups filed

- bd-bq4mjc6b (P4): tag writer-inserted separators with provenance.
- bd-go7corj6 (P4): a reader quirk, where an empty item after a comment-only line reads as text.
- bd-bumesax9 (P3): consecutive `(@)` example items are a reader parse error.
