title: Fill the q2 preview's VFS on demand, behind one exposure policy
description:
`q2 preview` now loads what a render reads on demand instead of guessing it up front. Design: `claude-notes/designs/preview-vfs-contract.md`; build log and measurements: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-07-preview-demand-driven-vfs.md`.

- Single-file preview syncs only the deck; includes, images, theme partials, bibliographies and components arrive when the render asks, and a file created later where the render looked shows up without a restart.
- Every path the preview serves goes through one exposure policy (no hidden, generated, out-of-tree or unknown-type files), and the server refuses requests whose `Host` isn't loopback, an IP, `--host`, or listed in `QUARTO_PREVIEW_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.
- The preview renders in a Web Worker, and an edit re-renders only if the render read it; PDF pages, which have no read set, now recompile on any edit.

Draft until Firefox e2e and the Windows cross-check have run; both were blocked locally.

### Validation

1. `cd hub-client && npm run build:wasm`, then `cargo xtask build-q2-preview-spa` and `cargo build --bin q2`.
2. Single-file deck, in a scratch folder: `deck.qmd` with `bibliography: refs.bib`, `format: html: theme: styles/deck.scss`, `![](img/a.svg)`, `{{< include parts/a.qmd >}}` (which includes `sub/b.qmd`) and a citation; `styles/deck.scss` with `/*-- scss:defaults --*/` importing `partials/vars` and setting `$body-bg: $deck-bg !default;`; `styles/partials/_vars.scss` setting `$deck-bg`; plus an unrelated `notes.qmd` and a `.env`. Run `q2 preview deck.qmd`: the theme colour, both includes, the image and the citation all render.
3. `curl http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/documents`: only the deck and the files the render read are listed; `notes.qmd` and `.env` are not.
4. Create `styles/partials/_extra.scss` setting `$deck-bg` to another colour, then add `@import "extra";` to `_vars.scss`: the page re-themes without a restart.
5. Edit `notes.qmd`: no re-render (`window.__renderTicks` in the devtools console stays put). Edit `refs.bib`: the citation updates.
6. `curl -H 'Host: evil.example' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health` is 403; `curl http://localhost:<port>/health` is 200. `curl "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/preview/file?path=.env"` is 403.
7. Project mode (`q2 preview` in a website with `output-dir: public`): files under `public/` and `index_files/` (beside `index.qmd`) are not in `/api/documents`; a new `.qmd` created during the session appears without a restart.
8. Devtools > Sources shows an `engine.worker` thread, and typing in the editor UI (`--allow-edit`) no longer blocks the page while it renders.
9. `q2 preview --share` from step 2, then `q2 preview --join <ticket>` on another machine or port: the deck renders the same for the guest.

title: Sync project `.scss` files into the live preview
description:
A project-local `.scss` `theme:` file and the partials it imports now render in live `q2 preview` the same as they do in `q2 render`, instead of failing with Q-14-4. Editing one on disk re-themes the open page. `quarto hub` now syncs project `.scss` files too.

Like images, every `.scss` file in the project directory is synced, whether or not a document uses it.

### Repro

1. Create a project with three files:

   `_quarto.yml`
   ```yaml
   project:
     type: default
   format:
     html:
       theme: custom.scss
   ```

   `custom.scss`
   ```scss
   /*-- scss:defaults --*/
   $body-bg: #ffe4e1;
   ```

   `index.qmd`
   ```markdown
   ---
   title: SCSS theme
   ---

   Hello.
   ```

2. Run `q2 preview` in the project directory. On `main`, the render fails with Q-14-4 "Theme file not found". On this branch, the page has a pink background.
3. Change `$body-bg` in `custom.scss` to `#e0ffff` and save. The open page turns light blue.

title: Fix attribution cold-build edit race
description:
## Summary

Fixes a race where typing while a long attribution history was loading could give new text stale authorship in the Authors overlay and Word/PowerPoint downloads.

- Processes edits that arrive during the initial attribution build before returning the result.
- Applies the same fix to both the overlay and downloads.
- Adds regression tests for multiple edits, disabling attribution, switching files, and late completion of an older build.
- Updates the Phase 6a plan and hub-client changelog.

Tracking: bd-oul15aql. No snapshot files changed.

## Verification

- Production hub-client build, including WASM: passed.
- Hub-client tests: 1,755 unit, 240 integration, and 478 WASM tests passed; all 109 DOM-parity fixtures matched.
- Browser test: created a 502-change history, typed while the initial build was paused, then confirmed the new text had the correct author and hover badge.
- Type checking, ESLint, formatting, Clippy, repository lint, and strict notes rendering: passed.
- Changelog WASM tests: 478 passed.

## Known unrelated failures

The full Rust workspace run used pandoc 3.13 and finished with 19,201 tests passed and 201 skipped. Its only failures were the two existing local knitr issues tracked by bd-54odm3rz/bd-qwscag8b and bd-b95dt1ia. This PR changes no Rust source.

title: Coalesce Monaco semantic tokenization
description:
Monaco now shares identical semantic-token requests and waits for a 300 ms model-quiet window before tokenizing. Base highlighting remains immediate, while semantic enrichment avoids redundant synchronous VFS/WASM work during typing.

* Coalesce concurrent and completed requests for the same path and content; retry empty results and clear cached state on disposal.
* Snapshot the latest content after the quiet window and honor cancellation before tokenization. A 50 ms window was rejected after it reintroduced multiple tokenization runs in Chromium.
* Reduce measured mount tokenization from 2 runs to 1 at both fixture scales.
* Reduce measured edit-burst tokenization from 2 to 1 run at 1x (84.7 → 45.0 ms) and from 3 to 1 at 8x (1054.0 → 367.9 ms).
* Add regression coverage, Phase 5 measurements, and a user-facing changelog entry.

## Verification

* `npm run build:all -w hub-client`
* `npm run test:ci -w hub-client` — 1,751 unit, 240 integration, and 478 WASM tests passed; 109/109 DOM parity fixtures passed.
* `npm run test:wasm -w hub-client` — 478/478 tests passed after the changelog update.
* `cargo xtask verify --skip-rust-tests --skip-hub-build` — all enabled legs passed.
* Scoped ESLint and `cargo fmt --check` passed.
* Real Chromium: two Playwright scenarios passed; final edited text and render completion were inspected.
* `cargo nextest run --workspace` — 19,201 passed and 201 skipped; the two unrelated failures are tracked as bd-54odm3rz/bd-qwscag8b and bd-b95dt1ia.

Part of bd-lxq4oac3.

title: npm-publish: build out-of-run workspace deps before testing
description:
## Summary

The first real `publish-npm.yml` run for `@quarto/annotated-qmd` ([run 42823245049](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/42823245049)) failed in the `pack` job, with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND .../node_modules/@quarto/pandoc-types/dist/index.js`. `annotated-qmd`'s tests import the *workspace* `@quarto/pandoc-types` through its `dist/`, and a clean checkout never builds it. Locally a stale `dist/` hid the problem; `ts-test-suite.yml` has its own build-all step. **Nothing was staged on npm**, because the stage job was skipped.

`scripts/npm-publish/pack.mjs` now builds every workspace package that the run transitively depends on but doesn't publish, in dependency order, before the run's own build and tests. The new pure helper `workspaceDepsToBuild` has 2 unit tests.

Strand: bd-htza1cii. bd-5f98vdw2 (a pack dry-run on PRs) would have caught this before release time.

## Testing

- `node --test scripts/npm-publish/*.test.mjs`: 16/16.
- Reproduced the CI failure locally by deleting `ts-packages/{pandoc-types,annotated-qmd}/dist`. Before the fix: `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. After: `building dependency @quarto/pandoc-types (not published in this run)`, then 174/174 tests, a clean pack, and the smoke import of the tarball passes.

## After merge

Re-dispatch `publish-npm.yml` with `packages: ts-packages/annotated-qmd`. The trusted-publisher config for `@quarto/annotated-qmd` was created on 2026-11-10 and is still within its 2-day window.

title: docs: replace the placeholder About page with "About Quarto 2"
description:
The About page in the docs navbar only says "About this site". This PR replaces it with a short "About Quarto 2" page: why Quarto 2 exists, its goals, its design principles, and how it relates to Quarto 1, Pandoc and Quarto Hub.

**This is a proposal.** The page states project positions, which is yours to decide, so please adopt, rewrite or close it as you see fit.

To keep it safe to merge, the page adds no new claims. Every statement paraphrases or quotes something the team has already said publicly, and links to it:

- the two blog posts ([What's next: Quarto 2](https://opensource.posit.co/blog/2026-04-06_whats-next-quarto-2/), [Parsing and Source Maps](https://opensource.posit.co/blog/2026-05-07_quarto-2-parsing/));

Nothing comes from `claude-notes/`. The page keeps the "not yet reviewed by a human" banner.

**Why.** Users keep asking the same questions in discussions: why a rewrite, what happens to Pandoc, how compatible it will be, whether Hub stays open source. The answers exist, but they are spread across blog posts and comment threads.

title: Gate preview AST capture when editing and comments are off
description:
Stacked on #1140 (`braid/bd-wpmqf039-preview-ast-capture`); please merge that PR first. This PR contains only the Phase 3B1 commits.

Strand: bd-wpmqf039 · Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-10-24-hub-client-main-thread-render-path.md`

## Overview

Preview rendering captured and serialized an untransformed AST on every render, even when neither editing nor comments could consume it. This PR adds a default-on, per-render capture option and skips that work only for read-only surfaces that do not need a source baseline.

- Add `captureUntransformedAst` to the single-document and project preview options and thread it through the TypeScript wrappers and both hot WASM paths.
- Preserve capture-on behavior when options or the flag are omitted, so existing native and raw-WASM callers retain their contract.
- Arm hub capture for editing or visible comments; arm SPA capture for `allowEdit`. When disabled, omit `untransformed_ast_json` without changing `ast_json`.
- Keep baseline-less comments readable but read-only until an armed render supplies the source index. Nested-buffer regeneration remains editing-only.
- Add native, raw-WASM, wrapper, comment, SPA, and host-transition coverage, and record the change in the hub-client changelog and Phase 3 plan.

Phase 3B2 comment-intent UX and Phase 3C transport changes remain deferred.

## Performance

Same release WASM, production wrapper/init path, warm SASS cache, 10 renders per scale. Flag-on is the Phase 3A comparison point; flag-off represents editing off and comments hidden in the hub, or `allowEdit=false` in the SPA.

| Path | Scale | Capture on | Capture off | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Single document | 1x | 164.935 ms/render | 86.728 ms/render | **−47.4%** |
| Single document | 8x | 1305.639 ms/render | 712.920 ms/render | **−45.4%** |
| Project | 1x | 170.617 ms/render | 90.004 ms/render | **−47.2%** |
| Project | 8x | 1345.331 ms/render | 712.938 ms/render | **−47.0%** |

Envelope bytes fell by about half. Armed editing-on and comments-visible controls retained the flag-on envelope bytes and timings, so they are not presented as unarmed wins.

## Verification

- Focused `quarto-core`: 8/8 passed; strict native clippy passed.
- Raw WASM capture/default compatibility and unchanged `applyNodeEdit` round trips: 31/31 passed.
- Preview runtime: 92/92 passed. Preview renderer: 643 unit and 723 integration tests passed.
- SPA: 95 unit and 97 integration tests passed, plus its production build.
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-rust-tests`: all 14 legs passed, including hub-client unit, integration, and WASM suites.
- Selected workspace suite: 19,193/19,193 passed. Exclusions are the documented R-package-version and load-sensitive cases from Phase 3A plus unrelated parser bug bd-wwmnuqxr. Standalone WASM clippy still reaches the pre-existing lints tracked in bd-wn2pd12d.
- Real Chromium hub smoke: 2/2 passed. Editing after an armed transition reached Automerge; comment add/resolve changed the QMD; baseline-less comments stayed read-only and recovered their controls after the armed render.
- Real Chromium SPA smoke: 2/2 passed. The default session stayed read-only, and `--allow-edit` wrote the observed edit to `index.qmd` on disk.
- No `.snap` files changed.

title: Execution records in use: preview and hub run from records; one presenter for every engine (RIU + RFU + OPR)
description:
## Execution records: preview and hub run from records, and every engine goes through one presenter

Preview and `provide-hub` now work from an ipynb execution record instead of the legacy capture cache. A record can come from an engine run, a file, or a Positron cache. One presenter turns a recorded cell into page output for Jupyter, Julia and knitr alike, and plain `q2 render` of Julia and knitr takes the same route. Three epics, developed on one integration branch, land together because each builds on the last. Main has the record writer behind an off-by-default gate; none of the consumer side below exists on main, so the command and metadata names are new, not renames:

1. **RIU, records in use.** Records replace the preview capture cache and can come from places other than an engine.
2. **RFU, RIU follow-up.** Closes the gaps the Positron demo exposed: a `q2 convert` command, knitr export, tests, and docs.
3. **OPR, one presenter path.** Every recorded cell goes through one presenter that reads what the cell supplies, not which engine made it.

The branch changes about 390 files, mostly in `quarto-core` and `quarto-preview`, and no `.snap` files.

### What changes for users

- **Record writing is on by default** for local preview and `provide-hub`. The record is the only thing the viewer needs; the legacy capture remains only for an engine that builds no record, and a diagnostic says so.
- **`execute: record-sources` chooses where a document's record comes from.** The source list (`engine`, `cache`, a directory, and so on) is one metadata key, set with `-M` on the command line. `preview`, `provide-hub`, `convert` and `render` read it through one reader, so a document gets its record from the first source that has one.
- **`q2 convert --to positron-ipynb`** exports a record as a Positron cache file, for Python, Julia and knitr documents.
- **Positron cache files import as records**, and the import gate asks whether the record declares kernel equivalence instead of testing the engine name.
- **Plain `q2 render` of Julia and knitr** builds the record in memory and presents it through the Rust presenter, writing nothing under `.quarto`. A cached knitr chunk becomes a record cell by reading its sidecar (level 3 cache hit), so knitr's cache still works. The LaTeX family, `pptx`, `context` and unknown knitr targets stay on the engine route.
- **Julia gains the capture facts knitr has** (expression starts, anchors, output kinds), through one runner change. Julia still shows only its last value, so it does not interleave as knitr does.
- **Presentation fixes that apply to every engine:** ANSI escapes are stripped in one function, group captions and panel ids are numbered, page dependencies for widget outputs are derived on every route, image size is read from output metadata, and engines can set cell and output attributes through `quarto_attrs`.

Jupyter output stays byte-identical unless a cell sets a new option, except for two documented preview and hub fixes (OPR-1a, OPR-1b) and one group-caption fix (OPR-7j). Marimo keeps the legacy capture splice and is outside this work.

### How it is built

- **One cell step, one document function.** Each cell runs through a single presenter step that takes optional inputs (anchors, starts, kinds, figure count, resolved options, echoed code). A single document-level function takes matched unit and cell pairs and returns a replacement, a skip with a reason, or an error. Callers keep their own matching and error policy.
- **Presentation is chosen by offer and acknowledgement,** not by engine name. A presenter feature switches on when a cell supplies the input it needs and degrades one input at a time when it does not.
- **`warning` and `message` are enforced exactly where the record's hash definition lists them as display-only.** When an option is in the hash, capture already enforced it.
- **A Quarto 1 parity harness** gates the plain-render switch per target, with the Julia targets graduated and the interleaving entries signed.
- **The Julia engine extension** is vendored as a subtree of the fork's `q2/node-port`. It is restored by `cargo xtask pull-extension-subtree julia-engine` as the last step before review, so the history ends in a subtree merge commit.

### What to check

- **The Windows run is not done.** `aws-lc-sys` cannot cross-compile from macOS, so RFU-6 needs a native Windows run of the changed crates and of the tests that exercise paths and file handles.
- **OPR-8 (final docs and end-to-end pass) is still open.** The user docs for `q2 convert`, `execution-records` and preview are written, but the embedded-docs refresh (`cargo xtask build-agents-docs`) is that plan's last step.
- **OPR-7d was cancelled.** Its work moved into OPR-7a through 7h, so a reader following the plan numbers will find a gap.
- **Positron fork work is outside this repo.** RFU-7 changed the fork's extension and demo guide on local commits that were never pushed.
- Reviewers who want the shape before the diff should read the three epic notes in `claude-notes/plans/`: `2026-11-02-records-in-use-epic.md`, `2026-11-08-rfu-epic-riu-follow-up.md`, `2026-11-07-one-presenter-path-epic.md`.

### Testing

- `cargo xtask lint` and `cargo clippy -p quarto-core -p pampa --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core -p pampa`: 13772 run, 13772 passed, 36 skipped, with pandoc 3.13 on `PATH` (the Julia subtree included). Under pandoc 3.12.1, 252 tests fail on the 3.13 version floor that main introduced; that is not a regression from this branch.
- `cargo xtask verify` (full, with the hub-client build) was started locally; results are posted below when it finishes.
- Not done: the Windows run (RFU-6).

title: Run Jupyter cells whose fence is longer than three backticks
description:
Fixes bd-f63cqoke. Found while fixing #1156.

## Problem

A Jupyter cell whose source contains a run of three or more backticks is silently not executed:

````markdown
```{python}
print("a ``` b")
```
````

renders as an inert `<pre class="{python}">` with no output and no warning. This breaks `output: asis` cells that print fenced code, such as a tabset of install commands, which is the #1156 reporter's use case.

## Cause

- The document is re-serialized to qmd before execution. The qmd writer (`determine_backticks`) emits a fence one longer than the longest backtick run anywhere in the block, so this cell becomes ````` ````{python} `````.
- The `.ipynb` converter does the same for a source line that *starts* with backticks (Quarto 1's rule).
- `runs_in_legacy_executor` (`crates/quarto-core/src/engine/units.rs`) required `fence_len == 3`, so the executor skipped those cells.

Quarto 1 opens a Jupyter cell on any run of three or more backticks (`jupyter.ts` `startCodeCellRegEx`), and knitr already ran these cells in q2. The fix changes the rule to `fence_len >= 3`.

## Tests

- **Unit** (`units.rs`, `text_execute.rs`): openers of 4 and 5 backticks run. A parse → qmd writer → executor plan round trip keeps the backtick-run cell. The `cells_nested` corpus fixture becomes a named divergence from the old regex finder.
- **Stored replay** (`ipynb_stored_replay.rs`): a notebook with both triggers (mid-line and line-leading runs) presents both stored outputs. This was red before the fix.
- **Live kernel smoke-all** (`smoke-all/jupyter/backtick-run-in-cell.qmd`, `requires: jupyter`): mid-line, `output: asis` tabset and control cells. Verified red with the old rule and green with the new one.

## Please look at

1. **Re-blessed presenter golden.** `presenter-goldens/notebooks/four-backtick-source` pinned the bug: the cell's stored `ok` output was dropped. That set's README asks for any golden change to be raised as a behavior change, so I'm raising it here. The README now records it as an intended exception, following the EXR-8 precedent.
2. **hub-client smoke-all runner change.** Both WASM-based runners now honor `run.requires` the way the Rust runner does: the vitest WASM runner (`src/test-utils/smokeAllFixtures.ts`) and the Playwright runner (`e2e/helpers/smokeAllDiscovery.ts`, a separate copy of `shouldSkip`; the Hub-Client E2E job caught it). WASM has no engine runtimes, so any `requires` entry skips the fixture. Side effect: `includes/code-cell/code-cell.qmd` (`requires: jupyter`, `eval: false`) no longer runs in either hub runner; it still runs natively. I did not add a `hub-client/changelog.md` entry, because the change is test-only and the changelog lists user-facing changes. Say if you want one anyway.
3. **Out of scope, filed separately.** Making the qmd writer count only backtick runs that can close a fence is bd-4wvmsld9. A knitr capture test that fails locally depending on the R setup (`rlang_error` vs `simpleError`) is bd-yibbojew.

Plan and investigation: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-11-jupyter-backtick-fence-cells.md`.

title: quarto-sass: dashboard theme files after `brand` can use `$brand-*` variables
description:
Closes #1132.

A dashboard with `theme: [cosmo, brand, custom.scss]` can now read `$brand-*` palette variables from `custom.scss` (e.g. `$navbar-bg: $brand-navy;`), as in Quarto 1. Plain `html` is unchanged; there the same theme still fails, as it does in Quarto 1.

## What changed

`crates/quarto-sass/src/compile.rs`:

- New `dashboard_brand_layers(config, context)`: when `config.dashboard_layer` is on and a brand resolved, returns `brand_to_layers(brand)`. This mirrors Quarto 1's `format-dashboard.ts:191`, which pushes the `_brand.yml` SCSS bundle a second time after the HTML theme bundle. User-layer defaults merge in reverse, so this copy's `$brand-*` defaults come first.
- The layers are appended after the theme layers (before the doc-vars layer) in all three themed assembly paths: `assemble_theme_scss`, the native `compile_with_doc_vars` and the WASM `compile_with_doc_vars`.
- The cache key is unchanged. Whenever a brand resolves, the `brand` token is in `theme:` (auto-injected if absent), and that token already hashes the brand.
- As in Quarto 1, a dashboard's bundle now carries the brand layers twice.

## Testing

- New unit tests in `compile.rs`, covering both `compile_theme_css` and `compile_with_doc_vars`:
  - `test_dashboard_theme_after_brand_can_use_brand_variables` failed before the fix with the issue's `Undefined variable` error and passes after it.
  - `test_html_theme_after_brand_cannot_use_brand_variables` pins the unchanged HTML behaviour (Quarto 1 parity).
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-sass`: 330/330 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core -E 'test(/dashboard|brand|theme/)'`: 334/334 passed.
- The issue's repro rendered with a local `q2` build. The dashboard renders, and the compiled CSS has `.navbar{background-color:#1f4e79}`. The `html` variant still fails with Q-14-6 `Undefined variable`.
- `cargo clippy -p quarto-sass --all-targets -- -D warnings` (host): clean.
- `cargo check -p quarto-sass --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`: passes.
- `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo xtask lint`: passes.
- `q2 render --strict` on the plan note: clean.

**Not verified:**

- Windows cross-clippy (`--target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) can't build `aws-lc-sys`'s C code from macOS. The change uses no platform-specific APIs.
- `cargo clippy --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` fails with 3 errors in `quarto-system-runtime` on `main` as well, so that failure predates this PR.
- The dark-variant bundle (brand with `light`/`dark` colours) is covered by the same code path but has no dedicated test.
- Not checked in a browser.

title: One terminal output-style policy: honor NO_COLOR / --color / tty for color and hyperlinks (#1135)
description:
Fixes #1135 (braid: bd-be8ve52f).

## Problem

q2 decided whether to emit ANSI color and OSC 8 hyperlinks in several places, and the places disagreed. Render diagnostics hard-coded both to on, so `NO_COLOR=1 q2 render index.qmd 2>log` wrote 162 SGR sequences and 2 OSC 8 links into the log. Three other paths had their own rules:

- the `-v` tracing logs honored `NO_COLOR` but colored even when redirected to a file;
- `ParseError`'s `Display` baked styling into stored strings, so render aborts leaked escapes too (a broken `_quarto.yml` gave 62 SGR and 2 OSC 8);
- `pampa` used the always-on library default.

The triage and the full audit are in `claude-notes/issue-reports/1135/triage.md`. The plan, with an end-to-end record, is in `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-11-terminal-output-style.md`.

## Change

**One policy, resolved once.** The new `quarto_util::output_style` module holds a pure `resolve()` and a `OnceLock` that is set on the main thread right after argument parsing. It decides each stream separately; the first matching rule wins:

1. `--color=never|always` (a new global flag on `q2` and `hub`);
2. `NO_COLOR` set to a non-empty value turns color off;
3. `CLICOLOR_FORCE` or `FORCE_COLOR` (non-empty, not `0`) turns color on;
4. `CLICOLOR=0` turns color off;
5. otherwise color is on when the stream is a tty and `TERM` supports color, or `CLICOLOR` / `CI` is set.

This is `anstream`'s precedence, so q2 agrees with clap's `--help`.

Hyperlinks have their own rule. They need color, a tty, and a terminal that `supports-hyperlinks` recognizes, or an explicit `FORCE_HYPERLINK`. Forcing color into a pipe never adds links. `get()` returns plain output when `init` never ran (libraries, tests, WASM).

**Every sink reads the policy.** That covers:

- render diagnostics and the counts clause;
- CLI diagnostics;
- `create` / `add` / `use`;
- the tracing layer (`with_ansi`);
- `hub`, `pampa`, `qmd-syntax-helper` and `quarto-preview`.

**No styling baked into strings.** `ParseError::render_with(&TextRenderOptions)` is new. `render()` and `Display` are now plain. Terminal sinks render with the resolved style:

- the abort paths;
- `RenderAbort::user_message`;
- `main`, which now wraps `run()` and prints a parse error through `terminal_style::format_error_report`. Every other error prints exactly as before.

String producers (WASM entry points, `ts_record`) now pass `plain()` explicitly.

**Docs.** New page: `docs/tools/terminal-output.qmd`.

## Behavior changes for reviewers

- **Fewer links.** Terminals that `supports-hyperlinks` doesn't recognize no longer get OSC 8 links unless `FORCE_HYPERLINK=1` is set. Examples are tmux and macOS Terminal.app. Before this change, links appeared wherever color did.
- **Updated test.** `json_errors::ipynb_diagnostic_hyperlinks_real_notebook` pinned "hyperlinks into a captured stderr". It now asks for them with `FORCE_HYPERLINK=1`.
- **`main`'s error output.** A parse error that reaches `main` no longer prints a doubled `Error:` header or repeats itself under `Caused by:`.
- **`--help`.** `q2 --help` follows the environment variables but not `--color`, because clap renders help before our flag is parsed. The docs say so.

The upstream default (`TextRenderOptions::default()` is styled) is out of scope here. It is filed as posit-dev/quarto-error-reporting#12.

## Tests (written first, seen failing)

- 20 resolver unit tests covering the precedence table.
- 13 binary-driven `q2` tests (`tests/integration/terminal_output_style.rs`): diagnostics, tracing, `--color`, the force and hyperlink variables, and the Dispatch and Scripts abort paths. Each abort path has a pipe test, which failed before the change, and a `--color=always` guard, which passed before and still passes, so no terminal path lost color.
- 2 binary-driven `pampa` tests.
- Unit tests for `ParseError::{Display, render_with}` and `format_error_report`.

## Verification

- Ran the #1135 repro through the binary, writing to a file: 0 SGR / 0 OSC 8, with or without `NO_COLOR`.
- Simulated a terminal with `script`. The abort and diagnostic outputs keep their before-change SGR / OSC 8 counts (I compared counts, not bytes).
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-rust-tests` passes, including the hub-client WASM build and the JS/TS suites.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 19355 of 19356 pass. The one failure is local-only (R/knitr `rlang_error`, bd-54odm3rz) and also fails on clean `main`.
- Clippy `-D warnings` passes on all touched crates. The Windows cross-clippy of `quarto-util` is clean. I did not cross-check the other crates for Windows; their changes contain no platform-specific code.

title: q2 add: keep unknown record keys, refuse newer records, pin line endings
description:
Makes `.quarto-source.yml` safe to share with other tools. Quarto Wizard's development version now writes this record too. Strand: bd-yjg91sls. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-11-quarto-source-record-contract.md`.

Fixes #1175. Fixes #1176. Part of #1177 (the line-ending rule). The spec and JSON Schema (#1177) and `track`/`commit` (#1178) are still under discussion in the plan doc, and aren't in this PR.

## Changes

**Unknown keys are kept (#1175).** `SourceRecord` gains a flattened `extra: serde_yaml::Mapping`, which keeps the keys in file order. `record::inspect` replaces `installed_state` and also returns the parsed record. `write_record` is now per extension: q2 sets the keys it owns (`version`, `source`, `kind`, `ref`, `files`) and copies every other key from the record being replaced. Nothing is carried over from an unreadable record or from one with a newer schema version.

**Newer schema versions (#1176).** `parse_record` reads `version` before parsing the rest. Above `RECORD_VERSION`, it returns `EditKind::NewerRecord(v)`. That goes through the existing local-changes refusal, so replacing the record needs `--force`, and the error adds an "Upgrade q2" hint. Checking the version first matters: a v2 record that doesn't fit v1's shapes is still reported as newer, not as unreadable. A version that is 0, missing or not an integer reports as unreadable.

**Line endings.** On Windows, Git's `core.autocrlf` (on by default in Git for Windows) rewrites LF to CRLF on checkout. Every text file then stops matching its hash and looks locally edited.
- Any run that writes an extension creates `_extensions/.gitattributes` with `* -text` when the file is missing. The file sits next to the extensions, not inside one, so it is never hashed and doesn't clash with a `.gitattributes` an extension ships. An existing file is never edited. `[No Change]` and `--dry-run` don't write it; the dry run prints "would also create". `--json` gains `gitattributes_written`.
- The rule is `-text`, not `eol=lf`: `eol=lf` converts on commit, which would break extensions that ship CRLF files. The plan doc has the reasoning and the precedents (cargo vendor, go.sum).
- A file that differs from its hash only by CRLF↔LF (either direction) is reported as `line endings changed`, with a hint that names autocrlf and the `.gitattributes` fix. It still needs `--force`, so other tools reading the record keep the same exact hash rule.

The user guide (`docs/guides/authoring/extensions.qmd`) has the new behavior.

## Testing

- New unit tests in `record.rs`: extra keys round-trip in order and don't count as edits; a newer version is reported even when the rest doesn't parse; version 0, missing or not an integer is unreadable; CRLF and LF conversions in both directions; a real edit made with CRLF still counts as modified.
- New end-to-end tests in `tests/integration/add.rs` follow the repros in #1175 and #1176, plus `.gitattributes` creation (dry run, No Change, existing file, JSON) and the line-endings message.
- Checked by hand in a real git repo: with a root `* text=auto`, `git check-attr` reports `text: unset` under `_extensions/`, and with `core.autocrlf=true` an LF file checks out as LF.
- `cargo xtask verify` (Rust steps), then a full workspace run: 19,288 tests passed. One local failure isn't related to this PR: `quarto-core` `knitr::capture_tests::capture_classifies_pieces` gets `rlang_error` instead of `simpleError` from my local R 4.6 install. This PR doesn't touch `quarto-core`.
- I couldn't cross-check the Windows build from macOS: `ring`'s build script needs a Windows C toolchain. The change uses no platform-specific APIs, and paths in the new code go through `Path::join`.

title: knitr capture: name the error the author raised, not rlang's wrapper (bd-54odm3rz)
description:
## Problem

On any machine with current CRAN packages, `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core capture_classifies_pieces` fails (`left: "rlang_error"`, `right: "simpleError"`). Because `cargo xtask verify` runs nextest fail-fast, this one failure stopped verify for every agent on such a machine. It was filed twice (bd-54odm3rz, bd-qwscag8b).

**Cause.** knitr 1.51 (yihui/knitr#2388) passes `rlang::entrace()` to evaluate as an error calling handler whenever rlang is installed. `entrace()` re-signals **every** chunk error as a new `rlang_error`, keeping the original condition in `$error` and dropping or replacing its call. `capture.R` named errors with `class(p)[[1]]`, so the records Q2 writes depended on the knitr version, and custom condition classes were lost too.

## Fix

`capture.R` unwraps the entraced condition (`capture_raised_error`) and takes `ename`, `evalue` and `call` from the condition the author raised. `text` stays as knitr formats it (now rlang's `Error in \`f()\`:\n! msg`), which matches what Quarto 1 shows: Quarto 1 has no structured error record and passes knitr's text through unchanged. Errors raised with `rlang::abort()` have no `$error` and keep their own class.

New test `capture_error_names_the_condition_the_author_raised` covers a custom condition class with a call, a plain `stop()` inside a function, and `rlang::abort()` with a custom class. Before the fix it reported `rlang_error` for the first two, with the custom condition's call lost.

## CI note

CI installs no R (by design), so the knitr tests, this one included, skip there. They only run on developer machines. Locally on main @ 3743b5d6a (R 4.6.0, knitr 1.52, evaluate 1.0.5, rlang 1.3.0): `cargo xtask verify` passes, and all 19252 Rust tests pass. Measuring and reducing that local exposure to knitr drift is filed as bd-qbkwun87.

The branch also carries the investigation plan (`claude-notes/plans/2026-11-11-knitr-rlang-error-ename.md`) with the R repro, the list of the 137 tests that start R locally, and a knitr-exposure analysis.

Related: bd-qwscag8b (closed as duplicate), bd-lnu81d4a (the separate SQL `#|` knitr change), bd-qbkwun87 (run live-R tests only on demand).

title: engine: reconcile metadata three ways so project values survive the engine round-trip
description:
On pages that run code, project, extension and format metadata no longer change across the engine run. This fixes:

- a project `brand:` file failing with Q-14-6 for documents in subdirectories (bd-08hfh3ut);
- `include-in-header` going missing from every engine page (bd-bfp32yw9);
- `css:` links resolving against the document's directory;
- and the class GH #1152 belonged to (extension theme paths with two underscores).

## The problem

`EngineExecutionStage` serializes the whole AST, including the fully merged metadata, to qmd, runs the engine, and reads the output back. Reconciliation compared blocks only. `apply_reconciliation` then took the re-read metadata wholesale ("executed metadata wins entirely"). The front matter doesn't survive that trip:
- strings come back as document markdown;
- `Path` values lose their kind and their project-relative base, since their spans now lie in the intermediate file in the document's directory;
- `_a_b`, `*`, `[x](y)`, `$x$`, `@ref` and newlines change.

The investigation's probe matrix is in the plan.

## The fix: a three-way metadata reconcile

`merge_markdown_into_ast` now also parses the exact text the engine received (the baseline) and reconciles three versions:
- **S0:** the real metadata;
- **S1:** the baseline's metadata;
- **S2:** the output's metadata.

S1 and S2 went through the same writer and reader, so where they agree (structural hash, spans ignored) the engine changed nothing. In that case S0 is kept, with its kind and span. Where they differ, the engine's value is taken. Maps recurse key by key: an engine-added key is taken, an engine-removed key is dropped, and a key the writer never emitted is kept. Equal-length arrays recurse item by item. Anything else takes S2. Front-matter span evaluation therefore still works, and nothing depends on provenance rules or masking.

- `crates/quarto-ast-reconcile/src/meta.rs` (new): `reconcile_meta`.
- `engine_execution.rs`: `merge_markdown_into_ast` takes the baseline. The engine loop passes `unmask(qmd)`.
- `record_splice.rs`: passes its pre-edit text as the baseline.
- **Revert of the GH #1152 fix (#1164):** `config_value_text`, `literal_config_strings`, `ConfigPath::from_value_in`, `literal_theme_meta`, and storing each engine intermediate's text in its source slot. The reconcile makes them unnecessary. `config_paths.rs` and `compile_theme_css.rs` are back to their pre-#1164 state.
- `marimo_records.rs` test fix. `marimo_record_replays_without_engine` set its empty registry on `ctx.engine_registry_override`. `render_qmd_to_html` overwrites that from `HtmlRenderConfig`, so the real marimo engine ran during the "replay without engine". Its header includes then duplicated the record splice's folded ones, because the round-trip no longer drops the folded copy. The test now passes the registry through the config. The only production record splice (`pass2_renderer.rs`, the hub-client HTML preview) renders with `execute: false`, so no engine runs after a splice there.

Blocks keep the two-way reconcile (decision 4 in the plan).

## Testing

New tests, each confirmed failing with the reconcile disabled, for the reported reason:
- `quarto-ast-reconcile` `meta::tests`: 11 unit tests over hand-built S0/S1/S2.
- `engine_execution::tests::engine_round_trip_keeps_untouched_metadata`: the probe matrix (`Path`, `Glob`, `Expr`, URL, markdown chars, HTML, cite, math, multiline, empty, bool) comes back equal, span included. `engine_change_to_metadata_is_taken` covers a value the engine rewrites.
- `record_splice::tests::splice_keeps_the_metadata_as_it_was`.
- `tests/integration/engine_metadata_round_trip.rs`: pages in `sub/` rendered through `render_to_file` with a `FixtureEngine`, so no Python or R is needed. It covers project `brand:` (failed with Q-14-6 on `sub/_brand.yml`), project `include-in-header` + `css:` + theme layer, and the GH #1152 extension theme partial.

Real engines, with the #1152 code reverted:
- The GH #1152 repro: 3 of 3 pages render, with jupyter and knitr.
- The investigation's `subdir-repro.sh`: correct `../styles.css` link and header on the engine page.
- The bd-08hfh3ut fixture: knitr and jupyter, root and `sub/`. All four pages render with the header and one shared theme bundle.
- A front-matter `title:` with an inline Python expression still renders evaluated (`Answer 42`).

Suites:

title: Give every document its own Jupyter kernel (bd-i7yz08uh)
description:
## Problem

Kernel sessions were keyed by (kernel name, working directory). In a project render the working directory is the project directory, so every Python document of a project shared one kernel:

- **Parallel render (`QUARTO_JOBS=2`)**: cells of different documents interleaved on that kernel, so a document could read a value another document had just set (`doc a sees owner = b`). The per-document execute variables from #1161 (`QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH` etc.) were also wrong for later cells.
- **Serial render (`QUARTO_JOBS=1`)**: a document could read the globals of whichever document ran before it, so results depended on render order.
- The daemon-wide sessions lock, taken per cell, also serialized cells on **unrelated** kernels.

Quarto 1 never shares a kernel between documents. Its one-shot path starts a fresh kernel per document, and its keepalive daemon is keyed by the document's path.

## Fix

- `SessionKey` gains `document` (`ExecutionContext.source_path`).
- `JupyterDaemon::acquire` returns a `SessionLease`, an owned guard on that session's own lock, which the document holds for its whole run. The map lock is never held across an await, so documents on different kernels now run in parallel. Kernels start without a shared lock. The old `start_lock` also kept concurrent `peek_ports` calls apart; a small reserved-port set now does that job, holding each kernel's ports until it is ready.
- `KernelScope` carries a policy:
  - `kernel_scope()` (`q2 render`) shuts a document's kernel down as soon as the document finishes, on both the success and error paths. At most `QUARTO_JOBS` kernels are alive at once.
  - `kernel_scope_retaining()` (`q2 preview`) keeps each document's kernel warm, **with its state**, for the next render of that document, as Quarto 1's keepalive daemon does. No reset on reuse.
- Docs: `guides/authoring/jupyter-kernels.qmd` gains "Each document has its own kernel"; `execution-context.qmd` drops the shared-kernel paragraph.

Design discussion and decisions: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-11-jupyter-kernel-doc-isolation.md`.

## Tests

The tests in the first two groups failed at `78b4863c6` before the fix:

- Fake kernel (CI-safe), `text_execute_isolation.rs`: two documents in one directory run on different kernel processes; a document's kernel is gone once it finishes; a retaining scope reuses a document's kernel across renders. The fake kernel gains a `KernelPid` output so a test can see which process ran a cell.
- Real Python, `jupyter_document_isolation_e2e.rs`: the interleave under `QUARTO_JOBS=2` (four cells, so the interleave happens every time at HEAD; the doc comment explains why) and the globals leak under `QUARTO_JOBS=1`. `render_leaves_no_kernel_behind` now expects one kernel per document, and both must be dead after exit.
- Lease tests in `fake_kernel.rs`: exclusive per document; a held lease doesn't block another document; `Release` shuts the kernel down; a waiter whose holder releases gets a fresh kernel the daemon tracks.
- The `QUARTO_JOBS=1` workaround #1161 added to `execute_env_cli_e2e.rs` is removed.

No snapshot files changed.

## Verification

- `cargo nextest run --workspace`: 19286 passed. Excluded: `knitr::capture_tests::capture_classifies_pieces`, which fails at `main` too on this machine because of knitr 1.52 (bd-3p8y4gdt, unrelated).
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build`: lints, clippy, build and the strict claude-notes render pass; the test step stops only on the knitr test above. The Jupyter engine is native-only, so the hub/WASM build is unaffected.
- Windows cross-check (`cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) cannot run from macOS (`ring`/`aws-lc-sys` build C). The change adds no platform-specific code or cfg gates.
- End to end with `q2 render` on the repro fixtures: correct results at `QUARTO_JOBS=1` and `2`, with no stray kernels afterwards. The interleave fixture renders in 7.2 s at `QUARTO_JOBS=2` versus 11.4 s at `1`.
- End to end with `q2 preview` (headless browser, two "Re-execute" clicks): `a.qmd` re-ran on the same kernel (same PID, `runs 1`, then `runs 2`), `b.qmd` had its own kernel, and after SIGINT both kernels were gone and their connection files removed.

## Second commit: graceful shutdown, and kernels dying at startup

The first CI run failed once on Ubuntu: `q1_equivalence_fixtures` hit `failed to create shell socket: Connect timed out after 30s`. It never reproduced locally in five full loops of all 301 Jupyter tests, and the rerun on `fa24d2750` passed. Investigating it found two things, both fixed in `fa24d2750`:

- **A regression from this PR: kernels were being SIGKILLed.** `KernelSession::shutdown()` was a thin wrapper around `shutdown_blocking()`, and that function has to skip the graceful `shutdown_request` when it runs on a tokio runtime thread. On `main`, kernels were shut down from `KernelScope::drop`, off the runtime. A document's lease now ends inside `engine_runtime().block_on`, so every kernel was killed and user `atexit` handlers never ran. `shutdown()` now sends the request on the current runtime and waits for the kernel to exit before the kill backstop. A new e2e test, `a_finished_documents_kernel_exits_gracefully`, has an `atexit` handler write a marker; it failed before the fix and passes now.
- **Diagnostics.** A kernel that died while starting surfaced only as that 30 s timeout, and its stderr was piped but never read. The shell connect now races the process exiting, and such a kernel fails at once with `ExitedDuringStartup`, carrying its exit code and stderr. This is tested with a fake kernel that exits at startup; I wrote that test alongside the change, not before it. If the timeout recurs, the message will now tell a dead kernel from a slow one. The cause of the original timeout is still unknown: a port collision, or a kernel that started slowly under load.

Follow-up found along the way: bd-wjg6sjxj (kernels orphaned when the owning process is killed by a signal; present on `main`).

title: Honor Jupyter `output: asis` (#1156)
description:
Fixes #1156.

## Problem

For a Jupyter cell, `#| output: asis` (or document-level `execute: output: asis`) was read only as a visibility flag. q2 wrapped the printed markdown in `.cell` / `.cell-output-stdout` divs as a code block, while Quarto 1 splices it into the document. knitr already worked, because its vendored `hooks.R` converts `output: asis` to `results = "asis"` before q2 sees the cell. The Jupyter path had nothing equivalent.

## Fix

This adds a Jupyter asis mode to the shared presenter (`CellOptions::output_asis`, read from the cell options after the document's `execute:` options are merged in) that matches Quarto 1's `jupyter.ts` (`asis`, lines ~1340–1738):

- **stdout** is written as is, as document markdown.
- **Every other output** keeps its own markup but loses its `.cell-output` div. stderr and errors become bare fences, an `execute_result` with only `text/plain` stays a fenced block, `text/markdown` is written raw, HTML becomes a bare `{=html}` block, and images become bare figure markdown.
- **The `.cell` div** is dropped unless something needs it (Quarto 1's `needCell`): classes, forwarded attributes, a caption, or a `tbl-` label.
- A cell's own `output: true` overrides a document-level `output: asis`.

This deliberately differs from knitr's `results = "asis"`, which writes a plain `execute_result` raw and keeps the markdown-display div. The differences are listed in the table in `claude-notes/issue-reports/1156/triage.md`. Since all three render paths go through `format_outputs_with`, the fix covers `.qmd`, stored `.ipynb` outputs, and record replay.

## Evidence

- `claude-notes/issue-reports/1156/` holds the repro, variant fixtures, and Quarto 1's intermediate markdown (`*.q1.md`, from `quarto render … -M keep-md:true`) as the expected output. With live Python kernels, q2 now renders every fixture like its `.q1.md`, including a generated tabset.
- 10 unit tests in `presenter/cell.rs` (`jupyter_asis_tests`) cover one output kind each, plus `needCell`, echo, and the document-level override.
- 2 end-to-end tests in `tests/integration/ipynb_stored_replay.rs` use stored outputs, so no kernel is needed in CI. Both fail without the fix.

## Out of scope (filed separately)

- **bd-f63cqoke**: a Jupyter cell whose source has ```` ``` ```` in the middle of a line (e.g. printing a fenced code block from a tabset generator) is silently not executed. The qmd writer re-serializes the cell with a 4-backtick fence, and `runs_in_legacy_executor` only accepts 3. The reporter's real use case may hit this.
- **bd-gyzi1s9e**: a plain cell label (`#| label: my-cell`) is never written as the `.cell` div's id, with or without asis. Quarto 1 writes it.

## Local verification

- `cargo nextest run --workspace` (19232 passed). Excluded: `capture_classifies_pieces`, which fails on `main` with local R packages (rlang 1.3.0). This is a known issue, bd-54odm3rz / bd-qwscag8b.
- All other `cargo xtask verify` steps pass. The exception is hub-mcp vitest, which timed out on different tests in each run while the machine's load average was ~32. That package doesn't touch the presenter.
- The Windows clippy cross-check can't build `quarto-core` from macOS (`aws-lc-sys` compiles C). The change contains no platform-specific code.

title: Shrink the Pandoc AST (88× → 18× of source) and stream the hub's AST JSON out of WASM memory
description:
Shrinks the in-memory Pandoc AST and takes the AST JSON out of the hub's WASM memory. Epic bd-4x6kih4c; study and all measurements are in `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-12-ast-string-storage-study.md`.

## Why

A study (bd-akgst1fi) measured the parsed AST of `claude-notes/plans` (26.3 MiB of Markdown) at 2,304 MiB of heap, 88× the source. 96% of that was `Vec<Inline>` and `Vec<Block>` buffers: `Inline` was 360 bytes (sized by `Link`) and `Block` 824 (sized by `Table`), so every `Space` paid for a `Link`.

The study started from the idea of borrowing `&str` from the source buffer. It recommends against adding a lifetime to the AST: text was 2.5% of the bytes, and Lua userdata, the cross-thread project index and reconcile all need owned data.

## What changed

| Change | Strand | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Box the cold `Inline` variants | bd-xrfun6mn | `Inline` 360 → 64 bytes (32 on wasm32) |
| Box the cold `Block` variants | bd-09g8zl30 | `Block` 824 → 64 bytes (32 on wasm32) |
| `Attr` and `AttrSourceInfo` become one-word handles | bd-gz80k6c6 | 104 / 80 → 8 / 8 bytes |
| Hub parse entry points stream the AST JSON to JS | bd-fz5ls4vq | AST JSON never sits in WASM memory |
| `ast-memory` (native) and `wasm-mem.mjs` (hub) tools | bd-akgst1fi, bd-r17a0k7v | measurement |

Compile-time assertions hold `Inline` and `Block` at 8 words.

## Results

Native, reader only (`ast-memory` on `claude-notes/plans`):

| | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| AST heap | 2,304 MiB (87.7× source) | 480 MiB (18.3×) |
| Peak RSS of the run | 2.75 GiB | 0.65 GiB |
| Parse wall time | 7.7 s | 6.1 s |

Hub WASM memory growth, one 188 KiB document (`wasm-mem.mjs`):

| | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| First parse | 57.1 MiB | 15.4 MiB |
| After 30 valid edits | 57.1 MiB | 15.6 MiB |
| After one failed parse | 57.1 MiB | 55.9 MiB |

## What reviewers should look at

Most of the diff is mechanical (`Box::new` at construction sites, `.into()` where a tuple becomes an `Attr`). The parts with real decisions:

- **`crates/quarto-pandoc-types/src/attr.rs`.** `Attr` and `AttrSourceInfo` store the empty case as a null pointer and `Deref` to their old shape (`AttrTuple`, `AttrSourceParts`), so `attr.0`, `attr.1.push(..)` and `attr_source.id` are unchanged. Mutable access to an empty value allocates; equality, `Debug` and serde look only at contents, so JSON and snapshots are unchanged.
- **`crates/pampa/src/filters.rs`.** The topdown filter macros gain a `boxed` arm.
- **`crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/shortcode_resolve.rs`.** Or-patterns that mixed boxed and unboxed variants are split.
- **`crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs`.** `parse_qmd_to_ast`, `parse_qmd_to_ast_with_attribution` and `parse_qmd_content` return a JS object instead of a JSON string. Its `ast` field is still the AST JSON as a string, written through `JsStringSink` in 64 KiB chunks. Direct callers drop one `JSON.parse`; `preview-runtime`'s wrapper, the two demos and two WASM test files are updated.

## Not in this PR

- `ecow` for `Str.text` (bd-v6cug77d) is on `feature/bd-v6cug77d-small-string-type-ast`. It removes 64% of AST heap blocks in the reader but is neutral end to end, so it is held back.
- One failed parse grows hub memory by 40 MiB (bd-q3ocwexr); node locations are sent twice on the wire (bd-vmdfc8y5).

## Test plan

- `cargo xtask verify` passes locally on macOS: clippy and lints, 19,937 Rust tests, hub-client WASM build and tests, the TypeScript package tests.
- Windows: only `quarto-pandoc-types` could be cross-checked from macOS (`cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`); the other touched crates depend on tree-sitter's C sources. The change uses no platform APIs. A native `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` on Windows would settle it.
- Not measured: end-to-end `q2 render` peak RSS before and after, and browser-side cost of the hub response.

## Measuring

```bash
cargo build --release -p perf-harness --bin ast-memory
./target/release/ast-memory claude-notes/plans

(cd hub-client && npm run build:wasm)
node crates/perf-harness/scripts/wasm-mem/wasm-mem.mjs crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/pkg claude-notes/plans
```

title: Retry a Jupyter kernel start that loses a port to another socket (bd-e87d5tmn)
description:
## Problem

Since #1173 (one Jupyter kernel per document), CI on `main` sometimes fails Jupyter e2e tests. The python kernel dies during startup with this error:

```
zmq.error.ZMQError: Address already in use (addr='tcp://127.0.0.1:38829')
```

There have been two failures so far, in two different tests:
- run 43235574747: `parallel_documents_do_not_interleave_on_a_kernel`
- run 43118290398: `render_leaves_no_kernel_behind`

## Cause

`reserve_ports` gets the kernel's ports from `runtimelib::peek_ports`. That function binds port 0, records the port and closes the listener. The kernel binds the port only after it starts, and in between any socket can take it. This race is a known TOCTOU, documented in runtimelib.

#1173 made the race much easier to hit:
- Kernel starts within a process now run concurrently. While one kernel starts, the shell/iopub connect for it keeps retrying, and every retry takes a fresh ephemeral source port. One of those can be a port that was peeked for another kernel but not yet bound. The `reserved_ports` set doesn't cover this case.
- Other nextest processes start kernels too, and the in-process reservation can't see them.
- A kernel per document means more kernel starts in total.

## Fix

The kernel has to bind the ports itself, so no reservation scheme can close the gap. Instead, the start is retried:
- `JupyterError::is_port_conflict()` recognizes a kernel that exited during startup with an `EADDRINUSE` message on stderr. It matches the POSIX, MSVC-CRT and Winsock wordings.
- `start_kernel` makes up to 3 attempts, each with freshly peeked ports. Any other startup failure is still returned immediately.

#1173 already reports a kernel that dies during startup right away instead of after a 30s timeout, so a retry costs only the kernel's startup time.

The full assessment is in `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-12-jupyter-kernel-port-race.md`.

## Tests

The fake kernel has a new mode, `QUARTO_FAKE_KERNEL_FAIL_FIRST=<n>:<path>`. It counts its spawns in `<path>` and exits with the ipykernel port-conflict message on the first `n` spawns. New tests cover three cases:
- one port conflict, then success (2 spawns)
- conflicts on every attempt, so it gives up after 3 spawns
- a startup failure that isn't a port conflict is not retried (1 spawn)

There are also unit tests for the message matching. The existing exit-at-startup test now uses a message that isn't a port conflict.

With the attempt count set to 1, the first two new tests fail.

`cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passes locally on macOS. I couldn't cross-check quarto-core for Windows with clippy from macOS, because tree-sitter's C build fails for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`. The change uses no platform-specific APIs.

title: quarto-sass: brand layers name the theme `brand` (dashboard value boxes use brand colours)
description:
Closes #1187.

With `theme: [cosmo, brand]`, dashboard value boxes now use the brand's `success` / `warning` / `info` colours instead of cosmo's overrides, as in Quarto 1.

## What changed

- `crates/quarto-sass/src/brand_layer.rs`: `brand_to_layers` always emits a theme-name layer (`$theme: "brand" !default;`), placed after the `defaults.bootstrap` layer and before the color and typography layers, matching Q1's `brandSassLayers` / `brandBootstrapSassLayers`. Defaults merge in reverse, so this `$theme` wins over the Bootswatch theme's. `brand` has no entry in `theme-override-value`'s table, so the colours fall back to `$success` etc.
- Side effect, also as in Q1: `navbar-default-offset` / `theme-navbar-bg` / `theme-navbar-fg` see `brand` rather than the Bootswatch name when a brand is present. An empty brand now yields one layer (the theme-name layer) rather than none.
- Tests: new `test_dashboard_value_boxes_use_brand_colors_over_bootswatch` in `compile.rs` (the issue's repro, compiled through `compile_theme_css`), and new `theme_name_layer_follows_bootstrap_defaults`. I also updated the layer-index assertions in `brand_layer_test.rs`.

## Testing

- New test failed before the fix (`#3aa716`, cosmo) and passes after (`#009e73`).
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-sass -p quarto-core`: 8721 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p quarto-sass --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: q2 render --dry-run: report Pass-1 diagnostics without rendering
description:
Adds `q2 render --dry-run` (braid strand `bd-render-dry-run-dyiq7d08`). It checks a document or project without rendering it: it discovers the project, resolves formats, parses every file and merges its metadata (Pass 1), and runs the project type's `pre_render` hook. It then reports every problem found and exits, using the same exit-code rules as a render. No code executes, no pre- or post-render script runs, and nothing is written, including `.quarto/`.

Plan, including the decisions and implementation notes: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-13-render-dry-run.md`. User docs: `docs/guides/projects/dry-run.qmd`.

## How it works

- **Orchestrator** (`quarto-core/src/project/orchestrator.rs`): `ProjectPipeline::with_dry_run` sends both `run()` and `run_with_book_support` to a new `run_dry`. In `run_with_book_support`, the switch happens after scope resolution and before the book dispatch branches.
  - Pass 1 under dry run **parses every file live**. It never reads the profile cache, because a cached profile carries no diagnostics, so a cache hit would hide that file's warnings. It never saves to the cache either.
  - Pass 1 can now **keep the non-fatal diagnostics** that the head stages produce. Until now it dropped them, because Pass 2 reruns those stages and reports the same diagnostics. They surface as `ProjectRenderSummary::pass1_diagnostics`, and `diagnostic_counts()` and `promote_warnings_to_errors()` cover the new field. A full render behaves as before.
  - A `pre_render` failure, such as a book chapter list naming a missing file (Q-5-35), becomes a project diagnostic instead of aborting the run.
  - The diagnostics a render reports before Pass 1 (from `run_head`) and the engine-resolution warning are now shared helpers, used by `run_head` and `run_dry` alike.
- **CLI**: `--dry-run`, which conflicts with `--clean-cache`. Output formatting lives in `commands/render_dry_run.rs`.
  - Text output ends with `Checked N files — 1 error, 2 warnings`. A single-file check prints this line too, so a clean run says "no problems found". With `-v`, it also lists the files a render would produce, each with its format.
  - With `--json-errors`, stderr keeps the real render's NDJSON records (`JsonPass1Failure`, `JsonDiagnostic`), so an existing consumer needs no changes. Stdout gets one summary object: `files_checked`, `files_failed`, `errors`, `warnings`, `strict`, `stopped_early`, and `files[]` under `-v`. Its JSON Schema is checked in at `crates/quarto/schemas/render-dry-run-summary.json`, with a drift test (regenerate with `QUARTO_REGEN_SCHEMAS=1`).
  - With `--dry-run --json-errors`, `-v` does not raise the log filter, so stderr stays pure NDJSON. Real renders are unchanged.

## Scope note for reviewers

Many familiar warnings come from Pass 2 and are **not** reported by a dry run. For example, Q-2-49 (`[text]` with no link target) is emitted by the `reference_link_diagnostics` transform. A dry run reports parse errors, warnings from the front matter and metadata merge (such as Q-5-29, a missing `css:` file), and project-level problems. The docs say this explicitly. Running cheap, engine-free diagnostic transforms in a dry run is a possible follow-up.

## Testing

- `crates/quarto/tests/integration/render_dry_run_cli.rs` has 14 end-to-end tests:
  - errors and warnings are reported, and the dry run writes nothing (byte-for-byte snapshot of the project tree);
  - warnings still appear when a real render has already filled the profile cache;
  - no code executes (a cell that would create a file leaves no trace);
  - a book with a missing chapter reports Q-5-35;
  - `-v` lists files with their formats;
  - `--strict` and `--fail-fast` work as with a render;
  - with `--json-errors`: stderr is pure NDJSON (with and without `-v`), the summary counts match stderr, a single file works, and a broken file produces the same `JsonPass1Failure` record as a real render.
- I checked that the tests catch a regression: with the cache bypass disabled, 6 of the 14 fail.
- Unit tests cover counting and promotion of the new summary field, and the summary JSON shape and schema drift.
- `cargo xtask verify` passes locally (19,965 Rust tests, plus the TS suites and builds).
- As a speed check, `--dry-run` on `docs/` checks 430 files in about 0.2 s, and on `claude-notes/` 1,828 files. Both are clean.

**Windows:** I couldn't run the cross-check `cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` from macOS, because `aws-lc-sys` compiles C for the target. The change adds no platform-specific code, and the tests build paths with `Path::join`. A native Windows run of `cargo clippy -p quarto -p quarto-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` would confirm.

title: q2 preview --hub-url: mirror a project from an existing sync server (bd-yq3awhmw)
description:
## What this does

`q2 preview` can now show a project that lives on an existing sync server (a running `q2 hub`) instead of a local directory:

```
q2 preview --hub-url ws://127.0.0.1:3000/ws --project <index-doc-id | share URL>
```

The preview's own hub runs with no local project and mirrors the remote one. The browser keeps talking to the preview's `/ws`, so all three UI modes work unchanged:

- **Default viewer**: follows the remote project read-only.
- **`--allow-edit`**: block edits in the viewer are written to the remote project.
- **`--ui editor`**: the full hub-client, editing the remote project.

Strand: bd-yq3awhmw. The analysis and spike results are in `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-13-preview-against-remote-hub.md`.

## The one non-obvious change: the share policy

samod's `ShareConfig.announce` also controls whether a hub *requests* documents it doesn't have (`can_request = can_write && announce`). The hub turns `announce` off for every peer (bd-jvag5d4w). So a plain peer connection to the remote hub never fetched anything, and never pushed documents created in the browser.

The new `HubSharePolicy` (`crates/quarto-hub/src/upstream.rs`) keeps `announce` off for every peer except peer ids recorded as the upstream. **A hub without `--hub-url` records none, so `q2 hub` and the normal preview behave exactly as before.** The existing test that pins the announce-off policy is untouched.

Other parts:

- `HubConfig::upstream`: mirror mode refuses a local project. It dials the upstream and records its peer id, again on every reconnect, before loading the index, because samod does not revive a `find()` that has already completed. It loads the upstream index and **never creates a new one**: an unknown project is an error rather than a silently empty project. It then prefetches the file documents in the background.
- **What `--allow-edit` means for a mirror.** Without it, browser clients get samod read-only access: they see every change, and their edits never reach the remote project. With it, edits go through. This matches what the flag means in local mode and keeps the editor's "edits won't be saved" banner accurate.
- **The CLI.** `--hub-url` requires `--project`. It conflicts with a path, `--no-project`, `--join`, `--static`, `--share`, `--to`, `-M` and `--profile`. `--project` accepts a bare id, an `automerge:` URL, or a `…/#/share/<id>?…` link.

## Testing

- **New integration tests:** `crates/quarto-hub/tests/integration/upstream_mirror.rs`, five tests, each running two real hubs over TCP. They check that:
  - the mirror fetches the index and the files;
  - an unknown project is an error;
  - edits and a new file reach the upstream;
  - a client's edit is forwarded with `--allow-edit` semantics and dropped without them.
- **The tests depend on the policy change.** With the old announce-off policy for the upstream peer, the fetch and push tests fail.
- **Unit tests** for `--project` parsing.
- **Manual end-to-end runs** against `q2 hub --project <dir>`, in all three modes:
  - the viewer followed an edit made to the hub's file on disk;
  - an `--allow-edit` block edit was written to the hub's file;
  - in the editor, a source edit and a "New file" both reached the hub's disk.
- **Local checks:** `cargo nextest` on `quarto-hub`, `quarto-preview` and `quarto` passed (1797 tests). `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` and clippy with `-D warnings` are clean.
- **Windows:** I couldn't cross-check from macOS, because `ring` and `aws-lc-sys` build C for the target. The new code uses no platform-specific APIs. A Windows check would be `cargo clippy -p quarto-hub --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

## Not in this PR (follow-ups listed in the plan)

- **Sign-in:** hubs that require it, such as quarto-hub.com, won't accept the connection yet, because peer connections send no credentials.
- **Editor wording:** in mirror mode, the editor's startup link still marks the session ephemeral, and the banner tooltip's wording is written for local mode.
- **Local-only routes:** re-run code, PDF and downloads need a local project folder, and they aren't hidden in mirror mode yet.

title: Fix io.popen deadlock in parallel renders on macOS (#1205)
description:
Fixes #1205 (bd-hf93wq9r).

## Problem

A Lua shortcode or filter that calls `io.popen` could hang `q2 render` forever, at 0% CPU, once pass 2 rendered several pages at once. Stock Lua defines `l_popen` on POSIX as `(fflush(NULL), popen(c, m))`. On macOS, `fflush(NULL)` runs `_fwalk`, which walks every open `FILE` **without a lock** and locks each one. Meanwhile a concurrent `fclose` (from `pclose`, or a plain `io.open`/`close` in another Lua state) destroys that `FILE`'s mutex in `__sfprelease` before clearing `_flags`. The walker then waits forever. q2 runs one Lua state per render thread, so extensions that shell out through `io.popen` deadlocked website renders.

The triage record is in `claude-notes/issue-reports/1205/triage.md`. It includes a standalone C repro with no Lua that deadlocks 3/3, the source-level mechanism from Apple's Libc, and prior art: musl hit the same Lua popen deadlock in 2018, and darwin-dev reported the same stack in 2014.

## Fix

Native Lua is built from the repo's own lua-src fork (`crates/lua-src-wasm`, applied via `[patch.crates-io]`). `liolib.c` only defines `l_popen`/`l_pclose` when `l_popen` is undefined, so the fork's `Build` now predefines them as plain `popen(c,m)`/`pclose(file)` on the POSIX targets (linux, bsd, apple):

- `io.popen` keeps exactly the stock semantics (`io.type`, `read`/`lines`/`write`, `close` returning the exit status), and every Lua state is covered.
- `popen`/`pclose` never walk the `FILE` list, so nothing on the `io.popen` path reaches `_fwalk` any more. `os.exit` was already replaced (GH #941), so Lua cannot reach `exit()`'s walk either.
- What the flush bought was ordering: a script's unflushed `io.write` output reached a shared stdout before the child's. `print` flushes on its own, and `pandoc.pipe` never had this behaviour.
- Windows' `_popen` never flushed, and the wasm targets have no popen, so neither is affected.

Alternatives considered: a global lock around `popen`/`pclose`/`fflush(NULL)` is not enough, because any `fclose` can be the other side of the race. Replacing `io.popen` in Rust via `mlua::ffi` works, but it is larger and needs unsafe code.

## Tests

- New `pampa` integration test `test_lua_popen_parallel`: 8 threads each run the real `apply_lua_filters` path with a filter looping `io.popen` plus `io.open`/`close`. **Before the fix it deadlocked past its 120 s deadline on macOS; after the fix it passes in about 0.5 s (6/6 runs).** macOS CI runs it.
- The reporter's 61-page repro (`claude-notes/issue-reports/1205/repro.sh`) renders 61/61 pages in about 1 s (3/3 runs). Before the fix it hung indefinitely.
- I confirmed by disassembly that the rebuilt `liolib.o`'s `io_popen` calls `_popen` directly, with no `fflush`.
- `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` passes locally on macOS: all 19,972 Rust tests, plus the hub-client, preview and MCP suites. The known flake `quarto-preview join_frontend::head_peek_timeout_closes` (bd-7kp7kjdq, a sub-millisecond margin) failed twice under full-suite load. It is unrelated, and it passed in the `--no-fail-fast` workspace run and when rerun alone.

## Cross-platform

- **Linux:** covered by CI. glibc is probably not affected by the libc race, but the change applies there too and is harmless.
- **Windows:** the build-script change is gated on the target string and does not apply to Windows. `cargo clippy -p lua-src --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -- -D warnings` is clean. `pampa` cannot be cross-checked from macOS, because its C build scripts (tree-sitter, aws-lc-sys) need MSVC. A Windows user could run `cargo clippy -p pampa --all-targets -- -D warnings` natively; the new test file uses no platform-specific APIs.

title: engine: run code cells in the document's directory; honor project execute-dir
description:
Closes #1202.

Code cells in a project document now run in the document's own directory, as in Quarto 1. They run from the project root only when `_quarto.yml` sets `project: execute-dir: project`. Before this change every engine ran from the project root, so a page in `sub/` that opened `data.csv` failed.

## What changed

- `crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/engine_execution.rs`: new `resolve_execute_dir` (document dir, or project root under `project: execute-dir: project`; only the `project:` key counts, as in Quarto 1). It sets `ExecutionContext.cwd`, which Jupyter and TS-protocol engines (Julia, extension engines) start in.
- `crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/mod.rs`: knitr now gets `ctx.cwd` as its root dir (`knit_root_dir`); before, it got the project root. The Rscript process still runs in the project dir (or the document's dir inside an renv), matching Quarto 1's `callR`. The figure-reading fallback now looks in the execute dir, then the document dir.
- `crates/quarto-core/src/engine/context.rs`: doc comment for `cwd`.

Quarto 1 references: `src/command/render/render-files.ts` (`cwd: flags.executeDir || dirname(source)`), `src/command/render/project.ts` (`execute-dir: project`), `src/resources/rmd/execute.R` (`knit_root_dir`).

**Not included:** `q2 render --execute-dir` is declared in `main.rs` but never passed to the render pipeline, and the same goes for `--execute-param(s)` and `--execute-daemon*`. Connecting it means threading a value through the render options, so it is filed separately as bd-rhdc3jb8.

## Testing

- New unit tests (`resolve_execute_dir`: default, `file`, `project`, single-file ignores `project`) and a new integration test `tests/integration/execute_dir.rs`, which renders a page in `sub/` with a file-backed fixture engine. The two document-dir cases failed before the fix, and all pass after it.
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core`: 8419 passed, 36 skipped.
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto`: 909 passed, 2 skipped.
- `cargo clippy -p quarto-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: Graphviz (dot) diagrams for the HTML formats
description:
A plain ```` ```dot ```` fence now draws a Graphviz diagram in HTML, RevealJS
and Dashboard output, in `q2 preview`, and in QuartoHub. It follows the
Mermaid pattern throughout. Strand: bd-ijlapt70.

## What is in it

- `q2 render`: a `graphviz-render` AST transform (Finalization phase, HTML
  formats only) that emits `<pre class="graphviz">` plus a vendored runtime,
  included only when the page has a diagram.
- Preview and QuartoHub: a React component that draws the diagram in the
  browser, so edits show up immediately. The render transform is excluded
  from the preview pipeline, as Mermaid's is.
- Runtime: `@viz-js/viz` 3.31.0 (Graphviz 16.1.0), vendored under
  `resources/graphviz/`. The wasm is embedded in the script, so pages work
  offline. About 1.3 MB, loaded only when needed.
- Cell options with `//|`: `label`, `fig-cap`, `fig-align`, `fig-alt`, and
  `graph-layout` (dot, neato, fdp, and the other built-in engines).
- Diagnostics: the brace form `{dot}` warns (Q-2-58) with a hint to drop the
  braces; bad option values warn (Q-2-47).
- Docs: a Graphviz section in the diagrams guide and updated error pages.
  The plan with evidence is `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-13-graphviz-support.md`.

## Checked

- Workspace tests: 19,979 of 19,982 pass locally. The 3 failures are not from
  this change: two need R or Python packages missing on my machine, and one
  `quarto-preview` test (`a_prose_edit_while_stopped_reuses_the_record_through_the_ref`)
  fails in parallel and fails the same way on main.
- `q2 render` to HTML, RevealJS and Dashboard, opened in Chrome, including
  offline.
- `q2 preview` for a document and for slides, and QuartoHub, in Chromium.
  Firefox and Safari checked by eye for preview.

## Decisions I would like a yes or no on

1. Client-side drawing for the HTML formats (this PR), with a render-time
   SVG path for other formats later.
2. A plain `dot` fence now draws a diagram instead of showing highlighted
   source. Mermaid made the same trade.
3. The preview sanitises Graphviz SVG (drops scripts, event handlers and
   non-http links), since diagram source is shared between collaborators.
4. Licence notice: Viz.js is MIT, but the bundle contains Graphviz object
   code under the EPL. Only the MIT licence file ships so far.

## Not done

- `cargo xtask verify` was not run to completion as one command (build,
  tests and hub build were run separately).
- The branch was 10 commits behind main when pushed. It merges cleanly, but
  the merged state was not tested locally.
- `file:`, `echo: true`, `fig-width`, `fig-height` and `fig-responsive` are
  not supported yet, and the Quarto 1 smoke fixtures are not ported.
- Rendered output (as opposed to preview) was not opened in Firefox or Safari.

## What comes next: Typst and the other non-HTML formats (bd-atz1c25y)

Those formats have no browser to draw the diagram, so the approach changes:
q2 runs Graphviz itself at render time, writes an SVG file, and puts an
image in the document. Until then they print the source as a code block,
as Mermaid does in Typst today.

How it differs from this PR:

- Layout happens during `q2 render`, not in the reader's browser, so a
  syntax error can become a source-mapped diagnostic instead of a box in
  the page.
- It needs a way to run Graphviz natively. A spike picks it; the options
  are still open.
- It must pin the same Graphviz version as the browser runtime, so a
  diagram looks the same in HTML and in Typst.
- The fence and the cell options stay the same, so documents do not change.
- The same path is the route to Mermaid in Typst, so it may be worth
  designing for both.
- Once it exists, `q2 render` to HTML could inline the SVG too. Preview and
  QuartoHub keep the browser component either way, because the hub build of
  q2 is itself wasm and cannot run a second Graphviz at render time.
