title: Hold cell output by default; add output-interleave to opt in
description:
## Summary

Every engine now presents a cell's outputs after its source by default. The new `output-interleave` option opts a cell or document into interleaving, so source and output alternate in execution order.

Julia changes the most. It used to interleave by default. It now matches Quarto 1 and holds its output. knitr keeps interleaving, because it declares `interleaves_output` on its engine entry. Quarto 1 interleaves knitr output the same way.

**This PR is stacked on #1197.** That PR vendors the Julia engine subtree up to `c8af0a4` (the `executeEnv` mapping). This PR adds one more fork commit, `4892bf5`, with its own `cargo xtask pull-extension-subtree julia-engine`. Review only the changes on top of #1197. This PR retargets to `main` when #1197 merges.

## Behavior

The presenter resolves interleaving in this order:

1. The cell's `#| output-interleave` value.
2. The document's `execute: output-interleave` value.
3. The engine's declaration. Engines that declare nothing hold their output.

The knitr options `results: hold`, `fig.show: hold`, and `fig.beforecode` now apply to any interleaved cell that has output anchors. Before, they applied only to knitr records. The presenter reads their values from the Quarto options, not from knitr's raw JSON.

`output-interleave` is display-only for every engine. It never reaches a cell as an attribute.

## Compatibility

- **Julia documents** that relied on interleaving now render held. Add `output-interleave: true` to keep the old layout.
- **knitr records** from before this change become stale and re-run, because `KNITR_HASH_VERSION` moves from 3 to 4. Old records lack the interleaving declaration and would otherwise render held.
- **Julia records** keep hash version 2. A record that sets `output-interleave` re-runs once. All other records are unaffected.
- **Jupyter** gains no interleaving. Its records carry no output anchors, so the option has no effect there yet.
- `fig.beforecode` is now a reader key for Jupyter. It is no longer forwarded as a `fig.beforecode='true'` cell attribute.

## The larger question

`claude-notes/research/2026-11-13-results-hold-across-engines.md` asks which of knitr's output-presentation features every engine can offer under a Quarto name, when each engine records different facts about where its outputs came from. This PR answers the first part for output placement. The note also covers the features that remain, such as `prompt` and numeric `echo`, and a possible IPython route to interleaving for Jupyter.

## Testing

- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core` on this stacked branch: 8411 passed, 36 skipped (`#[ignore]`d real-engine tests). The 8 tests beyond the unstacked count of 8403 come from #1197.
- `cargo clippy -p quarto-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo xtask lint` are clean.
- The live parity gate passes: 93 identical cases, 0 allowlisted, 0 blockers.
- End to end through `q2`: Julia held by default and interleaved with the option; knitr interleaved by default, held with `output-interleave: false` at document and cell scope, and `results: hold` unchanged. The invocations and output are in the plan.
- The Julia engine fork's 57 unit tests pass.
- No snapshot files changed.
- **Not run:** the Windows cross-clippy. The `wasmtime` and `aws-lc-sys` build scripts can't cross-compile from macOS. The change adds no platform APIs, `cfg` gates, or path assertions. A Windows user can run `cargo clippy -p quarto-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-13-output-interleave.md`.

title: Fix flaky fake Jupyter kernel: report a lost port instead of exiting 0 (bd-0w8rgjdf)
description:
Fixes the `test_fake_kernel_two_names_one_binary` flake seen on ubuntu CI (PR #1182, run 43109976168; PR #1201, run 43480871431):

```
ExitedDuringStartup { kernel: "fake-a", code: Some(0), stderr: "" }
```

## Cause

The daemon peeks five free ports, then spawns the kernel, which binds them itself. Something else can take a port in between; the daemon's comments already describe this race, and bd-e87d5tmn added a retry for it. The retry fires only when the kernel's **stderr** reports `Address already in use`, which is what ipykernel does.

The fake kernel (`fake_kernel.rs`) runs runtimelib's `TestKernel`, which binds its sockets inside a spawned task. The fake did `let _ = handle.await;`, discarding the bind error. The process then returned normally from its libtest entry, so it exited **0 with empty stderr**. The daemon couldn't tell that apart from any other early exit and failed without retrying.

## Fix

`run_kernel_process` now checks the task's result. On an error it prints the error to stderr and exits 1, the way ipykernel does, so the existing port-conflict retry covers the fake too. This change touches only the fake: the daemon is unchanged, so a real kernel that exits 0 during startup is still reported.

## Test

`test_fake_kernel_losing_a_port_reports_a_port_conflict` holds a port with a `TcpListener`, runs the fake-kernel entry on a connection file that names it, and asserts a non-zero exit that `is_port_conflict()`. Before the fix it failed with the CI signature (`code: Some(0), stderr: ""`). After the fix:

- all 12 `fake_kernel` tests pass;
- the 199 Jupyter tests in the quarto-core lib passed in each of 5 local runs (macOS);
- host clippy with `--all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

**Windows:** the cross-check (`--target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) can't run from macOS because the `tree-sitter` and `aws-lc-sys` build scripts fail. The change uses only std/tokio, and Winsock's `WSAEADDRINUSE` text is already one of the `is_port_conflict` markers. The new test relies on Windows refusing to bind a held port, so it is worth one native run: `cargo clippy -p quarto-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` plus the `fake_kernel` tests.

Plan and investigation: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-13-fake-kernel-startup-flake.md` (includes a shell repro under `fake-kernel-startup-flake-investigation/`).

Unrelated flake seen during local pre-flight, filed as bd-7j80wlkp: a real-ipykernel `jupyter_record_shadow` test timed out after 300s under full-suite load.

title: Publish q2 releases to PyPI as quarto2 (bd-2p7dwmqe)
description:
Adds a `quarto2` package on PyPI for every q2 release, published from this repo with trusted publishing (no tokens). Strand bd-2p7dwmqe; plan in `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-13-pypi-publishing.md`.

## Why an sdist that downloads at install time

Platform archives are 84–92 MB each and we release several times a week, so per-platform wheels would hit PyPI's 100 MB file limit soon and its 10 GB project limit in about six weeks. Like Quarto 1's `quarto-cli-pypi`, the sdist carries no binary. Unlike it:

- **Own build backend:** an in-tree, stdlib-only PEP 517 backend (`requires = []`) writes the wheel itself. The native `q2` goes in `.data/scripts/`, so the installed `q2` is the binary itself, with no Python wrapper.
- **Pinned checksums:** the sdist pins each platform archive's SHA-256, and the install aborts on a mismatch.
- **Correct wheel tags:** locally built wheels are tagged `py3-none-<host>`, never `any`, so a shared pip cache can't serve the wrong platform's binary.
- **No manual bump:** the version comes from the tag. `QUARTO2_DOWNLOAD_BASE` lets air-gapped sites use a mirror.

## What's here

- **`packaging/pypi/`:** the package plus 26 offline tests, including a real `pip install` against a fake release served from disk.
- **`.github/workflows/publish-pypi.yml`** (`workflow_dispatch`: `tag`, `target`, `post`). It builds the sdist from a published release's `checksums.sha256`, then smoke-installs it with pip and `uv tool install` on Linux x64/arm64, macOS and Windows x64/arm64. It uploads via OIDC to `pypi` or `testpypi`, then installs the version back from the index. The `pypi` environment (main only, required reviewer) gates the upload for now.
- **`release.yml`:** a new `pypi` job dispatches the workflow above after a published release. Dry runs skip it, and nightlies never reach it.
- **`.github/workflows/pypi-package.yml`:** PR tests on Linux, macOS and Windows, plus Python 3.9 as the floor. `cargo xtask verify` runs the same command in step 1 (`--skip-pypi-tests`), and a test fails if the two commands drift apart.
- **Docs:** a new § PyPI in the release runbook, and AGENTS.md lists the new verify flag.

## Verification

- `python3 -I -m unittest discover -s packaging/pypi/tests`: 26 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p xtask -E 'test(verify::)'`: passed. `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean, on host and on `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`. `cargo xtask lint`: clean. actionlint is clean on all three workflows.
- **End to end on macOS arm64, against the published v0.45.0:**
  - The sdist is 8,624 bytes, and `twine check --strict` passes on it.
  - `pip install` produced `venv/bin/q2` as a 178 MB Mach-O arm64 binary. `q2 --version` printed `q2 (quarto 2) 0.45.0`, as did `python -m quarto2 --version`.
  - `q2 render` produced the expected HTML; I opened it and checked.
  - `uv tool install` also works, and its cached wheel is tagged `py3-none-macosx_11_0_arm64`.
- **Not yet run:**
  - Linux and Windows installs; the `smoke` matrix covers them.
  - `publish-pypi.yml` itself. It can only be dispatched once it's on `main`. The plan after merge is a TestPyPI rehearsal for v0.45.0, then the first PyPI publish.

## Setup already done

- **PyPI and TestPyPI:** pending trusted publishers for `quarto2` (repo `quarto-dev/q2`, workflow `publish-pypi.yml`, environments `pypi` / `testpypi`).
- **GitHub:** environments `pypi` (deploys from `main` only, required reviewer) and `testpypi`.

title: Pass the execute environment to julia and marimo cells
description:
## Summary

Julia and marimo cells now see the same environment variables that knitr and Jupyter cells see. This extends #1161, which gave knitr and Jupyter the Quarto 1 execute environment, and closes the same gap for the two TypeScript engines. It also fixes a regression from Quarto 1, where both engines inherited the `_environment` values.

Quarto 2 never changes its own process environment. It computes the variables as data and hands them to each process that runs user code. The TypeScript engine protocol had no field to carry that data, so julia and marimo received nothing. This PR adds one optional field, `executeEnv`, to the `execute` options. It carries two sets of variables:

- The project environment: values from the `_environment` files, plus `QUARTO_PROFILE`.
- The per-document variables: `QUARTO_PROJECT_ROOT`, `QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH`, `QUARTO_DOCUMENT_FILE`, `QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO`, and `QUARTO_FIG_*`.

Per-document values win over project values, as they do for knitr. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-12-ts-engines-execute-env.md` (bd-x3h4zjhl).

## What changes

- **Rust (`quarto-core`):** `TsExecuteOptions` gains `execute_env`, a `BTreeMap` that Rust leaves out of the JSON when empty. `TsEngine::build_execute_options` fills it.
- **Host and types:** `@quarto/engine-host-node` copies `executeEnv` into a fresh object for each execute and never touches `process.env`. `@quarto/types` gains an optional, read-only `executeEnv` on `ExecuteOptions`. The embedded host bundle is rebuilt.
- **marimo:** The engine passes `executeEnv` to the `extract.py` process, the only process that runs cells. The `uv` dependency resolver doesn't get it.
- **julia:** The engine maps `executeEnv` to QuartoNotebookRunner's per-run `env`.
- **CI and `verify`:** Both now run the host package's typecheck.
- **Docs:** Four pages are updated: Execution Context, TS engines, Project Environment, and Profiles. The TS engines page gains a section on the contract for engine authors.

## Compatibility

Version skew is harmless in every direction. Nothing rejects unknown fields, so an old host or engine ignores `executeEnv`, and an old q2 sends nothing. Third-party engines opt in. An engine that ignores the field keeps working, and its code sees none of the variables.

## Fork changes

Both engines are changed in their forks and synced here:

| Engine | Fork commit | q2 sync |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| marimo | `d2558d1` | fixture sync, in `2e8ac7d6e` |
| julia | `c8af0a4` | subtree pull (`423574be7`, merge `e701196e5`); the `vendored.toml` pin is in `ad4e5b64e` |

## Testing

- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core -p quarto`: 9305 passed, 38 skipped (before the final rebase onto `main`).
- `cargo clippy -p quarto-core -p quarto --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Host package: 181 tests pass, and the typecheck is clean.
- Fork tests: marimo 40 of 40, julia 57 of 57.
- CLI end-to-end through the real binary: `execute_env_cli_e2e::` runs 4 tests, and all pass, including after the rebase. I inspected the `env.json` that the julia and marimo cells wrote. Each shows every `QUARTO_*` variable, `QUARTO_PROFILE=prod`, and both the `_environment` and profile values.
- Julia edge cases (17 tests in `julia_engine_e2e::`): a daemon rerender with a changed `fig-width`, two documents sharing a worker, a single file outside a project, and a path containing a space.

Julia is not installed in CI, so the julia end-to-end tests run only on a machine that has it. The marimo CLI test runs in CI.

## Notes for reviewers

- The test helper `printed()` in `julia_engine_e2e.rs` matched the code listing before the cell output. It now takes the last match. The product code was correct.
- `QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO` changes on every render, so QuartoNotebookRunner re-runs its package-loading hooks each time. The hooks are cheap and idempotent, and the worker doesn't restart.
- `executeEnv` can carry secrets from `_environment.local`. Neither q2 nor the host logs it.
- The history ends in a julia subtree merge commit, so it is not linear.

title: fix(hub): flush samod storage before dropping the hub context
description:
## Summary

samod saves index changes on background tasks, and dropping a `HubContext`
abandons the tasks that haven't run. `HubContext::shutdown()` now waits for
those writes to reach disk. The restart tests and the server stop path call it.

This fixes the flaky test
`capture_driver::tests::a_prose_edit_while_stopped_reuses_the_record_through_the_ref`.

## Cause

The test writes a `CaptureRef` to the hub index, drops the context, and opens
a second session on the same data directory. When the save loses the race with
the drop, the second session starts without the ref and runs the engine again.
The assertion fails with `left: 1, right: 0`.

The failure appears on ubuntu CI runners and not on macOS. It occurred in runs
43280245849, 43278693666, and 43461850260 (PR #1197, which doesn't touch
`quarto-preview`).

## Changes

- Add `HubContext::shutdown()`, which awaits `Repo::stop()`. `Repo::stop()`
  waits for pending storage tasks.
- Call `shutdown()` before `drop(ctx)` in the restart tests.
- Call `shutdown()` at the end of the server stop path, which had the same gap.
- Add `capture_ref_survives_restart_after_shutdown` to `quarto-hub`.

The two commits are separate. The second one, "flush samod storage on server
stop", is the only change to real server behavior, so you can review or revert
it on its own.

## Verification

Before the fix, the test failed in 1 of 170 runs under CPU load (12 busy-loop
processes and `cargo nextest run --stress-count`). A temporary test in
`quarto-hub`, with no engine involved, lost the ref in 1 of 5 runs. After the
fix, 600 of 600 stress runs pass.

- `cargo clippy -p quarto-preview -p quarto-hub --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  is clean.
- `cargo nextest run -p quarto-preview -p quarto-hub` passes: 884 passed,
  1 skipped.
- No snapshot files change.

## Review notes

- The new `quarto-hub` test passes deterministically but can't fail before the
  fix, because `shutdown()` doesn't exist there. The stress runs above are the
  evidence that the race is gone.
- The server stop change isn't exercised against a real `q2 preview` or `hub`
  stop. A stopped repo rejects further use, so check that nothing uses the
  context after `serve` returns.
- The sibling tests `restart_marks_existing_capture_stale_when_code_changed_offline`
  and `restart_clears_persisted_stale_flag_when_content_matches` reuse one
  context and don't reopen the data directory, so they don't have this race.

title: Honor -M in q2 preview engine runs and keep record copies current
description:
This change makes `q2 preview` run every engine under the session's `-M`
overlay and re-run a stale document on every save. A client, such as an
editor extension, can then keep the `.quarto` record copy current by passing
these flags:

```
-M 'execute:{record: true, record-sources: engine}'
-M 'preview:{engine: auto}'
```

Before this change, `-M` reached only the browser's render, not the engines.
Neither `execute: {record: true}` nor `execute: {echo: false}` took effect in
a preview run, so q2 never rewrote the copy. Under `auto`, a stale document
re-ran only when its staleness changed (bd-twox482l).

## Changes

The branch has four commits, one per item.

- **Hash.** `execute: {record: ...}` no longer changes a document's hash, so
  turning on recording doesn't make existing records stale. The hash
  definition's `version` isn't bumped. Each engine owns that field, and a
  bump would make every record stale. Records written with
  `execute: {record: true}` in front matter read as stale once, then refresh
  on the next run.
- **`overlay_free_run`.** The function moves from quarto-hub-provider to
  quarto-core, and the provider re-exports it.
- **`-M` in engine runs.** Startup captures, a file change's re-execute, the
  Re-execute button, and `auto` all run under `runtime_with_overlay()`. q2
  then makes the run describe the source again, because staleness is computed
  without the overlay. The cache key includes `-M`. The lint test
  `engine_runs_take_the_overlay_runtime` keeps new engine call sites on the
  overlay runtime. Re-execute reads the cache only when `cache` is one of the
  document's record sources. Under `auto`, a stale document re-runs on every
  save, including after a failed run and when it was stale at startup. If a
  save arrives during a run, q2 checks the document again when the run ends.
- **`preview.engine`.** You can set `preview.engine` with `-M`, including for
  `--static`. Under `auto`, `--share` lets guests' edits run code on the
  host. q2 now prints a warning at startup, and the preview and execution
  records guides describe the risk.

## Testing

- Seven new integration tests (`live_reexecute`, with a stub engine) fail on
  the source before the fix and pass after it. The tests drive staleness
  through `recompute_staleness`, not the file watcher (bd-9brz).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean on quarto-core,
  quarto-hub-provider, quarto-preview, and quarto.
- `nextest -p quarto-preview` passes 383 tests and skips 1 (the bd-9brz
  test). `nextest -p quarto -E 'test(preview)'` passes 121.
- An end-to-end run with the real binary and a Python kernel confirms the
  behavior. Startup wrote the copy. An edit and save, and then a revert and
  save, each re-ran the document and rewrote the copy. `q2 convert` with
  `record-sources: q2` then produced the notebook without running any code.
  The change was also used by hand in an editor with this build.
- `q2 render --strict` shows no warnings for the three notes files.

## Not tested

- The full `nextest -p quarto-hub-provider -p quarto` run. The move of
  `overlay_free_run` affects the provider.
- `nextest -p quarto-core` reports 249 failures on the development machine.
  The local pandoc is 3.12.1 and q2 requires 3.13, and two revealjs vendoring
  checks also fail. None of the failures are record or hash tests, but the
  results weren't compared against a clean `main`.
- The docs build. The same pandoc version limit applies.
- Windows. No cross-check was run.

## Follow-ups

- bd-k8ui7n5m: `-M` doesn't merge repeated keys, so a client passes one
  combined `execute` map.
- bd-stbigif1: q2 writes the `.quarto` copy in place, not atomically.

Closes bd-twox482l.

title: fix(hub-client): authors overlay matches the text shown, in replay, live and on branches
description:
With the authors overlay on, the preview could colour a text with attribution built for a different text. This fixes the three places that happened, then removes the cost the fix added to each keystroke.

Strand: bd-bay844no. Plan: `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-13-replay-attribution-at-heads.md`.

## Replay (bd-bay844no)

- **Symptom:** in replay, words were coloured for the wrong author, and the colours shifted from step to step.
- **Cause:** the attribution was built for the live document, then laid over the text of the replay step. Its offsets belong to the final text.
- **Fix:** attribution is built for the replay step itself. `ReplaySession.getHeadsAt` gives the step's change hashes, and `useAttribution` takes them as `atHeads`. A forward step applies only the new changes; a backward seek rebuilds, and the preview holds its render until that finishes.
- **Tests:** the runs at every step equal a build of the document forked at that step; forward steps apply only the new changes; a backward seek shows nothing stale.

## Live edits (bd-1ga6itse)

- **Symptom:** after an edit, words after the edit point showed the wrong author. With collaborators typing without pause, it never corrected.
- **Cause:** the preview re-rendered on every text change, but the attribution refreshed only after 500 ms without a change.
- **Fix:** each edit is folded into the attribution as its text arrives, with no debounce. If the history and the text shown differ in length, the text is drawn without the overlay instead of with shifted colours.
- **Tests:** continuous edits from two collaborators are followed in the same update; under concurrent edits to one sentence, each character is attributed to the author of the op that inserted it.

## Local branches (bd-1ewams7j)

- **Symptom:** on a local branch, the overlay showed main's authorship over the branch text, and branch edits were never attributed.
- **Cause:** the hook always read the synced main document.
- **Fix:** the hook takes `branchId` and reads the branch's document.
- **Tests:** branch runs come from the branch document; main's runs return on switching back.

## Cost of the synchronous update

- **Symptom:** with the debounce gone, every keystroke cost time proportional to the document: 2.2 ms at 10k characters, 8.8 ms at 40k, 35 ms at 160k (synthetic benchmark).
- **Cause:** each change was applied to a second copy of the document, and Automerge's `applyChanges` scales with document size however small the change. Each text change also rendered the preview twice, because the payload was state set from an effect.
- **Fix:**
  - When the new changes share one author and second, the update reads their patches from the live document, which Automerge keeps for the latest change. Measured 0.04 to 0.06 ms at 10k and 40k. The second copy is caught up, in one call, only when something must replay on it.
  - The attribution state moves to `AttributionStore`, read during render with `useSyncExternalStore`. A live edit or a forward replay step is one render with its own payload.
- **Tests:** patch-based updates equal a full build (single edits, deletions, mixed authors, a replay step, an unrelated history); a live edit and a forward replay step settle in one render; the hook works under StrictMode.

## Verification

- Hub-client unit tests (161 files, 1801 tests), the preview integration tests and `npm run build` pass locally.
- **Browser:** live typing with the overlay on was checked by hand against a local hub. A multi-author replay and a local branch were not checked in a browser.
- Locally, `npm run test:wasm` had 27 failures in `applyNodeEdit.wasm.test.ts` and `formatDetection.wasm.test.ts`. This PR does not touch the Rust WASM, and my local WASM build predates the latest Rust commits, so I expect CI to pass them; I did not rebuild to confirm.

## Known and not addressed

- A cold build (turning the overlay on, or a backward replay seek to a step not yet shown) still pays the per-change cost. A history whose changes cannot be batched is quadratic. Same as `main`.
- A replay step whose build failed is retried only after replay is left and re-entered.
